question: Find a comprehensive profile of all services, including their names, types, overall ratings, average ratings, total views, total clicks, review counts, operational hours, addresses, phone numbers, emails, websites, and descriptions, sorted by their overall rating in descending order and then by their names.
external_knowledge: None required for this query.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ServiceRatings AS ( SELECT r.service_id, AVG(r.rating) AS average_rating FROM reviews r GROUP BY r.service_id ), ServiceAnalytics AS ( SELECT a.service_id, SUM(CASE WHEN a.metric = 'views' THEN a.value ELSE 0 END) AS total_views, SUM(CASE WHEN a.metric = 'clicks' THEN a.value ELSE 0 END) AS total_clicks FROM analytics a GROUP BY a.service_id ), ServiceReviews AS ( SELECT r.service_id, COUNT(r.review_id) AS review_count FROM reviews r GROUP BY r.service_id ), ServiceHours AS ( SELECT sh.service_id, GROUP_CONCAT(sh.day || ' ' || sh.open_time || ' - ' || sh.close_time, ', ') AS operational_hours FROM service_hours sh GROUP BY sh.service_id ) SELECT s.service_id, s.name, st.type_name, IFNULL(sr.average_rating, 0) AS average_rating, IFNULL(sa.total_views, 0) AS total_views, IFNULL(sa.total_clicks, 0) AS total_clicks, IFNULL(srv.review_count, 0) AS review_count, IFNULL(sh.operational_hours, 'N/A') AS operational_hours, s.address, s.phone_number, s.email, s.website, s.rating AS overall_rating, s.operational_hours AS operational_hours, s.description FROM services s LEFT JOIN service_types st ON s.type_id = st.type_id LEFT JOIN ServiceRatings sr ON s.service_id = sr.service_id LEFT JOIN ServiceAnalytics sa ON s.service_id = sa.service_id LEFT JOIN ServiceReviews srv ON s.service_id = srv.service_id LEFT JOIN ServiceHours sh ON s.service_id = sh.service_id ORDER BY s.rating DESC, s.name
gold_sql.mysql: WITH ServiceRatings AS (SELECT r.service_id, AVG(r.rating) AS average_rating FROM reviews AS r GROUP BY r.service_id), ServiceAnalytics AS (SELECT a.service_id, SUM(CASE WHEN a.metric = 'views' THEN a.value ELSE 0 END) AS total_views, SUM(CASE WHEN a.metric = 'clicks' THEN a.value ELSE 0 END) AS total_clicks FROM analytics AS a GROUP BY a.service_id), ServiceReviews AS (SELECT r.service_id, COUNT(r.review_id) AS review_count FROM reviews AS r GROUP BY r.service_id), ServiceHours AS (SELECT sh.service_id, GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(sh.day, ' ', sh.open_time, ' - ', sh.close_time) SEPARATOR ', ') AS operational_hours FROM service_hours AS sh GROUP BY sh.service_id) SELECT s.service_id, s.name, st.type_name, COALESCE(sr.average_rating, 0) AS average_rating, COALESCE(sa.total_views, 0) AS total_views, COALESCE(sa.total_clicks, 0) AS total_clicks, COALESCE(srv.review_count, 0) AS review_count, COALESCE(sh.operational_hours, 'N/A') AS operational_hours, s.address, s.phone_number, s.email, s.website, s.rating AS overall_rating, s.operational_hours AS operational_hours, s.description FROM services AS s LEFT JOIN service_types AS st ON s.type_id = st.type_id LEFT JOIN ServiceRatings AS sr ON s.service_id = sr.service_id LEFT JOIN ServiceAnalytics AS sa ON s.service_id = sa.service_id LEFT JOIN ServiceReviews AS srv ON s.service_id = srv.service_id LEFT JOIN ServiceHours AS sh ON s.service_id = sh.service_id ORDER BY s.rating DESC, s.name
gold_sql.postgres: WITH ServiceRatings AS (SELECT r.service_id, AVG(r.rating) AS average_rating FROM reviews AS r GROUP BY r.service_id), ServiceAnalytics AS (SELECT a.service_id, SUM(CASE WHEN a.metric = 'views' THEN a.value ELSE 0 END) AS total_views, SUM(CASE WHEN a.metric = 'clicks' THEN a.value ELSE 0 END) AS total_clicks FROM analytics AS a GROUP BY a.service_id), ServiceReviews AS (SELECT r.service_id, COUNT(r.review_id) AS review_count FROM reviews AS r GROUP BY r.service_id), ServiceHours AS (SELECT sh.service_id, STRING_AGG(sh.day || ' ' || sh.open_time || ' - ' || sh.close_time, ', ') AS operational_hours FROM service_hours AS sh GROUP BY sh.service_id) SELECT s.service_id, s.name, st.type_name, COALESCE(sr.average_rating, 0) AS average_rating, COALESCE(sa.total_views, 0) AS total_views, COALESCE(sa.total_clicks, 0) AS total_clicks, COALESCE(srv.review_count, 0) AS review_count, COALESCE(sh.operational_hours, 'N/A') AS operational_hours, s.address, s.phone_number, s.email, s.website, s.rating AS overall_rating, s.operational_hours AS operational_hours, s.description FROM services AS s LEFT JOIN service_types AS st ON s.type_id = st.type_id LEFT JOIN ServiceRatings AS sr ON s.service_id = sr.service_id LEFT JOIN ServiceAnalytics AS sa ON s.service_id = sa.service_id LEFT JOIN ServiceReviews AS srv ON s.service_id = srv.service_id LEFT JOIN ServiceHours AS sh ON s.service_id = sh.service_id ORDER BY s.rating DESC NULLS LAST, s.name NULLS FIRST

question: Find the names, study names, decision tree names, study feature values, decision tree feature values, p-values for alternative and null hypotheses, types of statistical tests, chromosomal information, start and end positions, accuracy of decision trees, and researchers' names, along with a combined description of all matching features, ordered by the accuracy of the decision trees in descending order, for all genomic features that are relevant across different studies and decision trees.
external_knowledge:
- Genomic features refer to specific characteristics or attributes of the genome, such as genes or regulatory regions.
- Decision trees are a type of machine learning model used for classification or regression tasks.
- P-values are a measure of the strength of evidence against a null hypothesis in statistical hypothesis testing.
- Accuracy in the context of decision trees refers to the proportion of correctly classified instances out of all instances in the test dataset.
- Researchers in this context are scientists or academics involved in studies related to genomic features and decision trees.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH StudyFeatures AS ( SELECT sf.study_id, sf.feature_id, sf.value AS study_feature_value, sf.source AS study_feature_source, sf.version AS study_feature_version, sf.created_at AS study_feature_created_at, sf.updated_at AS study_feature_updated_at FROM study_features sf ), TreeFeatures AS ( SELECT fv.tree_id, fv.feature_id, fv.value AS tree_feature_value, fv.source AS feature_value_source, fv.version AS feature_value_version, fv.created_at AS feature_value_created_at, fv.updated_at AS feature_value_updated_at FROM feature_values fv ), FeatureStats AS ( SELECT fv.feature_id, fv.tree_id, st.p_val1, st.p_val0, st.test_type, st.confidence_interval, st.created_at AS stat_created_at, st.updated_at AS stat_updated_at FROM feature_values fv INNER JOIN statistical_values st ON fv.value_id = st.value_id ), RelevantFeatures AS ( SELECT sf.feature_id, sf.study_id, tf.tree_id, sf.study_feature_value, tf.tree_feature_value, fs.p_val1, fs.p_val0, fs.test_type, fs.confidence_interval FROM StudyFeatures sf INNER JOIN TreeFeatures tf ON sf.feature_id = tf.feature_id INNER JOIN FeatureStats fs ON tf.feature_id = fs.feature_id AND tf.tree_id = fs.tree_id ), FeatureDetails AS ( SELECT rf.feature_id, rf.study_id, rf.tree_id, rf.study_feature_value, rf.tree_feature_value, rf.p_val1, rf.p_val0, rf.test_type, rf.confidence_interval, gf.feature_name, gf.description, gf.chromosome, gf.start_position, gf.end_position, gf.strand, gf.source AS genomic_feature_source, gf.version AS genomic_feature_version, dt.tree_name, dt.description AS tree_description, dt.algorithm, dt.parameters, dt.accuracy, s.study_name, s.description AS study_description, r.name AS researcher_name, r.email AS researcher_email FROM RelevantFeatures rf INNER JOIN genomic_features gf ON rf.feature_id = gf.feature_id INNER JOIN decision_trees dt ON rf.tree_id = dt.tree_id INNER JOIN studies s ON rf.study_id = s.study_id INNER JOIN researchers r ON question: Can you tell me the names of the athletes and the sports they excel in, along with how much they typically take home in their respective fields?
external_knowledge:
- "excel in" refers to the sports in which athletes participate actively.
- "typically take home" refers to the average earnings calculated from the yearly earnings.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT a.athlete_name, s.sport_name, AVG(CAST(REPLACE(trim(ast.earnings, '$'), ',', '') AS REAL)) AS average_earnings FROM athletes a JOIN annual_stats ast ON a.athlete_id = ast.athlete_id JOIN sports s ON ast.sport_id = s.sport_id GROUP BY a.athlete_name, s.sport_name
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT a.athlete_name, s.sport_name, AVG(CAST(REPLACE(TRIM('$' FROM ast.earnings), ',', '') AS FLOAT)) AS average_earnings FROM athletes AS a JOIN annual_stats AS ast ON a.athlete_id = ast.athlete_id JOIN sports AS s ON ast.sport_id = s.sport_id GROUP BY a.athlete_name, s.sport_name

question: What are the titles, publication years, citation counts, and times cited for the top 10 most cited papers, along with their authors, affiliations, publication names, publishers, and databases?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH TopCitedPapers AS ( SELECT paper_id, title, publication_year, cited_reference_count AS citation_count, times_cited_all_databases FROM papers ORDER BY times_cited_all_databases DESC LIMIT 10 ), AuthorDetails AS ( SELECT pa.paper_id, GROUP_CONCAT(a.author_name, ', ') AS authors, GROUP_CONCAT(a.affiliation, ', ') AS affiliations FROM paper_authors pa JOIN authors a ON pa.author_id = a.author_id GROUP BY pa.paper_id ), PublicationDetails AS ( SELECT pp.paper_id, pub.publication_name, pub.publisher FROM paper_publications pp JOIN publications pub ON pp.publication_id = pub.publication_id ), DatabaseDetails AS ( SELECT pd.paper_id, GROUP_CONCAT(db.database_name, ', ') AS databases FROM paper_databases pd JOIN databases db ON pd.database_id = db.database_id GROUP BY pd.paper_id ) SELECT tcp.paper_id, tcp.title, tcp.publication_year, tcp.citation_count, tcp.times_cited_all_databases, COALESCE(ad.authors, '') AS authors, COALESCE(ad.affiliations, '') AS affiliations, COALESCE(pd.publication_name, '') AS publication_name, COALESCE(pd.publisher, '') AS publisher, COALESCE(dd.databases, '') AS databases FROM TopCitedPapers tcp LEFT JOIN AuthorDetails ad ON tcp.paper_id = ad.paper_id LEFT JOIN PublicationDetails pd ON tcp.paper_id = pd.paper_id LEFT JOIN DatabaseDetails dd ON tcp.paper_id = dd.paper_id

question: Find the details of maintenance activities and inspections that took place in 2023, including the activity type, inspection result, and the first name, last name, and email of the user who performed them, ordered from most recent to oldest.
external_knowledge: No specific external knowledge is required to understand the question; however, having knowledge of maintenance activities and inspections in the context of asset management (e.g., infrastructure, facilities) could enhance the understanding of the context in which this query is used.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT ma.activity_type, i.inspection_result, u.first_name, u.last_name, u.email FROM maintenance_activities ma LEFT JOIN inspections i ON ma.asset_id = i.asset_id AND ma.activity_date = i.inspection_date JOIN users u ON ma.performed_by = u.username WHERE strftime('%Y', ma.activity_date) = '2023' ORDER BY ma.activity_date DESC

question: What are the top 5 most accessed documents, including their types, categories, and contributing authors?
external_knowledge:
- `is_active` = 1 indicates that the document type and category are currently active and valid.
- The `access_count` is derived from the `access_logs` table, which records each access to a document.
- The `contribution_percentage` is a measure of each author's contribution to the document, and the total percentage is normalized to 100% for each document.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH DocumentDetails AS ( SELECT d.doc_id, d.title, dt.type_name AS document_type, c.category_name AS document_category, COUNT(a.access_id) AS access_count FROM documents d JOIN document_types dt ON d.type = dt.type_id JOIN categories c ON d.category = c.category_id LEFT JOIN access_logs a ON d.doc_id = a.doc_id WHERE c.is_active = 1 AND dt.is_active = 1 GROUP BY d.doc_id, d.title, dt.type_name, c.category_name ), AuthorsDetails AS ( SELECT da.doc_id, GROUP_CONCAT(a.author_name, ', ') AS authors FROM document_authors da JOIN authors a ON da.author_id = a.author_id GROUP BY da.doc_id ) SELECT dd.title, dd.document_type, dd.document_category, ad.authors, dd.access_count FROM DocumentDetails dd JOIN AuthorsDetails ad ON dd.doc_id = ad.doc_id ORDER BY dd.access_count DESC LIMIT 5

**Assistant**: Would you also like to know about the applicants for these job postings?
**User**: Yes, please include applicant names, emails, application dates, phone numbers, LinkedIn profiles, portfolio URLs, and application statuses in the results.
**Assistant**: Do you want any statistics about the applicants for each job posting?
**User**: Yes, I'd like to know the total number of applicants and the average years of experience required for each job.
**Assistant**: Should the results be ordered in a specific way?

question: What are the countries, their average points awarded, and the number of athletes for those countries that participated in the 'US Open' in 2022 and had an average points awarded above 100, listed in order of highest to lowest average points?
external_knowledge: US Open refers to a specific competition; '2022' refers to the year the competition took place; Average points awarded > 100 is the threshold for country performance.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT c.country_name, AVG(cr.points_awarded) AS average_points_awarded, COUNT(DISTINCT a.member_id) AS total_athletes FROM athletes a INNER JOIN countries c ON a.country = c.country_code INNER JOIN competition_results cr ON a.member_id = cr.member_id INNER JOIN competitions comp ON cr.competition_id = comp.competition_id WHERE comp.name = 'US Open' AND strftime('%Y', comp.start_date) = '2022' GROUP BY c.country_name HAVING AVG(cr.points_awarded) > 100 ORDER BY average_points_awarded DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT c.country_name, AVG(cr.points_awarded) AS average_points_awarded, COUNT(DISTINCT a.member_id) AS total_athletes FROM athletes AS a INNER JOIN countries AS c ON a.country = c.country_code INNER JOIN competition_results AS cr ON a.member_id = cr.member_id INNER JOIN competitions AS comp ON cr.competition_id = comp.competition_id WHERE comp.name = 'US Open' AND DATE_FORMAT(CAST(comp.start_date AS DATETIME), '%Y') = '2022' GROUP BY c.country_name HAVING AVG(cr.points_awarded) > 100 ORDER BY average_points_awarded DESC
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT c.country_name, AVG(cr.points_awarded) AS average_points_awarded, COUNT(DISTINCT a.member_id) AS total_athletes FROM athletes AS a INNER JOIN countries AS c ON a.country = c.country_code INNER JOIN competition_results AS cr ON a.member_id = cr.member_id INNER JOIN competitions AS comp ON cr.competition_id = comp.competition_id WHERE comp.name = 'US Open' AND TO_CHAR(CAST(comp.start_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY') = '2022' GROUP BY c.country_name HAVING AVG(cr.points_awarded) > 100 ORDER BY average_points_awarded DESC NULLS LAST

question: Could you provide a detailed report of each cycling event, including the participating team names, their ranks, completion statuses, average speeds, distances ridden, times, bicycle classes, locations, event types, registration dates, event statuses, the number of teams, the number of completions and non-completions, the average speed, the minimum and maximum event times, and the final rankings of the teams, all ordered by event ID and final rank?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH EventAndTeam AS ( SELECT e.event_id, e.ride_date, t.team_name, r.completion_status, r.rank, r.average_speed, e.distance_ridden, e.time, b.class_name AS bicycle_class_name, e.location, e.event_type, e.registration_open_date, e.registration_close_date, e.event_status, e.sortable_time, r.result_id, t.team_id FROM events e INNER JOIN teams t ON e.team_name = t.team_name LEFT JOIN results r ON e.event_id = r.event_id AND t.team_id = r.team_id LEFT JOIN bicycle_classes b ON e.bicycle_class = b.class_name ), EventAnalytics AS ( SELECT event_id, COUNT(team_id) AS number_of_teams, SUM(IIF(completion_status = 'FIN', 1, 0)) AS completions, SUM(IIF(completion_status = 'DNF', 1, 0)) AS non_completions, AVG(average_speed) AS avg_speed, MIN(sortable_time) AS min_event_time, MAX(sortable_time) AS max_event_time FROM EventAndTeam GROUP BY event_id ), RankedTeams AS ( SELECT event_id, team_name, rank, completion_status, average_speed, distance_ridden, time, bicycle_class_name, location, event_type, registration_open_date, registration_close_date, event_status, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY event_id ORDER BY sortable_time) AS final_rank FROM EventAndTeam ) SELECT et.event_id, et.ride_date, et.team_name, et.rank, et.completion_status, et.average_speed, et.distance_ridden, et.time, et.bicycle_class_name, et.location, et.event_type, et.registration_open_date, et.registration_close_date, et.event_status, ea.number_of_teams, ea.completions, ea.non_completions, ea.avg_speed, ea.min_event_time, ea.max_event_time, rt.final_rank FROM EventAndTeam et JOIN EventAnalytics ea ON et.event_id = ea.event_id JOIN RankedTeams rt ON et.event_id = rt.event_id AND et.team_name = rt.team_name ORDER BY et.event_id, rt.final_rank

question: Could you please identify the region with the highest average smoking intensity and provide the name of the region along with the number of smokers and their average smoking intensity?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RegionSmokers AS ( SELECT sd.region_id, r.region_name, SUM(sd.smoke_cigars_pipe + sd.smoke_both + sd.smoke_cigarettes) AS total_smokers, SUM(sd.smoke_cigars_pipe * sd.average_cigars_pipes_per_day) AS total_cigars_pipes_smoked, SUM(sd.smoke_cigarettes * sd.average_cigarettes_per_day) AS total_cigarettes_smoked FROM smoking_data sd INNER JOIN regions r ON sd.region_id = r.region_id GROUP BY sd.region_id, r.region_name ), RegionAverages AS ( SELECT rs.region_id, rs.region_name, rs.total_smokers, (rs.total_cigars_pipes_smoked + rs.total_cigarettes_smoked) / rs.total_smokers AS avg_smoking_intensity FROM RegionSmokers rs ), RegionRanking AS ( SELECT ra.region_id, ra.region_name, ra.total_smokers, ra.avg_smoking_intensity, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ra.avg_smoking_intensity DESC) AS intensity_rank FROM RegionAverages ra ) SELECT rr.region_name, rr.total_smokers, rr.avg_smoking_intensity FROM RegionRanking rr WHERE rr.intensity_rank = 1

question: What are the full titles, category paths, years of metrics, and impact factors for all journals, organized by their full titles, categories, and years?
external_knowledge: No additional external knowledge is necessary to clarify the question in this case.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RECURSIVE CategoryHierarchy AS ( SELECT category_id, category_name, description, parent_category_id, category_name AS full_path, 1 AS level FROM categories WHERE parent_category_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT c.category_id, c.category_name, c.description, c.parent_category_id, CH.full_path || ' > ' || c.category_name AS full_path, CH.level + 1 FROM categories c JOIN CategoryHierarchy CH ON c.parent_category_id = CH.category_id ) SELECT j.full_title, CH.full_path AS category_path, y.year_name, jm.journal_impact_factor FROM journals j JOIN CategoryHierarchy CH ON j.category_id = CH.category_id JOIN journal_metrics jm ON j.journal_id = jm.journal_id JOIN years y ON jm.year_id = y.year_id ORDER BY j.full_title, CH.full_path, y.year_name

question: Find the names of users who have placed more than three orders, reordered a product before, and have a total order cost greater than 50, and return their total order costs in descending order.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT u.user_name, SUM(o.total_cost) AS total_order_cost FROM users u INNER JOIN orders o ON u.user_id = o.user_id INNER JOIN order_frequency of ON u.user_id = of.user_id WHERE of.order_count > 3 AND of.reordered = 1 GROUP BY u.user_name HAVING SUM(o.total_cost) > 50 ORDER BY total_order_cost DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT u.user_name, SUM(o.total_cost) AS total_order_cost FROM users AS u INNER JOIN orders AS o ON u.user_id = o.user_id INNER JOIN order_frequency AS `of` ON u.user_id = `of`.user_id WHERE `of`.order_count > 3 AND `of`.reordered = 1 GROUP BY u.user_name HAVING SUM(o.total_cost) > 50 ORDER BY total_order_cost DESC
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT u.user_name, SUM(o.total_cost) AS total_order_cost FROM users AS u INNER JOIN orders AS o ON u.user_id = o.user_id INNER JOIN order_frequency AS of ON u.user_id = of.user_id WHERE of.order_count > 3 AND of.reordered = 1 GROUP BY u.user_name HAVING SUM(o.total_cost) > 50 ORDER BY total_order_cost DESC NULLS LAST

question:
**User**: I need a report on the current status of all users, including their goals and challenge participation.
**Assistant**: Sure, I can help with that. Do you want to know about the most recent goals and the highest-ranked challenges for each user?
**User**: Yes, exactly. I want to know if they have active goals, the remaining duration, and the last updated date. Also, if they are participating in any challenges, I want to know their rank and activity points.
**Assistant**: Got it. Do you also want a summary that combines both the goal and challenge information for each user, or should I provide them separately?
**User**: A combined summary would be ideal. It should clearly indicate whether a user has an active goal, a challenge, or neither.
**Assistant**: Understood. I will generate a report that includes the user's name, their most recent goal status (if any), and their highest-ranked challenge status (if any). If a user has no active goals or challenges, that will be noted as well.
**User**: That sounds perfect. Thank you.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RecentGoals AS ( SELECT g.user_id, g.target_duration - g.current_duration AS remaining_duration, g.last_updated, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY g.user_id ORDER BY g.last_updated DESC) AS rownum FROM goals g ), TopChallenges AS ( SELECT c.user_id, c.rank, c.activity_points, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.user_id ORDER BY c.rank ASC) AS ranknum FROM challenge_participants c ) SELECT u.user_name, CASE WHEN rg.rownum = 1 THEN 'Goal remaining: ' || CAST(rg.remaining_duration AS TEXT) || ' minutes, Last updated: ' || rg.last_updated ELSE 'No active goals' END AS goal_status, CASE WHEN tc.ranknum = 1 THEN 'Rank: ' || CAST(tc.rank AS TEXT) || ', Points: ' || CAST(tc.activity_points AS TEXT) ELSE 'Not participating in any challenge' END AS challenge_status FROM users u LEFT JOIN RecentGoals rg ON u.user_id = rg.user_id AND rg.rownum = 1 LEFT JOIN TopChallenges tc ON u.user_id = tc.user_id AND tc.ranknum = 1

question: What is the cumulative sales trend for each product in each region over time?
external_knowledge:
- Cumulative sales are the total sales accumulated over a period of time.
- The `strftime('%Y-%m', s.sale_date)` function extracts the year and month from the `sale_date` column.
- The `SUM` window function is used to calculate the running total of sales.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH MonthlySales AS ( SELECT s.region_id, p.product_id, strftime('%Y-%m', s.sale_date) AS sale_month, SUM(s.quantity_sold * CAST(s.sale_price AS REAL)) AS total_sales FROM sales s JOIN products p ON s.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY s.region_id, p.product_id, strftime('%Y-%m', s.sale_date) ), CumulativeSales AS ( SELECT ms.region_id, ms.product_id, ms.sale_month, ms.total_sales, SUM(ms.total_sales) OVER (PARTITION BY ms.region_id, ms.product_id ORDER BY ms.sale_month) AS cumulative_sales FROM MonthlySales ms ) SELECT cs.region_id, cs.product_id, cs.sale_month, cs.total_sales, cs.cumulative_sales FROM CumulativeSales cs ORDER BY cs.region_id, cs.product_id, cs.sale_month

question: What is the highest combined batting and bowling average for teams in a specific match?
external_knowledge: Batting average is calculated as the total runs scored by a team divided by the number of players on the team; Bowling average is calculated as the average number of runs conceded by a team per wicket taken.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH MatchBattingStats AS ( SELECT pmr.player_id, pmr.match_id, SUM(CASE WHEN pmr.batting_score IS NOT NULL THEN CAST(pmr.batting_score AS INTEGER) ELSE 0 END) AS runs_scored FROM player_match_records pmr WHERE pmr.match_id = 0 AND pmr.role_in_match = 'batsman' GROUP BY pmr.player_id, pmr.match_id ), MatchBowlingStats AS ( SELECT pmr.player_id, pmr.match_id, AVG(CASE WHEN pmr.bowling_wickets > 0 THEN CAST(pmr.bowling_runs AS REAL) / CAST(pmr.bowling_wickets AS REAL) ELSE 0 END) AS bowling_average FROM player_match_records pmr WHERE pmr.match_id = 0 AND pmr.role_in_match = 'bowler' GROUP BY pmr.player_id, pmr.match_id ), TeamBattingAverage AS ( SELECT tc.team_id, SUM(mbs.runs_scored) / COUNT(DISTINCT tc.player_id) AS batting_average FROM MatchBattingStats mbs JOIN team_compositions tc ON mbs.player_id = tc.player_id AND mbs.match_id = tc.match_id GROUP BY tc.team_id ), TeamBowlingAverage AS ( SELECT tc.team_id, AVG(mbs.bowling_average) AS bowling_average FROM MatchBowlingStats mbs JOIN team_compositions tc ON mbs.player_id = tc.player_id AND mbs.match_id = tc.match_id GROUP BY tc.team_id ), CombinedAverage AS ( SELECT tba.team_id, tba.batting_average, tbaa.bowling_average, (tba.batting_average + tbaa.bowling_average) AS total_average FROM TeamBattingAverage tba JOIN TeamBowlingAverage tbaa ON tba.team_id = tbaa.team_id ) SELECT MAX(ca.total_average) AS highest_combined_average FROM CombinedAverage ca

gold_sql.postgres: WITH MatchBattingStats AS (SELECT pmr.player_id, pmr.match_id, SUM(CASE WHEN NOT pmr.batting_score IS NULL THEN CAST(pmr.batting_score AS INT) ELSE 0 END) AS runs_scored FROM player_match_records AS pmr WHERE pmr.match_id = 0 AND pmr.role_in_match = 'batsman' GROUP BY pmr.player_id, pmr.match_id), MatchBowlingStats AS (SELECT pmr.player_id, pmr.match_id, AVG(CASE WHEN pmr.bowling_wickets > 0 THEN CAST(pmr.bowling_runs AS REAL) / NULLIF(CAST(pmr.bowling_wickets AS REAL), 0) ELSE 0 END) AS bowling_average FROM player_match_records AS pmr WHERE pmr.match_id = 0 AND pmr.role_in_match = 'bowler' GROUP BY pmr.player_id, pmr.match_id), TeamBattingAverage AS (SELECT tc.team_id, SUM(mbs.runs_scored) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT tc.player_id), 0) AS batting_average FROM MatchBattingStats AS mbs JOIN team_compositions AS tc ON mbs.player_id = tc.player_id AND mbs.match_id = tc.match_id GROUP BY tc.team_id), TeamBowlingAverage AS (SELECT tc.team_id, AVG(mbs.bowling_average) AS bowling_average FROM MatchBowlingStats AS mbs JOIN team_compositions AS tc ON mbs.player_id = tc.player_id AND mbs.match_id = tc.match_id GROUP BY tc.team_id), CombinedAverage AS (SELECT tba.team_id, tba.batting_average, tbaa.bowling_average, (tba.batting_average + tbaa.bowling_average) AS total_average FROM TeamBattingAverage AS tba JOIN TeamBowlingAverage AS tbaa ON tba.team_id = tbaa.team_id) SELECT MAX(ca.total_average) AS highest_combined_average FROM CombinedAverage AS ca

question: What is the average time it takes for each role to generate a log?
external_knowledge: - 'Average time' refers to the total duration divided by the total number of logs.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH SuccessfulLogs AS ( SELECT user_id, duration FROM data_generation_logs WHERE status = 'success' ), UserLogStats AS ( SELECT u.user_id, ur.role_name, SUM(CAST(REPLACE(duration, ' ', '') AS INTEGER)) AS total_duration, COUNT(*) AS total_logs FROM SuccessfulLogs sl INNER JOIN users u ON sl.user_id = u.user_id INNER JOIN user_roles ur ON u.role_id = ur.role_id GROUP BY u.user_id, ur.role_name ) SELECT role_name, AVG(total_duration / total_logs) AS "Average Duration Per Log by Role" FROM UserLogStats GROUP BY role_name

gold_sql.postgres: WITH SuccessfulLogs AS (SELECT user_id, duration FROM data_generation_logs WHERE status = 'success'), UserLogStats AS (SELECT u.user_id, ur.role_name, SUM(CAST(REPLACE(duration, ' ', '') AS INT)) AS total_duration, COUNT(*) AS total_logs FROM SuccessfulLogs AS sl INNER JOIN users AS u ON sl.user_id = u.user_id INNER JOIN user_roles AS ur ON u.role_id = ur.role_id GROUP BY u.user_id, ur.role_name) SELECT role_name, AVG(total_duration / NULLIF(total_logs, 0)) AS "Average Duration Per Log by Role" FROM UserLogStats GROUP BY role_name

question: Which stores, categorized by their type, had the best sales growth in 2013, and what were their customer satisfaction scores, weather conditions, and promotions on the last day of the year?
external_knowledge:
- The `sales_growth_rate` is a measure of how much sales have increased over the year.
- The `customer_satisfaction_score` reflects how satisfied customers are with the store.
- The `temperature` and `precipitation` data are recorded on the last day of the year (2013-12-31).
- Promotions are listed as a concatenated string of promotion types for each store.
- `PERCENT_RANK()` is used to rank stores based on their sales growth rate, where a rank of 1.0 indicates the best performance.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH PerformanceAndWeather AS ( SELECT sp.store_id, sp.sales_growth_rate, sp.customer_satisfaction_score, w.temperature, w.precipitation, st.store_type_name, GROUP_CONCAT(p.promotion_type, ', ') AS promotions FROM store_performance sp LEFT JOIN weather w ON sp.store_id = w.store_id AND w.date = '2013-12-31' LEFT JOIN store_types st ON sp.store_id = st.store_type_id LEFT JOIN promotions p ON sp.store_id = p.store_id WHERE sp.year = 2013 GROUP BY sp.store_id, sp.sales_growth_rate, sp.customer_satisfaction_score, w.temperature, w.precipitation, st.store_type_name ), RankedPerformance AS ( SELECT *, PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY sales_growth_rate DESC) AS sales_growth_rank FROM PerformanceAndWeather ) SELECT store_id, store_type_name, sales_growth_rate, customer_satisfaction_score, temperature, precipitation, promotions, sales_growth_rank FROM RankedPerformance WHERE sales_growth_rate IS NOT NULL ORDER BY sales_growth_rank

gold_sql.postgres: WITH PerformanceAndWeather AS (SELECT sp.store_id, sp.sales_growth_rate, sp.customer_satisfaction_score, w.temperature, w.precipitation, st.store_type_name, STRING_AGG(p.promotion_type, ', ') AS promotions FROM store_performance AS sp LEFT JOIN weather AS w ON sp.store_id = w.store_id AND w.date = '2013-12-31' LEFT JOIN store_types AS st ON sp.store_id = st.store_type_id LEFT JOIN promotions AS p ON sp.store_id = p.store_id WHERE sp.year = 2013 GROUP BY sp.store_id, sp.sales_growth_rate, sp.customer_satisfaction_score, w.temperature, w.precipitation, st.store_type_name), RankedPerformance AS (SELECT *, PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY sales_growth_rate DESC NULLS LAST) AS sales_growth_rank FROM PerformanceAndWeather) SELECT store_id, store_type_name, sales_growth_rate, customer_satisfaction_score, temperature, precipitation, promotions, sales_growth_rank FROM RankedPerformance WHERE NOT sales_growth_rate IS NULL ORDER BY sales_growth_rank NULLS FIRST

question: Hey! Can you tell me the average sale amount and the average number of interactions per customer for each city and year when sales were made? I'm really interested in seeing how these numbers vary across different cities and years.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT c.city, s.sale_year, AVG(CAST(REPLACE(trim(s.sale_amount, '$'), ',', '') AS REAL)) AS avg_sale_amount, SUM(ci.total_interactions) / COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS avg_interactions_per_customer FROM customers c INNER JOIN sales s ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS total_interactions FROM customer_interactions GROUP BY customer_id) ci ON c.customer_id = ci.customer_id GROUP BY c.city, s.sale_year

question: What are the names and ingredients of the top 5 most effective dishes, excluding the archived ones?

question: Could you please identify the users with the longest session duration and provide their names along with the concatenated list of segments they belong to?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH LongestSessionUsers AS ( SELECT ub.user_id, ub.total_duration FROM user_behavior ub WHERE ub.total_duration = (SELECT MAX(total_duration) FROM user_behavior) ), UserSegments AS ( SELECT ub.user_id, u.user_name, GROUP_CONCAT(s.segment_name) AS segments FROM LongestSessionUsers ub JOIN users u ON ub.user_id = u.user_id LEFT JOIN user_segments us ON ub.user_id = us.user_id LEFT JOIN segments s ON us.segment_id = s.segment_id GROUP BY ub.user_id, u.user_name ) SELECT us.user_name, us.segments FROM UserSegments us

question: Could you please gather a list of all models along with their performance labels and their respective hyperparameters, provided that they have at least one hyperparameter? Please sort the list alphabetically by model name and then by performance label.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ModelPerformance AS ( SELECT m.model_id, m.name AS model_name, mp.cv_score, mp.holdout_roc_auc_score, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY m.model_id ORDER BY mp.cv_score DESC) AS rank_cv, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY m.model_id ORDER BY mp.holdout_roc_auc_score DESC) AS rank_auc FROM models m LEFT JOIN model_performance mp ON m.model_id = mp.model_id ), HyperparameterDetails AS ( SELECT h.model_id, GROUP_CONCAT(h.name || ': ' || h.value, ', ') AS hyperparameters FROM hyperparameters h GROUP BY h.model_id ), CombinedModelInfo AS ( SELECT mp.model_id, mp.model_name, CASE WHEN mp.rank_cv = 1 THEN 'Best CV Score' WHEN mp.rank_auc = 1 THEN 'Best AUC Score' ELSE 'Other' END AS performance_label, hp.hyperparameters FROM ModelPerformance mp LEFT JOIN HyperparameterDetails hp ON mp.model_id = hp.model_id ) SELECT cmi.model_name, cmi.performance_label, cmi.hyperparameters FROM CombinedModelInfo cmi WHERE cmi.hyperparameters IS NOT NULL ORDER BY cmi.model_name, cmi.performance_label

question: Could you please list the top 5 items by total sales amount for each outlet, along with their total sales amounts, and format the results by outlet?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH SalesAmountCTE AS ( SELECT s.outlet_id, s.item_id, SUM(s.sale_amount) AS total_sales_amount FROM sales s GROUP BY s.outlet_id, s.item_id ), RankedSalesCTE AS ( SELECT sa.outlet_id, sa.item_id, sa.total_sales_amount, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY sa.outlet_id ORDER BY sa.total_sales_amount DESC) AS sales_rank FROM SalesAmountCTE sa ) SELECT o.outlet_id, GROUP_CONCAT(i.item_name || ' (' || rs.total_sales_amount || ')', ', ') AS top_items FROM RankedSalesCTE rs JOIN items i ON rs.item_id = i.item_id JOIN outlets o ON rs.outlet_id = o.outlet_id WHERE rs.sales_rank <= 5 GROUP BY o.outlet_id ORDER BY o.outlet_id

question: I want to know the employee IDs, review dates, ratings, comments, goals, average ratings, performance levels, and review years for all employee performance reviews that took place in 2023, ordered by employee ID and most recent review date, with the performance level categorized as 'Excellent', 'Good', or 'Needs Improvement' based on the rating.

question: Could you please gather information about all users who have placed more than one order, and list their names along with the total number of orders they have placed and the average number of days between their orders? I need the results sorted in descending order by the total number of orders and then in ascending order by the average days between orders.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH UserOrderSummary AS ( SELECT u.user_id, u.user_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, AVG(of.days_since_prior_order) AS avg_days_between_orders FROM users u INNER JOIN orders o ON u.user_id = o.user_id INNER JOIN order_frequency of ON u.user_id = of.user_id GROUP BY u.user_id, u.user_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 1 ) SELECT user_name, total_orders, avg_days_between_orders FROM UserOrderSummary ORDER BY total_orders DESC, avg_days_between_orders ASC

question: Could you tell me the top 3 most severe diseases for each crop, given that the crop has no leaf mildewing or chlorosis and has a healthy stem without lodging?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RankedDiseases AS ( SELECT ch.crop_name, d.disease_name, ds.severity_level, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ch.crop_name ORDER BY ds.severity_level DESC) AS severity_rank FROM crop_histories ch JOIN diseases d ON INSTR(ch.previous_diseases, d.disease_name) > 0 JOIN disease_severity ds ON ch.crop_history_id = ds.severity_id WHERE EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM leaf_conditions lc WHERE lc.leaf_mild = 0 AND lc.chlorosis = 0 ) AND EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM stem_conditions sc WHERE sc.stem = 1 AND sc.lodging = 0 ) ) SELECT crop_name, disease_name, severity_level FROM RankedDiseases WHERE severity_rank <= 3

question: I want to know the titles, company names, employment types, experience levels, years of experience required, countries, skills, salary ranges, benefits, posted dates, deadlines, recruiter names, total applications, average years of experience required, applicant names, applicant emails, applicant phone numbers, LinkedIn profiles, portfolio URLs, application statuses, status descriptions, application dates, and last updated dates for all job postings, along with their applicants' information, ordered by job title and applicant name.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH JobDetails AS ( SELECT j.job_id, j.title, c.company_name, e.type_name, l.level_name, j.years_exp, j.country, j.skills, j.salary_range, j.benefits, j.posted_date, j.deadline, r.name AS recruiter_name FROM jobs j INNER JOIN companies c ON j.company_id = c.company_id INNER JOIN employment_types e ON j.type = e.type_id INNER JOIN experience_levels l ON j.level = l.level_id INNER JOIN recruiters r ON j.recruiter_id = r.recruiter_id ), ApplicantDetails AS ( SELECT a.job_id, ap.name AS applicant_name, ap.email AS applicant_email, ap.phone AS applicant_phone, ap.linkedin_profile, ap.portfolio_url, s.status_name, s.description AS status_description, a.application_date, a.last_updated FROM job_applications a INNER JOIN applicants ap ON a.applicant_id = ap.applicant_id INNER JOIN application_status s ON a.status_id = s.status_id ), JobStats AS ( SELECT a.job_id, COUNT(a.application_id) AS total_applications, AVG(CAST(SUBSTR(jd.years_exp, 1, INSTR(jd.years_exp, '-') - 1) AS INTEGER)) AS avg_years_exp_required FROM job_applications a INNER JOIN JobDetails jd ON a.job_id = jd.job_id GROUP BY a.job_id ) SELECT jd.title, jd.company_name, jd.type_name AS employment_type, jd.level_name AS experience_level, jd.years_exp, jd.country, jd.skills, jd.salary_range, jd.benefits, jd.posted_date, jd.deadline, jd.recruiter_name, js.total_applications, js.avg_years_exp_required, ad.applicant_name, ad.applicant_email, ad.applicant_phone, ad.linkedin_profile, ad.portfolio_url, ad.status_name, ad.status_description, ad.application_date, ad.last_updated FROM JobDetails jd LEFT JOIN JobStats js ON jd.job_id = js.job_id LEFT JOIN ApplicantDetails ad ON jd.job_id = ad.job_id ORDER BY jd.title, ad.applicant_name

question: What are the names of the top 5 car models by sales in each region, along with their total units sold, total revenue generated, sales rank, the names of the top dealers selling these models, and the total price of their configurations?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH TopSellingModels AS ( SELECT s.region, m.model_name, SUM(s.quantity) AS total_units_sold, SUM(CAST(REPLACE(s.total_revenue, ',', '') AS REAL)) AS total_revenue_generated, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY s.region ORDER BY SUM(s.quantity) DESC) AS region_sales_rank FROM sales_data s JOIN car_models m ON s.model_id = m.model_id GROUP BY s.region, m.model_name ), TopDealersAndConfigurations AS ( SELECT tsm.region, tsm.model_name, tsm.total_units_sold, tsm.total_revenue_generated, tsm.region_sales_rank, d.dealer_name, COALESCE(SUM(CAST(REPLACE(c.price, ',', '') AS REAL)), 0) AS total_configuration_price FROM TopSellingModels tsm JOIN sales_data s ON tsm.region = s.region AND tsm.model_name = (SELECT m.model_name FROM car_models m WHERE m.model_id = s.model_id) JOIN dealers d ON s.dealer_id = d.dealer_id LEFT JOIN car_configurations c ON c.model_id = s.model_id WHERE tsm.region_sales_rank <= 5 GROUP BY tsm.region, tsm.model_name, tsm.total_units_sold, tsm.total_revenue_generated, tsm.region_sales_rank, d.dealer_name ) SELECT tdac.region, tdac.model_name, SUM(tdac.total_units_sold) AS total_units_sold, SUM(tdac.total_revenue_generated) AS total_revenue_generated, tdac.region_sales_rank, GROUP_CONCAT(tdac.dealer_name) AS top_dealers, SUM(tdac.total_configuration_price) AS total_configuration_price FROM TopDealersAndConfigurations tdac GROUP BY tdac.region, tdac.model_name, tdac.region_sales_rank ORDER BY tdac.region, tdac.region_sales_rank

question: Could you please gather all the information about each machine learning model, including the model names, algorithms used, their latest versions, creation dates of the latest versions, cross-validation scores, holdout scores, holdout ROC AUC scores, training times, evaluation times, their respective hyperparameters, comments, owner IDs, collaborator IDs, and display the results ordered by model ID and version in descending order of version creation date?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH LatestVersions AS ( SELECT mv.model_id, mv.version, mv.created_at, mv.version_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY mv.model_id ORDER BY mv.created_at DESC) AS rn FROM model_versions mv ), HyperparametersAgg AS ( SELECT h.model_id, GROUP_CONCAT(h.name || ': ' || h.value, ', ') AS hyperparameters FROM hyperparameters h GROUP BY h.model_id ), CommentsAgg AS ( SELECT mc.model_id, GROUP_CONCAT(mc.comment, ' | ') AS comments FROM model_comments mc GROUP BY mc.model_id ), OwnersCollaborators AS ( SELECT mo.model_id, MAX(CASE WHEN mo.ownership_type = 'owner' THEN mo.user_id ELSE NULL END) AS owner_id, GROUP_CONCAT(CASE WHEN mo.ownership_type = 'collaborator' THEN CAST(mo.user_id AS TEXT) ELSE NULL END, ', ') AS collaborator_id FROM model_ownership mo GROUP BY mo.model_id ) SELECT m.model_id, m.name, m.algorithm, lv.version, lv.created_at AS latest_version_created_at, vp.cv_score, vp.holdout_score, vp.holdout_roc_auc_score, vp.training_time, vp.evaluation_time, ha.hyperparameters, ca.comments, oc.owner_id, oc.collaborator_id FROM models m LEFT JOIN LatestVersions lv ON m.model_id = lv.model_id AND lv.rn = 1 LEFT JOIN version_performance vp ON lv.version_id = vp.version_id LEFT JOIN HyperparametersAgg ha ON m.model_id = ha.model_id LEFT JOIN CommentsAgg ca ON m.model_id = ca.model_id LEFT JOIN OwnersCollaborators oc ON m.model_id = oc.model_id ORDER BY m.model_id, lv.created_at DESC

question: Could you please gather the titles of the top 5 papers with the most citations that were published in 'Neural Information Processing Systems', along with their authors?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT p.title, GROUP_CONCAT(a.author_name, ', ') AS authors FROM papers p JOIN paper_publications pp ON p.paper_id = pp.paper_id JOIN publications pub ON pub.publication_id = pp.publication_id JOIN paper_authors pa ON p.paper_id = pa.paper_id JOIN authors a ON pa.author_id = a.author_id JOIN citations c ON p.paper_id = c.paper_id WHERE pub.publication_name = 'Neural Information Processing Systems' GROUP BY p.paper_id, p.title ORDER BY COUNT(c.citation_id) DESC LIMIT 5

question:
**User**: I want to get some information about resolutions.
**Assistant**: What kind of information about resolutions are you looking for?
**User**: I need the average size of the documents associated with them, but grouped by the month they were proposed.
**Assistant**: Do you want to consider all resolutions, or are there specific ones you're interested in?
**User**: Only those where both the proposed date and the document size are available.
**Assistant**: How would you like the results to be ordered?
**User**: In chronological order by the proposed month.
**Assistant**: Is there anything else you need to know about the resolutions or their documents?
**User**: No, that's all.
**Assistant**: OK, I will help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT STRFTIME('%Y-%m', r.proposed_date) AS proposed_month, AVG(rd.file_size) AS average_document_size FROM resolutions r JOIN resolution_documents rd ON r.resolution_id = rd.resolution_id WHERE r.proposed_date IS NOT NULL AND rd.file_size IS NOT NULL GROUP BY proposed_month ORDER BY proposed_month
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(CAST(r.proposed_date AS DATETIME), '%Y-%m') AS proposed_month, AVG(rd.file_size) AS average_document_size FROM resolutions AS r JOIN resolution_documents AS rd ON r.resolution_id = rd.resolution_id WHERE NOT r.proposed_date IS NULL AND NOT rd.file_size IS NULL GROUP BY proposed_month ORDER BY proposed_month
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT TO_CHAR(CAST(r.proposed_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY-MM') AS proposed_month, AVG(rd.file_size) AS average_document_size FROM resolutions AS r JOIN resolution_documents AS rd ON r.resolution_id = rd.resolution_id WHERE NOT r.proposed_date IS NULL AND NOT rd.file_size IS NULL GROUP BY proposed_month ORDER BY proposed_month NULLS FIRST

question: What is the comprehensive profile, including medical conditions, lifestyle, health outcomes, and healthcare providers, for patient 0?
external_knowledge: Patient 0's ID is used as a placeholder and should be replaced with the actual ID of the patient of interest; The comprehensive profile includes the patient's demographic information, a list of medical conditions with their average severity, lifestyle factors, health outcomes, and healthcare providers; A patient's ID is typically a unique identifier assigned by the healthcare system.

question: What are the predicted future inventory levels for each task, ordered by sequence and future inventory level, taking into account the current inventory levels, total production, required quantities, and task dependencies?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RECURSIVE WorkflowDependency AS ( SELECT tw.task_id, tw.workflow_id, tw.sequence, tw.dependency_task_id, CAST(tw.task_id AS TEXT) AS dependency_chain FROM task_workflows tw WHERE tw.dependency_task_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT tw.task_id, tw.workflow_id, tw.sequence, tw.dependency_task_id, CAST(wd.dependency_chain || ' -> ' || tw.task_id AS TEXT) AS dependency_chain FROM task_workflows tw INNER JOIN WorkflowDependency wd ON tw.dependency_task_id = wd.task_id ), TaskPerformance AS ( SELECT p.run_id, p.task_id, p.production_quantity, t.priority, t.machine_id, SUM(p.production_quantity) OVER (PARTITION BY p.task_id ORDER BY p.run_id) AS cumulative_production, SUM(p.production_quantity) OVER (PARTITION BY p.machine_id ORDER BY p.run_id) AS machine_cumulative_production FROM production_runs p INNER JOIN tasks t ON p.task_id = t.task_id ), InventoryStatus AS ( SELECT i.part_id, i.inventory_level, i.reorder_point, (SELECT SUM(tp.production_quantity) FROM production_runs tp WHERE tp.task_id IN (SELECT tp2.task_id FROM task_parts tp2 WHERE tp2.part_id = i.part_id)) AS total_production, (CASE WHEN i.inventory_level < i.reorder_point THEN 'LOW' ELSE 'OK' END) AS inventory_status FROM inventories i ), TaskAndPartAnalysis AS ( SELECT tp.task_id, tp.part_id, tp.production_rate, tp.required_quantity, ws.dependency_chain, ws.sequence, ts.inventory_status, ts.total_production, ts.inventory_level FROM task_parts tp INNER JOIN WorkflowDependency ws ON tp.task_id = ws.task_id INNER JOIN InventoryStatus ts ON tp.part_id = ts.part_id ), FutureInventoryAnalysis AS ( SELECT tap.task_id, tap.part_id, tap.production_rate, tap.required_quantity, tap.dependency_chain, tap.sequence, tap.inventory_status, tap.inventory_level + tap.total_production - (tap.required_quantity * tap.sequence) AS future_inventory_level FROM TaskAndPartAnalysis tap ) SELECT fa.task_id, fa.future_inventory_level FROM FutureInventoryAnalysis fa ORDER BY fa.sequence, fa.future_inventory_level

question: Find the usernames of active users whose average non-archived generated dataset size exceeds 1024 bytes and return their corresponding average dataset sizes in bytes.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT u.username, AVG(CAST(SUBSTR(gd.size_in_bytes, 1, LENGTH(gd.size_in_bytes) - 2) AS INTEGER)) AS average_size_bytes FROM users u INNER JOIN generated_datasets gd ON u.user_id = gd.user_id WHERE u.is_active = 1 AND gd.is_archived = 0 GROUP BY u.username HAVING AVG(CAST(SUBSTR(gd.size_in_bytes, 1, LENGTH(gd.size_in_bytes) - 2) AS INTEGER)) > 1024

gold_sql.postgres: SELECT u.username, AVG(CAST(SUBSTRING(gd.size_in_bytes FROM 1 FOR LENGTH(gd.size_in_bytes) - 2) AS INT)) AS average_size_bytes FROM users AS u INNER JOIN generated_datasets AS gd ON u.user_id = gd.user_id WHERE u.is_active = 1 AND gd.is_archived = 0 GROUP BY u.username HAVING AVG(CAST(SUBSTRING(gd.size_in_bytes FROM 1 FOR LENGTH(gd.size_in_bytes) - 2) AS INT)) > 1024

question: I want to know the names of the top 3 teams in each division for every season, along with their respective division names, winning percentages, division ranks, and the total number of times each team has been ranked among the top 3 in its division across all seasons.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH TeamPerformanceCTE AS ( SELECT s.team_id, s.season_id, s.rank, s.pct, t.team_name, d.division_name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.season_id, d.division_id ORDER BY s.pct DESC, s.rank ASC) AS performance_rank FROM standings s INNER JOIN teams t ON s.team_id = t.team_id INNER JOIN divisions d ON t.division_id = d.division_id ), TopPerformanceCTE AS ( SELECT team_id, season_id, rank, pct, team_name, division_name, performance_rank FROM TeamPerformanceCTE WHERE performance_rank <= 3 ) SELECT tp.team_name AS top_team_name, tp.division_name, tp.pct AS win_percentage, tp.rank AS division_rank, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY tp.team_id) AS times_in_top_three FROM TopPerformanceCTE tp ORDER BY tp.team_id, tp.season_id

question: Hey, could you help me find the average success rate of data generation configurations for each connector, relative to the best performing configurations for each connector? I'd love to know how they rank.

question: Could you tell me the names of the top 5 bowlers whose match bowling averages were better than their overall bowling averages, along with their match bowling averages, overall bowling averages, and the differences between the two, ordered by the largest improvements?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH PlayerAverage AS ( SELECT ps.player_id, ps.bowling_average AS overall_bowling_average FROM player_statistics ps ), MatchPerformance AS ( SELECT pmr.player_id, pmr.match_id, pmr.bowling_wickets, pmr.bowling_runs, (pmr.bowling_runs * 1.0 / pmr.bowling_wickets) AS match_bowling_average FROM player_match_records pmr WHERE pmr.role_in_match = 'bowler' ) SELECT p.player_name, ma.match_bowling_average, pa.overall_bowling_average, ma.match_bowling_average - pa.overall_bowling_average AS difference FROM MatchPerformance ma JOIN players p ON ma.player_id = p.player_id JOIN PlayerAverage pa ON ma.player_id = pa.player_id WHERE ma.match_bowling_average > pa.overall_bowling_average ORDER BY difference DESC LIMIT 5

question: What are the names and average times of the top 5 swimmers from each nationality who participated in Olympic events, ranked by their average time and NISCA score?

question: Return the connector, rows per second, number of rows, total number of datasets, total size in megabytes, maximum quality score, and the creator's username for all data generation configurations that have produced datasets with a maximum quality score greater than 0.9, along with the status of the latest generation log for each configuration, ordered by the total dataset size in descending order.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ConfigSummary AS ( SELECT dgc.config_id, dgc.connector, dgc.rows_per_second, dgc.number_of_rows, dgc.created_by, COUNT(gd.dataset_id) AS total_datasets, SUM(CAST(gd.size_in_bytes AS INTEGER)) / 1048576 AS total_size_mb, MAX(CAST(gd.quality_score AS REAL)) AS max_quality_score, u.username AS created_by_username FROM data_generation_configs dgc JOIN generated_datasets gd ON dgc.config_id = gd.config_id JOIN users u ON dgc.created_by = u.user_id GROUP BY dgc.config_id, dgc.connector, dgc.rows_per_second, dgc.number_of_rows, dgc.created_by, u.username HAVING MAX(CAST(gd.quality_score AS REAL)) > 0.9 ), LatestLog AS ( SELECT config_id, MAX(timestamp) AS latest_log_timestamp FROM data_generation_logs GROUP BY config_id ) SELECT cs.connector, cs.rows_per_second, cs.number_of_rows, cs.total_datasets, cs.total_size_mb, cs.max_quality_score, cs.created_by_username, dl.status AS latest_generation_status FROM ConfigSummary cs LEFT JOIN data_generation_logs dl ON cs.config_id = dl.config_id AND dl.timestamp = ( SELECT latest_log_timestamp FROM LatestLog ll WHERE ll.config_id = cs.config_id ) ORDER BY cs.total_size_mb DESC

question: Hey, I need a detailed report of all the road types, including their lanes, speed limits, priority levels, allowed vehicle classes, total traffic signals, operational traffic signals, total road conditions, closed road conditions, average repair times, emergency maintenance counts, total maintenance counts, total costs, and average costs. Additionally, I'd like to see the cumulative cost for each road type. Could you provide this information in order from road type name?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ActiveSignals AS ( SELECT rt.road_type_id, COUNT(ts.signal_id) AS signal_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ts.signal_status = 'operational' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS operational_signals FROM traffic_signals ts JOIN road_types rt ON ts.road_type_id = rt.road_type_id GROUP BY rt.road_type_id ), RoadConditionsSummary AS ( SELECT rc.road_type_id, COUNT(rc.condition_id) AS condition_count, COUNT(CASE WHEN rc.condition_status = 'closed' THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) AS closed_count, AVG(CASE WHEN rc.condition_status = 'closed' THEN CAST(SUBSTR(rc.estimated_repair_time, 1, INSTR(rc.estimated_repair_time, ' ') - 1) AS REAL) ELSE NULL END) AS avg_repair_time FROM road_conditions rc GROUP BY rc.road_type_id ), MaintenanceSummary AS ( SELECT rm.road_type_id, COUNT(rm.maintenance_id) AS maintenance_count, SUM(rm.cost) AS total_cost, AVG(rm.cost) AS avg_cost, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN rm.maintenance_type = 'emergency' THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) AS emergency_maint_count FROM road_maintenance rm GROUP BY rm.road_type_id ), RoadStats AS ( SELECT rt.road_type_id, rt.type_name, rt.lanes, rt.speed, rt.priority, rt.allowed_vehicle_classes, COALESCE(ac.signal_count, 0) AS signal_count, COALESCE(ac.operational_signals, 0) AS operational_signals, COALESCE(rcs.condition_count, 0) AS condition_count, COALESCE(rcs.closed_count, 0) AS closed_count, COALESCE(rcs.avg_repair_time, 0) AS avg_repair_time, COALESCE(ms.emergency_maint_count, 0) AS emergency_maint_count, COALESCE(ms.maintenance_count, 0) AS maintenance_count, COALESCE(ms.total_cost, 0) AS total_cost, COALESCE(ms.avg_cost, 0) AS avg_cost FROM road_types rt LEFT JOIN ActiveSignals ac ON rt.road_type_id = ac.road_type_id LEFT JOIN RoadConditionsSummary rcs ON rt.road_type_id = rcs.road_type_id LEFT JOIN MaintenanceSummary ms ON rt.road_type_id = ms.road_type_id ) SELECT rs.type_name, rs.lanes, rs.speed, rs.priority, rs.allowed_vehicle_classes, rs.signal_count, rs.operational_signals, rs.condition_count, rs.closed_count, rs.avg_repair_time, rs.emergency_maint_count, rs.maintenance_count, rs.total_cost, rs.avg_cost, SUM(rs.total_cost) OVER (ORDER BY rs.type_name ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_cost FROM RoadStats rs ORDER BY rs.type_name

1) AS FLOAT) ELSE NULL END) AS avg_repair_time FROM road_conditions AS rc GROUP BY rc.road_type_id), MaintenanceSummary AS (SELECT rm.road_type_id, COUNT(rm.maintenance_id) AS maintenance_count, SUM(rm.cost) AS total_cost, AVG(rm.cost) AS avg_cost, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN rm.maintenance_type = 'emergency' THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) AS emergency_maint_count FROM road_maintenance AS rm GROUP BY rm.road_type_id), RoadStats AS (SELECT rt.road_type_id, rt.type_name, rt.lanes, rt.speed, rt.priority, rt.allowed_vehicle_classes, COALESCE(ac.signal_count, 0) AS signal_count, COALESCE(ac.operational_signals, 0) AS operational_signals, COALESCE(rcs.condition_count, 0) AS condition_count, COALESCE(rcs.closed_count, 0) AS closed_count, COALESCE(rcs.avg_repair_time, 0) AS avg_repair_time, COALESCE(ms.emergency_maint_count, 0) AS emergency_maint_count, COALESCE(ms.maintenance_count, 0) AS maintenance_count, COALESCE(ms.total_cost, 0) AS total_cost, COALESCE(ms.avg_cost, 0) AS avg_cost FROM road_types AS rt LEFT JOIN ActiveSignals AS ac ON rt.road_type_id = ac.road_type_id LEFT JOIN RoadConditionsSummary AS rcs ON rt.road_type_id = rcs.road_type_id LEFT JOIN MaintenanceSummary AS ms ON rt.road_type_id = ms.road_type_id) SELECT rs.type_name, rs.lanes, rs.speed, rs.priority, rs.allowed_vehicle_classes, rs.signal_count, rs.operational_signals, rs.condition_count, rs.closed_count, rs.avg_repair_time, rs.emergency_maint_count, rs.maintenance_count, rs.total_cost, rs.avg_cost, SUM(rs.total_cost) OVER (ORDER BY rs.type_name ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_cost FROM RoadStats AS rs ORDER BY rs.type_name

question: Could you please gather a summary of the best decision tree for each researcher, including their name, the tree name, and its accuracy, where 'best' means the highest accuracy achieved by a researcher's decision tree?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH BestDecisionTrees AS ( SELECT r.name AS researcher_name, t.tree_name, t.accuracy, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY r.researcher_id ORDER BY t.accuracy DESC) AS tree_rank FROM researchers r JOIN studies s ON r.researcher_id = s.researcher_id JOIN feature_values fv ON s.study_id = fv.tree_id JOIN decision_trees t ON fv.tree_id = t.tree_id ) SELECT researcher_name || ' - ' || tree_name || ' - Accuracy: ' || CAST(accuracy AS TEXT) AS best_tree_summary FROM BestDecisionTrees WHERE tree_rank = 1

question: Competitors in 2015 stacking events, return their names and performance ranks, ordered by difficulty level and rank of top 5 performances in each competition.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH PerformanceCTE AS ( SELECT p.competitor_id, c.event_name, st.difficulty_level, p.rank, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.competition_id ORDER BY p.rank ASC) AS performance_rank FROM performances p JOIN competitions c ON p.competition_id = c.competition_id JOIN stack_types st ON p.stack_type_id = st.stack_type_id WHERE strftime('%Y', c.event_date) = '2015' ), FilteredPerformances AS ( SELECT p.competitor_id, p.event_name, p.difficulty_level, p.rank FROM PerformanceCTE p WHERE p.performance_rank <= 5 ) SELECT comp.name AS competitor_name, f.rank AS performance_rank FROM FilteredPerformances f JOIN competitors comp ON f.competitor_id = comp.competitor_id ORDER BY f.difficulty_level ASC, f.rank ASC

question: What are the users with their corresponding average success rates of creating data generation configurations, sorted from highest to lowest success rate?
external_knowledge: Success rate is calculated as the number of successful logs divided by the total number of logs; A higher success rate indicates better performance.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ConfigUsage AS ( SELECT dgc.config_id, dgc.created_by AS user_id, COUNT(dgl.log_id) AS total_logs, COUNT(CASE WHEN dgl.status = 'success' THEN 1 END) AS successful_logs FROM data_generation_configs dgc LEFT JOIN data_generation_logs dgl ON dgc.config_id = dgl.config_id GROUP BY dgc.config_id, dgc.created_by ), UserSuccessRates AS ( SELECT cu.user_id, AVG(CAST(cu.successful_logs AS REAL) / cu.total_logs) AS avg_success_rate FROM ConfigUsage cu GROUP BY cu.user_id ) SELECT us.user_id, us.avg_success_rate FROM UserSuccessRates us ORDER BY us.avg_success_rate DESC

question:
**User**: I want to create a comprehensive report on business performance.
**Assistant**: What type of businesses are you interested in? Are you looking for specific categories?
**User**: All categories, including their subcategories.
**Assistant**: What information do you need for each business in the report?
**User**: Name, city, category, revenue, visits, transaction details, and review information.
**Assistant**: For transaction details, do you need the number of transactions and total transaction amount? And for reviews, do you need the total count and average rating?
**User**: Yes, exactly. Also, include the average rating of the business itself.
**Assistant**: How would you like the report to be sorted?
**User**: Prioritize businesses by their revenue, then by their average rating, and finally by the number of visits.
**Assistant**: Is there any specific format you'd like for the category information in the report?
**User**: Please include the full category path, showing parent and child categories.
**Assistant**: Alright, I'll help you generate the report. Would you like to include all businesses or filter them in some way?
**User**: No filters, just all businesses.
**Assistant**: OK, I will help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RECURSIVE CategoryHierarchy AS ( SELECT category_id, category_name, parent_category_id, category_name AS full_path FROM categories WHERE parent_category_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT c.category_id, c.category_name, c.parent_category_id, ch.full_path || ' > ' || c.category_name AS full_path FROM categories c JOIN CategoryHierarchy ch ON c.parent_category_id = ch.category_id ), BusinessPerformance AS ( SELECT b.business_id, b.name, b.city, ch.full_path AS category_path, COALESCE(a.visits, 0) AS visits, COALESCE(a.ratings_count, 0) AS ratings_count, COALESCE(a.average_rating, 0) AS average_rating, COALESCE(a.revenue, 0) AS revenue FROM businesses b LEFT JOIN analytics a ON b.business_id = a.business_id LEFT JOIN business_categories bc ON b.business_id = bc.business_id LEFT JOIN CategoryHierarchy ch ON bc.category_id = ch.category_id ), TransactionSummary AS ( SELECT business_id, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count, SUM(amount) AS total_transaction_amount FROM transactions GROUP BY business_id ), ReviewSummary AS ( SELECT business_id, COUNT(*) AS review_count, AVG(rating) AS review_average_rating FROM reviews GROUP BY business_id ) SELECT bp.name, bp.city, bp.category_path, bp.revenue, bp.visits, ts.transaction_count, ts.total_transaction_amount, rs.review_count, bp.average_rating, rs.review_average_rating FROM BusinessPerformance bp LEFT JOIN TransactionSummary ts ON bp.business_id = ts.business_id LEFT JOIN ReviewSummary rs ON bp.business_id = rs.business_id ORDER BY bp.revenue DESC, bp.average_rating DESC, bp.visits DESC
gold_sql.mysql: WITH RECURSIVE CategoryHierarchy AS (SELECT category_id, category_name, parent_category_id, category_name AS full_path FROM categories WHERE parent_category_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT c.category_id, c.category_name, c.parent_category_id, CONCAT(ch.full_path, ' > ', c.category_name) AS full_path FROM categories AS c JOIN CategoryHierarchy AS ch ON c.parent_category_id = ch.category_id), BusinessPerformance AS (SELECT b.business_id, b.name, b.city, ch.full_path AS category_path, COALESCE(a.visits, 0) AS visits, COALESCE(a.ratings_count, 0) AS ratings_count, COALESCE(a.average_rating, 0) AS average_rating, COALESCE(a.revenue, 0) AS revenue FROM businesses AS b LEFT JOIN analytics AS a ON b.business_id = a.business_id LEFT JOIN business_categories AS bc ON b.business_id = bc.business_id LEFT JOIN CategoryHierarchy AS ch ON bc.category_id = ch.category_id), TransactionSummary AS (SELECT business_id, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count, SUM(amount) AS total_transaction_amount FROM transactions GROUP BY business_id), ReviewSummary AS (SELECT business_id, COUNT(*) AS review_count, AVG(rating) AS review_average_rating FROM reviews GROUP BY business_id) SELECT bp.name, bp.city, bp.category_path, bp.revenue, bp.visits, ts.transaction_count, ts.total_transaction_amount, rs.review_count, bp.average_rating, rs.review_average_rating FROM BusinessPerformance AS bp LEFT JOIN TransactionSummary AS ts ON bp.business_id = ts.business_id LEFT JOIN ReviewSummary AS rs ON bp.business_id = rs.business_id ORDER BY bp.revenue DESC, bp.average_rating DESC, bp.visits DESC

question: What are the survey names, participant counts, completed counts, completion rates, feedback counts, feedback rates, average satisfaction, average usefulness, average effectiveness, average visual attractiveness, average intention, total responses, and response rates for each survey, ordered by the completion rate in descending order?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH SurveyEngagement AS ( SELECT s.survey_id, s.survey_name, COUNT(sp.user_id) AS participant_count, SUM(CASE WHEN sp.participation_status = 'completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS completed_count, COUNT(f.feedback_id) AS feedback_count FROM surveys s LEFT JOIN survey_participants sp ON s.survey_id = sp.survey_id LEFT JOIN feedback f ON s.survey_id = f.survey_id GROUP BY s.survey_id, s.survey_name ), SurveyAnalytics AS ( SELECT a.survey_id, a.average_satisfaction, a.average_usefulness, a.average_effectiveness, a.average_visual_attractiveness, a.average_intention, a.total_responses, a.response_rate FROM analytics a ) SELECT se.survey_name, se.participant_count, se.completed_count, (se.completed_count / CAST(se.participant_count AS REAL) * 100) AS completion_rate, se.feedback_count, (se.feedback_count / CAST(se.participant_count AS REAL) * 100) AS feedback_rate, sa.average_satisfaction, sa.average_usefulness, sa.average_effectiveness, sa.average_visual_attractiveness, sa.average_intention, sa.total_responses, sa.response_rate FROM SurveyEngagement se LEFT JOIN SurveyAnalytics sa ON se.survey_id = sa.survey_id ORDER BY completion_rate DESC
gold_sql.mysql: WITH SurveyEngagement AS (SELECT s.survey_id, s.survey_name, COUNT(sp.user_id) AS participant_count, SUM(CASE WHEN sp.participation_status = 'completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS completed_count, COUNT(f.feedback_id) AS feedback_count FROM surveys AS s LEFT JOIN survey_participants AS sp ON s.survey_id = sp.survey_id LEFT JOIN feedback AS f ON s.survey_id = f.survey_id GROUP BY s.survey_id, s.survey_name), SurveyAnalytics AS (SELECT a.survey_id, a.average_satisfaction, a.average_usefulness, a.average_effectiveness, a.average_visual_attractiveness, a.average_intention, a.total_responses, a.response_rate FROM analytics AS a) SELECT se.survey_name, se.participant_count, se.completed_count, (se.completed_count / CAST(se.participant_count AS FLOAT) * 100) AS completion_rate, se.feedback_count, (se.feedback_count / CAST(se.participant_count AS FLOAT) * 100) AS feedback_rate, sa.average_satisfaction, sa.average_usefulness, sa.average_effectiveness, sa.average_visual_attractiveness, sa.average_intention, sa.total_responses, sa.response_rate FROM SurveyEngagement AS se LEFT JOIN SurveyAnalytics AS sa ON se.survey_id = sa.survey_id ORDER BY completion_rate DESC
gold_sql.postgres: WITH SurveyEngagement AS (SELECT s.survey_id, s.survey_name, COUNT(sp.user_id) AS participant_count, SUM(CASE WHEN sp.participation_status = 'completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS completed_count, COUNT(f.feedback_id) AS feedback_count FROM surveys AS s LEFT JOIN survey_participants AS sp ON s.survey_id = sp.survey_id LEFT JOIN feedback AS f ON s.survey_id = f.survey_id GROUP BY s.survey_id, s.survey_name), SurveyAnalytics AS (SELECT a.survey_id, a.average_satisfaction, a.average_usefulness, a.average_effectiveness, a.average_visual_attractiveness, a.average_intention, a.total_responses, a.response_rate FROM analytics AS a) SELECT se.survey_name, se.participant_count, se.completed_count, (se.completed_count / NULLIF(CAST(se.participant_count AS REAL), 0) * 100) AS completion_rate, se.feedback_count, (se.feedback_count / NULLIF(CAST(se.participant_count AS REAL), 0) * 100) AS feedback_rate, sa.average_satisfaction, sa.average_usefulness, sa.average_effectiveness, sa.average_visual_attractiveness, sa.average_intention, sa.total_responses, sa.response_rate FROM SurveyEngagement AS se LEFT JOIN SurveyAnalytics AS sa ON se.survey_id = sa.survey_id ORDER BY completion_rate DESC NULLS LAST

question:
**User**: I want to get some information about resolutions.
**Assistant**: Which information would you like to know about the resolutions?
**User**: I want to know the resolution text, current status, and some information about the votes.
**Assistant**: What kind of information about the votes are you looking for?
**User**: The total number of votes and the latest voting end date.
**Assistant**: Is there anything else you'd like to know about the resolutions?
**User**: Yes, I'd also like to know the top stakeholders associated with each resolution.
**Assistant**: How many top stakeholders would you like to know?
**User**: Just the top three.
**Assistant**: Is there a specific order you'd like to see the stakeholders in?
**User**: Yes, based on their stakeholder ID.
**Assistant**: I'll provide the information about the resolutions, including the top three stakeholders ranked by stakeholder ID. Is that correct?
**User**: Yes, that's correct.
**Assistant**: I'll help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ResolutionVoteSummary AS ( SELECT r.resolution_id, r.resolution_text, rs.status_name AS current_status, COUNT(rv.vote_id) AS vote_count, MAX(vs.voting_end_date) AS latest_voting_end_date FROM resolutions r JOIN resolution_status rs ON r.resolution_status_id = rs.status_id LEFT JOIN resolution_votes rv ON r.resolution_id = rv.resolution_id LEFT JOIN voting_sessions vs ON r.resolution_id = vs.resolution_id GROUP BY r.resolution_id, r.resolution_text, rs.status_name ), TopStakeholders AS ( SELECT rs.resolution_id, rs.stakeholder_name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY rs.resolution_id ORDER BY rs.stakeholder_id) AS stakeholder_rank FROM resolution_stakeholders rs ) SELECT rvs.resolution_id, rvs.resolution_text, rvs.current_status, rvs.vote_count, rvs.latest_voting_end_date, GROUP_CONCAT(CASE WHEN ts.stakeholder_rank <= 3 THEN ts.stakeholder_name ELSE NULL END, ', ') AS top_three_stakeholders FROM ResolutionVoteSummary rvs JOIN TopStakeholders ts ON rvs.resolution_id = ts.resolution_id GROUP BY rvs.resolution_id, rvs.resolution_text, rvs.current_status, rvs.vote_count, rvs.latest_voting_end_date

question: Could you provide a list of the songs that entered chart 1, including the song title, artist name, peak position, and the cumulative duration of all songs that entered on the same date up to and including each song, ordered by the entry date and entry position?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH BillboardEntries AS ( SELECT ce.entry_date, ce.entry_position, ce.peak_position, s.title, s.duration, a.name AS artist_name FROM chart_entries ce JOIN songs s ON ce.song_id = s.song_id JOIN artists a ON s.artist_id = a.artist_id WHERE ce.chart_id = 1 ), CumulativeDuration AS ( SELECT title, artist_name, peak_position, entry_date, entry_position, SUM(CAST(REPLACE(duration, ':', '') AS INTEGER)) OVER ( PARTITION BY entry_date ORDER BY entry_position ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS cumulative_duration FROM BillboardEntries ) SELECT title, artist_name, peak_position, cumulative_duration FROM CumulativeDuration ORDER BY entry_date, entry_position

question: Could you please gather the most recent unresolved flags and comments, along with their corresponding metadata, for each weather data entry and summarize the results by weather ID? I need to know the flag types, descriptions, and priorities, as well as the comment texts, approval statuses, and like counts, all grouped by weather ID.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH FlaggedData AS ( SELECT wdf.weather_id, wdf.flag_id, wdf.flag_type, wdf.flag_date, wdf.flag_description, wdf.priority, wdf.resolution_date, wdf.resolved_by, wdc.comment_id, wdc.comment_date, wdc.comment_text, wdc.is_approved, wdc.like_count, wdm.metadata_id, wdm.metadata_key, wdm.metadata_value, wdm.metadata_type, wdm.created_date, wdm.modified_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY wdf.weather_id ORDER BY wdf.flag_date DESC) AS flag_row_num, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY wdf.weather_id ORDER BY wdc.comment_date DESC) AS comment_row_num FROM weather_data_flags wdf LEFT JOIN weather_data_comments wdc ON wdf.weather_id = wdc.weather_id LEFT JOIN weather_data_metadata wdm ON wdf.weather_id = wdm.weather_id WHERE wdf.resolution_date IS NULL ), RecentFlagsComments AS ( SELECT weather_id, flag_id, flag_type, flag_date, flag_description, priority, resolution_date, resolved_by, comment_id, comment_date, comment_text, is_approved, like_count, metadata_id, metadata_key, metadata_value, metadata_type, created_date, modified_date FROM FlaggedData WHERE flag_row_num = 1 AND comment_row_num = 1 ) SELECT weather_id, GROUP_CONCAT(flag_type || ': ' || flag_description || ' (Priority: ' || priority || ')', ', ') AS recent_flag_details, GROUP_CONCAT(comment_text || ' (Approved: ' || is_approved || ', Likes: ' || like_count || ')', ', ') AS recent_comment_details FROM RecentFlagsComments GROUP BY weather_id

question: Find the match and player information for the champion of each match, where the champion is the player with the highest batting score and most bowling wickets.
external_knowledge: The term "champion" refers to the top-performing player in each match; A player's performance is determined by their batting score and bowling wickets; The player with the highest batting score and most bowling wickets is considered the best performer.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH PlayerPerformance AS ( SELECT pmr.match_id, pmr.player_id, pmr.batting_score, pmr.bowling_wickets, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY pmr.match_id ORDER BY CAST(pmr.batting_score AS INTEGER) DESC, pmr.bowling_wickets DESC) AS performance_rank FROM player_match_records pmr ) SELECT pp.match_id, pp.player_id FROM PlayerPerformance pp WHERE pp.performance_rank = 1

question: I want to know the concatenated details of the market data for the entry with `market_id = 1`, including the closing price, daily historical volatility, intra-day historical volatility, market indicator name and value, and the name of the data visualization, all formatted into a single string.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT GROUP_CONCAT( md.close || ' | ' || md.daily_hv || ' | ' || md.intra_hv || ' | ' || mi.indicator_name || ' - ' || mi.indicator_value || ' | ' || dv.visualization_name ) AS market_details FROM market_data md JOIN market_indicators mi ON md.market_id = mi.market_id JOIN data_visualizations dv ON md.market_id = dv.market_id WHERE md.market_id = 1
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(md.close, ' | ', md.daily_hv, ' | ', md.intra_hv, ' | ', mi.indicator_name, ' - ', mi.indicator_value, ' | ', dv.visualization_name) SEPARATOR ',') AS market_details FROM market_data AS md JOIN market_indicators AS mi ON md.market_id = mi.market_id JOIN data_visualizations AS dv ON md.market_id = dv.market_id WHERE md.market_id = 1

question:
**User**: I need to access a comprehensive patient profile.
**Assistant**: What specific details about the patients are you looking for?
**User**: I want to know their medical history, family history, cholesterol levels, blood pressure, and the results of their cardiovascular tests.
**Assistant**: That's a good starting point. What about their risk assessment and any recommendations provided?
**User**: Yes, please include the risk level, recommendations, assessment method, and any interventions suggested.
**Assistant**: How about lifestyle factors such as smoking status, diet quality, physical activity level, and dietary preferences?
**User**: Those are important, so yes, please include them.
**Assistant**: What about medications and appointment history?
**User**: Yes, that would be helpful. Can you also aggregate the medication names and list out all their appointments?
**Assistant**: I understand you'd like a comprehensive view. Is there a specific order you'd like the results in?
**User**: Just order them by patient ID.
**Assistant**: Alright, I'll compile all this information for you. Would you like anything else?
**User**: No, that's all.
**Assistant**: I'll put together the SQL query for you.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH PatientRiskAssessment AS ( SELECT p.patient_id, p.age, p.sex, p.cholesterol, p.blood_pressure, p.medical_history, p.family_history, ra.risk_level, ra.recommendations, ra.assessment_method, ra.recommended_interventions, AVG(cv.result) AS avg_test_result FROM patients p LEFT JOIN risk_assessments ra ON p.patient_id = ra.patient_id LEFT JOIN cardiovascular_tests cv ON p.patient_id = cv.patient_id GROUP BY p.patient_id, p.age, p.sex, p.cholesterol, p.blood_pressure, p.medical_history, p.family_history, ra.risk_level, ra.recommendations, ra.assessment_method, ra.recommended_interventions ), PatientMedications AS ( SELECT patient_id, GROUP_CONCAT(medication_name, ', ') AS medications FROM medications GROUP BY patient_id ), PatientLifestyle AS ( SELECT patient_id, smoking_status, exercise_frequency, diet_quality, physical_activity_level, dietary_preferences FROM lifestyle_factors ), PatientAppointments AS ( SELECT patient_id, GROUP_CONCAT(date || ' - ' || appointment_type, ', ') AS appointments FROM appointments GROUP BY patient_id ) SELECT pra.patient_id, pra.age, pra.sex, pra.cholesterol, pra.blood_pressure, pra.medical_history, pra.family_history, pra.risk_level, pra.recommendations, pra.assessment_method, pra.recommended_interventions, pra.avg_test_result, pm.medications, pl.smoking_status, pl.exercise_frequency, pl.diet_quality, pl.physical_activity_level, pl.dietary_preferences, pa.appointments FROM PatientRiskAssessment pra LEFT JOIN PatientMedications pm ON pra.patient_id = pm.patient_id LEFT JOIN PatientLifestyle pl ON pra.patient_id = pl.patient_id LEFT JOIN PatientAppointments pa ON pra.patient_id = pa.patient_id ORDER BY pra.patient_id
gold_sql.mysql: WITH PatientRiskAssessment AS (SELECT p.patient_id, p.age, p.sex, p.cholesterol, p.blood_pressure, p.medical_history, p.family_history, ra.risk_level, ra.recommendations, ra.assessment_method, ra.recommended_interventions, AVG(cv.result) AS avg_test_result FROM patients AS p LEFT JOIN risk_assessments AS ra ON p.patient_id = ra.patient_id LEFT JOIN cardiovascular_tests AS cv ON p.patient_id = cv.patient_id GROUP BY p.patient_id, p.age, p.sex, p.cholesterol, p.blood_pressure, p.medical_history, p.family_history, ra.risk_level, ra.recommendations, ra.assessment_method, ra.recommended_interventions), PatientMedications AS (SELECT patient_id, GROUP_CONCAT(medication_name SEPARATOR ', ') AS medications FROM medications GROUP BY patient_id), PatientLifestyle AS (SELECT patient_id, smoking_status, exercise_frequency, diet_quality, physical_activity_level, dietary_preferences FROM lifestyle_factors), PatientAppointments AS (SELECT patient_id, GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(date, ' - ', appointment_type) SEPARATOR ', ') AS appointments FROM appointments GROUP BY patient_id) SELECT pra.patient_id, pra.age, pra.sex, pra.cholesterol, pra.blood_pressure, pra.medical_history, pra.family_history, pra.risk_level, pra.recommendations, pra.assessment_method, pra.recommended_interventions, pra.avg_test_result, pm.medications, pl.smoking_status, pl.exercise_frequency, pl.diet_quality, pl.physical_activity_level, pl.dietary_preferences, pa.appointments FROM PatientRiskAssessment AS pra LEFT JOIN PatientMedications AS pm ON pra.patient_id = pm.patient_id LEFT JOIN PatientLifestyle AS pl ON pra.patient_id = pl.patient_id LEFT JOIN PatientAppointments AS pa ON pra.patient_id = pa.patient_id ORDER BY pra.patient_id
