question: Find the names of components that use the AXI4-Stream interface and have at least one active revision, along with the average version of those revisions.
external_knowledge: AXI4-Stream is a type of interface used in digital design; A component is considered active if its status is set to 'active'; Revision version refers to the version number of a design revision.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT dc.component_name, AVG(CAST(SUBSTR(dr.version, INSTR(dr.version, '.') + 1) AS REAL)) AS avg_revision_version FROM design_components dc INNER JOIN design_configurations dcg ON dc.component_id = dcg.component_id INNER JOIN design_interfaces di ON dcg.interface_id = di.interface_id INNER JOIN design_revisions dr ON dc.component_id = dr.component_id WHERE di.interface_type = 'AXI4-Stream' AND dr.status = 'active' GROUP BY dc.component_name HAVING COUNT(dr.revision_id) > 0
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT dc.component_name, AVG(CAST(SUBSTRING(dr.version, LOCATE('.', dr.version) + 1) AS FLOAT)) AS avg_revision_version FROM design_components AS dc INNER JOIN design_configurations AS dcg ON dc.component_id = dcg.component_id INNER JOIN design_interfaces AS di ON dcg.interface_id = di.interface_id INNER JOIN design_revisions AS dr ON dc.component_id = dr.component_id WHERE di.interface_type = 'AXI4-Stream' AND dr.status = 'active' GROUP BY dc.component_name HAVING COUNT(dr.revision_id) > 0
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT dc.component_name, AVG(CAST(SUBSTRING(dr.version FROM STRPOS(dr.version, '.') + 1) AS REAL)) AS avg_revision_version FROM design_components AS dc INNER JOIN design_configurations AS dcg ON dc.component_id = dcg.component_id INNER JOIN design_interfaces AS di ON dcg.interface_id = di.interface_id INNER JOIN design_revisions AS dr ON dc.component_id = dr.component_id WHERE di.interface_type = 'AXI4-Stream' AND dr.status = 'active' GROUP BY dc.component_name HAVING COUNT(dr.revision_id) > 0

question: Could you please gather the names of the top 5 most effective dishes, along with their average effectiveness ratings, the ingredients used in each dish, and the names of the users who have access to these dishes? I need this information for the non-archived dishes, and the results should be sorted in order of the average effectiveness rating from highest to lowest.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH TopDishes AS ( SELECT d.dish_id, d.dish_name, de.average_effectiveness_rating FROM dishes d INNER JOIN dish_effectiveness de ON d.dish_id = de.dish_id WHERE d.is_archived = 0 AND de.is_archived = 0 ORDER BY de.average_effectiveness_rating DESC LIMIT 5 ), DishIngredients AS ( SELECT di.dish_id, GROUP_CONCAT(i.ingredient_name) AS ingredients FROM dish_ingredients di INNER JOIN ingredients i ON di.ingredient_id = i.ingredient_id WHERE di.is_archived = 0 AND i.is_archived = 0 GROUP BY di.dish_id ), UserAccess AS ( SELECT uda.dish_id, GROUP_CONCAT(u.user_name) AS users FROM user_dish_access uda INNER JOIN users u ON uda.user_id = u.user_id WHERE uda.is_archived = 0 AND u.is_archived = 0 GROUP BY uda.dish_id ) SELECT td.dish_name, td.average_effectiveness_rating, di.ingredients, ua.users AS accessed_by FROM TopDishes td LEFT JOIN DishIngredients di ON td.dish_id = di.dish_id LEFT JOIN UserAccess ua ON td.dish_id = ua.dish_id ORDER BY td.average_effectiveness_rating DESC
gold_sql.mysql: WITH TopDishes AS (SELECT d.dish_id, d.dish_name, de.average_effectiveness_rating FROM dishes AS d INNER JOIN dish_effectiveness AS de ON d.dish_id = de.dish_id WHERE d.is_archived = 0 AND de.is_archived = 0 ORDER BY de.average_effectiveness_rating DESC LIMIT 5), DishIngredients AS (SELECT di.dish_id, GROUP_CONCAT(i.ingredient_name SEPARATOR ',') AS ingredients FROM dish_ingredients AS di INNER JOIN ingredients AS i ON di.ingredient_id = i.ingredient_id WHERE di.is_archived = 0 AND i.is_archived = 0 GROUP BY di.dish_id), UserAccess AS (SELECT uda.dish_id, GROUP_CONCAT(u.user_name SEPARATOR ',') AS users FROM user_dish_access AS uda INNER JOIN users AS u ON uda.user_id = u.user_id WHERE uda.is_archived = 0 AND u.is_archived = 0 GROUP BY uda.dish_id) SELECT td.dish_name, td.average_effectiveness_rating, di.ingredients, ua.users AS accessed_by FROM TopDishes AS td LEFT JOIN DishIngredients AS di ON td.dish_id = di.dish_id LEFT JOIN UserAccess AS ua ON td.dish_id = ua.dish_id ORDER BY td.average_effectiveness_rating DESC
gold_sql.postgres: WITH TopDishes AS (SELECT d.dish_id, d.dish_name, de.average_effectiveness_rating FROM dishes AS d INNER JOIN dish_effectiveness AS de ON d.dish_id = de.dish_id WHERE d.is_archived = 0 AND de.is_archived = 0 ORDER BY de.average_effectiveness_rating DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 5), DishIngredients AS (SELECT di.dish_id, STRING_AGG(i.ingredient_name, ',') AS ingredients FROM dish_ingredients AS di INNER JOIN ingredients AS i ON di.ingredient_id = i.ingredient_id WHERE di.is_archived = 0 AND i.is_archived = 0 GROUP BY di.dish_id), UserAccess AS (SELECT uda.dish_id, STRING_AGG(u.user_name, ',') AS users FROM user_dish_access AS uda INNER JOIN users AS u ON uda.user_id = u.user_id WHERE uda.is_archived = 0 AND u.is_archived = 0 GROUP BY uda.dish_id) SELECT td.dish_name, td.average_effectiveness_rating, di.ingredients, ua.users AS accessed_by FROM TopDishes AS td LEFT JOIN DishIngredients AS di ON td.dish_id = di.dish_id LEFT JOIN UserAccess AS ua ON td.dish_id = ua.dish_id ORDER BY td.average_effectiveness_rating DESC NULLS LAST

question: Find the monthly revenue and the number of distinct customers for each month with a total order value exceeding zero, ordered chronologically.
external_knowledge: ; "revenue exceeding zero" refers to months with at least one paid order; chronologically ordered results show the trend of revenue and customer count over time.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', o.order_date) AS order_month, SUM(o.total) AS total_revenue, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS unique_customers FROM orders o GROUP BY strftime('%Y-%m', o.order_date) HAVING SUM(o.total) > 0 ORDER BY order_month
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME), '%Y-%m') AS order_month, SUM(o.total) AS total_revenue, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS unique_customers FROM orders AS o GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME), '%Y-%m') HAVING SUM(o.total) > 0 ORDER BY order_month
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT TO_CHAR(CAST(o.order_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY-MM') AS order_month, SUM(o.total) AS total_revenue, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS unique_customers FROM orders AS o GROUP BY TO_CHAR(CAST(o.order_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY-MM') HAVING SUM(o.total) > 0 ORDER BY order_month NULLS FIRST

question: Can you provide a summary of the Evansville Otters' recent news, their next game schedule, their performance in the last 10 games, and their most recent statistical record?

question: Hey, could you show me a list of investors who have received dividends, including their names, the stocks they hold, whether their investment return is positive, negative, or neutral, the total number of alerts they have set, and the average 30-day closing price and dividend yield for their portfolio, ordered by their names and stocks?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH InvestorDividendPerformance AS ( SELECT i.investor_id, i.full_name, inv.stock_id, s.stock_symbol, inv.amount_invested, inv.dividend_received, inv.current_value, (inv.current_value - inv.amount_invested) / inv.amount_invested * 100 AS investment_return_percentage FROM investors i JOIN investments inv ON i.investor_id = inv.investor_id JOIN stocks s ON inv.stock_id = s.stock_id JOIN dividends div ON s.stock_id = div.stock_id WHERE inv.dividend_received > 0 ), HistoricalPerformanceSummary AS ( SELECT hp.stock_id, hp.closing_price, hp.dividend_yield, AVG(hp.closing_price) OVER (PARTITION BY hp.stock_id ORDER BY hp.date ROWS BETWEEN 30 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS avg_30d_closing_price, AVG(hp.dividend_yield) OVER (PARTITION BY hp.stock_id ORDER BY hp.date ROWS BETWEEN 30 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS avg_30d_dividend_yield FROM historical_performance hp ), AlertsSummary AS ( SELECT al.investor_id, al.stock_id, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY al.investor_id, al.stock_id) AS total_alerts FROM dividend_alerts al ) SELECT idp.full_name, idp.stock_symbol, CASE WHEN idp.investment_return_percentage > 0 THEN 'Positive' WHEN idp.investment_return_percentage < 0 THEN 'Negative' ELSE 'Neutral' END AS investment_return_status, COALESCE(als.total_alerts, 0) AS total_alerts_set, hps.avg_30d_closing_price, hps.avg_30d_dividend_yield FROM InvestorDividendPerformance idp LEFT JOIN HistoricalPerformanceSummary hps ON idp.stock_id = hps.stock_id LEFT JOIN AlertsSummary als ON idp.investor_id = als.investor_id AND idp.stock_id = als.stock_id ORDER BY idp.full_name, idp.stock_symbol
gold_sql.mysql: WITH InvestorDividendPerformance AS (SELECT i.investor_id, i.full_name, inv.stock_id, s.stock_symbol, inv.amount_invested, inv.dividend_received, inv.current_value, (inv.current_value - inv.amount_invested) / inv.amount_invested * 100 AS investment_return_percentage FROM investors AS i JOIN investments AS inv ON i.investor_id = inv.investor_id JOIN stocks AS s ON inv.stock_id = s.stock_id JOIN dividends AS `div` ON s.stock_id = `div`.stock_id WHERE inv.dividend_received > 0), HistoricalPerformanceSummary AS (SELECT hp.stock_id, hp.closing_price, hp.dividend_yield, AVG(hp.closing_price) OVER (PARTITION BY hp.stock_id ORDER BY hp.date ROWS BETWEEN 30 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS avg_30d_closing_price, AVG(hp.dividend_yield) OVER (PARTITION BY hp.stock_id ORDER BY hp.date ROWS BETWEEN 30 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS avg_30d_dividend_yield FROM historical_performance AS hp), AlertsSummary AS (SELECT al.investor_id, al.stock_id, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY al.investor_id, al.stock_id) AS total_alerts FROM dividend_alerts AS al) SELECT idp.full_name, idp.stock_symbol, CASE WHEN idp.investment_return_percentage > 0 THEN 'Positive' WHEN idp.investment_return_percentage < 0 THEN 'Negative' ELSE 'Neutral' END AS investment_return_status, COALESCE(als.total_alerts, 0) AS total_alerts_set, hps.avg_30d_closing_price, hps.avg_30d_dividend_yield FROM InvestorDividendPerformance AS idp LEFT JOIN HistoricalPerformanceSummary AS hps ON idp.stock_id = hps.stock_id LEFT JOIN AlertsSummary AS als ON idp.investor_id = als.investor_id AND idp.stock_id = als.stock_id ORDER BY idp.full_name, idp.stock_symbol

question: Return detailed information about each approved asset request, including the request ID, school name, asset name, quantity required, approval date, estimated cost, delivery address, total quantity contributed by all suppliers, and a list of all contributing suppliers.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ApprovedRequests AS ( SELECT r.request_id, r.school_id, r.asset_id, r.quantity_required, r.approval_date, r.estimated_cost, r.delivery_address FROM requests r WHERE r.approval_date IS NOT NULL ) SELECT ar.request_id, s.school_name, a.asset_name, ar.quantity_required, ar.approval_date, ar.estimated_cost, ar.delivery_address, SUM(c.quantity_contributed) AS total_contributed, GROUP_CONCAT(sup.supplier_name) AS contributors FROM ApprovedRequests ar JOIN schools s ON ar.school_id = s.school_id JOIN assets a ON ar.asset_id = a.asset_id JOIN contributions c ON ar.request_id = c.request_id JOIN suppliers sup ON c.supplier_id = sup.supplier_id GROUP BY ar.request_id, s.school_name, a.asset_name, ar.quantity_required, ar.approval_date, ar.estimated_cost, ar.delivery_address
gold_sql.mysql: WITH ApprovedRequests AS (SELECT r.request_id, r.school_id, r.asset_id, r.quantity_required, r.approval_date, r.estimated_cost, r.delivery_address FROM requests AS r WHERE NOT r.approval_date IS NULL) SELECT ar.request_id, s.school_name, a.asset_name, ar.quantity_required, ar.approval_date, ar.estimated_cost, ar.delivery_address, SUM(c.quantity_contributed) AS total_contributed, GROUP_CONCAT(sup.supplier_name SEPARATOR ',') AS contributors FROM ApprovedRequests AS ar JOIN schools AS s ON ar.school_id = s.school_id JOIN assets AS a ON ar.asset_id = a.asset_id JOIN contributions AS c ON ar.request_id = c.request_id JOIN suppliers AS sup ON c.supplier_id = sup.supplier_id GROUP BY ar.request_id, s.school_name, a.asset_name, ar.quantity_required, ar.approval_date, ar.estimated_cost, ar.delivery_address

question: What are the subjects of the messages in the conversation thread initiated by 'john.doe@example.com' that have been sent and are associated with active rules, ordered by the conversation level and then by the highest message count and maximum severity?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RECURSIVE ActiveMessages AS ( SELECT m.message_id, m.sender, m.recipient, m.subject, r.severity FROM messages m INNER JOIN message_rules r ON m.rule_id = r.rule_id WHERE m.status = 'Sent' AND r.active = 1 ), ConversationThread AS ( SELECT am.message_id, am.sender, am.recipient, am.subject, am.severity, 1 AS level FROM ActiveMessages am WHERE am.sender = 'john.doe@example.com' UNION ALL SELECT am.message_id, am.sender, am.recipient, am.subject, am.severity, ct.level + 1 AS level FROM ActiveMessages am INNER JOIN ConversationThread ct ON am.sender = ct.recipient ), MessageSummary AS ( SELECT ct.level, COUNT(ct.message_id) AS message_count, MAX(ct.severity) AS max_severity, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ct.subject) AS subjects FROM ConversationThread ct GROUP BY ct.level ) SELECT ms.subjects FROM MessageSummary ms ORDER BY ms.level, ms.message_count DESC, ms.max_severity DESC

question: Hey, could you help me find all forms created in 2023 that have at least one submission or one error? I'd love to know their IDs, names, statuses, how many submissions they've got, and how many errors they've got. Can you list them in order of the ones with the most submissions to the least, and if there's a tie, list them by the ones with the most errors?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT f.form_id, f.name, f.status, COUNT(fs.submission_id) AS submission_count, COUNT(fe.error_id) AS error_count FROM forms f LEFT JOIN form_submissions fs ON f.form_id = fs.form_id LEFT JOIN form_errors fe ON f.form_id = fe.form_id WHERE strftime('%Y', f.created_at) = '2023' GROUP BY f.form_id, f.name, f.status HAVING COUNT(fs.submission_id) > 0 OR COUNT(fe.error_id) > 0 ORDER BY submission_count DESC, error_count DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT f.form_id, f.name, f.status, COUNT(fs.submission_id) AS submission_count, COUNT(fe.error_id) AS error_count FROM forms AS f LEFT JOIN form_submissions AS fs ON f.form_id = fs.form_id LEFT JOIN form_errors AS fe ON f.form_id = fe.form_id WHERE DATE_FORMAT(CAST(f.created_at AS DATETIME), '%Y') = '2023' GROUP BY f.form_id, f.name, f.status HAVING COUNT(fs.submission_id) > 0 OR COUNT(fe.error_id) > 0 ORDER BY submission_count DESC, error_count DESC
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT f.form_id, f.name, f.status, COUNT(fs.submission_id) AS submission_count, COUNT(fe.error_id) AS error_count FROM forms AS f LEFT JOIN form_submissions AS fs ON f.form_id = fs.form_id LEFT JOIN form_errors AS fe ON f.form_id = fe.form_id WHERE TO_CHAR(CAST(f.created_at AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY') = '2023' GROUP BY f.form_id, f.name, f.status HAVING COUNT(fs.submission_id) > 0 OR COUNT(fe.error_id) > 0 ORDER BY submission_count DESC NULLS LAST, error_count DESC NULLS LAST

question: What is a comprehensive overview of each university, including their average early and mid-career pay, percentages of graduates contributing to societal improvement and in STEM fields, average alumni salary and satisfaction, and their overall rank, ordered from highest alumni satisfaction and lowest rank?
external_knowledge: ; The query assumes a broad definition of "comprehensive overview," encompassing both financial success and societal impact of universities' graduates. "Contributing to societal improvement" and being "in STEM fields" are binary (yes/no) conditions based on individual's self-reported data or predefined criteria not specified within the query. Alumni "satisfaction" likely refers to satisfaction with their educational experience.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH HistoricalDataSummary AS ( SELECT university_id, AVG(early_career_pay) AS avg_early_career_pay, AVG(mid_career_pay) AS avg_mid_career_pay, AVG(make_world_better_percent) AS avg_make_world_better_percent, AVG(stem_percent) AS avg_stem_percent FROM historical_data GROUP BY university_id ), AlumniFeedbackSummary AS ( SELECT university_id, AVG(salary) AS avg_alumni_salary, AVG(satisfaction_rating) AS avg_satisfaction, AVG(CAST(make_world_better AS REAL)) AS percent_make_world_better, AVG(CAST(stem_field AS REAL)) AS percent_in_stem FROM alumni_feedback GROUP BY university_id ), UniversityRanking AS ( SELECT university_id, AVG(rank) AS avg_rank, AVG(early_career_pay) AS avg_ranked_early_career_pay, AVG(mid_career_pay) AS avg_ranked_mid_career_pay, AVG(make_world_better_percent) AS avg_ranked_make_world_better, AVG(stem_percent) AS avg_ranked_stem FROM rankings GROUP BY university_id ), UniversityData AS ( SELECT u.university_id, u.name, hs.avg_early_career_pay, hs.avg_mid_career_pay, hs.avg_make_world_better_percent, hs.avg_stem_percent, af.avg_alumni_salary, af.avg_satisfaction, af.percent_make_world_better, af.percent_in_stem, ur.avg_rank, ur.avg_ranked_early_career_pay, ur.avg_ranked_mid_career_pay, ur.avg_ranked_make_world_better, ur.avg_ranked_stem FROM universities u LEFT JOIN HistoricalDataSummary hs ON u.university_id = hs.university_id LEFT JOIN AlumniFeedbackSummary af ON u.university_id = af.university_id LEFT JOIN UniversityRanking ur ON u.university_id = ur.university_id ) SELECT ud.name, ud.avg_early_career_pay, ud.avg_mid_career_pay, ud.avg_make_world_better_percent, ud.avg_stem_percent, ud.avg_alumni_salary, ud.avg_satisfaction, ud.percent_make_world_better, ud.percent_in_stem, ud.avg_rank, ud.avg_ranked_early_career_pay, ud.avg_ranked_mid_career_pay, ud.avg_ranked_make_world_better, ud.avg_ranked_stem FROM UniversityData ud ORDER BY ud.avg_satisfaction DESC, ud.avg_rank ASC

question: Could you please list the study name, part of speech, language, translation, and whether the comment contains the word 'review' for all concepts in study 1 where the comment includes the word 'review'?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT s.study_name, c.part_of_speech, c.language, ct.translation, CASE WHEN INSTR(cc.comment, 'review') > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS contains_review FROM studies s JOIN concepts c ON s.study_id = c.study_id JOIN concept_translations ct ON c.concept_id = ct.concept_id JOIN concept_comments cc ON c.concept_id = cc.concept_id WHERE s.study_id = 1 AND INSTR(cc.comment, 'review') > 0
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT s.study_name, c.part_of_speech, c.language, ct.translation, CASE WHEN LOCATE('review', cc.comment) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS contains_review FROM studies AS s JOIN concepts AS c ON s.study_id = c.study_id JOIN concept_translations AS ct ON c.concept_id = ct.concept_id JOIN concept_comments AS cc ON c.concept_id = cc.concept_id WHERE s.study_id = 1 AND LOCATE('review', cc.comment) > 0

question: What are the genres of the top-grossing movies, ranked by their average user ratings and box office revenues, with the top three movies for each genre featuring the most talented directors and actors?
external_knowledge: Top-grossing movies; Average user ratings are a measure of how well a movie is liked by its audience; Box office revenues are a measure of a movie's commercial success; Talented directors and actors are those who have a proven track record of producing high-quality movies.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RankedMovies AS ( SELECT m.movie_id, m.title, m.release_year, m.box_office, g.genre_name, AVG(r.rating) AS average_user_rating, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY g.genre_name ORDER BY AVG(r.rating) DESC, CAST(REPLACE(m.box_office, ',', '') AS INTEGER) DESC) AS genre_rank FROM movies m JOIN movie_genres mg ON m.movie_id = mg.movie_id JOIN genres g ON mg.genre_id = g.genre_id JOIN reviews r ON m.movie_id = r.movie_id GROUP BY m.movie_id, m.title, m.release_year, m.box_office, g.genre_name ), TopMovies AS ( SELECT rm.movie_id, rm.title, rm.release_year, rm.box_office, rm.genre_name, rm.average_user_rating, md.director_id, ma.actor_id FROM RankedMovies rm JOIN movie_directors md ON rm.movie_id = md.movie_id JOIN movie_actors ma ON rm.movie_id = ma.movie_id WHERE rm.genre_rank <= 3 AND ma.order_of_appearance = 1 ) SELECT tm.genre_name FROM TopMovies tm ORDER BY tm.genre_name, tm.average_user_rating DESC, CAST(REPLACE(tm.box_office, ',', '') AS INTEGER) DESC
gold_sql.mysql: WITH RankedMovies AS (SELECT m.movie_id, m.title, m.release_year, m.box_office, g.genre_name, AVG(r.rating) AS average_user_rating, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY g.genre_name ORDER BY AVG(r.rating) DESC, CAST(REPLACE(m.box_office, ',', '') AS SIGNED) DESC) AS genre_rank FROM movies AS m JOIN movie_genres AS mg ON m.movie_id = mg.movie_id JOIN genres AS g ON mg.genre_id = g.genre_id JOIN reviews AS r ON m.movie_id = r.movie_id GROUP BY m.movie_id, m.title, m.release_year, m.box_office, g.genre_name), TopMovies AS (SELECT rm.movie_id, rm.title, rm.release_year, rm.box_office, rm.genre_name, rm.average_user_rating, md.director_id, ma.actor_id FROM RankedMovies AS rm JOIN movie_directors AS md ON rm.movie_id = md.movie_id JOIN movie_actors AS ma ON rm.movie_id = ma.movie_id WHERE rm.genre_rank <= 3 AND ma.order_of_appearance = 1) SELECT tm.genre_name FROM TopMovies AS tm ORDER BY tm.genre_name, tm.average_user_rating DESC, CAST(REPLACE(tm.box_office, ',', '') AS SIGNED) DESC
gold_sql.postgres: WITH RankedMovies AS (SELECT m.movie_id, m.title, m.release_year, m.box_office, g.genre_name, AVG(r.rating) AS average_user_rating, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY g.genre_name ORDER BY AVG(r.rating) DESC NULLS LAST, CAST(REPLACE(m.box_office, ',', '') AS INT) DESC NULLS LAST) AS genre_rank FROM movies AS m JOIN movie_genres AS mg ON m.movie_id = mg.movie_id JOIN genres AS g ON mg.genre_id = g.genre_id JOIN reviews AS r ON m.movie_id = r.movie_id GROUP BY m.movie_id, m.title, m.release_year, m.box_office, g.genre_name), TopMovies AS (SELECT rm.movie_id, rm.title, rm.release_year, rm.box_office, rm.genre_name, rm.average_user_rating, md.director_id, ma.actor_id FROM RankedMovies AS rm JOIN movie_directors AS md ON rm.movie_id = md.movie_id JOIN movie_actors AS ma ON rm.movie_id = ma.movie_id WHERE rm.genre_rank <= 3 AND ma.order_of_appearance = 1) SELECT tm.genre_name FROM TopMovies AS tm ORDER BY tm.genre_name NULLS FIRST, tm.average_user_rating DESC NULLS LAST, CAST(REPLACE(tm.box_office, ',', '') AS INT) DESC NULLS LAST

question: Could you tell me how many distinct patients are part of studies where the data points have been validated with a 'range check' rule that specifies the value should be between 18 and 65, and the actual values in the data points meet this range?

gold_sql.postgres: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.patient_id) AS patient_count FROM patients AS p JOIN data_values AS dv ON p.patient_id = dv.patient_id JOIN validation_rules AS vr ON vr.study_id = p.study_id AND vr.data_point_id = dv.data_point_id WHERE vr.rule_type = 'range check' AND vr.rule_condition = 'value > 18 and value < 65' AND CAST(dv.value AS INT) BETWEEN 18 AND 65

question: Provide the name of the county, the type of highway user, the average speed of users involved, the number of incidents, the total number of non-suicide fatalities and injuries, the speed limit of the highway, the average daily traffic, the name of the rail equipment involved, and the number of incidents logged for each month, grouped by county, user type, speed limit, average daily traffic, rail equipment, and month, and order the results by county name and month.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT c.county_name, u.user_type_name, AVG(i.user_speed) AS avg_speed, COUNT(i.incident_id) AS num_incidents, SUM(i.non_suicide_fatality) AS total_fatalities, SUM(i.non_suicide_injury) AS total_injuries, h.speed_limit, h.average_daily_traffic, re.rail_equipment_name, strftime('%m', i.incident_date) AS month, COUNT(il.incident_id) AS num_incidents_logged FROM incidents i JOIN counties c ON i.county_id = c.county_id JOIN user_types u ON i.user_type_id = u.user_type_id JOIN highways h ON i.highway_id = h.highway_id JOIN rail_equipment_types re ON i.rail_equipment_id = re.rail_equipment_id LEFT JOIN incident_logs il ON i.incident_id = il.incident_id GROUP BY c.county_name, u.user_type_name, h.speed_limit, h.average_daily_traffic, re.rail_equipment_name, month ORDER BY c.county_name, month
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT c.county_name, u.user_type_name, AVG(i.user_speed) AS avg_speed, COUNT(i.incident_id) AS num_incidents, SUM(i.non_suicide_fatality) AS total_fatalities, SUM(i.non_suicide_injury) AS total_injuries, h.speed_limit, h.average_daily_traffic, re.rail_equipment_name, DATE_FORMAT(CAST(i.incident_date AS DATETIME), '%m') AS month, COUNT(il.incident_id) AS num_incidents_logged FROM incidents AS i JOIN counties AS c ON i.county_id = c.county_id JOIN user_types AS u ON i.user_type_id = u.user_type_id JOIN highways AS h ON i.highway_id = h.highway_id JOIN rail_equipment_types AS re ON i.rail_equipment_id = re.rail_equipment_id LEFT JOIN incident_logs AS il ON i.incident_id = il.incident_id GROUP BY c.county_name, u.user_type_name, h.speed_limit, h.average_daily_traffic, re.rail_equipment_name, month ORDER BY c.county_name, month
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT c.county_name, u.user_type_name, AVG(i.user_speed) AS avg_speed, COUNT(i.incident_id) AS num_incidents, SUM(i.non_suicide_fatality) AS total_fatalities, SUM(i.non_suicide_injury) AS total_injuries, h.speed_limit, h.average_daily_traffic, re.rail_equipment_name, TO_CHAR(CAST(i.incident_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'MM') AS month, COUNT(il.incident_id) AS num_incidents_logged FROM incidents AS i JOIN counties AS c ON i.county_id = c.county_id JOIN user_types AS u ON i.user_type_id = u.user_type_id JOIN highways AS h ON i.highway_id = h.highway_id JOIN rail_equipment_types AS re ON i.rail_equipment_id = re.rail_equipment_id LEFT JOIN incident_logs AS il ON i.incident_id = il.incident_id GROUP BY c.county_name, u.user_type_name, h.speed_limit, h.average_daily_traffic, re.rail_equipment_name, month ORDER BY c.county_name NULLS FIRST, month NULLS FIRST

question: Find the names of users who have reordered products before, along with the total number of orders and the average order cost for each user, but only include users who have placed more than one order.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT u.user_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, AVG(o.total_cost) AS average_order_cost FROM users u INNER JOIN orders o ON u.user_id = o.user_id INNER JOIN order_frequency of ON u.user_id = of.user_id WHERE of.reordered = 1 GROUP BY u.user_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 1
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT u.user_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, AVG(o.total_cost) AS average_order_cost FROM users AS u INNER JOIN orders AS o ON u.user_id = o.user_id INNER JOIN order_frequency AS `of` ON u.user_id = `of`.user_id WHERE `of`.reordered = 1 GROUP BY u.user_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 1
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT u.user_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, AVG(o.total_cost) AS average_order_cost FROM users AS u INNER JOIN orders AS o ON u.user_id = o.user_id INNER JOIN order_frequency AS of ON u.user_id = of.user_id WHERE of.reordered = 1 GROUP BY u.user_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 1

question: Find the usernames, total generations, successful generations, average generation durations, distinct datasets generated, latest dataset creation dates, and average quality scores for all active users who have generated data at least once.
external_knowledge: ; A user is considered active when their `is_active` flag is set to 1; A data generation process is considered successful when its `status` is 'success'; The duration is measured in seconds; The quality score is a measure of the dataset's quality, with higher scores indicating higher quality.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT u.username, COUNT(dgl.log_id) AS total_generations, SUM(CASE WHEN dgl.status = 'success' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS successful_generations, AVG(CAST(dgl.duration AS INTEGER)) AS average_duration_seconds, COUNT(DISTINCT g.dataset_id) AS distinct_datasets_generated, MAX(g.creation_date) AS latest_dataset_creation_date, AVG(g.quality_score) AS average_quality_score FROM users u INNER JOIN data_generation_logs dgl ON u.user_id = dgl.user_id LEFT JOIN generated_datasets g ON dgl.config_id = g.config_id AND u.user_id = g.user_id WHERE u.is_active = 1 GROUP BY u.username HAVING COUNT(dgl.log_id) > 0
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT u.username, COUNT(dgl.log_id) AS total_generations, SUM(CASE WHEN dgl.status = 'success' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS successful_generations, AVG(CAST(dgl.duration AS SIGNED)) AS average_duration_seconds, COUNT(DISTINCT g.dataset_id) AS distinct_datasets_generated, MAX(g.creation_date) AS latest_dataset_creation_date, AVG(g.quality_score) AS average_quality_score FROM users AS u INNER JOIN data_generation_logs AS dgl ON u.user_id = dgl.user_id LEFT JOIN generated_datasets AS g ON dgl.config_id = g.config_id AND u.user_id = g.user_id WHERE u.is_active = 1 GROUP BY u.username HAVING COUNT(dgl.log_id) > 0
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT u.username, COUNT(dgl.log_id) AS total_generations, SUM(CASE WHEN dgl.status = 'success' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS successful_generations, AVG(CAST(dgl.duration AS INT)) AS average_duration_seconds, COUNT(DISTINCT g.dataset_id) AS distinct_datasets_generated, MAX(g.creation_date) AS latest_dataset_creation_date, AVG(g.quality_score) AS average_quality_score FROM users AS u INNER JOIN data_generation_logs AS dgl ON u.user_id = dgl.user_id LEFT JOIN generated_datasets AS g ON dgl.config_id = g.config_id AND u.user_id = g.user_id WHERE u.is_active = 1 GROUP BY u.username HAVING COUNT(dgl.log_id) > 0

question: Return the title, publication year, citation count, authors, publication name, and total accesses for the top 5 most cited papers across all databases, ordered by citation count in descending order.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH MostCitedPapers AS ( SELECT paper_id, title, publication_year, times_cited_all_databases FROM papers ORDER BY times_cited_all_databases DESC LIMIT 5 ), AuthorList AS ( SELECT paper_id, GROUP_CONCAT(author_name, ', ') AS authors FROM paper_authors pa JOIN authors a ON pa.author_id = a.author_id GROUP BY paper_id ), PublicationName AS ( SELECT paper_id, publication_name FROM paper_publications pp JOIN publications p ON pp.publication_id = p.publication_id ), AccessCounts AS ( SELECT paper_id, COUNT(*) AS total_accesses FROM access_logs GROUP BY paper_id ) SELECT mc.title, mc.publication_year, mc.times_cited_all_databases, al.authors, pub.publication_name, ac.total_accesses FROM MostCitedPapers mc JOIN AuthorList al ON mc.paper_id = al.paper_id JOIN PublicationName pub ON mc.paper_id = pub.paper_id JOIN AccessCounts ac ON mc.paper_id = ac.paper_id ORDER BY mc.times_cited_all_databases DESC
gold_sql.mysql: WITH MostCitedPapers AS (SELECT paper_id, title, publication_year, times_cited_all_databases FROM papers ORDER BY times_cited_all_databases DESC LIMIT 5), AuthorList AS (SELECT paper_id, GROUP_CONCAT(author_name SEPARATOR ', ') AS authors FROM paper_authors AS pa JOIN authors AS a ON pa.author_id = a.author_id GROUP BY paper_id), PublicationName AS (SELECT paper_id, publication_name FROM paper_publications AS pp JOIN publications AS p ON pp.publication_id = p.publication_id), AccessCounts AS (SELECT paper_id, COUNT(*) AS total_accesses FROM access_logs GROUP BY paper_id) SELECT mc.title, mc.publication_year, mc.times_cited_all_databases, al.authors, pub.publication_name, ac.total_accesses FROM MostCitedPapers AS mc JOIN AuthorList AS al ON mc.paper_id = al.paper_id JOIN PublicationName AS pub ON mc.paper_id = pub.paper_id JOIN AccessCounts AS ac ON mc.paper_id = ac.paper_id ORDER BY mc.times_cited_all_databases DESC

question:
**User**: I want to query some drainage asset information.
**Assistant**: Which aspect of the drainage assets would you like to know more about?
**User**: I'm looking for information on maintenance activities.
**Assistant**: What specific maintenance activities would you like to focus on?
**User**: I'm interested in maintenance activities that have already been completed.
**Assistant**: What else would you like to know about these completed maintenance activities?
**User**: I want to know the average cost per outfall for each asset, considering only outfalls with good or fair water quality.
**Assistant**: Would you like to filter these results further?
**User**: Yes, I only want to see assets where the average cost per outfall is more than $100.
**Assistant**: How would you like the results to be sorted?
**User**: Sort them in descending order based on the average cost per outfall.
**Assistant**: OK, I will help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT ma.asset_id, (SUM(ma.actual_cost) / COUNT(DISTINCT of.outfall_id)) AS cost_per_outfall FROM maintenance_activities ma INNER JOIN outfalls of ON ma.asset_id = of.asset_id WHERE ma.status = 'Completed' AND of.water_quality IN ('Good', 'Fair') GROUP BY ma.asset_id HAVING (SUM(ma.actual_cost) / COUNT(DISTINCT of.outfall_id)) > 100 ORDER BY cost_per_outfall DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT ma.asset_id, (SUM(ma.actual_cost) / COUNT(DISTINCT `of`.outfall_id)) AS cost_per_outfall FROM maintenance_activities AS ma INNER JOIN outfalls AS `of` ON ma.asset_id = `of`.asset_id WHERE ma.status = 'Completed' AND `of`.water_quality IN ('Good', 'Fair') GROUP BY ma.asset_id HAVING (SUM(ma.actual_cost) / COUNT(DISTINCT `of`.outfall_id)) > 100 ORDER BY cost_per_outfall DESC
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT ma.asset_id, (SUM(ma.actual_cost) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT of.outfall_id), 0)) AS cost_per_outfall FROM maintenance_activities AS ma INNER JOIN outfalls AS of ON ma.asset_id = of.asset_id WHERE ma.status = 'Completed' AND of.water_quality IN ('Good', 'Fair') GROUP BY ma.asset_id HAVING (SUM(ma.actual_cost) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT of.outfall_id), 0)) > 100 ORDER BY cost_per_outfall DESC NULLS LAST

question: Could you please identify the top 3 countries with the highest average number of fatalities in incidents occurring after the year 2000, along with the total number of incidents, the number of unique ISO codes, and the corresponding event descriptions? Please arrange the results in descending order based on the average fatalities.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT i.country, COUNT(i.incident_id) AS total_incidents, AVG(i.fatalities) AS average_fatalities, COUNT(DISTINCT iso.iso_code) AS unique_iso_codes, GROUP_CONCAT(ei.event_description, '; ') AS event_descriptions FROM incidents i INNER JOIN incident_iso iso ON i.incident_id = iso.incident_id INNER JOIN incident_event_ids ei ON i.incident_id = ei.incident_id WHERE i.year > 2000 GROUP BY i.country ORDER BY average_fatalities DESC LIMIT 3
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT i.country, COUNT(i.incident_id) AS total_incidents, AVG(i.fatalities) AS average_fatalities, COUNT(DISTINCT iso.iso_code) AS unique_iso_codes, GROUP_CONCAT(ei.event_description SEPARATOR '; ') AS event_descriptions FROM incidents AS i INNER JOIN incident_iso AS iso ON i.incident_id = iso.incident_id INNER JOIN incident_event_ids AS ei ON i.incident_id = ei.incident_id WHERE i.year > 2000 GROUP BY i.country ORDER BY average_fatalities DESC LIMIT 3
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT i.country, COUNT(i.incident_id) AS total_incidents, AVG(i.fatalities) AS average_fatalities, COUNT(DISTINCT iso.iso_code) AS unique_iso_codes, STRING_AGG(ei.event_description, '; ') AS event_descriptions FROM incidents AS i INNER JOIN incident_iso AS iso ON i.incident_id = iso.incident_id INNER JOIN incident_event_ids AS ei ON i.incident_id = ei.incident_id WHERE i.year > 2000 GROUP BY i.country ORDER BY average_fatalities DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 3

question: What is the maximum average value between the average working years and the average GPA across all education levels?

question: Hey, can you show me the names of all active test configurations along with the different types of metrics collected and any notes associated with these configurations, but only for the most recent successful test run of each configuration?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RecentSuccessfulRuns AS ( SELECT run_id, config_id, run_status, start_time, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY config_id ORDER BY start_time DESC) AS rn FROM test_runs WHERE run_status = 'success' ) SELECT ts.config_id, tc.config_name, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT pm.metric_type) AS metrics_types, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT n.note_text) AS config_notes FROM RecentSuccessfulRuns ts JOIN test_configurations tc ON ts.config_id = tc.config_id JOIN performance_metrics pm ON ts.run_id = pm.run_id LEFT JOIN notes n ON tc.config_id = n.entity_id AND n.entity_type = 'test_config' WHERE ts.rn = 1 AND tc.active_status = 1 GROUP BY ts.config_id, tc.config_name
gold_sql.mysql: WITH RecentSuccessfulRuns AS (SELECT run_id, config_id, run_status, start_time, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY config_id ORDER BY start_time DESC) AS rn FROM test_runs WHERE run_status = 'success') SELECT ts.config_id, tc.config_name, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT pm.metric_type SEPARATOR ',') AS metrics_types, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT n.note_text SEPARATOR ',') AS config_notes FROM RecentSuccessfulRuns AS ts JOIN test_configurations AS tc ON ts.config_id = tc.config_id JOIN performance_metrics AS pm ON ts.run_id = pm.run_id LEFT JOIN notes AS n ON tc.config_id = n.entity_id AND n.entity_type = 'test_config' WHERE ts.rn = 1 AND tc.active_status = 1 GROUP BY ts.config_id, tc.config_name

question: What are the names of the countries, the corresponding indicator names, the average values of these indicators, their trends over time, the dates of the latest notifications, and the access counts for each indicator in each country, listed in order from country name to indicator name?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH AvgValues AS ( SELECT country_id, indicator_id, AVG(value) AS avg_value FROM data_values GROUP BY country_id, indicator_id ), Trends AS ( SELECT country_id, indicator_id, (MAX(value) - MIN(value)) / (MAX(year_id) - MIN(year_id)) AS trend FROM data_values GROUP BY country_id, indicator_id ), LatestNotifications AS ( SELECT country_id, indicator_id, MAX(notification_date) AS latest_notification_date FROM notifications GROUP BY country_id, indicator_id ), AccessCounts AS ( SELECT country_id, indicator_id, COUNT(access_id) AS access_count FROM access_logs GROUP BY country_id, indicator_id ) SELECT c.country_name, i.indicator_name, av.avg_value, t.trend, ln.latest_notification_date, ac.access_count FROM countries c JOIN AvgValues av ON c.country_id = av.country_id JOIN Trends t ON av.country_id = t.country_id AND av.indicator_id = t.indicator_id JOIN indicators i ON av.indicator_id = i.indicator_id LEFT JOIN LatestNotifications ln ON av.country_id = ln.country_id AND av.indicator_id = ln.indicator_id LEFT JOIN AccessCounts ac ON av.country_id = ac.country_id AND av.indicator_id = ac.indicator_id ORDER BY c.country_name, i.indicator_name

question: What are the names, divisions, ranks, win counts, loss counts, average points scored during the regular season, and games behind the leader, for top three teams of each division, including the division leaders, across all seasons between 2020 and 2023?
external_knowledge: A team is considered a division leader if it has the highest rank within its division. The rank of a team is its position within the division based on their performance; Games behind the leader is calculated as the difference between a team's rank and the rank of the division leader.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH TeamPerformanceCTE AS ( SELECT t.team_name, s.season_name, st.rank AS team_rank, d.division_name, st.wins AS total_wins, st.losses AS total_losses, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.season_id, d.division_id ORDER BY st.rank) AS team_position, (SELECT AVG(CAST(SUBSTR(g.score, 1, INSTR(g.score, '-') - 1) AS INTEGER)) FROM games g WHERE g.team_id = st.team_id AND g.game_type = 'regular season' AND g.game_date BETWEEN s.start_date AND s.end_date) AS avg_points_scored FROM standings st INNER JOIN teams t ON st.team_id = t.team_id INNER JOIN seasons s ON st.season_id = s.season_id INNER JOIN divisions d ON t.division_id = d.division_id WHERE s.start_date BETWEEN '2020-01-01' AND '2023-12-31' ) SELECT team_name, season_name, division_name, team_rank, total_wins, total_losses, avg_points_scored, team_position AS games_behind FROM TeamPerformanceCTE WHERE team_position <= 3 ORDER BY season_name, division_name, team_rank
gold_sql.mysql: WITH TeamPerformanceCTE AS (SELECT t.team_name, s.season_name, st.`rank` AS team_rank, d.division_name, st.wins AS total_wins, st.losses AS total_losses, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.season_id, d.division_id ORDER BY st.`rank`) AS team_position, (SELECT AVG(CAST(SUBSTRING(g.score, 1, LOCATE('-', g.score) - 1) AS SIGNED)) FROM games AS g WHERE g.team_id = st.team_id AND g.game_type = 'regular season' AND g.game_date BETWEEN s.start_date AND s.end_date) AS avg_points_scored FROM standings AS st INNER JOIN teams AS t ON st.team_id = t.team_id INNER JOIN seasons AS s ON st.season_id = s.season_id INNER JOIN divisions AS d ON t.division_id = d.division_id WHERE s.start_date BETWEEN '2020-01-01' AND '2023-12-31') SELECT team_name, season_name, division_name, team_rank, total_wins, total_losses, avg_points_scored, team_position AS games_behind FROM TeamPerformanceCTE WHERE team_position <= 3 ORDER BY season_name, division_name, team_rank
gold_sql.postgres: WITH TeamPerformanceCTE AS (SELECT t.team_name, s.season_name, st.rank AS team_rank, d.division_name, st.wins AS total_wins, st.losses AS total_losses, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.season_id, d.division_id ORDER BY st.rank NULLS FIRST) AS team_position, (SELECT AVG(CAST(SUBSTRING(g.score FROM 1 FOR STRPOS(g.score, '-') - 1) AS INT)) FROM games AS g WHERE g.team_id = st.team_id AND g.game_type = 'regular season' AND g.game_date BETWEEN s.start_date AND s.end_date) AS avg_points_scored FROM standings AS st INNER JOIN teams AS t ON st.team_id = t.team_id INNER JOIN seasons AS s ON st.season_id = s.season_id INNER JOIN divisions AS d ON t.division_id = d.division_id WHERE s.start_date BETWEEN '2020-01-01' AND '2023-12-31') SELECT team_name, season_name, division_name, team_rank, total_wins, total_losses, avg_points_scored, team_position AS games_behind FROM TeamPerformanceCTE WHERE team_position <= 3 ORDER BY season_name NULLS FIRST, division_name NULLS FIRST, team_rank NULLS FIRST

gold_sql.postgres: SELECT p.name, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT m.mission_name, ',') AS missions_participated FROM personnel AS p INNER JOIN personnel_missions AS pm ON p.personnel_id = pm.personnel_id INNER JOIN missions AS m ON pm.mission_id = m.mission_id WHERE p.status IN ('Active', 'KIA', 'MIA') GROUP BY p.name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT m.mission_id) > 0

question:
**User**: I want to retrieve detailed information about our test cases.
**Assistant**: What specific details would you like to know about the test cases?
**User**: I need to know the test case ID, summary, pre-conditions, test data, expected results, status, priority, creation information, and category.
**Assistant**: Would you like to include any execution results in the output?
**User**: Yes, please include the latest execution results, including the execution ID, status, date, executed by, duration, comments, and CI/CD pipeline ID.
**Assistant**: How about the user who created the test case? Would you like to include their details?
**User**: Yes, please include the user's name, email, role, department, phone number, creation date, and last login date.
**Assistant**: One more thing, would you like to include any test logs in the output?
**User**: Yes, please include any available logs, or 'No logs available' if there are none.
**Assistant**: Finally, how would you like the results to be filtered?
**User**: I only need the latest execution result for each test case.
**Assistant**: OK, I will help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH LatestExecution AS ( SELECT ter.test_case_id, ter.execution_id, ter.status AS execution_status, ter.execution_date, ter.executed_by, ter.duration, ter.comments, ter.ci_cd_pipeline_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ter.test_case_id ORDER BY ter.execution_date DESC) AS rn FROM test_execution_results ter ) SELECT tc.test_case_id, tc.summary, tc.pre_conditions, tc.test_data, tc.expected_results, tc.status AS test_case_status, tc.priority, tc.created_by, tc.created_date, tc.last_modified_by, tc.last_modified_date, tc.category, le.execution_id, le.execution_status, le.execution_date, le.executed_by, le.duration, le.comments, le.ci_cd_pipeline_id, u.user_name, u.email, u.role, u.department, u.phone_number, u.created_date AS user_created_date, u.last_login_date, COALESCE((SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(tl.log_message, ' | ') FROM test_logs tl WHERE tl.execution_id = le.execution_id GROUP BY tl.execution_id), 'No logs available') AS log_messages FROM test_cases tc JOIN LatestExecution le ON tc.test_case_id = le.test_case_id AND le.rn = 1 JOIN users u ON tc.created_by = u.user_id

gold_sql.postgres: WITH LatestExecution AS (SELECT ter.test_case_id, ter.execution_id, ter.status AS execution_status, ter.execution_date, ter.executed_by, ter.duration, ter.comments, ter.ci_cd_pipeline_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ter.test_case_id ORDER BY ter.execution_date DESC NULLS LAST) AS rn FROM test_execution_results AS ter) SELECT tc.test_case_id, tc.summary, tc.pre_conditions, tc.test_data, tc.expected_results, tc.status AS test_case_status, tc.priority, tc.created_by, tc.created_date, tc.last_modified_by, tc.last_modified_date, tc.category, le.execution_id, le.execution_status, le.execution_date, le.executed_by, le.duration, le.comments, le.ci_cd_pipeline_id, u.user_name, u.email, u.role, u.department, u.phone_number, u.created_date AS user_created_date, u.last_login_date, COALESCE((SELECT STRING_AGG(tl.log_message, ' | ') FROM test_logs AS tl WHERE tl.execution_id = le.execution_id GROUP BY tl.execution_id), 'No logs available') AS log_messages FROM test_cases AS tc JOIN LatestExecution AS le ON tc.test_case_id = le.test_case_id AND le.rn = 1 JOIN users AS u ON tc.created_by = u.user_id

question: What are the names of the machine learning models, their total runs, average performance metric values, and their top three most influential features along with the importance of these features?
external_knowledge: In the context of machine learning, a model's performance is often measured using metrics such as mean squared error (mse), mean absolute error (mae), root mean squared error (rmse), and R-squared score (r2_score). Feature importance refers to how much each feature contributes to the model's predictions. This information is crucial for understanding and optimizing the models.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ModelRuns AS ( SELECT m.model_id, m.model_name, COUNT(DISTINCT mr.run_id) AS total_runs FROM models m JOIN model_runs mr ON m.model_id = mr.model_id GROUP BY m.model_id, m.model_name ), ModelMetrics AS ( SELECT m.model_id, AVG(pm.value) AS avg_metric_value FROM models m JOIN performance_metrics pm ON m.model_id = pm.run_id GROUP BY m.model_id ), TopFeatures AS ( SELECT m.model_id, m.model_name, mf.feature_name, mf.importance, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY m.model_id ORDER BY mf.importance DESC) AS feature_rank FROM models m JOIN model_feature_importances mf ON m.model_id = mf.run_id ), Top3Features AS ( SELECT tf.model_id, tf.model_name, tf.feature_name, tf.importance FROM TopFeatures tf WHERE tf.feature_rank <= 3 ) SELECT mr.model_name, mr.total_runs, mm.avg_metric_value, GROUP_CONCAT(tf.feature_name || ' (' || tf.importance || ')', ', ') AS top_3_features FROM ModelRuns mr JOIN ModelMetrics mm ON mr.model_id = mm.model_id LEFT JOIN Top3Features tf ON mr.model_id = tf.model_id GROUP BY mr.model_name, mr.total_runs, mm.avg_metric_value ORDER BY mr.model_name
gold_sql.mysql: WITH ModelRuns AS (SELECT m.model_id, m.model_name, COUNT(DISTINCT mr.run_id) AS total_runs FROM models AS m JOIN model_runs AS mr ON m.model_id = mr.model_id GROUP BY m.model_id, m.model_name), ModelMetrics AS (SELECT m.model_id, AVG(pm.value) AS avg_metric_value FROM models AS m JOIN performance_metrics AS pm ON m.model_id = pm.run_id GROUP BY m.model_id), TopFeatures AS (SELECT m.model_id, m.model_name, mf.feature_name, mf.importance, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY m.model_id ORDER BY mf.importance DESC) AS feature_rank FROM models AS m JOIN model_feature_importances AS mf ON m.model_id = mf.run_id), Top3Features AS (SELECT tf.model_id, tf.model_name, tf.feature_name, tf.importance FROM TopFeatures AS tf WHERE tf.feature_rank <= 3) SELECT mr.model_name, mr.total_runs, mm.avg_metric_value, GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(tf.feature_name, ' (', tf.importance, ')') SEPARATOR ', ') AS top_3_features FROM ModelRuns AS mr JOIN ModelMetrics AS mm ON mr.model_id = mm.model_id LEFT JOIN Top3Features AS tf ON mr.model_id = tf.model_id GROUP BY mr.model_name, mr.total_runs, mm.avg_metric_value ORDER BY mr.model_name
gold_sql.postgres: WITH ModelRuns AS (SELECT m.model_id, m.model_name, COUNT(DISTINCT mr.run_id) AS total_runs FROM models AS m JOIN model_runs AS mr ON m.model_id = mr.model_id GROUP BY m.model_id, m.model_name), ModelMetrics AS (SELECT m.model_id, AVG(pm.value) AS avg_metric_value FROM models AS m JOIN performance_metrics AS pm ON m.model_id = pm.run_id GROUP BY m.model_id), TopFeatures AS (SELECT m.model_id, m.model_name, mf.feature_name, mf.importance, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY m.model_id ORDER BY mf.importance DESC NULLS LAST) AS feature_rank FROM models AS m JOIN model_feature_importances AS mf ON m.model_id = mf.run_id), Top3Features AS (SELECT tf.model_id, tf.model_name, tf.feature_name, tf.importance FROM TopFeatures AS tf WHERE tf.feature_rank <= 3) SELECT mr.model_name, mr.total_runs, mm.avg_metric_value, STRING_AGG(tf.feature_name || ' (' || tf.importance || ')', ', ') AS top_3_features FROM ModelRuns AS mr JOIN ModelMetrics AS mm ON mr.model_id = mm.model_id LEFT JOIN Top3Features AS tf ON mr.model_id = tf.model_id GROUP BY mr.model_name, mr.total_runs, mm.avg_metric_value ORDER BY mr.model_name NULLS FIRST

question: Could you provide detailed information on patients with a moderate risk level, including their demographics, risk assessments, lifestyle factors, and cardiovascular test results?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH PatientRiskCTE AS ( SELECT p.patient_id, p.age, p.sex, p.ethnicity, ra.risk_level, ra.recommendations, ra.recommended_interventions, lf.smoking_status, lf.exercise_frequency, lf.diet_quality, lf.physical_activity_level, lf.dietary_preferences FROM patients p INNER JOIN risk_assessments ra ON p.patient_id = ra.patient_id INNER JOIN lifestyle_factors lf ON p.patient_id = lf.patient_id WHERE ra.risk_level = 'moderate' ) SELECT prc.patient_id, prc.age, prc.sex, prc.ethnicity, prc.risk_level, prc.recommendations, prc.recommended_interventions, prc.smoking_status, prc.exercise_frequency, prc.diet_quality, prc.physical_activity_level, prc.dietary_preferences, GROUP_CONCAT(ct.test_type || ': ' || ct.result) AS test_results FROM PatientRiskCTE prc LEFT JOIN cardiovascular_tests ct ON prc.patient_id = ct.patient_id GROUP BY prc.patient_id, prc.age, prc.sex, prc.ethnicity, prc.risk_level, prc.recommendations, prc.recommended_interventions, prc.smoking_status, prc.exercise_frequency, prc.diet_quality, prc.physical_activity_level, prc.dietary_preferences

question: What is the total amount of fuel and the total cost of fuel for completed operations, grouped by the model of the aircraft and the operation status, where the operations are associated with locations that experienced emergencies on the same day?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH OperationFuelCTE AS ( SELECT o.operation_id, o.aircraft_id, a.model AS aircraft_model, f.fuel_amount, f.fuel_cost, o.status AS operation_status FROM operations o JOIN fuel_records f ON o.operation_id = f.operation_id JOIN aircraft a ON o.aircraft_id = a.aircraft_id JOIN emergencies e ON o.location = e.location AND o.date = strftime('%Y-%m-%d', e.date_time_utc) ) SELECT aircraft_model, operation_status, SUM(fuel_amount) AS total_fuel_amount, SUM(fuel_cost) AS total_fuel_cost FROM OperationFuelCTE WHERE operation_status = 'completed' GROUP BY aircraft_model, operation_status

question: Hey! Could you give me the file path, recording date, and recording time for the audio file with ID 1? Also, I'd like to know all the tags associated with it, the name of the annotator who created the annotation, and the file path to the annotation, but only if the annotator has an ID of 1.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT af.audio_path, af.recording_date, af.recording_time, GROUP_CONCAT(t.tag_name) AS tags, u.user_name AS annotator_name, ann.annot_path AS annotation_path FROM audio_files af LEFT JOIN audio_tags at ON af.audio_id = at.audio_id LEFT JOIN tags t ON at.tag_id = t.tag_id LEFT JOIN annotations ann ON af.audio_id = ann.audio_id LEFT JOIN users u ON ann.annotator_id = u.user_id WHERE af.audio_id = 1 AND u.user_id = 1 GROUP BY af.audio_path, af.recording_date, af.recording_time, u.user_name, ann.annot_path
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT af.audio_path, af.recording_date, af.recording_time, GROUP_CONCAT(t.tag_name SEPARATOR ',') AS tags, u.user_name AS annotator_name, ann.annot_path AS annotation_path FROM audio_files AS af LEFT JOIN audio_tags AS at ON af.audio_id = at.audio_id LEFT JOIN tags AS t ON at.tag_id = t.tag_id LEFT JOIN annotations AS ann ON af.audio_id = ann.audio_id LEFT JOIN users AS u ON ann.annotator_id = u.user_id WHERE af.audio_id = 1 AND u.user_id = 1 GROUP BY af.audio_path, af.recording_date, af.recording_time, u.user_name, ann.annot_path
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT af.audio_path, af.recording_date, af.recording_time, STRING_AGG(t.tag_name, ',') AS tags, u.user_name AS annotator_name, ann.annot_path AS annotation_path FROM audio_files AS af LEFT JOIN audio_tags AS at ON af.audio_id = at.audio_id LEFT JOIN tags AS t ON at.tag_id = t.tag_id LEFT JOIN annotations AS ann ON af.audio_id = ann.audio_id LEFT JOIN users AS u ON ann.annotator_id = u.user_id WHERE af.audio_id = 1 AND u.user_id = 1 GROUP BY af.audio_path, af.recording_date, af.recording_time, u.user_name, ann.annot_path

question: Could you tell me the title of the song, the names of the artist(s), and the peak position of the song on the 'Billboard Hot 100' chart?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT s.title AS song_title, GROUP_CONCAT(a.name) AS artist_names, ce.peak_position AS peak_position FROM chart_entries ce INNER JOIN songs s ON ce.song_id = s.song_id INNER JOIN artists a ON s.artist_id = a.artist_id WHERE ce.chart_id = (SELECT chart_id FROM charts WHERE chart_name = 'Billboard Hot 100') GROUP BY s.title, ce.peak_position
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT s.title AS song_title, GROUP_CONCAT(a.name SEPARATOR ',') AS artist_names, ce.peak_position AS peak_position FROM chart_entries AS ce INNER JOIN songs AS s ON ce.song_id = s.song_id INNER JOIN artists AS a ON s.artist_id = a.artist_id WHERE ce.chart_id = (SELECT chart_id FROM charts WHERE chart_name = 'Billboard Hot 100') GROUP BY s.title, ce.peak_position
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT s.title AS song_title, STRING_AGG(a.name, ',') AS artist_names, ce.peak_position AS peak_position FROM chart_entries AS ce INNER JOIN songs AS s ON ce.song_id = s.song_id INNER JOIN artists AS a ON s.artist_id = a.artist_id WHERE ce.chart_id = (SELECT chart_id FROM charts WHERE chart_name = 'Billboard Hot 100') GROUP BY s.title, ce.peak_position

question: For each age group, region, year, socioeconomic status, and smoking intensity, provide a summary of the average smoking prevalence, average deaths, and death rate per smoker, ordered by age group, region, year, socioeconomic status, and smoking intensity.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH SmokingPrevalence AS ( SELECT age_group, r.region_name, (smoke_cigars_pipe + smoke_both + smoke_cigarettes) * 1.0 / population AS smoking_prevalence, year, socioeconomic_status, smoking_intensity, deaths FROM smoking_data sd JOIN regions r ON sd.region_id = r.region_id ), RegionAverages AS ( SELECT age_group, region_name, AVG(smoking_prevalence) AS avg_smoking_prevalence, AVG(deaths) AS avg_deaths, socioeconomic_status, smoking_intensity, year FROM SmokingPrevalence GROUP BY age_group, region_name, socioeconomic_status, smoking_intensity, year ) SELECT age_group, region_name, year, socioeconomic_status, smoking_intensity, avg_smoking_prevalence, avg_deaths, (avg_deaths * 1.0 / avg_smoking_prevalence) AS death_rate_per_smoker FROM RegionAverages ORDER BY age_group, region_name, year, socioeconomic_status, smoking_intensity
gold_sql.mysql: WITH SmokingPrevalence AS (SELECT age_group, r.region_name, (smoke_cigars_pipe + smoke_both + smoke_cigarettes) * 1.0 / population AS smoking_prevalence, year, socioeconomic_status, smoking_intensity, deaths FROM smoking_data AS sd JOIN regions AS r ON sd.region_id = r.region_id), RegionAverages AS (SELECT age_group, region_name, AVG(smoking_prevalence) AS avg_smoking_prevalence, AVG(deaths) AS avg_deaths, socioeconomic_status, smoking_intensity, year FROM SmokingPrevalence GROUP BY age_group, region_name, socioeconomic_status, smoking_intensity, year) SELECT age_group, region_name, year, socioeconomic_status, smoking_intensity, avg_smoking_prevalence, avg_deaths, (avg_deaths * 1.0 / avg_smoking_prevalence) AS death_rate_per_smoker FROM RegionAverages ORDER BY age_group, region_name, year, socioeconomic_status, smoking_intensity
gold_sql.postgres: WITH SmokingPrevalence AS (SELECT age_group, r.region_name, (smoke_cigars_pipe + smoke_both + smoke_cigarettes) * 1.0 / NULLIF(population, 0) AS smoking_prevalence, year, socioeconomic_status, smoking_intensity, deaths FROM smoking_data AS sd JOIN regions AS r ON sd.region_id = r.region_id), RegionAverages AS (SELECT age_group, region_name, AVG(smoking_prevalence) AS avg_smoking_prevalence, AVG(deaths) AS avg_deaths, socioeconomic_status, smoking_intensity, year FROM SmokingPrevalence GROUP BY age_group, region_name, socioeconomic_status, smoking_intensity, year) SELECT age_group, region_name, year, socioeconomic_status, smoking_intensity, avg_smoking_prevalence, avg_deaths, (avg_deaths * 1.0 / NULLIF(avg_smoking_prevalence, 0)) AS death_rate_per_smoker FROM RegionAverages ORDER BY age_group NULLS FIRST, region_name NULLS FIRST, year NULLS FIRST, socioeconomic_status NULLS FIRST, smoking_intensity NULLS FIRST

question: Could you please gather all the movie details, including their titles, release years, languages, countries, genres, average ratings, latest reviews, watch counts, actors, and directors, and then categorize them into 'Top Rated Movie', 'Top Director', or 'Other' based on their average ratings and the directors' overall average ratings? Also, provide a summary of each movie including its title, year, director, average rating, actors, genres, watch count, and latest review. Limit the top directors to the top 5 with the highest average ratings.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH MovieDetails AS ( SELECT m.movie_id, m.title, m.release_year, m.language, m.country, GROUP_CONCAT(g.genre_name, ', ') AS genres, AVG(r.rating) AS average_rating, MAX(r.review) AS latest_review, COUNT(DISTINCT wh.watched_id) AS watch_count, GROUP_CONCAT(a.name, ', ') AS actors, d.name AS director_name FROM movies m LEFT JOIN movie_genres mg ON m.movie_id = mg.movie_id LEFT JOIN genres g ON mg.genre_id = g.genre_id LEFT JOIN ratings r ON m.movie_id = r.movie_id LEFT JOIN watched_history wh ON m.movie_id = wh.movie_id LEFT JOIN movie_actors ma ON m.movie_id = ma.movie_id LEFT JOIN actors a ON ma.actor_id = a.actor_id LEFT JOIN directors d ON m.director_id = d.director_id GROUP BY m.movie_id, m.title, m.release_year, m.language, m.country, d.name ), TopRatedMovies AS ( SELECT movie_id, MAX(average_rating) AS max_rating FROM MovieDetails GROUP BY movie_id ), TopDirectors AS ( SELECT director_name, AVG(average_rating) AS avg_director_rating FROM MovieDetails GROUP BY director_name ORDER BY avg_director_rating DESC LIMIT 5 ) SELECT MD.movie_id, MD.title, MD.release_year, MD.language, MD.country, MD.genres, MD.average_rating, MD.latest_review, MD.watch_count, MD.actors, MD.director_name, CASE WHEN MD.movie_id IN (SELECT movie_id FROM TopRatedMovies) THEN 'Top Rated Movie' WHEN MD.director_name IN (SELECT director_name FROM TopDirectors) THEN 'Top Director' ELSE 'Other' END AS movie_category, 'Title: ' || MD.title || ', Year: ' || MD.release_year || ', Director: ' || MD.director_name || ', Average Rating: ' || MD.average_rating || ', Actors: ' || MD.actors || ', Genres: ' || MD.genres || ', Watch Count: ' || MD.watch_count || ', Latest Review: ' || MD.latest_review AS summary FROM MovieDetails MD
gold_sql.mysql: WITH MovieDetails AS (SELECT m.movie_id, m.title, m.release_year, m.language, m.country, GROUP_CONCAT(g.genre_name SEPARATOR ', ') AS genres, AVG(r.rating) AS average_rating, MAX(r.review) AS latest_review, COUNT(DISTINCT wh.watched_id) AS watch_count, GROUP_CONCAT(a.name SEPARATOR ', ') AS actors, d.name AS director_name FROM movies AS m LEFT JOIN movie_genres AS mg ON m.movie_id = mg.movie_id LEFT JOIN genres AS g ON mg.genre_id = g.genre_id LEFT JOIN ratings AS r ON m.movie_id = r.movie_id LEFT JOIN watched_history AS wh ON m.movie_id = wh.movie_id LEFT JOIN movie_actors AS ma ON m.movie_id = ma.movie_id LEFT JOIN actors AS a ON ma.actor_id = a.actor_id LEFT JOIN directors AS d ON m.director_id = d.director_id GROUP BY m.movie_id, m.title, m.release_year, m.language, m.country, d.name), TopRatedMovies AS (SELECT movie_id, MAX(average_rating) AS max_rating FROM MovieDetails GROUP BY movie_id), TopDirectors AS (SELECT director_name, AVG(average_rating) AS avg_director_rating FROM MovieDetails GROUP BY director_name ORDER BY avg_director_rating DESC LIMIT 5) SELECT MD.movie_id, MD.title, MD.release_year, MD.language, MD.country, MD.genres, MD.average_rating, MD.latest_review, MD.watch_count, MD.actors, MD.director_name, CASE WHEN MD.movie_id IN (SELECT movie_id FROM TopRatedMovies) THEN 'Top Rated Movie' WHEN MD.director_name IN (SELECT director_name FROM TopDirectors) THEN 'Top Director' ELSE 'Other' END AS movie_category, CONCAT('Title: ', MD.title, ', Year: ', MD.release_year, ', Director: ', MD.director_name, ', Average Rating: ', MD.average_rating, ', Actors: ', MD.actors, ', Genres: ', MD.genres, ', Watch Count: ', MD.watch_count, ', Latest Review: ', MD.latest_review) AS summary FROM MovieDetails AS MD
gold_sql.postgres: WITH MovieDetails AS (SELECT m.movie_id, m.title, m.release_year, m.language, m.country, STRING_AGG(g.genre_name, ', ') AS genres, AVG(r.rating) AS average_rating, MAX(r.review) AS latest_review, COUNT(DISTINCT wh.watched_id) AS watch_count, STRING_AGG(a.name, ', ') AS actors, d.name AS director_name FROM movies AS m LEFT JOIN movie_genres AS mg ON m.movie_id = mg.movie_id LEFT JOIN genres AS g ON mg.genre_id = g.genre_id LEFT JOIN ratings AS r ON m.movie_id = r.movie_id LEFT JOIN watched_history AS wh ON m.movie_id = wh.movie_id LEFT JOIN movie_actors AS ma ON m.movie_id = ma.movie_id LEFT JOIN actors AS a ON ma.actor_id = a.actor_id LEFT JOIN directors AS d ON m.director_id = d.director_id GROUP BY m.movie_id, m.title, m.release_year, m.language, m.country, d.name), TopRatedMovies AS (SELECT movie_id, MAX(average_rating) AS max_rating FROM MovieDetails GROUP BY movie_id), TopDirectors AS (SELECT director_name, AVG(average_rating) AS avg_director_rating FROM MovieDetails GROUP BY director_name ORDER BY avg_director_rating DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 5) SELECT MD.movie_id, MD.title, MD.release_year, MD.language, MD.country, MD.genres, MD.average_rating, MD.latest_review, MD.watch_count, MD.actors, MD.director_name, CASE WHEN MD.movie_id IN (SELECT movie_id FROM TopRatedMovies) THEN 'Top Rated Movie' WHEN MD.director_name IN (SELECT director_name FROM TopDirectors) THEN 'Top Director' ELSE 'Other' END AS movie_category, 'Title: ' || MD.title || ', Year: ' || MD.release_year || ', Director: ' || MD.director_name || ', Average Rating: ' || MD.average_rating || ', Actors: ' || MD.actors || ', Genres: ' || MD.genres || ', Watch Count: ' || MD.watch_count || ', Latest Review: ' || MD.latest_review AS summary FROM MovieDetails AS MD

question: List all committees, including their names, total number of adopted resolutions, average drafts per adopted resolution, and the latest meeting date, ordered alphabetically by committee name.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT c.committee_name, COUNT(CASE WHEN r.status = 'Adopted' THEN r.resolution_id END) AS total_resolutions, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN r.status = 'Adopted' THEN r.draft_id END) * 1.0 / COUNT(CASE WHEN r.status = 'Adopted' THEN r.resolution_id END) AS avg_drafts_per_resolution, MAX(m.meeting_date) AS latest_meeting_date FROM committees c LEFT JOIN resolutions r ON c.committee_id = r.committee_id LEFT JOIN meeting_records m ON c.committee_id = m.committee_id GROUP BY c.committee_name, c.committee_id ORDER BY c.committee_name
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT c.committee_name, COUNT(CASE WHEN r.status = 'Adopted' THEN r.resolution_id END) AS total_resolutions, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN r.status = 'Adopted' THEN r.draft_id END) * 1.0 / COUNT(CASE WHEN r.status = 'Adopted' THEN r.resolution_id END) AS avg_drafts_per_resolution, MAX(m.meeting_date) AS latest_meeting_date FROM committees AS c LEFT JOIN resolutions AS r ON c.committee_id = r.committee_id LEFT JOIN meeting_records AS m ON c.committee_id = m.committee_id GROUP BY c.committee_name, c.committee_id ORDER BY c.committee_name
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT c.committee_name, COUNT(CASE WHEN r.status = 'Adopted' THEN r.resolution_id END) AS total_resolutions, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN r.status = 'Adopted' THEN r.draft_id END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(CASE WHEN r.status = 'Adopted' THEN r.resolution_id END), 0) AS avg_drafts_per_resolution, MAX(m.meeting_date) AS latest_meeting_date FROM committees AS c LEFT JOIN resolutions AS r ON c.committee_id = r.committee_id LEFT JOIN meeting_records AS m ON c.committee_id = m.committee_id GROUP BY c.committee_name, c.committee_id ORDER BY c.committee_name NULLS FIRST

question: Could you please identify the subsector that had the highest economic value in the year 2011-12 and provide its name?

- the names and total quantities sold of the top three selling products,

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ProductPerformance AS ( SELECT oi.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM order_items oi INNER JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY oi.product_id, p.product_name ), TopSellingProducts AS ( SELECT product_name, total_quantity_sold FROM ProductPerformance ORDER BY total_quantity_sold DESC LIMIT 3 ), BottomSellingProducts AS ( SELECT product_name, total_quantity_sold FROM ProductPerformance ORDER BY total_quantity_sold ASC LIMIT 3 ), LowStockProducts AS ( SELECT p.product_name, s.size_category, i.stock_quantity FROM inventory i INNER JOIN products p ON i.product_id = p.product_id INNER JOIN sizes s ON i.size_id = s.size_id WHERE i.low_stock_alert = 1 ), CustomerSpending AS ( SELECT c.first_name, c.last_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c INNER JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 5 ), MonthlySales AS ( SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', o.order_date) AS month, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM orders o GROUP BY month ORDER BY month ) SELECT 'Top Selling Products' AS category, product_name, total_quantity_sold FROM TopSellingProducts UNION ALL SELECT 'Bottom Selling Products' AS category, product_name, total_quantity_sold FROM BottomSellingProducts UNION ALL SELECT 'Low Stock Products' AS category, product_name || ' - ' || size_category AS product_size, stock_quantity FROM LowStockProducts UNION ALL SELECT 'Top Spending Customers' AS category, first_name || ' ' || last_name AS customer_name, total_spent FROM CustomerSpending UNION ALL SELECT 'Monthly Sales' AS category, month, total_sales FROM MonthlySales

question: Gather the titles of all videos that have blossomed into a garden of comments, along with the bouquet of tags that describe them and the count of their blooming comments.
external_knowledge: "blossomed into a garden of comments" refers to videos that have received at least one comment; "bouquet of tags" refers to the concatenated list of tags associated with each video.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT v.title, GROUP_CONCAT(vt.tag_name) AS bouquet_of_tags, COUNT(c.comment_id) AS total_comments FROM videos v JOIN video_tags vt ON v.video_id = vt.video_id LEFT JOIN comments c ON v.video_id = c.video_id GROUP BY v.video_id, v.title HAVING COUNT(c.comment_id) > 0
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT v.title, GROUP_CONCAT(vt.tag_name SEPARATOR ',') AS bouquet_of_tags, COUNT(c.comment_id) AS total_comments FROM videos AS v JOIN video_tags AS vt ON v.video_id = vt.video_id LEFT JOIN comments AS c ON v.video_id = c.video_id GROUP BY v.video_id, v.title HAVING COUNT(c.comment_id) > 0
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT v.title, STRING_AGG(vt.tag_name, ',') AS bouquet_of_tags, COUNT(c.comment_id) AS total_comments FROM videos AS v JOIN video_tags AS vt ON v.video_id = vt.video_id LEFT JOIN comments AS c ON v.video_id = c.video_id GROUP BY v.video_id, v.title HAVING COUNT(c.comment_id) > 0

question:
**User**: I want to evaluate the performance of our drivers.
**Assistant**: What kind of performance metrics are you interested in?
**User**: I would like to know the total orders they've completed, how many were delivered on time, and how many were delayed.
**Assistant**: That's a good start. What about customer feedback? Should that be included in the evaluation?
**User**: Yes, please include the average customer feedback ratings for each driver.
**Assistant**: How would you like to rank the drivers' performance? Is it based solely on the percentage of on-time deliveries?
**User**: No, consider the total orders and average feedback ratings as well.
**Assistant**: Should the drivers be ranked in descending order of their on-time delivery percentages, and then by total orders, and finally by average feedback ratings?
**User**: Yes, that sounds correct.
**Assistant**: One last thing, would you like to see the driver names along with their performance metrics?
**User**: Yes, please include their names.
**Assistant**: Alright, I'll help you translate your request into an SQL query.
**Assistant**: Just to confirm, you want me to generate a report that lists all the drivers, their total orders, on-time deliveries, delayed deliveries, average customer feedback ratings, and an overall performance ranking, right?
**User**: Yes, that's correct.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH DriverPerformance AS ( SELECT d.driver_id, d.driver_name, COUNT(dl.log_id) AS total_orders, SUM(CASE WHEN dl.delivery_time <= o.committed_completion_time THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS on_time_deliveries, SUM(CASE WHEN dl.delivery_time > o.committed_completion_time THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS delayed_deliveries, AVG(cf.rating) AS average_feedback, (SUM(CASE WHEN dl.delivery_time <= o.committed_completion_time THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(dl.log_id)) AS on_time_percentage FROM drivers d LEFT JOIN order_assignments oa ON d.driver_id = oa.driver_id LEFT JOIN delivery_logs dl ON oa.order_id = dl.order_id LEFT JOIN orders o ON dl.order_id = o.order_id LEFT JOIN customer_feedback cf ON dl.order_id = cf.order_id GROUP BY d.driver_id, d.driver_name ) SELECT driver_name, total_orders, on_time_deliveries, delayed_deliveries, average_feedback, on_time_percentage, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY on_time_percentage DESC, total_orders DESC, average_feedback DESC) AS performance_rank FROM DriverPerformance ORDER BY performance_rank
gold_sql.mysql: WITH DriverPerformance AS (SELECT d.driver_id, d.driver_name, COUNT(dl.log_id) AS total_orders, SUM(CASE WHEN dl.delivery_time <= o.committed_completion_time THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS on_time_deliveries, SUM(CASE WHEN dl.delivery_time > o.committed_completion_time THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS delayed_deliveries, AVG(cf.rating) AS average_feedback, (SUM(CASE WHEN dl.delivery_time <= o.committed_completion_time THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(dl.log_id)) AS on_time_percentage FROM drivers AS d LEFT JOIN order_assignments AS oa ON d.driver_id = oa.driver_id LEFT JOIN delivery_logs AS dl ON oa.order_id = dl.order_id LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON dl.order_id = o.order_id LEFT JOIN customer_feedback AS cf ON dl.order_id = cf.order_id GROUP BY d.driver_id, d.driver_name) SELECT driver_name, total_orders, on_time_deliveries, delayed_deliveries, average_feedback, on_time_percentage, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY on_time_percentage DESC, total_orders DESC, average_feedback DESC) AS performance_rank FROM DriverPerformance ORDER BY performance_rank
gold_sql.postgres: WITH DriverPerformance AS (SELECT d.driver_id, d.driver_name, COUNT(dl.log_id) AS total_orders, SUM(CASE WHEN dl.delivery_time <= o.committed_completion_time THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS on_time_deliveries, SUM(CASE WHEN dl.delivery_time > o.committed_completion_time THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS delayed_deliveries, AVG(cf.rating) AS average_feedback, (SUM(CASE WHEN dl.delivery_time <= o.committed_completion_time THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(dl.log_id), 0)) AS on_time_percentage FROM drivers AS d LEFT JOIN order_assignments AS oa ON d.driver_id = oa.driver_id LEFT JOIN delivery_logs AS dl ON oa.order_id = dl.order_id LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON dl.order_id = o.order_id LEFT JOIN customer_feedback AS cf ON dl.order_id = cf.order_id GROUP BY d.driver_id, d.driver_name) SELECT driver_name, total_orders, on_time_deliveries, delayed_deliveries, average_feedback, on_time_percentage, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY on_time_percentage DESC NULLS LAST, total_orders DESC NULLS LAST, average_feedback DESC NULLS LAST) AS performance_rank FROM DriverPerformance ORDER BY performance_rank NULLS FIRST

question: Return each customer's name, the total number of accounts, total balance, total transactions, average balance per account, and total alerts.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT c.customer_name, COUNT(ac.account_id) AS total_accounts, SUM(CAST(REPLACE(trim(ac.balance, '$'), ',', '') AS REAL)) AS total_balance, COUNT(t.transaction_id) AS total_transactions, AVG(CAST(REPLACE(trim(ac.balance, '$'), ',', '') AS REAL)) AS average_balance_per_account, COUNT(aa.alert_id) AS total_alerts FROM customers AS c LEFT JOIN accounts AS ac ON ac.customer_id = c.customer_id LEFT JOIN transactions AS t ON t.account_id = ac.account_id LEFT JOIN account_alerts AS aa ON aa.account_id = ac.account_id GROUP BY c.customer_name

question: Could you provide a summary of the total amount spent, the total number of items ordered, and the average price of orders for each customer, including details of the products they ordered?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH OrderSummary AS ( SELECT o.customer_id, o.order_id, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)) AS total_order_amount, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_items, AVG(oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)) AS average_order_price FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY o.customer_id, o.order_id ), ProductDetails AS ( SELECT oi.order_id, p.product_id, p.name AS product_name, p.price AS product_price, p.abv AS product_abv, p.size AS product_size FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id ) SELECT os.customer_id, c.customer_name, SUM(os.total_order_amount) AS total_spent, SUM(os.total_items) AS total_items, AVG(os.average_order_price) AS avg_order_price, GROUP_CONCAT(pd.product_name) AS products_ordered FROM OrderSummary os JOIN customers c ON os.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN ProductDetails pd ON os.order_id = pd.order_id GROUP BY os.customer_id, c.customer_name ORDER BY os.customer_id
gold_sql.mysql: WITH OrderSummary AS (SELECT o.customer_id, o.order_id, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)) AS total_order_amount, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_items, AVG(oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)) AS average_order_price FROM orders AS o JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY o.customer_id, o.order_id), ProductDetails AS (SELECT oi.order_id, p.product_id, p.name AS product_name, p.price AS product_price, p.abv AS product_abv, p.size AS product_size FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id) SELECT os.customer_id, c.customer_name, SUM(os.total_order_amount) AS total_spent, SUM(os.total_items) AS total_items, AVG(os.average_order_price) AS avg_order_price, GROUP_CONCAT(pd.product_name SEPARATOR ',') AS products_ordered FROM OrderSummary AS os JOIN customers AS c ON os.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN ProductDetails AS pd ON os.order_id = pd.order_id GROUP BY os.customer_id, c.customer_name ORDER BY os.customer_id
gold_sql.postgres: WITH OrderSummary AS (SELECT o.customer_id, o.order_id, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)) AS total_order_amount, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_items, AVG(oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)) AS average_order_price FROM orders AS o JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY o.customer_id, o.order_id), ProductDetails AS (SELECT oi.order_id, p.product_id, p.name AS product_name, p.price AS product_price, p.abv AS product_abv, p.size AS product_size FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id) SELECT os.customer_id, c.customer_name, SUM(os.total_order_amount) AS total_spent, SUM(os.total_items) AS total_items, AVG(os.average_order_price) AS avg_order_price, STRING_AGG(pd.product_name, ',') AS products_ordered FROM OrderSummary AS os JOIN customers AS c ON os.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN ProductDetails AS pd ON os.order_id = pd.order_id GROUP BY os.customer_id, c.customer_name ORDER BY os.customer_id NULLS FIRST
