question: I want to know the concept ID, English description, Concepticon gloss, translations, access level, notes, note authors, and creation dates for each concept in the studies. Additionally, I would like to see the number of users with admin access for each study, all ordered by the concept ID.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH Translations AS ( SELECT concept_id, GROUP_CONCAT(translation, ', ') AS translations FROM concept_translations GROUP BY concept_id ), AdminCounts AS ( SELECT study_id, COUNT(*) AS admin_count FROM user_study_access WHERE access_level = 'admin' GROUP BY study_id ) SELECT c.concept_id, c.english AS concept_english, c.concepticon_gloss, IFNULL(t.translations, '') AS translations, ua.access_level, sn.note, sn.created_by AS note_author, sn.created_date, ac.admin_count FROM concepts c LEFT JOIN Translations t ON c.concept_id = t.concept_id LEFT JOIN user_study_access ua ON c.study_id = ua.study_id LEFT JOIN study_notes sn ON c.study_id = sn.study_id LEFT JOIN AdminCounts ac ON c.study_id = ac.study_id ORDER BY c.concept_id
gold_sql.mysql: WITH Translations AS (SELECT concept_id, GROUP_CONCAT(translation SEPARATOR ', ') AS translations FROM concept_translations GROUP BY concept_id), AdminCounts AS (SELECT study_id, COUNT(*) AS admin_count FROM user_study_access WHERE access_level = 'admin' GROUP BY study_id) SELECT c.concept_id, c.english AS concept_english, c.concepticon_gloss, COALESCE(t.translations, '') AS translations, ua.access_level, sn.note, sn.created_by AS note_author, sn.created_date, ac.admin_count FROM concepts AS c LEFT JOIN Translations AS t ON c.concept_id = t.concept_id LEFT JOIN user_study_access AS ua ON c.study_id = ua.study_id LEFT JOIN study_notes AS sn ON c.study_id = sn.study_id LEFT JOIN AdminCounts AS ac ON c.study_id = ac.study_id ORDER BY c.concept_id
gold_sql.postgres: WITH Translations AS (SELECT concept_id, STRING_AGG(translation, ', ') AS translations FROM concept_translations GROUP BY concept_id), AdminCounts AS (SELECT study_id, COUNT(*) AS admin_count FROM user_study_access WHERE access_level = 'admin' GROUP BY study_id) SELECT c.concept_id, c.english AS concept_english, c.concepticon_gloss, COALESCE(t.translations, '') AS translations, ua.access_level, sn.note, sn.created_by AS note_author, sn.created_date, ac.admin_count FROM concepts AS c LEFT JOIN Translations AS t ON c.concept_id = t.concept_id LEFT JOIN user_study_access AS ua ON c.study_id = ua.study_id LEFT JOIN study_notes AS sn ON c.study_id = sn.study_id LEFT JOIN AdminCounts AS ac ON c.study_id = ac.study_id ORDER BY c.concept_id NULLS FIRST

question:
**User**: I want to get a summary of all the teams that won championships.
**Assistant**: What specific details about these teams would you like to know?
**User**: I'd like to know their names, how many championships they've won, their total wins, the equipment they used, and any feedback from participants.
**Assistant**: Would you also like to include information about the events they participated in and won?
**User**: Yes, that would be helpful. And can you summarize all this information in a single string for each team?
**Assistant**: I'll combine all the relevant data into a single string that includes the team's ID, name, championships won, total wins, equipment details, and participant feedback. Is there anything else you'd like me to include or filter by?
**User**: No, that sounds perfect. Please go ahead and prepare the query.
**Assistant**: Alright, I've prepared the query. It will provide a comprehensive summary of the winning teams, including their performance statistics and participant feedback.
**User**: Great, let me see the results.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH WinningTeams AS ( SELECT c.team_id, t.team_name, c.year FROM championships c INNER JOIN teams t ON c.team_id = t.team_id ), TeamStats AS ( SELECT wt.team_id, wt.team_name, COUNT(wt.year) AS championships_won, SUM(d.wins) AS total_wins FROM WinningTeams wt INNER JOIN drivers d ON d.team_id = wt.team_id GROUP BY wt.team_id, wt.team_name ), EquipmentDetails AS ( SELECT es.team_id, es.equipment_type, es.specification, es.supplier FROM equipment_specs es WHERE es.team_id IN (SELECT team_id FROM WinningTeams) ), Feedback AS ( SELECT ef.event_id, p.name AS participant_name, ef.rating, ef.comments FROM event_feedback ef INNER JOIN participants p ON ef.participant_id = p.participant_id WHERE ef.event_id IN (SELECT event_id FROM WinningTeams) ) SELECT GROUP_CONCAT( CAST(TS.team_id AS TEXT) || ', ' || TS.team_name || ', won ' || CAST(TS.championships_won AS TEXT) || ' championships, with ' || CAST(TS.total_wins AS TEXT) || ' total wins, using ' || ED.equipment_type || ' (' || ED.specification || ') from ' || ED.supplier || ', received feedback rating: ' || FB.rating || ', comments: ' || FB.comments ) AS team_performance_summary FROM TeamStats TS LEFT JOIN EquipmentDetails ED ON TS.team_id = ED.team_id LEFT JOIN Feedback FB ON FB.event_id IN (SELECT event_id FROM WinningTeams WHERE team_id = TS.team_id) GROUP BY TS.team_id

question: Return the device names, configuration names, version names, version numbers, users who last modified the configurations, and creation dates for the latest version of each device configuration, along with their corresponding settings, ordered by device name and version creation date in descending order.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH DeviceConfigurations AS ( SELECT d.device_name, c.config_name, v.version_name, v.version_number, u.user_name AS last_modified_by, v.created_date AS version_created_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY d.device_id ORDER BY v.created_date DESC) AS rn FROM devices d JOIN configurations c ON d.device_id = c.device_id JOIN versions v ON c.version_id = v.version_id JOIN users u ON v.created_by = u.user_id ), FilteredConfigurations AS ( SELECT device_name, config_name, version_name, version_number, last_modified_by, version_created_date FROM DeviceConfigurations WHERE rn = 1 ) SELECT f.device_name, f.config_name, f.version_name, f.version_number, f.last_modified_by, f.version_created_date, GROUP_CONCAT(s.setting_name || ' (' || s.value || ')') AS settings FROM FilteredConfigurations f JOIN settings s ON s.device_id = (SELECT device_id FROM devices WHERE device_name = f.device_name) GROUP BY f.device_name, f.config_name, f.version_name, f.version_number, f.last_modified_by, f.version_created_date ORDER BY f.device_name, f.version_created_date DESC

question: Which neighbourhood has the highest total sales value, and what are the details of the average price per square foot, the list of buyers, their preferred neighbourhoods, and the average property value in that neighbourhood?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH NeighbourhoodSales AS ( SELECT n.neighbourhood_name, s.sale_price, h.average_sqft, b.buyer_name, b.preferred_neighbourhoods FROM sales s JOIN agent_listings al ON s.listing_id = al.listing_id JOIN neighbourhoods n ON al.listing_id = n.neighbourhood_id JOIN house_types h ON al.listing_id = h.house_type_id JOIN buyers b ON s.buyer_id = b.buyer_id ), NeighbourhoodSalesAggregations AS ( SELECT neighbourhood_name, SUM(sale_price) AS total_sales_value, AVG(sale_price / average_sqft) AS avg_price_per_sqft, GROUP_CONCAT(buyer_name) AS buyers, GROUP_CONCAT(preferred_neighbourhoods) AS preferred_neighbourhoods FROM NeighbourhoodSales GROUP BY neighbourhood_name ), TopNeighbourhood AS ( SELECT neighbourhood_name, total_sales_value, avg_price_per_sqft, buyers, preferred_neighbourhoods FROM NeighbourhoodSalesAggregations ORDER BY total_sales_value DESC LIMIT 1 ) SELECT tn.neighbourhood_name, tn.total_sales_value, tn.avg_price_per_sqft, tn.buyers, tn.preferred_neighbourhoods, n.average_property_value AS neighbourhood_avg_property_value FROM TopNeighbourhood tn JOIN neighbourhoods n ON tn.neighbourhood_name = n.neighbourhood_name

question: Hey! Could you show me the top 5 most cited papers across all databases? I'd love to know their titles, publication years, the number of times they've been cited, their authors, the publications they were featured in, and the number of databases they've been cited in, all ordered by the number of citations in descending order?

question:
**User**: I want to get some statistics on burglary offenses.
**Assistant**: Sure, what specific information are you looking for?
**User**: I want to know the subcategories of burglary offenses and the demographic groups involved.
**Assistant**: Got it. Do you want to see the total number of offenses for each subcategory as well?
**User**: Yes, that would be helpful.
**Assistant**: Alright. To clarify, you want to see the subcategories of burglary offenses, the demographic details (gender, ethnicity, age group, and income level) of the groups involved, and the total number of offenses for each subcategory. Is that correct?

question: What are the names of users, their frequency of accessing mutation data, and the details of the mutations they accessed, specifically those related to the antibiotic ofloxacin?
external_knowledge: Ofloxacin is a type of antibiotic; 'mutation data' refers to the information stored in the 'mutations' table, specifically the 'mutation_details' column; 'accessing mutation data' implies the events logged in the 'access_logs' table.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT u.user_name, COUNT(DISTINCT a.access_id) AS number_of_accesses, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT m.mutation_details) AS mutation_details FROM users u INNER JOIN access_logs a ON u.user_id = a.user_id INNER JOIN mutations m ON a.mutation_id = m.mutation_id INNER JOIN antibiotics ab ON a.antibiotic_id = ab.antibiotic_id WHERE ab.antibiotic_name = 'ofloxacin' GROUP BY u.user_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.access_id) > 0
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT u.user_name, COUNT(DISTINCT a.access_id) AS number_of_accesses, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT m.mutation_details SEPARATOR ',') AS mutation_details FROM users AS u INNER JOIN access_logs AS a ON u.user_id = a.user_id INNER JOIN mutations AS m ON a.mutation_id = m.mutation_id INNER JOIN antibiotics AS ab ON a.antibiotic_id = ab.antibiotic_id WHERE ab.antibiotic_name = 'ofloxacin' GROUP BY u.user_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.access_id) > 0

question: Could you show me a list of all rules, including their IDs, box names, names, event types, event subjects, event objects, priorities, condition expressions, hierarchy levels, and paths? I'd also like to see the total rule count and average priority for each box, the total rule count and average priority for each event type, and a cumulative count of rules for each box, ordered by box name, hierarchy level, and rule ID?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RECURSIVE RuleHierarchy AS ( SELECT r.rule_id, r.box_name, r.event_type, r.event_subject, r.event_object, r.priority, r.condition_expression, 1 AS level, CAST(r.rule_id AS TEXT) AS hierarchy_path FROM rules r WHERE r.condition_expression NOT LIKE '%rule_id =%' UNION ALL SELECT rr.rule_id, rr.box_name, rr.event_type, rr.event_subject, rr.event_object, rr.priority, rr.condition_expression, rh.level + 1, rh.hierarchy_path || ' -> ' || CAST(rr.rule_id AS TEXT) FROM rules rr INNER JOIN RuleHierarchy rh ON rr.condition_expression LIKE '%rule_id = ' || CAST(rh.rule_id AS TEXT) || '%' ), RuleStats AS ( SELECT rh.box_name, AVG(rh.priority) AS average_priority, COUNT(*) AS rule_count FROM RuleHierarchy rh GROUP BY rh.box_name ), EventStats AS ( SELECT rh.event_type, COUNT(*) AS rule_count, AVG(rh.priority) AS average_priority FROM RuleHierarchy rh GROUP BY rh.event_type ), FinalStats AS ( SELECT r.rule_id, r.box_name, r.name, r.event_type, r.event_subject, r.event_object, r.priority, r.condition_expression, rh.level, rh.hierarchy_path, rs.rule_count AS box_rule_count, rs.average_priority AS box_avg_priority, es.rule_count AS event_type_rule_count, es.average_priority AS event_type_avg_priority FROM rules r INNER JOIN RuleHierarchy rh ON r.rule_id = rh.rule_id LEFT JOIN RuleStats rs ON r.box_name = rs.box_name LEFT JOIN EventStats es ON r.event_type = es.event_type ) SELECT fs.rule_id, fs.box_name, fs.name, fs.event_type, fs.event_subject, fs.event_object, fs.priority, fs.condition_expression, fs.level, fs.hierarchy_path, fs.box_rule_count, fs.box_avg_priority, fs.event_type_rule_count, fs.event_type_avg_priority, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY fs.box_name ORDER BY fs.level, fs.rule_id) AS cumulative_rule_count FROM FinalStats fs ORDER BY fs.box_name, fs.level, fs.rule_id

question: Find the titles of the top 5 papers with the most citations, including the number of citations and the names of the databases in which they are cited, ranked in descending order of citation count.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH CitationsAndDatabases AS ( SELECT p.paper_id, p.title, COUNT(c.citation_id) AS total_citations, GROUP_CONCAT(d.database_name) AS cited_in_databases FROM papers p JOIN citations c ON p.paper_id = c.paper_id JOIN paper_databases pd ON p.paper_id = pd.paper_id JOIN databases d ON pd.database_id = d.database_id GROUP BY p.paper_id, p.title ), RankedPapers AS ( SELECT paper_id, title, total_citations, cited_in_databases, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total_citations DESC) AS citation_rank FROM CitationsAndDatabases ) SELECT title || ' (' || total_citations || ' citations in ' || cited_in_databases || ')' AS result FROM RankedPapers WHERE citation_rank <= 5 ORDER BY citation_rank

question: For Atlanta airport in January 2022, return the airport code, delay reason names, total delays, and average delay minutes for each delay reason, considering only delay reasons with at least one delay.

question: What are the task names, average energy consumption, task counts, robot models, arm names, and user names for the tasks with the highest energy consumption for each task type, considering only tasks that were completed in the year 2023?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH TaskEnergyCTE AS ( SELECT tp.task_type_id, tp.energy_consumption, tp.output_quality, rm.model_name AS robot_model, ra.arm_name, rt.task_name, u.user_name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY tp.task_type_id ORDER BY tp.energy_consumption DESC) AS energy_rank FROM tasks_performed tp INNER JOIN robot_arms ra ON tp.arm_id = ra.arm_id INNER JOIN robots r ON ra.robot_id = r.robot_id INNER JOIN robot_models rm ON r.model_id = rm.model_id INNER JOIN robot_tasks rt ON tp.task_type_id = rt.task_id INNER JOIN users u ON tp.user_id = u.user_id WHERE tp.status = 'completed' AND strftime('%Y', tp.start_time) = '2023' ), AverageEnergyCTE AS ( SELECT task_type_id, AVG(energy_consumption) AS avg_energy_consumption, COUNT(task_type_id) AS task_count FROM TaskEnergyCTE GROUP BY task_type_id ) SELECT te.task_name, ae.avg_energy_consumption, ae.task_count, te.robot_model, te.arm_name, te.user_name FROM AverageEnergyCTE ae INNER JOIN TaskEnergyCTE te ON ae.task_type_id = te.task_type_id WHERE te.energy_rank = 1

gold_sql.postgres: WITH TaskEnergyCTE AS (SELECT tp.task_type_id, tp.energy_consumption, tp.output_quality, rm.model_name AS robot_model, ra.arm_name, rt.task_name, u.user_name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY tp.task_type_id ORDER BY tp.energy_consumption DESC NULLS LAST) AS energy_rank FROM tasks_performed AS tp INNER JOIN robot_arms AS ra ON tp.arm_id = ra.arm_id INNER JOIN robots AS r ON ra.robot_id = r.robot_id INNER JOIN robot_models AS rm ON r.model_id = rm.model_id INNER JOIN robot_tasks AS rt ON tp.task_type_id = rt.task_id INNER JOIN users AS u ON tp.user_id = u.user_id WHERE tp.status = 'completed' AND TO_CHAR(CAST(tp.start_time AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY') = '2023'), AverageEnergyCTE AS (SELECT task_type_id, AVG(energy_consumption) AS avg_energy_consumption, COUNT(task_type_id) AS task_count FROM TaskEnergyCTE GROUP BY task_type_id) SELECT te.task_name, ae.avg_energy_consumption, ae.task_count, te.robot_model, te.arm_name, te.user_name FROM AverageEnergyCTE AS ae INNER JOIN TaskEnergyCTE AS te ON ae.task_type_id = te.task_type_id WHERE te.energy_rank = 1

question: Could you tell me, for each month, how many total orders were placed and what the total sales were, considering the quantity, unit price, and discount applied to each order item?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', o.order_date) AS order_month, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)) AS total_sales FROM orders o INNER JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY order_month ORDER BY order_month
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME), '%Y-%m') AS order_month, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)) AS total_sales FROM orders AS o INNER JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY order_month ORDER BY order_month
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT TO_CHAR(CAST(o.order_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY-MM') AS order_month, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)) AS total_sales FROM orders AS o INNER JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY order_month ORDER BY order_month NULLS FIRST

total_investment, SUM(e.annual_revenue) AS total_annual_revenue FROM enterprises e GROUP BY e.district_id, e.campaign_id ), CampaignJlgFormation AS ( SELECT jf.campaign_id, COUNT(jf.jlg_id) AS question: Find the season-by-season performance of World Series teams, including their cumulative wins and losses, along with details of each game, such as game date, location, umpire, and version information, in chronological order.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH TeamPerformance AS ( SELECT ws.team_id_winner AS team_id, ws.wins, ws.losses, ws.year_id, t.city, t.state, y.year AS season_year, 'Win' AS result FROM world_series ws INNER JOIN teams t ON ws.team_id_winner = t.team_id INNER JOIN years y ON ws.year_id = y.year_id UNION ALL SELECT ws.team_id_loser AS team_id, ws.losses AS wins, ws.wins AS losses, ws.year_id, t.city, t.state, y.year AS season_year, 'Loss' AS result FROM world_series ws INNER JOIN teams t ON ws.team_id_loser = t.team_id INNER JOIN years y ON ws.year_id = y.year_id ), CumulativePerformance AS ( SELECT team_id, season_year, SUM(wins) OVER (PARTITION BY team_id ORDER BY season_year) AS cumulative_wins, SUM(losses) OVER (PARTITION BY team_id ORDER BY season_year) AS cumulative_losses FROM TeamPerformance ), GameDetails AS ( SELECT ws.game_id, ws.game_date, ws.game_location, u.umpire_name, dv.version_number, dv.update_date, dv.description FROM world_series ws INNER JOIN umpires u ON ws.umpire_id = u.umpire_id INNER JOIN data_versions dv ON ws.year_id = dv.version_id ), FullAnalysis AS ( SELECT cp.season_year, cp.team_id, cp.cumulative_wins, cp.cumulative_losses, tp.city, tp.state, gd.game_date, gd.game_location, gd.umpire_name, gd.version_number, gd.update_date, gd.description FROM CumulativePerformance cp INNER JOIN TeamPerformance tp ON cp.team_id = tp.team_id AND cp.season_year = tp.season_year INNER JOIN GameDetails gd ON gd.game_date BETWEEN cp.season_year || '-01-01' AND cp.season_year || '-12-31' ) SELECT season_year, team_id, city, state, cumulative_wins, cumulative_losses, game_date, game_location, umpire_name, version_number, update_date, description FROM FullAnalysis ORDER BY season_year, team_id, game_date

question: Could you provide a detailed overview of all machine learning models, including their names, algorithms, descriptions, owners' names and emails, associated dataset names and descriptions, dataset sizes, split ratios, cross-validation scores, holdout scores, ROC AUC scores, training and evaluation times, hyperparameters, and comments, ordered alphabetically by model name?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ModelBaseInfo AS ( SELECT m.model_id, m.name AS model_name, m.algorithm, m.description AS model_desc, mo.user_id, u.name AS owner_name, u.email AS owner_email FROM models m INNER JOIN model_ownership mo ON m.model_id = mo.model_id INNER JOIN users u ON mo.user_id = u.user_id WHERE mo.ownership_type = 'owner' ), ModelData AS ( SELECT mb.model_id, mb.model_name, mb.algorithm, mb.model_desc, mb.owner_name, mb.owner_email, ds.dataset_id, ds.name AS dataset_name, ds.description AS dataset_desc, ds.size AS dataset_size, md.split_ratio FROM ModelBaseInfo mb INNER JOIN model_dataset md ON mb.model_id = md.model_id INNER JOIN datasets ds ON md.dataset_id = ds.dataset_id ), ModelPerformance AS ( SELECT mp.model_id, mp.cv_score, mp.holdout_score, mp.holdout_roc_auc_score, mp.training_time, mp.evaluation_time FROM model_performance mp ), ModelHyperparameters AS ( SELECT mh.model_id, GROUP_CONCAT(hp.name || '=' || hp.value, ', ') AS hyperparameters FROM models mh INNER JOIN hyperparameters hp ON mh.model_id = hp.model_id GROUP BY mh.model_id ), ModelComments AS ( SELECT mc.model_id, GROUP_CONCAT(mc.comment, ' | ') AS comments FROM model_comments mc GROUP BY mc.model_id ) SELECT md.model_id, md.model_name, md.algorithm, md.model_desc, md.owner_name, md.owner_email, md.dataset_name, md.dataset_desc, md.dataset_size, md.split_ratio, mp.cv_score, mp.holdout_score, mp.holdout_roc_auc_score, mp.training_time, mp.evaluation_time, mh.hyperparameters, mc.comments FROM ModelData md LEFT JOIN ModelPerformance mp ON md.model_id = mp.model_id LEFT JOIN ModelHyperparameters mh ON md.model_id = mh.model_id LEFT JOIN ModelComments mc ON md.model_id = mc.model_id ORDER BY md.model_name

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH CompanyRevenue AS ( SELECT r.company_id, r.year, r.quarter, SUM(r.revenue) AS total_revenue FROM revenue_distribution r WHERE r.year >= 2018 GROUP BY r.company_id, r.year, r.quarter ), CompanyHistory AS ( SELECT h.company_id, h.date, h.mkt_cap, h.ind_rev, h.percent_tot_rev, h.quarter FROM historical_data h WHERE h.date >= '2018-01-01' ), AccessCount AS ( SELECT a.company_id, COUNT(a.access_id) AS access_count FROM access_logs a WHERE a.access_date >= '2018-01-01' GROUP BY a.company_id ) SELECT c.company_id, c.company_name, c.ticker, c.ceo_name, c.headquarters_location, c.founded_year, c.website, COALESCE(i.industry_name, 'Unknown') AS industry_name, cr.year, cr.quarter, cr.total_revenue, ch.mkt_cap, ch.ind_rev, ch.percent_tot_rev, ac.access_count FROM companies c JOIN company_industries ci ON c.company_id = ci.company_id AND ci.primary_classification = 1 LEFT JOIN industries i ON ci.industry_id = i.industry_id AND i.active_status = 1 LEFT JOIN CompanyRevenue cr ON c.company_id = cr.company_id LEFT JOIN CompanyHistory ch ON c.company_id = ch.company_id AND cr.year = CAST(strftime('%Y', ch.date) AS INTEGER) AND cr.quarter = ch.quarter LEFT JOIN AccessCount ac ON c.company_id = ac.company_id WHERE c.active_status = 1 ORDER BY c.company_id, cr.year, cr.quarter

question: What are the titles, average ratings, numbers of reviews, numbers of awards, and directors of the top 5 movies with the highest average ratings that are 4 or above?
external_knowledge: A high average rating (e.g., 4 or 5 out of 5) typically indicates a well-received movie among audiences and critics; Awards are often a measure of a movie's quality and impact in the film industry.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH MovieRatings AS ( SELECT r.movie_id, AVG(r.rating) AS avg_rating, COUNT(r.review_id) AS num_reviews FROM reviews r GROUP BY r.movie_id ), MovieAwards AS ( SELECT m.movie_id, COUNT(a.award_id) AS num_awards FROM movies m LEFT JOIN awards a ON m.movie_id = a.movie_id GROUP BY m.movie_id ), MovieDirectors AS ( SELECT md.movie_id, GROUP_CONCAT(d.name, ', ') AS director_names FROM movie_directors md JOIN directors d ON md.director_id = d.director_id GROUP BY md.movie_id ), TopRatedMovies AS ( SELECT m.movie_id, m.title, mr.avg_rating, mr.num_reviews, COALESCE(ma.num_awards, 0) AS num_awards FROM movies m JOIN MovieRatings mr ON m.movie_id = mr.movie_id LEFT JOIN MovieAwards ma ON m.movie_id = ma.movie_id WHERE mr.avg_rating >= 4 ORDER BY mr.avg_rating DESC LIMIT 5 ) SELECT trm.title AS Title, ROUND(trm.avg_rating, 2) AS "Average Rating", trm.num_reviews AS "Number of Reviews", trm.num_awards AS "Number of Awards", COALESCE(md.director_names, 'Unknown') AS Directors FROM TopRatedMovies trm LEFT JOIN MovieDirectors md ON trm.movie_id = md.movie_id

question: Which marketing campaigns are most effective, considering their engagement rates, sales performance, and the strength of their item recommendations, and rank them from highest to lowest effectiveness?
external_knowledge: Campaign effectiveness refers to how well a marketing campaign achieves its intended goals, such as increasing sales or customer engagement. Engagement rate is a measure of how actively engaged customers are with a campaign, usually calculated as the number of engaged customers divided by the total number of customers. Sales performance is often measured by total sales and transaction count. The strength of item recommendations can be evaluated using association rules, which are rules that describe the relationship between different items, and are often characterized by metrics such as confidence and lift.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH CampaignEngagement AS ( SELECT c.campaign_id, COUNT(cc.customer_id) AS total_customers, SUM(CASE WHEN cc.engagement_status = 'engaged' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS engaged_customers, SUM(CASE WHEN cc.engagement_status = 'engaged' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(cc.customer_id) AS engagement_rate FROM marketing_campaigns c LEFT JOIN campaign_customers cc ON c.campaign_id = cc.campaign_id GROUP BY c.campaign_id ), SalesPerformance AS ( SELECT ci.campaign_id, SUM(ti.quantity * ti.item_price) AS total_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT ti.transaction_id) AS transaction_count FROM campaign_items ci LEFT JOIN transaction_items ti ON ci.item_id = ti.item_id GROUP BY ci.campaign_id ), ItemRecommendations AS ( SELECT c.campaign_id, AVG(a.confidence) AS avg_recommendation_confidence, AVG(a.lift) AS avg_recommendation_lift, AVG(a.rule_strength) AS avg_recommendation_strength FROM marketing_campaigns c LEFT JOIN campaign_items ci ON c.campaign_id = ci.campaign_id LEFT JOIN association_rules a ON a.antecedent_items LIKE '%'||ci.item_id||'%' WHERE a.confidence > 0.9 AND a.lift > 1.0 GROUP BY c.campaign_id ), EffectiveCampaigns AS ( SELECT ce.campaign_id, ce.engagement_rate, sp.total_sales, sp.transaction_count, ir.avg_recommendation_confidence, ir.avg_recommendation_lift, ir.avg_recommendation_strength, (ce.engagement_rate + sp.total_sales + ir.avg_recommendation_strength) AS campaign_effectiveness FROM CampaignEngagement ce LEFT JOIN SalesPerformance sp ON ce.campaign_id = sp.campaign_id LEFT JOIN ItemRecommendations ir ON ce.campaign_id = ir.campaign_id ) SELECT ec.campaign_id, ec.campaign_effectiveness FROM EffectiveCampaigns ec ORDER BY ec.campaign_effectiveness DESC

question: Hey! Could you help me find out which teams and players scored the highest for their team or individually in any given season? I'd love to know the team names, player names, the seasons, their maximum team scores, and their personal best scores, all sorted by season and team name.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH SeasonScores AS ( SELECT t.team_name, p.first_name || ' ' || p.last_name AS player_name, strftime('%Y', m.match_date) AS season, s.final_score, MAX(s.final_score) OVER (PARTITION BY t.team_id, strftime('%Y', m.match_date)) AS max_team_score, MAX(s.final_score) OVER (PARTITION BY p.player_id, strftime('%Y', m.match_date)) AS max_player_score FROM scores s JOIN matches m ON s.match_id = m.match_id JOIN players p ON s.player_id = p.player_id JOIN teams t ON s.team_id = t.team_id ) SELECT team_name, player_name, season, max_team_score, max_player_score FROM SeasonScores WHERE final_score = max_team_score OR final_score = max_player_score ORDER BY season, team_name

gold_sql.postgres: WITH SeasonScores AS (SELECT t.team_name, p.first_name || ' ' || p.last_name AS player_name, TO_CHAR(CAST(m.match_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY') AS season, s.final_score, MAX(s.final_score) OVER (PARTITION BY t.team_id, TO_CHAR(CAST(m.match_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY')) AS max_team_score, MAX(s.final_score) OVER (PARTITION BY p.player_id, TO_CHAR(CAST(m.match_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY')) AS max_player_score FROM scores AS s JOIN matches AS m ON s.match_id = m.match_id JOIN players AS p ON s.player_id = p.player_id JOIN teams AS t ON s.team_id = t.team_id) SELECT team_name, player_name, season, max_team_score, max_player_score FROM SeasonScores WHERE final_score = max_team_score OR final_score = max_player_score ORDER BY season NULLS FIRST, team_name NULLS FIRST

question: Can you show me a list of all products, including their descriptions, prices, weights, materials, colors, sizes, styles, review counts, average ratings, total inventory, brand names, and full category paths, sorted by highest average rating, then highest total inventory, and finally lowest price?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RECURSIVE CategoryHierarchy AS ( SELECT category_id, category_name, parent_category_id, category_name AS full_category_path FROM categories WHERE parent_category_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT c.category_id, c.category_name, c.parent_category_id, ch.full_category_path || ' > ' || c.category_name AS full_category_path FROM categories c JOIN CategoryHierarchy ch ON c.parent_category_id = ch.category_id ), ProductReviews AS ( SELECT product_id, COUNT(review_id) AS review_count, AVG(rating) AS average_rating FROM product_reviews GROUP BY product_id ), ProductInventory AS ( SELECT product_id, SUM(quantity) AS total_inventory FROM skus JOIN inventory ON skus.sku_id = inventory.sku_id GROUP BY product_id ) SELECT p.product_id, p.description, p.price, p.weight, p.material, p.color, p.size, p.style, COALESCE(pr.review_count, 0) AS review_count, COALESCE(pr.average_rating, 0) AS average_rating, COALESCE(pi.total_inventory, 0) AS total_inventory, b.brand_name, ch.full_category_path FROM products p JOIN brands b ON p.brand_id = b.brand_id JOIN CategoryHierarchy ch ON p.category_id = ch.category_id LEFT JOIN ProductReviews pr ON p.product_id = pr.product_id LEFT JOIN ProductInventory pi ON p.product_id = pi.product_id ORDER BY pr.average_rating DESC, pi.total_inventory DESC, p.price ASC

question:
**User**: I want to get detailed information about the rally events.
**Assistant**: What kind of details are you looking for?
**User**: I want to know about the event name, date, location, number of participants, and any feedback from the participants.
**Assistant**: Would you also like to include the sponsors and any penalties incurred during the events?
**User**: Yes, please include those as well. Can you summarize the feedback, sponsors, and penalties?
**Assistant**: How would you like the sponsors and penalties to be summarized?
**User**: For sponsors, I'd like to see the sponsor's name and type. For penalties, I'd like to see the penalty time and type.
**Assistant**: And what if an event doesn't have any feedback, sponsors, or penalties?
**User**: Let's include a message indicating that, such as 'No feedback', 'No sponsors', or 'No penalties'.
**Assistant**: Finally, would you like the results to be ordered in any particular way?
**User**: Yes, please order them by event ID.
**Assistant**: I can help you create a query for that. Let me just put it together.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH EventFeedback AS ( SELECT ef.event_id, GROUP_CONCAT(CAST(ef.rating AS TEXT) || ': ' || ef.comments, ' | ') AS feedback_summary FROM event_feedback ef GROUP BY ef.event_id ), EventSponsors AS ( SELECT es.event_id, GROUP_CONCAT(es.sponsor_name || ' (' || es.sponsor_type || ')', ', ') AS sponsors_summary FROM event_sponsors es GROUP BY es.event_id ), EventPenalties AS ( SELECT p.event_id, GROUP_CONCAT(CAST(p.penalty_time AS TEXT) || ' min (' || p.penalty_type || ')', ', ') AS penalties_summary FROM penalties p GROUP BY p.event_id ), EventDetails AS ( SELECT e.event_id, e.event_name, e.event_date, e.location, e.total_participants, ef.feedback_summary, es.sponsors_summary, ep.penalties_summary FROM events e LEFT JOIN EventFeedback ef ON e.event_id = ef.event_id LEFT JOIN EventSponsors es ON e.event_id = es.event_id LEFT JOIN EventPenalties ep ON e.event_id = ep.event_id ) SELECT event_id || ': ' || event_name || ' (' || event_date || ')' || ' - ' || location || ' - ' || 'Participants: ' || total_participants || ', ' || 'Feedback: ' || coalesce(feedback_summary, 'No feedback') || ', ' || 'Sponsors: ' || coalesce(sponsors_summary, 'No sponsors') || ', ' || 'Penalties: ' || coalesce(penalties_summary, 'No penalties') AS event_summary FROM EventDetails ORDER BY event_id
gold_sql.mysql: WITH EventFeedback AS (SELECT ef.event_id, GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(CAST(ef.rating AS CHAR), ': ', ef.comments) SEPARATOR ' | ') AS feedback_summary FROM event_feedback AS ef GROUP BY ef.event_id), EventSponsors AS (SELECT es.event_id, GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(es.sponsor_name, ' (', es.sponsor_type, ')') SEPARATOR ', ') AS sponsors_summary FROM event_sponsors AS es GROUP BY es.event_id), EventPenalties AS (SELECT p.event_id, GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(CAST(p.penalty_time AS CHAR), ' min (', p.penalty_type, ')') SEPARATOR ', ') AS penalties_summary FROM penalties AS p GROUP BY p.event_id), EventDetails AS (SELECT e.event_id, e.event_name, e.event_date, e.location, e.total_participants, ef.feedback_summary, es.sponsors_summary, ep.penalties_summary FROM events AS e LEFT JOIN EventFeedback AS ef ON e.event_id = ef.event_id LEFT JOIN EventSponsors AS es ON e.event_id = es.event_id LEFT JOIN EventPenalties AS ep ON e.event_id = ep.event_id) SELECT CONCAT(event_id, ': ', event_name, ' (', event_date, ')', ' - ', location, ' - ', 'Participants: ', total_participants, ', ', 'Feedback: ', COALESCE(feedback_summary, 'No feedback'), ', ', 'Sponsors: ', COALESCE(sponsors_summary, 'No sponsors'), ', ', 'Penalties: ', COALESCE(penalties_summary, 'No penalties')) AS event_summary FROM EventDetails ORDER BY event_id
gold_sql.postgres: WITH EventFeedback AS (SELECT ef.event_id, STRING_AGG(CAST(ef.rating AS TEXT) || ': ' || ef.comments, ' | ') AS feedback_summary FROM event_feedback AS ef GROUP BY ef.event_id), EventSponsors AS (SELECT es.event_id, STRING_AGG(es.sponsor_name || ' (' || es.sponsor_type || ')', ', ') AS sponsors_summary FROM event_sponsors AS es GROUP BY es.event_id), EventPenalties AS (SELECT p.event_id, STRING_AGG(CAST(p.penalty_time AS TEXT) || ' min (' || p.penalty_type || ')', ', ') AS penalties_summary FROM penalties AS p GROUP BY p.event_id), EventDetails AS (SELECT e.event_id, e.event_name, e.event_date, e.location, e.total_participants, ef.feedback_summary, es.sponsors_summary, ep.penalties_summary FROM events AS e LEFT JOIN EventFeedback AS ef ON e.event_id = ef.event_id LEFT JOIN EventSponsors AS es ON e.event_id = es.event_id LEFT JOIN EventPenalties AS ep ON e.event_id = ep.event_id) SELECT event_id || ': ' || event_name || ' (' || event_date || ')' || ' - ' || location || ' - ' || 'Participants: ' || total_participants || ', ' || 'Feedback: ' || COALESCE(feedback_summary, 'No feedback') || ', ' || 'Sponsors: ' || COALESCE(sponsors_summary, 'No sponsors') || ', ' || 'Penalties: ' || COALESCE(penalties_summary, 'No penalties') AS event_summary FROM EventDetails ORDER BY event_id NULLS FIRST

question: Hey, can you show me a list of dishes that have an average effectiveness rating higher than 7, along with their primary ingredients? I'd love to see the names of these dishes and what they're made of.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT d.dish_name, GROUP_CONCAT(i.ingredient_name, ', ') AS primary_ingredients FROM dishes d INNER JOIN dish_effectiveness de ON d.dish_id = de.dish_id INNER JOIN dish_ingredients di ON d.dish_id = di.dish_id INNER JOIN ingredients i ON di.ingredient_id = i.ingredient_id WHERE de.average_effectiveness_rating > 7 GROUP BY d.dish_name

question: What is the comprehensive report of active product releases, including the release details, the user who released it, and a concatenated string of all status changes for each release?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ActiveReleases AS ( SELECT r.release_id, r.product_id, p.product_name, r.release_name, r.release_type, r.status, r.release_date, r.deadline, u.username AS released_by_username FROM releases r JOIN products p ON r.product_id = p.product_id JOIN users u ON r.released_by = u.user_id WHERE p.status = 'active' AND r.status = 'released' ), StatusChanges AS ( SELECT r.release_id, GROUP_CONCAT( ih.change_date || ', ' || ih.change_type || ', ' || u.username || ', ' || ih.old_value || ' -> ' || ih.new_value, '; ' ) AS status_changes FROM ActiveReleases r LEFT JOIN issue_history ih ON r.release_id = ih.issue_id LEFT JOIN users u ON ih.changed_by = u.user_id WHERE ih.change_type = 'status updated' GROUP BY r.release_id ) SELECT ar.product_name || ', ' || ar.release_name || ', ' || ar.release_type || ', ' || ar.release_date || ', ' || ar.deadline || ', ' || ar.released_by_username || ': ' || sc.status_changes AS composite_info FROM ActiveReleases ar LEFT JOIN StatusChanges sc ON ar.release_id = sc.release_id
gold_sql.mysql: WITH ActiveReleases AS (SELECT r.release_id, r.product_id, p.product_name, r.release_name, r.release_type, r.status, r.release_date, r.deadline, u.username AS released_by_username FROM releases AS r JOIN products AS p ON r.product_id = p.product_id JOIN users AS u ON r.released_by = u.user_id WHERE p.status = 'active' AND r.status = 'released'), StatusChanges AS (SELECT r.release_id, GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(ih.change_date, ', ', ih.change_type, ', ', u.username, ', ', ih.old_value, ' -> ', ih.new_value) SEPARATOR '; ') AS status_changes FROM ActiveReleases AS r LEFT JOIN issue_history AS ih ON r.release_id = ih.issue_id LEFT JOIN users AS u ON ih.changed_by = u.user_id WHERE ih.change_type = 'status updated' GROUP BY r.release_id) SELECT CONCAT(ar.product_name, ', ', ar.release_name, ', ', ar.release_type, ', ', ar.release_date, ', ', ar.deadline, ', ', ar.released_by_username, ': ', sc.status_changes) AS composite_info FROM ActiveReleases AS ar LEFT JOIN StatusChanges AS sc ON ar.release_id = sc.release_id
gold_sql.postgres: WITH ActiveReleases AS (SELECT r.release_id, r.product_id, p.product_name, r.release_name, r.release_type, r.status, r.release_date, r.deadline, u.username AS released_by_username FROM releases AS r JOIN products AS p ON r.product_id = p.product_id JOIN users AS u ON r.released_by = u.user_id WHERE p.status = 'active' AND r.status = 'released'), StatusChanges AS (SELECT r.release_id, STRING_AGG(ih.change_date || ', ' || ih.change_type || ', ' || u.username || ', ' || ih.old_value || ' -> ' || ih.new_value, '; ') AS status_changes FROM ActiveReleases AS r LEFT JOIN issue_history AS ih ON r.release_id = ih.issue_id LEFT JOIN users AS u ON ih.changed_by = u.user_id WHERE ih.change_type = 'status updated' GROUP BY r.release_id) SELECT ar.product_name || ', ' || ar.release_name || ', ' || ar.release_type || ', ' || ar.release_date || ', ' || ar.deadline || ', ' || ar.released_by_username || ': ' || sc.status_changes AS composite_info FROM ActiveReleases AS ar LEFT JOIN StatusChanges AS sc ON ar.release_id = sc.release_id

question: Could you provide me with the names of the packages, the types of imports they have, and the concatenated list of tags associated with the projects that use these packages?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT p.package_name, i.import_type, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT pt.tag) AS project_tags FROM packages p JOIN imports i ON p.package_id = i.package_id JOIN project_packages pp ON p.package_id = pp.package_id JOIN projects pr ON pp.project_id = pr.project_id LEFT JOIN project_tags pt ON pr.project_id = pt.project_id GROUP BY p.package_name, i.import_type
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT p.package_name, i.import_type, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT pt.tag SEPARATOR ',') AS project_tags FROM packages AS p JOIN imports AS i ON p.package_id = i.package_id JOIN project_packages AS pp ON p.package_id = pp.package_id JOIN projects AS pr ON pp.project_id = pr.project_id LEFT JOIN project_tags AS pt ON pr.project_id = pt.project_id GROUP BY p.package_name, i.import_type
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT p.package_name, i.import_type, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT pt.tag, ',') AS project_tags FROM packages AS p JOIN imports AS i ON p.package_id = i.package_id JOIN project_packages AS pp ON p.package_id = pp.package_id JOIN projects AS pr ON pp.project_id = pr.project_id LEFT JOIN project_tags AS pt ON pr.project_id = pt.project_id GROUP BY p.package_name, i.import_type

question:
**User**: I need to generate a comprehensive report about the electricity demand in different areas.
**Assistant**: Which areas are you interested in? LSOA areas or size bands?
**User**: Both. I need information about LSOA areas and size bands.
**Assistant**: What kind of information would you like to include in the report for LSOA areas?
**User**: I would like to know the LSOA code, name, region, population, and area size.
**Assistant**: And what about the size bands? What information would you like to include?
**User**: The size band name, minimum capacity, maximum capacity, and average usage would be great.
**Assistant**: I see. What kind of demand data would you like to include in the report? Historical demand, projected demand, or both?
**User**: Both historical and projected demand data. I'd also like to know the total historical demand, average projection value, and average confidence level.
**Assistant**: How would you like the report to be ordered?
**User**: Order it by year, LSOA code, and size band name.
**Assistant**: Okay, I will help you generate the report with the specified details.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH HistoricalDemand AS ( SELECT lsoa_id, size_band_id, year, SUM(demand_value) AS total_historical_demand FROM electricity_demand GROUP BY lsoa_id, size_band_id, year ), ProjectedDemand AS ( SELECT lsoa_id, size_band_id, year, AVG(projection_value) AS average_projection_value, AVG(confidence_level) AS average_confidence_level FROM projections GROUP BY lsoa_id, size_band_id, year ), CombinedData AS ( SELECT hd.lsoa_id, hd.size_band_id, hd.year, hd.total_historical_demand, pd.average_projection_value, pd.average_confidence_level FROM HistoricalDemand hd LEFT JOIN ProjectedDemand pd ON hd.lsoa_id = pd.lsoa_id AND hd.size_band_id = pd.size_band_id AND hd.year = pd.year ) SELECT l.lsoa_code || ' - ' || l.lsoa_name || ' (' || l.region || ') - ' || 'Year: ' || CAST(cd.year AS TEXT) || ' - ' || 'Population: ' || CAST(l.population AS TEXT) || ' - ' || 'Area Size: ' || CAST(l.area_size AS TEXT) || ' km² - ' || 'Size Band: ' || sb.size_band_name || ' - ' || 'Min Capacity: ' || CAST(sb.min_capacity AS TEXT) || ' kW - ' || 'Max Capacity: ' || CAST(sb.max_capacity AS TEXT) || ' kW - ' || 'Average Usage: ' || CAST(sb.average_usage AS TEXT) || ' kWh - ' || 'Total Historical Demand: ' || CAST(cd.total_historical_demand AS TEXT) || ' kWh - ' || 'Average Projection Value: ' || CAST(cd.average_projection_value AS TEXT) || ' kWh - ' || 'Average Confidence Level: ' || CAST(cd.average_confidence_level AS TEXT) AS detailed_report FROM CombinedData cd JOIN lsoa_areas l ON cd.lsoa_id = l.lsoa_id JOIN size_bands sb ON cd.size_band_id = sb.size_band_id ORDER BY cd.year, l.lsoa_code, sb.size_band_name
gold_sql.mysql: WITH HistoricalDemand AS (SELECT lsoa_id, size_band_id, year, SUM(demand_value) AS total_historical_demand FROM electricity_demand GROUP BY lsoa_id, size_band_id, year), ProjectedDemand AS (SELECT lsoa_id, size_band_id, year, AVG(projection_value) AS average_projection_value, AVG(confidence_level) AS average_confidence_level FROM projections GROUP BY lsoa_id, size_band_id, year), CombinedData AS (SELECT hd.lsoa_id, hd.size_band_id, hd.year, hd.total_historical_demand, pd.average_projection_value, pd.average_confidence_level FROM HistoricalDemand AS hd LEFT JOIN ProjectedDemand AS pd ON hd.lsoa_id = pd.lsoa_id AND hd.size_band_id = pd.size_band_id AND hd.year = pd.year) SELECT CONCAT(l.lsoa_code, ' - ', l.lsoa_name, ' (', l.region, ') - ', 'Year: ', CAST(cd.year AS CHAR), ' - ', 'Population: ', CAST(l.population AS CHAR), ' - ', 'Area Size: ', CAST(l.area_size AS CHAR), ' km² - ', 'Size Band: ', sb.size_band_name, ' - ', 'Min Capacity: ', CAST(sb.min_capacity AS CHAR), ' kW - ', 'Max Capacity: ', CAST(sb.max_capacity AS CHAR), ' kW - ', 'Average Usage: ', CAST(sb.average_usage AS CHAR), ' kWh - ', 'Total Historical Demand: ', CAST(cd.total_historical_demand AS CHAR), ' kWh - ', 'Average Projection Value: ', CAST(cd.average_projection_value AS CHAR), ' kWh - ', 'Average Confidence Level: ', CAST(cd.average_confidence_level AS CHAR)) AS detailed_report FROM CombinedData AS cd JOIN lsoa_areas AS l ON cd.lsoa_id = l.lsoa_id JOIN size_bands AS sb ON cd.size_band_id = sb.size_band_id ORDER BY cd.year, l.lsoa_code, sb.size_band_name
gold_sql.postgres: WITH HistoricalDemand AS (SELECT lsoa_id, size_band_id, year, SUM(demand_value) AS total_historical_demand FROM electricity_demand GROUP BY lsoa_id, size_band_id, year), ProjectedDemand AS (SELECT lsoa_id, size_band_id, year, AVG(projection_value) AS average_projection_value, AVG(confidence_level) AS average_confidence_level FROM projections GROUP BY lsoa_id, size_band_id, year), CombinedData AS (SELECT hd.lsoa_id, hd.size_band_id, hd.year, hd.total_historical_demand, pd.average_projection_value, pd.average_confidence_level FROM HistoricalDemand AS hd LEFT JOIN ProjectedDemand AS pd ON hd.lsoa_id = pd.lsoa_id AND hd.size_band_id = pd.size_band_id AND hd.year = pd.year) SELECT l.lsoa_code || ' - ' || l.lsoa_name || ' (' || l.region || ') - ' || 'Year: ' || CAST(cd.year AS TEXT) || ' - ' || 'Population: ' || CAST(l.population AS TEXT) || ' - ' || 'Area Size: ' || CAST(l.area_size AS TEXT) || ' km² - ' || 'Size Band: ' || sb.size_band_name || ' - ' || 'Min Capacity: ' || CAST(sb.min_capacity AS TEXT) || ' kW - ' || 'Max Capacity: ' || CAST(sb.max_capacity AS TEXT) || ' kW - ' || 'Average Usage: ' || CAST(sb.average_usage AS TEXT) || ' kWh - ' || 'Total Historical Demand: ' || CAST(cd.total_historical_demand AS TEXT) || ' kWh - ' || 'Average Projection Value: ' || CAST(cd.average_projection_value AS TEXT) || ' kWh - ' || 'Average Confidence Level: ' || CAST(cd.average_confidence_level AS TEXT) AS detailed_report FROM CombinedData AS cd JOIN lsoa_areas AS l ON cd.lsoa_id = l.lsoa_id JOIN size_bands AS sb ON cd.size_band_id = sb.size_band_id ORDER BY cd.year NULLS FIRST, l.lsoa_code NULLS FIRST, sb.size_band_name NULLS FIRST

question:
**User**: I want to analyze the performance of basketball players.
**Assistant**: Which aspects of their performance would you like to analyze?
**User**: I'd like to know their average shot distance, number of made shots, and the percentage of shots made.
**Assistant**: Would you like to analyze these statistics by player, team, game date, or action type?
**User**: All of the above. I'd also like to know the shot zone area where the shots were taken.
**Assistant**: Would you like the results sorted in any particular order?
**User**: Yes, I'd like them sorted by player name, game date, action type, and shot zone area.
**Assistant**: Is there anything else you need?
**User**: No, that's all.
**Assistant**: OK, I will help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT p.player_name, s.game_date, s.action_type, s.shot_zone_area, AVG(s.shot_distance) AS avg_shot_distance, SUM(CASE WHEN s.shot_made_flag = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS made_shots, COUNT(s.shot_made_flag) AS total_shots, (SUM(CASE WHEN s.shot_made_flag = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(s.shot_made_flag)) * 100 AS made_percentage FROM shots s INNER JOIN players p ON s.player_id = p.player_id GROUP BY p.player_name, s.game_date, s.action_type, s.shot_zone_area ORDER BY p.player_name, s.game_date, s.action_type, s.shot_zone_area
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT p.player_name, s.game_date, s.action_type, s.shot_zone_area, AVG(s.shot_distance) AS avg_shot_distance, SUM(CASE WHEN s.shot_made_flag = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS made_shots, COUNT(s.shot_made_flag) AS total_shots, (SUM(CASE WHEN s.shot_made_flag = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(s.shot_made_flag)) * 100 AS made_percentage FROM shots AS s INNER JOIN players AS p ON s.player_id = p.player_id GROUP BY p.player_name, s.game_date, s.action_type, s.shot_zone_area ORDER BY p.player_name, s.game_date, s.action_type, s.shot_zone_area
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT p.player_name, s.game_date, s.action_type, s.shot_zone_area, AVG(s.shot_distance) AS avg_shot_distance, SUM(CASE WHEN s.shot_made_flag = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS made_shots, COUNT(s.shot_made_flag) AS total_shots, (SUM(CASE WHEN s.shot_made_flag = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(s.shot_made_flag), 0)) * 100 AS made_percentage FROM shots AS s INNER JOIN players AS p ON s.player_id = p.player_id GROUP BY p.player_name, s.game_date, s.action_type, s.shot_zone_area ORDER BY p.player_name NULLS FIRST, s.game_date NULLS FIRST, s.action_type NULLS FIRST, s.shot_zone_area NULLS FIRST

question: Find all content types and their corresponding TLS versions, along with the average content lengths and associated technologies, for websites that returned a successful HTTP status code and belong to a report with user ID 0, where the average content length exceeds 1000 bytes, and return the results sorted by content type and TLS version.

question:
**User**: I want to inquire about some assignment information.
**Assistant**: What specific aspects of the assignments are you interested in learning more about?
**User**: I'd like to know the overall details of the assignments, including their average grades and how they're graded.
**Assistant**: Would you like to know the average grade for each assignment over time, or just the most recent average grade?
**User**: I'm interested in both the overall average grade and the most recent monthly average grade for each assignment.
**Assistant**: That's helpful. What about the criteria used for grading? Is there something specific you'd like to know about them?
**User**: Yes, I'd like to know the most important criterion for grading each assignment.
**Assistant**: By most important, do you mean the criterion with the highest weight?
**User**: Exactly. And could you please rank these criteria so the most weighted one is listed first for each assignment?
**Assistant**: I'll make sure to prioritize them based on their weights. Would you like the results ordered in any specific way?
**User**: Ordering by assignment ID would be helpful, and within each assignment, list the criteria by their rank.
**Assistant**: I'll arrange the results as you've requested. I'll get the assignment details along with their overall and recent average grades, and the most weighted criterion for each, ordered by assignment ID and criterion rank.
**Assistant**: Is there anything else you'd like me to include in the query?
**User**: No, that covers everything. Please proceed with translating my request into an SQL query.
**Assistant**: Okay, I'll help you with that.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH AssignmentAverageGrades AS ( SELECT assignment_id, AVG(grade) AS average_grade FROM submissions GROUP BY assignment_id ), GradingTrends AS ( SELECT assignment_id, strftime('%Y-%m', submission_date) AS submission_month, AVG(grade) AS monthly_average_grade FROM submissions GROUP BY assignment_id, strftime('%Y-%m', submission_date) ), RankedCriteria AS ( SELECT criterion_id, assignment_id, criterion_name, weight, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY assignment_id ORDER BY weight DESC) AS criterion_rank FROM criteria ) SELECT a.assignment_id, a.assignment_name, a.assignment_type, a.total_points, COALESCE(aag.average_grade, 0) AS overall_average_grade, COALESCE(gt.monthly_average_grade, 0) AS latest_monthly_average_grade, rc.criterion_name, rc.weight, rc.criterion_rank FROM assignments a LEFT JOIN AssignmentAverageGrades aag ON a.assignment_id = aag.assignment_id LEFT JOIN GradingTrends gt ON a.assignment_id = gt.assignment_id AND gt.submission_month = ( SELECT MAX(submission_month) FROM GradingTrends gt2 WHERE gt2.assignment_id = a.assignment_id ) LEFT JOIN RankedCriteria rc ON a.assignment_id = rc.assignment_id AND rc.criterion_rank = 1 ORDER BY a.assignment_id, rc.criterion_rank

question: Can you please provide a list of summaries for all training sessions, including the model name, type, version, dataset name, creator, average metric value, maximum batch time, and metric count, ordered from the most recent sessions to the oldest?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT m.model_name || ' (' || m.type || ' ' || m.version || ') - ' || 'Dataset: ' || COALESCE(d.dataset_name, 'Unknown') || ' - ' || 'Creator: ' || u.user_name || ' - ' || 'Avg Metric Value: ' || COALESCE(CAST(am.avg_metric_value AS TEXT), 'N/A') || ' - ' || 'Max Batch Time: ' || COALESCE(CAST(am.max_batch_time AS TEXT), 'N/A') || ' - ' || 'Metric Count: ' || COALESCE(CAST(am.metric_count AS TEXT), '0') AS session_summary FROM training_sessions ts JOIN models m ON ts.model_id = m.model_id JOIN users u ON ts.created_by = u.user_id LEFT JOIN ( SELECT session_id, AVG(value) AS avg_metric_value, MAX(batch_time) AS max_batch_time, COUNT(*) AS metric_count FROM training_metrics GROUP BY session_id ) am ON ts.session_id = am.session_id LEFT JOIN datasets d ON m.dataset_id = d.dataset_id ORDER BY ts.start_time DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT CONCAT(m.model_name, ' (', m.type, ' ', m.version, ') - ', 'Dataset: ', COALESCE(d.dataset_name, 'Unknown'), ' - ', 'Creator: ', u.user_name, ' - ', 'Avg Metric Value: ', COALESCE(CAST(am.avg_metric_value AS CHAR), 'N/A'), ' - ', 'Max Batch Time: ', COALESCE(CAST(am.max_batch_time AS CHAR), 'N/A'), ' - ', 'Metric Count: ', COALESCE(CAST(am.metric_count AS CHAR), '0')) AS session_summary FROM training_sessions AS ts JOIN models AS m ON ts.model_id = m.model_id JOIN users AS u ON ts.created_by = u.user_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT session_id, AVG(value) AS avg_metric_value, MAX(batch_time) AS max_batch_time, COUNT(*) AS metric_count FROM training_metrics GROUP BY session_id) AS am ON ts.session_id = am.session_id LEFT JOIN datasets AS d ON m.dataset_id = d.dataset_id ORDER BY ts.start_time DESC

question: Could you please list the top 10 restaurants based on their average ratings and the number of reviews they have received? I also need to know how many orders each of these restaurants has handled, the types of cuisines they offer, and the total number of cuisines they serve. The results should be sorted by average rating in descending order, followed by the number of reviews in descending order, and finally by the restaurant names in alphabetical order.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RestaurantRatings AS ( SELECT r.restaurant_id, AVG(CAST(re.rating AS REAL)) AS avg_rating, COUNT(re.review_id) AS review_count FROM restaurants r LEFT JOIN reviews re ON r.restaurant_id = re.restaurant_id GROUP BY r.restaurant_id ), TopRestaurants AS ( SELECT rr.restaurant_id, r.name AS restaurant_name, rr.avg_rating, rr.review_count, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM RestaurantRatings rr INNER JOIN restaurants r ON rr.restaurant_id = r.restaurant_id LEFT JOIN orders o ON r.restaurant_id = o.restaurant_id WHERE rr.review_count > 0 GROUP BY rr.restaurant_id, r.name, rr.avg_rating, rr.review_count ORDER BY rr.avg_rating DESC, rr.review_count DESC, r.name LIMIT 10 ), CuisineCounts AS ( SELECT tr.restaurant_id, GROUP_CONCAT(c.cuisine_name, ', ') AS cuisines, COUNT(rc.cuisine_id) AS cuisine_count FROM TopRestaurants tr INNER JOIN restaurant_cuisines rc ON tr.restaurant_id = rc.restaurant_id INNER JOIN cuisines c ON rc.cuisine_id = c.cuisine_id GROUP BY tr.restaurant_id ) SELECT tr.restaurant_id, tr.restaurant_name, tr.avg_rating, tr.review_count, tr.order_count, cc.cuisines, cc.cuisine_count FROM TopRestaurants tr INNER JOIN CuisineCounts cc ON tr.restaurant_id = cc.restaurant_id ORDER BY tr.avg_rating DESC, tr.review_count DESC, tr.restaurant_name
gold_sql.mysql: WITH RestaurantRatings AS (SELECT r.restaurant_id, AVG(CAST(re.rating AS FLOAT)) AS avg_rating, COUNT(re.review_id) AS review_count FROM restaurants AS r LEFT JOIN reviews AS re ON r.restaurant_id = re.restaurant_id GROUP BY r.restaurant_id), TopRestaurants AS (SELECT rr.restaurant_id, r.name AS restaurant_name, rr.avg_rating, rr.review_count, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM RestaurantRatings AS rr INNER JOIN restaurants AS r ON rr.restaurant_id = r.restaurant_id LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON r.restaurant_id = o.restaurant_id WHERE rr.review_count > 0 GROUP BY rr.restaurant_id, r.name, rr.avg_rating, rr.review_count ORDER BY rr.avg_rating DESC, rr.review_count DESC, r.name LIMIT 10), CuisineCounts AS (SELECT tr.restaurant_id, GROUP_CONCAT(c.cuisine_name SEPARATOR ', ') AS cuisines, COUNT(rc.cuisine_id) AS cuisine_count FROM TopRestaurants AS tr INNER JOIN restaurant_cuisines AS rc ON tr.restaurant_id = rc.restaurant_id INNER JOIN cuisines AS c ON rc.cuisine_id = c.cuisine_id GROUP BY tr.restaurant_id) SELECT tr.restaurant_id, tr.restaurant_name, tr.avg_rating, tr.review_count, tr.order_count, cc.cuisines, cc.cuisine_count FROM TopRestaurants AS tr INNER JOIN CuisineCounts AS cc ON tr.restaurant_id = cc.restaurant_id ORDER BY tr.avg_rating DESC, tr.review_count DESC, tr.restaurant_name

question: What are the names of the top 5 tracks by the artist with ID 1, their total play counts in the year 2023, along with the artist name?
external_knowledge: Artist ID '1' refers to a specific artist in the database; The year '2023' is the specific time frame of interest for the interactions; The tracks are ranked based on total play duration and play count, with higher values indicating more popular tracks.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH TopTracks AS ( SELECT t.track_id, t.track_name, a.artist_name, SUM(ui.play_duration) AS total_play_duration, COUNT(ui.interaction_id) AS play_count FROM tracks t JOIN artists a ON t.artist_id = a.artist_id JOIN user_interactions ui ON t.track_id = ui.track_id WHERE a.artist_id = '1' AND ui.interaction_type = 'play' AND strftime('%Y', ui.interaction_date) = '2023' GROUP BY t.track_id, t.track_name, a.artist_name ORDER BY total_play_duration DESC, play_count DESC LIMIT 5 ) SELECT artist_name AS "Top Artist", track_name AS "Top Track", play_count AS "Total Plays" FROM TopTracks
gold_sql.mysql: WITH TopTracks AS (SELECT t.track_id, t.track_name, a.artist_name, SUM(ui.play_duration) AS total_play_duration, COUNT(ui.interaction_id) AS play_count FROM tracks AS t JOIN artists AS a ON t.artist_id = a.artist_id JOIN user_interactions AS ui ON t.track_id = ui.track_id WHERE a.artist_id = '1' AND ui.interaction_type = 'play' AND DATE_FORMAT(CAST(ui.interaction_date AS DATETIME), '%Y') = '2023' GROUP BY t.track_id, t.track_name, a.artist_name ORDER BY total_play_duration DESC, play_count DESC LIMIT 5) SELECT artist_name AS `Top Artist`, track_name AS `Top Track`, play_count AS `Total Plays` FROM TopTracks
gold_sql.postgres: WITH TopTracks AS (SELECT t.track_id, t.track_name, a.artist_name, SUM(ui.play_duration) AS total_play_duration, COUNT(ui.interaction_id) AS play_count FROM tracks AS t JOIN artists AS a ON t.artist_id = a.artist_id JOIN user_interactions AS ui ON t.track_id = ui.track_id WHERE a.artist_id = '1' AND ui.interaction_type = 'play' AND TO_CHAR(CAST(ui.interaction_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY') = '2023' GROUP BY t.track_id, t.track_name, a.artist_name ORDER BY total_play_duration DESC NULLS LAST, play_count DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 5) SELECT artist_name AS "Top Artist", track_name AS "Top Track", play_count AS "Total Plays" FROM TopTracks

question: Find the treatment outcomes for the first instance of each combination of treatment adherence and vaccination status.
external_knowledge: Treatment adherence refers to whether a patient has followed their prescribed treatment regimen; Vaccination status can be 'fully vaccinated', 'partially vaccinated', or 'not vaccinated', which are categories used to describe a patient's level of vaccination against a particular disease.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH PatientOutcomeCTE AS ( SELECT p.patient_id, p.vaccination_status, t.treatment_adherence, t.treatment_outcome, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t.treatment_adherence, p.vaccination_status ORDER BY p.patient_id) AS outcome_rank FROM patients p JOIN treatment t ON p.patient_id = t.patient_id ) SELECT GROUP_CONCAT( CASE WHEN treatment_adherence = 1 THEN 'Adherent: ' ELSE 'Non-adherent: ' END || CASE WHEN vaccination_status = 'fully vaccinated' THEN 'Fully Vaccinated' WHEN vaccination_status = 'partially vaccinated' THEN 'Partially Vaccinated' ELSE 'Not Vaccinated' END || ' - ' || treatment_outcome, ', ' ) AS OutcomeSummary FROM PatientOutcomeCTE WHERE outcome_rank = 1
gold_sql.mysql: WITH PatientOutcomeCTE AS (SELECT p.patient_id, p.vaccination_status, t.treatment_adherence, t.treatment_outcome, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t.treatment_adherence, p.vaccination_status ORDER BY p.patient_id) AS outcome_rank FROM patients AS p JOIN treatment AS t ON p.patient_id = t.patient_id) SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(CASE WHEN treatment_adherence = 1 THEN 'Adherent: ' ELSE 'Non-adherent: ' END, CASE WHEN vaccination_status = 'fully vaccinated' THEN 'Fully Vaccinated' WHEN vaccination_status = 'partially vaccinated' THEN 'Partially Vaccinated' ELSE 'Not Vaccinated' END, ' - ', treatment_outcome) SEPARATOR ', ') AS OutcomeSummary FROM PatientOutcomeCTE WHERE outcome_rank = 1
gold_sql.postgres: WITH PatientOutcomeCTE AS (SELECT p.patient_id, p.vaccination_status, t.treatment_adherence, t.treatment_outcome, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t.treatment_adherence, p.vaccination_status ORDER BY p.patient_id NULLS FIRST) AS outcome_rank FROM patients AS p JOIN treatment AS t ON p.patient_id = t.patient_id) SELECT STRING_AGG(CASE WHEN treatment_adherence = 1 THEN 'Adherent: ' ELSE 'Non-adherent: ' END || CASE WHEN vaccination_status = 'fully vaccinated' THEN 'Fully Vaccinated' WHEN vaccination_status = 'partially vaccinated' THEN 'Partially Vaccinated' ELSE 'Not Vaccinated' END || ' - ' || treatment_outcome, ', ') AS OutcomeSummary FROM PatientOutcomeCTE WHERE outcome_rank = 1

question: What are the names of neighborhoods with property taxes above 200, along with their average median house prices, number of development projects, total feedback, positive feedback percentages, and the highest and lowest median incomes across all neighborhoods, ordered by average median house price in descending order?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT n.name AS neighborhood_name, AVG(r.median_house_price) AS avg_median_house_price, COUNT(DISTINCT udp.project_id) AS num_development_projects, COUNT(pf.feedback_id) AS total_feedback, SUM(CASE WHEN pf.feedback_type = 'positive' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(pf.feedback_id) * 100 AS positive_feedback_percentage, (SELECT MAX(n.median_income) FROM neighborhoods n) AS highest_income, (SELECT MIN(n.median_income) FROM neighborhoods n) AS lowest_income FROM real_estate_data r INNER JOIN neighborhoods n ON r.neighborhood_id = n.neighborhood_id LEFT JOIN urban_development_projects udp ON n.neighborhood_id = udp.neighborhood_id LEFT JOIN public_feedback pf ON udp.project_id = pf.project_id WHERE r.property_tax > 200 GROUP BY n.name ORDER BY avg_median_house_price DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT n.name AS neighborhood_name, AVG(r.median_house_price) AS avg_median_house_price, COUNT(DISTINCT udp.project_id) AS num_development_projects, COUNT(pf.feedback_id) AS total_feedback, SUM(CASE WHEN pf.feedback_type = 'positive' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(pf.feedback_id) * 100 AS positive_feedback_percentage, (SELECT MAX(n.median_income) FROM neighborhoods AS n) AS highest_income, (SELECT MIN(n.median_income) FROM neighborhoods AS n) AS lowest_income FROM real_estate_data AS r INNER JOIN neighborhoods AS n ON r.neighborhood_id = n.neighborhood_id LEFT JOIN urban_development_projects AS udp ON n.neighborhood_id = udp.neighborhood_id LEFT JOIN public_feedback AS pf ON udp.project_id = pf.project_id WHERE r.property_tax > 200 GROUP BY n.name ORDER BY avg_median_house_price DESC
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT n.name AS neighborhood_name, AVG(r.median_house_price) AS avg_median_house_price, COUNT(DISTINCT udp.project_id) AS num_development_projects, COUNT(pf.feedback_id) AS total_feedback, SUM(CASE WHEN pf.feedback_type = 'positive' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(pf.feedback_id), 0) * 100 AS positive_feedback_percentage, (SELECT MAX(n.median_income) FROM neighborhoods AS n) AS highest_income, (SELECT MIN(n.median_income) FROM neighborhoods AS n) AS lowest_income FROM real_estate_data AS r INNER JOIN neighborhoods AS n ON r.neighborhood_id = n.neighborhood_id LEFT JOIN urban_development_projects AS udp ON n.neighborhood_id = udp.neighborhood_id LEFT JOIN public_feedback AS pf ON udp.project_id = pf.project_id WHERE r.property_tax > 200 GROUP BY n.name ORDER BY avg_median_house_price DESC NULLS LAST

question: Hey, could you provide me with a list of all project managers along with their total number of projects, the number of successful, canceled, and failed projects, the total failures and cancellations, reasons for these failures and cancellations, and their overall success rate? I'd love to see the results ordered from highest to lowest success rate.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ProjectMetrics AS ( SELECT u.user_id, u.user_name, COUNT(p.project_id) AS total_projects, SUM(CASE WHEN p.status = 'completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS successful_projects, SUM(CASE WHEN p.status = 'canceled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS canceled_projects, SUM(CASE WHEN p.status = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed_projects FROM users u INNER JOIN projects p ON u.user_id = p.manager_id GROUP BY u.user_id, u.user_name ), ProjectFailures AS ( SELECT p.manager_id, COUNT(pf.failure_id) AS total_failures, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT pf.reason) AS failure_reasons FROM projects p LEFT JOIN project_failures pf ON p.project_id = pf.project_id GROUP BY p.manager_id ), ProjectCancellations AS ( SELECT p.manager_id, COUNT(pc.cancellation_id) AS total_cancellations, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT pc.reason) AS cancellation_reasons FROM projects p LEFT JOIN project_cancellations pc ON p.project_id = pc.project_id GROUP BY p.manager_id ) SELECT pm.user_name, pm.total_projects, pm.successful_projects, pm.canceled_projects, pm.failed_projects, COALESCE(pf.total_failures, 0) AS total_failures, COALESCE(pf.failure_reasons, 'No failures') AS failure_reasons, COALESCE(pc.total_cancellations, 0) AS total_cancellations, COALESCE(pc.cancellation_reasons, 'No cancellations') AS cancellation_reasons, (pm.successful_projects * 1.0 / pm.total_projects) * 100 AS success_rate FROM ProjectMetrics pm LEFT JOIN ProjectFailures pf ON pm.user_id = pf.manager_id LEFT JOIN ProjectCancellations pc ON pm.user_id = pc.manager_id ORDER BY success_rate DESC

question: Retrieve a comprehensive summary of all routes, including their names, city IDs, service types, active statuses, route types, start and end times, average city populations, numbers of wheelchair-accessible stops, and detailed lists of service changes, ordered by route ID.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH AveragePopulation AS ( SELECT r.route_id, AVG(c.population) AS avg_city_population FROM routes r JOIN cities c ON r.city_id = c.city_id GROUP BY r.route_id ), AccessibleStops AS ( SELECT sr.route_id, COUNT(s.stop_id) AS accessible_stops FROM stop_routes sr JOIN stops s ON sr.stop_id = s.stop_id WHERE s.wheelchair_accessible = 1 GROUP BY sr.route_id ), ServiceChanges AS ( SELECT sc.route_id, GROUP_CONCAT(sc.change_type || ' - ' || sc.change_description, ', ') AS service_changes FROM service_changes sc GROUP BY sc.route_id ) SELECT r.route_id, r.route_name, r.city_id, r.service_type, r.active, r.route_type, r.start_time, r.end_time, ap.avg_city_population, asp.accessible_stops, sc.service_changes FROM routes r LEFT JOIN AveragePopulation ap ON r.route_id = ap.route_id LEFT JOIN AccessibleStops asp ON r.route_id = asp.route_id LEFT JOIN ServiceChanges sc ON r.route_id = sc.route_id ORDER BY r.route_id

question: I want to know the names, outstanding amounts, contact emails, and phone numbers for all departments that have outstanding fees, sorted from highest to lowest by the outstanding amount.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH FeeSummary AS ( SELECT f.dept_id, SUM(CAST(REPLACE(f.amount, ',', '') AS REAL)) AS total_fees, SUM(CAST(REPLACE(f.paid_to_date, ',', '') AS REAL)) AS total_paid, COALESCE(SUM(CAST(REPLACE(fc.credit_amount, ',', '') AS REAL)), 0) AS total_credits FROM fees f LEFT JOIN fee_credits fc ON f.fee_id = fc.fee_id GROUP BY f.dept_id ), OutstandingFees AS ( SELECT fs.dept_id, fs.total_fees - fs.total_paid + fs.total_credits AS outstanding_amount FROM FeeSummary fs ) SELECT d.dept_name, of.outstanding_amount, d.contact_email, d.phone_number FROM departments d JOIN OutstandingFees of ON d.dept_id = of.dept_id WHERE of.outstanding_amount > 0 ORDER BY of.outstanding_amount DESC

question: What are the IDs, average response times, and corresponding user feedback for active chatbot deployments from 2022 and 2023 with an average response time greater than 1 second, and list them from slowest to fastest?
external_knowledge: Active chatbot deployments are those currently operational and available for use; Average response time greater than 1 refers to a response time greater than 1 second; The time range of 2022 and 2023 is the period of interest for this query.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT bd.deployment_id, AVG(bu.response_time) AS avg_response_time, GROUP_CONCAT(bu.user_feedback) AS user_feedbacks FROM bot_deployments bd JOIN bot_usage bu ON bd.deployment_id = bu.deployment_id WHERE bd.status = 'active' AND bu.access_date BETWEEN '2022-01-01' AND '2023-12-31' GROUP BY bd.deployment_id HAVING AVG(bu.response_time) > 1 ORDER BY avg_response_time DESC

gold_sql.postgres: SELECT bd.deployment_id, AVG(bu.response_time) AS avg_response_time, STRING_AGG(bu.user_feedback, ',') AS user_feedbacks FROM bot_deployments AS bd JOIN bot_usage AS bu ON bd.deployment_id = bu.deployment_id WHERE bd.status = 'active' AND bu.access_date BETWEEN '2022-01-01' AND '2023-12-31' GROUP BY bd.deployment_id HAVING AVG(bu.response_time) > 1 ORDER BY avg_response_time DESC NULLS LAST

question: What are the names of all models, their hyperparameters, associated experiment names, counts of total and pending experiments, and deployment details across different environments, listed alphabetically by model name?
external_knowledge: ; The term 'hyperparameters' refers to the variables set before training a machine learning model; 'deployment' in this context means moving a model to a production or staging environment; 'pending experiments' are those that have not started yet.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ModelHyperparameters AS ( SELECT m.model_id, m.model_name, GROUP_CONCAT(hp.hyperparameter_name || '=' || hp.hyperparameter_value, ', ') AS hyperparameters FROM models m LEFT JOIN hyperparameters hp ON m.model_id = hp.model_id GROUP BY m.model_id, m.model_name ), ModelExperiments AS ( SELECT e.model_id, GROUP_CONCAT(e.experiment_name, ', ') AS experiment_names, COUNT(*) AS experiment_count, COUNT(CASE WHEN e.status = 'pending' THEN 1 END) AS pending_experiments FROM experiments e GROUP BY e.model_id ), ModelDeployments AS ( SELECT mdh.model_id, GROUP_CONCAT(mdh.environment || ': ' || mdh.deployment_status, ', ') AS deployment_details, COUNT(*) AS deployment_count FROM model_deployment_history mdh GROUP BY mdh.model_id ) SELECT mh.model_name, mh.hyperparameters, me.experiment_names, me.experiment_count, me.pending_experiments, md.deployment_details, md.deployment_count FROM ModelHyperparameters mh LEFT JOIN ModelExperiments me ON mh.model_id = me.model_id LEFT JOIN ModelDeployments md ON mh.model_id = md.model_id ORDER BY mh.model_name
gold_sql.mysql: WITH ModelHyperparameters AS (SELECT m.model_id, m.model_name, GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(hp.hyperparameter_name, '=', hp.hyperparameter_value) SEPARATOR ', ') AS hyperparameters FROM models AS m LEFT JOIN hyperparameters AS hp ON m.model_id = hp.model_id GROUP BY m.model_id, m.model_name), ModelExperiments AS (SELECT e.model_id, GROUP_CONCAT(e.experiment_name SEPARATOR ', ') AS experiment_names, COUNT(*) AS experiment_count, COUNT(CASE WHEN e.status = 'pending' THEN 1 END) AS pending_experiments FROM experiments AS e GROUP BY e.model_id), ModelDeployments AS (SELECT mdh.model_id, GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(mdh.environment, ': ', mdh.deployment_status) SEPARATOR ', ') AS deployment_details, COUNT(*) AS deployment_count FROM model_deployment_history AS mdh GROUP BY mdh.model_id) SELECT mh.model_name, mh.hyperparameters, me.experiment_names, me.experiment_count, me.pending_experiments, md.deployment_details, md.deployment_count FROM ModelHyperparameters AS mh LEFT JOIN ModelExperiments AS me ON mh.model_id = me.model_id LEFT JOIN ModelDeployments AS md ON mh.model_id = md.model_id ORDER BY mh.model_name
gold_sql.postgres: WITH ModelHyperparameters AS (SELECT m.model_id, m.model_name, STRING_AGG(hp.hyperparameter_name || '=' || hp.hyperparameter_value, ', ') AS hyperparameters FROM models AS m LEFT JOIN hyperparameters AS hp ON m.model_id = hp.model_id GROUP BY m.model_id, m.model_name), ModelExperiments AS (SELECT e.model_id, STRING_AGG(e.experiment_name, ', ') AS experiment_names, COUNT(*) AS experiment_count, COUNT(CASE WHEN e.status = 'pending' THEN 1 END) AS pending_experiments FROM experiments AS e GROUP BY e.model_id), ModelDeployments AS (SELECT mdh.model_id, STRING_AGG(mdh.environment || ': ' || mdh.deployment_status, ', ') AS deployment_details, COUNT(*) AS deployment_count FROM model_deployment_history AS mdh GROUP BY mdh.model_id) SELECT mh.model_name, mh.hyperparameters, me.experiment_names, me.experiment_count, me.pending_experiments, md.deployment_details, md.deployment_count FROM ModelHyperparameters AS mh LEFT JOIN ModelExperiments AS me ON mh.model_id = me.model_id LEFT JOIN ModelDeployments AS md ON mh.model_id = md.model_id ORDER BY mh.model_name NULLS FIRST

question: Find the stock identifiers of the champions in each stock exchange, the ones with the highest trading volume.
external_knowledge: "Champions" refers to the stocks with the highest trading volume in each exchange, implying a competition where the stock with the highest volume is considered the winner.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH MaxVolumeCTE AS ( SELECT msd.stock_id, s.exchange_id, MAX(CAST(msd.volume AS INTEGER)) AS max_volume FROM stocks s INNER JOIN member_stock_data msd ON s.stock_id = msd.stock_id GROUP BY msd.stock_id, s.exchange_id ), RankedStocksCTE AS ( SELECT mv.stock_id, mv.exchange_id, mv.max_volume, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY mv.exchange_id ORDER BY mv.max_volume DESC) AS volume_rank FROM MaxVolumeCTE mv ) SELECT rs.stock_id FROM RankedStocksCTE rs WHERE rs.volume_rank = 1

question: Hey, can you show me a detailed list of all plenary items, including their titles, categories (with full paths), dates they were tabled and discussed, types, descriptions, statuses, sequence numbers, session IDs, the IDs of users who last accessed them, the dates and types of their last accesses, reasons for these accesses, and the breakdown of yes, no, and abstain votes for each item, ordered by the sequence number and item ID?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RECURSIVE CategoryHierarchy AS ( SELECT category_id, category_name, description, parent_category_id, CAST(category_name AS TEXT) AS full_path, 1 AS level FROM categories WHERE parent_category_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT c.category_id, c.category_name, c.description, c.parent_category_id, CAST(ch.full_path || ' > ' || c.category_name AS TEXT) AS full_path, ch.level + 1 FROM categories c JOIN CategoryHierarchy ch ON c.parent_category_id = ch.category_id ), PlenaryItemDetails AS ( SELECT pi.item_id, pi.title, pi.category_id, ch.full_path AS category_path, pi.tabled_date, pi.plenary_date, pi.item_type, pi.description, pi.status, si.sequence_number, si.session_id FROM plenary_items pi JOIN CategoryHierarchy ch ON pi.category_id = ch.category_id LEFT JOIN session_items si ON pi.item_id = si.item_id ), LatestAccess AS ( SELECT item_id, MAX(access_date) AS latest_access_date FROM item_access_logs GROUP BY item_id ), AccessLogs AS ( SELECT ial.item_id, ial.user_id, ial.access_date, ial.access_type, ial.access_reason FROM item_access_logs ial JOIN LatestAccess la ON ial.item_id = la.item_id AND ial.access_date = la.latest_access_date ), VoteCounts AS ( SELECT v.item_id, SUM(CASE WHEN v.vote_cast = 'yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS yes_votes, SUM(CASE WHEN v.vote_cast = 'no' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS no_votes, SUM(CASE WHEN v.vote_cast = 'abstain' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS abstain_votes FROM votes v GROUP BY v.item_id ) SELECT pid.title, pid.category_path, pid.tabled_date, pid.plenary_date, pid.item_type, pid.description, pid.status, pid.sequence_number, pid.session_id, al.user_id, al.access_date, al.access_type, al.access_reason, vc.yes_votes, vc.no_votes, vc.abstain_votes FROM PlenaryItemDetails pid LEFT JOIN AccessLogs al ON pid.item_id = al.item_id LEFT JOIN VoteCounts vc ON pid.item_id = vc.item_id ORDER BY pid.sequence_number, pid.item_id

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH HistoricalPeriods AS ( SELECT u.word_id, u.date, u.usage_count, h.period_name FROM usage_stats u JOIN words w ON u.word_id = w.word_id LEFT JOIN historical_periods h ON u.date BETWEEN h.start_year || '-01-01' AND h.end_year || '-12-31' WHERE w.word_form = 'report' ), CumulativeUsage AS ( SELECT w.word_form, h.date, h.period_name, SUM(h.usage_count) OVER (ORDER BY h.date) AS cumulative_usage_count FROM HistoricalPeriods h JOIN words w ON h.word_id = w.word_id WHERE w.word_form = 'report' ) SELECT word_form, date, period_name, cumulative_usage_count FROM CumulativeUsage ORDER BY date

question: I want to know the file names, graph types, collaborator counts, total report counts, counts of summary and detailed reports, tags, average metric values, access counts, total access durations, and unique user counts for all graphs, ordered by graph ID.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH GraphCollaborators AS ( SELECT graph_id, COUNT(user_id) AS collaborator_count FROM collaborations GROUP BY graph_id ), GraphReports AS ( SELECT graph_id, COUNT(report_id) AS report_count, COUNT(CASE WHEN report_type = 'summary' THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) AS summary_report_count, COUNT(CASE WHEN report_type = 'detailed' THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) AS detailed_report_count FROM reports GROUP BY graph_id ), GraphTagSummary AS ( SELECT graph_id, GROUP_CONCAT(tag_name, ', ') AS tags FROM graph_tags GROUP BY graph_id ), GraphMetrics AS ( SELECT graph_id, AVG(CAST(metric_value AS REAL)) AS avg_metric_value FROM graph_metrics GROUP BY graph_id ), GraphAccessSummary AS ( SELECT graph_id, COUNT(access_id) AS access_count, SUM(access_duration) AS total_access_duration, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS unique_user_count FROM access_logs GROUP BY graph_id ) SELECT g.graph_id, g.file_name, g.graph_type, gc.collaborator_count, gr.report_count, gr.summary_report_count, gr.detailed_report_count, gts.tags, gm.avg_metric_value, gas.access_count, gas.total_access_duration, gas.unique_user_count FROM graphs g LEFT JOIN GraphCollaborators gc ON g.graph_id = gc.graph_id LEFT JOIN GraphReports gr ON g.graph_id = gr.graph_id LEFT JOIN GraphTagSummary gts ON g.graph_id = gts.graph_id LEFT JOIN GraphMetrics gm ON g.graph_id = gm.graph_id LEFT JOIN GraphAccessSummary gas ON g.graph_id = gas.graph_id ORDER BY g.graph_id
