question: Could you please list the names of the software products that have had a major release and have also had at least one database update after that major release?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT sp.product_name FROM software_products sp JOIN versions v ON sp.product_id = v.product_id JOIN databases d ON sp.product_id = d.product_id JOIN database_updates du ON d.database_id = du.database_id WHERE v.major_release = 1 AND du.update_date > v.release_date GROUP BY sp.product_name
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT sp.product_name FROM software_products AS sp JOIN versions AS v ON sp.product_id = v.product_id JOIN `databases` AS d ON sp.product_id = d.product_id JOIN database_updates AS du ON d.database_id = du.database_id WHERE v.major_release = 1 AND du.update_date > v.release_date GROUP BY sp.product_name
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT sp.product_name FROM software_products AS sp JOIN versions AS v ON sp.product_id = v.product_id JOIN databases AS d ON sp.product_id = d.product_id JOIN database_updates AS du ON d.database_id = du.database_id WHERE v.major_release = 1 AND du.update_date > v.release_date GROUP BY sp.product_name

question: Gather the articles that have blossomed in the eyes of the audience, along with their source, the industries they touch, and the number of times they've been seen.
external_knowledge: 'Articles that have blossomed in the eyes of the audience' refers to articles that have at least one view; 'the industries they touch' refers to the industries associated with the articles.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT a.article_id, s.source_name, GROUP_CONCAT(i.industry_name) AS industries, COUNT(v.view_id) AS view_count FROM articles a JOIN sources s ON a.source_id = s.source_id JOIN article_industries ai ON a.article_id = ai.article_id JOIN industries i ON ai.industry_id = i.industry_id JOIN article_views v ON a.article_id = v.article_id GROUP BY a.article_id, s.source_name HAVING COUNT(v.view_id) > 0
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT a.article_id, s.source_name, GROUP_CONCAT(i.industry_name SEPARATOR ',') AS industries, COUNT(v.view_id) AS view_count FROM articles AS a JOIN sources AS s ON a.source_id = s.source_id JOIN article_industries AS ai ON a.article_id = ai.article_id JOIN industries AS i ON ai.industry_id = i.industry_id JOIN article_views AS v ON a.article_id = v.article_id GROUP BY a.article_id, s.source_name HAVING COUNT(v.view_id) > 0
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT a.article_id, s.source_name, STRING_AGG(i.industry_name, ',') AS industries, COUNT(v.view_id) AS view_count FROM articles AS a JOIN sources AS s ON a.source_id = s.source_id JOIN article_industries AS ai ON a.article_id = ai.article_id JOIN industries AS i ON ai.industry_id = i.industry_id JOIN article_views AS v ON a.article_id = v.article_id GROUP BY a.article_id, s.source_name HAVING COUNT(v.view_id) > 0

question: What are the top cumulative average percentages achieved by students within each course when ordered from highest to lowest?
external_knowledge: This question assumes that the cumulative average percentage is a measure of a student's overall performance within a course; 'top' refers to the highest values in the cumulative average percentage.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH StudentQualifications AS ( SELECT s.student_id, q.course_id, q.date_awarded, g.percentage_range FROM students s INNER JOIN qualifications q ON s.student_id = q.student_id INNER JOIN grades g ON q.grade_id = g.grade_id ), ExtractedPercentage AS ( SELECT student_id, course_id, date_awarded, CAST(SUBSTR(percentage_range, 1, INSTR(percentage_range, '-') - 1) AS REAL) AS average_percentage FROM StudentQualifications ), CumulativeAverages AS ( SELECT student_id, course_id, SUM(average_percentage) OVER (PARTITION BY course_id ORDER BY date_awarded) AS cumulative_average FROM ExtractedPercentage ) SELECT course_id, MAX(cumulative_average) AS top_cumulative_average FROM CumulativeAverages GROUP BY course_id ORDER BY top_cumulative_average DESC
gold_sql.mysql: WITH StudentQualifications AS (SELECT s.student_id, q.course_id, q.date_awarded, g.percentage_range FROM students AS s INNER JOIN qualifications AS q ON s.student_id = q.student_id INNER JOIN grades AS g ON q.grade_id = g.grade_id), ExtractedPercentage AS (SELECT student_id, course_id, date_awarded, CAST(SUBSTRING(percentage_range, 1, LOCATE('-', percentage_range) - 1) AS FLOAT) AS average_percentage FROM StudentQualifications), CumulativeAverages AS (SELECT student_id, course_id, SUM(average_percentage) OVER (PARTITION BY course_id ORDER BY date_awarded) AS cumulative_average FROM ExtractedPercentage) SELECT course_id, MAX(cumulative_average) AS top_cumulative_average FROM CumulativeAverages GROUP BY course_id ORDER BY top_cumulative_average DESC

question: What is the average traffic congestion level in the first region during the accidents that took place throughout the day on April 1st, 2023?
external_knowledge: Traffic congestion level is assumed to be directly related to traffic density, with higher density indicating more congestion; Accidents are a type of incident that affects traffic flow; The hour range of an incident affects the time period considered for average traffic density; region_id = 1 refers to a specific geographic area of interest.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT AVG(td.density) AS average_density_during_incidents FROM traffic_data td INNER JOIN incident_reports ir ON td.region_id = ir.region_id WHERE td.region_id = 1 AND ir.incident_type = 'Accident' AND ir.start_time BETWEEN '2023-04-01 00:00:00' AND '2023-04-01 23:59:59' AND td.hour BETWEEN CAST(strftime('%H', ir.start_time) AS INTEGER) AND CAST(strftime('%H', ir.end_time) AS INTEGER)
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT AVG(td.density) AS average_density_during_incidents FROM traffic_data AS td INNER JOIN incident_reports AS ir ON td.region_id = ir.region_id WHERE td.region_id = 1 AND ir.incident_type = 'Accident' AND ir.start_time BETWEEN '2023-04-01 00:00:00' AND '2023-04-01 23:59:59' AND td.hour BETWEEN CAST(DATE_FORMAT(CAST(ir.start_time AS DATETIME), '%H') AS SIGNED) AND CAST(DATE_FORMAT(CAST(ir.end_time AS DATETIME), '%H') AS SIGNED)
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT AVG(td.density) AS average_density_during_incidents FROM traffic_data AS td INNER JOIN incident_reports AS ir ON td.region_id = ir.region_id WHERE td.region_id = 1 AND ir.incident_type = 'Accident' AND ir.start_time BETWEEN '2023-04-01 00:00:00' AND '2023-04-01 23:59:59' AND td.hour BETWEEN CAST(TO_CHAR(CAST(ir.start_time AS TIMESTAMP), 'HH24') AS INT) AND CAST(TO_CHAR(CAST(ir.end_time AS TIMESTAMP), 'HH24') AS INT)

question: Could you please gather all the information about each job posting, including the job title, category name, location name, contact email, the total number of applications received, the status of these applications along with their respective counts, and whether the skills of the applicants match the required skills for the job? I need this information sorted by job ID and application status.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ApplicationCounts AS ( SELECT job_id, COUNT(*) AS application_count FROM applications GROUP BY job_id ), ApplicationStatusDistribution AS ( SELECT job_id, status, COUNT(*) AS status_count FROM applications GROUP BY job_id, status ), JobDetails AS ( SELECT p.job_id, p.job_title, c.category_name, l.location_name, l.contact_email, p.skills_required FROM job_postings p INNER JOIN categories c ON p.category_id = c.category_id INNER JOIN locations l ON p.location_id = l.location_id ), ApplicantSkills AS ( SELECT a.job_id, u.user_id, GROUP_CONCAT(us.skill) AS applicant_skills FROM applications a INNER JOIN users u ON a.user_id = u.user_id LEFT JOIN user_skills us ON u.user_id = us.user_id GROUP BY a.job_id, u.user_id ), JobApplicantSkillMatch AS ( SELECT js.job_id, js.skills_required, askill.user_id, CASE WHEN askill.applicant_skills LIKE '%' || js.skills_required || '%' THEN 'Match' ELSE 'No Match' END AS skill_match FROM JobDetails js INNER JOIN ApplicantSkills askill ON js.job_id = askill.job_id ) SELECT jd.job_id, jd.job_title, jd.category_name, jd.location_name, jd.contact_email, ac.application_count, acd.status, acd.status_count, js.skill_match FROM JobDetails jd LEFT JOIN ApplicationCounts ac ON jd.job_id = ac.job_id LEFT JOIN ApplicationStatusDistribution acd ON jd.job_id = acd.job_id LEFT JOIN JobApplicantSkillMatch js ON jd.job_id = js.job_id ORDER BY jd.job_id, acd.status
gold_sql.mysql: WITH ApplicationCounts AS (SELECT job_id, COUNT(*) AS application_count FROM applications GROUP BY job_id), ApplicationStatusDistribution AS (SELECT job_id, status, COUNT(*) AS status_count FROM applications GROUP BY job_id, status), JobDetails AS (SELECT p.job_id, p.job_title, c.category_name, l.location_name, l.contact_email, p.skills_required FROM job_postings AS p INNER JOIN categories AS c ON p.category_id = c.category_id INNER JOIN locations AS l ON p.location_id = l.location_id), ApplicantSkills AS (SELECT a.job_id, u.user_id, GROUP_CONCAT(us.skill SEPARATOR ',') AS applicant_skills FROM applications AS a INNER JOIN users AS u ON a.user_id = u.user_id LEFT JOIN user_skills AS us ON u.user_id = us.user_id GROUP BY a.job_id, u.user_id), JobApplicantSkillMatch AS (SELECT js.job_id, js.skills_required, askill.user_id, CASE WHEN askill.applicant_skills LIKE CONCAT('%', js.skills_required, '%') THEN 'Match' ELSE 'No Match' END AS skill_match FROM JobDetails AS js INNER JOIN ApplicantSkills AS askill ON js.job_id = askill.job_id) SELECT jd.job_id, jd.job_title, jd.category_name, jd.location_name, jd.contact_email, ac.application_count, acd.status, acd.status_count, js.skill_match FROM JobDetails AS jd LEFT JOIN ApplicationCounts AS ac ON jd.job_id = ac.job_id LEFT JOIN ApplicationStatusDistribution AS acd ON jd.job_id = acd.job_id LEFT JOIN JobApplicantSkillMatch AS js ON jd.job_id = js.job_id ORDER BY jd.job_id, acd.status
gold_sql.postgres: WITH ApplicationCounts AS (SELECT job_id, COUNT(*) AS application_count FROM applications GROUP BY job_id), ApplicationStatusDistribution AS (SELECT job_id, status, COUNT(*) AS status_count FROM applications GROUP BY job_id, status), JobDetails AS (SELECT p.job_id, p.job_title, c.category_name, l.location_name, l.contact_email, p.skills_required FROM job_postings AS p INNER JOIN categories AS c ON p.category_id = c.category_id INNER JOIN locations AS l ON p.location_id = l.location_id), ApplicantSkills AS (SELECT a.job_id, u.user_id, STRING_AGG(us.skill, ',') AS applicant_skills FROM applications AS a INNER JOIN users AS u ON a.user_id = u.user_id LEFT JOIN user_skills AS us ON u.user_id = us.user_id GROUP BY a.job_id, u.user_id), JobApplicantSkillMatch AS (SELECT js.job_id, js.skills_required, askill.user_id, CASE WHEN askill.applicant_skills LIKE '%' || js.skills_required || '%' THEN 'Match' ELSE 'No Match' END AS skill_match FROM JobDetails AS js INNER JOIN ApplicantSkills AS askill ON js.job_id = askill.job_id) SELECT jd.job_id, jd.job_title, jd.category_name, jd.location_name, jd.contact_email, ac.application_count, acd.status, acd.status_count, js.skill_match FROM JobDetails AS jd LEFT JOIN ApplicationCounts AS ac ON jd.job_id = ac.job_id LEFT JOIN ApplicationStatusDistribution AS acd ON jd.job_id = acd.job_id LEFT JOIN JobApplicantSkillMatch AS js ON jd.job_id = js.job_id ORDER BY jd.job_id NULLS FIRST, acd.status NULLS FIRST

question: Find the names of all customers who have churned, along with their total usage amounts and total payments, ordered from the highest total payment to the lowest, and for customers with the same total payment, ordered from the highest total usage to the lowest.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ChurnedCustomers AS ( SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name FROM churn ch INNER JOIN customers c ON ch.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE ch.has_churned = 1 ), TotalUsage AS ( SELECT cu.customer_id, SUM(u.usage_amount) AS total_usage FROM ChurnedCustomers cu LEFT JOIN usage u ON cu.customer_id = u.customer_id GROUP BY cu.customer_id ), TotalPayments AS ( SELECT cu.customer_id, SUM(p.amount_paid) AS total_paid FROM ChurnedCustomers cu LEFT JOIN payments p ON cu.customer_id = p.customer_id GROUP BY cu.customer_id ) SELECT cc.first_name || ' ' || cc.last_name AS customer_name, COALESCE(tu.total_usage, 0) AS total_usage, COALESCE(tp.total_paid, 0) AS total_paid FROM ChurnedCustomers cc LEFT JOIN TotalUsage tu ON cc.customer_id = tu.customer_id LEFT JOIN TotalPayments tp ON cc.customer_id = tp.customer_id ORDER BY total_paid DESC, total_usage DESC
gold_sql.mysql: WITH ChurnedCustomers AS (SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name FROM churn AS ch INNER JOIN customers AS c ON ch.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE ch.has_churned = 1), TotalUsage AS (SELECT cu.customer_id, SUM(u.usage_amount) AS total_usage FROM ChurnedCustomers AS cu LEFT JOIN `usage` AS u ON cu.customer_id = u.customer_id GROUP BY cu.customer_id), TotalPayments AS (SELECT cu.customer_id, SUM(p.amount_paid) AS total_paid FROM ChurnedCustomers AS cu LEFT JOIN payments AS p ON cu.customer_id = p.customer_id GROUP BY cu.customer_id) SELECT CONCAT(cc.first_name, ' ', cc.last_name) AS customer_name, COALESCE(tu.total_usage, 0) AS total_usage, COALESCE(tp.total_paid, 0) AS total_paid FROM ChurnedCustomers AS cc LEFT JOIN TotalUsage AS tu ON cc.customer_id = tu.customer_id LEFT JOIN TotalPayments AS tp ON cc.customer_id = tp.customer_id ORDER BY total_paid DESC, total_usage DESC
gold_sql.postgres: WITH ChurnedCustomers AS (SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name FROM churn AS ch INNER JOIN customers AS c ON ch.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE ch.has_churned = 1), TotalUsage AS (SELECT cu.customer_id, SUM(u.usage_amount) AS total_usage FROM ChurnedCustomers AS cu LEFT JOIN usage AS u ON cu.customer_id = u.customer_id GROUP BY cu.customer_id), TotalPayments AS (SELECT cu.customer_id, SUM(p.amount_paid) AS total_paid FROM ChurnedCustomers AS cu LEFT JOIN payments AS p ON cu.customer_id = p.customer_id GROUP BY cu.customer_id) SELECT cc.first_name || ' ' || cc.last_name AS customer_name, COALESCE(tu.total_usage, 0) AS total_usage, COALESCE(tp.total_paid, 0) AS total_paid FROM ChurnedCustomers AS cc LEFT JOIN TotalUsage AS tu ON cc.customer_id = tu.customer_id LEFT JOIN TotalPayments AS tp ON cc.customer_id = tp.customer_id ORDER BY total_paid DESC NULLS LAST, total_usage DESC NULLS LAST

question: Could you provide the titles of albums released after the year 2000 along with the names of their respective artists, sorted alphabetically by album title?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT albums.title, artists.artist_name FROM albums JOIN artists ON albums.artist_id = artists.artist_id WHERE strftime('%Y', albums.release_date) > '2000' ORDER BY albums.title
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT albums.title, artists.artist_name FROM albums JOIN artists ON albums.artist_id = artists.artist_id WHERE DATE_FORMAT(CAST(albums.release_date AS DATETIME), '%Y') > '2000' ORDER BY albums.title
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT albums.title, artists.artist_name FROM albums JOIN artists ON albums.artist_id = artists.artist_id WHERE TO_CHAR(CAST(albums.release_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY') > '2000' ORDER BY albums.title NULLS FIRST

question: Find the names of patients along with the names of their associated diseases and a summary of their engagement details, including the total number of engagements, the number of nutrition plan reviews, the number of precaution consultations, and a list of precautions for each disease.

question: Find the names and preferred weather checking methods of active respondents from the 'South Atlantic' region who are somewhat likely to use a smartwatch for weather checking.

question: Return the names of all models along with their average precision, latest deployment dates, model versions, deployment environments, deployment statuses, usernames and email addresses of the users who last interacted with the models, dates of the last updates, and all comments on the models, and rank the models based on their average precision in descending order.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ModelMetrics AS ( SELECT model_id, AVG(precision) AS avg_precision FROM evaluation_metrics GROUP BY model_id ), LatestDeployments AS ( SELECT model_id, deployment_date, model_version, environment, deployment_status, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY model_id ORDER BY deployment_date DESC) AS latest_deployment FROM model_deployment_history ), UserActivity AS ( SELECT model_id, u.username, u.email, m.updated_at AS last_updated FROM models m INNER JOIN users u ON u.user_id = ( SELECT user_id FROM model_comments WHERE model_id = m.model_id ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1 ) ), ModelComments AS ( SELECT model_id, GROUP_CONCAT(comment, ' | ') AS all_comments FROM model_comments GROUP BY model_id ) SELECT m.model_name, mm.avg_precision, ld.deployment_date, ld.model_version, ld.environment, ld.deployment_status, ua.username, ua.email, ua.last_updated, mc.all_comments, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY mm.avg_precision DESC) AS model_rank FROM models m JOIN ModelMetrics mm ON m.model_id = mm.model_id LEFT JOIN LatestDeployments ld ON m.model_id = ld.model_id AND ld.latest_deployment = 1 JOIN UserActivity ua ON m.model_id = ua.model_id LEFT JOIN ModelComments mc ON m.model_id = mc.model_id ORDER BY model_rank

question:
**User**: I'm looking for detailed information about different document types in our system.
**Assistant**: What kind of information would you like to know about each document type?
**User**: I want to know the category, who created it, when it was created, and the latest version.
**Assistant**: Would you also like to know about the attributes associated with each document type?
**User**: Yes, specifically the active attributes and their values.
**Assistant**: Are you interested in any object type information related to the document types?
**User**: Yes, I'd like to know the object type name, the number of attributes it has, and the average version number of those attributes.
**Assistant**: Is there a particular order you'd like the results to be in?
**User**: Please order them by document type ID.
**Assistant**: OK, I will help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH LatestDocumentVersions AS ( SELECT doc_type_id, MAX(version_nbr) AS latest_version FROM document_versions GROUP BY doc_type_id ), ActiveDocumentAttributes AS ( SELECT dt.doc_type_id, dt.doc_type_name, a.attr_name, a.attr_value FROM document_types dt JOIN attributes a ON dt.doc_type_id = a.doc_type_id WHERE a.active_ind = 'Y' ), ObjectStats AS ( SELECT ot.obj_type_id, ot.obj_type_name, COUNT(oa.obj_attr_id) AS attribute_count, AVG(oa.version_nbr) AS avg_version FROM object_types ot LEFT JOIN object_attributes oa ON ot.obj_type_id = oa.obj_type_id GROUP BY ot.obj_type_id, ot.obj_type_name ) SELECT dt.doc_type_id, dt.doc_type_name, dt.category, dt.created_by, dt.created_date, ldv.latest_version, GROUP_CONCAT(ada.attr_name || ': ' || ada.attr_value) AS active_attributes, os.obj_type_name, os.attribute_count, os.avg_version FROM document_types dt LEFT JOIN LatestDocumentVersions ldv ON dt.doc_type_id = ldv.doc_type_id LEFT JOIN ActiveDocumentAttributes ada ON dt.doc_type_id = ada.doc_type_id LEFT JOIN ObjectStats os ON os.obj_type_name = dt.doc_type_name GROUP BY dt.doc_type_id, dt.doc_type_name, dt.category, dt.created_by, dt.created_date, ldv.latest_version, os.obj_type_name, os.attribute_count, os.avg_version ORDER BY dt.doc_type_id

gold_sql.postgres: WITH LatestDocumentVersions AS (SELECT doc_type_id, MAX(version_nbr) AS latest_version FROM document_versions GROUP BY doc_type_id), ActiveDocumentAttributes AS (SELECT dt.doc_type_id, dt.doc_type_name, a.attr_name, a.attr_value FROM document_types AS dt JOIN attributes AS a ON dt.doc_type_id = a.doc_type_id WHERE a.active_ind = 'Y'), ObjectStats AS (SELECT ot.obj_type_id, ot.obj_type_name, COUNT(oa.obj_attr_id) AS attribute_count, AVG(oa.version_nbr) AS avg_version FROM object_types AS ot LEFT JOIN object_attributes AS oa ON ot.obj_type_id = oa.obj_type_id GROUP BY ot.obj_type_id, ot.obj_type_name) SELECT dt.doc_type_id, dt.doc_type_name, dt.category, dt.created_by, dt.created_date, ldv.latest_version, STRING_AGG(ada.attr_name || ': ' || ada.attr_value, ',') AS active_attributes, os.obj_type_name, os.attribute_count, os.avg_version FROM document_types AS dt LEFT JOIN LatestDocumentVersions AS ldv ON dt.doc_type_id = ldv.doc_type_id LEFT JOIN ActiveDocumentAttributes AS ada ON dt.doc_type_id = ada.doc_type_id LEFT JOIN ObjectStats AS os ON os.obj_type_name = dt.doc_type_name GROUP BY dt.doc_type_id, dt.doc_type_name, dt.category, dt.created_by, dt.created_date, ldv.latest_version, os.obj_type_name, os.attribute_count, os.avg_version ORDER BY dt.doc_type_id NULLS FIRST

question:
**User**: I want to gather information about a top participant involved in robot classes.
**Assistant**: Certainly! Could you specify which participants and what criteria you would like to use to determine the 'top' participant?
**User**: I'm interested in participants who are registered in active robot classes and are part of a team. The one with the highest number of team members should be considered the top participant.
**Assistant**: Understood. Could you also specify which information you would like to retrieve for this top participant?
**User**: Yes, I would like to know their name, email, the team they are part of, the robot class they are registered in, and the category of that class.
**Assistant**: Is there anything else you need?
**User**: No, that covers everything.
**Assistant**: OK, I will help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT p.name AS 'Top Participant', p.email AS 'Email', p.team_name AS 'Team Name', r.robot_class AS 'Robot Class', c.category_name AS 'Category' FROM participants p INNER JOIN robot_classes r ON p.robot_class_id = r.class_id INNER JOIN categories c ON r.category = c.category_name WHERE r.is_active = 1 AND p.team_name IS NOT NULL ORDER BY p.team_member_count DESC LIMIT 1
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT p.name AS `Top Participant`, p.email AS `Email`, p.team_name AS `Team Name`, r.robot_class AS `Robot Class`, c.category_name AS `Category` FROM participants AS p INNER JOIN robot_classes AS r ON p.robot_class_id = r.class_id INNER JOIN categories AS c ON r.category = c.category_name WHERE r.is_active = 1 AND NOT p.team_name IS NULL ORDER BY p.team_member_count DESC LIMIT 1
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT p.name AS "Top Participant", p.email AS "Email", p.team_name AS "Team Name", r.robot_class AS "Robot Class", c.category_name AS "Category" FROM participants AS p INNER JOIN robot_classes AS r ON p.robot_class_id = r.class_id INNER JOIN categories AS c ON r.category = c.category_name WHERE r.is_active = 1 AND NOT p.team_name IS NULL ORDER BY p.team_member_count DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1

question:
**User**: I want to find the top boats in each race.
**Assistant**: Which specific details would you like to know about the top boats?
**User**: I need the boat name, boat type, handicap, owner name, owner email, rank, elapsed time, corrected time, final rank, final points, and the rank by points.
**Assistant**: Do you want to consider all races or only completed ones?
**User**: Only completed races.
**Assistant**: How many top boats per race would you like to see?
**User**: The top three.
**Assistant**: Would you like the results ordered by anything specific?
**User**: Yes, by the race ID and then the rank by points.
**Assistant**: I will now translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RaceStats AS ( SELECT r.race_id, rr.boat_id, rr.rank, rr.elapsed_time, rr.corrected_time, rr.final_rank, rr.final_points, b.boat_name, b.boat_type, b.hcap, o.owner_name, o.owner_email, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY r.race_id ORDER BY rr.final_points DESC) AS rank_by_points FROM races r INNER JOIN race_results rr ON r.race_id = rr.race_id INNER JOIN boats b ON rr.boat_id = b.boat_id INNER JOIN owners o ON b.owner_id = o.owner_id WHERE r.race_status = 'Completed' ), TopBoats AS ( SELECT race_id, boat_id, boat_name, boat_type, hcap, owner_name, owner_email, rank, elapsed_time, corrected_time, final_rank, final_points, rank_by_points FROM RaceStats WHERE rank_by_points <= 3 ) SELECT tb.race_id, tb.boat_name, tb.boat_type, tb.hcap, tb.owner_name, tb.owner_email, tb.rank, tb.elapsed_time, tb.corrected_time, tb.final_rank, tb.final_points, tb.rank_by_points FROM TopBoats tb ORDER BY tb.race_id, tb.rank_by_points

question: I want to know the names of weather stations and their average cloud cover values in 2023, but only for stations where the average cloud cover is greater than 0.5.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT ws.station_name, AVG(cc.cloud_cover) AS average_cloud_cover FROM weather_stations ws JOIN weather_data wd ON ws.station_id = wd.station_id JOIN cloud_cover cc ON wd.data_id = cc.data_id WHERE strftime('%Y', wd.timestamp) = '2023' GROUP BY ws.station_name HAVING AVG(cc.cloud_cover) > 0.5
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT ws.station_name, AVG(cc.cloud_cover) AS average_cloud_cover FROM weather_stations AS ws JOIN weather_data AS wd ON ws.station_id = wd.station_id JOIN cloud_cover AS cc ON wd.data_id = cc.data_id WHERE DATE_FORMAT(CAST(wd.timestamp AS DATETIME), '%Y') = '2023' GROUP BY ws.station_name HAVING AVG(cc.cloud_cover) > 0.5
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT ws.station_name, AVG(cc.cloud_cover) AS average_cloud_cover FROM weather_stations AS ws JOIN weather_data AS wd ON ws.station_id = wd.station_id JOIN cloud_cover AS cc ON wd.data_id = cc.data_id WHERE TO_CHAR(CAST(wd.timestamp AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY') = '2023' GROUP BY ws.station_name HAVING AVG(cc.cloud_cover) > 0.5

question: What is the number of elements in each group of the periodic table, listed in order from the group with the most elements to the group with the least?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT g.group_name, COUNT(pg.element_id) AS element_count FROM groups g JOIN periodic_table pg ON g.group_id = pg.group_id GROUP BY g.group_name ORDER BY element_count DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT g.group_name, COUNT(pg.element_id) AS element_count FROM `groups` AS g JOIN periodic_table AS pg ON g.group_id = pg.group_id GROUP BY g.group_name ORDER BY element_count DESC
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT g.group_name, COUNT(pg.element_id) AS element_count FROM groups AS g JOIN periodic_table AS pg ON g.group_id = pg.group_id GROUP BY g.group_name ORDER BY element_count DESC NULLS LAST

question: Hey! Could you give me a list of the top 10 countries with a happiness score above 7.0 in 2017, along with their happiness scores, ranks, average GDP per capita, and average family support scores? I'd love to see all this info in a single string for each country.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH TopHappiness AS ( SELECT c.country_name, h.happiness_score, h.happiness_rank, e.gdp_per_capita, s.family_score FROM happiness_scores h JOIN countries c ON h.country_id = c.country_id LEFT JOIN economic_factors e ON h.country_id = e.country_id LEFT JOIN social_factors s ON h.country_id = s.country_id WHERE h.year = 2017 AND h.happiness_score > 7.0 ), AggregatedData AS ( SELECT country_name, happiness_score, happiness_rank, AVG(gdp_per_capita) AS avg_gdp_per_capita, AVG(family_score) AS avg_family_score FROM TopHappiness GROUP BY country_name, happiness_score, happiness_rank ORDER BY happiness_score DESC LIMIT 10 ) SELECT GROUP_CONCAT( country_name || ': Happiness Score ' || happiness_score || ', Rank ' || happiness_rank || ', Avg GDP per Capita ' || avg_gdp_per_capita || ', Avg Family Score ' || avg_family_score, '; ' ) AS concatenated_results FROM AggregatedData
gold_sql.mysql: WITH TopHappiness AS (SELECT c.country_name, h.happiness_score, h.happiness_rank, e.gdp_per_capita, s.family_score FROM happiness_scores AS h JOIN countries AS c ON h.country_id = c.country_id LEFT JOIN economic_factors AS e ON h.country_id = e.country_id LEFT JOIN social_factors AS s ON h.country_id = s.country_id WHERE h.year = 2017 AND h.happiness_score > 7.0), AggregatedData AS (SELECT country_name, happiness_score, happiness_rank, AVG(gdp_per_capita) AS avg_gdp_per_capita, AVG(family_score) AS avg_family_score FROM TopHappiness GROUP BY country_name, happiness_score, happiness_rank ORDER BY happiness_score DESC LIMIT 10) SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(country_name, ': Happiness Score ', happiness_score, ', Rank ', happiness_rank, ', Avg GDP per Capita ', avg_gdp_per_capita, ', Avg Family Score ', avg_family_score) SEPARATOR '; ') AS concatenated_results FROM AggregatedData
gold_sql.postgres: WITH TopHappiness AS (SELECT c.country_name, h.happiness_score, h.happiness_rank, e.gdp_per_capita, s.family_score FROM happiness_scores AS h JOIN countries AS c ON h.country_id = c.country_id LEFT JOIN economic_factors AS e ON h.country_id = e.country_id LEFT JOIN social_factors AS s ON h.country_id = s.country_id WHERE h.year = 2017 AND h.happiness_score > 7.0), AggregatedData AS (SELECT country_name, happiness_score, happiness_rank, AVG(gdp_per_capita) AS avg_gdp_per_capita, AVG(family_score) AS avg_family_score FROM TopHappiness GROUP BY country_name, happiness_score, happiness_rank ORDER BY happiness_score DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10) SELECT STRING_AGG(country_name || ': Happiness Score ' || happiness_score || ', Rank ' || happiness_rank || ', Avg GDP per Capita ' || avg_gdp_per_capita || ', Avg Family Score ' || avg_family_score, '; ') AS concatenated_results FROM AggregatedData

question: Could you please calculate the average age group from the survey data? I really need to know the average numerical value of the age ranges.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT AVG( (CAST(SUBSTR(age_group, 1, INSTR(age_group, '-') - 1) AS REAL) + CAST(SUBSTR(age_group, INSTR(age_group, '-') + 1) AS REAL)) / 2 ) AS average_age_group FROM survey_data
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT AVG((CAST(SUBSTRING(age_group, 1, LOCATE('-', age_group) - 1) AS FLOAT) + CAST(SUBSTRING(age_group, LOCATE('-', age_group) + 1) AS FLOAT)) / 2) AS average_age_group FROM survey_data
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT AVG((CAST(SUBSTRING(age_group FROM 1 FOR STRPOS(age_group, '-') - 1) AS REAL) + CAST(SUBSTRING(age_group FROM STRPOS(age_group, '-') + 1) AS REAL)) / NULLIF(2, 0)) AS average_age_group FROM survey_data

question: Hey! Can you help me get a list of all Pokémon along with their abilities and moves? I'd love to see them sorted by their names.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH PokemonAbilities AS ( SELECT pa.pokemon_id, GROUP_CONCAT(a.ability_name, ', ') AS ability_names FROM pokemon_abilities pa JOIN abilities a ON pa.ability_id = a.ability_id GROUP BY pa.pokemon_id ), PokemonMoves AS ( SELECT pm.pokemon_id, GROUP_CONCAT(m.move_name, ', ') AS move_names FROM pokemon_moves pm JOIN moves m ON pm.move_id = m.move_id GROUP BY pm.pokemon_id ) SELECT p.name, IFNULL(pa.ability_names, 'No abilities') AS ability_names, IFNULL(pm.move_names, 'No moves') AS move_names FROM pokemon p LEFT JOIN PokemonAbilities pa ON p.pokemon_id = pa.pokemon_id LEFT JOIN PokemonMoves pm ON p.pokemon_id = pm.pokemon_id ORDER BY p.name
gold_sql.mysql: WITH PokemonAbilities AS (SELECT pa.pokemon_id, GROUP_CONCAT(a.ability_name SEPARATOR ', ') AS ability_names FROM pokemon_abilities AS pa JOIN abilities AS a ON pa.ability_id = a.ability_id GROUP BY pa.pokemon_id), PokemonMoves AS (SELECT pm.pokemon_id, GROUP_CONCAT(m.move_name SEPARATOR ', ') AS move_names FROM pokemon_moves AS pm JOIN moves AS m ON pm.move_id = m.move_id GROUP BY pm.pokemon_id) SELECT p.name, COALESCE(pa.ability_names, 'No abilities') AS ability_names, COALESCE(pm.move_names, 'No moves') AS move_names FROM pokemon AS p LEFT JOIN PokemonAbilities AS pa ON p.pokemon_id = pa.pokemon_id LEFT JOIN PokemonMoves AS pm ON p.pokemon_id = pm.pokemon_id ORDER BY p.name
gold_sql.postgres: WITH PokemonAbilities AS (SELECT pa.pokemon_id, STRING_AGG(a.ability_name, ', ') AS ability_names FROM pokemon_abilities AS pa JOIN abilities AS a ON pa.ability_id = a.ability_id GROUP BY pa.pokemon_id), PokemonMoves AS (SELECT pm.pokemon_id, STRING_AGG(m.move_name, ', ') AS move_names FROM pokemon_moves AS pm JOIN moves AS m ON pm.move_id = m.move_id GROUP BY pm.pokemon_id) SELECT p.name, COALESCE(pa.ability_names, 'No abilities') AS ability_names, COALESCE(pm.move_names, 'No moves') AS move_names FROM pokemon AS p LEFT JOIN PokemonAbilities AS pa ON p.pokemon_id = pa.pokemon_id LEFT JOIN PokemonMoves AS pm ON p.pokemon_id = pm.pokemon_id ORDER BY p.name NULLS FIRST

question: Find the titles of active journals, their average impact factor values, and the number of articles in each, but only for journals with an average impact factor value greater than 2.0.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT j.title AS Journal_Title, AVG(if.impact_factor_value) AS Avg_Impact_Factor, COUNT(a.article_id) AS Num_Articles FROM journals j JOIN impact_factors if ON j.journal_id = if.journal_id JOIN journal_issues ji ON j.journal_id = ji.journal_id JOIN articles a ON ji.issue_id = a.issue_id WHERE j.status = 'active' GROUP BY j.journal_id, j.title HAVING AVG(if.impact_factor_value) > 2.0
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT j.title AS Journal_Title, AVG(`if`.impact_factor_value) AS Avg_Impact_Factor, COUNT(a.article_id) AS Num_Articles FROM journals AS j JOIN impact_factors AS `if` ON j.journal_id = `if`.journal_id JOIN journal_issues AS ji ON j.journal_id = ji.journal_id JOIN articles AS a ON ji.issue_id = a.issue_id WHERE j.status = 'active' GROUP BY j.journal_id, j.title HAVING AVG(`if`.impact_factor_value) > 2.0
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT j.title AS Journal_Title, AVG(if.impact_factor_value) AS Avg_Impact_Factor, COUNT(a.article_id) AS Num_Articles FROM journals AS j JOIN impact_factors AS if ON j.journal_id = if.journal_id JOIN journal_issues AS ji ON j.journal_id = ji.journal_id JOIN articles AS a ON ji.issue_id = a.issue_id WHERE j.status = 'active' GROUP BY j.journal_id, j.title HAVING AVG(if.impact_factor_value) > 2.0

question: Could you tell me the number of attacks conducted by the terrorist group 'ISIS' for each type of attack?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT at.attack_type_name, COUNT(a.attack_id) AS number_of_attacks FROM attacks a JOIN groups g ON a.group_id = g.group_id JOIN attack_types at ON a.attack_type_id = at.attack_type_id WHERE g.group_name = 'ISIS' GROUP BY at.attack_type_name
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT at.attack_type_name, COUNT(a.attack_id) AS number_of_attacks FROM attacks AS a JOIN `groups` AS g ON a.group_id = g.group_id JOIN attack_types AS at ON a.attack_type_id = at.attack_type_id WHERE g.group_name = 'ISIS' GROUP BY at.attack_type_name
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT at.attack_type_name, COUNT(a.attack_id) AS number_of_attacks FROM attacks AS a JOIN groups AS g ON a.group_id = g.group_id JOIN attack_types AS at ON a.attack_type_id = at.attack_type_id WHERE g.group_name = 'ISIS' GROUP BY at.attack_type_name

question: Could you please provide a ranked list of all exits in the 'Office Building' located in 'Othertown', including the exit name, type, capacity, whether it is for emergency use only, the total number of students who exited through each one, the average exit time, and any identified bottlenecks?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH BuildingExits AS ( SELECT b.building_name, e.exit_id, e.exit_name, e.exit_type, e.exit_capacity, e.is_emergency_only, f.floor_id FROM buildings b JOIN floors f ON b.building_id = f.building_id JOIN exits e ON f.floor_id = e.floor_id WHERE b.building_name = 'Office Building' AND b.city = 'Othertown' ), ExitResults AS ( SELECT er.exit_id, SUM(er.number_of_students) AS total_students, AVG(er.average_exit_time) AS average_exit_time, GROUP_CONCAT(er.bottleneck_report) AS bottlenecks FROM simulation_results er JOIN BuildingExits be ON er.exit_id = be.exit_id GROUP BY er.exit_id ), RankedExits AS ( SELECT be.building_name, be.exit_id, be.exit_name, be.exit_type, be.exit_capacity, be.is_emergency_only, er.total_students, er.average_exit_time, er.bottlenecks, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(er.total_students, 0) DESC) AS exit_rank FROM BuildingExits be LEFT JOIN ExitResults er ON be.exit_id = er.exit_id ) SELECT exit_rank, exit_name, exit_type, exit_capacity, is_emergency_only, total_students, average_exit_time, bottlenecks FROM RankedExits
gold_sql.mysql: WITH BuildingExits AS (SELECT b.building_name, e.exit_id, e.exit_name, e.exit_type, e.exit_capacity, e.is_emergency_only, f.floor_id FROM buildings AS b JOIN floors AS f ON b.building_id = f.building_id JOIN exits AS e ON f.floor_id = e.floor_id WHERE b.building_name = 'Office Building' AND b.city = 'Othertown'), ExitResults AS (SELECT er.exit_id, SUM(er.number_of_students) AS total_students, AVG(er.average_exit_time) AS average_exit_time, GROUP_CONCAT(er.bottleneck_report SEPARATOR ',') AS bottlenecks FROM simulation_results AS er JOIN BuildingExits AS be ON er.exit_id = be.exit_id GROUP BY er.exit_id), RankedExits AS (SELECT be.building_name, be.exit_id, be.exit_name, be.exit_type, be.exit_capacity, be.is_emergency_only, er.total_students, er.average_exit_time, er.bottlenecks, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(er.total_students, 0) DESC) AS exit_rank FROM BuildingExits AS be LEFT JOIN ExitResults AS er ON be.exit_id = er.exit_id) SELECT exit_rank, exit_name, exit_type, exit_capacity, is_emergency_only, total_students, average_exit_time, bottlenecks FROM RankedExits
gold_sql.postgres: WITH BuildingExits AS (SELECT b.building_name, e.exit_id, e.exit_name, e.exit_type, e.exit_capacity, e.is_emergency_only, f.floor_id FROM buildings AS b JOIN floors AS f ON b.building_id = f.building_id JOIN exits AS e ON f.floor_id = e.floor_id WHERE b.building_name = 'Office Building' AND b.city = 'Othertown'), ExitResults AS (SELECT er.exit_id, SUM(er.number_of_students) AS total_students, AVG(er.average_exit_time) AS average_exit_time, STRING_AGG(er.bottleneck_report, ',') AS bottlenecks FROM simulation_results AS er JOIN BuildingExits AS be ON er.exit_id = be.exit_id GROUP BY er.exit_id), RankedExits AS (SELECT be.building_name, be.exit_id, be.exit_name, be.exit_type, be.exit_capacity, be.is_emergency_only, er.total_students, er.average_exit_time, er.bottlenecks, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(er.total_students, 0) DESC NULLS LAST) AS exit_rank FROM BuildingExits AS be LEFT JOIN ExitResults AS er ON be.exit_id = er.exit_id) SELECT exit_rank, exit_name, exit_type, exit_capacity, is_emergency_only, total_students, average_exit_time, bottlenecks FROM RankedExits

question: For the event with ID 1, list the names, event names, ranks, and total scores of the top 3 participants.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RankedParticipants AS ( SELECT p.name AS participant_name, e.event_name, r.rank, r.total_score, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY r.total_score DESC) AS participant_rank FROM participants p JOIN rankings r ON p.participant_id = r.participant_id JOIN events e ON r.event_id = e.event_id WHERE e.event_id = 1 ) SELECT participant_name, event_name, rank, total_score FROM RankedParticipants WHERE participant_rank <= 3
gold_sql.mysql: WITH RankedParticipants AS (SELECT p.name AS participant_name, e.event_name, r.`rank`, r.total_score, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY r.total_score DESC) AS participant_rank FROM participants AS p JOIN rankings AS r ON p.participant_id = r.participant_id JOIN events AS e ON r.event_id = e.event_id WHERE e.event_id = 1) SELECT participant_name, event_name, `rank`, total_score FROM RankedParticipants WHERE participant_rank <= 3
gold_sql.postgres: WITH RankedParticipants AS (SELECT p.name AS participant_name, e.event_name, r.rank, r.total_score, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY r.total_score DESC NULLS LAST) AS participant_rank FROM participants AS p JOIN rankings AS r ON p.participant_id = r.participant_id JOIN events AS e ON r.event_id = e.event_id WHERE e.event_id = 1) SELECT participant_name, event_name, rank, total_score FROM RankedParticipants WHERE participant_rank <= 3

question: What are the names of the top-performing subjects in each condition, along with the condition names and success rates, ranked in descending order of success rate, considering only the top 10 results?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH SubjectPerformance AS ( SELECT e.subject_id, e.condition, COUNT(e.experiment_id) AS total_trials, SUM(e.correct) AS correct_trials, CAST(SUM(e.correct) AS REAL) / COUNT(e.experiment_id) AS success_rate FROM experiments e GROUP BY e.subject_id, e.condition ), TopPerformers AS ( SELECT condition, MAX(success_rate) AS success_rate FROM SubjectPerformance GROUP BY condition ), FilteredResults AS ( SELECT sp.subject_id, sp.condition, sp.success_rate, s.subject_name, c.condition_name FROM SubjectPerformance sp JOIN TopPerformers tp ON sp.condition = tp.condition AND sp.success_rate = tp.success_rate JOIN subjects s ON sp.subject_id = s.subject_id JOIN conditions c ON sp.condition = c.condition_id ) SELECT subject_name, condition_name, success_rate FROM FilteredResults ORDER BY success_rate DESC LIMIT 10
gold_sql.mysql: WITH SubjectPerformance AS (SELECT e.subject_id, e.`condition`, COUNT(e.experiment_id) AS total_trials, SUM(e.correct) AS correct_trials, CAST(SUM(e.correct) AS FLOAT) / COUNT(e.experiment_id) AS success_rate FROM experiments AS e GROUP BY e.subject_id, e.`condition`), TopPerformers AS (SELECT `condition`, MAX(success_rate) AS success_rate FROM SubjectPerformance GROUP BY `condition`), FilteredResults AS (SELECT sp.subject_id, sp.`condition`, sp.success_rate, s.subject_name, c.condition_name FROM SubjectPerformance AS sp JOIN TopPerformers AS tp ON sp.`condition` = tp.`condition` AND sp.success_rate = tp.success_rate JOIN subjects AS s ON sp.subject_id = s.subject_id JOIN conditions AS c ON sp.`condition` = c.condition_id) SELECT subject_name, condition_name, success_rate FROM FilteredResults ORDER BY success_rate DESC LIMIT 10
gold_sql.postgres: WITH SubjectPerformance AS (SELECT e.subject_id, e.condition, COUNT(e.experiment_id) AS total_trials, SUM(e.correct) AS correct_trials, CAST(SUM(e.correct) AS REAL) / NULLIF(COUNT(e.experiment_id), 0) AS success_rate FROM experiments AS e GROUP BY e.subject_id, e.condition), TopPerformers AS (SELECT condition, MAX(success_rate) AS success_rate FROM SubjectPerformance GROUP BY condition), FilteredResults AS (SELECT sp.subject_id, sp.condition, sp.success_rate, s.subject_name, c.condition_name FROM SubjectPerformance AS sp JOIN TopPerformers AS tp ON sp.condition = tp.condition AND sp.success_rate = tp.success_rate JOIN subjects AS s ON sp.subject_id = s.subject_id JOIN conditions AS c ON sp.condition = c.condition_id) SELECT subject_name, condition_name, success_rate FROM FilteredResults ORDER BY success_rate DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

question: Hey! Can you show me the titles of journals and their publishers where the journals have an impact factor greater than 2.5, their download metric is more than 150, and the average download value is over 180? I'd love to see them sorted by the highest average download values.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT j.title AS journal_title, p.name AS publisher_name FROM journals j JOIN publishers p ON j.publisher_id = p.publisher_id JOIN impact_factors if ON j.journal_id = if.journal_id JOIN publication_metrics pm ON j.journal_id = pm.journal_id WHERE if.impact_factor_value > 2.5 AND pm.metric_name = 'downloads' AND pm.metric_value > 150 GROUP BY j.title, p.name HAVING AVG(pm.metric_value) > 180 ORDER BY AVG(pm.metric_value) DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT j.title AS journal_title, p.name AS publisher_name FROM journals AS j JOIN publishers AS p ON j.publisher_id = p.publisher_id JOIN impact_factors AS `if` ON j.journal_id = `if`.journal_id JOIN publication_metrics AS pm ON j.journal_id = pm.journal_id WHERE `if`.impact_factor_value > 2.5 AND pm.metric_name = 'downloads' AND pm.metric_value > 150 GROUP BY j.title, p.name HAVING AVG(pm.metric_value) > 180 ORDER BY AVG(pm.metric_value) DESC
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT j.title AS journal_title, p.name AS publisher_name FROM journals AS j JOIN publishers AS p ON j.publisher_id = p.publisher_id JOIN impact_factors AS if ON j.journal_id = if.journal_id JOIN publication_metrics AS pm ON j.journal_id = pm.journal_id WHERE if.impact_factor_value > 2.5 AND pm.metric_name = 'downloads' AND pm.metric_value > 150 GROUP BY j.title, p.name HAVING AVG(pm.metric_value) > 180 ORDER BY AVG(pm.metric_value) DESC NULLS LAST

question: What is a comprehensive summary of each motor's status, location, motor type, fault code, fault description, severity level, category, maintenance actions, latest performance metrics (including speed, temperature, and vibration level), and predictive model details (including model type, accuracy, and last trained date) for all motors, including both faulty and non-faulty motors with the same fault codes, ordered by motor ID?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH LatestPerformance AS ( SELECT motor_id, MAX(timestamp) AS latest_timestamp FROM motor_performance_metrics GROUP BY motor_id ), LatestModel AS ( SELECT motor_id, MAX(last_trained) AS latest_training FROM predictive_maintenance_models GROUP BY motor_id ), MaintenanceActions AS ( SELECT motor_id, GROUP_CONCAT(action_taken, '; ') AS maintenance_actions FROM maintenance_logs GROUP BY motor_id ) SELECT 'Motor ID: ' || m.motor_id || '; Status: ' || m.status || '; Location: ' || m.location || '; Motor Type: ' || m.motor_type || '; Fault Code: ' || COALESCE(f.code, 'None') || '; Fault Description: ' || COALESCE(f.description, 'None') || '; Severity Level: ' || COALESCE(f.severity_level, 'None') || '; Category: ' || COALESCE(f.category, 'None') || '; Maintenance Actions: ' || COALESCE(ma.maintenance_actions, 'None') || '; Latest Performance: ' || COALESCE(mp.timestamp, 'None') || '; Speed: ' || COALESCE(mp.speed, 'None') || '; Temperature: ' || COALESCE(mp.temperature, 'None') || '; Vibration Level: ' || COALESCE(mp.vibration_level, 'None') || '; Predictive Model: ' || COALESCE(pm.model_type, 'None') || '; Model Accuracy: ' || COALESCE(pm.model_accuracy, 'None') || '; Last Trained: ' || COALESCE(pm.last_trained, 'None') AS motor_summary FROM motor_states m LEFT JOIN diagnostic_reports dr ON m.motor_id = dr.motor_id LEFT JOIN fault_codes f ON dr.fault_code_id = f.fault_code_id LEFT JOIN MaintenanceActions ma ON m.motor_id = ma.motor_id LEFT JOIN motor_performance_metrics mp ON m.motor_id = mp.motor_id AND mp.timestamp = ( SELECT latest_timestamp FROM LatestPerformance WHERE motor_id = m.motor_id ) LEFT JOIN predictive_maintenance_models pm ON m.motor_id = pm.motor_id AND pm.last_trained = ( SELECT latest_training FROM LatestModel WHERE motor_id = m.motor_id ) ORDER BY m.motor_id
gold_sql.mysql: WITH LatestPerformance AS (SELECT motor_id, MAX(timestamp) AS latest_timestamp FROM motor_performance_metrics GROUP BY motor_id), LatestModel AS (SELECT motor_id, MAX(last_trained) AS latest_training FROM predictive_maintenance_models GROUP BY motor_id), MaintenanceActions AS (SELECT motor_id, GROUP_CONCAT(action_taken SEPARATOR '; ') AS maintenance_actions FROM maintenance_logs GROUP BY motor_id) SELECT CONCAT('Motor ID: ', m.motor_id, '; Status: ', m.status, '; Location: ', m.location, '; Motor Type: ', m.motor_type, '; Fault Code: ', COALESCE(f.code, 'None'), '; Fault Description: ', COALESCE(f.description, 'None'), '; Severity Level: ', COALESCE(f.severity_level, 'None'), '; Category: ', COALESCE(f.category, 'None'), '; Maintenance Actions: ', COALESCE(ma.maintenance_actions, 'None'), '; Latest Performance: ', COALESCE(mp.timestamp, 'None'), '; Speed: ', COALESCE(mp.speed, 'None'), '; Temperature: ', COALESCE(mp.temperature, 'None'), '; Vibration Level: ', COALESCE(mp.vibration_level, 'None'), '; Predictive Model: ', COALESCE(pm.model_type, 'None'), '; Model Accuracy: ', COALESCE(pm.model_accuracy, 'None'), '; Last Trained: ', COALESCE(pm.last_trained, 'None')) AS motor_summary FROM motor_states AS m LEFT JOIN diagnostic_reports AS dr ON m.motor_id = dr.motor_id LEFT JOIN fault_codes AS f ON dr.fault_code_id = f.fault_code_id LEFT JOIN MaintenanceActions AS ma ON m.motor_id = ma.motor_id LEFT JOIN motor_performance_metrics AS mp ON m.motor_id = mp.motor_id AND mp.timestamp = (SELECT latest_timestamp FROM LatestPerformance WHERE motor_id = m.motor_id) LEFT JOIN predictive_maintenance_models AS pm ON m.motor_id = pm.motor_id AND pm.last_trained = (SELECT latest_training FROM LatestModel WHERE motor_id = m.motor_id) ORDER BY m.motor_id

question: What are all the information about each vessel including their specifications, builder details, registration history, and ownership timeline, ordered by vessel ID?

question: Find the names of regions having over 50 healthcare facilities, last updated in 2023, where the average number of pregnant women registered in the first trimester exceeds 1000, along with the average number of first-trimester registrations and the total number of pregnancies in these regions, ranked by the total number of pregnancies in descending order.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT r.region_name, AVG(m.pregnant_women_registered_first_trimester) AS avg_first_trimester_registration, SUM(m.total_pregnant_women) AS total_pregnancies FROM regions r JOIN maternal_health m ON r.region_id = m.region_id WHERE r.healthcare_facilities > 50 AND strftime('%Y', m.last_updated) = '2023' GROUP BY r.region_name HAVING AVG(m.pregnant_women_registered_first_trimester) > 1000 ORDER BY total_pregnancies DESC

question:
**User**: I want to find information on outbreaks.
**Assistant**: What kind of information about outbreaks are you looking for?
**User**: I need to know the names of the etiology, total number of cases, year, location, dates, and status for each outbreak, as well as any contributing factors, interventions, and reports related to them.
**Assistant**: You want detailed information on each outbreak, including factors and interventions. Do you need this for all outbreaks or just the most severe ones of each etiology type?
**User**: I'm interested in the most severe outbreaks of each type, based on the total number of cases.
**Assistant**: So, you want to rank outbreaks of the same etiology type by their total case count and get the IDs of the top ones. Should these be ordered in any particular way?
**User**: Yes, by their total case count in descending order.
**Assistant**: Alright, I'll help you with that. Just to confirm, you want a list of outbreak IDs for the most severe instance of each etiology type, ordered by the total number of cases in descending order, along with their respective details.
**User**: That's correct.
**Assistant**: OK, I will translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH OutbreakDetails AS ( SELECT o.outbreak_id, e.name AS etiology_name, o.total_cases, o.outbreak_year, l.location_name, o.start_date, o.end_date, o.status FROM outbreaks o JOIN etiologies e ON o.etiology_id = e.etiology_id JOIN locations l ON o.location_id = l.location_id ), FactorDetails AS ( SELECT of.outbreak_id, GROUP_CONCAT(f.factor_description) AS factors FROM outbreak_factors of JOIN factors f ON of.factor_id = f.factor_id GROUP BY of.outbreak_id ), InterventionDetails AS ( SELECT i.outbreak_id, GROUP_CONCAT(i.intervention_type, ', ') AS interventions FROM interventions i GROUP BY i.outbreak_id ), ReportDetails AS ( SELECT orp.outbreak_id, GROUP_CONCAT(ra.agency_name, ', ') AS reporting_agencies FROM outbreak_reports orp JOIN reporting_agencies ra ON orp.agency_id = ra.agency_id GROUP BY orp.outbreak_id ), CombinedOutbreakData AS ( SELECT od.outbreak_id, od.etiology_name, od.total_cases, od.outbreak_year, od.location_name, od.start_date, od.end_date, od.status, fd.factors, id.interventions, rd.reporting_agencies FROM OutbreakDetails od LEFT JOIN FactorDetails fd ON od.outbreak_id = fd.outbreak_id LEFT JOIN InterventionDetails id ON od.outbreak_id = id.outbreak_id LEFT JOIN ReportDetails rd ON od.outbreak_id = rd.outbreak_id ), RankedOutbreaks AS ( SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY etiology_name ORDER BY total_cases DESC) AS row_num FROM CombinedOutbreakData ) SELECT outbreak_id, etiology_name, total_cases, outbreak_year, location_name, start_date, end_date, status, factors, interventions, reporting_agencies FROM RankedOutbreaks WHERE row_num = 1 ORDER BY total_cases DESC

question: Return the names of the top 3 teams in each soccer competition, ranked by the difference between their actual and predicted goal differences, along with the names of the competitions.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH MatchPerformanceCTE AS ( SELECT m.match_id, m.team_id, m.competition_id, CAST(SUBSTR(m.full_time_score, 1, 1) AS INTEGER) - CAST(SUBSTR(m.full_time_score, 3, 1) AS INTEGER) AS actual_goal_difference, p.predicted_goals_scored - p.predicted_goals_conceded AS expected_goal_difference FROM matches m INNER JOIN predictions p ON m.match_id = p.match_id ), TeamPerformanceCTE AS ( SELECT mp.team_id, mp.competition_id, SUM(mp.actual_goal_difference) AS total_actual_goal_difference, SUM(mp.expected_goal_difference) AS total_expected_goal_difference FROM MatchPerformanceCTE mp GROUP BY mp.team_id, mp.competition_id ), TeamComparison AS ( SELECT tp.team_id, tp.competition_id, tp.total_actual_goal_difference, tp.total_expected_goal_difference, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY tp.competition_id ORDER BY (tp.total_actual_goal_difference - tp.total_expected_goal_difference) DESC) AS performance_rank FROM TeamPerformanceCTE tp ) SELECT t.team_name, c.competition_name FROM TeamComparison tc INNER JOIN teams t ON tc.team_id = t.team_id INNER JOIN competitions c ON tc.competition_id = c.competition_id WHERE tc.performance_rank <= 3 ORDER BY c.competition_name, tc.performance_rank

question: Could you tell me the names of the top 3 players with the highest total playtime and the upgrades they have completed?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH PlayerPlaytime AS ( SELECT p.player_id, p.player_name, SUM(gs.duration) AS total_playtime FROM players p JOIN game_sessions gs ON p.player_id = gs.player_id GROUP BY p.player_id, p.player_name ORDER BY total_playtime DESC LIMIT 3 ) SELECT pp.player_name, GROUP_CONCAT(u.upgrade_name) AS completed_upgrades FROM PlayerPlaytime pp JOIN player_upgrades pu ON pp.player_id = pu.player_id JOIN upgrades u ON pu.upgrade_id = u.upgrade_id GROUP BY pp.player_id, pp.player_name

question: Find the vehicle configurations with a clean bill of health that have successfully participated in test runs with flying colors.
external_knowledge: 'successfully participated in test runs with flying colors' refers to a success rate above 75% and test runs that are 'completed'; 'clean bill of health' refers to a vehicle health status of 'good'.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH CompletedTestRuns AS ( SELECT tr.vehicle_config_id FROM test_runs tr WHERE tr.test_run_status = 'completed' AND CAST(SUBSTR(tr.success_rate, 1, INSTR(tr.success_rate, '%') - 1) AS REAL) > 75 ) SELECT DISTINCT ctr.vehicle_config_id FROM CompletedTestRuns ctr INNER JOIN vehicle_health vh ON ctr.vehicle_config_id = vh.vehicle_config_id WHERE vh.health_status = 'good'
gold_sql.mysql: WITH CompletedTestRuns AS (SELECT tr.vehicle_config_id FROM test_runs AS tr WHERE tr.test_run_status = 'completed' AND CAST(SUBSTRING(tr.success_rate, 1, LOCATE('%', tr.success_rate) - 1) AS FLOAT) > 75) SELECT DISTINCT ctr.vehicle_config_id FROM CompletedTestRuns AS ctr INNER JOIN vehicle_health AS vh ON ctr.vehicle_config_id = vh.vehicle_config_id WHERE vh.health_status = 'good'
gold_sql.postgres: WITH CompletedTestRuns AS (SELECT tr.vehicle_config_id FROM test_runs AS tr WHERE tr.test_run_status = 'completed' AND CAST(SUBSTRING(tr.success_rate FROM 1 FOR STRPOS(tr.success_rate, '%') - 1) AS REAL) > 75) SELECT DISTINCT ctr.vehicle_config_id FROM CompletedTestRuns AS ctr INNER JOIN vehicle_health AS vh ON ctr.vehicle_config_id = vh.vehicle_config_id WHERE vh.health_status = 'good'

question: Imagine each school's athletic prowess in passing and rushing as a river that flows into a lake, where the lake represents the cumulative effort of all the reports generated by users. Can you find the school names, their total passing and rushing yards, the names of the users who generated reports, the dates of these reports, and the cumulative total of passing and rushing yards for each report, as the reports are chronologically recorded by the users?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH SchoolStats AS ( SELECT ss.school_id, s.school_name, SUM(CASE WHEN ss.stat_name = 'total_passing_yards' THEN CAST(ss.stat_value AS INTEGER) ELSE 0 END) AS total_passing_yards, SUM(CASE WHEN ss.stat_name = 'total_rushing_yards' THEN CAST(ss.stat_value AS INTEGER) ELSE 0 END) AS total_rushing_yards FROM season_statistics ss JOIN schools s ON ss.school_id = s.school_id GROUP BY ss.school_id, s.school_name ), UserReports AS ( SELECT r.report_id, r.report_date, r.user_id, u.user_name FROM reports r JOIN users u ON r.user_id = u.user_id ) SELECT ss.school_name, ss.total_passing_yards, ss.total_rushing_yards, ur.user_name, ur.report_date, SUM(ss.total_passing_yards + ss.total_rushing_yards) OVER (PARTITION BY ur.report_id ORDER BY ur.user_name) AS cumulative_yards FROM SchoolStats ss JOIN UserReports ur ON ss.school_id = ur.user_id ORDER BY ur.user_name, ur.report_date
gold_sql.mysql: WITH SchoolStats AS (SELECT ss.school_id, s.school_name, SUM(CASE WHEN ss.stat_name = 'total_passing_yards' THEN CAST(ss.stat_value AS SIGNED) ELSE 0 END) AS total_passing_yards, SUM(CASE WHEN ss.stat_name = 'total_rushing_yards' THEN CAST(ss.stat_value AS SIGNED) ELSE 0 END) AS total_rushing_yards FROM season_statistics AS ss JOIN schools AS s ON ss.school_id = s.school_id GROUP BY ss.school_id, s.school_name), UserReports AS (SELECT r.report_id, r.report_date, r.user_id, u.user_name FROM reports AS r JOIN users AS u ON r.user_id = u.user_id) SELECT ss.school_name, ss.total_passing_yards, ss.total_rushing_yards, ur.user_name, ur.report_date, SUM(ss.total_passing_yards + ss.total_rushing_yards) OVER (PARTITION BY ur.report_id ORDER BY ur.user_name) AS cumulative_yards FROM SchoolStats AS ss JOIN UserReports AS ur ON ss.school_id = ur.user_id ORDER BY ur.user_name, ur.report_date
gold_sql.postgres: WITH SchoolStats AS (SELECT ss.school_id, s.school_name, SUM(CASE WHEN ss.stat_name = 'total_passing_yards' THEN CAST(ss.stat_value AS INT) ELSE 0 END) AS total_passing_yards, SUM(CASE WHEN ss.stat_name = 'total_rushing_yards' THEN CAST(ss.stat_value AS INT) ELSE 0 END) AS total_rushing_yards FROM season_statistics AS ss JOIN schools AS s ON ss.school_id = s.school_id GROUP BY ss.school_id, s.school_name), UserReports AS (SELECT r.report_id, r.report_date, r.user_id, u.user_name FROM reports AS r JOIN users AS u ON r.user_id = u.user_id) SELECT ss.school_name, ss.total_passing_yards, ss.total_rushing_yards, ur.user_name, ur.report_date, SUM(ss.total_passing_yards + ss.total_rushing_yards) OVER (PARTITION BY ur.report_id ORDER BY ur.user_name NULLS FIRST) AS cumulative_yards FROM SchoolStats AS ss JOIN UserReports AS ur ON ss.school_id = ur.user_id ORDER BY ur.user_name NULLS FIRST, ur.report_date NULLS FIRST

question: Could you provide the latest evaluation metrics (including epoch, training loss, validation loss, accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, AUC, and mean squared error) along with hyperparameters and experiment information (including username, experiment name, and status) for each model?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH LatestEvaluationMetrics AS ( SELECT e.model_id, e.epoch, e.train_loss, e.valid_loss, e.accuracy, e.precision, e.recall, e.f1_score, e.auc, e.mean_squared_error, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY e.model_id ORDER BY e.epoch DESC) AS rn FROM evaluation_metrics e ), ModelHyperparameters AS ( SELECT h.model_id, GROUP_CONCAT(h.hyperparameter_name || ': ' || h.hyperparameter_value, ', ') as hyperparameters FROM hyperparameters h GROUP BY h.model_id ), ExperimentsInfo AS ( SELECT ex.experiment_id, ex.model_id, u.username, ex.experiment_name, ex.status FROM experiments ex INNER JOIN users u ON ex.user_id = u.user_id ) SELECT m.model_name, le.epoch, le.train_loss, le.valid_loss, le.accuracy, le.precision, le.recall, le.f1_score, le.auc, le.mean_squared_error, mh.hyperparameters, ei.username, ei.experiment_name, ei.status FROM models m JOIN LatestEvaluationMetrics le ON m.model_id = le.model_id AND le.rn = 1 JOIN ModelHyperparameters mh ON m.model_id = mh.model_id JOIN experiment_models em ON m.model_id = em.model_id JOIN ExperimentsInfo ei ON em.experiment_id = ei.experiment_id
gold_sql.mysql: WITH LatestEvaluationMetrics AS (SELECT e.model_id, e.epoch, e.train_loss, e.valid_loss, e.accuracy, e.`precision`, e.recall, e.f1_score, e.auc, e.mean_squared_error, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY e.model_id ORDER BY e.epoch DESC) AS rn FROM evaluation_metrics AS e), ModelHyperparameters AS (SELECT h.model_id, GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(h.hyperparameter_name, ': ', h.hyperparameter_value) SEPARATOR ', ') AS hyperparameters FROM hyperparameters AS h GROUP BY h.model_id), ExperimentsInfo AS (SELECT ex.experiment_id, ex.model_id, u.username, ex.experiment_name, ex.status FROM experiments AS ex INNER JOIN users AS u ON ex.user_id = u.user_id) SELECT m.model_name, le.epoch, le.train_loss, le.valid_loss, le.accuracy, le.`precision`, le.recall, le.f1_score, le.auc, le.mean_squared_error, mh.hyperparameters, ei.username, ei.experiment_name, ei.status FROM models AS m JOIN LatestEvaluationMetrics AS le ON m.model_id = le.model_id AND le.rn = 1 JOIN ModelHyperparameters AS mh ON m.model_id = mh.model_id JOIN experiment_models AS em ON m.model_id = em.model_id JOIN ExperimentsInfo AS ei ON em.experiment_id = ei.experiment_id
gold_sql.postgres: WITH LatestEvaluationMetrics AS (SELECT e.model_id, e.epoch, e.train_loss, e.valid_loss, e.accuracy, e.precision, e.recall, e.f1_score, e.auc, e.mean_squared_error, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY e.model_id ORDER BY e.epoch DESC NULLS LAST) AS rn FROM evaluation_metrics AS e), ModelHyperparameters AS (SELECT h.model_id, STRING_AGG(h.hyperparameter_name || ': ' || h.hyperparameter_value, ', ') AS hyperparameters FROM hyperparameters AS h GROUP BY h.model_id), ExperimentsInfo AS (SELECT ex.experiment_id, ex.model_id, u.username, ex.experiment_name, ex.status FROM experiments AS ex INNER JOIN users AS u ON ex.user_id = u.user_id) SELECT m.model_name, le.epoch, le.train_loss, le.valid_loss, le.accuracy, le.precision, le.recall, le.f1_score, le.auc, le.mean_squared_error, mh.hyperparameters, ei.username, ei.experiment_name, ei.status FROM models AS m JOIN LatestEvaluationMetrics AS le ON m.model_id = le.model_id AND le.rn = 1 JOIN ModelHyperparameters AS mh ON m.model_id = mh.model_id JOIN experiment_models AS em ON m.model_id = em.model_id JOIN ExperimentsInfo AS ei ON em.experiment_id = ei.experiment_id

question: Find all configuration details, including configuration ID, signal name, component name, project name, creator and updater full names, signal type and description, and relevant notification details, specifically the notified user's full name, notification message, and creation date, for all configurations, ordered by configuration ID.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ConfigDetails AS ( SELECT c.config_id, c.signal_id, c.component_id, c.project_id, c.config_version, c.created_at, c.updated_at, c.created_by, c.updated_by, s.signal_name, co.component_name, p.project_name, u1.first_name AS creator_first_name, u1.last_name AS creator_last_name, u2.first_name AS updater_first_name, u2.last_name AS updater_last_name, st.type_name, st.description AS type_description FROM configurations c JOIN signals s ON c.signal_id = s.signal_id JOIN components co ON c.component_id = co.component_id JOIN users u1 ON c.created_by = u1.user_id JOIN users u2 ON c.updated_by = u2.user_id JOIN projects p ON c.project_id = p.project_id JOIN signal_types st ON s.type = st.type_name ), NotificationDetails AS ( SELECT n.notification_id, n.user_id, n.message, n.created_at AS notification_created_at, u.first_name AS notification_user_first_name, u.last_name AS notification_user_last_name FROM notifications n JOIN users u ON n.user_id = u.user_id ), FinalResult AS ( SELECT cd.config_id, cd.signal_name, cd.component_name, cd.project_name, cd.creator_first_name || ' ' || cd.creator_last_name AS creator_full_name, cd.updater_first_name || ' ' || cd.updater_last_name AS updater_full_name, cd.type_name, cd.type_description, n.notification_user_first_name || ' ' || n.notification_user_last_name AS notified_user_full_name, n.message AS notification_message, n.notification_created_at FROM ConfigDetails cd LEFT JOIN NotificationDetails n ON n.message LIKE '%' || cd.signal_name || '%' ) SELECT config_id || ' | ' || signal_name || ' | ' || component_name || ' | ' || project_name || ' | ' || creator_full_name || ' | ' || updater_full_name || ' | ' || type_name || ' | ' || IFNULL(type_description, 'N/A') || ' | ' || IFNULL(notified_user_full_name, 'N/A') || ' | ' || IFNULL(notification_message, 'No notification') || ' | ' || IFNULL(notification_created_at, 'N/A') AS config_details FROM FinalResult ORDER BY config_id

question: Could you provide a list of teams participating in the 'World Cup qualifiers' competition, including their total matches, total wins, goal difference, average attendance, and indicate whether their reports have been accessed by analysts, ranked by their goal difference in descending order?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH CompetitionCTE AS ( SELECT c.competition_id FROM competitions c WHERE c.competition_name = 'World Cup qualifiers' ), TeamPerformanceCTE AS ( SELECT m.team_id, t.team_name, COUNT(*) AS total_matches, SUM(CASE WHEN m.result = 'win' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS total_wins, SUM(CASE WHEN m.result = 'win' THEN (CAST(SUBSTR(m.full_time_score, 1, 1) AS INTEGER) - CAST(SUBSTR(m.full_time_score, 3, 1) AS INTEGER)) WHEN m.result = 'loss' THEN (CAST(SUBSTR(m.full_time_score, 3, 1) AS INTEGER) - CAST(SUBSTR(m.full_time_score, 1, 1) AS INTEGER)) ELSE 0 END) AS goal_difference, AVG(m.attendance) AS avg_attendance FROM matches m JOIN teams t ON m.team_id = t.team_id JOIN CompetitionCTE cc ON m.competition_id = cc.competition_id GROUP BY m.team_id, t.team_name ), AccessedReportsCTE AS ( SELECT r.team_id FROM reports r JOIN user_access ua ON r.report_id = ua.report_id JOIN users u ON ua.user_id = u.user_id WHERE u.role = 'analyst' GROUP BY r.team_id ) SELECT tp.team_name, tp.total_matches, tp.total_wins, tp.goal_difference, tp.avg_attendance, CASE WHEN ar.team_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'Accessed by Analysts' ELSE 'Not Accessed' END AS report_access_status FROM TeamPerformanceCTE tp LEFT JOIN AccessedReportsCTE ar ON tp.team_id = ar.team_id ORDER BY tp.goal_difference DESC
gold_sql.mysql: WITH CompetitionCTE AS (SELECT c.competition_id FROM competitions AS c WHERE c.competition_name = 'World Cup qualifiers'), TeamPerformanceCTE AS (SELECT m.team_id, t.team_name, COUNT(*) AS total_matches, SUM(CASE WHEN m.result = 'win' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS total_wins, SUM(CASE WHEN m.result = 'win' THEN (CAST(SUBSTRING(m.full_time_score, 1, 1) AS SIGNED) - CAST(SUBSTRING(m.full_time_score, 3, 1) AS SIGNED)) WHEN m.result = 'loss' THEN (CAST(SUBSTRING(m.full_time_score, 3, 1) AS SIGNED) - CAST(SUBSTRING(m.full_time_score, 1, 1) AS SIGNED)) ELSE 0 END) AS goal_difference, AVG(m.attendance) AS avg_attendance FROM matches AS m JOIN teams AS t ON m.team_id = t.team_id JOIN CompetitionCTE AS cc ON m.competition_id = cc.competition_id GROUP BY m.team_id, t.team_name), AccessedReportsCTE AS (SELECT r.team_id FROM reports AS r JOIN user_access AS ua ON r.report_id = ua.report_id JOIN users AS u ON ua.user_id = u.user_id WHERE u.role = 'analyst' GROUP BY r.team_id) SELECT tp.team_name, tp.total_matches, tp.total_wins, tp.goal_difference, tp.avg_attendance, CASE WHEN NOT ar.team_id IS NULL THEN 'Accessed by Analysts' ELSE 'Not Accessed' END AS report_access_status FROM TeamPerformanceCTE AS tp LEFT JOIN AccessedReportsCTE AS ar ON tp.team_id = ar.team_id ORDER BY tp.goal_difference DESC
gold_sql.postgres: WITH CompetitionCTE AS (SELECT c.competition_id FROM competitions AS c WHERE c.competition_name = 'World Cup qualifiers'), TeamPerformanceCTE AS (SELECT m.team_id, t.team_name, COUNT(*) AS total_matches, SUM(CASE WHEN m.result = 'win' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS total_wins, SUM(CASE WHEN m.result = 'win' THEN (CAST(SUBSTRING(m.full_time_score FROM 1 FOR 1) AS INT) - CAST(SUBSTRING(m.full_time_score FROM 3 FOR 1) AS INT)) WHEN m.result = 'loss' THEN (CAST(SUBSTRING(m.full_time_score FROM 3 FOR 1) AS INT) - CAST(SUBSTRING(m.full_time_score FROM 1 FOR 1) AS INT)) ELSE 0 END) AS goal_difference, AVG(m.attendance) AS avg_attendance FROM matches AS m JOIN teams AS t ON m.team_id = t.team_id JOIN CompetitionCTE AS cc ON m.competition_id = cc.competition_id GROUP BY m.team_id, t.team_name), AccessedReportsCTE AS (SELECT r.team_id FROM reports AS r JOIN user_access AS ua ON r.report_id = ua.report_id JOIN users AS u ON ua.user_id = u.user_id WHERE u.role = 'analyst' GROUP BY r.team_id) SELECT tp.team_name, tp.total_matches, tp.total_wins, tp.goal_difference, tp.avg_attendance, CASE WHEN NOT ar.team_id IS NULL THEN 'Accessed by Analysts' ELSE 'Not Accessed' END AS report_access_status FROM TeamPerformanceCTE AS tp LEFT JOIN AccessedReportsCTE AS ar ON tp.team_id = ar.team_id ORDER BY tp.goal_difference DESC NULLS LAST

question: Which teams, in their ascendant journey through the league ranks, have American players on their roster who played games in the year 2023, and what is the vibrant tapestry of details surrounding these teams, their players, and the games they've participated in?
external_knowledge:
- "ascendant journey through the league ranks" refers to teams being ordered by their current ranking in the league.
- "vibrant tapestry of details" includes team information, player specifics, and game-related data.
- "games they've participated in" specifically refers to games played in the year 2023.
- "American players" are those with a nationality specified as 'American'.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT t.team_name, t.position, t.home_stadium, t.head_coach, t.established_date, p.first_name, p.last_name, p.position, p.date_of_birth, p.nationality, g.opponent_id, g.game_date, g.score, g.result, g.game_duration, g.attendance FROM teams t INNER JOIN players p ON t.team_id = p.team_id INNER JOIN games g ON t.team_id = g.team_id WHERE p.nationality = 'American' AND strftime('%Y', g.game_date) = '2023' ORDER BY t.position ASC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT t.team_name, t.position, t.home_stadium, t.head_coach, t.established_date, p.first_name, p.last_name, p.position, p.date_of_birth, p.nationality, g.opponent_id, g.game_date, g.score, g.result, g.game_duration, g.attendance FROM teams AS t INNER JOIN players AS p ON t.team_id = p.team_id INNER JOIN games AS g ON t.team_id = g.team_id WHERE p.nationality = 'American' AND DATE_FORMAT(CAST(g.game_date AS DATETIME), '%Y') = '2023' ORDER BY t.position ASC
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT t.team_name, t.position, t.home_stadium, t.head_coach, t.established_date, p.first_name, p.last_name, p.position, p.date_of_birth, p.nationality, g.opponent_id, g.game_date, g.score, g.result, g.game_duration, g.attendance FROM teams AS t INNER JOIN players AS p ON t.team_id = p.team_id INNER JOIN games AS g ON t.team_id = g.team_id WHERE p.nationality = 'American' AND TO_CHAR(CAST(g.game_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY') = '2023' ORDER BY t.position ASC NULLS FIRST

question:
**User**: I'm looking for some information on climate datasets.
**Assistant**: Sure! Could you specify which datasets you are interested in?
**User**: I need details about the datasets accessed by researchers from the University of California.
**Assistant**: Okay. Would you like to know about all datasets accessed by these researchers, or just the most recently accessed one?
**User**: Just the most recently accessed one.
**Assistant**: Alright. What specific information would you like to retrieve for this dataset?
**User**: I need the dataset name, the variables it includes, the update frequency, a brief description, and information about the variables like their names and descriptions.
**Assistant**: Is there any other information you would like to include in your query?
**User**: No, that covers everything I need.
**Assistant**: Understood. I will help you formulate your request into an SQL query to get the information you need.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT d.dataset_name, d.variables, d.update_frequency, d.description, v.variable_name, v.description AS variable_description FROM datasets d JOIN access_logs a ON d.dataset_id = a.dataset_id JOIN users u ON a.user_id = u.user_id JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT variable_name, description FROM variables) v WHERE u.institution = 'University of California' AND u.role = 'researcher' AND d.variables LIKE '%' || v.variable_name || '%' ORDER BY a.access_date DESC LIMIT 1
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT d.dataset_name, d.variables, d.update_frequency, d.description, v.variable_name, v.description AS variable_description FROM datasets AS d JOIN access_logs AS a ON d.dataset_id = a.dataset_id JOIN users AS u ON a.user_id = u.user_id, (SELECT DISTINCT variable_name, description FROM variables) AS v WHERE u.institution = 'University of California' AND u.role = 'researcher' AND d.variables LIKE CONCAT('%', v.variable_name, '%') ORDER BY a.access_date DESC LIMIT 1
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT d.dataset_name, d.variables, d.update_frequency, d.description, v.variable_name, v.description AS variable_description FROM datasets AS d JOIN access_logs AS a ON d.dataset_id = a.dataset_id JOIN users AS u ON a.user_id = u.user_id, (SELECT DISTINCT variable_name, description FROM variables) AS v WHERE u.institution = 'University of California' AND u.role = 'researcher' AND d.variables LIKE '%' || v.variable_name || '%' ORDER BY a.access_date DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1

question:
**User**: I want to find some information about movies.
**Assistant**: What type of information are you looking for about movies?
**User**: I want to know the title of the movie, the genre, the cast members, the characters they played, and the year the movie was released.
**Assistant**: Do you want to filter the movies by any specific release years?
**User**: Yes, I want movies released between 2000 and 2020.
**Assistant**: Are you interested in specific genres?
**User**: Yes, I'm interested in Science Fiction and Drama movies.
**Assistant**: Would you like to know any additional details about these movies?
**User**: Yes, what is the average year that these movies received awards?
**Assistant**: Do you want to include movies that have not received any awards?
**User**: No, I only want movies that have received at least one award.
**Assistant**: How would you like the results to be ordered?
**User**: Order them by release year and then by the average year that awards were received.
**Assistant**: I will help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT m.title AS movie_title, g.genre_name AS genre, cm.full_name AS cast_member_name, mc.character_name AS character, m.release_year AS release_year, AVG(ma.year) AS average_award_year FROM movies m INNER JOIN movie_genres mg ON m.movie_id = mg.movie_id INNER JOIN genres g ON mg.genre_id = g.genre_id INNER JOIN movie_cast mc ON m.movie_id = mc.movie_id INNER JOIN cast_members cm ON mc.cast_member_id = cm.cast_member_id INNER JOIN movie_awards ma ON m.movie_id = ma.movie_id WHERE m.release_year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2020 AND g.genre_name IN ('Science Fiction', 'Drama') GROUP BY m.title, g.genre_name, cm.full_name, mc.character_name, m.release_year ORDER BY m.release_year, average_award_year
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT m.title AS movie_title, g.genre_name AS genre, cm.full_name AS cast_member_name, mc.character_name AS `character`, m.release_year AS release_year, AVG(ma.year) AS average_award_year FROM movies AS m INNER JOIN movie_genres AS mg ON m.movie_id = mg.movie_id INNER JOIN genres AS g ON mg.genre_id = g.genre_id INNER JOIN movie_cast AS mc ON m.movie_id = mc.movie_id INNER JOIN cast_members AS cm ON mc.cast_member_id = cm.cast_member_id INNER JOIN movie_awards AS ma ON m.movie_id = ma.movie_id WHERE m.release_year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2020 AND g.genre_name IN ('Science Fiction', 'Drama') GROUP BY m.title, g.genre_name, cm.full_name, mc.character_name, m.release_year ORDER BY m.release_year, average_award_year
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT m.title AS movie_title, g.genre_name AS genre, cm.full_name AS cast_member_name, mc.character_name AS character, m.release_year AS release_year, AVG(ma.year) AS average_award_year FROM movies AS m INNER JOIN movie_genres AS mg ON m.movie_id = mg.movie_id INNER JOIN genres AS g ON mg.genre_id = g.genre_id INNER JOIN movie_cast AS mc ON m.movie_id = mc.movie_id INNER JOIN cast_members AS cm ON mc.cast_member_id = cm.cast_member_id INNER JOIN movie_awards AS ma ON m.movie_id = ma.movie_id WHERE m.release_year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2020 AND g.genre_name IN ('Science Fiction', 'Drama') GROUP BY m.title, g.genre_name, cm.full_name, mc.character_name, m.release_year ORDER BY m.release_year NULLS FIRST, average_award_year NULLS FIRST

question: What is the average satisfaction level, and what are the common suggestions for improvement for students in Course 1?
external_knowledge: Course 1 refers to a specific course identified by the unique identifier `course_id` in the database; Satisfaction level is measured on a scale of 1-10; Improvement suggestions are provided by students to enhance the course.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT AVG(f.satisfaction_level) AS average_satisfaction, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT f.improvement_suggestions) AS common_suggestions FROM feedback f WHERE f.course_id = 1
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT AVG(f.satisfaction_level) AS average_satisfaction, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT f.improvement_suggestions SEPARATOR ',') AS common_suggestions FROM feedback AS f WHERE f.course_id = 1
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT AVG(f.satisfaction_level) AS average_satisfaction, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT f.improvement_suggestions, ',') AS common_suggestions FROM feedback AS f WHERE f.course_id = 1
