question: Could you provide a list of the most critical defects for each module in the 'ExampleCodebase', including the module names and the defect types, formatted as a single concatenated string?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RankedDefects AS ( SELECT m.name AS module_name, dt.name AS defect_type_name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY m.id ORDER BY dd.flash_score DESC, dd.fix_freq DESC) AS rn FROM defect_data dd JOIN module m ON dd.module_id = m.id JOIN defect_type dt ON dd.defect_type_id = dt.id JOIN codebase c ON m.codebase_id = c.id WHERE c.name = 'ExampleCodebase' ) SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(module_name || ' - ' || defect_type_name, ' - ') FROM RankedDefects WHERE rn = 1
gold_sql.mysql: WITH RankedDefects AS (SELECT m.name AS module_name, dt.name AS defect_type_name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY m.id ORDER BY dd.flash_score DESC, dd.fix_freq DESC) AS rn FROM defect_data AS dd JOIN module AS m ON dd.module_id = m.id JOIN defect_type AS dt ON dd.defect_type_id = dt.id JOIN codebase AS c ON m.codebase_id = c.id WHERE c.name = 'ExampleCodebase') SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(module_name, ' - ', defect_type_name) SEPARATOR ' - ') FROM RankedDefects WHERE rn = 1
gold_sql.postgres: WITH RankedDefects AS (SELECT m.name AS module_name, dt.name AS defect_type_name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY m.id ORDER BY dd.flash_score DESC NULLS LAST, dd.fix_freq DESC NULLS LAST) AS rn FROM defect_data AS dd JOIN module AS m ON dd.module_id = m.id JOIN defect_type AS dt ON dd.defect_type_id = dt.id JOIN codebase AS c ON m.codebase_id = c.id WHERE c.name = 'ExampleCodebase') SELECT STRING_AGG(module_name || ' - ' || defect_type_name, ' - ') FROM RankedDefects WHERE rn = 1

question: Find the names, years, and manufacturers of all car models, along with their total quantity sold, total revenue, average sale price, total discount amount, average customer ratings, review counts, sample reviews, lists of features (including safety, comfort, and technology features), warranty durations, warranty coverage descriptions, user roles, and contact information for users in each role.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH CarSales AS ( SELECT c.car_id, c.car_name, c.year, m.manufacturer_name, SUM(s.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(s.quantity * s.price) AS total_revenue, AVG(s.price) AS avg_sale_price, SUM(s.quantity * s.price * s.discount / 100) AS total_discount_amount FROM cars c JOIN sales s ON c.car_id = s.car_id JOIN manufacturers m ON c.manufacturer_id = m.manufacturer_id GROUP BY c.car_id, c.car_name, c.year, m.manufacturer_name ), CarReviews AS ( SELECT r.car_id, AVG(r.rating) AS avg_rating, COUNT(r.review_id) AS review_count, GROUP_CONCAT(r.review_text, ', ') AS sample_reviews FROM reviews r GROUP BY r.car_id ), CarFeatures AS ( SELECT f.car_id, GROUP_CONCAT(f.feature_name, ', ') AS features_list, GROUP_CONCAT(CASE WHEN f.feature_group = 'safety' THEN f.feature_name ELSE '' END, ', ') AS safety_features, GROUP_CONCAT(CASE WHEN f.feature_group = 'comfort' THEN f.feature_name ELSE '' END, ', ') AS comfort_features, GROUP_CONCAT(CASE WHEN f.feature_group = 'technology' THEN f.feature_name ELSE '' END, ', ') AS tech_features FROM features f GROUP BY f.car_id ), CarWarranty AS ( SELECT w.car_id, w.duration_years, w.coverage_description FROM warranty w ), UserFeedback AS ( SELECT u.role, GROUP_CONCAT(u.email, ', ') AS user_emails, GROUP_CONCAT(u.phone, ', ') AS user_phones FROM users u GROUP BY u.role ) SELECT cs.car_name, cs.year, cs.manufacturer_name, cs.total_quantity_sold, cs.total_revenue, cs.avg_sale_price, cs.total_discount_amount, cr.avg_rating, cr.review_count, cr.sample_reviews, cf.features_list, cf.safety_features, cf.comfort_features, cf.tech_features, cw.duration_years, cw.coverage_description, uf.role, uf.user_emails, uf.user_phones FROM CarSales cs LEFT JOIN CarReviews cr ON cs.car_id = cr.car_id LEFT JOIN CarFeatures cf ON cs.car_id = cf.car_id LEFT JOIN CarWarranty cw ON cs.car_id = cw.car_id CROSS JOIN UserFeedback uf
gold_sql.mysql: WITH CarSales AS (SELECT c.car_id, c.car_name, c.year, m.manufacturer_name, SUM(s.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(s.quantity * s.price) AS total_revenue, AVG(s.price) AS avg_sale_price, SUM(s.quantity * s.price * s.discount / 100) AS total_discount_amount FROM cars AS c JOIN sales AS s ON c.car_id = s.car_id JOIN manufacturers AS m ON c.manufacturer_id = m.manufacturer_id GROUP BY c.car_id, c.car_name, c.year, m.manufacturer_name), CarReviews AS (SELECT r.car_id, AVG(r.rating) AS avg_rating, COUNT(r.review_id) AS review_count, GROUP_CONCAT(r.review_text SEPARATOR ', ') AS sample_reviews FROM reviews AS r GROUP BY r.car_id), CarFeatures AS (SELECT f.car_id, GROUP_CONCAT(f.feature_name SEPARATOR ', ') AS features_list, GROUP_CONCAT(CASE WHEN f.feature_group = 'safety' THEN f.feature_name ELSE '' END SEPARATOR ', ') AS safety_features, GROUP_CONCAT(CASE WHEN f.feature_group = 'comfort' THEN f.feature_name ELSE '' END SEPARATOR ', ') AS comfort_features, GROUP_CONCAT(CASE WHEN f.feature_group = 'technology' THEN f.feature_name ELSE '' END SEPARATOR ', ') AS tech_features FROM features AS f GROUP BY f.car_id), CarWarranty AS (SELECT w.car_id, w.duration_years, w.coverage_description FROM warranty AS w), UserFeedback AS (SELECT u.role, GROUP_CONCAT(u.email SEPARATOR ', ') AS user_emails, GROUP_CONCAT(u.phone SEPARATOR ', ') AS user_phones FROM users AS u GROUP BY u.role) SELECT cs.car_name, cs.year, cs.manufacturer_name, cs.total_quantity_sold, cs.total_revenue, cs.avg_sale_price, cs.total_discount_amount, cr.avg_rating, cr.review_count, cr.sample_reviews, cf.features_list, cf.safety_features, cf.comfort_features, cf.tech_features, cw.duration_years, cw.coverage_description, uf.role, uf.user_emails, uf.user_phones FROM CarSales AS cs LEFT JOIN CarReviews AS cr ON cs.car_id = cr.car_id LEFT JOIN CarFeatures AS cf ON cs.car_id = cf.car_id LEFT JOIN CarWarranty AS cw ON cs.car_id = cw.car_id CROSS JOIN UserFeedback AS uf
gold_sql.postgres: WITH CarSales AS (SELECT c.car_id, c.car_name, c.year, m.manufacturer_name, SUM(s.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(s.quantity * s.price) AS total_revenue, AVG(s.price) AS avg_sale_price, SUM(s.quantity * s.price * s.discount / NULLIF(100, 0)) AS total_discount_amount FROM cars AS c JOIN sales AS s ON c.car_id = s.car_id JOIN manufacturers AS m ON c.manufacturer_id = m.manufacturer_id GROUP BY c.car_id, c.car_name, c.year, m.manufacturer_name), CarReviews AS (SELECT r.car_id, AVG(r.rating) AS avg_rating, COUNT(r.review_id) AS review_count, STRING_AGG(r.review_text, ', ') AS sample_reviews FROM reviews AS r GROUP BY r.car_id), CarFeatures AS (SELECT f.car_id, STRING_AGG(f.feature_name, ', ') AS features_list, STRING_AGG(CASE WHEN f.feature_group = 'safety' THEN f.feature_name ELSE '' END, ', ') AS safety_features, STRING_AGG(CASE WHEN f.feature_group = 'comfort' THEN f.feature_name ELSE '' END, ', ') AS comfort_features, STRING_AGG(CASE WHEN f.feature_group = 'technology' THEN f.feature_name ELSE '' END, ', ') AS tech_features FROM features AS f GROUP BY f.car_id), CarWarranty AS (SELECT w.car_id, w.duration_years, w.coverage_description FROM warranty AS w), UserFeedback AS (SELECT u.role, STRING_AGG(u.email, ', ') AS user_emails, STRING_AGG(u.phone, ', ') AS user_phones FROM users AS u GROUP BY u.role) SELECT cs.car_name, cs.year, cs.manufacturer_name, cs.total_quantity_sold, cs.total_revenue, cs.avg_sale_price, cs.total_discount_amount, cr.avg_rating, cr.review_count, cr.sample_reviews, cf.features_list, cf.safety_features, cf.comfort_features, cf.tech_features, cw.duration_years, cw.coverage_description, uf.role, uf.user_emails, uf.user_phones FROM CarSales AS cs LEFT JOIN CarReviews AS cr ON cs.car_id = cr.car_id LEFT JOIN CarFeatures AS cf ON cs.car_id = cf.car_id LEFT JOIN CarWarranty AS cw ON cs.car_id = cw.car_id CROSS JOIN UserFeedback AS uf

question:
**User**: I want to analyze property sales data over time, considering median income and market sentiment.
**Assistant**: Sure! Could you specify what kind of analysis you're looking for? For example, are you interested in average prices, trends over time, or specific demographic areas?
**User**: I want to see the average adjusted sale price over time, where the adjusted sale price is the sale price divided by the median income.
**Assistant**: Got it. Would you like to see this data broken down by any specific demographic areas or market sentiments?
**User**: No, just the overall trend over time.
**Assistant**: Understood. I will prepare a query that calculates the average adjusted sale price over time, grouped by month. Is there anything else you need?
**User**: No, that's all.
**Assistant**: OK, I will help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', sale_date) AS sale_month, AVG(sale_price / median_income) AS avg_adjusted_sale_price FROM property_data pd JOIN demographic_data dd ON pd.demo_id = dd.demo_id GROUP BY sale_month ORDER BY sale_month
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(CAST(sale_date AS DATETIME), '%Y-%m') AS sale_month, AVG(sale_price / median_income) AS avg_adjusted_sale_price FROM property_data AS pd JOIN demographic_data AS dd ON pd.demo_id = dd.demo_id GROUP BY sale_month ORDER BY sale_month

question:
**User**: I want to get a summary of survey responses.
**Assistant**: What kind of information are you looking for in the summary?
**User**: I want to know the number of responses, average response values, and the date range of responses for each category and group.
**Assistant**: Do you want to include any additional information in the summary, such as the names of users who accessed the responses?
**User**: No, just the category and group names are enough.
**Assistant**: Would you like to order the results by any specific criteria, such as category name or group name?
**User**: Yes, please order by category name and then group name.
**Assistant**: Is there a specific format you'd like the summary to be in, such as a string with all the information?
**User**: Yes, a string with all the information would be great.
**Assistant**: I'll help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT c.category_name || ' - ' || g.group_name || ' (' || COUNT(r.response_id) || ' responses, ' || AVG(r.value) || ' avg, ' || MIN(r.response_date) || ' to ' || MAX(r.response_date) || ')' AS category_group_summary FROM responses r INNER JOIN surveys s ON r.survey_id = s.survey_id INNER JOIN categories c ON s.category_id = c.category_id INNER JOIN groups g ON s.group_id = g.group_id GROUP BY c.category_name, g.group_name ORDER BY c.category_name, g.group_name
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT CONCAT(c.category_name, ' - ', g.group_name, ' (', COUNT(r.response_id), ' responses, ', AVG(r.value), ' avg, ', MIN(r.response_date), ' to ', MAX(r.response_date), ')') AS category_group_summary FROM responses AS r INNER JOIN surveys AS s ON r.survey_id = s.survey_id INNER JOIN categories AS c ON s.category_id = c.category_id INNER JOIN `groups` AS g ON s.group_id = g.group_id GROUP BY c.category_name, g.group_name ORDER BY c.category_name, g.group_name
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT c.category_name || ' - ' || g.group_name || ' (' || COUNT(r.response_id) || ' responses, ' || AVG(r.value) || ' avg, ' || MIN(r.response_date) || ' to ' || MAX(r.response_date) || ')' AS category_group_summary FROM responses AS r INNER JOIN surveys AS s ON r.survey_id = s.survey_id INNER JOIN categories AS c ON s.category_id = c.category_id INNER JOIN groups AS g ON s.group_id = g.group_id GROUP BY c.category_name, g.group_name ORDER BY c.category_name NULLS FIRST, g.group_name NULLS FIRST

question: What are the names of the teams and competitions, along with the total number of matches played, total goals scored, total goals conceded, and average attendance for each team in each competition?
external_knowledge: The full_time_score is in the format 'X-Y', where X is the score of the team and Y is the score of the opponent; The query assumes that the team_id in the matches table refers to the team that scored the first value in the full_time_score.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH MatchStats AS ( SELECT m.team_id, c.competition_id, COUNT(*) AS total_matches, SUM(CASE WHEN m.full_time_score LIKE '%-%' THEN CAST(SUBSTR(m.full_time_score, 1, INSTR(m.full_time_score, '-') - 1) AS INTEGER) ELSE 0 END) AS total_goals_scored, SUM(CASE WHEN m.full_time_score LIKE '%-%' THEN CAST(SUBSTR(m.full_time_score, INSTR(m.full_time_score, '-') + 1) AS INTEGER) ELSE 0 END) AS total_goals_conceded, AVG(m.attendance) AS avg_attendance FROM matches m JOIN competitions c ON m.competition_id = c.competition_id GROUP BY m.team_id, c.competition_id ) SELECT t.team_name, c.competition_name, ms.total_matches, ms.total_goals_scored, ms.total_goals_conceded, ms.avg_attendance FROM MatchStats ms JOIN teams t ON ms.team_id = t.team_id JOIN competitions c ON ms.competition_id = c.competition_id
gold_sql.mysql: WITH MatchStats AS (SELECT m.team_id, c.competition_id, COUNT(*) AS total_matches, SUM(CASE WHEN m.full_time_score LIKE '%-%' THEN CAST(SUBSTRING(m.full_time_score, 1, LOCATE('-', m.full_time_score) - 1) AS SIGNED) ELSE 0 END) AS total_goals_scored, SUM(CASE WHEN m.full_time_score LIKE '%-%' THEN CAST(SUBSTRING(m.full_time_score, LOCATE('-', m.full_time_score) + 1) AS SIGNED) ELSE 0 END) AS total_goals_conceded, AVG(m.attendance) AS avg_attendance FROM matches AS m JOIN competitions AS c ON m.competition_id = c.competition_id GROUP BY m.team_id, c.competition_id) SELECT t.team_name, c.competition_name, ms.total_matches, ms.total_goals_scored, ms.total_goals_conceded, ms.avg_attendance FROM MatchStats AS ms JOIN teams AS t ON ms.team_id = t.team_id JOIN competitions AS c ON ms.competition_id = c.competition_id
gold_sql.postgres: WITH MatchStats AS (SELECT m.team_id, c.competition_id, COUNT(*) AS total_matches, SUM(CASE WHEN m.full_time_score LIKE '%-%' THEN CAST(SUBSTRING(m.full_time_score FROM 1 FOR STRPOS(m.full_time_score, '-') - 1) AS INT) ELSE 0 END) AS total_goals_scored, SUM(CASE WHEN m.full_time_score LIKE '%-%' THEN CAST(SUBSTRING(m.full_time_score FROM STRPOS(m.full_time_score, '-') + 1) AS INT) ELSE 0 END) AS total_goals_conceded, AVG(m.attendance) AS avg_attendance FROM matches AS m JOIN competitions AS c ON m.competition_id = c.competition_id GROUP BY m.team_id, c.competition_id) SELECT t.team_name, c.competition_name, ms.total_matches, ms.total_goals_scored, ms.total_goals_conceded, ms.avg_attendance FROM MatchStats AS ms JOIN teams AS t ON ms.team_id = t.team_id JOIN competitions AS c ON ms.competition_id = c.competition_id

question: Return the names, ingredients, preparation methods, average prices, order counts, and availability of active food items, ordered alphabetically by food name.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH FoodIngredients AS ( SELECT fi.food_id, GROUP_CONCAT(i.ingredient_name, ', ') AS ingredients FROM food_ingredients fi INNER JOIN ingredients i ON fi.ingredient_id = i.ingredient_id GROUP BY fi.food_id ), FoodPricing AS ( SELECT p.food_id, AVG(CAST(REPLACE(p.price, ',', '') AS REAL)) AS average_price FROM pricing p GROUP BY p.food_id ), FoodOrders AS ( SELECT oi.food_id, COUNT(oi.order_id) AS order_count FROM order_items oi GROUP BY oi.food_id ), FoodAvailability AS ( SELECT mi.food_id, mi.available FROM menu_items mi ) SELECT f.food_name, fi.ingredients, f.preparation_method, fp.average_price, fo.order_count, fa.available FROM foods f LEFT JOIN FoodIngredients fi ON f.food_id = fi.food_id LEFT JOIN FoodPricing fp ON f.food_id = fp.food_id LEFT JOIN FoodOrders fo ON f.food_id = fo.food_id LEFT JOIN FoodAvailability fa ON f.food_id = fa.food_id WHERE f.status = 'active' ORDER BY f.food_name

question: Could you please gather all the users and display their full names along with the total number of successful accesses they made? If a user has no successful accesses, please indicate 0, and order the list from the users with the most successful accesses to the least, breaking ties alphabetically by last name and then first name?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH SuccessfulAccesses AS ( SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS access_count FROM access_logs WHERE access_status = 'success' GROUP BY user_id ) SELECT u.first_name || ' ' || u.last_name AS user_full_name, COALESCE(sa.access_count, 0) AS total_successful_accesses FROM users u LEFT JOIN SuccessfulAccesses sa ON u.user_id = sa.user_id ORDER BY sa.access_count DESC NULLS LAST, u.last_name, u.first_name

question: Could you provide the total spent by type of transaction for each month?
external_knowledge:
- Total spent refers to the sum of all transactions.
- Type of transaction refers to different kinds of transactions such as credit card payments, loan repayments, etc.
- Each month is defined by the year and month extracted from the transaction date.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', transaction_date) AS Year_Month, transaction_type, SUM(amount) AS Total_Amount_Spent FROM credit_transactions GROUP BY Year_Month, transaction_type

question: Hey, can you show me a list of casinos along with their overall ratings, average user ratings, total number of ratings, percentage of ratings that are 4 or higher, number of games, country, currency, license information, establishment year, types of bonuses offered, and the latest bonus expiry date? question: Could you please gather information about the students who have graduated from 'I.D.E. Chepauk, Chennai' and have an average grade percentage between 70 and 80? I need to know each student's overall average percentage, the average percentage for students from 'I.D.E. Chepauk, Chennai', the average percentage for each course, and the total number of graduated students, all ordered by student ID and the date the qualification was awarded.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH GradeAverages AS ( SELECT grade_id, (CAST(SUBSTR(percentage_range, 1, INSTR(percentage_range, '-') - 1) AS REAL) + CAST(SUBSTR(percentage_range, INSTR(percentage_range, '-') + 2) AS REAL)) / 2 AS average_percentage FROM grades ), QualificationDetails AS ( SELECT q.qualification_id, q.student_id, c.course_name, i.institution_name, ga.average_percentage, q.date_awarded, s.graduation_date, s.status FROM qualifications q INNER JOIN courses c ON q.course_id = c.course_id INNER JOIN institutions i ON q.institution_id = i.institution_id INNER JOIN GradeAverages ga ON q.grade_id = ga.grade_id INNER JOIN students s ON q.student_id = s.student_id WHERE i.institution_name = 'I.D.E. Chepauk, Chennai' AND s.status = 'graduated' ) SELECT qd.student_id, AVG(qd.average_percentage) OVER (PARTITION BY qd.student_id) AS avg_percentage_overall, AVG(qd.average_percentage) OVER () AS avg_percentage_per_institution, AVG(qd.average_percentage) OVER (PARTITION BY qd.course_name) AS avg_percentage_per_course, COUNT(qd.student_id) OVER (PARTITION BY qd.status) AS student_count_per_status FROM QualificationDetails qd ORDER BY qd.student_id, qd.date_awarded

question: Find the names of holidays with fixed dates, their corresponding regions, and the number of associated events for each holiday, but only include holidays that have at least one associated event.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT h.holiday_name, GROUP_CONCAT(r.region_name, ', ') AS region_names, COUNT(e.event_id) AS event_count FROM holidays h INNER JOIN holiday_region_mapping hrm ON h.holiday_id = hrm.holiday_id INNER JOIN regions r ON hrm.region_id = r.region_id LEFT JOIN events e ON h.holiday_id = e.holiday_id WHERE h.is_fixed = 1 GROUP BY h.holiday_name HAVING COUNT(e.event_id) > 0

question: What are the ranks of the top 5 reviewers who reviewed the highest number of high-quality annotations for images uploaded in 2023?

question: Find the product IDs of the top 10 selling products and return a concatenated string of product details, including the title, total sales amount, customer preferences count, and total inventory, for each product, ordered by sales rank and total sales amount in descending order.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH TopSellingProducts AS ( SELECT p.product_id, p.title, SUM(s.quantity_sold * s.sale_price) AS total_sales_amount FROM products p JOIN sales s ON p.product_id = s.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.title ORDER BY total_sales_amount DESC LIMIT 10 ), CustomerPreferences AS ( SELECT cp.product_id, COUNT(DISTINCT cp.customer_id) AS customer_preferences_count FROM customer_preferences cp JOIN TopSellingProducts tsp ON cp.product_id = tsp.product_id GROUP BY cp.product_id ), TotalInventory AS ( SELECT li.product_id, SUM(li.quantity) AS total_inventory FROM location_inventory li JOIN TopSellingProducts tsp ON li.product_id = tsp.product_id GROUP BY li.product_id ) SELECT tsp.product_id, tsp.title || ' - Total Sales: $' || tsp.total_sales_amount || ' - Customer Preferences: ' || IFNULL(c.customer_preferences_count, 0) || ' - Total Inventory: ' || IFNULL(i.total_inventory, 0) AS product_details FROM TopSellingProducts tsp LEFT JOIN CustomerPreferences c ON tsp.product_id = c.product_id LEFT JOIN TotalInventory i ON tsp.product_id = i.product_id ORDER BY tsp.total_sales_amount DESC

question: Rank equipment by their comparative performance scores, calculated based on their maintenance history, average performance metrics, latest performance metrics, and alert records.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH MaintenanceSummary AS ( SELECT e.equipment_id, COUNT(m.maintenance_id) AS maintenance_count, AVG(m.cost) AS avg_maintenance_cost, MAX(m.maintenance_date) AS last_maintenance_date, MIN(m.maintenance_date) AS first_maintenance_date FROM equipment e LEFT JOIN maintenance_records m ON e.equipment_id = m.equipment_id GROUP BY e.equipment_id ), PerformanceBaseline AS ( SELECT p.equipment_id, AVG(p.rpm) AS avg_rpm, AVG(p.thrust) AS avg_thrust, AVG(p.efficiency) AS avg_efficiency, AVG(p.energy_consumption) AS avg_energy_consumption FROM performance_metrics p GROUP BY p.equipment_id ), AlertsAnalysis AS ( SELECT a.equipment_id, COUNT(a.alert_id) AS alert_count, SUM(CASE WHEN a.severity_level = 'high' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS high_severity_alerts, SUM(CASE WHEN a.severity_level = 'medium' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS medium_severity_alerts, SUM(CASE WHEN a.severity_level = 'low' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS low_severity_alerts FROM alerts a GROUP BY a.equipment_id ), RecentPerformance AS ( SELECT p.equipment_id, p.rpm, p.thrust, p.efficiency, p.energy_consumption, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.equipment_id ORDER BY p.recorded_time DESC) AS row_num FROM performance_metrics p ), LatestPerformance AS ( SELECT rp.equipment_id, rp.rpm, rp.thrust, rp.efficiency, rp.energy_consumption FROM RecentPerformance rp WHERE rp.row_num = 1 ) SELECT e.equipment_name, ((lp.rpm / pb.avg_rpm) + (lp.thrust / pb.avg_thrust) + (pb.avg_efficiency / lp.efficiency) - (lp.energy_consumption / pb.avg_energy_consumption) - ms.maintenance_count - aa.alert_count) / 5 AS comparative_score FROM equipment e JOIN MaintenanceSummary ms ON e.equipment_id = ms.equipment_id JOIN PerformanceBaseline pb ON e.equipment_id = pb.equipment_id JOIN LatestPerformance lp ON e.equipment_id = lp.equipment_id JOIN AlertsAnalysis aa ON e.equipment_id = aa.equipment_id ORDER BY comparative_score DESC

question: I want to identify sales data points that have associated data quality issues, count the number of issues for each, and categorize the predicted sales values for these data points into 'Low Prediction', 'Medium Prediction', or 'High Prediction' based on their values, for the year 2023. The results should be ordered by the sales ID.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH Sales2023 AS ( SELECT sales_id FROM sales_data WHERE strftime('%Y', sales_date) = '2023' ), SalesWithIssues AS ( SELECT s.sales_id, COUNT(dqi.issue_id) AS issue_count FROM Sales2023 s JOIN data_quality dqi ON s.sales_id = dqi.sales_id GROUP BY s.sales_id ), SalesWithPredictions AS ( SELECT si.sales_id, si.issue_count, CAST(REPLACE(p.prediction_value, ',', '') AS REAL) AS prediction_value FROM SalesWithIssues si LEFT JOIN predictions p ON si.sales_id = p.sales_id WHERE p.sales_id IS NOT NULL ) SELECT swp.sales_id, swp.issue_count, CASE WHEN swp.prediction_value BETWEEN 100000 AND 200000 THEN 'Medium Prediction' WHEN swp.prediction_value > 200000 THEN 'High Prediction' ELSE 'Low Prediction' END AS prediction_category FROM SalesWithPredictions swp ORDER BY swp.sales_id

question: I want to know the names, types, pharmacy services, staff counts, total sales, total sales amounts, supply chain counts, total supply quantities, sales ranks, supply chain buckets, bucket sizes, and average sales amounts for all stores, ordered from the lowest to the highest sales rank.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH StoreData AS ( SELECT s.store_id, s.name, s.address, st.type_name, GROUP_CONCAT(ps.service_name, ', ') AS pharmacy_services, COUNT(ss.staff_id) AS staff_count, COUNT(sa.sale_id) AS total_sales, SUM(CAST(sa.total_amount AS REAL)) AS total_sales_amount, COUNT(sc.supplier_id) AS supply_chain_count, SUM(sc.quantity) AS total_supply_quantity FROM stores s LEFT JOIN store_store_types stt ON s.store_id = stt.store_id LEFT JOIN store_types st ON st.type_id = stt.type_id LEFT JOIN store_pharmacy_services sps ON s.store_id = sps.store_id LEFT JOIN pharmacy_services ps ON ps.service_id = sps.service_id LEFT JOIN store_staff ss ON ss.store_id = s.store_id LEFT JOIN sales sa ON sa.store_id = s.store_id LEFT JOIN supply_chain sc ON sc.store_id = s.store_id GROUP BY s.store_id, s.name, s.address, st.type_name ), RankedStores AS ( SELECT sd.store_id, sd.name, sd.address, sd.type_name, sd.pharmacy_services, sd.staff_count, sd.total_sales, sd.total_sales_amount, sd.supply_chain_count, sd.total_supply_quantity, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY sd.total_sales_amount ASC) AS sales_rank, NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY sd.total_supply_quantity DESC) AS supply_chain_bucket FROM StoreData sd ) SELECT rs.name, rs.type_name, rs.pharmacy_services, rs.staff_count, rs.total_sales, rs.total_sales_amount, rs.supply_chain_count, rs.total_supply_quantity, rs.sales_rank, rs.supply_chain_bucket, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY rs.supply_chain_bucket) AS bucket_size, AVG(rs.total_sales_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY rs.supply_chain_bucket) AS bucket_avg_sales_amount FROM RankedStores rs ORDER BY rs.sales_rank ASC

question: I want to know the number of unique participants, run ID, run notes, run status, experiment name, and a concatenated list of whether the consent form was signed and participation notes for all completed runs in the experiment with ID 1, where there is at least one participant in the run.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT rp.participant_id) AS num_participants, r.run_id, r.run_notes, r.run_status, e.exp_name, GROUP_CONCAT(CASE WHEN rp.consent_form_signed = 1 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END) AS consent_signed, GROUP_CONCAT(rp.participation_notes) AS participation_notes FROM runs r JOIN experiments e ON r.exp_id = e.exp_id JOIN run_participants rp ON rp.run_id = r.run_id WHERE r.run_status = 'completed' AND e.exp_id = 1 GROUP BY r.run_id, r.run_notes, r.run_status, e.exp_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT rp.participant_id) > 0
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT rp.participant_id) AS num_participants, r.run_id, r.run_notes, r.run_status, e.exp_name, GROUP_CONCAT(CASE WHEN rp.consent_form_signed = 1 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END SEPARATOR ',') AS consent_signed, GROUP_CONCAT(rp.participation_notes SEPARATOR ',') AS participation_notes FROM runs AS r JOIN experiments AS e ON r.exp_id = e.exp_id JOIN run_participants AS rp ON rp.run_id = r.run_id WHERE r.run_status = 'completed' AND e.exp_id = 1 GROUP BY r.run_id, r.run_notes, r.run_status, e.exp_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT rp.participant_id) > 0

question:

**User**: I want to know how many of our software products have been released and how many unique users have accessed the databases associated with these released products.
**Assistant**: To clarify, you want to count the number of released software products and the number of unique users who have accessed the databases related to these products, correct?
**User**: Yes, that's right.
**Assistant**: Is there anything else you need to know, or can I proceed with formulating the SQL query for this information?
**User**: That's all I need.
**Assistant**: OK, I will help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ReleasedProducts AS ( SELECT product_id FROM software_products WHERE development_status = 'released' ), DatabaseAccesses AS ( SELECT DISTINCT a.user_id FROM access_logs a JOIN databases d ON a.resource_accessed = d.database_name WHERE d.product_id IN (SELECT product_id FROM ReleasedProducts) ) SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ReleasedProducts) AS released_product_count, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM DatabaseAccesses) AS unique_user_count

question: What is the monthly average compliance rate of water quality tests, for each test parameter, over time?
external_knowledge:
- Compliance rate is a measure of how well water quality tests meet the EPA standards, calculated as 1 minus the ratio of failing samples to total samples.
- The `strftime('%Y-%m', wqt.test_date)` function extracts the year and month from the `test_date` to group the data by month.
- A higher compliance rate indicates better adherence to water quality standards.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH MonthlyComplianceRates AS ( SELECT test_parameter, strftime('%Y-%m', test_date) AS month, 1.0 - (CAST(number_of_samples_failing AS REAL) / number_of_samples_tested) AS compliance_rate FROM water_quality_tests ) SELECT month, test_parameter, AVG(compliance_rate) AS average_compliance_rate FROM MonthlyComplianceRates GROUP BY month, test_parameter ORDER BY month, test_parameter
gold_sql.mysql: WITH MonthlyComplianceRates AS (SELECT test_parameter, DATE_FORMAT(CAST(test_date AS DATETIME), '%Y-%m') AS month, 1.0 - (CAST(number_of_samples_failing AS FLOAT) / number_of_samples_tested) AS compliance_rate FROM water_quality_tests) SELECT month, test_parameter, AVG(compliance_rate) AS average_compliance_rate FROM MonthlyComplianceRates GROUP BY month, test_parameter ORDER BY month, test_parameter
gold_sql.postgres: WITH MonthlyComplianceRates AS (SELECT test_parameter, TO_CHAR(CAST(test_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY-MM') AS month, 1.0 - (CAST(number_of_samples_failing AS REAL) / NULLIF(number_of_samples_tested, 0)) AS compliance_rate FROM water_quality_tests) SELECT month, test_parameter, AVG(compliance_rate) AS average_compliance_rate FROM MonthlyComplianceRates GROUP BY month, test_parameter ORDER BY month NULLS FIRST, test_parameter NULLS FIRST

question: Can you please retrieve a list of all components, including their names, categories, maximum SN74 and ABT performance values, and the users with permissions for each component, ordered by component ID?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ComponentMetrics AS ( SELECT p.component_id, MAX(p.sn74) AS max_sn74, MAX(p.abt) AS max_abt FROM performance_metrics p GROUP BY p.component_id ), ComponentPermissions AS ( SELECT ucp.component_id, GROUP_CONCAT(u.username, ', ') AS users_with_permissions FROM user_component_permissions ucp JOIN users u ON ucp.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY ucp.component_id ) SELECT c.component_id, c.component_name, cat.category_name, cm.max_sn74, cm.max_abt, cp.users_with_permissions FROM components c JOIN categories cat ON c.category_id = cat.category_id LEFT JOIN ComponentMetrics cm ON c.component_id = cm.component_id LEFT JOIN ComponentPermissions cp ON c.component_id = cp.component_id ORDER BY c.component_id
gold_sql.mysql: WITH ComponentMetrics AS (SELECT p.component_id, MAX(p.sn74) AS max_sn74, MAX(p.abt) AS max_abt FROM performance_metrics AS p GROUP BY p.component_id), ComponentPermissions AS (SELECT ucp.component_id, GROUP_CONCAT(u.username SEPARATOR ', ') AS users_with_permissions FROM user_component_permissions AS ucp JOIN users AS u ON ucp.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY ucp.component_id) SELECT c.component_id, c.component_name, cat.category_name, cm.max_sn74, cm.max_abt, cp.users_with_permissions FROM components AS c JOIN categories AS cat ON c.category_id = cat.category_id LEFT JOIN ComponentMetrics AS cm ON c.component_id = cm.component_id LEFT JOIN ComponentPermissions AS cp ON c.component_id = cp.component_id ORDER BY c.component_id

question: Find the top 5 states with the highest number of active cases, including their populations, and list them in a summary.
external_knowledge: These states are the ones struggling the most with the current health crisis; the number of active cases is a strong indicator of the severity of the situation; population is an important factor in understanding the proportion of affected individuals.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH LatestHealthData AS ( SELECT hd.state_id, hd.active_cases, hd.date_recorded, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY hd.state_id ORDER BY hd.date_recorded DESC) AS rn FROM health_data hd ), TopStates AS ( SELECT s.state_name, s.population, lhd.active_cases FROM states s JOIN LatestHealthData lhd ON s.state_id = lhd.state_id WHERE lhd.rn = 1 ORDER BY lhd.active_cases DESC LIMIT 5 ) SELECT GROUP_CONCAT( TopStates.state_name || ' (Population: ' || TopStates.population || ', Active Cases: ' || TopStates.active_cases, '; ') AS top_states_summary FROM TopStates
gold_sql.mysql: WITH LatestHealthData AS (SELECT hd.state_id, hd.active_cases, hd.date_recorded, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY hd.state_id ORDER BY hd.date_recorded DESC) AS rn FROM health_data AS hd), TopStates AS (SELECT s.state_name, s.population, lhd.active_cases FROM states AS s JOIN LatestHealthData AS lhd ON s.state_id = lhd.state_id WHERE lhd.rn = 1 ORDER BY lhd.active_cases DESC LIMIT 5) SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(TopStates.state_name, ' (Population: ', TopStates.population, ', Active Cases: ', TopStates.active_cases) SEPARATOR '; ') AS top_states_summary FROM TopStates
gold_sql.postgres: WITH LatestHealthData AS (SELECT hd.state_id, hd.active_cases, hd.date_recorded, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY hd.state_id ORDER BY hd.date_recorded DESC NULLS LAST) AS rn FROM health_data AS hd), TopStates AS (SELECT s.state_name, s.population, lhd.active_cases FROM states AS s JOIN LatestHealthData AS lhd ON s.state_id = lhd.state_id WHERE lhd.rn = 1 ORDER BY lhd.active_cases DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 5) SELECT STRING_AGG(TopStates.state_name || ' (Population: ' || TopStates.population || ', Active Cases: ' || TopStates.active_cases, '; ') AS top_states_summary FROM TopStates

question: Which seasons have schools accumulated more than 2500 passing yards, and can you provide this information ordered by the start year of the season and the cumulative passing yards in descending order?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT s.season_id, s.season_name, s.start_year, SUM(CAST(ss.stat_value AS INTEGER)) AS total_passing_yards FROM seasons s INNER JOIN season_statistics ss ON s.season_id = ss.season_id WHERE ss.stat_name = 'total_passing_yards' GROUP BY s.season_id, s.season_name, s.start_year HAVING SUM(CAST(ss.stat_value AS INTEGER)) > 2500 ORDER BY s.start_year, total_passing_yards DESC

gold_sql.postgres: SELECT s.season_id, s.season_name, s.start_year, SUM(CAST(ss.stat_value AS INT)) AS total_passing_yards FROM seasons AS s INNER JOIN season_statistics AS ss ON s.season_id = ss.season_id WHERE ss.stat_name = 'total_passing_yards' GROUP BY s.season_id, s.season_name, s.start_year HAVING SUM(CAST(ss.stat_value AS INT)) > 2500 ORDER BY s.start_year NULLS FIRST, total_passing_yards DESC NULLS LAST

question: What are the brands, pest effectiveness, average quantity sold, total revenue, average rating, and review count for each product, listed in order of most reviewed and highest revenue products?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ProductPestEffectiveness AS ( SELECT p.product_id, p.brand, GROUP_CONCAT( CASE WHEN p.adult_flea = 1 THEN 'Adult Fleas' WHEN p.eggs = 1 THEN 'Eggs' WHEN p.larvae = 1 THEN 'Larvae' WHEN p.tick = 1 THEN 'Ticks' WHEN p.mosquito = 1 THEN 'Mosquitoes' WHEN p.heartworm = 1 THEN 'Heartworms' WHEN p.ear_mite = 1 THEN 'Ear Mites' WHEN p.sarcoptic_mange = 1 THEN 'Sarcoptic Mange' END, ', ' ) AS pest_effectiveness FROM products p GROUP BY p.product_id, p.brand ), SalesPerformance AS ( SELECT s.product_id, AVG(s.quantity_sold) AS avg_quantity_sold, SUM(s.revenue) AS total_revenue FROM sales_data s GROUP BY s.product_id ), ReviewPerformance AS ( SELECT r.product_id, AVG(r.rating) AS avg_rating, COUNT(r.review_id) AS review_count FROM reviews r GROUP BY r.product_id ) SELECT pe.brand, pe.pest_effectiveness, sp.avg_quantity_sold, sp.total_revenue, rp.avg_rating, rp.review_count FROM ProductPestEffectiveness pe JOIN SalesPerformance sp ON pe.product_id = sp.product_id JOIN ReviewPerformance rp ON pe.product_id = rp.product_id ORDER BY rp.review_count DESC, sp.total_revenue DESC

question: Return the user IDs, authors, regions, languages, average engagement scores, average sentiment scores, and topics of interest for all users, including their interest scores in each topic.

question:
**User**: I want to query some model information.
**Assistant**: What kind of model information would you like to know?
**User**: I want to know about model usage and performance.
**Assistant**: What specific metrics would you like to know about model usage?
**User**: I want to know the average batch size for both GPU and DLA processing, the number of successful and failed accesses, and the number of distinct users for each model.
**Assistant**: What about performance metrics?
**User**: I'd like to know the average accuracy and F1 score for each model.
**Assistant**: How about user activity? Would you like to know anything about that?
**User**: Yes, I want to know the number of models accessed by each user.
**Assistant**: Would you like to filter the results by any specific condition?
**User**: Yes, I want to count the number of models with at least one successful access.
**Assistant**: Is there anything else you need?
**User**: No.
**Assistant**: OK, I will help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ModelUsageStats AS ( SELECT m.model_id, m.model_name, m.framework, m.devices, AVG(m.batch_size_gpu) AS avg_batch_size_gpu, AVG(m.batch_size_dla) AS avg_batch_size_dla, SUM(CASE WHEN mal.status = 'success' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS successful_access_count, SUM(CASE WHEN mal.status = 'failure' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed_access_count, COUNT(DISTINCT mal.user_id) AS distinct_users_count FROM models m LEFT JOIN model_access_logs mal ON m.model_id = mal.model_id GROUP BY m.model_id, m.model_name, m.framework, m.devices ), PerformanceMetrics AS ( SELECT mv.model_id, AVG(CAST(SUBSTR(mv.performance_metrics, INSTR(mv.performance_metrics, '"accuracy":') + 11, INSTR(mv.performance_metrics, ', "f1_score"') - INSTR(mv.performance_metrics, '"accuracy":') - 11) AS REAL)) AS avg_accuracy, AVG(CAST(SUBSTR(mv.performance_metrics, INSTR(mv.performance_metrics, '"f1_score":') + 10, INSTR(mv.performance_metrics, '}') - INSTR(mv.performance_metrics, '"f1_score":') - 10) AS REAL)) AS avg_f1_score FROM model_versions mv GROUP BY mv.model_id ), UserActivity AS ( SELECT mal.user_id, um.username, COUNT(mal.model_id) AS models_accessed_count FROM model_access_logs mal INNER JOIN user_management um ON mal.user_id = um.user_id GROUP BY mal.user_id, um.username ), ModelUserActivity AS ( SELECT mus.model_id, mus.model_name, mus.framework, mus.devices, mus.avg_batch_size_gpu, mus.avg_batch_size_dla, mus.successful_access_count, mus.failed_access_count, mus.distinct_users_count, pm.avg_accuracy, pm.avg_f1_score, uac.username, uac.models_accessed_count FROM ModelUsageStats mus LEFT JOIN PerformanceMetrics pm ON mus.model_id = pm.model_id LEFT JOIN UserActivity uac ON uac.user_id = mus.distinct_users_count ) SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN mua.successful_access_count > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS active_models_count FROM ModelUserActivity mua
gold_sql.mysql: WITH ModelUsageStats AS (SELECT m.model_id, m.model_name, m.framework, m.devices, AVG(m.batch_size_gpu) AS avg_batch_size_gpu, AVG(m.batch_size_dla) AS avg_batch_size_dla, SUM(CASE WHEN mal.status = 'success' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS successful_access_count, SUM(CASE WHEN mal.status = 'failure' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed_access_count, COUNT(DISTINCT mal.user_id) AS distinct_users_count FROM models AS m LEFT JOIN model_access_logs AS mal ON m.model_id = mal.model_id GROUP BY m.model_id, m.model_name, m.framework, m.devices), PerformanceMetrics AS (SELECT mv.model_id, AVG(CAST(SUBSTRING(mv.performance_metrics, LOCATE('"accuracy":', mv.performance_metrics) + 11, LOCATE(', "f1_score"', mv.performance_metrics) - LOCATE('"accuracy":', mv.performance_metrics) - 11) AS FLOAT)) AS avg_accuracy, AVG(CAST(SUBSTRING(mv.performance_metrics, LOCATE('"f1_score":', mv.performance_metrics) + 10, LOCATE('}', mv.performance_metrics) - LOCATE('"f1_score":', mv.performance_metrics) - 10) AS FLOAT)) AS avg_f1_score FROM model_versions AS mv GROUP BY mv.model_id), UserActivity AS (SELECT mal.user_id, um.username, COUNT(mal.model_id) AS models_accessed_count FROM model_access_logs AS mal INNER JOIN user_management AS um ON mal.user_id = um.user_id GROUP BY mal.user_id, um.username), ModelUserActivity AS (SELECT mus.model_id, mus.model_name, mus.framework, mus.devices, mus.avg_batch_size_gpu, mus.avg_batch_size_dla, mus.successful_access_count, mus.failed_access_count, mus.distinct_users_count, pm.avg_accuracy, pm.avg_f1_score, uac.username, uac.models_accessed_count FROM ModelUsageStats AS mus LEFT JOIN PerformanceMetrics AS pm ON mus.model_id = pm.model_id LEFT JOIN UserActivity AS uac ON uac.user_id = mus.distinct_users_count) SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN mua.successful_access_count > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS active_models_count FROM ModelUserActivity AS mua
gold_sql.postgres: WITH ModelUsageStats AS (SELECT m.model_id, m.model_name, m.framework, m.devices, AVG(m.batch_size_gpu) AS avg_batch_size_gpu, AVG(m.batch_size_dla) AS avg_batch_size_dla, SUM(CASE WHEN mal.status = 'success' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS successful_access_count, SUM(CASE WHEN mal.status = 'failure' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed_access_count, COUNT(DISTINCT mal.user_id) AS distinct_users_count FROM models AS m LEFT JOIN model_access_logs AS mal ON m.model_id = mal.model_id GROUP BY m.model_id, m.model_name, m.framework, m.devices), PerformanceMetrics AS (SELECT mv.model_id, AVG(CAST(SUBSTRING(mv.performance_metrics FROM STRPOS(mv.performance_metrics, '"accuracy":') + 11 FOR STRPOS(mv.performance_metrics, ', "f1_score"') - STRPOS(mv.performance_metrics, '"accuracy":') - 11) AS REAL)) AS avg_accuracy, AVG(CAST(SUBSTRING(mv.performance_metrics FROM STRPOS(mv.performance_metrics, '"f1_score":') + 10 FOR STRPOS(mv.performance_metrics, '}') - STRPOS(mv.performance_metrics, '"f1_score":') - 10) AS REAL)) AS avg_f1_score FROM model_versions AS mv GROUP BY mv.model_id), UserActivity AS (SELECT mal.user_id, um.username, COUNT(mal.model_id) AS models_accessed_count FROM model_access_logs AS mal INNER JOIN user_management AS um ON mal.user_id = um.user_id GROUP BY mal.user_id, um.username), ModelUserActivity AS (SELECT mus.model_id, mus.model_name, mus.framework, mus.devices, mus.avg_batch_size_gpu, mus.avg_batch_size_dla, mus.successful_access_count, mus.failed_access_count, mus.distinct_users_count, pm.avg_accuracy, pm.avg_f1_score, uac.username, uac.models_accessed_count FROM ModelUsageStats AS mus LEFT JOIN PerformanceMetrics AS pm ON mus.model_id = pm.model_id LEFT JOIN UserActivity AS uac ON uac.user_id = mus.distinct_users_count) SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN mua.successful_access_count > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS active_models_count FROM ModelUserActivity AS mua

question: Imagine you are navigating the financial markets, where each instrument is a ship sailing through a sea of data. Your task is to chart the course of these ships, tracking their cumulative trading volume over time, as seen through the eyes of a seasoned analyst. What are the instrument IDs, dates, closing prices, cumulative volumes, analyst names, data source names, and analyst emails for each financial instrument, ordered by instrument ID and date?
external_knowledge:
- 'Cumulative volume' refers to the sum of trading volumes for each financial instrument over time.
- 'Analyst' is a user role that indicates a person responsible for analyzing financial data.
- 'Financial instrument' refers to a tradable asset such as a stock, bond, or derivative.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH Analysts AS ( SELECT user_id, user_name, email FROM users WHERE role = 'analyst' ), FinancialDataWithCumulativeVolume AS ( SELECT instrument_id, date, close_price, volume, SUM(CAST(volume AS INTEGER)) OVER (PARTITION BY instrument_id ORDER BY date) AS cumulative_volume, data_source_id FROM financial_data ) SELECT fdf.instrument_id, fdf.date, fdf.close_price, fdf.cumulative_volume, a.user_name AS analyst_name, ds.source_name, a.email FROM FinancialDataWithCumulativeVolume fdf JOIN data_sources ds ON fdf.data_source_id = ds.data_source_id JOIN Analysts a ON 1=1 -- Joining all analysts with each row; adjust if a specific analyst is required ORDER BY fdf.instrument_id, fdf.date
gold_sql.mysql: WITH Analysts AS (SELECT user_id, user_name, email FROM users WHERE role = 'analyst'), FinancialDataWithCumulativeVolume AS (SELECT instrument_id, date, close_price, volume, SUM(CAST(volume AS SIGNED)) OVER (PARTITION BY instrument_id ORDER BY date) AS cumulative_volume, data_source_id FROM financial_data) SELECT fdf.instrument_id, fdf.date, fdf.close_price, fdf.cumulative_volume, a.user_name AS analyst_name, ds.source_name, a.email FROM FinancialDataWithCumulativeVolume AS fdf JOIN data_sources AS ds ON fdf.data_source_id = ds.data_source_id JOIN Analysts AS a ON 1 = 1 /* Joining all analysts with each row; adjust if a specific analyst is required ORDER BY fdf.instrument_id, fdf.date */
gold_sql.postgres: WITH Analysts AS (SELECT user_id, user_name, email FROM users WHERE role = 'analyst'), FinancialDataWithCumulativeVolume AS (SELECT instrument_id, date, close_price, volume, SUM(CAST(volume AS INT)) OVER (PARTITION BY instrument_id ORDER BY date NULLS FIRST) AS cumulative_volume, data_source_id FROM financial_data) SELECT fdf.instrument_id, fdf.date, fdf.close_price, fdf.cumulative_volume, a.user_name AS analyst_name, ds.source_name, a.email FROM FinancialDataWithCumulativeVolume AS fdf JOIN data_sources AS ds ON fdf.data_source_id = ds.data_source_id JOIN Analysts AS a ON 1 = 1 /* Joining all analysts with each row; adjust if a specific analyst is required ORDER BY fdf.instrument_id, fdf.date */

question: Could you provide the IDs, names, ranks, occupations, places of residence, and branches of those soldiers who have participated in various activities and, consequently, have some event descriptions logged?
external_knowledge:
- Soldiers refer to personnel in the Army branch.
- Participating in various activities implies involvement in events recorded in the database.
- Event descriptions are the activities or events in which the personnel have been involved.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT p.personnel_id, p.name, r.rank_name, o.occupation_name, res.residence_name, p.service_branch, GROUP_CONCAT(e.event_description, ', ') AS event_descriptions FROM personnel p INNER JOIN ranks r ON p.rank_id = r.rank_id INNER JOIN occupations o ON p.occupation_id = o.occupation_id INNER JOIN residences res ON p.residence_id = res.residence_id INNER JOIN events e ON p.personnel_id = e.personnel_id WHERE p.service_branch = 'Army' GROUP BY p.personnel_id, p.name, r.rank_name, o.occupation_name, res.residence_name, p.service_branch
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT p.personnel_id, p.name, r.rank_name, o.occupation_name, res.residence_name, p.service_branch, GROUP_CONCAT(e.event_description SEPARATOR ', ') AS event_descriptions FROM personnel AS p INNER JOIN ranks AS r ON p.rank_id = r.rank_id INNER JOIN occupations AS o ON p.occupation_id = o.occupation_id INNER JOIN residences AS res ON p.residence_id = res.residence_id INNER JOIN events AS e ON p.personnel_id = e.personnel_id WHERE p.service_branch = 'Army' GROUP BY p.personnel_id, p.name, r.rank_name, o.occupation_name, res.residence_name, p.service_branch
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT p.personnel_id, p.name, r.rank_name, o.occupation_name, res.residence_name, p.service_branch, STRING_AGG(e.event_description, ', ') AS event_descriptions FROM personnel AS p INNER JOIN ranks AS r ON p.rank_id = r.rank_id INNER JOIN occupations AS o ON p.occupation_id = o.occupation_id INNER JOIN residences AS res ON p.residence_id = res.residence_id INNER JOIN events AS e ON p.personnel_id = e.personnel_id WHERE p.service_branch = 'Army' GROUP BY p.personnel_id, p.name, r.rank_name, o.occupation_name, res.residence_name, p.service_branch

question:
**User**: I want to combine traffic data with incident reports and traffic predictions.
**Assistant**: Which specific data points from the traffic data would you like to include?
**User**: I'm interested in the region name, hour, total output, density, and average speed.
**Assistant**: Would you like to know anything from the incident reports?
**User**: Yes, I'd like to know the incident type and severity, but only if there were incidents during the hour the traffic data was collected.
**Assistant**: What about traffic predictions? Is there anything specific you'd like to know from that?
**User**: Yes, I'd like to see the predicted output, density, and speed if they're available for the hour in question.
**Assistant**: You also want to calculate the cumulative total output for each region over time, correct?
**User**: Exactly, and please order the results by region name and hour.
**Assistant**: One last thing, are you filtering these results by any specific conditions or would you like all available data?
**User**: No filtering needed, I want all available data.
**Assistant**: Is there anything else you need?
**User**: No, that's it.
**Assistant**: OK, I will help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT r.region_name, td.hour, td.total_output, td.density, td.average_speed, SUM(td.total_output) OVER (PARTITION BY r.region_name ORDER BY td.hour) AS cumulative_total_output, ir.incident_type, ir.incident_severity, tp.predicted_output, tp.predicted_density, tp.predicted_speed FROM traffic_data td JOIN regions r ON td.region_id = r.region_id LEFT JOIN incident_reports ir ON td.region_id = ir.region_id AND td.hour BETWEEN CAST(strftime('%H', ir.start_time) AS INTEGER) AND CAST(strftime('%H', ir.end_time) AS INTEGER) LEFT JOIN traffic_predictions tp ON td.region_id = tp.region_id AND td.hour = CAST(strftime('%H', tp.prediction_time) AS INTEGER) ORDER BY r.region_name, td.hour
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT r.region_name, td.hour, td.total_output, td.density, td.average_speed, SUM(td.total_output) OVER (PARTITION BY r.region_name ORDER BY td.hour) AS cumulative_total_output, ir.incident_type, ir.incident_severity, tp.predicted_output, tp.predicted_density, tp.predicted_speed FROM traffic_data AS td JOIN regions AS r ON td.region_id = r.region_id LEFT JOIN incident_reports AS ir ON td.region_id = ir.region_id AND td.hour BETWEEN CAST(DATE_FORMAT(CAST(ir.start_time AS DATETIME), '%H') AS SIGNED) AND CAST(DATE_FORMAT(CAST(ir.end_time AS DATETIME), '%H') AS SIGNED) LEFT JOIN traffic_predictions AS tp ON td.region_id = tp.region_id AND td.hour = CAST(DATE_FORMAT(CAST(tp.prediction_time AS DATETIME), '%H') AS SIGNED) ORDER BY r.region_name, td.hour
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT r.region_name, td.hour, td.total_output, td.density, td.average_speed, SUM(td.total_output) OVER (PARTITION BY r.region_name ORDER BY td.hour NULLS FIRST) AS cumulative_total_output, ir.incident_type, ir.incident_severity, tp.predicted_output, tp.predicted_density, tp.predicted_speed FROM traffic_data AS td JOIN regions AS r ON td.region_id = r.region_id LEFT JOIN incident_reports AS ir ON td.region_id = ir.region_id AND td.hour BETWEEN CAST(TO_CHAR(CAST(ir.start_time AS TIMESTAMP), 'HH24') AS INT) AND CAST(TO_CHAR(CAST(ir.end_time AS TIMESTAMP), 'HH24') AS INT) LEFT JOIN traffic_predictions AS tp ON td.region_id = tp.region_id AND td.hour = CAST(TO_CHAR(CAST(tp.prediction_time AS TIMESTAMP), 'HH24') AS INT) ORDER BY r.region_name NULLS FIRST, td.hour NULLS FIRST

question: Could you please compile a list of all holidays, including their corresponding region hierarchies? I need the holiday names along with their region paths, which should include all parent regions, and organize the results in alphabetical order by holiday name and region path.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RECURSIVE RegionHierarchy AS ( SELECT region_id, region_name, CAST(region_name AS TEXT) AS region_path FROM regions WHERE parent_region_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT r.region_id, r.region_name, CAST(rh.region_path || ' > ' || r.region_name AS TEXT) AS region_path FROM regions r JOIN RegionHierarchy rh ON r.parent_region_id = rh.region_id ) SELECT h.holiday_name, rh.region_path AS region_hierarchy FROM holidays h JOIN holiday_region_mapping hrm ON h.holiday_id = hrm.holiday_id JOIN RegionHierarchy rh ON hrm.region_id = rh.region_id ORDER BY h.holiday_name, rh.region_path
gold_sql.mysql: WITH RECURSIVE RegionHierarchy AS (SELECT region_id, region_name, CAST(region_name AS CHAR) AS region_path FROM regions WHERE parent_region_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT r.region_id, r.region_name, CAST(CONCAT(rh.region_path, ' > ', r.region_name) AS CHAR) AS region_path FROM regions AS r JOIN RegionHierarchy AS rh ON r.parent_region_id = rh.region_id) SELECT h.holiday_name, rh.region_path AS region_hierarchy FROM holidays AS h JOIN holiday_region_mapping AS hrm ON h.holiday_id = hrm.holiday_id JOIN RegionHierarchy AS rh ON hrm.region_id = rh.region_id ORDER BY h.holiday_name, rh.region_path
gold_sql.postgres: WITH RECURSIVE RegionHierarchy AS (SELECT region_id, region_name, CAST(region_name AS TEXT) AS region_path FROM regions WHERE parent_region_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT r.region_id, r.region_name, CAST(rh.region_path || ' > ' || r.region_name AS TEXT) AS region_path FROM regions AS r JOIN RegionHierarchy AS rh ON r.parent_region_id = rh.region_id) SELECT h.holiday_name, rh.region_path AS region_hierarchy FROM holidays AS h JOIN holiday_region_mapping AS hrm ON h.holiday_id = hrm.holiday_id JOIN RegionHierarchy AS rh ON hrm.region_id = rh.region_id ORDER BY h.holiday_name NULLS FIRST, rh.region_path NULLS FIRST

question: Could you please gather information on the players who have won the MVP award, showing their names, points per game, and player efficiency ratings for the seasons they won the award, and list them in order from highest to lowest points per game?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT p.first_name || ' ' || p.last_name AS player_name, ps.points_per_game, ps.player_efficiency_rating FROM players p JOIN player_seasons ps ON p.player_id = ps.player_id JOIN player_awards pa ON p.player_id = pa.player_id WHERE pa.award_name = 'MVP' AND ps.season_year = CAST(pa.award_year AS TEXT) ORDER BY ps.points_per_game DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT CONCAT(p.first_name, ' ', p.last_name) AS player_name, ps.points_per_game, ps.player_efficiency_rating FROM players AS p JOIN player_seasons AS ps ON p.player_id = ps.player_id JOIN player_awards AS pa ON p.player_id = pa.player_id WHERE pa.award_name = 'MVP' AND ps.season_year = CAST(pa.award_year AS CHAR) ORDER BY ps.points_per_game DESC

question: Could you provide the titles of the top 3 most viewed videos for each channel, along with their view counts, like counts, comment counts, and categories, ordered by channel title and view rank?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ChannelVideoEngagementCTE AS ( SELECT c.channel_id, c.title AS channel_title, v.video_id, v.title AS video_title, ve.view_count, ve.like_count, ve.comment_count, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY c.channel_id ORDER BY ve.view_count DESC) as view_rank FROM channels c INNER JOIN videos v ON c.channel_id = v.channel_id INNER JOIN video_engagement ve ON v.video_id = ve.video_id ), VideoCategoryCTE AS ( SELECT vc.video_id, GROUP_CONCAT(cc.category_name) AS categories FROM video_categories vc INNER JOIN channel_categories cc ON vc.category_id = cc.category_id GROUP BY vc.video_id ) SELECT cve.channel_title, cve.video_title, cve.view_count, cve.like_count, cve.comment_count, vc.categories, cve.view_rank FROM ChannelVideoEngagementCTE cve INNER JOIN VideoCategoryCTE vc ON cve.video_id = vc.video_id WHERE cve.view_rank <= 3 ORDER BY cve.channel_title, cve.view_rank
gold_sql.mysql: WITH ChannelVideoEngagementCTE AS (SELECT c.channel_id, c.title AS channel_title, v.video_id, v.title AS video_title, ve.view_count, ve.like_count, ve.comment_count, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY c.channel_id ORDER BY ve.view_count DESC) AS view_rank FROM channels AS c INNER JOIN videos AS v ON c.channel_id = v.channel_id INNER JOIN video_engagement AS ve ON v.video_id = ve.video_id), VideoCategoryCTE AS (SELECT vc.video_id, GROUP_CONCAT(cc.category_name SEPARATOR ',') AS categories FROM video_categories AS vc INNER JOIN channel_categories AS cc ON vc.category_id = cc.category_id GROUP BY vc.video_id) SELECT cve.channel_title, cve.video_title, cve.view_count, cve.like_count, cve.comment_count, vc.categories, cve.view_rank FROM ChannelVideoEngagementCTE AS cve INNER JOIN VideoCategoryCTE AS vc ON cve.video_id = vc.video_id WHERE cve.view_rank <= 3 ORDER BY cve.channel_title, cve.view_rank
gold_sql.postgres: WITH ChannelVideoEngagementCTE AS (SELECT c.channel_id, c.title AS channel_title, v.video_id, v.title AS video_title, ve.view_count, ve.like_count, ve.comment_count, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY c.channel_id ORDER BY ve.view_count DESC NULLS LAST) AS view_rank FROM channels AS c INNER JOIN videos AS v ON c.channel_id = v.channel_id INNER JOIN video_engagement AS ve ON v.video_id = ve.video_id), VideoCategoryCTE AS (SELECT vc.video_id, STRING_AGG(cc.category_name, ',') AS categories FROM video_categories AS vc INNER JOIN channel_categories AS cc ON vc.category_id = cc.category_id GROUP BY vc.video_id) SELECT cve.channel_title, cve.video_title, cve.view_count, cve.like_count, cve.comment_count, vc.categories, cve.view_rank FROM ChannelVideoEngagementCTE AS cve INNER JOIN VideoCategoryCTE AS vc ON cve.video_id = vc.video_id WHERE cve.view_rank <= 3 ORDER BY cve.channel_title NULLS FIRST, cve.view_rank NULLS FIRST

question: Which countries have experienced the highest explosion in population growth?
external_knowledge: An explosion in population growth can be equated to the highest rates of population growth over a period of time, typically measured by the average annual rate of change in population; Population growth rate is a key indicator of a country's socio-economic dynamics.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH PopulationGrowth AS ( SELECT c.country_id, c.country_name, MIN(h.year) AS earliest_year, MAX(h.year) AS latest_year, MIN(h.population) AS earliest_population, MAX(h.population) AS latest_population, (MAX(h.population) - MIN(h.population)) / (MAX(h.year) - MIN(h.year)) AS population_growth_rate FROM countries c INNER JOIN historical_data h ON c.country_id = h.country_id GROUP BY c.country_id, c.country_name ) SELECT pg.country_name, pg.population_growth_rate FROM PopulationGrowth pg ORDER BY pg.population_growth_rate DESC
gold_sql.mysql: WITH PopulationGrowth AS (SELECT c.country_id, c.country_name, MIN(h.year) AS earliest_year, MAX(h.year) AS latest_year, MIN(h.population) AS earliest_population, MAX(h.population) AS latest_population, (MAX(h.population) - MIN(h.population)) / (MAX(h.year) - MIN(h.year)) AS population_growth_rate FROM countries AS c INNER JOIN historical_data AS h ON c.country_id = h.country_id GROUP BY c.country_id, c.country_name) SELECT pg.country_name, pg.population_growth_rate FROM PopulationGrowth AS pg ORDER BY pg.population_growth_rate DESC
gold_sql.postgres: WITH PopulationGrowth AS (SELECT c.country_id, c.country_name, MIN(h.year) AS earliest_year, MAX(h.year) AS latest_year, MIN(h.population) AS earliest_population, MAX(h.population) AS latest_population, (MAX(h.population) - MIN(h.population)) / NULLIF((MAX(h.year) - MIN(h.year)), 0) AS population_growth_rate FROM countries AS c INNER JOIN historical_data AS h ON c.country_id = h.country_id GROUP BY c.country_id, c.country_name) SELECT pg.country_name, pg.population_growth_rate FROM PopulationGrowth AS pg ORDER BY pg.population_growth_rate DESC NULLS LAST

question: Could you please gather all icon types that have been used more than once, along with the number of times they are used and the names of users who have access to the projects that use these icons? I really need to know the results sorted by the most frequently used icon types!

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT it.icon_type_name, COUNT(piu.project_icon_usage_id) AS usage_count, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT u.user_name) AS user_names FROM icon_types it INNER JOIN project_icon_usage piu ON it.icon_type_id = piu.icon_type_id INNER JOIN user_access ua ON piu.project_id = ua.project_id INNER JOIN users u ON ua.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY it.icon_type_id, it.icon_type_name HAVING COUNT(piu.project_icon_usage_id) > 1 ORDER BY usage_count DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT it.icon_type_name, COUNT(piu.project_icon_usage_id) AS usage_count, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT u.user_name SEPARATOR ',') AS user_names FROM icon_types AS it INNER JOIN project_icon_usage AS piu ON it.icon_type_id = piu.icon_type_id INNER JOIN user_access AS ua ON piu.project_id = ua.project_id INNER JOIN users AS u ON ua.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY it.icon_type_id, it.icon_type_name HAVING COUNT(piu.project_icon_usage_id) > 1 ORDER BY usage_count DESC
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT it.icon_type_name, COUNT(piu.project_icon_usage_id) AS usage_count, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT u.user_name, ',') AS user_names FROM icon_types AS it INNER JOIN project_icon_usage AS piu ON it.icon_type_id = piu.icon_type_id INNER JOIN user_access AS ua ON piu.project_id = ua.project_id INNER JOIN users AS u ON ua.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY it.icon_type_id, it.icon_type_name HAVING COUNT(piu.project_icon_usage_id) > 1 ORDER BY usage_count DESC NULLS LAST

question:

question: Hey, can you find the best success rate for each test scenario and software version, considering only the completed test runs where the vehicle health is good? I'd love to know the scenario names, software version numbers, and their corresponding best success rates.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH TestRunCTE AS ( SELECT tr.test_scenario_id, tr.software_version_id, sv.version_number, vs.scenario_name, tr.success_rate, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY tr.test_scenario_id, tr.software_version_id ORDER BY CAST(SUBSTR(tr.success_rate, 1, INSTR(tr.success_rate, '%') - 1) AS REAL) DESC) AS success_rate_rank FROM test_runs tr JOIN test_scenarios vs ON tr.test_scenario_id = vs.scenario_id JOIN software_versions sv ON tr.software_version_id = sv.version_id JOIN vehicle_health vh ON tr.vehicle_config_id = vh.vehicle_config_id WHERE tr.test_run_status = 'completed' AND vh.health_status = 'good' ) SELECT scenario_name, version_number, MAX(success_rate) AS best_success_rate FROM TestRunCTE WHERE success_rate_rank = 1 GROUP BY scenario_name, version_number
gold_sql.mysql: WITH TestRunCTE AS (SELECT tr.test_scenario_id, tr.software_version_id, sv.version_number, vs.scenario_name, tr.success_rate, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY tr.test_scenario_id, tr.software_version_id ORDER BY CAST(SUBSTRING(tr.success_rate, 1, LOCATE('%', tr.success_rate) - 1) AS FLOAT) DESC) AS success_rate_rank FROM test_runs AS tr JOIN test_scenarios AS vs ON tr.test_scenario_id = vs.scenario_id JOIN software_versions AS sv ON tr.software_version_id = sv.version_id JOIN vehicle_health AS vh ON tr.vehicle_config_id = vh.vehicle_config_id WHERE tr.test_run_status = 'completed' AND vh.health_status = 'good') SELECT scenario_name, version_number, MAX(success_rate) AS best_success_rate FROM TestRunCTE WHERE success_rate_rank = 1 GROUP BY scenario_name, version_number
gold_sql.postgres: WITH TestRunCTE AS (SELECT tr.test_scenario_id, tr.software_version_id, sv.version_number, vs.scenario_name, tr.success_rate, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY tr.test_scenario_id, tr.software_version_id ORDER BY CAST(SUBSTRING(tr.success_rate FROM 1 FOR STRPOS(tr.success_rate, '%') - 1) AS REAL) DESC NULLS LAST) AS success_rate_rank FROM test_runs AS tr JOIN test_scenarios AS vs ON tr.test_scenario_id = vs.scenario_id JOIN software_versions AS sv ON tr.software_version_id = sv.version_id JOIN vehicle_health AS vh ON tr.vehicle_config_id = vh.vehicle_config_id WHERE tr.test_run_status = 'completed' AND vh.health_status = 'good') SELECT scenario_name, version_number, MAX(success_rate) AS best_success_rate FROM TestRunCTE WHERE success_rate_rank = 1 GROUP BY scenario_name, version_number

question: Could you please gather all product categories along with their names, descriptions, total sales volumes, total revenues, average customer engagement, promotion counts, promotion details, latest market trends, and top contributing users (including usernames, job titles, and change counts) for each category? Please order the results by the total revenue in descending order.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH CategoryPerformanceCTE AS ( SELECT category_id, SUM(sales_volume) AS total_sales_volume, SUM(revenue) AS total_revenue, AVG(customer_engagement) AS average_customer_engagement, MAX(record_date) AS latest_record_date FROM category_performance GROUP BY category_id ), PromotionCTE AS ( SELECT category_id, COUNT(promotion_id) AS promotion_count, GROUP_CONCAT(promotion_details) AS promotion_details FROM category_promotions GROUP BY category_id ), LatestMarketTrendCTE AS ( SELECT cp.category_id, cp.market_trend FROM category_performance cp INNER JOIN ( SELECT category_id, MAX(record_date) AS latest_record_date FROM category_performance GROUP BY category_id ) latest_cp ON cp.category_id = latest_cp.category_id AND cp.record_date = latest_cp.latest_record_date ), TopUsersCTE AS ( SELECT cl.category_id, u.username, u.job_title, COUNT(cl.log_id) AS change_count FROM category_logs cl INNER JOIN users u ON cl.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY cl.category_id, u.username, u.job_title ), TopContributorCTE AS ( SELECT category_id, MAX(change_count) AS max_change_count FROM TopUsersCTE GROUP BY category_id ) SELECT pc.category_id, pc.name, pc.description, cp.total_sales_volume, cp.total_revenue, cp.average_customer_engagement, COALESCE(p.promotion_count, 0) AS promotion_count, p.promotion_details, lmt.market_trend, tu.username, tu.job_title, tu.change_count FROM product_categories pc LEFT JOIN CategoryPerformanceCTE cp ON pc.category_id = cp.category_id LEFT JOIN PromotionCTE p ON pc.category_id = p.category_id LEFT JOIN LatestMarketTrendCTE lmt ON pc.category_id = lmt.category_id LEFT JOIN TopUsersCTE tu ON pc.category_id = tu.category_id AND tu.change_count = ( SELECT max_change_count FROM TopContributorCTE WHERE category_id = pc.category_id ) ORDER BY cp.total_revenue DESC
gold_sql.mysql: WITH CategoryPerformanceCTE AS (SELECT category_id, SUM(sales_volume) AS total_sales_volume, SUM(revenue) AS total_revenue, AVG(customer_engagement) AS average_customer_engagement, MAX(record_date) AS latest_record_date FROM category_performance GROUP BY category_id), PromotionCTE AS (SELECT category_id, COUNT(promotion_id) AS promotion_count, GROUP_CONCAT(promotion_details SEPARATOR ',') AS promotion_details FROM category_promotions GROUP BY category_id), LatestMarketTrendCTE AS (SELECT cp.category_id, cp.market_trend FROM category_performance AS cp INNER JOIN (SELECT category_id, MAX(record_date) AS latest_record_date FROM category_performance GROUP BY category_id) AS latest_cp ON cp.category_id = latest_cp.category_id AND cp.record_date = latest_cp.latest_record_date), TopUsersCTE AS (SELECT cl.category_id, u.username, u.job_title, COUNT(cl.log_id) AS change_count FROM category_logs AS cl INNER JOIN users AS u ON cl.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY cl.category_id, u.username, u.job_title), TopContributorCTE AS (SELECT category_id, MAX(change_count) AS max_change_count FROM TopUsersCTE GROUP BY category_id) SELECT pc.category_id, pc.name, pc.description, cp.total_sales_volume, cp.total_revenue, cp.average_customer_engagement, COALESCE(p.promotion_count, 0) AS promotion_count, p.promotion_details, lmt.market_trend, tu.username, tu.job_title, tu.change_count FROM product_categories AS pc LEFT JOIN CategoryPerformanceCTE AS cp ON pc.category_id = cp.category_id LEFT JOIN PromotionCTE AS p ON pc.category_id = p.category_id LEFT JOIN LatestMarketTrendCTE AS lmt ON pc.category_id = lmt.category_id LEFT JOIN TopUsersCTE AS tu ON pc.category_id = tu.category_id AND tu.change_count = (SELECT max_change_count FROM TopContributorCTE WHERE category_id = pc.category_id) ORDER BY cp.total_revenue DESC
gold_sql.postgres: WITH CategoryPerformanceCTE AS (SELECT category_id, SUM(sales_volume) AS total_sales_volume, SUM(revenue) AS total_revenue, AVG(customer_engagement) AS average_customer_engagement, MAX(record_date) AS latest_record_date FROM category_performance GROUP BY category_id), PromotionCTE AS (SELECT category_id, COUNT(promotion_id) AS promotion_count, STRING_AGG(promotion_details, ',') AS promotion_details FROM category_promotions GROUP BY category_id), LatestMarketTrendCTE AS (SELECT cp.category_id, cp.market_trend FROM category_performance AS cp INNER JOIN (SELECT category_id, MAX(record_date) AS latest_record_date FROM category_performance GROUP BY category_id) AS latest_cp ON cp.category_id = latest_cp.category_id AND cp.record_date = latest_cp.latest_record_date), TopUsersCTE AS (SELECT cl.category_id, u.username, u.job_title, COUNT(cl.log_id) AS change_count FROM category_logs AS cl INNER JOIN users AS u ON cl.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY cl.category_id, u.username, u.job_title), TopContributorCTE AS (SELECT category_id, MAX(change_count) AS max_change_count FROM TopUsersCTE GROUP BY category_id) SELECT pc.category_id, pc.name, pc.description, cp.total_sales_volume, cp.total_revenue, cp.average_customer_engagement, COALESCE(p.promotion_count, 0) AS promotion_count, p.promotion_details, lmt.market_trend, tu.username, tu.job_title, tu.change_count FROM product_categories AS pc LEFT JOIN CategoryPerformanceCTE AS cp ON pc.category_id = cp.category_id LEFT JOIN PromotionCTE AS p ON pc.category_id = p.category_id LEFT JOIN LatestMarketTrendCTE AS lmt ON pc.category_id = lmt.category_id LEFT JOIN TopUsersCTE AS tu ON pc.category_id = tu.category_id AND tu.change_count = (SELECT max_change_count FROM TopContributorCTE WHERE category_id = pc.category_id) ORDER BY cp.total_revenue DESC NULLS LAST

question: Find the names and locations of the sites with the highest and lowest traffic volumes on August 31, 2018, along with their total traffic and average traffic per hour, and categorize them as having the highest, lowest, or average traffic volume for that day.
external_knowledge: August 31, 2018, is the specific date for which the traffic volume analysis is performed; The traffic volume refers to the total count of all vehicles (sum of large and small vehicles) on a particular date.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH DailyTraffic AS ( SELECT site_id, SUM(total_vehicle_count) AS total_vehicles, COUNT(DISTINCT strftime('%H', collection_date)) AS hours_count FROM traffic_data WHERE DATE(collection_date) = '2018-08-31' GROUP BY site_id ), SiteStats AS ( SELECT dt.site_id, dt.total_vehicles, dt.hours_count, dt.total_vehicles / dt.hours_count AS avg_vehicles_per_hour, MAX(dt.total_vehicles) OVER () AS max_total, MIN(dt.total_vehicles) OVER () AS min_total FROM DailyTraffic dt ) SELECT ms.site_name, ms.location, ss.total_vehicles, ss.avg_vehicles_per_hour, CASE WHEN ss.total_vehicles = ss.max_total THEN 'Highest' WHEN ss.total_vehicles = ss.min_total THEN 'Lowest' ELSE 'Average' END AS traffic_volume_rank FROM SiteStats ss JOIN monitoring_sites ms ON ss.site_id = ms.site_id ORDER BY ss.total_vehicles DESC
gold_sql.mysql: WITH DailyTraffic AS (SELECT site_id, SUM(total_vehicle_count) AS total_vehicles, COUNT(DISTINCT DATE_FORMAT(CAST(collection_date AS DATETIME), '%H')) AS hours_count FROM traffic_data WHERE DATE(collection_date) = '2018-08-31' GROUP BY site_id), SiteStats AS (SELECT dt.site_id, dt.total_vehicles, dt.hours_count, dt.total_vehicles / dt.hours_count AS avg_vehicles_per_hour, MAX(dt.total_vehicles) OVER () AS max_total, MIN(dt.total_vehicles) OVER () AS min_total FROM DailyTraffic AS dt) SELECT ms.site_name, ms.location, ss.total_vehicles, ss.avg_vehicles_per_hour, CASE WHEN ss.total_vehicles = ss.max_total THEN 'Highest' WHEN ss.total_vehicles = ss.min_total THEN 'Lowest' ELSE 'Average' END AS traffic_volume_rank FROM SiteStats AS ss JOIN monitoring_sites AS ms ON ss.site_id = ms.site_id ORDER BY ss.total_vehicles DESC
gold_sql.postgres: WITH DailyTraffic AS (SELECT site_id, SUM(total_vehicle_count) AS total_vehicles, COUNT(DISTINCT TO_CHAR(CAST(collection_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'HH24')) AS hours_count FROM traffic_data WHERE DATE(collection_date) = '2018-08-31' GROUP BY site_id), SiteStats AS (SELECT dt.site_id, dt.total_vehicles, dt.hours_count, dt.total_vehicles / NULLIF(dt.hours_count, 0) AS avg_vehicles_per_hour, MAX(dt.total_vehicles) OVER () AS max_total, MIN(dt.total_vehicles) OVER () AS min_total FROM DailyTraffic AS dt) SELECT ms.site_name, ms.location, ss.total_vehicles, ss.avg_vehicles_per_hour, CASE WHEN ss.total_vehicles = ss.max_total THEN 'Highest' WHEN ss.total_vehicles = ss.min_total THEN 'Lowest' ELSE 'Average' END AS traffic_volume_rank FROM SiteStats AS ss JOIN monitoring_sites AS ms ON ss.site_id = ms.site_id ORDER BY ss.total_vehicles DESC NULLS LAST

question: What are the titles of the most influential articles based on their citation impact, considering the top three with the highest scores?
external_knowledge: Influence score is a measure of an article's impact, calculated by dividing the total citation count by the number of authors; Articles with higher influence scores are considered more influential.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ArticleInfluence AS ( SELECT a.article_id, a.title, a.doi, COUNT(DISTINCT aa.author_id) AS author_count, SUM(c.citation_count) AS total_citations, (SUM(c.citation_count) / COUNT(DISTINCT aa.author_id)) AS influence_score FROM articles a LEFT JOIN article_authors aa ON a.article_id = aa.article_id LEFT JOIN citations c ON a.article_id = c.article_id GROUP BY a.article_id, a.title, a.doi ), RankedArticles AS ( SELECT article_id, title, doi, author_count, total_citations, influence_score, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY influence_score DESC) AS influence_rank FROM ArticleInfluence ) SELECT title FROM RankedArticles WHERE influence_rank <= 3
gold_sql.mysql: WITH ArticleInfluence AS (SELECT a.article_id, a.title, a.doi, COUNT(DISTINCT aa.author_id) AS author_count, SUM(c.citation_count) AS total_citations, (SUM(c.citation_count) / COUNT(DISTINCT aa.author_id)) AS influence_score FROM articles AS a LEFT JOIN article_authors AS aa ON a.article_id = aa.article_id LEFT JOIN citations AS c ON a.article_id = c.article_id GROUP BY a.article_id, a.title, a.doi), RankedArticles AS (SELECT article_id, title, doi, author_count, total_citations, influence_score, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY influence_score DESC) AS influence_rank FROM ArticleInfluence) SELECT title FROM RankedArticles WHERE influence_rank <= 3
gold_sql.postgres: WITH ArticleInfluence AS (SELECT a.article_id, a.title, a.doi, COUNT(DISTINCT aa.author_id) AS author_count, SUM(c.citation_count) AS total_citations, (SUM(c.citation_count) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT aa.author_id), 0)) AS influence_score FROM articles AS a LEFT JOIN article_authors AS aa ON a.article_id = aa.article_id LEFT JOIN citations AS c ON a.article_id = c.article_id GROUP BY a.article_id, a.title, a.doi), RankedArticles AS (SELECT article_id, title, doi, author_count, total_citations, influence_score, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY influence_score DESC NULLS LAST) AS influence_rank FROM ArticleInfluence) SELECT title FROM RankedArticles WHERE influence_rank <= 3

question: List each department's manager and their respective department's average hours worked per month, sorted by department and month.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH DepartmentManagers AS ( SELECT d.department_id, e.first_name AS manager_first_name, e.last_name AS manager_last_name FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.manager_id = e.employee_id ), MonthlyHours AS ( SELECT e.department_id, strftime('%Y-%m', a.date) AS month, AVG(a.hours_worked) AS average_hours_worked FROM attendance a JOIN employees e ON a.employee_id = e.employee_id GROUP BY e.department_id, strftime('%Y-%m', a.date) ) SELECT dm.department_id, dm.manager_first_name || ' ' || dm.manager_last_name AS department_manager, mh.month, mh.average_hours_worked FROM DepartmentManagers dm JOIN MonthlyHours mh ON dm.department_id = mh.department_id ORDER BY dm.department_id, mh.month
gold_sql.mysql: WITH DepartmentManagers AS (SELECT d.department_id, e.first_name AS manager_first_name, e.last_name AS manager_last_name FROM departments AS d JOIN employees AS e ON d.manager_id = e.employee_id), MonthlyHours AS (SELECT e.department_id, DATE_FORMAT(CAST(a.date AS DATETIME), '%Y-%m') AS month, AVG(a.hours_worked) AS average_hours_worked FROM attendance AS a JOIN employees AS e ON a.employee_id = e.employee_id GROUP BY e.department_id, DATE_FORMAT(CAST(a.date AS DATETIME), '%Y-%m')) SELECT dm.department_id, CONCAT(dm.manager_first_name, ' ', dm.manager_last_name) AS department_manager, mh.month, mh.average_hours_worked FROM DepartmentManagers AS dm JOIN MonthlyHours AS mh ON dm.department_id = mh.department_id ORDER BY dm.department_id, mh.month

question: Find the average level of concern and average level of knowledge about seasonal flu, as well as the average rank based on age, for all adult respondents (18 years old or older) who have received a seasonal flu vaccine.

question:
