question: What is the average warranty period in months for active 'RG-S5310 Switch Series' products that have a latest user manual available?
external_knowledge: The warranty period is usually specified in years or months; 1 year is equivalent to 12 months.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT AVG( CASE WHEN p.warranty_period LIKE '%years%' THEN CAST(SUBSTR(p.warranty_period, 1, INSTR(p.warranty_period, ' ') - 1) AS REAL) * 12 WHEN p.warranty_period LIKE '%months%' THEN CAST(SUBSTR(p.warranty_period, 1, INSTR(p.warranty_period, ' ') - 1) AS REAL) ELSE NULL END ) AS average_warranty_months FROM products p INNER JOIN product_families pf ON p.product_family = pf.family_name LEFT JOIN product_documents pd ON p.product_id = pd.product_id WHERE p.is_active = 1 AND pf.family_name = 'RG-S5310 Switch Series' AND pd.document_type = 'user manual' AND pd.is_latest = 1
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT AVG(CASE WHEN p.warranty_period LIKE '%years%' THEN CAST(SUBSTRING(p.warranty_period, 1, LOCATE(' ', p.warranty_period) - 1) AS FLOAT) * 12 WHEN p.warranty_period LIKE '%months%' THEN CAST(SUBSTRING(p.warranty_period, 1, LOCATE(' ', p.warranty_period) - 1) AS FLOAT) ELSE NULL END) AS average_warranty_months FROM products AS p INNER JOIN product_families AS pf ON p.product_family = pf.family_name LEFT JOIN product_documents AS pd ON p.product_id = pd.product_id WHERE p.is_active = 1 AND pf.family_name = 'RG-S5310 Switch Series' AND pd.document_type = 'user manual' AND pd.is_latest = 1
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT AVG(CASE WHEN p.warranty_period LIKE '%years%' THEN CAST(SUBSTRING(p.warranty_period FROM 1 FOR STRPOS(p.warranty_period, ' ') - 1) AS REAL) * 12 WHEN p.warranty_period LIKE '%months%' THEN CAST(SUBSTRING(p.warranty_period FROM 1 FOR STRPOS(p.warranty_period, ' ') - 1) AS REAL) ELSE NULL END) AS average_warranty_months FROM products AS p INNER JOIN product_families AS pf ON p.product_family = pf.family_name LEFT JOIN product_documents AS pd ON p.product_id = pd.product_id WHERE p.is_active = 1 AND pf.family_name = 'RG-S5310 Switch Series' AND pd.document_type = 'user manual' AND pd.is_latest = 1

question: What information is available about public machine learning models, including their evaluation metrics, fairness metrics, and the actions performed on them by different users?
external_knowledge: Public models refer to machine learning models that are accessible and usable by anyone, as opposed to private models which are restricted; Evaluation metrics such as accuracy, F1 score, precision, and recall are used to assess the performance of machine learning models; Fairness metrics like disparate impact and demographic parity difference help in evaluating the fairness of models across different groups.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ModelEvals AS ( SELECT m.model_id, m.model_name, m.description, m.framework, m.algorithm, m.dataset, m.is_public, e.evaluation_id, e.accuracy, e.f1_score, e.precision, e.recall, e.evaluation_date, e.train_accuracy, e.train_f1_score, e.train_precision, e.train_recall, fm.avg_abs_odds_diff, fm.balanced_acc, fm.theil_index, fm.disparate_impact, fm.demographic_parity_diff, fm.equal_opportunity_diff, fm.group_coefficient_of_variation FROM models m INNER JOIN evaluations e ON m.model_id = e.model_id LEFT JOIN fairness_metrics fm ON e.evaluation_id = fm.evaluation_id ), EvalLogs AS ( SELECT el.evaluation_id, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT u.user_name) AS users_involved, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT el.action) AS actions_performed FROM evaluation_logs el INNER JOIN users u ON el.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY el.evaluation_id ) SELECT me.model_id, me.model_name, me.description, me.framework, me.algorithm, me.dataset, me.is_public, me.evaluation_id, me.accuracy, me.f1_score, me.precision, me.recall, me.evaluation_date, me.train_accuracy, me.train_f1_score, me.train_precision, me.train_recall, me.avg_abs_odds_diff, me.balanced_acc, me.theil_index, me.disparate_impact, me.demographic_parity_diff, me.equal_opportunity_diff, me.group_coefficient_of_variation, el.users_involved, el.actions_performed FROM ModelEvals me LEFT JOIN EvalLogs el ON me.evaluation_id = el.evaluation_id WHERE me.is_public = 1 ORDER BY me.model_name ASC
gold_sql.mysql: WITH ModelEvals AS (SELECT m.model_id, m.model_name, m.description, m.framework, m.algorithm, m.dataset, m.is_public, e.evaluation_id, e.accuracy, e.f1_score, e.`precision`, e.recall, e.evaluation_date, e.train_accuracy, e.train_f1_score, e.train_precision, e.train_recall, fm.avg_abs_odds_diff, fm.balanced_acc, fm.theil_index, fm.disparate_impact, fm.demographic_parity_diff, fm.equal_opportunity_diff, fm.group_coefficient_of_variation FROM models AS m INNER JOIN evaluations AS e ON m.model_id = e.model_id LEFT JOIN fairness_metrics AS fm ON e.evaluation_id = fm.evaluation_id), EvalLogs AS (SELECT el.evaluation_id, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT u.user_name SEPARATOR ',') AS users_involved, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT el.action SEPARATOR ',') AS actions_performed FROM evaluation_logs AS el INNER JOIN users AS u ON el.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY el.evaluation_id) SELECT me.model_id, me.model_name, me.description, me.framework, me.algorithm, me.dataset, me.is_public, me.evaluation_id, me.accuracy, me.f1_score, me.`precision`, me.recall, me.evaluation_date, me.train_accuracy, me.train_f1_score, me.train_precision, me.train_recall, me.avg_abs_odds_diff, me.balanced_acc, me.theil_index, me.disparate_impact, me.demographic_parity_diff, me.equal_opportunity_diff, me.group_coefficient_of_variation, el.users_involved, el.actions_performed FROM ModelEvals AS me LEFT JOIN EvalLogs AS el ON me.evaluation_id = el.evaluation_id WHERE me.is_public = 1 ORDER BY me.model_name ASC
gold_sql.postgres: WITH ModelEvals AS (SELECT m.model_id, m.model_name, m.description, m.framework, m.algorithm, m.dataset, m.is_public, e.evaluation_id, e.accuracy, e.f1_score, e.precision, e.recall, e.evaluation_date, e.train_accuracy, e.train_f1_score, e.train_precision, e.train_recall, fm.avg_abs_odds_diff, fm.balanced_acc, fm.theil_index, fm.disparate_impact, fm.demographic_parity_diff, fm.equal_opportunity_diff, fm.group_coefficient_of_variation FROM models AS m INNER JOIN evaluations AS e ON m.model_id = e.model_id LEFT JOIN fairness_metrics AS fm ON e.evaluation_id = fm.evaluation_id), EvalLogs AS (SELECT el.evaluation_id, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT u.user_name, ',') AS users_involved, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT el.action, ',') AS actions_performed FROM evaluation_logs AS el INNER JOIN users AS u ON el.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY el.evaluation_id) SELECT me.model_id, me.model_name, me.description, me.framework, me.algorithm, me.dataset, me.is_public, me.evaluation_id, me.accuracy, me.f1_score, me.precision, me.recall, me.evaluation_date, me.train_accuracy, me.train_f1_score, me.train_precision, me.train_recall, me.avg_abs_odds_diff, me.balanced_acc, me.theil_index, me.disparate_impact, me.demographic_parity_diff, me.equal_opportunity_diff, me.group_coefficient_of_variation, el.users_involved, el.actions_performed FROM ModelEvals AS me LEFT JOIN EvalLogs AS el ON me.evaluation_id = el.evaluation_id WHERE me.is_public = 1 ORDER BY me.model_name ASC NULLS FIRST

question:
**User**: I want to analyze some video data.
**Assistant**: What specific information about the videos are you looking to analyze?
**User**: I'd like to know the average visibility and confidence of objects in the videos, as well as the average quality of the frames.
**Assistant**: That's interesting. Would you like to group this information by video ID, capture location, and resolution?
**User**: Yes, that would be helpful. Also, can you include any alert information associated with the videos?
**Assistant**: I can do that. Would you like to see the count and messages of the alerts for each capture location and resolution?
**User**: Yes, that would be great. And can you also tell me how many distinct object classes are detected in the videos?
**Assistant**: I can do that. Finally, how would you like the results to be ordered?
**User**: I'd like to see the results ordered by the total number of alerts in descending order, followed by capture location and resolution.
**Assistant**: OK, I will help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH VideoStats AS ( SELECT v.video_id, v.capture_location, v.resolution, AVG(o.visibility) AS avg_visibility, AVG(o.confidence) AS avg_confidence, AVG(f.quality) AS avg_frame_quality FROM videos v JOIN frames f ON v.video_id = f.video_id JOIN objects o ON f.frame_id = o.frame_id GROUP BY v.video_id, v.capture_location, v.resolution ), AlertSummary AS ( SELECT v.capture_location, v.resolution, COUNT(a.alert_id) AS alert_count, GROUP_CONCAT(a.alert_message, ', ') AS alert_messages FROM videos v JOIN alerts a ON v.video_id = a.video_id GROUP BY v.capture_location, v.resolution ), CombinedStats AS ( SELECT vs.capture_location, vs.resolution, vs.avg_visibility, vs.avg_confidence, vs.avg_frame_quality, COALESCE(asum.alert_count, 0) AS total_alerts, asum.alert_messages FROM VideoStats vs LEFT JOIN AlertSummary asum ON vs.capture_location = asum.capture_location AND vs.resolution = asum.resolution ) SELECT capture_location, resolution, CAST(avg_visibility AS REAL) AS avg_visibility, CAST(avg_confidence AS REAL) AS avg_confidence, CAST(avg_frame_quality AS REAL) AS avg_frame_quality, total_alerts, alert_messages, ( SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT o.class) FROM objects o JOIN frames f ON o.frame_id = f.frame_id JOIN videos v ON f.video_id = v.video_id WHERE v.capture_location = cs.capture_location AND v.resolution = cs.resolution ) AS distinct_object_classes FROM CombinedStats cs ORDER BY total_alerts DESC, capture_location, resolution

question: Could you please gather all the active datasets along with their most recent version information, including the version number, creation date, variables, attribute summaries for each variable, and details about the users who have shared the dataset, including the share date and permission level? Additionally, I need to know the total count of users with read-write access for each dataset, and please organize this information by dataset name, version, variable name, and share date in ascending order?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ActiveDatasets AS ( SELECT dataset_id, name AS dataset_name FROM datasets WHERE status = 'active' ), RecentVersions AS ( SELECT d.dataset_id, d.dataset_name, dv.version, dv.created_date AS version_created_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY d.dataset_id ORDER BY dv.created_date DESC) AS version_order FROM ActiveDatasets d LEFT JOIN dataset_versions dv ON d.dataset_id = dv.dataset_id ), MostRecentVersions AS ( SELECT dataset_id, dataset_name, version, version_created_date FROM RecentVersions WHERE version_order = 1 ), VariablesAttributes AS ( SELECT v.dataset_id, v.name AS variable_name, a.name AS attribute_name, a.value AS attribute_value, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY v.variable_id ORDER BY a.attribute_id) AS attribute_order FROM variables v LEFT JOIN attributes a ON v.variable_id = a.variable_id ), VariableAttributesSummary AS ( SELECT dataset_id, variable_name, GROUP_CONCAT(CASE WHEN attribute_order = 1 THEN attribute_name ELSE NULL END || ' - ' || attribute_value, ', ') AS attribute_summary FROM VariablesAttributes GROUP BY dataset_id, variable_name ), UserShares AS ( SELECT ds.dataset_id, u.name AS user_name, ds.shared_date, ds.permission FROM dataset_sharing ds INNER JOIN users u ON ds.user_id = u.user_id ) SELECT mrv.dataset_name, mrv.version, mrv.version_created_date, vas.variable_name, vas.attribute_summary, us.user_name, us.shared_date, us.permission, SUM(CASE WHEN us.permission = 'read-write' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY mrv.dataset_id) AS rw_share_count FROM MostRecentVersions mrv LEFT JOIN VariableAttributesSummary vas ON mrv.dataset_id = vas.dataset_id LEFT JOIN UserShares us ON mrv.dataset_id = us.dataset_id ORDER BY mrv.dataset_name, mrv.version, vas.variable_name, us.shared_date

question: Could you provide a comprehensive summary of all incidents, including incident ID, date, state, city, address, type, total casualties (fatalities and injuries), the number of responses along with their first and last response times, the number of updates along with their first and last update times, and the number of files along with their names, ordered from most recent to least recent by incident date?

question: What are the methods, paths, median response times, and failure rates of the top-performing endpoints for each HTTP method, considering both the fastest response times and the highest failure rates?
external_knowledge: Endpoints with low median response times are considered "top-performing" in terms of speed; Endpoints with high failure rates require further investigation to identify potential issues; HTTP methods (e.g., GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) are distinct categories for endpoint performance evaluation.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH EndpointMetrics AS ( SELECT ep.method, ep.path, pm.median_response_time, (pm.failure_count * 1.0 / pm.request_count) AS failure_rate FROM endpoints ep INNER JOIN performance_metrics pm ON ep.endpoint_id = pm.endpoint_id ), EndpointRanking AS ( SELECT em.method, em.path, em.median_response_time, em.failure_rate, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY em.method ORDER BY em.median_response_time ASC) AS response_time_rank, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY em.method ORDER BY em.failure_rate DESC) AS failure_rate_rank FROM EndpointMetrics em ) SELECT rank.method, rank.path, rank.median_response_time, rank.failure_rate FROM EndpointRanking rank WHERE rank.response_time_rank <= 3 OR rank.failure_rate_rank <= 3 ORDER BY rank.method, rank.median_response_time
gold_sql.mysql: WITH EndpointMetrics AS (SELECT ep.method, ep.path, pm.median_response_time, (pm.failure_count * 1.0 / pm.request_count) AS failure_rate FROM endpoints AS ep INNER JOIN performance_metrics AS pm ON ep.endpoint_id = pm.endpoint_id), EndpointRanking AS (SELECT em.method, em.path, em.median_response_time, em.failure_rate, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY em.method ORDER BY em.median_response_time ASC) AS response_time_rank, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY em.method ORDER BY em.failure_rate DESC) AS failure_rate_rank FROM EndpointMetrics AS em) SELECT `rank`.method, `rank`.path, `rank`.median_response_time, `rank`.failure_rate FROM EndpointRanking AS `rank` WHERE `rank`.response_time_rank <= 3 OR `rank`.failure_rate_rank <= 3 ORDER BY `rank`.method, `rank`.median_response_time
gold_sql.postgres: WITH EndpointMetrics AS (SELECT ep.method, ep.path, pm.median_response_time, (pm.failure_count * 1.0 / NULLIF(pm.request_count, 0)) AS failure_rate FROM endpoints AS ep INNER JOIN performance_metrics AS pm ON ep.endpoint_id = pm.endpoint_id), EndpointRanking AS (SELECT em.method, em.path, em.median_response_time, em.failure_rate, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY em.method ORDER BY em.median_response_time ASC NULLS FIRST) AS response_time_rank, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY em.method ORDER BY em.failure_rate DESC NULLS LAST) AS failure_rate_rank FROM EndpointMetrics AS em) SELECT rank.method, rank.path, rank.median_response_time, rank.failure_rate FROM EndpointRanking AS rank WHERE rank.response_time_rank <= 3 OR rank.failure_rate_rank <= 3 ORDER BY rank.method NULLS FIRST, rank.median_response_time NULLS FIRST

question: Hey, could you please provide me with a list of all the datasets, including their names, file paths, statuses, latest versions, sharers' names, departments, shared dates, and permission levels? question: In the vast garden of knowledge, which wise souls have gathered the most fruit from the tree of nutrition, and how much have they harvested?
external_knowledge:
- "Wise souls" refers to users who have taken nutrition-related assessments.

question: Find a detailed report of all timing parameters, including their names, diagram names, categories, versions, values, units, conditions, notes, and access statistics such as the number of times they were accessed, the users who accessed them, and the first and last access dates, sorted by parameter name, diagram name, and access frequency in descending order.
external_knowledge:
- In the context of this database, timing parameters are critical components that define the timing characteristics of a system or process.
- Access statistics can help identify which parameters are most frequently accessed and by whom, providing insights into usage patterns and potential areas for optimization.
- Understanding the relationships between timing parameters, their values, and access history can aid in troubleshooting, maintenance, and improvement of the system.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ParameterInfo AS ( SELECT tp.param_id, tp.param_name, td.diag_name, td.category, td.version, pd.value, pd.unit, c.condition, n.note FROM timing_parameters tp LEFT JOIN parameter_values pd ON tp.param_id = pd.param_id LEFT JOIN timing_diagrams td ON pd.diag_id = td.diag_id LEFT JOIN conditions c ON tp.param_id = c.param_id LEFT JOIN notes n ON tp.param_id = n.param_id ), AccessLogs AS ( SELECT al.param_id, COUNT(al.user_id) AS access_count, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT u.username) AS accessed_by, MIN(al.access_date) AS first_access, MAX(al.access_date) AS last_access FROM access_logs al JOIN users u ON al.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY al.param_id ) SELECT pi.param_name, pi.diag_name, pi.category, pi.version, pi.value, pi.unit, pi.condition, pi.note, al.access_count, al.accessed_by, al.first_access, al.last_access FROM ParameterInfo pi LEFT JOIN AccessLogs al ON pi.param_id = al.param_id ORDER BY pi.param_name, pi.diag_name, al.access_count DESC
gold_sql.mysql: WITH ParameterInfo AS (SELECT tp.param_id, tp.param_name, td.diag_name, td.category, td.version, pd.value, pd.unit, c.`condition`, n.note FROM timing_parameters AS tp LEFT JOIN parameter_values AS pd ON tp.param_id = pd.param_id LEFT JOIN timing_diagrams AS td ON pd.diag_id = td.diag_id LEFT JOIN conditions AS c ON tp.param_id = c.param_id LEFT JOIN notes AS n ON tp.param_id = n.param_id), AccessLogs AS (SELECT al.param_id, COUNT(al.user_id) AS access_count, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT u.username SEPARATOR ',') AS accessed_by, MIN(al.access_date) AS first_access, MAX(al.access_date) AS last_access FROM access_logs AS al JOIN users AS u ON al.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY al.param_id) SELECT pi.param_name, pi.diag_name, pi.category, pi.version, pi.value, pi.unit, pi.`condition`, pi.note, al.access_count, al.accessed_by, al.first_access, al.last_access FROM ParameterInfo AS pi LEFT JOIN AccessLogs AS al ON pi.param_id = al.param_id ORDER BY pi.param_name, pi.diag_name, al.access_count DESC
gold_sql.postgres: WITH ParameterInfo AS (SELECT tp.param_id, tp.param_name, td.diag_name, td.category, td.version, pd.value, pd.unit, c.condition, n.note FROM timing_parameters AS tp LEFT JOIN parameter_values AS pd ON tp.param_id = pd.param_id LEFT JOIN timing_diagrams AS td ON pd.diag_id = td.diag_id LEFT JOIN conditions AS c ON tp.param_id = c.param_id LEFT JOIN notes AS n ON tp.param_id = n.param_id), AccessLogs AS (SELECT al.param_id, COUNT(al.user_id) AS access_count, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT u.username, ',') AS accessed_by, MIN(al.access_date) AS first_access, MAX(al.access_date) AS last_access FROM access_logs AS al JOIN users AS u ON al.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY al.param_id) SELECT pi.param_name, pi.diag_name, pi.category, pi.version, pi.value, pi.unit, pi.condition, pi.note, al.access_count, al.accessed_by, al.first_access, al.last_access FROM ParameterInfo AS pi LEFT JOIN AccessLogs AS al ON pi.param_id = al.param_id ORDER BY pi.param_name NULLS FIRST, pi.diag_name NULLS FIRST, al.access_count DESC NULLS LAST

question: I want to know a summary of each model's performance, including the model name, a list of average performance metrics along with their respective metric names, and the timestamp of the last update, considering the most recent evaluation results for each model.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ModelPerformanceCTE AS ( SELECT m.model_id, m.model_name, br.mean_value AS avg_mean_value, mt.metric_name, br.updated_at AS last_updated, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY m.model_id, mt.metric_name ORDER BY br.updated_at DESC) as row_num FROM models m INNER JOIN evaluations e ON m.model_id = e.model_id INNER JOIN benchmark_results br ON e.evaluation_id = br.evaluation_id INNER JOIN metrics mt ON br.metric_id = mt.metric_id ) SELECT model_name || ': ' || GROUP_CONCAT(CAST(avg_mean_value AS TEXT) || ' (' || metric_name || ')', ', ') || ' [Updated: ' || MAX(last_updated) || ']' AS model_performance_summary FROM ModelPerformanceCTE mpc WHERE mpc.row_num = 1 GROUP BY mpc.model_name, mpc.model_id
gold_sql.mysql: WITH ModelPerformanceCTE AS (SELECT m.model_id, m.model_name, br.mean_value AS avg_mean_value, mt.metric_name, br.updated_at AS last_updated, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY m.model_id, mt.metric_name ORDER BY br.updated_at DESC) AS row_num FROM models AS m INNER JOIN evaluations AS e ON m.model_id = e.model_id INNER JOIN benchmark_results AS br ON e.evaluation_id = br.evaluation_id INNER JOIN metrics AS mt ON br.metric_id = mt.metric_id) SELECT CONCAT(model_name, ': ', GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(CAST(avg_mean_value AS CHAR), ' (', metric_name, ')') SEPARATOR ', '), ' [Updated: ', MAX(last_updated), ']') AS model_performance_summary FROM ModelPerformanceCTE AS mpc WHERE mpc.row_num = 1 GROUP BY mpc.model_name, mpc.model_id
gold_sql.postgres: WITH ModelPerformanceCTE AS (SELECT m.model_id, m.model_name, br.mean_value AS avg_mean_value, mt.metric_name, br.updated_at AS last_updated, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY m.model_id, mt.metric_name ORDER BY br.updated_at DESC NULLS LAST) AS row_num FROM models AS m INNER JOIN evaluations AS e ON m.model_id = e.model_id INNER JOIN benchmark_results AS br ON e.evaluation_id = br.evaluation_id INNER JOIN metrics AS mt ON br.metric_id = mt.metric_id) SELECT model_name || ': ' || STRING_AGG(CAST(avg_mean_value AS TEXT) || ' (' || metric_name || ')', ', ') || ' [Updated: ' || MAX(last_updated) || ']' AS model_performance_summary FROM ModelPerformanceCTE AS mpc WHERE mpc.row_num = 1 GROUP BY mpc.model_name, mpc.model_id

question: What are the summaries of completed model runs with average performance metrics above a certain threshold, including their run IDs, average performance metrics, and hyperparameters?
external_knowledge: The "certain threshold" refers to the average h_estimate being greater than 0.5; the hyperparameters are specified as "name: value" pairs; and summaries are for model runs with a "completed" status.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT mr.run_id, AVG(pm.h_estimate) AS average_h_estimate, GROUP_CONCAT(hp.name || ': ' || hp.value, ', ') AS hyperparameters FROM model_runs mr INNER JOIN performance_metrics pm ON mr.run_id = pm.run_id LEFT JOIN hyperparameters hp ON mr.run_id = hp.run_id WHERE mr.status = 'completed' GROUP BY mr.run_id HAVING AVG(pm.h_estimate) > 0.5
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT mr.run_id, AVG(pm.h_estimate) AS average_h_estimate, GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(hp.name, ': ', hp.value) SEPARATOR ', ') AS hyperparameters FROM model_runs AS mr INNER JOIN performance_metrics AS pm ON mr.run_id = pm.run_id LEFT JOIN hyperparameters AS hp ON mr.run_id = hp.run_id WHERE mr.status = 'completed' GROUP BY mr.run_id HAVING AVG(pm.h_estimate) > 0.5
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT mr.run_id, AVG(pm.h_estimate) AS average_h_estimate, STRING_AGG(hp.name || ': ' || hp.value, ', ') AS hyperparameters FROM model_runs AS mr INNER JOIN performance_metrics AS pm ON mr.run_id = pm.run_id LEFT JOIN hyperparameters AS hp ON mr.run_id = hp.run_id WHERE mr.status = 'completed' GROUP BY mr.run_id HAVING AVG(pm.h_estimate) > 0.5

question: Return the dataset IDs, names, latest versions, and latest version creation dates for all datasets, along with a list of users they are shared with (including their names, emails, and permissions) and a list of variables (including their names, data types, units, descriptions, coordinate systems, and attributes).

question: What are the runs with the highest view access ratios?
external_knowledge: The view access ratio is calculated as the number of 'view' access events divided by the total number of access events for each run; view access ratio = (number of 'view' access events) / (total number of access events).

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT r.run_id, AVG(CASE WHEN a.access_type = 'view' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(a.access_type) AS view_ratio FROM runs r LEFT JOIN access_logs a ON r.run_id = a.run_id GROUP BY r.run_id ORDER BY view_ratio DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT r.run_id, AVG(CASE WHEN a.access_type = 'view' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(a.access_type) AS view_ratio FROM runs AS r LEFT JOIN access_logs AS a ON r.run_id = a.run_id GROUP BY r.run_id ORDER BY view_ratio DESC
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT r.run_id, AVG(CASE WHEN a.access_type = 'view' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(a.access_type), 0) AS view_ratio FROM runs AS r LEFT JOIN access_logs AS a ON r.run_id = a.run_id GROUP BY r.run_id ORDER BY view_ratio DESC NULLS LAST

question: Hey! Could you help me find out which loan officers have an approval rate over 50%, and also check if any of their approvals have been flagged as potential issues? I'd love to know their names, emails, and whether they have any flagged approvals.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH OfficerApprovals AS ( SELECT la.officer_id, COUNT(la.application_id) AS approvals_count, COUNT(DISTINCT ar.application_id) AS review_count, (COUNT(la.application_id) * 100.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT ar.application_id)) AS approval_rate FROM loan_approvals la LEFT JOIN application_reviews ar ON la.application_id = ar.application_id GROUP BY la.officer_id HAVING (COUNT(la.application_id) * 100.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT ar.application_id)) > 50 ), FlaggedApprovals AS ( SELECT DISTINCT la.officer_id FROM loan_approvals la JOIN audit_logs al ON la.application_id = CAST(al.action_description AS INTEGER) WHERE al.action_description LIKE '%loan approved%' AND al.action = 'flagged' ) SELECT lo.first_name, lo.last_name, lo.email, CASE WHEN fa.officer_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_potential_issues FROM OfficerApprovals oa JOIN loan_officers lo ON oa.officer_id = lo.officer_id LEFT JOIN FlaggedApprovals fa ON oa.officer_id = fa.officer_id ORDER BY has_potential_issues DESC, approval_rate DESC

gold_sql.postgres: WITH OfficerApprovals AS (SELECT la.officer_id, COUNT(la.application_id) AS approvals_count, COUNT(DISTINCT ar.application_id) AS review_count, (COUNT(la.application_id) * 100.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT ar.application_id), 0)) AS approval_rate FROM loan_approvals AS la LEFT JOIN application_reviews AS ar ON la.application_id = ar.application_id GROUP BY la.officer_id HAVING (COUNT(la.application_id) * 100.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT ar.application_id), 0)) > 50), FlaggedApprovals AS (SELECT DISTINCT la.officer_id FROM loan_approvals AS la JOIN audit_logs AS al ON la.application_id = CAST(al.action_description AS INT) WHERE al.action_description LIKE '%loan approved%' AND al.action = 'flagged') SELECT lo.first_name, lo.last_name, lo.email, CASE WHEN NOT fa.officer_id IS NULL THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_potential_issues FROM OfficerApprovals AS oa JOIN loan_officers AS lo ON oa.officer_id = lo.officer_id LEFT JOIN FlaggedApprovals AS fa ON oa.officer_id = fa.officer_id ORDER BY has_potential_issues DESC NULLS LAST, approval_rate DESC NULLS LAST

question: Hey, can you show me the categories and groups from the 2018 survey where the average response value is greater than 0.6, considering only responses with values above 0.5? I'd love to see the average response values for these categories and groups, and can you sort them in descending order of their average response values?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT c.category_name, g.group_name, AVG(r.value) AS average_response_value FROM responses r INNER JOIN surveys s ON r.survey_id = s.survey_id INNER JOIN categories c ON s.category_id = c.category_id INNER JOIN groups g ON s.group_id = g.group_id WHERE r.year = 2018 AND r.value > 0.5 GROUP BY c.category_name, g.group_name HAVING AVG(r.value) > 0.6 ORDER BY average_response_value DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT c.category_name, g.group_name, AVG(r.value) AS average_response_value FROM responses AS r INNER JOIN surveys AS s ON r.survey_id = s.survey_id INNER JOIN categories AS c ON s.category_id = c.category_id INNER JOIN `groups` AS g ON s.group_id = g.group_id WHERE r.year = 2018 AND r.value > 0.5 GROUP BY c.category_name, g.group_name HAVING AVG(r.value) > 0.6 ORDER BY average_response_value DESC

question: What are the names of the weather stations and the number of days with recorded data for each month of the year 2023, listed in order from January to December for each station?

question: I want to know the monthly revenue for each product category and region, along with the forecast model and model type used, for each month. The results should be ordered by month, region name, and category.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH MonthlySales AS ( SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', s.timestamp) AS month, p.category, r.region_name, SUM(s.revenue) AS monthly_revenue FROM sales_data s JOIN products p ON s.product_id = p.product_id JOIN regions r ON s.region_id = r.region_id GROUP BY strftime('%Y-%m', s.timestamp), p.category, r.region_name ) SELECT ms.month, ms.category, ms.region_name, ms.monthly_revenue, fm.model_name, fm.model_type FROM MonthlySales ms JOIN sales_forecasts sf ON ms.month = strftime('%Y-%m', sf.timestamp) JOIN forecast_models fm ON sf.model_id = fm.model_id ORDER BY ms.month, ms.region_name, ms.category

question: Could you please identify the months for each store where the total sales exceeded the average monthly sales by at least 20%? I need to know the store ID, the sale month, the total sales, and whether these sales exceeded the average by 20% or more.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH MonthlySales AS ( SELECT store_id, strftime('%Y-%m', sale_date) AS sale_month, SUM(ext_price) AS total_sales FROM sales GROUP BY store_id, strftime('%Y-%m', sale_date) ), MonthlyAverage AS ( SELECT store_id, AVG(total_sales) AS avg_monthly_sales FROM MonthlySales GROUP BY store_id ) SELECT ms.store_id, ms.sale_month, ms.total_sales, CASE WHEN (ms.total_sales - ma.avg_monthly_sales) / ma.avg_monthly_sales >= 0.2 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS exceeds_20_percent FROM MonthlySales ms JOIN MonthlyAverage ma ON ms.store_id = ma.store_id WHERE (ms.total_sales - ma.avg_monthly_sales) / ma.avg_monthly_sales >= 0.2 ORDER BY ms.store_id, ms.sale_month

question: Could you please calculate the total number of songs played by each user, grouped by their subscription level, for users located in 'Harrisburg-Carlisle, PA' and sessions that started in April 2023? Ensure that only users who have played at least one song are included in the results.

question: For E. coli outbreaks, return the location names, total cases, and the number of contributing factors for locations with at least one contributing factor.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT l.location_name, o.total_cases, COUNT(of.outbreak_factor_id) AS num_contributing_factors FROM outbreaks o INNER JOIN etiologies e ON o.etiology_id = e.etiology_id INNER JOIN locations l ON o.location_id = l.location_id LEFT JOIN outbreak_factors of ON o.outbreak_id = of.outbreak_id WHERE e.name = 'E. coli' GROUP BY l.location_name, o.total_cases HAVING COUNT(of.outbreak_factor_id) > 0
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT l.location_name, o.total_cases, COUNT(`of`.outbreak_factor_id) AS num_contributing_factors FROM outbreaks AS o INNER JOIN etiologies AS e ON o.etiology_id = e.etiology_id INNER JOIN locations AS l ON o.location_id = l.location_id LEFT JOIN outbreak_factors AS `of` ON o.outbreak_id = `of`.outbreak_id WHERE e.name = 'E. coli' GROUP BY l.location_name, o.total_cases HAVING COUNT(`of`.outbreak_factor_id) > 0
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT l.location_name, o.total_cases, COUNT(of.outbreak_factor_id) AS num_contributing_factors FROM outbreaks AS o INNER JOIN etiologies AS e ON o.etiology_id = e.etiology_id INNER JOIN locations AS l ON o.location_id = l.location_id LEFT JOIN outbreak_factors AS of ON o.outbreak_id = of.outbreak_id WHERE e.name = 'E. coli' GROUP BY l.location_name, o.total_cases HAVING COUNT(of.outbreak_factor_id) > 0

question: For each user, find the top 3 longest physical therapy sessions, including the session ID, user name, start time, end time, duration, location, and any additional notes.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH TherapySessions AS ( SELECT s.session_id, s.user_id, u.user_name, s.start_time, s.end_time, s.duration, s.location, s.notes, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.user_id ORDER BY CAST(SUBSTR(s.duration, 1, INSTR(s.duration, ' ') - 1) AS INTEGER) DESC) AS session_rank FROM sessions s INNER JOIN users u ON s.user_id = u.user_id INNER JOIN activities a ON s.activity_id = a.activity_id WHERE a.activity_name = 'physical_therapy' ) SELECT session_id, user_name, start_time, end_time, duration, location, notes FROM TherapySessions WHERE session_rank <= 3
gold_sql.mysql: WITH TherapySessions AS (SELECT s.session_id, s.user_id, u.user_name, s.start_time, s.end_time, s.duration, s.location, s.notes, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.user_id ORDER BY CAST(SUBSTRING(s.duration, 1, LOCATE(' ', s.duration) - 1) AS SIGNED) DESC) AS session_rank FROM sessions AS s INNER JOIN users AS u ON s.user_id = u.user_id INNER JOIN activities AS a ON s.activity_id = a.activity_id WHERE a.activity_name = 'physical_therapy') SELECT session_id, user_name, start_time, end_time, duration, location, notes FROM TherapySessions WHERE session_rank <= 3
gold_sql.postgres: WITH TherapySessions AS (SELECT s.session_id, s.user_id, u.user_name, s.start_time, s.end_time, s.duration, s.location, s.notes, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.user_id ORDER BY CAST(SUBSTRING(s.duration FROM 1 FOR STRPOS(s.duration, ' ') - 1) AS INT) DESC NULLS LAST) AS session_rank FROM sessions AS s INNER JOIN users AS u ON s.user_id = u.user_id INNER JOIN activities AS a ON s.activity_id = a.activity_id WHERE a.activity_name = 'physical_therapy') SELECT session_id, user_name, start_time, end_time, duration, location, notes FROM TherapySessions WHERE session_rank <= 3

question: Return the identifiers, accuracies, F1 scores, precisions, recalls, and evaluation dates of models with accuracies greater than 0.9, listed in order from most recently evaluated.

gold_sql.mysql: SELECT model_id, accuracy, f1_score, `precision`, recall, date_evaluated FROM model_performance WHERE accuracy > 0.9 ORDER BY date_evaluated DESC

question: Hey, can you show me the top 10 healthcare providers with the most patients and highest average confidence scores for their diabetes predictions from 2022 onwards? I'd like to see their IDs, names, locations, the total number of patients they've treated, how many of those patients have diabetes, their average confidence scores, and the actual diabetes rates among their patients. Please rank them based on the total number of patients and average confidence scores.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ProviderPatientData AS ( SELECT hp.provider_id, hp.provider_name, hp.location, pp.patient_id, dp.confidence_score, dp.actual_diabetes FROM healthcare_providers hp INNER JOIN patients_providers pp ON hp.provider_id = pp.provider_id INNER JOIN diabetes_predictions dp ON pp.patient_id = dp.patient_id WHERE dp.predicted_on >= '2022-01-01' ), ProviderPerformance AS ( SELECT provider_id, provider_name, location, COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) AS total_patients, SUM(CASE WHEN actual_diabetes = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS diabetic_patients, AVG(confidence_score) AS avg_confidence_score, SUM(CASE WHEN actual_diabetes = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) AS actual_diabetes_rate FROM ProviderPatientData GROUP BY provider_id, provider_name, location ), RankedProviders AS ( SELECT provider_id, provider_name, location, total_patients, diabetic_patients, avg_confidence_score, actual_diabetes_rate, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total_patients DESC, avg_confidence_score DESC) AS provider_rank FROM ProviderPerformance ) SELECT provider_id, provider_name, location, total_patients, diabetic_patients, avg_confidence_score, actual_diabetes_rate, 'Rank: ' || CAST(provider_rank AS TEXT) AS provider_rank_info FROM RankedProviders WHERE provider_rank <= 10 ORDER BY provider_rank
gold_sql.mysql: WITH ProviderPatientData AS (SELECT hp.provider_id, hp.provider_name, hp.location, pp.patient_id, dp.confidence_score, dp.actual_diabetes FROM healthcare_providers AS hp INNER JOIN patients_providers AS pp ON hp.provider_id = pp.provider_id INNER JOIN diabetes_predictions AS dp ON pp.patient_id = dp.patient_id WHERE dp.predicted_on >= '2022-01-01'), ProviderPerformance AS (SELECT provider_id, provider_name, location, COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) AS total_patients, SUM(CASE WHEN actual_diabetes = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS diabetic_patients, AVG(confidence_score) AS avg_confidence_score, SUM(CASE WHEN actual_diabetes = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) AS actual_diabetes_rate FROM ProviderPatientData GROUP BY provider_id, provider_name, location), RankedProviders AS (SELECT provider_id, provider_name, location, total_patients, diabetic_patients, avg_confidence_score, actual_diabetes_rate, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total_patients DESC, avg_confidence_score DESC) AS provider_rank FROM ProviderPerformance) SELECT provider_id, provider_name, location, total_patients, diabetic_patients, avg_confidence_score, actual_diabetes_rate, CONCAT('Rank: ', CAST(provider_rank AS CHAR)) AS provider_rank_info FROM RankedProviders WHERE provider_rank <= 10 ORDER BY provider_rank
gold_sql.postgres: WITH ProviderPatientData AS (SELECT hp.provider_id, hp.provider_name, hp.location, pp.patient_id, dp.confidence_score, dp.actual_diabetes FROM healthcare_providers AS hp INNER JOIN patients_providers AS pp ON hp.provider_id = pp.provider_id INNER JOIN diabetes_predictions AS dp ON pp.patient_id = dp.patient_id WHERE dp.predicted_on >= '2022-01-01'), ProviderPerformance AS (SELECT provider_id, provider_name, location, COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) AS total_patients, SUM(CASE WHEN actual_diabetes = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS diabetic_patients, AVG(confidence_score) AS avg_confidence_score, SUM(CASE WHEN actual_diabetes = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id), 0) AS actual_diabetes_rate FROM ProviderPatientData GROUP BY provider_id, provider_name, location), RankedProviders AS (SELECT provider_id, provider_name, location, total_patients, diabetic_patients, avg_confidence_score, actual_diabetes_rate, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total_patients DESC NULLS LAST, avg_confidence_score DESC NULLS LAST) AS provider_rank FROM ProviderPerformance) SELECT provider_id, provider_name, location, total_patients, diabetic_patients, avg_confidence_score, actual_diabetes_rate, 'Rank: ' || CAST(provider_rank AS TEXT) AS provider_rank_info FROM RankedProviders WHERE provider_rank <= 10 ORDER BY provider_rank NULLS FIRST

question: Find the names of the etiologies, the contributing factors, the current status, and the total number of cases for outbreaks reported by the CDC, grouped by the etiology name, outbreak status, and total cases.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT e.name AS etiology_name, GROUP_CONCAT(f.factor_description) AS contributing_factors, o.status, o.total_cases FROM outbreaks o INNER JOIN etiologies e ON o.etiology_id = e.etiology_id LEFT JOIN outbreak_factors of ON o.outbreak_id = of.outbreak_id LEFT JOIN factors f ON of.factor_id = f.factor_id INNER JOIN outbreak_reports orr ON o.outbreak_id = orr.outbreak_id INNER JOIN reporting_agencies ra ON orr.agency_id = ra.agency_id WHERE ra.agency_name = 'CDC' GROUP BY e.name, o.status, o.total_cases
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT e.name AS etiology_name, GROUP_CONCAT(f.factor_description SEPARATOR ',') AS contributing_factors, o.status, o.total_cases FROM outbreaks AS o INNER JOIN etiologies AS e ON o.etiology_id = e.etiology_id LEFT JOIN outbreak_factors AS `of` ON o.outbreak_id = `of`.outbreak_id LEFT JOIN factors AS f ON `of`.factor_id = f.factor_id INNER JOIN outbreak_reports AS orr ON o.outbreak_id = orr.outbreak_id INNER JOIN reporting_agencies AS ra ON orr.agency_id = ra.agency_id WHERE ra.agency_name = 'CDC' GROUP BY e.name, o.status, o.total_cases
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT e.name AS etiology_name, STRING_AGG(f.factor_description, ',') AS contributing_factors, o.status, o.total_cases FROM outbreaks AS o INNER JOIN etiologies AS e ON o.etiology_id = e.etiology_id LEFT JOIN outbreak_factors AS of ON o.outbreak_id = of.outbreak_id LEFT JOIN factors AS f ON of.factor_id = f.factor_id INNER JOIN outbreak_reports AS orr ON o.outbreak_id = orr.outbreak_id INNER JOIN reporting_agencies AS ra ON orr.agency_id = ra.agency_id WHERE ra.agency_name = 'CDC' GROUP BY e.name, o.status, o.total_cases

question: Who are the operators with the longest usage duration for instruments, and in which departments do they work? Additionally, limit the results to the top 2 departments.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH UsageRankCTE AS ( SELECT iu.usage_id, iu.instrument_id, iu.department_id, iu.operator_name, iu.usage_duration, d.department_name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( PARTITION BY iu.department_id ORDER BY CAST(SUBSTR(iu.usage_duration, 1, INSTR(iu.usage_duration, ' ') - 1) AS REAL) DESC ) AS usage_rank FROM instrument_usage iu INNER JOIN departments d ON iu.department_id = d.department_id ) SELECT ur.operator_name, ur.department_name FROM UsageRankCTE ur WHERE ur.usage_rank = 1 ORDER BY CAST(SUBSTR(ur.usage_duration, 1, INSTR(ur.usage_duration, ' ') - 1) AS REAL) DESC LIMIT 2
gold_sql.mysql: WITH UsageRankCTE AS (SELECT iu.usage_id, iu.instrument_id, iu.department_id, iu.operator_name, iu.usage_duration, d.department_name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY iu.department_id ORDER BY CAST(SUBSTRING(iu.usage_duration, 1, LOCATE(' ', iu.usage_duration) - 1) AS FLOAT) DESC) AS usage_rank FROM instrument_usage AS iu INNER JOIN departments AS d ON iu.department_id = d.department_id) SELECT ur.operator_name, ur.department_name FROM UsageRankCTE AS ur WHERE ur.usage_rank = 1 ORDER BY CAST(SUBSTRING(ur.usage_duration, 1, LOCATE(' ', ur.usage_duration) - 1) AS FLOAT) DESC LIMIT 2
gold_sql.postgres: WITH UsageRankCTE AS (SELECT iu.usage_id, iu.instrument_id, iu.department_id, iu.operator_name, iu.usage_duration, d.department_name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY iu.department_id ORDER BY CAST(SUBSTRING(iu.usage_duration FROM 1 FOR STRPOS(iu.usage_duration, ' ') - 1) AS REAL) DESC NULLS LAST) AS usage_rank FROM instrument_usage AS iu INNER JOIN departments AS d ON iu.department_id = d.department_id) SELECT ur.operator_name, ur.department_name FROM UsageRankCTE AS ur WHERE ur.usage_rank = 1 ORDER BY CAST(SUBSTRING(ur.usage_duration FROM 1 FOR STRPOS(ur.usage_duration, ' ') - 1) AS REAL) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 2

question: I would like to know the names of recruitment boards along with the total number of job applications, the number of shortlisted applications, the average number of vacancies, and the percentage of shortlisted applications for each board, listed in order from the board with the most applications to the board with the least.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ApplicationCounts AS ( SELECT rb.board_id, rb.board_name, COUNT(a.application_id) AS total_applications, SUM(CASE WHEN a.status = 'shortlisted' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS shortlisted_applications FROM recruitment_boards rb LEFT JOIN job_postings jp ON rb.board_id = jp.board_id LEFT JOIN applications a ON jp.job_id = a.job_id GROUP BY rb.board_id, rb.board_name ), VacancyStats AS ( SELECT board_id, AVG(number_of_vacancies) AS avg_vacancies FROM job_postings GROUP BY board_id ) SELECT ac.board_name, ac.total_applications, ac.shortlisted_applications, vs.avg_vacancies, (ac.shortlisted_applications * 100.0 / ac.total_applications) AS shortlisted_percentage FROM ApplicationCounts ac LEFT JOIN VacancyStats vs ON ac.board_id = vs.board_id ORDER BY ac.total_applications DESC
gold_sql.mysql: WITH ApplicationCounts AS (SELECT rb.board_id, rb.board_name, COUNT(a.application_id) AS total_applications, SUM(CASE WHEN a.status = 'shortlisted' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS shortlisted_applications FROM recruitment_boards AS rb LEFT JOIN job_postings AS jp ON rb.board_id = jp.board_id LEFT JOIN applications AS a ON jp.job_id = a.job_id GROUP BY rb.board_id, rb.board_name), VacancyStats AS (SELECT board_id, AVG(number_of_vacancies) AS avg_vacancies FROM job_postings GROUP BY board_id) SELECT ac.board_name, ac.total_applications, ac.shortlisted_applications, vs.avg_vacancies, (ac.shortlisted_applications * 100.0 / ac.total_applications) AS shortlisted_percentage FROM ApplicationCounts AS ac LEFT JOIN VacancyStats AS vs ON ac.board_id = vs.board_id ORDER BY ac.total_applications DESC
gold_sql.postgres: WITH ApplicationCounts AS (SELECT rb.board_id, rb.board_name, COUNT(a.application_id) AS total_applications, SUM(CASE WHEN a.status = 'shortlisted' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS shortlisted_applications FROM recruitment_boards AS rb LEFT JOIN job_postings AS jp ON rb.board_id = jp.board_id LEFT JOIN applications AS a ON jp.job_id = a.job_id GROUP BY rb.board_id, rb.board_name), VacancyStats AS (SELECT board_id, AVG(number_of_vacancies) AS avg_vacancies FROM job_postings GROUP BY board_id) SELECT ac.board_name, ac.total_applications, ac.shortlisted_applications, vs.avg_vacancies, (ac.shortlisted_applications * 100.0 / NULLIF(ac.total_applications, 0)) AS shortlisted_percentage FROM ApplicationCounts AS ac LEFT JOIN VacancyStats AS vs ON ac.board_id = vs.board_id ORDER BY ac.total_applications DESC NULLS LAST

question: What are the average closing prices for different types of financial instruments in 2022, ranked from highest to lowest?
external_knowledge: The year in question is 2022, which is the year of interest for calculating the average closing prices of the financial instruments; Financial instruments can be stocks, bonds, derivatives, etc.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT i.instrument_type, AVG(p.close_price) AS avg_closing_price_2022 FROM instruments i JOIN historical_prices p ON i.instrument_id = p.instrument_id WHERE strftime('%Y', p.date) = '2022' GROUP BY i.instrument_type ORDER BY avg_closing_price_2022 DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT i.instrument_type, AVG(p.close_price) AS avg_closing_price_2022 FROM instruments AS i JOIN historical_prices AS p ON i.instrument_id = p.instrument_id WHERE DATE_FORMAT(CAST(p.date AS DATETIME), '%Y') = '2022' GROUP BY i.instrument_type ORDER BY avg_closing_price_2022 DESC
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT i.instrument_type, AVG(p.close_price) AS avg_closing_price_2022 FROM instruments AS i JOIN historical_prices AS p ON i.instrument_id = p.instrument_id WHERE TO_CHAR(CAST(p.date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY') = '2022' GROUP BY i.instrument_type ORDER BY avg_closing_price_2022 DESC NULLS LAST

question: Could you please calculate the average success rates of test runs with zero anomalies and those with one or more anomalies on each test run date, ordered from earliest to latest, including the actual run dates in the results?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH TestRunDetails AS ( SELECT tr.run_id, tr.run_date, tr.success_rate, COUNT(an.anomaly_id) OVER (PARTITION BY tr.run_id) AS num_anomalies FROM test_runs tr LEFT JOIN anomalies an ON tr.run_id = an.run_id ) SELECT run_date, AVG(CASE WHEN num_anomalies = 0 THEN CAST(SUBSTR(success_rate, 1, INSTR(success_rate, '%') - 1) AS REAL) ELSE NULL END) AS avg_success_rate_no_anomalies, AVG(CASE WHEN num_anomalies > 0 THEN CAST(SUBSTR(success_rate, 1, INSTR(success_rate, '%') - 1) AS REAL) ELSE NULL END) AS avg_success_rate_with_anomalies FROM TestRunDetails GROUP BY run_date ORDER BY run_date
gold_sql.mysql: WITH TestRunDetails AS (SELECT tr.run_id, tr.run_date, tr.success_rate, COUNT(an.anomaly_id) OVER (PARTITION BY tr.run_id) AS num_anomalies FROM test_runs AS tr LEFT JOIN anomalies AS an ON tr.run_id = an.run_id) SELECT run_date, AVG(CASE WHEN num_anomalies = 0 THEN CAST(SUBSTRING(success_rate, 1, LOCATE('%', success_rate) - 1) AS FLOAT) ELSE NULL END) AS avg_success_rate_no_anomalies, AVG(CASE WHEN num_anomalies > 0 THEN CAST(SUBSTRING(success_rate, 1, LOCATE('%', success_rate) - 1) AS FLOAT) ELSE NULL END) AS avg_success_rate_with_anomalies FROM TestRunDetails GROUP BY run_date ORDER BY run_date
gold_sql.postgres: WITH TestRunDetails AS (SELECT tr.run_id, tr.run_date, tr.success_rate, COUNT(an.anomaly_id) OVER (PARTITION BY tr.run_id) AS num_anomalies FROM test_runs AS tr LEFT JOIN anomalies AS an ON tr.run_id = an.run_id) SELECT run_date, AVG(CASE WHEN num_anomalies = 0 THEN CAST(SUBSTRING(success_rate FROM 1 FOR STRPOS(success_rate, '%') - 1) AS REAL) ELSE NULL END) AS avg_success_rate_no_anomalies, AVG(CASE WHEN num_anomalies > 0 THEN CAST(SUBSTRING(success_rate FROM 1 FOR STRPOS(success_rate, '%') - 1) AS REAL) ELSE NULL END) AS avg_success_rate_with_anomalies FROM TestRunDetails GROUP BY run_date ORDER BY run_date NULLS FIRST

question: Prepare a detailed report on store performance, including names, franchise names, operational hours, sales data, feedback ratings, sales rankings, and feedback quartiles for all stores.
external_knowledge:
* The sales rank is based on the total sales amount, with the highest sales amount ranking first; 
* The feedback quartile divides stores into four groups based on the total number of feedback entries, with the group having the most feedback being the first quartile and the group having the least feedback being the fourth quartile.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH StoreOperations AS ( SELECT s.store_id, s.name AS store_name, fr.franchise_name, o.opening_hours, o.closing_hours, o.days_open FROM stores s LEFT JOIN store_franchises sf ON s.store_id = sf.store_id LEFT JOIN franchises fr ON sf.franchise_id = fr.franchise_id LEFT JOIN operations o ON s.store_id = o.store_id ), SalesSummary AS ( SELECT ss.store_id, SUM(ss.quantity_sold) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(ss.total_amount) AS total_sales_amount, COUNT(ss.sale_id) AS total_sales, AVG(ss.quantity_sold) AS avg_quantity_sold, AVG(ss.total_amount) AS avg_sales_amount FROM sales ss GROUP BY ss.store_id ), FeedbackSummary AS ( SELECT f.store_id, COUNT(f.feedback_id) AS total_feedback, AVG(f.rating) AS average_feedback_rating FROM feedback f GROUP BY f.store_id ), StoreAnalysis AS ( SELECT so.store_id, so.store_name, so.franchise_name, so.opening_hours, so.closing_hours, so.days_open, ss.total_quantity_sold, ss.total_sales_amount, ss.total_sales, ss.avg_quantity_sold, ss.avg_sales_amount, fb.total_feedback, fb.average_feedback_rating FROM StoreOperations so LEFT JOIN SalesSummary ss ON so.store_id = ss.store_id LEFT JOIN FeedbackSummary fb ON so.store_id = fb.store_id ), FinalSummary AS ( SELECT sa.store_name, sa.franchise_name, sa.opening_hours, sa.closing_hours, sa.days_open, sa.total_quantity_sold, sa.total_sales_amount, sa.total_sales, sa.avg_quantity_sold, sa.avg_sales_amount, sa.total_feedback, sa.average_feedback_rating, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY sa.total_sales_amount DESC) AS sales_rank, NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY sa.total_feedback) AS feedback_quartile FROM StoreAnalysis sa ) SELECT GROUP_CONCAT( store_name || ', ' || franchise_name || ', ' || opening_hours || ' - ' || closing_hours || ', ' || days_open || ', ' || total_quantity_sold || ', ' || total_sales_amount || ', ' || total_sales || ', ' || avg_quantity_sold || ', ' || avg_sales_amount || ', ' || total_feedback || ', ' || average_feedback_rating || ', ' || sales_rank || ', ' || feedback_quartile ) AS report FROM FinalSummary
gold_sql.mysql: WITH StoreOperations AS (SELECT s.store_id, s.name AS store_name, fr.franchise_name, o.opening_hours, o.closing_hours, o.days_open FROM stores AS s LEFT JOIN store_franchises AS sf ON s.store_id = sf.store_id LEFT JOIN franchises AS fr ON sf.franchise_id = fr.franchise_id LEFT JOIN operations AS o ON s.store_id = o.store_id), SalesSummary AS (SELECT ss.store_id, SUM(ss.quantity_sold) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(ss.total_amount) AS total_sales_amount, COUNT(ss.sale_id) AS total_sales, AVG(ss.quantity_sold) AS avg_quantity_sold, AVG(ss.total_amount) AS avg_sales_amount FROM sales AS ss GROUP BY ss.store_id), FeedbackSummary AS (SELECT f.store_id, COUNT(f.feedback_id) AS total_feedback, AVG(f.rating) AS average_feedback_rating FROM feedback AS f GROUP BY f.store_id), StoreAnalysis AS (SELECT so.store_id, so.store_name, so.franchise_name, so.opening_hours, so.closing_hours, so.days_open, ss.total_quantity_sold, ss.total_sales_amount, ss.total_sales, ss.avg_quantity_sold, ss.avg_sales_amount, fb.total_feedback, fb.average_feedback_rating FROM StoreOperations AS so LEFT JOIN SalesSummary AS ss ON so.store_id = ss.store_id LEFT JOIN FeedbackSummary AS fb ON so.store_id = fb.store_id), FinalSummary AS (SELECT sa.store_name, sa.franchise_name, sa.opening_hours, sa.closing_hours, sa.days_open, sa.total_quantity_sold, sa.total_sales_amount, sa.total_sales, sa.avg_quantity_sold, sa.avg_sales_amount, sa.total_feedback, sa.average_feedback_rating, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY sa.total_sales_amount DESC) AS sales_rank, NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY sa.total_feedback) AS feedback_quartile FROM StoreAnalysis AS sa) SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(store_name, ', ', franchise_name, ', ', opening_hours, ' - ', closing_hours, ', ', days_open, ', ', total_quantity_sold, ', ', total_sales_amount, ', ', total_sales, ', ', avg_quantity_sold, ', ', avg_sales_amount, ', ', total_feedback, ', ', average_feedback_rating, ', ', sales_rank, ', ', feedback_quartile) SEPARATOR ',') AS report FROM FinalSummary
gold_sql.postgres: WITH StoreOperations AS (SELECT s.store_id, s.name AS store_name, fr.franchise_name, o.opening_hours, o.closing_hours, o.days_open FROM stores AS s LEFT JOIN store_franchises AS sf ON s.store_id = sf.store_id LEFT JOIN franchises AS fr ON sf.franchise_id = fr.franchise_id LEFT JOIN operations AS o ON s.store_id = o.store_id), SalesSummary AS (SELECT ss.store_id, SUM(ss.quantity_sold) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(ss.total_amount) AS total_sales_amount, COUNT(ss.sale_id) AS total_sales, AVG(ss.quantity_sold) AS avg_quantity_sold, AVG(ss.total_amount) AS avg_sales_amount FROM sales AS ss GROUP BY ss.store_id), FeedbackSummary AS (SELECT f.store_id, COUNT(f.feedback_id) AS total_feedback, AVG(f.rating) AS average_feedback_rating FROM feedback AS f GROUP BY f.store_id), StoreAnalysis AS (SELECT so.store_id, so.store_name, so.franchise_name, so.opening_hours, so.closing_hours, so.days_open, ss.total_quantity_sold, ss.total_sales_amount, ss.total_sales, ss.avg_quantity_sold, ss.avg_sales_amount, fb.total_feedback, fb.average_feedback_rating FROM StoreOperations AS so LEFT JOIN SalesSummary AS ss ON so.store_id = ss.store_id LEFT JOIN FeedbackSummary AS fb ON so.store_id = fb.store_id), FinalSummary AS (SELECT sa.store_name, sa.franchise_name, sa.opening_hours, sa.closing_hours, sa.days_open, sa.total_quantity_sold, sa.total_sales_amount, sa.total_sales, sa.avg_quantity_sold, sa.avg_sales_amount, sa.total_feedback, sa.average_feedback_rating, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY sa.total_sales_amount DESC NULLS LAST) AS sales_rank, NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY sa.total_feedback NULLS FIRST) AS feedback_quartile FROM StoreAnalysis AS sa) SELECT STRING_AGG(store_name || ', ' || franchise_name || ', ' || opening_hours || ' - question: Hey there! Can you give me a list of jazz artists who were born before 1950, just their names and make sure you include those with known birth dates, please sort them by their birth year starting from the oldest?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT artist_name FROM artists WHERE LOWER(genre) = 'jazz' AND birth_date IS NOT NULL AND STRFTIME('%Y', birth_date) < '1950' ORDER BY STRFTIME('%Y', birth_date) ASC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT artist_name FROM artists WHERE LOWER(genre) = 'jazz' AND NOT birth_date IS NULL AND DATE_FORMAT(CAST(birth_date AS DATETIME), '%Y') < '1950' ORDER BY DATE_FORMAT(CAST(birth_date AS DATETIME), '%Y') ASC
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT artist_name FROM artists WHERE LOWER(genre) = 'jazz' AND NOT birth_date IS NULL AND TO_CHAR(CAST(birth_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY') < '1950' ORDER BY TO_CHAR(CAST(birth_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY') ASC NULLS FIRST

question: I want to know the product names, average ratings, review counts, positive review percentages, stock quantities, stock quartiles, brand names, and category names for all products, ranked within their respective stock quartiles based on their average ratings in descending order, providing an overall analysis of product performance across different stock levels.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ProductReviews AS ( SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, AVG(r.rating) AS average_rating, COUNT(r.review_id) AS review_count, COUNT(CASE WHEN r.rating >= 4 THEN r.review_id END) * 1.0 / COUNT(r.review_id) * 100 AS positive_review_percentage, p.brand_id, p.category_id FROM products p LEFT JOIN reviews r ON p.product_id = r.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name, p.brand_id, p.category_id ), StockLevels AS ( SELECT i.product_id, i.stock_quantity, NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY i.stock_quantity) AS stock_quartile FROM inventory i ), ProductAnalysis AS ( SELECT pr.product_id, pr.product_name, pr.average_rating, pr.review_count, pr.positive_review_percentage, sl.stock_quantity, sl.stock_quartile, b.brand_name, c.category_name FROM ProductReviews pr INNER JOIN StockLevels sl ON pr.product_id = sl.product_id INNER JOIN brands b ON pr.brand_id = b.brand_id INNER JOIN categories c ON pr.category_id = c.category_id ) SELECT pa.product_name, pa.average_rating, pa.review_count, pa.positive_review_percentage, pa.stock_quantity, pa.stock_quartile, pa.brand_name, pa.category_name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY pa.stock_quartile ORDER BY pa.average_rating DESC) as rank_within_quartile FROM ProductAnalysis pa ORDER BY pa.stock_quartile, rank_within_quartile

question: What are the usernames and details of their active groups and projects for all active users?
external_knowledge: Active users are those with the 'is_active' flag set to 1 in the users table; active groups and projects refer to group and project memberships where 'is_active' is set to 1.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT u.username, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT g.name) AS active_groups, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT p.name) AS active_projects FROM users u LEFT JOIN group_memberships gm ON u.usrkeypk = gm.usrkeypk AND gm.is_active = 1 LEFT JOIN groups g ON gm.grpkeypk = g.grpkeypk AND g.is_active = 1 LEFT JOIN project_memberships pm ON u.usrkeypk = pm.usrkeypk AND pm.is_active = 1 LEFT JOIN projects p ON pm.projectno = p.projectno AND p.is_active = 1 WHERE u.is_active = 1 GROUP BY u.usrkeypk, u.username ORDER BY u.username
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT u.username, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT g.name SEPARATOR ',') AS active_groups, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT p.name SEPARATOR ',') AS active_projects FROM users AS u LEFT JOIN group_memberships AS gm ON u.usrkeypk = gm.usrkeypk AND gm.is_active = 1 LEFT JOIN `groups` AS g ON gm.grpkeypk = g.grpkeypk AND g.is_active = 1 LEFT JOIN project_memberships AS pm ON u.usrkeypk = pm.usrkeypk AND pm.is_active = 1 LEFT JOIN projects AS p ON pm.projectno = p.projectno AND p.is_active = 1 WHERE u.is_active = 1 GROUP BY u.usrkeypk, u.username ORDER BY u.username
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT u.username, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT g.name, ',') AS active_groups, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT p.name, ',') AS active_projects FROM users AS u LEFT JOIN group_memberships AS gm ON u.usrkeypk = gm.usrkeypk AND gm.is_active = 1 LEFT JOIN groups AS g ON gm.grpkeypk = g.grpkeypk AND g.is_active = 1 LEFT JOIN project_memberships AS pm ON u.usrkeypk = pm.usrkeypk AND pm.is_active = 1 LEFT JOIN projects AS p ON pm.projectno = p.projectno AND p.is_active = 1 WHERE u.is_active = 1 GROUP BY u.usrkeypk, u.username ORDER BY u.username NULLS FIRST

question: What are the names, categories, latest versions, and attribute details of all document types, including attribute names, values, and the number of definitions for each attribute?
external_knowledge:
- Document types are categories that define the structure and content of documents; A document can have attributes such as name, description, and category.
- Attributes can have multiple definitions, indicating the attribute's possible values or meanings; The attribute definition count represents the total number of definitions for each attribute.
- The latest version of a document type refers to the most recent version number, which is essential for version control and tracking changes.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH LatestDocumentVersions AS ( SELECT dv.doc_type_id, MAX(dv.version_nbr) as max_version FROM document_versions dv GROUP BY dv.doc_type_id ), DocumentTypeWithLatestVersion AS ( SELECT dt.doc_type_id, dt.doc_type_name, dt.description, dt.category, ldv.max_version, dt.created_by, dt.created_date, dt.modified_by, dt.modified_date FROM document_types dt INNER JOIN LatestDocumentVersions ldv ON dt.doc_type_id = ldv.doc_type_id ), AttributeDefinitionCounts AS ( SELECT a.attr_id, COUNT(ad.attr_defn_id) as attr_def_count FROM attributes a LEFT JOIN attribute_definitions ad ON a.attr_id = ad.attr_id GROUP BY a.attr_id ), AttributesWithCounts AS ( SELECT at.doc_type_id, at.attr_name, at.attr_value, at.version_nbr, at.sort_cd, at.active_ind, at.data_type, at.required_ind, adc.attr_def_count FROM attributes at LEFT JOIN AttributeDefinitionCounts adc ON at.attr_id = adc.attr_id ), AttributesAggregated AS ( SELECT awc.doc_type_id, GROUP_CONCAT( awc.attr_name || ': ' || awc.attr_value || ' (Def Count: ' || awc.attr_def_count || ')', ', ' ) as attributes_info FROM AttributesWithCounts awc GROUP BY awc.doc_type_id ) SELECT dtwlv.doc_type_name || ' (' || dtwlv.category || ') - Latest Version: ' || dtwlv.max_version || ', Attributes: ' || aa.attributes_info as complex_info FROM DocumentTypeWithLatestVersion dtwlv LEFT JOIN AttributesAggregated aa ON dtwlv.doc_type_id = aa.doc_type_id ORDER BY dtwlv.doc_type_name
gold_sql.mysql: WITH LatestDocumentVersions AS (SELECT dv.doc_type_id, MAX(dv.version_nbr) AS max_version FROM document_versions AS dv GROUP BY dv.doc_type_id), DocumentTypeWithLatestVersion AS (SELECT dt.doc_type_id, dt.doc_type_name, dt.description, dt.category, ldv.max_version, dt.created_by, dt.created_date, dt.modified_by, dt.modified_date FROM document_types AS dt INNER JOIN LatestDocumentVersions AS ldv ON dt.doc_type_id = ldv.doc_type_id), AttributeDefinitionCounts AS (SELECT a.attr_id, COUNT(ad.attr_defn_id) AS attr_def_count FROM attributes AS a LEFT JOIN attribute_definitions AS ad ON a.attr_id = ad.attr_id GROUP BY a.attr_id), AttributesWithCounts AS (SELECT at.doc_type_id, at.attr_name, at.attr_value, at.version_nbr, at.sort_cd, at.active_ind, at.data_type, at.required_ind, adc.attr_def_count FROM attributes AS at LEFT JOIN AttributeDefinitionCounts AS adc ON at.attr_id = adc.attr_id), AttributesAggregated AS (SELECT awc.doc_type_id, GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(awc.attr_name, ': ', awc.attr_value, ' (Def Count: ', awc.attr_def_count, ')') SEPARATOR ', ') AS attributes_info FROM AttributesWithCounts AS awc GROUP BY awc.doc_type_id) SELECT CONCAT(dtwlv.doc_type_name, ' (', dtwlv.category, ') - Latest Version: ', dtwlv.max_version, ', Attributes: ', aa.attributes_info) AS complex_info FROM DocumentTypeWithLatestVersion AS dtwlv LEFT JOIN AttributesAggregated AS aa ON dtwlv.doc_type_id = aa.doc_type_id ORDER BY dtwlv.doc_type_name
gold_sql.postgres: WITH LatestDocumentVersions AS (SELECT dv.doc_type_id, MAX(dv.version_nbr) AS max_version FROM document_versions AS dv GROUP BY dv.doc_type_id), DocumentTypeWithLatestVersion AS (SELECT dt.doc_type_id, dt.doc_type_name, dt.description, dt.category, ldv.max_version, dt.created_by, dt.created_date, dt.modified_by, dt.modified_date FROM document_types AS dt INNER JOIN LatestDocumentVersions AS ldv ON dt.doc_type_id = ldv.doc_type_id), AttributeDefinitionCounts AS (SELECT a.attr_id, COUNT(ad.attr_defn_id) AS attr_def_count FROM attributes AS a LEFT JOIN attribute_definitions AS ad ON a.attr_id = ad.attr_id GROUP BY a.attr_id), AttributesWithCounts AS (SELECT at.doc_type_id, at.attr_name, at.attr_value, at.version_nbr, at.sort_cd, at.active_ind, at.data_type, at.required_ind, adc.attr_def_count FROM attributes AS at LEFT JOIN AttributeDefinitionCounts AS adc ON at.attr_id = adc.attr_id), AttributesAggregated AS (SELECT awc.doc_type_id, STRING_AGG(awc.attr_name || ': ' || awc.attr_value || ' (Def Count: ' || awc.attr_def_count || ')', ', ') AS attributes_info FROM AttributesWithCounts AS awc GROUP BY awc.doc_type_id) SELECT dtwlv.doc_type_name || ' (' || dtwlv.category || ') - Latest Version: ' || dtwlv.max_version || ', Attributes: ' || aa.attributes_info AS complex_info FROM DocumentTypeWithLatestVersion AS dtwlv LEFT JOIN AttributesAggregated AS aa ON dtwlv.doc_type_id = aa.doc_type_id ORDER BY dtwlv.doc_type_name NULLS FIRST

question:
**User**: I want to get some detailed information about users and their activities related to images.
**Assistant**: What kind of information about users are you interested in?
**User**: I'd like to know their usernames, emails, and total accesses.
**Assistant**: And what about their activities? Are you looking for information about images they've annotated?
**User**: Yes, I'd like to know the total annotations they've made, their average confidence level in those annotations, and the dates of their first and last annotations.
**Assistant**: Do you also want to include any file details, such as file sizes and upload dates?
**User**: Yes, please include the maximum file size and the earliest upload date for each image.
**Assistant**: And how would you like this information to be presented?
**User**: I'd like it grouped by user ID, username, email, annotation count, average confidence, maximum file size, and total accesses.
**Assistant**: Lastly, would you like to order the results in any particular way?
**User**: Yes, please order it by user ID.
**Assistant**: Alright, I'll help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH UserDetails AS ( SELECT u.user_id, u.username, u.email, COUNT(a.access_id) AS total_accesses FROM users u LEFT JOIN access_logs a ON u.user_id = a.user_id GROUP BY u.user_id, u.username, u.email ), ImageDetails AS ( SELECT i.image_id, i.path, i.class_id, c.class_name, COUNT(ia.annotation_id) AS annotation_count, AVG(ia.confidence_level) AS avg_confidence, MIN(ia.annotation_date) AS first_annotation_date, MAX(ia.annotation_date) AS last_annotation_date FROM images i LEFT JOIN image_annotations ia ON i.image_id = ia.image_id LEFT JOIN classes c ON i.class_id = c.class_id GROUP BY i.image_id, i.path, i.class_id, c.class_name ), UserImageAnnotations AS ( SELECT ud.user_id, ud.username, ud.email, ud.total_accesses, ia.image_id, ia.annotation_id, ia.confidence_level FROM UserDetails ud LEFT JOIN image_annotations ia ON ud.user_id = ia.user_id ), FileDetails AS ( SELECT image_id, MAX(file_size) AS max_file_size, MIN(upload_date) AS first_upload_date FROM image_files GROUP BY image_id ), FinalQuery AS ( SELECT uia.user_id, uia.username, uia.email, id.annotation_count, id.avg_confidence, id.first_annotation_date, id.last_annotation_date, uia.total_accesses, fd.max_file_size, fd.first_upload_date FROM UserImageAnnotations uia LEFT JOIN ImageDetails id ON uia.image_id = id.image_id LEFT JOIN FileDetails fd ON uia.image_id = fd.image_id ) SELECT user_id, username, email, SUM(annotation_count) AS 'Total Annotations', AVG(avg_confidence) AS 'Average Annotation Confidence', MAX(max_file_size) AS 'Max File Size (MB)', MAX(total_accesses) AS 'Total Accesses' FROM FinalQuery GROUP BY user_id, username, email ORDER BY user_id
gold_sql.mysql: WITH UserDetails AS (SELECT u.user_id, u.username, u.email, COUNT(a.access_id) AS total_accesses FROM users AS u LEFT JOIN access_logs AS a ON u.user_id = a.user_id GROUP BY u.user_id, u.username, u.email), ImageDetails AS (SELECT i.image_id, i.path, i.class_id, c.class_name, COUNT(ia.annotation_id) AS annotation_count, AVG(ia.confidence_level) AS avg_confidence, MIN(ia.annotation_date) AS first_annotation_date, MAX(ia.annotation_date) AS last_annotation_date FROM images AS i LEFT JOIN image_annotations AS ia ON i.image_id = ia.image_id LEFT JOIN classes AS c ON i.class_id = c.class_id GROUP BY i.image_id, i.path, i.class_id, c.class_name), UserImageAnnotations AS (SELECT ud.user_id, ud.username, ud.email, ud.total_accesses, ia.image_id, ia.annotation_id, ia.confidence_level FROM UserDetails AS ud LEFT JOIN image_annotations AS ia ON ud.user_id = ia.user_id), FileDetails AS (SELECT image_id, MAX(file_size) AS max_file_size, MIN(upload_date) AS first_upload_date FROM image_files GROUP BY image_id), FinalQuery AS (SELECT uia.user_id, uia.username, uia.email, id.annotation_count, id.avg_confidence, id.first_annotation_date, id.last_annotation_date, uia.total_accesses, fd.max_file_size, fd.first_upload_date FROM UserImageAnnotations AS uia LEFT JOIN ImageDetails AS id ON uia.image_id = id.image_id LEFT JOIN FileDetails AS fd ON uia.image_id = fd.image_id) SELECT user_id, username, email, SUM(annotation_count) AS `Total Annotations`, AVG(avg_confidence) AS `Average Annotation Confidence`, MAX(max_file_size) AS `Max File Size (MB)`, MAX(total_accesses) AS `Total Accesses` FROM FinalQuery GROUP BY user_id, username, email ORDER BY user_id

question: Return the movie ID, genres, and languages for movies in the watchlist of the user with the highest number of watchlist entries.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH most_productive_user AS ( SELECT user_id FROM watchlists GROUP BY user_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1 ), most_productive_watchlist AS ( SELECT movie_id FROM watchlists WHERE user_id = (SELECT user_id FROM most_productive_user) ), movie_details AS ( SELECT movies.id AS movie_id, genres.name AS genre, languages.name AS language FROM most_productive_watchlist INNER JOIN movie_genres ON most_productive_watchlist.movie_id = movie_genres.movie_id INNER JOIN genres ON movie_genres.genre_id = genres.id INNER JOIN movie_languages ON most_productive_watchlist.movie_id = movie_languages.movie_id INNER JOIN languages ON movie_languages.language_id = languages.id INNER JOIN movies ON most_productive_watchlist.movie_id = movies.id ) SELECT movie_id, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT genre) AS genres, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT language) AS languages FROM movie_details GROUP BY movie_id
gold_sql.mysql: WITH most_productive_user AS (SELECT user_id FROM watchlists GROUP BY user_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1), most_productive_watchlist AS (SELECT movie_id FROM watchlists WHERE user_id = (SELECT user_id FROM most_productive_user)), movie_details AS (SELECT movies.id AS movie_id, genres.name AS genre, languages.name AS language FROM most_productive_watchlist INNER JOIN movie_genres ON most_productive_watchlist.movie_id = movie_genres.movie_id INNER JOIN genres ON movie_genres.genre_id = genres.id INNER JOIN movie_languages ON most_productive_watchlist.movie_id = movie_languages.movie_id INNER JOIN languages ON movie_languages.language_id = languages.id INNER JOIN movies ON most_productive_watchlist.movie_id = movies.id) SELECT movie_id, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT genre SEPARATOR ',') AS genres, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT language SEPARATOR ',') AS languages FROM movie_details GROUP BY movie_id
gold_sql.postgres: WITH most_productive_user AS (SELECT user_id FROM watchlists GROUP BY user_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1), most_productive_watchlist AS (SELECT movie_id FROM watchlists WHERE user_id = (SELECT user_id FROM most_productive_user)), movie_details AS (SELECT movies.id AS movie_id, genres.name AS genre, languages.name AS language FROM most_productive_watchlist INNER JOIN movie_genres ON most_productive_watchlist.movie_id = movie_genres.movie_id INNER JOIN genres ON movie_genres.genre_id = genres.id INNER JOIN movie_languages ON most_productive_watchlist.movie_id = movie_languages.movie_id INNER JOIN languages ON movie_languages.language_id = languages.id INNER JOIN movies ON most_productive_watchlist.movie_id = movies.id) SELECT movie_id, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT genre, ',') AS genres, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT language, ',') AS languages FROM movie_details GROUP BY movie_id

question: Hey, I'm looking for the average height in centimeters for each clothing type, but only for active clothing types that have at least one measurement. Could you show me the clothing type along with its average height?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT ct.clothing_type_name, AVG(CAST(SUBSTR(m.height_cmft, 1, INSTR(m.height_cmft, ' ') - 1) AS REAL)) AS avg_height_cm FROM measurements m INNER JOIN clothing_types ct ON m.clothing_type_id = ct.clothing_type_id WHERE ct.is_active = 1 GROUP BY ct.clothing_type_name HAVING COUNT(m.measurement_id) > 0
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT ct.clothing_type_name, AVG(CAST(SUBSTRING(m.height_cmft, 1, LOCATE(' ', m.height_cmft) - 1) AS FLOAT)) AS avg_height_cm FROM measurements AS m INNER JOIN clothing_types AS ct ON m.clothing_type_id = ct.clothing_type_id WHERE ct.is_active = 1 GROUP BY ct.clothing_type_name HAVING COUNT(m.measurement_id) > 0
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT ct.clothing_type_name, AVG(CAST(SUBSTRING(m.height_cmft FROM 1 FOR STRPOS(m.height_cmft, ' ') - 1) AS REAL)) AS avg_height_cm FROM measurements AS m INNER JOIN clothing_types AS ct ON m.clothing_type_id = ct.clothing_type_id WHERE ct.is_active = 1 GROUP BY ct.clothing_type_name HAVING COUNT(m.measurement_id) > 0

question: What are the urbanization levels, corresponding average population growth rates, and the names of cities within each level for all groups of highly populated cities (more than 1 million residents) with a growth rate above 0, where the average growth rate is higher than 0.5, ordered from highest to lowest average growth rate?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT c.urbanization_level, AVG(c.population_growth_rate) AS avg_growth_rate, GROUP_CONCAT(c.city_name) AS cities FROM cities c WHERE c.population > 1000000 AND c.population_growth_rate > 0 GROUP BY c.urbanization_level HAVING AVG(c.population_growth_rate) > 0.5 ORDER BY avg_growth_rate DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT c.urbanization_level, AVG(c.population_growth_rate) AS avg_growth_rate, GROUP_CONCAT(c.city_name SEPARATOR ',') AS cities FROM cities AS c WHERE c.population > 1000000 AND c.population_growth_rate > 0 GROUP BY c.urbanization_level HAVING AVG(c.population_growth_rate) > 0.5 ORDER BY avg_growth_rate DESC
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT c.urbanization_level, AVG(c.population_growth_rate) AS avg_growth_rate, STRING_AGG(c.city_name, ',') AS cities FROM cities AS c WHERE c.population > 1000000 AND c.population_growth_rate > 0 GROUP BY c.urbanization_level HAVING AVG(c.population_growth_rate) > 0.5 ORDER BY avg_growth_rate DESC NULLS LAST

question: I want to know the unique identifiers for each outbreak, ordered from lowest to highest, including their detailed information such as etiology, cases, locations, contributing factors, interventions, and report statuses.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH OutbreakDetails AS ( SELECT o.outbreak_id, o.etiology_id, o.total_cases, o.outbreak_year, o.location_id, o.start_date, o.end_date, o.status, e.name AS etiology_name, e.description AS etiology_description, e.common_sources, e.transmission_methods, l.location_name, l.city, l.state, l.country FROM outbreaks o JOIN etiologies e ON o.etiology_id = e.etiology_id JOIN locations l ON o.location_id = l.location_id ), OutbreakFactors AS ( SELECT of.outbreak_id, GROUP_CONCAT(f.factor_description, ', ') AS contributing_factors FROM outbreak_factors of JOIN factors f ON of.factor_id = f.factor_id GROUP BY of.outbreak_id ), CaseCounts AS ( SELECT c.outbreak_id, COUNT(c.case_id) AS case_count, SUM(c.hospitalized) AS hospitalized_count FROM cases c GROUP BY c.outbreak_id ), InterventionDetails AS ( SELECT i.outbreak_id, GROUP_CONCAT(i.intervention_type, ', ') AS interventions, GROUP_CONCAT(i.effectiveness, ', ') AS intervention_effectiveness FROM interventions i GROUP BY i.outbreak_id ), ReportStatus AS ( SELECT r.outbreak_id, GROUP_CONCAT(r.report_status, ', ') AS report_statuses FROM outbreak_reports r GROUP BY r.outbreak_id ) SELECT od.outbreak_id AS "Outbreak ID", od.etiology_name, od.etiology_description, od.common_sources, od.transmission_methods, od.total_cases, od.outbreak_year, od.location_name, od.city, od.state, od.country, od.start_date, od.end_date, od.status, of.contributing_factors, cc.case_count, cc.hospitalized_count, id.interventions, id.intervention_effectiveness, rs.report_statuses FROM OutbreakDetails od LEFT JOIN OutbreakFactors of ON od.outbreak_id = of.outbreak_id LEFT JOIN CaseCounts cc ON od.outbreak_id = cc.outbreak_id LEFT JOIN InterventionDetails id ON od.outbreak_id = id.outbreak_id LEFT JOIN ReportStatus rs ON od.outbreak_id = rs.outbreak_id ORDER BY od.outbreak_id
