question: For experiments that ended in 2023, return the experiment names and the average volume of samples used, excluding experiments that did not use any samples.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT e.experiment_name, AVG(es.volume_used) AS average_sample_volume FROM experiments e JOIN experiment_samples es ON e.experiment_id = es.experiment_id WHERE strftime('%Y', e.end_date) = '2023' GROUP BY e.experiment_name HAVING COUNT(es.experiment_sample_id) > 0
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT e.experiment_name, AVG(es.volume_used) AS average_sample_volume FROM experiments AS e JOIN experiment_samples AS es ON e.experiment_id = es.experiment_id WHERE DATE_FORMAT(CAST(e.end_date AS DATETIME), '%Y') = '2023' GROUP BY e.experiment_name HAVING COUNT(es.experiment_sample_id) > 0
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT e.experiment_name, AVG(es.volume_used) AS average_sample_volume FROM experiments AS e JOIN experiment_samples AS es ON e.experiment_id = es.experiment_id WHERE TO_CHAR(CAST(e.end_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY') = '2023' GROUP BY e.experiment_name HAVING COUNT(es.experiment_sample_id) > 0

question: Find the three most recent comments, along with their authors' usernames and roles, for each incident; also include the names and ranks of officers involved in these incidents, their roles, and the names of any associated files, listing 'No File' if none exist, and rank these results by incident, comment recency, and officer involvement.
external_knowledge: None required for this query.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RecentComments AS ( SELECT ic.incident_id, ic.user_id, ic.comment_date_time, ic.comment_text, u.username, u.user_role, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ic.incident_id ORDER BY ic.comment_date_time DESC) AS comment_rank FROM incident_comments ic INNER JOIN users u ON ic.user_id = u.user_id ), TopComments AS ( SELECT rc.incident_id, rc.user_id, rc.comment_date_time, rc.comment_text, rc.username, rc.user_role, rc.comment_rank FROM RecentComments rc WHERE rc.comment_rank <= 3 ), OfficerInvolvements AS ( SELECT ii.incident_id, ii.officer_id, ii.incident_involvement_role, o.officer_name, o.officer_rank FROM incident_involvement ii INNER JOIN officers o ON ii.officer_id = o.officer_id ), IncidentFiles AS ( SELECT if.incident_id, if.file_name FROM incident_files if ) SELECT tc.incident_id, tc.username, tc.user_role, tc.comment_date_time, tc.comment_text, tc.comment_rank, oi.officer_name, oi.officer_rank, oi.incident_involvement_role, IFNULL(iff.file_name, 'No File') AS file_name FROM TopComments tc LEFT JOIN OfficerInvolvements oi ON tc.incident_id = oi.incident_id LEFT JOIN IncidentFiles iff ON tc.incident_id = iff.incident_id ORDER BY tc.incident_id, tc.comment_date_time, oi.incident_involvement_role
gold_sql.mysql: WITH RecentComments AS (SELECT ic.incident_id, ic.user_id, ic.comment_date_time, ic.comment_text, u.username, u.user_role, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ic.incident_id ORDER BY ic.comment_date_time DESC) AS comment_rank FROM incident_comments AS ic INNER JOIN users AS u ON ic.user_id = u.user_id), TopComments AS (SELECT rc.incident_id, rc.user_id, rc.comment_date_time, rc.comment_text, rc.username, rc.user_role, rc.comment_rank FROM RecentComments AS rc WHERE rc.comment_rank <= 3), OfficerInvolvements AS (SELECT ii.incident_id, ii.officer_id, ii.incident_involvement_role, o.officer_name, o.officer_rank FROM incident_involvement AS ii INNER JOIN officers AS o ON ii.officer_id = o.officer_id), IncidentFiles AS (SELECT `if`.incident_id, `if`.file_name FROM incident_files AS `if`) SELECT tc.incident_id, tc.username, tc.user_role, tc.comment_date_time, tc.comment_text, tc.comment_rank, oi.officer_name, oi.officer_rank, oi.incident_involvement_role, COALESCE(iff.file_name, 'No File') AS file_name FROM TopComments AS tc LEFT JOIN OfficerInvolvements AS oi ON tc.incident_id = oi.incident_id LEFT JOIN IncidentFiles AS iff ON tc.incident_id = iff.incident_id ORDER BY tc.incident_id, tc.comment_date_time, oi.incident_involvement_role
gold_sql.postgres: WITH RecentComments AS (SELECT ic.incident_id, ic.user_id, ic.comment_date_time, ic.comment_text, u.username, u.user_role, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ic.incident_id ORDER BY ic.comment_date_time DESC NULLS LAST) AS comment_rank FROM incident_comments AS ic INNER JOIN users AS u ON ic.user_id = u.user_id), TopComments AS (SELECT rc.incident_id, rc.user_id, rc.comment_date_time, rc.comment_text, rc.username, rc.user_role, rc.comment_rank FROM RecentComments AS rc WHERE rc.comment_rank <= 3), OfficerInvolvements AS (SELECT ii.incident_id, ii.officer_id, ii.incident_involvement_role, o.officer_name, o.officer_rank FROM incident_involvement AS ii INNER JOIN officers AS o ON ii.officer_id = o.officer_id), IncidentFiles AS (SELECT if.incident_id, if.file_name FROM incident_files AS if) SELECT tc.incident_id, tc.username, tc.user_role, tc.comment_date_time, tc.comment_text, tc.comment_rank, oi.officer_name, oi.officer_rank, oi.incident_involvement_role, COALESCE(iff.file_name, 'No File') AS file_name FROM TopComments AS tc LEFT JOIN OfficerInvolvements AS oi ON tc.incident_id = oi.incident_id LEFT JOIN IncidentFiles AS iff ON tc.incident_id = iff.incident_id ORDER BY tc.incident_id NULLS FIRST, tc.comment_date_time NULLS FIRST, oi.incident_involvement_role NULLS FIRST

question: Hey! Could you help me get a list of users along with the total size of files they've accessed, the number of unique files they've accessed, and how many times they successfully accessed files? I only need users who have accessed at least one file, and I'd like the list sorted by the total file size, with the biggest files first.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT u.user_name, SUM(CAST(f.file_size AS INTEGER)) AS total_file_size, COUNT(DISTINCT fal.file_id) AS unique_file_count, SUM(CASE WHEN fal.is_successful = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS successful_access_count FROM users u JOIN file_access_logs fal ON u.user_id = fal.user_id JOIN files f ON fal.file_id = f.file_id GROUP BY u.user_id, u.user_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT fal.file_id) > 0 ORDER BY total_file_size DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT u.user_name, SUM(CAST(f.file_size AS SIGNED)) AS total_file_size, COUNT(DISTINCT fal.file_id) AS unique_file_count, SUM(CASE WHEN fal.is_successful = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS successful_access_count FROM users AS u JOIN file_access_logs AS fal ON u.user_id = fal.user_id JOIN files AS f ON fal.file_id = f.file_id GROUP BY u.user_id, u.user_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT fal.file_id) > 0 ORDER BY total_file_size DESC
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT u.user_name, SUM(CAST(f.file_size AS INT)) AS total_file_size, COUNT(DISTINCT fal.file_id) AS unique_file_count, SUM(CASE WHEN fal.is_successful = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS successful_access_count FROM users AS u JOIN file_access_logs AS fal ON u.user_id = fal.user_id JOIN files AS f ON fal.file_id = f.file_id GROUP BY u.user_id, u.user_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT fal.file_id) > 0 ORDER BY total_file_size DESC NULLS LAST

question: I would like to know, for each year, the number of movies that were released, based on the movies' release dates, and sorted from the year with the highest number of movies to the lowest. Could you also exclude any years where the release date information is missing or null?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT CAST(SUBSTR(release_date, 1, 4) AS INTEGER) AS release_year, COUNT(*) AS movie_count FROM movies WHERE release_date IS NOT NULL GROUP BY release_year ORDER BY movie_count DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT CAST(SUBSTRING(release_date, 1, 4) AS SIGNED) AS release_year, COUNT(*) AS movie_count FROM movies WHERE NOT release_date IS NULL GROUP BY release_year ORDER BY movie_count DESC
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT CAST(SUBSTRING(release_date FROM 1 FOR 4) AS INT) AS release_year, COUNT(*) AS movie_count FROM movies WHERE NOT release_date IS NULL GROUP BY release_year ORDER BY movie_count DESC NULLS LAST

question: Find the 'Vision Zero' program's progress report, comprising the total number of tasks, completed tasks, and the names of all team members involved; only include programs with active tasks.
external_knowledge: Vision Zero refers to a traffic safety initiative that aims to eliminate traffic fatalities and severe injuries. A program's progress report is a summary of its current status, including completed and pending tasks, and team members contributing to it; Active tasks imply tasks that have been assigned and are either ongoing or completed.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT p.program_name, COUNT(a.action_item_id) AS total_action_items, SUM(CASE WHEN s.status_name = 'completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS completed_action_items, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT tm.team_member_name) AS associated_team_members FROM traffic_safety_programs p JOIN action_item_objectives aio ON p.program_id = aio.objective_id JOIN action_items a ON aio.action_item_id = a.action_item_id JOIN statuses s ON a.status = s.status_id LEFT JOIN action_item_assignments ai ON a.action_item_id = ai.action_item_id LEFT JOIN team_members tm ON ai.team_member_id = tm.team_member_id WHERE p.program_name = 'Vision Zero' GROUP BY p.program_name HAVING COUNT(a.action_item_id) > 0
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT p.program_name, COUNT(a.action_item_id) AS total_action_items, SUM(CASE WHEN s.status_name = 'completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS completed_action_items, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT tm.team_member_name SEPARATOR ',') AS associated_team_members FROM traffic_safety_programs AS p JOIN action_item_objectives AS aio ON p.program_id = aio.objective_id JOIN action_items AS a ON aio.action_item_id = a.action_item_id JOIN statuses AS s ON a.status = s.status_id LEFT JOIN action_item_assignments AS ai ON a.action_item_id = ai.action_item_id LEFT JOIN team_members AS tm ON ai.team_member_id = tm.team_member_id WHERE p.program_name = 'Vision Zero' GROUP BY p.program_name HAVING COUNT(a.action_item_id) > 0
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT p.program_name, COUNT(a.action_item_id) AS total_action_items, SUM(CASE WHEN s.status_name = 'completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS completed_action_items, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT tm.team_member_name, ',') AS associated_team_members FROM traffic_safety_programs AS p JOIN action_item_objectives AS aio ON p.program_id = aio.objective_id JOIN action_items AS a ON aio.action_item_id = a.action_item_id JOIN statuses AS s ON a.status = s.status_id LEFT JOIN action_item_assignments AS ai ON a.action_item_id = ai.action_item_id LEFT JOIN team_members AS tm ON ai.team_member_id = tm.team_member_id WHERE p.program_name = 'Vision Zero' GROUP BY p.program_name HAVING COUNT(a.action_item_id) > 0

question: Who are the customers with the top average call duration in 2023?
external_knowledge:
- 'top average call duration' refers to the highest average call duration in the specified year;
- '2023' is the year for which the call data is being analyzed.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH CustomerAvgCallDuration AS ( SELECT c.customer_id, AVG(cd.call_duration) AS avg_call_duration FROM customers c JOIN call_details cd ON c.customer_id = cd.customer_id WHERE strftime('%Y', cd.call_date) = '2023' GROUP BY c.customer_id ), RankedCustomerAvgCallDuration AS ( SELECT customer_id, avg_call_duration, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY avg_call_duration DESC) as customer_rank FROM CustomerAvgCallDuration ) SELECT customer_id FROM RankedCustomerAvgCallDuration WHERE customer_rank = 1
gold_sql.mysql: WITH CustomerAvgCallDuration AS (SELECT c.customer_id, AVG(cd.call_duration) AS avg_call_duration FROM customers AS c JOIN call_details AS cd ON c.customer_id = cd.customer_id WHERE DATE_FORMAT(CAST(cd.call_date AS DATETIME), '%Y') = '2023' GROUP BY c.customer_id), RankedCustomerAvgCallDuration AS (SELECT customer_id, avg_call_duration, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY avg_call_duration DESC) AS customer_rank FROM CustomerAvgCallDuration) SELECT customer_id FROM RankedCustomerAvgCallDuration WHERE customer_rank = 1
gold_sql.postgres: WITH CustomerAvgCallDuration AS (SELECT c.customer_id, AVG(cd.call_duration) AS avg_call_duration FROM customers AS c JOIN call_details AS cd ON c.customer_id = cd.customer_id WHERE TO_CHAR(CAST(cd.call_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY') = '2023' GROUP BY c.customer_id), RankedCustomerAvgCallDuration AS (SELECT customer_id, avg_call_duration, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY avg_call_duration DESC NULLS LAST) AS customer_rank FROM CustomerAvgCallDuration) SELECT customer_id FROM RankedCustomerAvgCallDuration WHERE customer_rank = 1

question: What is the concatenated list of business types that are associated with the 'Individual' ownership type, metaphorically speaking, like finding the names of the trees that grow from a single seed?
external_knowledge:
- 'Individual' ownership type refers to a type of business ownership where the business is owned by a single person;
- The `business_type_id` of 0 is a specific identifier that might represent a default or placeholder value in the database.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(bt.business_type_name, ', ') AS combined_business_types FROM business_types bt WHERE bt.business_type_id = 0
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(bt.business_type_name SEPARATOR ', ') AS combined_business_types FROM business_types AS bt WHERE bt.business_type_id = 0
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT STRING_AGG(bt.business_type_name, ', ') AS combined_business_types FROM business_types AS bt WHERE bt.business_type_id = 0

question:
**User**: I want to find out some information about our datasets.
**Assistant**: That sounds great. Can you tell me what kind of datasets you're looking for?
**User**: I want to see active datasets.
**Assistant**: Active datasets, okay. What specific details would you like to know about these active datasets?
**User**: I would like to know the dataset ID, name, upload date, who uploaded it, file size, data source, status, data type, and also what version is the latest, including version details and any quality metrics.
**Assistant**: That's a comprehensive list. You want the latest version details and quality metrics for each active dataset. Would you like this information formatted in a specific way?
**User**: Yes, please format it so it's easy to read, like a string that includes all the dataset details, version information, and quality metrics.
**Assistant**: Will you need any additional filtering or sorting for this dataset information?
**User**: No, just the latest version details for each active dataset and their quality metrics as described.
**Assistant**: Alright, I will help you translate your request into an SQL query to retrieve this information.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH LatestVersion AS ( SELECT dv.dataset_id, dv.version_number, dv.update_date, dv.version_description, dv.version_status, dv.updated_by, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dv.dataset_id ORDER BY dv.version_number DESC) AS version_rank FROM dataset_versions dv ), ActiveDatasets AS ( SELECT d.dataset_id, d.name AS dataset_name, d.upload_date, d.uploaded_by, d.file_size, d.data_source, d.status, dt.data_type_name, u.username AS uploaded_by_username FROM datasets d JOIN users u ON d.uploaded_by = u.user_id JOIN data_types dt ON d.data_type = dt.data_type_id WHERE d.status = 'active' ), DatasetQuality AS ( SELECT dq.dataset_id, GROUP_CONCAT(dq.metric_name || ': ' || dq.metric_value) AS quality_metrics FROM data_quality dq GROUP BY dq.dataset_id ), FinalDataset AS ( SELECT ad.dataset_id, ad.dataset_name, ad.upload_date, ad.uploaded_by_username, ad.file_size, ad.data_source, ad.status, ad.data_type_name, lv.version_number, lv.update_date, lv.version_description, lv.version_status, dq.quality_metrics FROM ActiveDatasets ad LEFT JOIN LatestVersion lv ON ad.dataset_id = lv.dataset_id AND lv.version_rank = 1 LEFT JOIN DatasetQuality dq ON ad.dataset_id = dq.dataset_id ) SELECT 'Dataset ID: ' || dataset_id || ', Name: ' || dataset_name || ', Upload Date: ' || upload_date || ', Uploaded By: ' || uploaded_by_username || ', File Size: ' || file_size || ' MB, Data Source: ' || data_source || ', Status: ' || status || ', Data Type: ' || data_type_name || ', Latest Version: ' || version_number || ', Update Date: ' || update_date || ', Version Description: ' || version_description || ', Version Status: ' || version_status || ', Quality Metrics: ' || quality_metrics AS dataset_info FROM FinalDataset

question: Can you show me the names and types of government entities, along with their latest report's publication date, data source, data timestamp, and a list of filter values used in these reports, ordered from newest to oldest?

question: Hey, can you show me the current value, initial value, gain, and return for each of my users' portfolios, along with the market performance and alpha (the difference between the portfolio return and the market return), ordered by the user's ID? I'd like to see the total current value, total initial value, total gain, total net gain, total return, average market return, average portfolio return, and alpha for each user.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH PortfolioValue AS ( SELECT up.user_id, up.number_of_shares, up.purchase_price, sd.close_price, (up.number_of_shares * sd.close_price) AS current_value, (up.number_of_shares * up.purchase_price) AS initial_value, (up.number_of_shares * sd.close_price) - (up.number_of_shares * up.purchase_price) AS gain, ((up.number_of_shares * sd.close_price) - (up.number_of_shares * up.purchase_price)) / (up.number_of_shares * up.purchase_price) AS return FROM user_portfolios up INNER JOIN stock_data sd ON up.ticker = sd.ticker AND sd.date = (SELECT MAX(date) FROM stock_data WHERE ticker = up.ticker) WHERE up.is_active = 1 ), MarketPerformance AS ( SELECT md.market_index, md.date, (md.market_value - LAG(md.market_value) OVER (PARTITION BY md.market_index ORDER BY md.date)) / LAG(md.market_value) OVER (PARTITION BY md.market_index ORDER BY md.date) AS market_return FROM market_data md ), PortfolioSummary AS ( SELECT pv.user_id, SUM(pv.current_value) AS total_current_value, SUM(pv.initial_value) AS total_initial_value, SUM(pv.gain) AS total_gain, SUM(pv.current_value) - SUM(pv.initial_value) AS total_net_gain, SUM(pv.current_value) / SUM(pv.initial_value) - 1 AS total_return FROM PortfolioValue pv GROUP BY pv.user_id ), MarketReturn AS ( SELECT mp.date, AVG(mp.market_return) AS average_market_return FROM MarketPerformance mp GROUP BY mp.date ), FinalAnalysis AS ( SELECT ps.user_id, ps.total_current_value, ps.total_initial_value, ps.total_gain, ps.total_net_gain, ps.total_return, mr.average_market_return, ps.total_return - mr.average_market_return AS alpha FROM PortfolioSummary ps CROSS JOIN MarketReturn mr ) SELECT fa.user_id, fa.total_current_value, fa.total_initial_value, fa.total_gain, fa.total_net_gain, fa.total_return, fa.average_market_return, fa.alpha FROM FinalAnalysis fa ORDER BY fa.user_id

question: Incidents in 2019 with more than one response, return their IDs, dates, states, cities, addresses, response counts, and average casualties, ordered by date, state, and city.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT i.incident_id, i.incident_date, s.state_name, c.city_name, i.address, COUNT(r.response_id) AS response_count, AVG(coalesce(cas.fatalities, 0) + coalesce(cas.injuries, 0)) AS avg_casualties FROM incidents i INNER JOIN states s ON i.state_id = s.state_id INNER JOIN cities c ON i.city_id = c.city_id LEFT JOIN incident_responses r ON i.incident_id = r.incident_id LEFT JOIN casualties cas ON i.incident_id = cas.incident_id WHERE strftime('%Y', i.incident_date) = '2019' GROUP BY i.incident_id, i.incident_date, s.state_name, c.city_name, i.address HAVING COUNT(r.response_id) > 1 ORDER BY i.incident_date, s.state_name, c.city_name

question: What are the names of the top 3 models based on precision, and what are their associated classification labels?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH TopPerformingModels AS ( SELECT m.model_id, m.model_name, p.precision, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY p.precision DESC) AS precision_rank FROM classification_models m INNER JOIN model_performance p ON m.model_id = p.model_id ) SELECT tpm.model_name, GROUP_CONCAT(cl.label_name, ', ') AS top_labels FROM TopPerformingModels tpm INNER JOIN model_class_labels mcl ON tpm.model_id = mcl.model_id INNER JOIN class_labels cl ON mcl.label_id = cl.label_id WHERE tpm.precision_rank <= 3 GROUP BY tpm.model_name
gold_sql.mysql: WITH TopPerformingModels AS (SELECT m.model_id, m.model_name, p.`precision`, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY p.`precision` DESC) AS precision_rank FROM classification_models AS m INNER JOIN model_performance AS p ON m.model_id = p.model_id) SELECT tpm.model_name, GROUP_CONCAT(cl.label_name SEPARATOR ', ') AS top_labels FROM TopPerformingModels AS tpm INNER JOIN model_class_labels AS mcl ON tpm.model_id = mcl.model_id INNER JOIN class_labels AS cl ON mcl.label_id = cl.label_id WHERE tpm.precision_rank <= 3 GROUP BY tpm.model_name
gold_sql.postgres: WITH TopPerformingModels AS (SELECT m.model_id, m.model_name, p.precision, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY p.precision DESC NULLS LAST) AS precision_rank FROM classification_models AS m INNER JOIN model_performance AS p ON m.model_id = p.model_id) SELECT tpm.model_name, STRING_AGG(cl.label_name, ', ') AS top_labels FROM TopPerformingModels AS tpm INNER JOIN model_class_labels AS mcl ON tpm.model_id = mcl.model_id INNER JOIN class_labels AS cl ON mcl.label_id = cl.label_id WHERE tpm.precision_rank <= 3 GROUP BY tpm.model_name

question: Could you provide a detailed report of user activities related to SQL Server editions, including the user's name, type of activity (comparison or recommendation), activity date, the name of the edition involved, and the analysis of the edition's features such as total features, core features, and advanced features, along with the reason for any recommendations, user requirements, and whether the recommendations were accepted?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH UserActivities AS ( SELECT u.user_name, a.activity_type, a.activity_date, CASE WHEN a.activity_type = 'comparison' THEN ( SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(e.edition_name) FROM editions e JOIN comparisons c ON a.user_id = c.user_id WHERE c.comparison_date = a.activity_date AND c.selected_editions LIKE '%' || e.edition_id || '%' ) WHEN a.activity_type = 'recommendation' THEN ( SELECT e.edition_name FROM editions e WHERE e.edition_id = ( SELECT r.recommended_edition_id FROM recommendations r WHERE r.user_id = a.user_id AND r.recommendation_date = a.activity_date ) ) END AS edition_name, a.activity_details, r.reason, r.user_requirements, r.is_accepted FROM audit_logs a LEFT JOIN users u ON a.user_id = u.user_id LEFT JOIN recommendations r ON a.user_id = r.user_id AND a.activity_date = r.recommendation_date ), EditionAnalysis AS ( SELECT e.edition_name, COUNT(edf.edition_feature_id) AS total_features, SUM(CASE WHEN edf.is_core_feature = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS core_features, SUM(CASE WHEN f.is_advanced = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS advanced_features FROM editions e LEFT JOIN edition_features edf ON e.edition_id = edf.edition_id LEFT JOIN features f ON edf.feature_id = f.feature_id GROUP BY e.edition_name ) SELECT ua.user_name, ua.activity_type, ua.activity_date, ua.edition_name, ea.total_features, ea.core_features, ea.advanced_features, ua.reason, ua.user_requirements, ua.is_accepted FROM UserActivities ua LEFT JOIN EditionAnalysis ea ON ua.edition_name = ea.edition_name ORDER BY ua.user_name, ua.activity_date

question: What are the names, versions, and details of the latest revisions of all IC designs, including the creators, approvers, pin information, and user access records, listed in order of most recent revisions?
external_knowledge: There is no external knowledge necessary for this query.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH LatestRevisions AS ( SELECT r.design_id, r.revision_date, r.description, r.created_by, r.approved_by, r.approved_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY r.design_id ORDER BY r.revision_date DESC) AS rn FROM revisions r ), FilteredRevisions AS ( SELECT lr.design_id, lr.revision_date, lr.description, lr.created_by, lr.approved_by, lr.approved_at FROM LatestRevisions lr WHERE lr.rn = 1 ), DesignPinInfo AS ( SELECT dp.design_id, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT p.pin_name || ' (' || p.io_type || ', ' || p.functionality || ', ' || p.voltage_range || ', ' || p.current_rating || ')') AS pin_information FROM design_pins dp JOIN pins p ON dp.pin_id = p.pin_id GROUP BY dp.design_id ), UserAccessInfo AS ( SELECT a.design_id, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT u.user_name || ' (' || u.email || ', ' || a.access_date || ', ' || a.ip_address || ')') AS user_access FROM access_logs a JOIN users u ON a.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY a.design_id ) SELECT d.design_name, d.version, fr.revision_date, fr.description, u1.user_name AS created_by, u2.user_name AS approved_by, dpi.pin_information, uai.user_access FROM ic_designs d JOIN FilteredRevisions fr ON d.design_id = fr.design_id LEFT JOIN DesignPinInfo dpi ON d.design_id = dpi.design_id LEFT JOIN UserAccessInfo uai ON d.design_id = uai.design_id LEFT JOIN users u1 ON fr.created_by = u1.user_id LEFT JOIN users u2 ON fr.approved_by = u2.user_id ORDER BY fr.revision_date DESC
gold_sql.mysql: WITH LatestRevisions AS (SELECT r.design_id, r.revision_date, r.description, r.created_by, r.approved_by, r.approved_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY r.design_id ORDER BY r.revision_date DESC) AS rn FROM revisions AS r), FilteredRevisions AS (SELECT lr.design_id, lr.revision_date, lr.description, lr.created_by, lr.approved_by, lr.approved_at FROM LatestRevisions AS lr WHERE lr.rn = 1), DesignPinInfo AS (SELECT dp.design_id, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT CONCAT(p.pin_name, ' (', p.io_type, ', ', p.functionality, ', ', p.voltage_range, ', ', p.current_rating, ')') SEPARATOR ',') AS pin_information FROM design_pins AS dp JOIN pins AS p ON dp.pin_id = p.pin_id GROUP BY dp.design_id), UserAccessInfo AS (SELECT a.design_id, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT CONCAT(u.user_name, ' (', u.email, ', ', a.access_date, ', ', a.ip_address, ')') SEPARATOR ',') AS user_access FROM access_logs AS a JOIN users AS u ON a.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY a.design_id) SELECT d.design_name, d.version, fr.revision_date, fr.description, u1.user_name AS created_by, u2.user_name AS approved_by, dpi.pin_information, uai.user_access FROM ic_designs AS d JOIN FilteredRevisions AS fr ON d.design_id = fr.design_id LEFT JOIN DesignPinInfo AS dpi ON d.design_id = dpi.design_id LEFT JOIN UserAccessInfo AS uai ON d.design_id = uai.design_id LEFT JOIN users AS u1 ON fr.created_by = u1.user_id LEFT JOIN users AS u2 ON fr.approved_by = u2.user_id ORDER BY fr.revision_date DESC
gold_sql.postgres: WITH LatestRevisions AS (SELECT r.design_id, r.revision_date, r.description, r.created_by, r.approved_by, r.approved_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY r.design_id ORDER BY r.revision_date DESC NULLS LAST) AS rn FROM revisions AS r), FilteredRevisions AS (SELECT lr.design_id, lr.revision_date, lr.description, lr.created_by, lr.approved_by, lr.approved_at FROM LatestRevisions AS lr WHERE lr.rn = 1), DesignPinInfo AS (SELECT dp.design_id, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT p.pin_name || ' (' || p.io_type || ', ' || p.functionality || ', ' || p.voltage_range || ', ' || p.current_rating || ')', ',') AS pin_information FROM design_pins AS dp JOIN pins AS p ON dp.pin_id = p.pin_id GROUP BY dp.design_id), UserAccessInfo AS (SELECT a.design_id, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT u.user_name || ' (' || u.email || ', ' || a.access_date || ', ' || a.ip_address || ')', ',') AS user_access FROM access_logs AS a JOIN users AS u ON a.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY a.design_id) SELECT d.design_name, d.version, fr.revision_date, fr.description, u1.user_name AS created_by, u2.user_name AS approved_by, dpi.pin_information, uai.user_access FROM ic_designs AS d JOIN FilteredRevisions AS fr ON d.design_id = fr.design_id LEFT JOIN DesignPinInfo AS dpi ON d.design_id = dpi.design_id LEFT JOIN UserAccessInfo AS uai ON d.design_id = uai.design_id LEFT JOIN users AS u1 ON fr.created_by = u1.user_id LEFT JOIN users AS u2 ON fr.approved_by = u2.user_id ORDER BY fr.revision_date DESC NULLS LAST

question: Could you provide the latest live weather conditions and the latest forecast for each meteorological station, including the station name, the time of the record (or forecast), and the weather or forecast condition, ordered by the most recent record or forecast time?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH LatestLiveRecords AS ( SELECT station_id, MAX(record_time) AS latest_record_time FROM weather_records GROUP BY station_id ), LatestForecasts AS ( SELECT station_id, MAX(forecast_time) AS latest_forecast_time FROM forecast_data GROUP BY station_id ), LiveConditions AS ( SELECT wr.station_id, wr.record_time, wr.weather_condition FROM weather_records wr INNER JOIN LatestLiveRecords l ON wr.station_id = l.station_id AND wr.record_time = l.latest_record_time ), ForecastConditions AS ( SELECT fd.station_id, fd.forecast_time, 'Forecast: ' || fd.predicted_temp || '°C, ' || fd.predicted_humidity || '% RH, ' || fd.predicted_wind_speed || ' km/h, ' || fd.predicted_visibility || ' km' AS forecast_condition FROM forecast_data fd INNER JOIN LatestForecasts l ON fd.station_id = l.station_id AND fd.forecast_time = l.latest_forecast_time ) SELECT sn.station_name, COALESCE(lc.record_time, fc.forecast_time) AS record_time, COALESCE(lc.weather_condition, fc.forecast_condition) AS condition FROM LiveConditions lc FULL OUTER JOIN ForecastConditions fc ON lc.station_id = fc.station_id JOIN meteorological_stations sn ON COALESCE(lc.station_id, fc.station_id) = sn.station_id ORDER BY record_time DESC

question: For the game with title '1', return the names, countries, tournament names, years, game titles, ranks, competitive scores, and rounds won by players in tournaments that took place in 2018 or later, along with the total count of players, average rank, and percentile rank of each player in the game, ordered by their ranks.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH PlayerTournamentPerformance AS ( SELECT tr.player_id, tr.tournament_id, tr.rank, tr.comp_score, tr.rounds_won, t.tournament_name, t.year, p.player_name, p.country, t.game_title, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY tr.player_id ORDER BY tr.year DESC) as latest_performance FROM tournament_results tr INNER JOIN players p ON tr.player_id = p.player_id INNER JOIN tournaments t ON tr.tournament_id = t.tournament_id ), TopPlayerTournamentPerformance AS ( SELECT player_id, tournament_id, rank, comp_score, rounds_won, tournament_name, year, player_name, country, game_title FROM PlayerTournamentPerformance WHERE latest_performance = 1 ) SELECT pptp.player_name, pptp.country, pptp.tournament_name, pptp.year, pptp.game_title, pptp.rank, pptp.comp_score, pptp.rounds_won, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY pptp.game_title) as game_title_count, AVG(pptp.rank) OVER (PARTITION BY pptp.game_title) as average_rank, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM TopPlayerTournamentPerformance pptp2 WHERE pptp2.game_title = pptp.game_title AND pptp2.rank < pptp.rank) / COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY pptp.game_title) as rank_percentile FROM TopPlayerTournamentPerformance pptp WHERE pptp.year >= 2018 AND pptp.game_title = '1' ORDER BY pptp.rank

question: I want to know the production activity details, including the activity, quantity produced, cumulative quantity, garment name, size name, user role, date, and activity rank for each garment and size combination, along with their measurements, ordered by garment name, size name, and activity rank.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ProductionActivity AS ( SELECT pl.log_id, pl.activity, pl.quantity, pl.date, pl.user_id, pl.garment_id, pl.size_id, u.role, sz.size_name, gt.garment_name, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY pl.garment_id, pl.size_id ORDER BY pl.date) AS activity_rank, SUM(pl.quantity) OVER (PARTITION BY pl.garment_id, pl.size_id ORDER BY pl.date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_quantity FROM production_logs pl INNER JOIN users u ON pl.user_id = u.user_id INNER JOIN sizes sz ON pl.size_id = sz.size_id INNER JOIN garment_types gt ON pl.garment_id = gt.garment_id ), MeasurementSummary AS ( SELECT ms.size_id, GROUP_CONCAT(ms.measurement_name || ': ' || CAST(ms.value AS TEXT) || ' ' || ms.unit, ', ') AS measurements FROM measurements ms GROUP BY ms.size_id ) SELECT pa.log_id, pa.activity, pa.quantity, pa.cumulative_quantity, pa.garment_name, pa.size_name, pa.role AS role_name, pa.date, pa.activity_rank, ms.measurements FROM ProductionActivity pa LEFT JOIN MeasurementSummary ms ON pa.size_id = ms.size_id ORDER BY pa.garment_name, pa.size_name, pa.activity_rank

question: Create a comprehensive report that, for each educational media, describes the status, total distributions, total copies distributed, distribution types, user access frequency, access methods, locations from which users accessed the media, shortest access duration, longest access duration, number of production sessions, production locations, and equipment used during production.
external_knowledge: None required for this query.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH MediaDistributionSummary AS ( SELECT mr.title, mr.status AS media_status, COUNT(md.distribution_id) AS total_distributions, SUM(md.quantity) AS total_distributed_copies, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT md.status) AS distribution_statuses FROM media_records mr LEFT JOIN media_distribution md ON mr.media_id = md.media_id GROUP BY mr.title, mr.status ), UserAccessSummary AS ( SELECT mr.title, COUNT(*) AS access_count, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ma.access_type) AS access_types, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ma.access_location) AS access_locations, MIN(ma.session_duration) AS min_session_duration, MAX(ma.session_duration) AS max_session_duration FROM media_records mr LEFT JOIN media_access ma ON mr.media_id = ma.media_id GROUP BY mr.title ), ProductionSessionSummary AS ( SELECT mr.title, COUNT(ps.production_id) AS total_sessions, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ps.location) AS session_locations, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ps.equipment_used) AS equipment_used FROM media_records mr LEFT JOIN media_production ps ON mr.media_id = ps.media_id GROUP BY mr.title ) SELECT GROUP_CONCAT( 'Title: ' || ms.title || ', Media Status: ' || ms.media_status || ', Total Distributions: ' || ms.total_distributions || ', Total Distributed Copies: ' || ms.total_distributed_copies || ', Distribution Statuses: ' || ms.distribution_statuses || ', Access Count: ' || us.access_count || ', Access Types: ' || us.access_types || ', Access Locations: ' || us.access_locations || ', Min Session Duration: ' || us.min_session_duration || ', Max Session Duration: ' || us.max_session_duration || ', Total Production Sessions: ' || ps.total_sessions || ', Session Locations: ' || ps.session_locations || ', Equipment Used: ' || ps.equipment_used ) AS comprehensive_report FROM MediaDistributionSummary ms LEFT JOIN UserAccessSummary us ON ms.title = us.title LEFT JOIN ProductionSessionSummary ps ON ms.title = ps.title

question: What are the titles, average ratings, total reviews, publication dates, publishers, and authors of the top 5 most reviewed books?
external_knowledge: ; The "most reviewed" books refer to the top 5 books with the highest total reviews; A "book" in this context refers to an entry in the books table.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH TopReviewedBooks AS ( SELECT book_id, title, avg_rating, total_reviews, publication_date, publisher FROM books ORDER BY total_reviews DESC LIMIT 5 ) SELECT trb.title, trb.avg_rating, trb.total_reviews, trb.publication_date, trb.publisher, GROUP_CONCAT(a.author_name) AS authors FROM TopReviewedBooks trb JOIN book_authors ba ON trb.book_id = ba.book_id JOIN authors a ON ba.author_id = a.author_id GROUP BY trb.book_id, trb.title, trb.avg_rating, trb.total_reviews, trb.publication_date, trb.publisher ORDER BY trb.total_reviews DESC
gold_sql.mysql: WITH TopReviewedBooks AS (SELECT book_id, title, avg_rating, total_reviews, publication_date, publisher FROM books ORDER BY total_reviews DESC LIMIT 5) SELECT trb.title, trb.avg_rating, trb.total_reviews, trb.publication_date, trb.publisher, GROUP_CONCAT(a.author_name SEPARATOR ',') AS authors FROM TopReviewedBooks AS trb JOIN book_authors AS ba ON trb.book_id = ba.book_id JOIN authors AS a ON ba.author_id = a.author_id GROUP BY trb.book_id, trb.title, trb.avg_rating, trb.total_reviews, trb.publication_date, trb.publisher ORDER BY trb.total_reviews DESC

question: What are the names of the top 5 projects with the highest cumulative jobs created and state tax revenue?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ProjectMetrics AS ( SELECT p.project_id, p.project_name, SUM(CASE WHEN pm.metric_name = 'Actual Jobs Created' THEN CAST(REPLACE(pm.metric_value, ',', '') AS INTEGER) ELSE 0 END) AS total_jobs, SUM(CASE WHEN pm.metric_name = 'Actual State Tax Revenue' THEN CAST(REPLACE(pm.metric_value, ',', '') AS INTEGER) ELSE 0 END) AS total_tax_revenue FROM projects p LEFT JOIN project_metrics pm ON p.project_id = pm.project_id GROUP BY p.project_id, p.project_name ), RankedProjects AS ( SELECT project_name, total_jobs, total_tax_revenue, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total_jobs + total_tax_revenue DESC) AS project_rank FROM ProjectMetrics ) SELECT project_name FROM RankedProjects WHERE project_rank <= 5

question: What is a comprehensive list of movies, including their titles, directors, writers, release years, runtimes, languages, countries of origin, budgets, revenues, numbers of awards, and average ratings, ordered chronologically and then alphabetically?
external_knowledge: This question provides a comprehensive overview of each movie in the database, covering key attributes and relationships with directors and writers. The query does not require any domain-specific knowledge beyond understanding the database schema.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT m.movie_id, m.title, m.year, d.director_name, m.runtime, m.language, m.country, m.budget, m.revenue, IFNULL(a.award_count, 0) AS award_count, IFNULL(r.average_rating, 0) AS average_rating, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT w.writer_name || ' (' || mw.writing_credit || ')') AS writers FROM movies m LEFT JOIN directors d ON m.director_id = d.director_id LEFT JOIN movie_writers mw ON m.movie_id = mw.movie_id LEFT JOIN writers w ON mw.writer_id = w.writer_id LEFT JOIN ( SELECT movie_id, COUNT(award_id) AS award_count FROM awards GROUP BY movie_id ) a ON m.movie_id = a.movie_id LEFT JOIN ( SELECT movie_id, AVG(rating_value) AS average_rating FROM ratings GROUP BY movie_id ) r ON m.movie_id = r.movie_id GROUP BY m.movie_id, m.title, m.year, d.director_name, m.runtime, m.language, m.country, m.budget, m.revenue, a.award_count, r.average_rating ORDER BY m.year, m.title
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT m.movie_id, m.title, m.year, d.director_name, m.runtime, m.language, m.country, m.budget, m.revenue, COALESCE(a.award_count, 0) AS award_count, COALESCE(r.average_rating, 0) AS average_rating, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT CONCAT(w.writer_name, ' (', mw.writing_credit, ')') SEPARATOR ',') AS writers FROM movies AS m LEFT JOIN directors AS d ON m.director_id = d.director_id LEFT JOIN movie_writers AS mw ON m.movie_id = mw.movie_id LEFT JOIN writers AS w ON mw.writer_id = w.writer_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT movie_id, COUNT(award_id) AS award_count FROM awards GROUP BY movie_id) AS a ON m.movie_id = a.movie_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT movie_id, AVG(rating_value) AS average_rating FROM ratings GROUP BY movie_id) AS r ON m.movie_id = r.movie_id GROUP BY m.movie_id, m.title, m.year, d.director_name, m.runtime, m.language, m.country, m.budget, m.revenue, a.award_count, r.average_rating ORDER BY m.year, m.title
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT m.movie_id, m.title, m.year, d.director_name, m.runtime, m.language, m.country, m.budget, m.revenue, COALESCE(a.award_count, 0) AS award_count, COALESCE(r.average_rating, 0) AS average_rating, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT w.writer_name || ' (' || mw.writing_credit || ')', ',') AS writers FROM movies AS m LEFT JOIN directors AS d ON m.director_id = d.director_id LEFT JOIN movie_writers AS mw ON m.movie_id = mw.movie_id LEFT JOIN writers AS w ON mw.writer_id = w.writer_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT movie_id, COUNT(award_id) AS award_count FROM awards GROUP BY movie_id) AS a ON m.movie_id = a.movie_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT movie_id, AVG(rating_value) AS average_rating FROM ratings GROUP BY movie_id) AS r ON m.movie_id = r.movie_id GROUP BY m.movie_id, m.title, m.year, d.director_name, m.runtime, m.language, m.country, m.budget, m.revenue, a.award_count, r.average_rating ORDER BY m.year NULLS FIRST, m.title NULLS FIRST

question:
**User**: I'd like to analyze endpoint performance and user request failure rates.
**Assistant**: What specific endpoint metrics are you interested in analyzing?
**User**: I'd like to know the average response time and average content size for each endpoint.
**Assistant**: That's a good starting point. Would you like to relate these metrics to user behavior, such as request failure rates?
**User**: Yes, that would be helpful. Can we identify the user with the highest request failure rate?
**Assistant**: We can calculate the failure rate for each user by dividing their total failures by their total requests. Would you like to analyze the endpoints based on this top user failure rate?
**User**: Yes, that sounds like a good idea. How can we combine these metrics to get a better understanding of endpoint performance?
**Assistant**: We can combine the average response time, average content size, and top user failure rate for each endpoint. How would you like the results to be ordered?
**User**: I'd like to see the endpoints with the slowest response times first.
**Assistant**: So, to summarize, you'd like to analyze endpoint performance by average response time, average content size, and top user failure rate, and you'd like the results to be ordered by average response time in descending order. Is that correct?
**User**: Yes, that's correct.
**Assistant**: I will help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH EndpointMetrics AS ( SELECT pm.endpoint_id, AVG(pm.average_response_time) AS avg_response_time, AVG(cs.average_content_size) AS avg_content_size FROM performance_metrics pm INNER JOIN content_sizes cs ON pm.endpoint_id = cs.endpoint_id GROUP BY pm.endpoint_id ), UserRequests AS ( SELECT u.user_id, COUNT(r.request_id) AS total_requests, COUNT(r.error_message) AS total_failures FROM users u LEFT JOIN requests r ON u.user_id = r.user_id GROUP BY u.user_id ), TopUserFailureRate AS ( SELECT user_id, total_requests, total_failures, (CAST(total_failures AS REAL) / total_requests) AS failure_rate FROM UserRequests ORDER BY failure_rate DESC LIMIT 1 ), EndpointAnalysis AS ( SELECT em.endpoint_id, em.avg_response_time, em.avg_content_size, (SELECT failure_rate FROM TopUserFailureRate) AS top_user_failure_rate FROM EndpointMetrics em ) SELECT e.path, e.method, ea.avg_response_time, ea.avg_content_size, ea.top_user_failure_rate FROM EndpointAnalysis ea INNER JOIN endpoints e ON ea.endpoint_id = e.endpoint_id ORDER BY ea.avg_response_time DESC

gold_sql.postgres: WITH EndpointMetrics AS (SELECT pm.endpoint_id, AVG(pm.average_response_time) AS avg_response_time, AVG(cs.average_content_size) AS avg_content_size FROM performance_metrics AS pm INNER JOIN content_sizes AS cs ON pm.endpoint_id = cs.endpoint_id GROUP BY pm.endpoint_id), UserRequests AS (SELECT u.user_id, COUNT(r.request_id) AS total_requests, COUNT(r.error_message) AS total_failures FROM users AS u LEFT JOIN requests AS r ON u.user_id = r.user_id GROUP BY u.user_id), TopUserFailureRate AS (SELECT user_id, total_requests, total_failures, (CAST(total_failures AS REAL) / NULLIF(total_requests, 0)) AS failure_rate FROM UserRequests ORDER BY failure_rate DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1), EndpointAnalysis AS (SELECT em.endpoint_id, em.avg_response_time, em.avg_content_size, (SELECT failure_rate FROM TopUserFailureRate) AS top_user_failure_rate FROM EndpointMetrics AS em) SELECT e.path, e.method, ea.avg_response_time, ea.avg_content_size, ea.top_user_failure_rate FROM EndpointAnalysis AS ea INNER JOIN endpoints AS e ON ea.endpoint_id = e.endpoint_id ORDER BY ea.avg_response_time DESC NULLS LAST

question:
**User**: I want to get information about popular books.
**Assistant**: What do you mean by popular books? Is it based on the number of downloads, reviews, or ratings?
**User**: Based on all three actually. I want books with the most downloads, reviews, and highest ratings.
**Assistant**: Okay, that's a good starting point. Would you like to know the authors and categories associated with these books as well?
**User**: Yes, that would be great. And can you please provide the top 10 books based on these criteria?
**Assistant**: Alright, so just to confirm, you want the titles, authors, and categories of the top 10 books with the most downloads, reviews, and highest ratings. Is that correct?
**User**: That's correct.
**Assistant**: Great, I'll help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH BookStats AS ( SELECT b.book_id, b.title, b.total_reviews, b.avg_rating, COUNT(d.download_id) AS download_count, GROUP_CONCAT(a.author_name) AS authors, GROUP_CONCAT(c.category_name) AS categories FROM books b LEFT JOIN book_downloads d ON b.book_id = d.book_id LEFT JOIN book_authors ba ON b.book_id = ba.book_id LEFT JOIN authors a ON ba.author_id = a.author_id LEFT JOIN book_categories bc ON b.book_id = bc.book_id LEFT JOIN categories c ON bc.category_id = c.category_id GROUP BY b.book_id, b.title, b.total_reviews, b.avg_rating ), RankedBooks AS ( SELECT bs.book_id, bs.title, bs.total_reviews, bs.avg_rating, bs.download_count, bs.authors, bs.categories, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY bs.download_count DESC, bs.total_reviews DESC, bs.avg_rating DESC) AS book_rank FROM BookStats bs ) SELECT rb.title, rb.authors, rb.categories FROM RankedBooks rb WHERE rb.book_rank <= 10

gold_sql.postgres: WITH BookStats AS (SELECT b.book_id, b.title, b.total_reviews, b.avg_rating, COUNT(d.download_id) AS download_count, STRING_AGG(a.author_name, ',') AS authors, STRING_AGG(c.category_name, ',') AS categories FROM books AS b LEFT JOIN book_downloads AS d ON b.book_id = d.book_id LEFT JOIN book_authors AS ba ON b.book_id = ba.book_id LEFT JOIN authors AS a ON ba.author_id = a.author_id LEFT JOIN book_categories AS bc ON b.book_id = bc.book_id LEFT JOIN categories AS c ON bc.category_id = c.category_id GROUP BY b.book_id, b.title, b.total_reviews, b.avg_rating), RankedBooks AS (SELECT bs.book_id, bs.title, bs.total_reviews, bs.avg_rating, bs.download_count, bs.authors, bs.categories, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY bs.download_count DESC NULLS LAST, bs.total_reviews DESC NULLS LAST, bs.avg_rating DESC NULLS LAST) AS book_rank FROM BookStats AS bs) SELECT rb.title, rb.authors, rb.categories FROM RankedBooks AS rb WHERE rb.book_rank <= 10

question: Return the loan IDs, first and last names of applicants, trimmed assessment dates, and risk factors for all loans, ordered by loan ID and risk factor in descending order.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT l.loan_id, a.first_name, a.last_name, LTRIM(c.assessment_date, '202') AS assessment_trimmed_date, CASE WHEN c.risk_level = 'low' THEN 0.9 WHEN c.risk_level = 'medium' THEN 0.75 WHEN c.risk_level = 'high' THEN 0.5 ELSE 0.6 END AS risk_factor FROM applicants a JOIN loans l ON a.applicant_id = l.applicant_id LEFT JOIN credit_risk_assessments c ON l.loan_id = c.loan_id ORDER BY l.loan_id, risk_factor DESC

question: What are the top 10 crops at Farm A based on their cumulative performance score, which combines yield and health metrics, for the year 2023?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH FarmAData AS ( SELECT cp.crop_id, cp.yield, cp.health_score, l.location_name FROM crop_performance cp JOIN locations l ON cp.location_id = l.location_id WHERE l.location_name = 'Farm A' AND strftime('%Y', cp.harvest_date) = '2023' ), CumulativePerformance AS ( SELECT fad.crop_id, c.crop_name, SUM(fad.yield) OVER (PARTITION BY fad.crop_id) AS total_yield, AVG(fad.health_score) OVER (PARTITION BY fad.crop_id) AS avg_health_score, (SUM(fad.yield) OVER (PARTITION BY fad.crop_id) + AVG(fad.health_score) OVER (PARTITION BY fad.crop_id)) / 2 AS cumulative_performance_score FROM FarmAData fad JOIN crops c ON fad.crop_id = c.crop_id ) SELECT cp.crop_name, cp.total_yield, cp.avg_health_score, cp.cumulative_performance_score FROM CumulativePerformance cp ORDER BY cp.cumulative_performance_score DESC LIMIT 10

question: What is the total attendance and revenue for the playoff games that extended beyond the regular playing time?
external_knowledge:
- "Extended beyond the regular playing time" refers to games where `overtime` is set to 1;
- "Playoff games" are identified by the `playoffs` table.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT SUM(a.total_attendance) AS total_playoff_attendance, SUM(CAST(a.revenue AS INTEGER)) AS total_playoff_revenue FROM games g INNER JOIN playoffs p ON g.game_id = p.game_id INNER JOIN attendance a ON g.game_id = a.game_id WHERE g.overtime = 1
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT SUM(a.total_attendance) AS total_playoff_attendance, SUM(CAST(a.revenue AS SIGNED)) AS total_playoff_revenue FROM games AS g INNER JOIN playoffs AS p ON g.game_id = p.game_id INNER JOIN attendance AS a ON g.game_id = a.game_id WHERE g.overtime = 1
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT SUM(a.total_attendance) AS total_playoff_attendance, SUM(CAST(a.revenue AS INT)) AS total_playoff_revenue FROM games AS g INNER JOIN playoffs AS p ON g.game_id = p.game_id INNER JOIN attendance AS a ON g.game_id = a.game_id WHERE g.overtime = 1

question: What is a summary of a high-confidence, non-archived 'TEST' interaction, including the names of the interacting entities, the type and subtype of interaction, the confidence score, and the interaction date, limited to one result?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH HighConfidenceInteractions AS ( SELECT i.interaction_id, e1.entity_name AS start_entity_name, e2.entity_name AS end_entity_name, it.interaction_type_name, ist.interaction_subtype_name, i.confidence_score, i.interaction_date FROM interactions i INNER JOIN entities e1 ON i.start_entity_id = e1.entity_id INNER JOIN entities e2 ON i.end_entity_id = e2.entity_id INNER JOIN interaction_types it ON i.interaction_type_id = it.interaction_type_id INNER JOIN interaction_subtypes ist ON i.interaction_subtype_id = ist.interaction_subtype_id WHERE it.interaction_type_name = 'TEST' AND it.is_archived = 0 AND ist.is_archived = 0 AND i.confidence_score > 0.5 ) SELECT start_entity_name || ' interacts with ' || end_entity_name || ' by ' || interaction_type_name || ' (' || interaction_subtype_name || ') with confidence ' || CAST(confidence_score AS TEXT) || ' on ' || interaction_date AS interaction_summary FROM HighConfidenceInteractions LIMIT 1
gold_sql.mysql: WITH HighConfidenceInteractions AS (SELECT i.interaction_id, e1.entity_name AS start_entity_name, e2.entity_name AS end_entity_name, it.interaction_type_name, ist.interaction_subtype_name, i.confidence_score, i.interaction_date FROM interactions AS i INNER JOIN entities AS e1 ON i.start_entity_id = e1.entity_id INNER JOIN entities AS e2 ON i.end_entity_id = e2.entity_id INNER JOIN interaction_types AS it ON i.interaction_type_id = it.interaction_type_id INNER JOIN interaction_subtypes AS ist ON i.interaction_subtype_id = ist.interaction_subtype_id WHERE it.interaction_type_name = 'TEST' AND it.is_archived = 0 AND ist.is_archived = 0 AND i.confidence_score > 0.5) SELECT CONCAT(start_entity_name, ' interacts with ', end_entity_name, ' by ', interaction_type_name, ' (', interaction_subtype_name, ') with confidence ', CAST(confidence_score AS CHAR), ' on ', interaction_date) AS interaction_summary FROM HighConfidenceInteractions LIMIT 1
gold_sql.postgres: WITH HighConfidenceInteractions AS (SELECT i.interaction_id, e1.entity_name AS start_entity_name, e2.entity_name AS end_entity_name, it.interaction_type_name, ist.interaction_subtype_name, i.confidence_score, i.interaction_date FROM interactions AS i INNER JOIN entities AS e1 ON i.start_entity_id = e1.entity_id INNER JOIN entities AS e2 ON i.end_entity_id = e2.entity_id INNER JOIN interaction_types AS it ON i.interaction_type_id = it.interaction_type_id INNER JOIN interaction_subtypes AS ist ON i.interaction_subtype_id = ist.interaction_subtype_id WHERE it.interaction_type_name = 'TEST' AND it.is_archived = 0 AND ist.is_archived = 0 AND i.confidence_score > 0.5) SELECT start_entity_name || ' interacts with ' || end_entity_name || ' by ' || interaction_type_name || ' (' || interaction_subtype_name || ') with confidence ' || CAST(confidence_score AS TEXT) || ' on ' || interaction_date AS interaction_summary FROM HighConfidenceInteractions LIMIT 1

question: List the names of students with a cumulative GPA less than 3.0, along with their advisers' names, cumulative GPAs, the number of times they have struggled, and the details of their struggles in courses with a difficulty level greater than 3, including the course names, difficulty levels, and reasons.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH StrugglingStudents AS ( SELECT s.student_id, s.student_name, a.adviser_name, g.cumulative_gpa, COUNT(str.struggle_id) AS number_of_struggles FROM students s JOIN gpa g ON s.student_id = g.student_id JOIN advisers a ON s.adviser_id = a.adviser_id LEFT JOIN struggle str ON s.student_id = str.student_id WHERE g.cumulative_gpa < 3.0 GROUP BY s.student_id, s.student_name, a.adviser_name, g.cumulative_gpa ), StruggleDetails AS ( SELECT str.student_id, c.course_name, str.difficulty_level, str.reason FROM struggle str JOIN courses c ON str.course_id = c.course_id WHERE str.difficulty_level > 3 ) SELECT ss.student_name, ss.adviser_name, ss.cumulative_gpa, ss.number_of_struggles, GROUP_CONCAT(sd.course_name || ': Difficulty ' || sd.difficulty_level || ', Reason: ' || sd.reason) AS struggles FROM StrugglingStudents ss LEFT JOIN StruggleDetails sd ON ss.student_id = sd.student_id GROUP BY ss.student_id, ss.student_name, ss.adviser_name, ss.cumulative_gpa, ss.number_of_struggles
gold_sql.mysql: WITH StrugglingStudents AS (SELECT s.student_id, s.student_name, a.adviser_name, g.cumulative_gpa, COUNT(str.struggle_id) AS number_of_struggles FROM students AS s JOIN gpa AS g ON s.student_id = g.student_id JOIN advisers AS a ON s.adviser_id = a.adviser_id LEFT JOIN struggle AS str ON s.student_id = str.student_id WHERE g.cumulative_gpa < 3.0 GROUP BY s.student_id, s.student_name, a.adviser_name, g.cumulative_gpa), StruggleDetails AS (SELECT str.student_id, c.course_name, str.difficulty_level, str.reason FROM struggle AS str JOIN courses AS c ON str.course_id = c.course_id WHERE str.difficulty_level > 3) SELECT ss.student_name, ss.adviser_name, ss.cumulative_gpa, ss.number_of_struggles, GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(sd.course_name, ': Difficulty ', sd.difficulty_level, ', Reason: ', sd.reason) SEPARATOR ',') AS struggles FROM StrugglingStudents AS ss LEFT JOIN StruggleDetails AS sd ON ss.student_id = sd.student_id GROUP BY ss.student_id, ss.student_name, ss.adviser_name, ss.cumulative_gpa, ss.number_of_struggles
gold_sql.postgres: WITH StrugglingStudents AS (SELECT s.student_id, s.student_name, a.adviser_name, g.cumulative_gpa, COUNT(str.struggle_id) AS number_of_struggles FROM students AS s JOIN gpa AS g ON s.student_id = g.student_id JOIN advisers AS a ON s.adviser_id = a.adviser_id LEFT JOIN struggle AS str ON s.student_id = str.student_id WHERE g.cumulative_gpa < 3.0 GROUP BY s.student_id, s.student_name, a.adviser_name, g.cumulative_gpa), StruggleDetails AS (SELECT str.student_id, c.course_name, str.difficulty_level, str.reason FROM struggle AS str JOIN courses AS c ON str.course_id = c.course_id WHERE str.difficulty_level > 3) SELECT ss.student_name, ss.adviser_name, ss.cumulative_gpa, ss.number_of_struggles, STRING_AGG(sd.course_name || ': Difficulty ' || sd.difficulty_level || ', Reason: ' || sd.reason, ',') AS struggles FROM StrugglingStudents AS ss LEFT JOIN StruggleDetails AS sd ON ss.student_id = sd.student_id GROUP BY ss.student_id, ss.student_name, ss.adviser_name, ss.cumulative_gpa, ss.number_of_struggles

question: Could you please provide the maximum and minimum adjusted closing prices and their corresponding dates for the stock with `symbol_id = 1`, along with the total number of access events and the total data size accessed in kilobytes for the same stock, and also the GDP value for the date '2023-03-31'?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH StockPriceExtrema AS ( SELECT MAX(adj_close) AS max_adj_close, MIN(adj_close) AS min_adj_close, MAX(CASE WHEN adj_close = (SELECT MAX(adj_close) FROM stock_prices WHERE symbol_id = 1) THEN date END) AS max_adj_close_date, MIN(CASE WHEN adj_close = (SELECT MIN(adj_close) FROM stock_prices WHERE symbol_id = 1) THEN date END) AS min_adj_close_date FROM stock_prices WHERE symbol_id = 1 ), UserAccessVolume AS ( SELECT COUNT(access_id) AS access_count, SUM(CAST(RTRIM(data_size, ' B') AS REAL)) / 1024 AS total_data_size_kb FROM user_access WHERE symbol_id = 1 ), GDPIndicator AS ( SELECT value AS gdp_value FROM economic_indicators WHERE indicator_name = 'GDP' AND date = '2023-03-31' ) SELECT spep.max_adj_close, spep.min_adj_close, spep.max_adj_close_date, spep.min_adj_close_date, uav.access_count, uav.total_data_size_kb, gi.gdp_value FROM StockPriceExtrema spep CROSS JOIN UserAccessVolume uav CROSS JOIN GDPIndicator gi

question: Hey, could you show me a list of words along with their parts of speech, usage counts, and the historical periods they were used in? I'd love to see the total usage count for each word in each period, as well as the number of unique users who accessed each word and the number of translations available for each word. Could you sort the results by the word form and the name of the historical period?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH WordUsageByPeriod AS ( SELECT u.word_id, p.period_id, p.period_name, SUM(u.usage_count) AS total_usage_count FROM usage_stats u INNER JOIN historical_periods p ON u.date BETWEEN p.start_year || '-01-01' AND p.end_year || '-12-31' GROUP BY u.word_id, p.period_id, p.period_name ), UserAccessByWord AS ( SELECT a.word_id, COUNT(DISTINCT a.user_id) AS unique_users FROM access_logs a GROUP BY a.word_id ), TranslationsByWord AS ( SELECT t.word_id, COUNT(t.translation_id) AS translation_count FROM translations t GROUP BY t.word_id ) SELECT w.word_form, w.pos, w.usage_count, wp.period_name, wp.total_usage_count, uaw.unique_users, tbw.translation_count FROM words w LEFT JOIN WordUsageByPeriod wp ON w.word_id = wp.word_id LEFT JOIN UserAccessByWord uaw ON w.word_id = uaw.word_id LEFT JOIN TranslationsByWord tbw ON w.word_id = tbw.word_id ORDER BY w.word_form, wp.period_name

question:
**User**: I want to get information about executive remuneration.
**Assistant**: Which executives would you like to know about?
**User**: All of them, but only for a specific year.
**Assistant**: Which year are you interested in?
**User**: 2021.
**Assistant**: What specific information about these executives do you want to know?
**User**: Their average remuneration, based on their designations.
**Assistant**: Do you want to filter these designations by any specific criteria?
**User**: Yes, I want to ensure their remuneration falls within the typical salary range for their designation.
**Assistant**: How would you like the results ordered?
**User**: By designation name.
**Assistant**: Is there anything else you need?
**User**: No.
**Assistant**: OK, I will help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT d.designation_name, AVG(cp.remuneration) AS average_remuneration, d.salary_range FROM executives e JOIN compensation_packages cp ON e.executive_id = cp.executive_id JOIN executive_designations ed ON e.executive_id = ed.executive_id JOIN designations d ON ed.designation_id = d.designation_id WHERE cp.year = 2021 GROUP BY d.designation_name, d.salary_range HAVING MIN(cp.remuneration) >= CAST(SUBSTR(d.salary_range, 1, INSTR(d.salary_range, ' - ') - 1) AS REAL) AND MAX(cp.remuneration) <= CAST(SUBSTR(d.salary_range, INSTR(d.salary_range, ' - ') + 3) AS REAL) ORDER BY d.designation_name

gold_sql.postgres: SELECT d.designation_name, AVG(cp.remuneration) AS average_remuneration, d.salary_range FROM executives AS e JOIN compensation_packages AS cp ON e.executive_id = cp.executive_id JOIN executive_designations AS ed ON e.executive_id = ed.executive_id JOIN designations AS d ON ed.designation_id = d.designation_id WHERE cp.year = 2021 GROUP BY d.designation_name, d.salary_range HAVING MIN(cp.remuneration) >= CAST(SUBSTRING(d.salary_range FROM 1 FOR STRPOS(d.salary_range, ' - ') - 1) AS REAL) AND MAX(cp.remuneration) <= CAST(SUBSTRING(d.salary_range FROM STRPOS(d.salary_range, ' - ') + 3) AS REAL) ORDER BY d.designation_name NULLS FIRST

question: What are the top neighborhoods in terms of total fines issued each month, and how much are the total fines for these top neighborhoods?
external_knowledge:
- 'Top neighborhoods' refers to the neighborhoods with the highest total fines issued each month, limited to the top 3.
- 'Total fines' include the sum of all fines issued in the top neighborhoods for each month.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH MonthlyFines AS ( SELECT c.citation_month_and_year AS month, n.neighborhood_name, SUM(cast(c.fine_amount as REAL)) AS total_fine FROM citations c JOIN neighborhoods n ON c.neighborhood_id = n.neighborhood_id GROUP BY c.citation_month_and_year, n.neighborhood_name ), RankedNeighborhoods AS ( SELECT month, neighborhood_name, total_fine, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY month ORDER BY total_fine DESC) AS rank_in_month FROM MonthlyFines ), TopNeighborhoods AS ( SELECT month, neighborhood_name, total_fine FROM RankedNeighborhoods WHERE rank_in_month <= 3 ) SELECT month, SUM(total_fine) AS total_top_fines, GROUP_CONCAT(neighborhood_name, ', ') AS top_neighborhoods FROM TopNeighborhoods GROUP BY month ORDER BY month
gold_sql.mysql: WITH MonthlyFines AS (SELECT c.citation_month_and_year AS month, n.neighborhood_name, SUM(CAST(c.fine_amount AS FLOAT)) AS total_fine FROM citations AS c JOIN neighborhoods AS n ON c.neighborhood_id = n.neighborhood_id GROUP BY c.citation_month_and_year, n.neighborhood_name), RankedNeighborhoods AS (SELECT month, neighborhood_name, total_fine, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY month ORDER BY total_fine DESC) AS rank_in_month FROM MonthlyFines), TopNeighborhoods AS (SELECT month, neighborhood_name, total_fine FROM RankedNeighborhoods WHERE rank_in_month <= 3) SELECT month, SUM(total_fine) AS total_top_fines, GROUP_CONCAT(neighborhood_name SEPARATOR ', ') AS top_neighborhoods FROM TopNeighborhoods GROUP BY month ORDER BY month
gold_sql.postgres: WITH MonthlyFines AS (SELECT c.citation_month_and_year AS month, n.neighborhood_name, SUM(CAST(c.fine_amount AS REAL)) AS total_fine FROM citations AS c JOIN neighborhoods AS n ON c.neighborhood_id = n.neighborhood_id GROUP BY c.citation_month_and_year, n.neighborhood_name), RankedNeighborhoods AS (SELECT month, neighborhood_name, total_fine, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY month ORDER BY total_fine DESC NULLS LAST) AS rank_in_month FROM MonthlyFines), TopNeighborhoods AS (SELECT month, neighborhood_name, total_fine FROM RankedNeighborhoods WHERE rank_in_month <= 3) SELECT month, SUM(total_fine) AS total_top_fines, STRING_AGG(neighborhood_name, ', ') AS top_neighborhoods FROM TopNeighborhoods GROUP BY month ORDER BY month NULLS FIRST

question: Return the order IDs, order dates, customer names, product names, category names, total fee amounts, and order ranks for all orders, ordered by the order date and the order rank.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH OrderFees AS ( SELECT t.order_id, SUM(CAST(sf.fee_amount AS REAL)) AS total_fee_amount FROM seller_fees sf JOIN financial_transactions t ON sf.transaction_id = t.transaction_id GROUP BY t.order_id ), RankedOrders AS ( SELECT o.order_id, o.order_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY o.order_date ORDER BY o.order_id) AS order_rank FROM orders o ) SELECT o.order_id, o.order_date, c.customer_name, p.product_name, pc.category_name, COALESCE(of.total_fee_amount, 0) AS total_fee_amount, ro.order_rank FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN products p ON o.product_id = p.product_id JOIN product_categories pc ON p.category_id = pc.category_id LEFT JOIN OrderFees of ON o.order_id = of.order_id JOIN RankedOrders ro ON o.order_id = ro.order_id ORDER BY o.order_date, ro.order_rank
gold_sql.mysql: WITH OrderFees AS (SELECT t.order_id, SUM(CAST(sf.fee_amount AS FLOAT)) AS total_fee_amount FROM seller_fees AS sf JOIN financial_transactions AS t ON sf.transaction_id = t.transaction_id GROUP BY t.order_id), RankedOrders AS (SELECT o.order_id, o.order_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY o.order_date ORDER BY o.order_id) AS order_rank FROM orders AS o) SELECT o.order_id, o.order_date, c.customer_name, p.product_name, pc.category_name, COALESCE(`of`.total_fee_amount, 0) AS total_fee_amount, ro.order_rank FROM orders AS o JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN products AS p ON o.product_id = p.product_id JOIN product_categories AS pc ON p.category_id = pc.category_id LEFT JOIN OrderFees AS `of` ON o.order_id = `of`.order_id JOIN RankedOrders AS ro ON o.order_id = ro.order_id ORDER BY o.order_date, ro.order_rank
gold_sql.postgres: WITH OrderFees AS (SELECT t.order_id, SUM(CAST(sf.fee_amount AS REAL)) AS total_fee_amount FROM seller_fees AS sf JOIN financial_transactions AS t ON sf.transaction_id = t.transaction_id GROUP BY t.order_id), RankedOrders AS (SELECT o.order_id, o.order_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY o.order_date ORDER BY o.order_id NULLS FIRST) AS order_rank FROM orders AS o) SELECT o.order_id, o.order_date, c.customer_name, p.product_name, pc.category_name, COALESCE(of.total_fee_amount, 0) AS total_fee_amount, ro.order_rank FROM orders AS o JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN products AS p ON o.product_id = p.product_id JOIN product_categories AS pc ON p.category_id = pc.category_id LEFT JOIN OrderFees AS of ON o.order_id = of.order_id JOIN RankedOrders AS ro ON o.order_id = ro.order_id ORDER BY o.order_date NULLS FIRST, ro.order_rank NULLS FIRST

question: What is the average number of firearms per 100 inhabitants in 2012 for countries with a population of over 10 million that experienced at least one mass shooting event that year?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT AVG(fs.guns_per_100_inhabitants) AS average_firearms_2012 FROM firearm_statistics fs JOIN population_data pd ON fs.country_id = pd.country_id JOIN mass_shootings ms ON fs.country_id = ms.country_id WHERE fs.year = 2012 AND pd.year = 2012 AND ms.year = 2012 AND CAST(pd.population AS INTEGER) > 10000000 GROUP BY fs.country_id HAVING COUNT(ms.shooting_id) >= 1

question: What are the survey questions, categories, groups, access frequencies, average response values, and the names of the users who most frequently access each survey response?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH AccessFrequency AS ( SELECT r.survey_id, COUNT(al.access_id) AS access_count FROM responses r JOIN access_logs al ON r.response_id = al.response_id GROUP BY r.survey_id ), AverageResponse AS ( SELECT r.survey_id, AVG(r.value) AS average_value FROM responses r GROUP BY r.survey_id ), UserAccessPatterns AS ( SELECT r.survey_id, al.user_id, COUNT(al.access_id) AS user_access_count FROM responses r JOIN access_logs al ON r.response_id = al.response_id GROUP BY r.survey_id, al.user_id ), TopUserAccess AS ( SELECT uap.survey_id, uap.user_id, uap.user_access_count FROM UserAccessPatterns uap INNER JOIN ( SELECT survey_id, MAX(user_access_count) AS max_user_access_count FROM UserAccessPatterns GROUP BY survey_id ) t ON uap.survey_id = t.survey_id AND uap.user_access_count = t.max_user_access_count ) SELECT s.survey_id, s.question_text, c.category_name, g.group_name, af.access_count, ar.average_value, u.user_name AS top_access_user FROM surveys s JOIN categories c ON s.category_id = c.category_id JOIN groups g ON s.group_id = g.group_id JOIN AccessFrequency af ON s.survey_id = af.survey_id JOIN AverageResponse ar ON s.survey_id = ar.survey_id JOIN TopUserAccess tua ON s.survey_id = tua.survey_id JOIN users u ON tua.user_id = u.user_id ORDER BY s.survey_id

question: What is a summary of sensor positions, experiment names, and corresponding sample counts for each trial, excluding samples that failed quality control?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH SampleCounts AS ( SELECT t.trial_id, t.experiment_name, s.sensor_position, COUNT(*) AS sample_count FROM samples sa JOIN sensors s ON sa.sensor_id = s.sensor_id JOIN trials t ON sa.trial_id = t.trial_id WHERE sa.quality_control != 'Failed' GROUP BY t.trial_id, t.experiment_name, s.sensor_position ) SELECT sc.trial_id, GROUP_CONCAT(sc.sensor_position || ' - ' || sc.experiment_name || ': ' || CAST(sc.sample_count AS TEXT), ', ') AS sensor_experiment_sample_summary FROM SampleCounts sc GROUP BY sc.trial_id

question: Find the configuration IDs of the top 10 configurations within each build environment with the most dependencies, ordered by their build time spans in descending order.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ConfigDependencies AS ( SELECT c.config_id, c.build_environment, COUNT(DISTINCT dep.dependency_name) AS dependency_count, MAX(CAST(strftime('%Y-%m-%d', b.build_date) AS DATE)) - MIN(CAST(strftime('%Y-%m-%d', b.build_date) AS DATE)) AS build_time_span_days FROM configurations c LEFT JOIN dependencies dep ON c.config_id = dep.config_id LEFT JOIN build_logs b ON c.config_id = b.config_id GROUP BY c.config_id, c.build_environment ), RankedConfigs AS ( SELECT cd.config_id, cd.build_environment, cd.dependency_count, cd.build_time_span_days, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cd.build_environment ORDER BY cd.dependency_count DESC) AS dependency_rank FROM ConfigDependencies cd ) SELECT rc.config_id FROM RankedConfigs rc WHERE rc.dependency_rank <= 10 ORDER BY rc.build_time_span_days DESC

question: What are the store names, their corresponding franchise names, services offered, customer feedback, cumulative sales over time, and marketing campaigns for all stores, ordered by the store ID?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH StoreFranchiseDetails AS ( SELECT s.store_id, s.name AS store_name, f.franchise_name FROM stores s INNER JOIN store_franchises sf ON s.store_id = sf.store_id INNER JOIN franchises f ON sf.franchise_id = f.franchise_id ), ServiceDetails AS ( SELECT ss.store_id, GROUP_CONCAT(sv.service_name, ', ') AS services_offered FROM store_services ss INNER JOIN services sv ON ss.service_id = sv.service_id GROUP BY ss.store_id ), FeedbackDetails AS ( SELECT fb.store_id, GROUP_CONCAT(fb.customer_name || ' (' || fb.rating || ' stars): ' || fb.feedback_text, ' | ') AS feedback_received FROM feedback fb GROUP BY fb.store_id ), CumulativeSales AS ( SELECT sl.store_id, SUM(sl.quantity_sold * i.price) OVER (PARTITION BY sl.store_id ORDER BY sl.sale_date) AS cumulative_sales FROM sales sl INNER JOIN inventory i ON sl.item_id = i.item_id ), CampaignDetails AS ( SELECT mc.store_id, GROUP_CONCAT(mc.campaign_name || ' (' || mc.start_date || ' to ' || mc.end_date || ')', ', ') AS campaigns FROM marketing_campaigns mc GROUP BY mc.store_id ) SELECT sfd.store_id, sfd.store_name, sfd.franchise_name, sd.services_offered, fd.feedback_received, cs.cumulative_sales, cd.campaigns FROM StoreFranchiseDetails sfd LEFT JOIN ServiceDetails sd ON sfd.store_id = sd.store_id LEFT JOIN FeedbackDetails fd ON sfd.store_id = fd.store_id LEFT JOIN CumulativeSales cs ON sfd.store_id = cs.store_id LEFT JOIN CampaignDetails cd ON sfd.store_id = cd.store_id ORDER BY sfd.store_id

question: Hey, can you show me the names of the top three countries with the most registrations, along with their average ages? I'd love to know which countries they are and what their average ages are!

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH CountryRegistrations AS ( SELECT a.country_id, COUNT(*) AS registration_count FROM analytics a GROUP BY a.country_id ORDER BY registration_count DESC LIMIT 3 ), CountryAges AS ( SELECT a.country_id, AVG((CAST(SUBSTR(ag.age_range, 1, INSTR(ag.age_range, '-') - 1) AS INTEGER) + CAST(SUBSTR(ag.age_range, INSTR(ag.age_range, '-') + 1) AS INTEGER)) / 2.0) AS average_age FROM analytics a JOIN ages ag ON a.age_id = ag.age_id WHERE a.country_id IN (SELECT country_id FROM CountryRegistrations) GROUP BY a.country_id ) SELECT c.country_name, ca.average_age FROM CountryAges ca JOIN countries c ON ca.country_id = c.country_id

question: What are the dates and results of the simulations' analyses, and when were the corresponding visualizations created, including their settings? Additionally, provide the numeric representation of these dates.

question: Hey! I'm looking for information on countries in South Asia. Could you tell me the names of these countries, their official languages, capital cities, and the population of each capital? I'd love to see the list arranged alphabetically by country name.

gold_sql.mysql: SELECT c.country_name, GROUP_CONCAT(l.language_name SEPARATOR ',') AS official_languages, cap.capital_name, cap.population FROM countries AS c LEFT JOIN languages AS l ON c.country_id = l.country_id AND l.is_official = 1 LEFT JOIN capitals AS cap ON c.country_id = cap.country_id WHERE c.region = 'South Asia' GROUP BY c.country_name, cap.capital_name, cap.population ORDER BY c.country_name
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT c.country_name, STRING_AGG(l.language_name, ',') AS official_languages, cap.capital_name, cap.population FROM countries AS c LEFT JOIN languages AS l ON c.country_id = l.country_id AND l.is_official = 1 LEFT JOIN capitals AS cap ON c.country_id = cap.country_id WHERE c.region = 'South Asia' GROUP BY c.country_name, cap.capital_name, cap.population ORDER BY c.country_name NULLS FIRST

question: Could you tell me the top 3 most accessed prizes, including the names of the associated laureates, the motivations behind the awards, the number of times they were accessed, and their average access durations?

gold_sql.mysql: WITH AccessSummary AS (SELECT prize_id, COUNT(access_id) AS access_count, AVG(access_duration) AS avg_access_duration FROM access_logs GROUP BY prize_id ORDER BY access_count DESC LIMIT 3) SELECT LPD.prize_id, LPD.full_name AS laureate_name, LPD.motivation, ASD.access_count, ASD.avg_access_duration FROM AccessSummary AS ASD JOIN laureate_prizes AS LP ON ASD.prize_id = LP.prize_id JOIN laureates AS L ON LP.laureate_id = L.laureate_id JOIN (SELECT prize_id, GROUP_CONCAT(full_name SEPARATOR ', ') AS full_name, motivation FROM (SELECT LP.prize_id, L.full_name, LP.motivation FROM laureate_prizes AS LP JOIN laureates AS L ON LP.laureate_id = L.laureate_id) AS LPD GROUP BY prize_id, motivation) AS LPD ON ASD.prize_id = LPD.prize_id ORDER BY ASD.access_count DESC

question: Identify the occupation and education level combinations where seasoned professionals, with more than 10 years of experience on average, have spent more than 5 years in the workforce, and determine the average work experience and average salary for these groups, ranking them by their wealth of experience and highest average salary.
external_knowledge: A "seasoned professional" refers to someone with a significant amount of work experience, typically more than 10 years; Average salary is a rough estimate and may not accurately represent individual salaries; More than 5 years in the workforce means the individual has at least 6 years of work experience.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT o.occupation_name, e.education_level, AVG(i.work_experience_years) AS average_work_experience, AVG(CAST(s.salary_range_high AS INTEGER) - CAST(s.salary_range_low AS INTEGER)) / 2 AS average_salary FROM individuals i INNER JOIN occupations o ON i.occupation_id = o.occupation_id INNER JOIN education_levels e ON i.education_id = e.education_id INNER JOIN salary_classes s ON i.salary_class_id = s.salary_class_id WHERE i.work_experience_years > 5 GROUP BY o.occupation_name, e.education_level HAVING AVG(i.work_experience_years) > 10 ORDER BY average_work_experience DESC, average_salary DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT o.occupation_name, e.education_level, AVG(i.work_experience_years) AS average_work_experience, AVG(CAST(s.salary_range_high AS SIGNED) - CAST(s.salary_range_low AS SIGNED)) / 2 AS average_salary FROM individuals AS i INNER JOIN occupations AS o ON i.occupation_id = o.occupation_id INNER JOIN education_levels AS e ON i.education_id = e.education_id INNER JOIN salary_classes AS s ON i.salary_class_id = s.salary_class_id WHERE i.work_experience_years > 5 GROUP BY o.occupation_name, e.education_level HAVING AVG(i.work_experience_years) > 10 ORDER BY average_work_experience DESC, average_salary DESC
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT o.occupation_name, e.education_level, AVG(i.work_experience_years) AS average_work_experience, AVG(CAST(s.salary_range_high AS INT) - CAST(s.salary_range_low AS INT)) / NULLIF(2, 0) AS average_salary FROM individuals AS i INNER JOIN occupations AS o ON i.occupation_id = o.occupation_id INNER JOIN education_levels AS e ON i.education_id = e.education_id INNER JOIN salary_classes AS s ON i.salary_class_id = s.salary_class_id WHERE i.work_experience_years > 5 GROUP BY o.occupation_name, e.education_level HAVING AVG(i.work_experience_years) > 10 ORDER BY average_work_experience DESC NULLS LAST, average_salary DESC NULLS LAST

question: What is a comprehensive report of all outbreaks, including their etiology names, locations, cities, states, countries, total cases, outbreak years, start dates, end dates, statuses, contributing factors, numbers of confirmed cases, suspected cases, hospitalized cases, and cumulative cases by outbreak year, ordered by outbreak year and outbreak ID?
