gold_sql.sqlite: WITH OutbreakDetails AS ( SELECT o.outbreak_id, e.name AS etiology_name, l.location_name, l.city, l.state, l.country, o.total_cases, o.outbreak_year, o.start_date, o.end_date, o.status FROM outbreaks o INNER JOIN locations l ON o.location_id = l.location_id INNER JOIN etiologies e ON o.etiology_id = e.etiology_id ), OutbreakFactors AS ( SELECT of.outbreak_id, GROUP_CONCAT(f.factor_description, ', ') AS contributing_factors FROM outbreak_factors of INNER JOIN factors f ON of.factor_id = f.factor_id GROUP BY of.outbreak_id ), CaseStatus AS ( SELECT c.outbreak_id, SUM(CASE WHEN c.case_status = 'confirmed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS confirmed_cases, SUM(CASE WHEN c.case_status = 'suspected' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS suspected_cases, SUM(c.hospitalized) AS hospitalized_cases FROM cases c GROUP BY c.outbreak_id ), CumulativeCases AS ( SELECT o.outbreak_year, o.outbreak_id, SUM(o.total_cases) OVER (PARTITION BY o.outbreak_year ORDER BY o.outbreak_id) AS cumulative_cases FROM OutbreakDetails o ) SELECT od.outbreak_id, od.etiology_name, od.location_name, od.city, od.state, od.country, od.total_cases, od.outbreak_year, od.start_date, od.end_date, od.status, of.contributing_factors, cs.confirmed_cases, cs.suspected_cases, cs.hospitalized_cases, cc.cumulative_cases FROM OutbreakDetails od LEFT JOIN OutbreakFactors of ON od.outbreak_id = of.outbreak_id LEFT JOIN CaseStatus cs ON od.outbreak_id = cs.outbreak_id LEFT JOIN CumulativeCases cc ON od.outbreak_id = cc.outbreak_id ORDER BY od.outbreak_year, od.outbreak_id
gold_sql.mysql: WITH OutbreakDetails AS (SELECT o.outbreak_id, e.name AS etiology_name, l.location_name, l.city, l.state, l.country, o.total_cases, o.outbreak_year, o.start_date, o.end_date, o.status FROM outbreaks AS o INNER JOIN locations AS l ON o.location_id = l.location_id INNER JOIN etiologies AS e ON o.etiology_id = e.etiology_id), OutbreakFactors AS (SELECT `of`.outbreak_id, GROUP_CONCAT(f.factor_description SEPARATOR ', ') AS contributing_factors FROM outbreak_factors AS `of` INNER JOIN factors AS f ON `of`.factor_id = f.factor_id GROUP BY `of`.outbreak_id), CaseStatus AS (SELECT c.outbreak_id, SUM(CASE WHEN c.case_status = 'confirmed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS confirmed_cases, SUM(CASE WHEN c.case_status = 'suspected' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS suspected_cases, SUM(c.hospitalized) AS hospitalized_cases FROM cases AS c GROUP BY c.outbreak_id), CumulativeCases AS (SELECT o.outbreak_year, o.outbreak_id, SUM(o.total_cases) OVER (PARTITION BY o.outbreak_year ORDER BY o.outbreak_id) AS cumulative_cases FROM OutbreakDetails AS o) SELECT od.outbreak_id, od.etiology_name, od.location_name, od.city, od.state, od.country, od.total_cases, od.outbreak_year, od.start_date, od.end_date, od.status, `of`.contributing_factors, cs.confirmed_cases, cs.suspected_cases, cs.hospitalized_cases, cc.cumulative_cases FROM OutbreakDetails AS od LEFT JOIN OutbreakFactors AS `of` ON od.outbreak_id = `of`.outbreak_id LEFT JOIN CaseStatus AS cs ON od.outbreak_id = cs.outbreak_id LEFT JOIN CumulativeCases AS cc ON od.outbreak_id = cc.outbreak_id ORDER BY od.outbreak_year, od.outbreak_id
gold_sql.postgres: WITH OutbreakDetails AS (SELECT o.outbreak_id, e.name AS etiology_name, l.location_name, l.city, l.state, l.country, o.total_cases, o.outbreak_year, o.start_date, o.end_date, o.status FROM outbreaks AS o INNER JOIN locations AS l ON o.location_id = l.location_id INNER JOIN etiologies AS e ON o.etiology_id = e.etiology_id), OutbreakFactors AS (SELECT of.outbreak_id, STRING_AGG(f.factor_description, ', ') AS contributing_factors FROM outbreak_factors AS of INNER JOIN factors AS f ON of.factor_id = f.factor_id GROUP BY of.outbreak_id), CaseStatus AS (SELECT c.outbreak_id, SUM(CASE WHEN c.case_status = 'confirmed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS confirmed_cases, SUM(CASE WHEN c.case_status = 'suspected' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS suspected_cases, SUM(c.hospitalized) AS hospitalized_cases FROM cases AS c GROUP BY c.outbreak_id), CumulativeCases AS (SELECT o.outbreak_year, o.outbreak_id, SUM(o.total_cases) OVER (PARTITION BY o.outbreak_year ORDER BY o.outbreak_id NULLS FIRST) AS cumulative_cases FROM OutbreakDetails AS o) SELECT od.outbreak_id, od.etiology_name, od.location_name, od.city, od.state, od.country, od.total_cases, od.outbreak_year, od.start_date, od.end_date, od.status, of.contributing_factors, cs.confirmed_cases, cs.suspected_cases, cs.hospitalized_cases, cc.cumulative_cases FROM OutbreakDetails AS od LEFT JOIN OutbreakFactors AS of ON od.outbreak_id = of.outbreak_id LEFT JOIN CaseStatus AS cs ON od.outbreak_id = cs.outbreak_id LEFT JOIN CumulativeCases AS cc ON od.outbreak_id = cc.outbreak_id ORDER BY od.outbreak_year NULLS FIRST, od.outbreak_id NULLS FIRST

question: I want to find out the names and owners of all files that are smaller than 5MB and have been accessed at least once, along with the total size of these files and the number of times each file has been accessed.

gold_sql.postgres: SELECT f.file_name, u.user_name AS owner_name, SUM(CAST(f.file_size AS INT)) AS total_file_size, COUNT(fal.log_id) AS total_accesses FROM files AS f JOIN users AS u ON f.owner_id = u.user_id JOIN file_access_logs AS fal ON f.file_id = fal.file_id WHERE CAST(f.file_size AS INT) < 5242880 GROUP BY f.file_name, u.user_name

question: Unpack the winds of time and find the identifiers and latest whispers from each weather beacon, revealing their recent breaths (wind speed), gleams (radiation), and warmth (temperature).

gold_sql.mysql: SELECT w.station_id, w.wind_speed AS `Recent Breaths`, w.radiation AS `Gleams`, w.temperature AS `Warmth` FROM weather_data AS w JOIN (SELECT station_id, MAX(prediction_date) AS latest_date FROM weather_data GROUP BY station_id) AS latest ON w.station_id = latest.station_id AND w.prediction_date = latest.latest_date ORDER BY w.station_id
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT w.station_id, w.wind_speed AS "Recent Breaths", w.radiation AS "Gleams", w.temperature AS "Warmth" FROM weather_data AS w JOIN (SELECT station_id, MAX(prediction_date) AS latest_date FROM weather_data GROUP BY station_id) AS latest ON w.station_id = latest.station_id AND w.prediction_date = latest.latest_date ORDER BY w.station_id NULLS FIRST

question: I want to know the names and identification numbers of all fire stations, along with their aggregated water safety check results and bulk water check results, for stations that have had at least one water safety or bulk water check that resulted in either 'safe' or 'unsafe'.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT fs.station_id, fs.name, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ws.check_result) AS water_safety_results, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT bw.check_result) AS bulk_water_results FROM fire_stations fs LEFT JOIN water_safety ws ON fs.station_id = ws.station_id LEFT JOIN bulk_water bw ON fs.station_id = bw.station_id WHERE (ws.check_result IN ('unsafe', 'safe') OR bw.check_result IN ('unsafe', 'safe')) GROUP BY fs.station_id, fs.name HAVING COUNT(ws.check_id) > 0 OR COUNT(bw.check_id) > 0
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT fs.station_id, fs.name, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ws.check_result SEPARATOR ',') AS water_safety_results, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT bw.check_result SEPARATOR ',') AS bulk_water_results FROM fire_stations AS fs LEFT JOIN water_safety AS ws ON fs.station_id = ws.station_id LEFT JOIN bulk_water AS bw ON fs.station_id = bw.station_id WHERE (ws.check_result IN ('unsafe', 'safe') OR bw.check_result IN ('unsafe', 'safe')) GROUP BY fs.station_id, fs.name HAVING COUNT(ws.check_id) > 0 OR COUNT(bw.check_id) > 0
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT fs.station_id, fs.name, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT ws.check_result, ',') AS water_safety_results, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT bw.check_result, ',') AS bulk_water_results FROM fire_stations AS fs LEFT JOIN water_safety AS ws ON fs.station_id = ws.station_id LEFT JOIN bulk_water AS bw ON fs.station_id = bw.station_id WHERE (ws.check_result IN ('unsafe', 'safe') OR bw.check_result IN ('unsafe', 'safe')) GROUP BY fs.station_id, fs.name HAVING COUNT(ws.check_id) > 0 OR COUNT(bw.check_id) > 0

question: What are the names, average hit percentages, and injury details for players on teams coached by coach 0, listed from highest to lowest average hit percentage?

gold_sql.mysql: SELECT p.full_name, AVG(ps.hit_percentage) AS average_hit_percentage, GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(pi.injury_date, ', ', pi.injury_type, ', ', pi.status) SEPARATOR '; ') AS injury_details FROM players AS p INNER JOIN player_statistics AS ps ON p.player_id = ps.player_id LEFT JOIN player_injuries AS pi ON p.player_id = pi.player_id INNER JOIN teams AS t ON p.team_id = t.team_id WHERE t.coach_id = 0 GROUP BY p.player_id, p.full_name ORDER BY average_hit_percentage DESC
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT p.full_name, AVG(ps.hit_percentage) AS average_hit_percentage, STRING_AGG(pi.injury_date || ', ' || pi.injury_type || ', ' || pi.status, '; ') AS injury_details FROM players AS p INNER JOIN player_statistics AS ps ON p.player_id = ps.player_id LEFT JOIN player_injuries AS pi ON p.player_id = pi.player_id INNER JOIN teams AS t ON p.team_id = t.team_id WHERE t.coach_id = 0 GROUP BY p.player_id, p.full_name ORDER BY average_hit_percentage DESC NULLS LAST

question: Gather the names of employees, the total number of days they have taken off this year, and their latest performance ratings, ensuring that all employees are included, even if they have no time off or performance evaluation records.
external_knowledge:
- "latest performance evaluation" refers to the most recent evaluation date for each employee;
- "total days off in the current year" means the sum of days off taken between January 1 and the current date of the year.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH LatestPerformanceEvaluations AS ( SELECT emp_id, MAX(eval_date) AS max_eval_date FROM performance_evaluations GROUP BY emp_id ), LatestEvalDetails AS ( SELECT p.emp_id, p.rating FROM performance_evaluations p INNER JOIN LatestPerformanceEvaluations lpe ON p.emp_id = lpe.emp_id AND p.eval_date = lpe.max_eval_date ), RecentTimeOff AS ( SELECT emp_id, SUM(num_days) AS total_days_off FROM time_off_requests WHERE strftime('%Y', start_date) = strftime('%Y', 'now') GROUP BY emp_id ) SELECT e.emp_name, COALESCE(rt.total_days_off, 0) AS total_days_off, le.rating FROM employees e LEFT JOIN RecentTimeOff rt ON e.emp_id = rt.emp_id LEFT JOIN LatestEvalDetails le ON e.emp_id = le.emp_id

question: Can you list the project leaders, their respective projects, and the tools they are using, along with the tools' versions, sorted from the newest to the oldest version?
external_knowledge:
- "Project leaders" refer to the individuals responsible for overseeing the projects.
- "Tools" can be software, hardware, or any other resources used to accomplish tasks within the project.
- "Versions" refer to different iterations of these tools, often denoted by numerical values.
- The term "newest to the oldest version" means sorting versions numerically from highest to lowest.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT u.user_name AS "Project Leader", p.project_name AS "Project Name", t.tool_name AS "Tool Name", t.version AS "Tool Version" FROM users u INNER JOIN projects p ON u.user_id = p.project_leader_id INNER JOIN project_tools pt ON p.project_id = pt.project_id INNER JOIN tools t ON pt.tool_id = t.tool_id ORDER BY CAST(REPLACE(t.version, '.', '') AS INTEGER) DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT u.user_name AS `Project Leader`, p.project_name AS `Project Name`, t.tool_name AS `Tool Name`, t.version AS `Tool Version` FROM users AS u INNER JOIN projects AS p ON u.user_id = p.project_leader_id INNER JOIN project_tools AS pt ON p.project_id = pt.project_id INNER JOIN tools AS t ON pt.tool_id = t.tool_id ORDER BY CAST(REPLACE(t.version, '.', '') AS SIGNED) DESC
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT u.user_name AS "Project Leader", p.project_name AS "Project Name", t.tool_name AS "Tool Name", t.version AS "Tool Version" FROM users AS u INNER JOIN projects AS p ON u.user_id = p.project_leader_id INNER JOIN project_tools AS pt ON p.project_id = pt.project_id INNER JOIN tools AS t ON pt.tool_id = t.tool_id ORDER BY CAST(REPLACE(t.version, '.', '') AS INT) DESC NULLS LAST

question: For high-quality data where the air temperature exceeds 20 degrees Celsius, return the geographic area, the hour of the day, the average air temperature, and the average solar irradiation, ordered by geographic area and hour of the day.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT l.geographic_area, STRFTIME('%H', e.time) AS hour_of_day, AVG(e.air_temperature_celsius) AS avg_air_temperature, AVG(e.solar_irradiation_w_m2) AS avg_solar_irradiation FROM environmental_data e INNER JOIN monitoring_stations m ON e.station_id = m.station_id INNER JOIN locations l ON m.location_id = l.location_id WHERE e.data_quality = 'high' GROUP BY l.geographic_area, STRFTIME('%H', e.time) HAVING AVG(e.air_temperature_celsius) > 20 ORDER BY l.geographic_area, hour_of_day
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT l.geographic_area, DATE_FORMAT(CAST(e.time AS DATETIME), '%H') AS hour_of_day, AVG(e.air_temperature_celsius) AS avg_air_temperature, AVG(e.solar_irradiation_w_m2) AS avg_solar_irradiation FROM environmental_data AS e INNER JOIN monitoring_stations AS m ON e.station_id = m.station_id INNER JOIN locations AS l ON m.location_id = l.location_id WHERE e.data_quality = 'high' GROUP BY l.geographic_area, DATE_FORMAT(CAST(e.time AS DATETIME), '%H') HAVING AVG(e.air_temperature_celsius) > 20 ORDER BY l.geographic_area, hour_of_day
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT l.geographic_area, TO_CHAR(CAST(e.time AS TIMESTAMP), 'HH24') AS hour_of_day, AVG(e.air_temperature_celsius) AS avg_air_temperature, AVG(e.solar_irradiation_w_m2) AS avg_solar_irradiation FROM environmental_data AS e INNER JOIN monitoring_stations AS m ON e.station_id = m.station_id INNER JOIN locations AS l ON m.location_id = l.location_id WHERE e.data_quality = 'high' GROUP BY l.geographic_area, TO_CHAR(CAST(e.time AS TIMESTAMP), 'HH24') HAVING AVG(e.air_temperature_celsius) > 20 ORDER BY l.geographic_area NULLS FIRST, hour_of_day NULLS FIRST

question: Hey! Can you help me figure out the average measurement value for women in the adult age group? I want to make sure there are multiple measurements to get a good average.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT bs.gender, bs.age_group, AVG(CAST(SUBSTR(bs.measurement_value, 1, INSTR(bs.measurement_value, 'c') - 1) AS REAL)) AS avg_measurement_value FROM body_measurements bs WHERE bs.gender = 'Women' AND bs.age_group = 'Adult' GROUP BY bs.gender, bs.age_group HAVING COUNT(bs.measurement_id) > 1
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT bs.gender, bs.age_group, AVG(CAST(SUBSTRING(bs.measurement_value, 1, LOCATE('c', bs.measurement_value) - 1) AS FLOAT)) AS avg_measurement_value FROM body_measurements AS bs WHERE bs.gender = 'Women' AND bs.age_group = 'Adult' GROUP BY bs.gender, bs.age_group HAVING COUNT(bs.measurement_id) > 1
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT bs.gender, bs.age_group, AVG(CAST(SUBSTRING(bs.measurement_value FROM 1 FOR STRPOS(bs.measurement_value, 'c') - 1) AS REAL)) AS avg_measurement_value FROM body_measurements AS bs WHERE bs.gender = 'Women' AND bs.age_group = 'Adult' GROUP BY bs.gender, bs.age_group HAVING COUNT(bs.measurement_id) > 1

question: Which setting had the highest combined count of cases, active staff, and active non-staff members in April 2023?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH CaseCounts AS ( SELECT c.setting_id, COUNT(*) AS case_count FROM cases c WHERE strftime('%Y-%m', c.case_date) = '2023-04' GROUP BY c.setting_id ), StaffCounts AS ( SELECT st.setting_id, COUNT(*) AS staff_count FROM staff st WHERE st.status = 'active' GROUP BY st.setting_id ), NonStaffCounts AS ( SELECT ns.setting_id, COUNT(*) AS non_staff_count FROM non_staff ns WHERE ns.status = 'active' GROUP BY ns.setting_id ) SELECT s.setting_id, COALESCE(c.case_count, 0) + COALESCE(st.staff_count, 0) + COALESCE(ns.non_staff_count, 0) AS combined_count FROM settings s LEFT JOIN CaseCounts c ON s.setting_id = c.setting_id LEFT JOIN StaffCounts st ON s.setting_id = st.setting_id LEFT JOIN NonStaffCounts ns ON s.setting_id = ns.setting_id ORDER BY combined_count DESC LIMIT 1

gold_sql.postgres: WITH CaseCounts AS (SELECT c.setting_id, COUNT(*) AS case_count FROM cases AS c WHERE TO_CHAR(CAST(c.case_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY-MM') = '2023-04' GROUP BY c.setting_id), StaffCounts AS (SELECT st.setting_id, COUNT(*) AS staff_count FROM staff AS st WHERE st.status = 'active' GROUP BY st.setting_id), NonStaffCounts AS (SELECT ns.setting_id, COUNT(*) AS non_staff_count FROM non_staff AS ns WHERE ns.status = 'active' GROUP BY ns.setting_id) SELECT s.setting_id, COALESCE(c.case_count, 0) + COALESCE(st.staff_count, 0) + COALESCE(ns.non_staff_count, 0) AS combined_count FROM settings AS s LEFT JOIN CaseCounts AS c ON s.setting_id = c.setting_id LEFT JOIN StaffCounts AS st ON s.setting_id = st.setting_id LEFT JOIN NonStaffCounts AS ns ON s.setting_id = ns.setting_id ORDER BY combined_count DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1

question:
**User**: I need to generate a report on fees.
**Assistant**: What information would you like to include in the report?
**User**: I want to see the fee details, payment details, credit details, and any remarks for each fee.
**Assistant**: What specific details would you like to see under each category?
**User**: For fee details, I'd like to see the fee ID, fee type name, fee description, amount, paid to date, credit amount, credit remark, department name, head of department, contact email, and phone number. For payment details, I just need the total paid amount. For credit details, the total credited amount would be great. And for remarks, please include any remarks associated with each fee.
**Assistant**: How would you like to arrange the report?
**User**: I'd like it sorted by fee ID.
**Assistant**: Is there anything else you'd like to include or any specific conditions you'd like to apply?
**User**: No, that's all for now.
**Assistant**: Okay, I'll help you generate the report based on your requirements.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH FeeDetails AS ( SELECT f.fee_id AS "Fee ID", ft.fee_type_name AS "Fee Type Name", f.description AS "Fee Description", f.amount AS "Amount", f.paid_to_date AS "Paid to Date", f.credit_amount AS "Credit Amount", f.credit_remark AS "Credit Remark", d.dept_name AS "Department Name", d.head_of_department AS "Head of Department", d.contact_email AS "Contact Email", d.phone_number AS "Phone Number" FROM fees f INNER JOIN fee_types ft ON f.fee_type_id = ft.fee_type_id INNER JOIN departments d ON f.dept_id = d.dept_id ), PaymentDetails AS ( SELECT fp.fee_id AS "Fee ID", SUM(CAST(fp.payment_amount AS REAL)) AS "Total Paid" FROM fee_payments fp WHERE fp.payment_status = 'successful' GROUP BY fp.fee_id ), CreditDetails AS ( SELECT fc.fee_id AS "Fee ID", SUM(CAST(fc.credit_amount AS REAL)) AS "Total Credited" FROM fee_credits fc GROUP BY fc.fee_id ), RemarkDetails AS ( SELECT fr.fee_id AS "Fee ID", GROUP_CONCAT(fr.remark_text) AS "Remarks" FROM fee_remarks fr GROUP BY fr.fee_id ) SELECT fd."Fee ID", fd."Fee Type Name", fd."Fee Description", fd."Amount", COALESCE(pd."Total Paid", 0) AS "Total Paid", COALESCE(cd."Total Credited", 0) AS "Total Credited", fd."Paid to Date", fd."Credit Amount", fd."Credit Remark", fd."Department Name", fd."Head of Department", fd."Contact Email", fd."Phone Number", rd."Remarks" FROM FeeDetails fd LEFT JOIN PaymentDetails pd ON fd."Fee ID" = pd."Fee ID" LEFT JOIN CreditDetails cd ON fd."Fee ID" = cd."Fee ID" LEFT JOIN RemarkDetails rd ON fd."Fee ID" = rd."Fee ID" ORDER BY fd."Fee ID"
gold_sql.mysql: WITH FeeDetails AS (SELECT f.fee_id AS `Fee ID`, ft.fee_type_name AS `Fee Type Name`, f.description AS `Fee Description`, f.amount AS `Amount`, f.paid_to_date AS `Paid to Date`, f.credit_amount AS `Credit Amount`, f.credit_remark AS `Credit Remark`, d.dept_name AS `Department Name`, d.head_of_department AS `Head of Department`, d.contact_email AS `Contact Email`, d.phone_number AS `Phone Number` FROM fees AS f INNER JOIN fee_types AS ft ON f.fee_type_id = ft.fee_type_id INNER JOIN departments AS d ON f.dept_id = d.dept_id), PaymentDetails AS (SELECT fp.fee_id AS `Fee ID`, SUM(CAST(fp.payment_amount AS FLOAT)) AS `Total Paid` FROM fee_payments AS fp WHERE fp.payment_status = 'successful' GROUP BY fp.fee_id), CreditDetails AS (SELECT fc.fee_id AS `Fee ID`, SUM(CAST(fc.credit_amount AS FLOAT)) AS `Total Credited` FROM fee_credits AS fc GROUP BY fc.fee_id), RemarkDetails AS (SELECT fr.fee_id AS `Fee ID`, GROUP_CONCAT(fr.remark_text SEPARATOR ',') AS `Remarks` FROM fee_remarks AS fr GROUP BY fr.fee_id) SELECT fd.`Fee ID`, fd.`Fee Type Name`, fd.`Fee Description`, fd.`Amount`, COALESCE(pd.`Total Paid`, 0) AS `Total Paid`, COALESCE(cd.`Total Credited`, 0) AS `Total Credited`, fd.`Paid to Date`, fd.`Credit Amount`, fd.`Credit Remark`, fd.`Department Name`, fd.`Head of Department`, fd.`Contact Email`, fd.`Phone Number`, rd.`Remarks` FROM FeeDetails AS fd LEFT JOIN PaymentDetails AS pd ON fd.`Fee ID` = pd.`Fee ID` LEFT JOIN CreditDetails AS cd ON fd.`Fee ID` = cd.`Fee ID` LEFT JOIN RemarkDetails AS rd ON fd.`Fee ID` = rd.`Fee ID` ORDER BY fd.`Fee ID`
gold_sql.postgres: WITH FeeDetails AS (SELECT f.fee_id AS "Fee ID", ft.fee_type_name AS "Fee Type Name", f.description AS "Fee Description", f.amount AS "Amount", f.paid_to_date AS "Paid to Date", f.credit_amount AS "Credit Amount", f.credit_remark AS "Credit Remark", d.dept_name AS "Department Name", d.head_of_department AS "Head of Department", d.contact_email AS "Contact Email", d.phone_number AS "Phone Number" FROM fees AS f INNER JOIN fee_types AS ft ON f.fee_type_id = ft.fee_type_id INNER JOIN departments AS d ON f.dept_id = d.dept_id), PaymentDetails AS (SELECT fp.fee_id AS "Fee ID", SUM(CAST(fp.payment_amount AS REAL)) AS "Total Paid" FROM fee_payments AS fp WHERE fp.payment_status = 'successful' GROUP BY fp.fee_id), CreditDetails AS (SELECT fc.fee_id AS "Fee ID", SUM(CAST(fc.credit_amount AS REAL)) AS "Total Credited" FROM fee_credits AS fc GROUP BY fc.fee_id), RemarkDetails AS (SELECT fr.fee_id AS "Fee ID", STRING_AGG(fr.remark_text, ',') AS "Remarks" FROM fee_remarks AS fr GROUP BY fr.fee_id) SELECT fd."Fee ID", fd."Fee Type Name", fd."Fee Description", fd."Amount", COALESCE(pd."Total Paid", 0) AS "Total Paid", COALESCE(cd."Total Credited", 0) AS "Total Credited", fd."Paid to Date", fd."Credit Amount", fd."Credit Remark", fd."Department Name", fd."Head of Department", fd."Contact Email", fd."Phone Number", rd."Remarks" FROM FeeDetails AS fd LEFT JOIN PaymentDetails AS pd ON fd."Fee ID" = pd."Fee ID" LEFT JOIN CreditDetails AS cd ON fd."Fee ID" = cd."Fee ID" LEFT JOIN RemarkDetails AS rd ON fd."Fee ID" = rd."Fee ID" ORDER BY fd."Fee ID" NULLS FIRST

question:
**User**: I want to find the best-performing team in a specific week.
**Assistant**: Sure, which week and month are you interested in?
**User**: The first week of October 2023.
**Assistant**: Got it. Do you have any specific criteria for ranking the teams, such as their win percentage or rank?
**User**: I want the teams with an average win percentage greater than 0.8 and a weekly rank of 5 or lower.
**Assistant**: Understood. What information would you like to know about these teams? For example, their ID, average win percentage, or total points scored?
**User**: I need the team ID, average win percentage, and total points scored (both the team's score and the opponent's score combined).
**Assistant**: Should I limit the results to the top 1 team based on the total points scored?
**User**: Yes, just the top 1 team.
**Assistant**: Is there anything else you need?
**User**: No, that's all.
**Assistant**: OK, I will help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT tp.team_id, AVG(tp.avg_win_pct) AS avg_win_percentage, SUM(g.score + g.opponent_score) AS total_points FROM team_performance tp JOIN games g ON tp.team_id = g.team_id WHERE tp.week_number = 1 AND strftime('%Y-%m', g.game_date) = '2023-10' AND tp.rank_week <= 5 GROUP BY tp.team_id HAVING AVG(tp.avg_win_pct) > 0.8 ORDER BY total_points DESC LIMIT 1

question: Could you provide a summary of the top-performing team in the most recent week, including the team's ID and average win percentage, the statistics of one player from that team, and the title of one recent news article related to the team?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RecentWeek AS ( SELECT MAX(week_number) AS most_recent_week FROM team_performance ), TopPerformingTeam AS ( SELECT team_id, AVG(avg_win_pct) AS avg_win_pct FROM team_performance WHERE week_number = (SELECT most_recent_week FROM RecentWeek) GROUP BY team_id ORDER BY avg_win_pct DESC LIMIT 1 ), RecentPlayerStats AS ( SELECT ps.player_id, p.player_name, ps.game_id, ps.points, ps.assists, ps.rebounds, ps.steals, ps.blocks FROM player_statistics ps INNER JOIN players p ON ps.player_id = p.player_id WHERE p.team_id = (SELECT team_id FROM TopPerformingTeam) LIMIT 1 ), RecentNewsArticles AS ( SELECT article_title FROM news_articles WHERE team_id = (SELECT team_id FROM TopPerformingTeam) ORDER BY article_date DESC LIMIT 1 ) SELECT ( SELECT 'Top-Performing Team ID: ' || team_id || ', Average Win Percentage: ' || CAST(avg_win_pct AS TEXT) FROM TopPerformingTeam ) || ( SELECT ', Player Stats - Player: ' || player_name || ', Points: ' || CAST(points AS TEXT) || ', Assists: ' || CAST(assists AS TEXT) || ', Rebounds: ' || CAST(rebounds AS TEXT) || ', Steals: ' || CAST(steals AS TEXT) || ', Blocks: ' || CAST(blocks AS TEXT) FROM RecentPlayerStats ) || ( SELECT ', Recent News - Title: ' || article_title FROM RecentNewsArticles ) AS Analysis

question: What is the overall energy efficiency of the solar panels after their most recent maintenance during the year 2023?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH LastMaintenance AS ( SELECT panel_id, MAX(timestamp) AS last_maintenance FROM maintenance GROUP BY panel_id ), FilteredAnalytics AS ( SELECT a.panel_id, a.timestamp, (a.energy_production + a.energy_consumption) / 2 AS energy_efficiency FROM analytics a JOIN LastMaintenance lm ON a.panel_id = lm.panel_id AND a.timestamp > lm.last_maintenance WHERE strftime('%Y', a.timestamp) = '2023' ) SELECT AVG(energy_efficiency) AS total_energy_efficiency FROM FilteredAnalytics

question: Find all patients who have experienced seizures, and return their age, sex, ethnicity, the number of seizures, mean seizure length, and a list of prescribed medications, grouped by patient demographics and seizure characteristics, and ordered by patient ID.

question: Hey, could you show me the symbols of stocks with a total trading volume of over a million, along with their average volume-weighted prices, listed from the highest to the lowest average volume-weighted price?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT s.stock_symbol, AVG(CAST(sd.volume_weighted_average_price AS REAL)) AS avg_vwap FROM stocks s JOIN stock_data sd ON s.stock_id = sd.stock_id GROUP BY s.stock_id, s.stock_symbol HAVING SUM(CAST(sd.volume AS INTEGER)) > 1000000 ORDER BY avg_vwap DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT s.stock_symbol, AVG(CAST(sd.volume_weighted_average_price AS FLOAT)) AS avg_vwap FROM stocks AS s JOIN stock_data AS sd ON s.stock_id = sd.stock_id GROUP BY s.stock_id, s.stock_symbol HAVING SUM(CAST(sd.volume AS SIGNED)) > 1000000 ORDER BY avg_vwap DESC

question: What is the average sentiment of the seasons, as reflected by the user ratings, where each season must have at least two voices of wisdom?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT s.season_name, AVG(uf.rating) AS average_sentiment FROM user_feedback uf JOIN seasons s ON (strftime('%m', uf.feedback_date) BETWEEN '01' AND '03' AND s.season_name = 'Spring') OR (strftime('%m', uf.feedback_date) BETWEEN '04' AND '06' AND s.season_name = 'Summer') OR (strftime('%m', uf.feedback_date) BETWEEN '07' AND '09' AND s.season_name = 'Autumn') OR (strftime('%m', uf.feedback_date) BETWEEN '10' AND '12' AND s.season_name = 'Winter') GROUP BY s.season_name HAVING COUNT(uf.feedback_id) >= 2

question: Can you please get a list of all suppliers along with their total orders, on-time delivery percentages, and quality control pass percentages, and rank them in descending order of on-time delivery percentages and then quality control pass percentages, so I can see which suppliers have the best on-time delivery and quality control records?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH SupplierPerformance AS ( SELECT s.supplier_id, s.supplier_name, COUNT(DISTINCT po.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(CASE WHEN od.delivery_status = 'Delivered' AND od.expected_delivery_date >= po.order_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS orders_delivered_on_time, SUM(CASE WHEN qc.status = 'Passed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS relays_passed_qc, COUNT(DISTINCT od.order_detail_id) AS total_relays FROM suppliers s LEFT JOIN purchase_orders po ON s.supplier_id = po.supplier_id LEFT JOIN order_details od ON po.order_id = od.order_id LEFT JOIN quality_control qc ON od.relay_id = qc.relay_id GROUP BY s.supplier_id, s.supplier_name ) SELECT supplier_name, total_orders, CAST(orders_delivered_on_time AS REAL) * 100 / total_orders AS on_time_delivery_percentage, CAST(relays_passed_qc AS REAL) * 100 / total_relays AS qc_pass_percentage FROM SupplierPerformance ORDER BY on_time_delivery_percentage DESC, qc_pass_percentage DESC

question:
**User**: I'd like to find information about clients and their units.
**Assistant**: Which units would you like to know about?
**User**: The ones that are currently in transit.
**Assistant**: What client information would you like to see about these units?
**User**: Just the client names and how many units they have in transit.
**Assistant**: Would you also like to see the details of the units, like their IDs and statuses?
**User**: Yes, that would be helpful.
**Assistant**: Do you want to see this information for all clients with units in transit, or just the top few?
**User**: I'd like to see the top 3 clients with the most units in transit.
**Assistant**: I understand. I'll retrieve the names of the top 3 clients with the most units in transit, along with the number of units and their details. Is there anything else you need?
**User**: No, that's all.
**Assistant**: I'll help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ClientUnitsCTE AS ( SELECT u.current_client_id, c.client_name, COUNT(u.unit_id) AS unit_count, GROUP_CONCAT(u.unit_number || ' - ' || u.status, ', ') AS unit_details FROM units u INNER JOIN clients c ON u.current_client_id = c.client_id WHERE u.status = 'in transit' GROUP BY u.current_client_id, c.client_name ), RankedClientsCTE AS ( SELECT current_client_id, client_name, unit_count, unit_details, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY unit_count DESC) AS client_rank FROM ClientUnitsCTE ) SELECT client_name, unit_count, unit_details FROM RankedClientsCTE WHERE client_rank <= 3

question: What are the names of customers who have churned, ordered by the total amount of money they would have paid if they hadn't left the service and the number of services they were using?
external_knowledge: Churned customers refer to customers who have stopped using a service or product. Total revenue lost is calculated by summing up the total charges from the bills table where the bill date is less than or equal to the churn date. The total number of services used and total usage are calculated by joining the customer services and usage tables.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ChurnedCustomers AS ( SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, ch.churn_date FROM customers c INNER JOIN churn ch ON c.customer_id = ch.customer_id WHERE ch.has_churned = 1 ), FinancialImpact AS ( SELECT cc.customer_id, SUM(b.total_charge) AS total_churned_revenue FROM ChurnedCustomers cc INNER JOIN bills b ON cc.customer_id = b.customer_id WHERE b.bill_date <= cc.churn_date GROUP BY cc.customer_id ), ServiceImpact AS ( SELECT cc.customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT cs.service_id) AS total_services, SUM(u.usage_amount) AS total_usage FROM ChurnedCustomers cc LEFT JOIN customer_services cs ON cc.customer_id = cs.customer_id LEFT JOIN usage u ON cc.customer_id = u.customer_id AND cs.service_id = u.service_id GROUP BY cc.customer_id ) SELECT cc.customer_id, cc.first_name || ' ' || cc.last_name AS full_name, fi.total_churned_revenue, si.total_services FROM ChurnedCustomers cc LEFT JOIN FinancialImpact fi ON cc.customer_id = fi.customer_id LEFT JOIN ServiceImpact si ON cc.customer_id = si.customer_id ORDER BY fi.total_churned_revenue DESC, si.total_services DESC

question: What are the dates, station names, precipitation amounts, total daily precipitation amounts, and percentage contributions of the top precipitation stations to the total daily precipitation, along with their corresponding category names, for each day, listed in descending order by date?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RankedStations AS ( SELECT w.date, w.station_id, w.precipitation, st.station_name, w.category_id, SUM(w.precipitation) OVER (PARTITION BY w.date) AS total_daily_precipitation, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY w.date ORDER BY w.precipitation DESC) AS precipitation_rank FROM weather_data w INNER JOIN weather_stations st ON w.station_id = st.station_id ), TopPrecipitation AS ( SELECT rs.date, rs.station_id, rs.precipitation, rs.station_name, rs.category_id, rs.total_daily_precipitation FROM RankedStations rs WHERE rs.precipitation_rank = 1 ) SELECT tp.date, tp.station_name, tp.precipitation, tp.total_daily_precipitation, (tp.precipitation * 100.0 / tp.total_daily_precipitation) AS percentage_contribution, wdc.category_name FROM TopPrecipitation tp INNER JOIN weather_data_categories wdc ON tp.category_id = wdc.category_id ORDER BY tp.date DESC

question: Find the primary and additional languages woven into the cultural tapestry of each union territory.
external_knowledge: In this context, "primary languages" refers to the languages that are predominantly spoken in a union territory (is_additional = 0); "additional languages" are those that are also spoken but may not be as widely used (is_additional = 1).

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT ut.name AS territory_name, GROUP_CONCAT(CASE WHEN ul.is_additional = 0 THEN l.name ELSE NULL END) AS primary_languages, GROUP_CONCAT(CASE WHEN ul.is_additional = 1 THEN l.name ELSE NULL END) AS additional_languages FROM union_territories ut JOIN ut_languages ul ON ut.ut_id = ul.ut_id JOIN languages l ON ul.language_id = l.language_id GROUP BY ut.name
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT ut.name AS territory_name, GROUP_CONCAT(CASE WHEN ul.is_additional = 0 THEN l.name ELSE NULL END SEPARATOR ',') AS primary_languages, GROUP_CONCAT(CASE WHEN ul.is_additional = 1 THEN l.name ELSE NULL END SEPARATOR ',') AS additional_languages FROM union_territories AS ut JOIN ut_languages AS ul ON ut.ut_id = ul.ut_id JOIN languages AS l ON ul.language_id = l.language_id GROUP BY ut.name
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT ut.name AS territory_name, STRING_AGG(CASE WHEN ul.is_additional = 0 THEN l.name ELSE NULL END, ',') AS primary_languages, STRING_AGG(CASE WHEN ul.is_additional = 1 THEN l.name ELSE NULL END, ',') AS additional_languages FROM union_territories AS ut JOIN ut_languages AS ul ON ut.ut_id = ul.ut_id JOIN languages AS l ON ul.language_id = l.language_id GROUP BY ut.name

question:
**User**: I want to find the top 3 longest access durations for each month and database.
**Assistant**: Sure, I can help with that. Could you please specify the information you need for each of these top 3 access durations?
**User**: I need the destination IP, the user's name, and the database name.
**Assistant**: Got it. Do you have any specific month or database in mind, or should this be done for all months and databases?
**User**: It should be done for all months and databases.
**Assistant**: Understood. I will create a query that finds the top 3 longest access durations for each month and database, along with the destination IP, user name, and database name. Is there anything else you need?
**User**: No, that's all.
**Assistant**: OK, I will help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RankedAccessLogs AS ( SELECT a.destination_ip, u.user_name, db.database_name, strftime('%Y-%m', a.access_date) AS access_month, a.duration, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY strftime('%Y-%m', a.access_date), db.database_name ORDER BY a.duration DESC) AS duration_rank FROM access_logs a INNER JOIN users u ON a.user_id = u.user_id INNER JOIN databases db ON a.database_id = db.database_id ) SELECT destination_ip, user_name, database_name, access_month, duration FROM RankedAccessLogs WHERE duration_rank <= 3 ORDER BY access_month, database_name, duration DESC
gold_sql.mysql: WITH RankedAccessLogs AS (SELECT a.destination_ip, u.user_name, db.database_name, DATE_FORMAT(CAST(a.access_date AS DATETIME), '%Y-%m') AS access_month, a.duration, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY DATE_FORMAT(CAST(a.access_date AS DATETIME), '%Y-%m'), db.database_name ORDER BY a.duration DESC) AS duration_rank FROM access_logs AS a INNER JOIN users AS u ON a.user_id = u.user_id INNER JOIN `databases` AS db ON a.database_id = db.database_id) SELECT destination_ip, user_name, database_name, access_month, duration FROM RankedAccessLogs WHERE duration_rank <= 3 ORDER BY access_month, database_name, duration DESC
gold_sql.postgres: WITH RankedAccessLogs AS (SELECT a.destination_ip, u.user_name, db.database_name, TO_CHAR(CAST(a.access_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY-MM') AS access_month, a.duration, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY TO_CHAR(CAST(a.access_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY-MM'), db.database_name ORDER BY a.duration DESC NULLS LAST) AS duration_rank FROM access_logs AS a INNER JOIN users AS u ON a.user_id = u.user_id INNER JOIN databases AS db ON a.database_id = db.database_id) SELECT destination_ip, user_name, database_name, access_month, duration FROM RankedAccessLogs WHERE duration_rank <= 3 ORDER BY access_month NULLS FIRST, database_name NULLS FIRST, duration DESC NULLS LAST

question: Which counties have the highest combined impact of their median home value, median household income, high school graduation rate, and unemployment rate?
external_knowledge: ; The impact index is a custom metric used to calculate the combined effect of a county's median home value, median household income, and high school graduation rate.; The min_rate is the minimum of the high school graduation rate and unemployment rate, indicating a potential correlation between education and employment.; The query is focusing on the year 2020, which might be a specific point of interest due to various economic and social factors.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH EconomicData AS ( SELECT ei.county_id, ei.median_household_income, ei.median_home_value, ed.high_school_graduation_rate, dd.unemployment_rate FROM economic_indicators ei JOIN education_data ed ON ei.county_id = ed.county_id AND ei.year = ed.year JOIN demographic_data dd ON ei.county_id = dd.county_id AND dd.year = 2020 WHERE ei.year = 2020 AND ed.year = 2020 ), CombinedData AS ( SELECT e.county_id, c.county_name, c.state_name, e.median_household_income, e.median_home_value, e.high_school_graduation_rate, e.unemployment_rate, MIN(e.high_school_graduation_rate, e.unemployment_rate) AS min_rate, (e.median_home_value - e.median_household_income) * (e.high_school_graduation_rate / 100) AS impact_index FROM EconomicData e JOIN counties c ON e.county_id = c.county_id ), FinalAnalysis AS ( SELECT cd.county_name, cd.state_name, cd.min_rate, cd.impact_index FROM CombinedData cd ) SELECT fa.county_name, fa.state_name, MAX(fa.min_rate) AS max_min_rate, SUM(fa.impact_index) AS total_impact_index FROM FinalAnalysis fa GROUP BY fa.county_name, fa.state_name ORDER BY total_impact_index DESC
gold_sql.mysql: WITH EconomicData AS (SELECT ei.county_id, ei.median_household_income, ei.median_home_value, ed.high_school_graduation_rate, dd.unemployment_rate FROM economic_indicators AS ei JOIN education_data AS ed ON ei.county_id = ed.county_id AND ei.year = ed.year JOIN demographic_data AS dd ON ei.county_id = dd.county_id AND dd.year = 2020 WHERE ei.year = 2020 AND ed.year = 2020), CombinedData AS (SELECT e.county_id, c.county_name, c.state_name, e.median_household_income, e.median_home_value, e.high_school_graduation_rate, e.unemployment_rate, LEAST(e.high_school_graduation_rate, e.unemployment_rate) AS min_rate, (e.median_home_value - e.median_household_income) * (e.high_school_graduation_rate / 100) AS impact_index FROM EconomicData AS e JOIN counties AS c ON e.county_id = c.county_id), FinalAnalysis AS (SELECT cd.county_name, cd.state_name, cd.min_rate, cd.impact_index FROM CombinedData AS cd) SELECT fa.county_name, fa.state_name, MAX(fa.min_rate) AS max_min_rate, SUM(fa.impact_index) AS total_impact_index FROM FinalAnalysis AS fa GROUP BY fa.county_name, fa.state_name ORDER BY total_impact_index DESC

question: Return the names of players along with their overall performance scores, calculated based on their latest ranking, wins, aces, and double faults, and rank the results in descending order of performance score.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH LatestRankings AS ( SELECT r.player_id, r.rank, r.points FROM rankings r INNER JOIN ( SELECT player_id, MAX(date) AS max_date FROM rankings GROUP BY player_id ) latest ON r.player_id = latest.player_id AND r.date = latest.max_date ), PlayerWins AS ( SELECT m.player1_id AS player_id, COUNT(CASE WHEN m.score LIKE '%-0,%-0' THEN 1 END) AS wins FROM matches m GROUP BY m.player1_id ), PlayerStats AS ( SELECT s.player_id, SUM(CASE WHEN s.stat_type = 'aces' THEN s.stat_value ELSE 0 END) AS aces, SUM(CASE WHEN s.stat_type = 'double faults' THEN s.stat_value ELSE 0 END) AS double_faults FROM statistics s GROUP BY s.player_id ) SELECT p.player_name, (lr.rank * 0.5 + IFNULL(pw.wins, 0) * 1.5 + IFNULL(ps.aces, 0) * 0.2 - IFNULL(ps.double_faults, 0) * 0.1) AS performance_score FROM players p LEFT JOIN LatestRankings lr ON p.player_id = lr.player_id LEFT JOIN PlayerWins pw ON p.player_id = pw.player_id LEFT JOIN PlayerStats ps ON p.player_id = ps.player_id ORDER BY performance_score DESC
gold_sql.mysql: WITH LatestRankings AS (SELECT r.player_id, r.`rank`, r.points FROM rankings AS r INNER JOIN (SELECT player_id, MAX(date) AS max_date FROM rankings GROUP BY player_id) AS latest ON r.player_id = latest.player_id AND r.date = latest.max_date), PlayerWins AS (SELECT m.player1_id AS player_id, COUNT(CASE WHEN m.score LIKE '%-0,%-0' THEN 1 END) AS wins FROM matches AS m GROUP BY m.player1_id), PlayerStats AS (SELECT s.player_id, SUM(CASE WHEN s.stat_type = 'aces' THEN s.stat_value ELSE 0 END) AS aces, SUM(CASE WHEN s.stat_type = 'double faults' THEN s.stat_value ELSE 0 END) AS double_faults FROM statistics AS s GROUP BY s.player_id) SELECT p.player_name, (lr.`rank` * 0.5 + COALESCE(pw.wins, 0) * 1.5 + COALESCE(ps.aces, 0) * 0.2 - COALESCE(ps.double_faults, 0) * 0.1) AS performance_score FROM players AS p LEFT JOIN LatestRankings AS lr ON p.player_id = lr.player_id LEFT JOIN PlayerWins AS pw ON p.player_id = pw.player_id LEFT JOIN PlayerStats AS ps ON p.player_id = ps.player_id ORDER BY performance_score DESC
gold_sql.postgres: WITH LatestRankings AS (SELECT r.player_id, r.rank, r.points FROM rankings AS r INNER JOIN (SELECT player_id, MAX(date) AS max_date FROM rankings GROUP BY player_id) AS latest ON r.player_id = latest.player_id AND r.date = latest.max_date), PlayerWins AS (SELECT m.player1_id AS player_id, COUNT(CASE WHEN m.score LIKE '%-0,%-0' THEN 1 END) AS wins FROM matches AS m GROUP BY m.player1_id), PlayerStats AS (SELECT s.player_id, SUM(CASE WHEN s.stat_type = 'aces' THEN s.stat_value ELSE 0 END) AS aces, SUM(CASE WHEN s.stat_type = 'double faults' THEN s.stat_value ELSE 0 END) AS double_faults FROM statistics AS s GROUP BY s.player_id) SELECT p.player_name, (lr.rank * 0.5 + COALESCE(pw.wins, 0) * 1.5 + COALESCE(ps.aces, 0) * 0.2 - COALESCE(ps.double_faults, 0) * 0.1) AS performance_score FROM players AS p LEFT JOIN LatestRankings AS lr ON p.player_id = lr.player_id LEFT JOIN PlayerWins AS pw ON p.player_id = pw.player_id LEFT JOIN PlayerStats AS ps ON p.player_id = ps.player_id ORDER BY performance_score DESC NULLS LAST

question: I want to know the names of online feeds with a higher-than-average number of listeners, along with the number of listeners for each feed, the county name, and the total number of listeners in the state where the feed is located.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH OnlineFeedsCTE AS ( SELECT f.feed_id, f.feed_name, f.listeners, c.county_name, c.state FROM feeds f JOIN counties c ON f.county_id = c.county_id WHERE f.status = 'Online' ), StateListenerCTE AS ( SELECT state, SUM(listeners) AS total_listeners FROM OnlineFeedsCTE GROUP BY state ) SELECT of.feed_name, of.listeners, of.county_name, sl.total_listeners FROM OnlineFeedsCTE of JOIN StateListenerCTE sl ON of.state = sl.state WHERE of.listeners > (SELECT AVG(listeners) FROM feeds WHERE status = 'Online')
gold_sql.mysql: WITH OnlineFeedsCTE AS (SELECT f.feed_id, f.feed_name, f.listeners, c.county_name, c.state FROM feeds AS f JOIN counties AS c ON f.county_id = c.county_id WHERE f.status = 'Online'), StateListenerCTE AS (SELECT state, SUM(listeners) AS total_listeners FROM OnlineFeedsCTE GROUP BY state) SELECT `of`.feed_name, `of`.listeners, `of`.county_name, sl.total_listeners FROM OnlineFeedsCTE AS `of` JOIN StateListenerCTE AS sl ON `of`.state = sl.state WHERE `of`.listeners > (SELECT AVG(listeners) FROM feeds WHERE status = 'Online')

question: What are the names of the top 5 most accessed prizes along with their corresponding laureates?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH AccessCountCTE AS ( SELECT p.prize_id, p.prize_name, COUNT(al.access_id) AS access_count FROM prizes p JOIN access_logs al ON p.prize_id = al.prize_id GROUP BY p.prize_id, p.prize_name ORDER BY access_count DESC LIMIT 5 ), TopPrizeLaureates AS ( SELECT ac.prize_name, l.full_name FROM AccessCountCTE ac JOIN laureate_prizes lp ON ac.prize_id = lp.prize_id JOIN laureates l ON lp.laureate_id = l.laureate_id ) SELECT prize_name || ' - ' || GROUP_CONCAT(full_name, ', ') AS prize_and_laureates FROM TopPrizeLaureates GROUP BY prize_name ORDER BY prize_name
gold_sql.mysql: WITH AccessCountCTE AS (SELECT p.prize_id, p.prize_name, COUNT(al.access_id) AS access_count FROM prizes AS p JOIN access_logs AS al ON p.prize_id = al.prize_id GROUP BY p.prize_id, p.prize_name ORDER BY access_count DESC LIMIT 5), TopPrizeLaureates AS (SELECT ac.prize_name, l.full_name FROM AccessCountCTE AS ac JOIN laureate_prizes AS lp ON ac.prize_id = lp.prize_id JOIN laureates AS l ON lp.laureate_id = l.laureate_id) SELECT CONCAT(prize_name, ' - ', GROUP_CONCAT(full_name SEPARATOR ', ')) AS prize_and_laureates FROM TopPrizeLaureates GROUP BY prize_name ORDER BY prize_name
gold_sql.postgres: WITH AccessCountCTE AS (SELECT p.prize_id, p.prize_name, COUNT(al.access_id) AS access_count FROM prizes AS p JOIN access_logs AS al ON p.prize_id = al.prize_id GROUP BY p.prize_id, p.prize_name ORDER BY access_count DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 5), TopPrizeLaureates AS (SELECT ac.prize_name, l.full_name FROM AccessCountCTE AS ac JOIN laureate_prizes AS lp ON ac.prize_id = lp.prize_id JOIN laureates AS l ON lp.laureate_id = l.laureate_id) SELECT prize_name || ' - ' || STRING_AGG(full_name, ', ') AS prize_and_laureates FROM TopPrizeLaureates GROUP BY prize_name ORDER BY prize_name NULLS FIRST

question: Hey! Could you help me find the top 5 movies based on their average ratings, popularity in watchlists, and the number of reviews? I'd love to know their titles, average ratings, how often they appear in watchlists, their genres, and the number of reviews they have.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH MovieRatings AS ( SELECT m.movie_id, AVG(CAST(r.rating AS REAL)) AS avg_rating, COUNT(r.rating_id) AS review_count FROM movies m LEFT JOIN ratings r ON m.movie_id = r.movie_id GROUP BY m.movie_id ), MovieWatchlists AS ( SELECT m.movie_id, COUNT(w.watchlist_id) AS watchlist_count FROM movies m LEFT JOIN watchlists w ON m.movie_id = w.movie_id GROUP BY m.movie_id ), MovieGenres AS ( SELECT mg.movie_id, GROUP_CONCAT(g.genre_name) AS genres FROM movie_genres mg INNER JOIN genres g ON mg.genre_id = g.genre_id GROUP BY mg.movie_id ) SELECT m.movie_id, m.name, mr.avg_rating, mw.watchlist_count, mg.genres, mr.review_count FROM movies m LEFT JOIN MovieRatings mr ON m.movie_id = mr.movie_id LEFT JOIN MovieWatchlists mw ON m.movie_id = mw.movie_id LEFT JOIN MovieGenres mg ON m.movie_id = mg.movie_id ORDER BY mr.avg_rating DESC, mw.watchlist_count DESC, mr.review_count DESC LIMIT 5
gold_sql.mysql: WITH MovieRatings AS (SELECT m.movie_id, AVG(CAST(r.rating AS FLOAT)) AS avg_rating, COUNT(r.rating_id) AS review_count FROM movies AS m LEFT JOIN ratings AS r ON m.movie_id = r.movie_id GROUP BY m.movie_id), MovieWatchlists AS (SELECT m.movie_id, COUNT(w.watchlist_id) AS watchlist_count FROM movies AS m LEFT JOIN watchlists AS w ON m.movie_id = w.movie_id GROUP BY m.movie_id), MovieGenres AS (SELECT mg.movie_id, GROUP_CONCAT(g.genre_name SEPARATOR ',') AS genres FROM movie_genres AS mg INNER JOIN genres AS g ON mg.genre_id = g.genre_id GROUP BY mg.movie_id) SELECT m.movie_id, m.name, mr.avg_rating, mw.watchlist_count, mg.genres, mr.review_count FROM movies AS m LEFT JOIN MovieRatings AS mr ON m.movie_id = mr.movie_id LEFT JOIN MovieWatchlists AS mw ON m.movie_id = mw.movie_id LEFT JOIN MovieGenres AS mg ON m.movie_id = mg.movie_id ORDER BY mr.avg_rating DESC, mw.watchlist_count DESC, mr.review_count DESC LIMIT 5
gold_sql.postgres: WITH MovieRatings AS (SELECT m.movie_id, AVG(CAST(r.rating AS REAL)) AS avg_rating, COUNT(r.rating_id) AS review_count FROM movies AS m LEFT JOIN ratings AS r ON m.movie_id = r.movie_id GROUP BY m.movie_id), MovieWatchlists AS (SELECT m.movie_id, COUNT(w.watchlist_id) AS watchlist_count FROM movies AS m LEFT JOIN watchlists AS w ON m.movie_id = w.movie_id GROUP BY m.movie_id), MovieGenres AS (SELECT mg.movie_id, STRING_AGG(g.genre_name, ',') AS genres FROM movie_genres AS mg INNER JOIN genres AS g ON mg.genre_id = g.genre_id GROUP BY mg.movie_id) SELECT m.movie_id, m.name, mr.avg_rating, mw.watchlist_count, mg.genres, mr.review_count FROM movies AS m LEFT JOIN MovieRatings AS mr ON m.movie_id = mr.movie_id LEFT JOIN MovieWatchlists AS mw ON m.movie_id = mw.movie_id LEFT JOIN MovieGenres AS mg ON m.movie_id = mg.movie_id ORDER BY mr.avg_rating DESC NULLS LAST, mw.watchlist_count DESC NULLS LAST, mr.review_count DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 5

question: Find the wire types, their total usage in 2023, and the average stock level for each plant, but only for the plants with some stock left, and rank the results by total usage from highest to lowest; a 'wire type' refers to a unique combination of AWG size, temperature rating, and material.
external_knowledge: A "wire type" is identified by a unique combination of its AWG size, temperature rating, and material; This query does not include plants with zero stock; Only the year 2023 is considered for usage.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT w.awg_size, w.temperature_rating, w.material, SUM(wu.quantity_used) AS total_quantity_used, p.plant_name, AVG(i.quantity_in_stock) AS average_stock_quantity FROM wire_usage wu JOIN wire_types w ON wu.wire_type_id = w.wire_type_id JOIN inventory i ON w.wire_type_id = i.wire_type_id JOIN plants p ON i.plant_id = p.plant_id WHERE strftime('%Y', wu.date_used) = '2023' GROUP BY w.awg_size, w.temperature_rating, w.material, p.plant_name HAVING AVG(i.quantity_in_stock) > 0 ORDER BY total_quantity_used DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT w.awg_size, w.temperature_rating, w.material, SUM(wu.quantity_used) AS total_quantity_used, p.plant_name, AVG(i.quantity_in_stock) AS average_stock_quantity FROM wire_usage AS wu JOIN wire_types AS w ON wu.wire_type_id = w.wire_type_id JOIN inventory AS i ON w.wire_type_id = i.wire_type_id JOIN plants AS p ON i.plant_id = p.plant_id WHERE DATE_FORMAT(CAST(wu.date_used AS DATETIME), '%Y') = '2023' GROUP BY w.awg_size, w.temperature_rating, w.material, p.plant_name HAVING AVG(i.quantity_in_stock) > 0 ORDER BY total_quantity_used DESC
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT w.awg_size, w.temperature_rating, w.material, SUM(wu.quantity_used) AS total_quantity_used, p.plant_name, AVG(i.quantity_in_stock) AS average_stock_quantity FROM wire_usage AS wu JOIN wire_types AS w ON wu.wire_type_id = w.wire_type_id JOIN inventory AS i ON w.wire_type_id = i.wire_type_id JOIN plants AS p ON i.plant_id = p.plant_id WHERE TO_CHAR(CAST(wu.date_used AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY') = '2023' GROUP BY w.awg_size, w.temperature_rating, w.material, p.plant_name HAVING AVG(i.quantity_in_stock) > 0 ORDER BY total_quantity_used DESC NULLS LAST

question:
**User**: I need to find out the cumulative scores of players in a specific game mode and difficulty level.
**Assistant**: Sure, which game mode and difficulty level are you interested in?
**User**: Single-player mode and easy difficulty level.
**Assistant**: Got it. Do you want to include any additional conditions, such as the maximum number of players allowed in the game?
**User**: Yes, I only want to include levels where the maximum number of players is 4 or more.
**Assistant**: Understood. What specific information do you need about the players, such as their IDs, progress, or scores?
**User**: I just need the player IDs and their cumulative scores.
**Assistant**: Is there anything else you need to know or any other conditions to add?
**User**: No, that's all.
**Assistant**: OK, I will help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH FilteredLevels AS ( SELECT gl.level_id, gl.name, gl.game_mode, gl.difficulty_level FROM game_levels gl WHERE gl.game_mode = 'Single-player' AND gl.difficulty_level = 'Easy' ), FilteredProgress AS ( SELECT pp.player_id, pp.level_id, pp.score FROM player_progress pp JOIN FilteredLevels fl ON pp.level_id = fl.level_id ), MaxPlayersLevels AS ( SELECT fps.player_id, fps.level_id, fps.score, gs.value AS max_players FROM FilteredProgress fps JOIN game_settings gs ON gs.name = 'MaxPlayers' ), CumulativeScores AS ( SELECT mpl.player_id, SUM(mpl.score) AS cumulative_score FROM MaxPlayersLevels mpl WHERE CAST(mpl.max_players AS INTEGER) >= 4 GROUP BY mpl.player_id ) SELECT player_id, cumulative_score FROM CumulativeScores
gold_sql.mysql: WITH FilteredLevels AS (SELECT gl.level_id, gl.name, gl.game_mode, gl.difficulty_level FROM game_levels AS gl WHERE gl.game_mode = 'Single-player' AND gl.difficulty_level = 'Easy'), FilteredProgress AS (SELECT pp.player_id, pp.level_id, pp.score FROM player_progress AS pp JOIN FilteredLevels AS fl ON pp.level_id = fl.level_id), MaxPlayersLevels AS (SELECT fps.player_id, fps.level_id, fps.score, gs.value AS max_players FROM FilteredProgress AS fps JOIN game_settings AS gs ON gs.name = 'MaxPlayers'), CumulativeScores AS (SELECT mpl.player_id, SUM(mpl.score) AS cumulative_score FROM MaxPlayersLevels AS mpl WHERE CAST(mpl.max_players AS SIGNED) >= 4 GROUP BY mpl.player_id) SELECT player_id, cumulative_score FROM CumulativeScores
