question: What is the average monthly data usage for the entire year 2023 of customers who are on the 'Super-User Residential Package' and have an active account?
external_knowledge: ; This question assumes that the date range (2023-01-01 to 2023-12-31) represents the entire year 2023.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', ul.date) AS month, AVG(ul.total_data_usage) AS average_monthly_usage FROM customers c INNER JOIN service_plans sp ON c.plan_id = sp.plan_id INNER JOIN usage_logs ul ON c.customer_id = ul.customer_id WHERE sp.name = 'Super-User Residential Package' AND c.account_status = 'active' AND ul.date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-12-31' GROUP BY month
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(CAST(ul.date AS DATETIME), '%Y-%m') AS month, AVG(ul.total_data_usage) AS average_monthly_usage FROM customers AS c INNER JOIN service_plans AS sp ON c.plan_id = sp.plan_id INNER JOIN usage_logs AS ul ON c.customer_id = ul.customer_id WHERE sp.name = 'Super-User Residential Package' AND c.account_status = 'active' AND ul.date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-12-31' GROUP BY month
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT TO_CHAR(CAST(ul.date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY-MM') AS month, AVG(ul.total_data_usage) AS average_monthly_usage FROM customers AS c INNER JOIN service_plans AS sp ON c.plan_id = sp.plan_id INNER JOIN usage_logs AS ul ON c.customer_id = ul.customer_id WHERE sp.name = 'Super-User Residential Package' AND c.account_status = 'active' AND ul.date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-12-31' GROUP BY month

question: What are the details of the assessments, including their titles, the number of questions, average ratings, when they were created, who created them, and when feedback was given?
external_knowledge:
- The `audit_logs` table contains logs of various actions, including creation and feedback actions for assessments.
- The `assessment_questions` table links questions to assessments.
- The `feedback` table stores user ratings for assessments.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH AssessmentDetails AS ( SELECT a.assessment_id, a.title, a.created_at, u.name AS creator_name, COUNT(aq.question_id) AS question_count, AVG(f.rating) AS average_rating FROM assessments a JOIN users u ON a.user_id = u.user_id LEFT JOIN assessment_questions aq ON a.assessment_id = aq.assessment_id LEFT JOIN feedback f ON a.assessment_id = f.assessment_id GROUP BY a.assessment_id, a.title, a.created_at, u.name ), AuditCreation AS ( SELECT a.log_id, a.timestamp AS creation_timestamp, CAST(SUBSTR(a.description, INSTR(a.description, 'assessment ') + 10, INSTR(a.description, '.') - INSTR(a.description, 'assessment ') - 10) AS INTEGER) AS assessment_id FROM audit_logs a WHERE a.action = 'Created assessment' ), FeedbackLogs AS ( SELECT a.log_id, a.timestamp AS feedback_timestamp, CAST(SUBSTR(a.description, INSTR(a.description, 'assessment ') + 10, INSTR(a.description, '.') - INSTR(a.description, 'assessment ') - 10) AS INTEGER) AS assessment_id FROM audit_logs a WHERE a.action LIKE '%feedback%' ) SELECT ad.title, ad.question_count, ad.average_rating, ad.created_at, ad.creator_name, ac.creation_timestamp, fl.feedback_timestamp FROM AssessmentDetails ad LEFT JOIN AuditCreation ac ON ad.assessment_id = ac.assessment_id LEFT JOIN FeedbackLogs fl ON ad.assessment_id = fl.assessment_id ORDER BY ad.created_at DESC
gold_sql.mysql: WITH AssessmentDetails AS (SELECT a.assessment_id, a.title, a.created_at, u.name AS creator_name, COUNT(aq.question_id) AS question_count, AVG(f.rating) AS average_rating FROM assessments AS a JOIN users AS u ON a.user_id = u.user_id LEFT JOIN assessment_questions AS aq ON a.assessment_id = aq.assessment_id LEFT JOIN feedback AS f ON a.assessment_id = f.assessment_id GROUP BY a.assessment_id, a.title, a.created_at, u.name), AuditCreation AS (SELECT a.log_id, a.timestamp AS creation_timestamp, CAST(SUBSTRING(a.description, LOCATE('assessment ', a.description) + 10, LOCATE('.', a.description) - LOCATE('assessment ', a.description) - 10) AS SIGNED) AS assessment_id FROM audit_logs AS a WHERE a.action = 'Created assessment'), FeedbackLogs AS (SELECT a.log_id, a.timestamp AS feedback_timestamp, CAST(SUBSTRING(a.description, LOCATE('assessment ', a.description) + 10, LOCATE('.', a.description) - LOCATE('assessment ', a.description) - 10) AS SIGNED) AS assessment_id FROM audit_logs AS a WHERE a.action LIKE '%feedback%') SELECT ad.title, ad.question_count, ad.average_rating, ad.created_at, ad.creator_name, ac.creation_timestamp, fl.feedback_timestamp FROM AssessmentDetails AS ad LEFT JOIN AuditCreation AS ac ON ad.assessment_id = ac.assessment_id LEFT JOIN FeedbackLogs AS fl ON ad.assessment_id = fl.assessment_id ORDER BY ad.created_at DESC
gold_sql.postgres: WITH AssessmentDetails AS (SELECT a.assessment_id, a.title, a.created_at, u.name AS creator_name, COUNT(aq.question_id) AS question_count, AVG(f.rating) AS average_rating FROM assessments AS a JOIN users AS u ON a.user_id = u.user_id LEFT JOIN assessment_questions AS aq ON a.assessment_id = aq.assessment_id LEFT JOIN feedback AS f ON a.assessment_id = f.assessment_id GROUP BY a.assessment_id, a.title, a.created_at, u.name), AuditCreation AS (SELECT a.log_id, a.timestamp AS creation_timestamp, CAST(SUBSTRING(a.description FROM STRPOS(a.description, 'assessment ') + 10 FOR STRPOS(a.description, '.') - STRPOS(a.description, 'assessment ') - 10) AS INT) AS assessment_id FROM audit_logs AS a WHERE a.action = 'Created assessment'), FeedbackLogs AS (SELECT a.log_id, a.timestamp AS feedback_timestamp, CAST(SUBSTRING(a.description FROM STRPOS(a.description, 'assessment ') + 10 FOR STRPOS(a.description, '.') - STRPOS(a.description, 'assessment ') - 10) AS INT) AS assessment_id FROM audit_logs AS a WHERE a.action LIKE '%feedback%') SELECT ad.title, ad.question_count, ad.average_rating, ad.created_at, ad.creator_name, ac.creation_timestamp, fl.feedback_timestamp FROM AssessmentDetails AS ad LEFT JOIN AuditCreation AS ac ON ad.assessment_id = ac.assessment_id LEFT JOIN FeedbackLogs AS fl ON ad.assessment_id = fl.assessment_id ORDER BY ad.created_at DESC NULLS LAST

question:
**User**: I want to query some model information.
**Assistant**: Which models' information would you like to query?
**User**: All of them.
**Assistant**: What information would you like to know about the models?
**User**: Their names, average F1-scores, number of hyperparameters, latest version numbers, deployment statuses, and latest comments.
**Assistant**: Would you also like to view the hyperparameters for each model?
**User**: Yes, please include a list of hyperparameters.
**Assistant**: How would you like the results to be ordered?
**User**: Order them by model name.
**Assistant**: Is there anything else you need?
**User**: No, that's all.
**Assistant**: OK, I will help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ModelStats AS ( SELECT m.model_id, AVG(em.f1_score) AS avg_f1_score, COUNT(hp.hyperparameter_id) AS hyperparameter_count FROM models m LEFT JOIN evaluation_metrics em ON m.model_id = em.model_id LEFT JOIN hyperparameters hp ON m.model_id = hp.model_id GROUP BY m.model_id ), DetailedModelInfo AS ( SELECT m.model_id, m.model_name, mv.version_number, mdh.deployment_status, mc.comment AS latest_comment FROM models m LEFT JOIN model_versions mv ON m.model_id = mv.model_id LEFT JOIN model_deployment_history mdh ON m.model_id = mdh.model_id LEFT JOIN ( SELECT model_id, comment_id, comment FROM model_comments WHERE (model_id, created_at) IN ( SELECT model_id, MAX(created_at) FROM model_comments GROUP BY model_id ) ) mc ON m.model_id = mc.model_id ), HyperparametersSummary AS ( SELECT model_id, GROUP_CONCAT(hyperparameter_name || ': ' || hyperparameter_value, ', ') AS hyperparameters_list FROM hyperparameters GROUP BY model_id ) SELECT m.model_name, COALESCE(ms.avg_f1_score, 0) AS avg_f1_score, COALESCE(ms.hyperparameter_count, 0) AS hyperparameter_count, COALESCE(dmi.version_number, 'N/A') AS latest_version, COALESCE(dmi.deployment_status, 'N/A') AS latest_deployment_status, COALESCE(dmi.latest_comment, 'No comments') AS latest_comment, COALESCE(hs.hyperparameters_list, 'No hyperparameters') AS hyperparameters_list FROM models m LEFT JOIN ModelStats ms ON m.model_id = ms.model_id LEFT JOIN DetailedModelInfo dmi ON m.model_id = dmi.model_id LEFT JOIN HyperparametersSummary hs ON m.model_id = hs.model_id ORDER BY m.model_name
gold_sql.mysql: WITH ModelStats AS (SELECT m.model_id, AVG(em.f1_score) AS avg_f1_score, COUNT(hp.hyperparameter_id) AS hyperparameter_count FROM models AS m LEFT JOIN evaluation_metrics AS em ON m.model_id = em.model_id LEFT JOIN hyperparameters AS hp ON m.model_id = hp.model_id GROUP BY m.model_id), DetailedModelInfo AS (SELECT m.model_id, m.model_name, mv.version_number, mdh.deployment_status, mc.comment AS latest_comment FROM models AS m LEFT JOIN model_versions AS mv ON m.model_id = mv.model_id LEFT JOIN model_deployment_history AS mdh ON m.model_id = mdh.model_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT model_id, comment_id, comment FROM model_comments WHERE (model_id, created_at) IN (SELECT model_id, MAX(created_at) FROM model_comments GROUP BY model_id)) AS mc ON m.model_id = mc.model_id), HyperparametersSummary AS (SELECT model_id, GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(hyperparameter_name, ': ', hyperparameter_value) SEPARATOR ', ') AS hyperparameters_list FROM hyperparameters GROUP BY model_id) SELECT m.model_name, COALESCE(ms.avg_f1_score, 0) AS avg_f1_score, COALESCE(ms.hyperparameter_count, 0) AS hyperparameter_count, COALESCE(dmi.version_number, 'N/A') AS latest_version, COALESCE(dmi.deployment_status, 'N/A') AS latest_deployment_status, COALESCE(dmi.latest_comment, 'No comments') AS latest_comment, COALESCE(hs.hyperparameters_list, 'No hyperparameters') AS hyperparameters_list FROM models AS m LEFT JOIN ModelStats AS ms ON m.model_id = ms.model_id LEFT JOIN DetailedModelInfo AS dmi ON m.model_id = dmi.model_id LEFT JOIN HyperparametersSummary AS hs ON m.model_id = hs.model_id ORDER BY m.model_name
gold_sql.postgres: WITH ModelStats AS (SELECT m.model_id, AVG(em.f1_score) AS avg_f1_score, COUNT(hp.hyperparameter_id) AS hyperparameter_count FROM models AS m LEFT JOIN evaluation_metrics AS em ON m.model_id = em.model_id LEFT JOIN hyperparameters AS hp ON m.model_id = hp.model_id GROUP BY m.model_id), DetailedModelInfo AS (SELECT m.model_id, m.model_name, mv.version_number, mdh.deployment_status, mc.comment AS latest_comment FROM models AS m LEFT JOIN model_versions AS mv ON m.model_id = mv.model_id LEFT JOIN model_deployment_history AS mdh ON m.model_id = mdh.model_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT model_id, comment_id, comment FROM model_comments WHERE (model_id, created_at) IN (SELECT model_id, MAX(created_at) FROM model_comments GROUP BY model_id)) AS mc ON m.model_id = mc.model_id), HyperparametersSummary AS (SELECT model_id, STRING_AGG(hyperparameter_name || ': ' || hyperparameter_value, ', ') AS hyperparameters_list FROM hyperparameters GROUP BY model_id) SELECT m.model_name, COALESCE(ms.avg_f1_score, 0) AS avg_f1_score, COALESCE(ms.hyperparameter_count, 0) AS hyperparameter_count, COALESCE(dmi.version_number, 'N/A') AS latest_version, COALESCE(dmi.deployment_status, 'N/A') AS latest_deployment_status, COALESCE(dmi.latest_comment, 'No comments') AS latest_comment, COALESCE(hs.hyperparameters_list, 'No hyperparameters') AS hyperparameters_list FROM models AS m LEFT JOIN ModelStats AS ms ON m.model_id = ms.model_id LEFT JOIN DetailedModelInfo AS dmi ON m.model_id = dmi.model_id LEFT JOIN HyperparametersSummary AS hs ON m.model_id = hs.model_id ORDER BY m.model_name NULLS FIRST

question: What are the names of the top three teams in each soccer competition, ranked by their performance?
external_knowledge: Performance is measured by the number of wins, with goal difference used as a tiebreaker; The top three teams are the ones with the highest rankings in each competition, which corresponds to the teams with the most wins and the best goal difference.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH CompetitionTeamPerformance AS ( SELECT c.competition_name, t.team_name, c.stage, SUM(CASE WHEN m.result = 'win' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS wins, SUM(CASE WHEN m.result = 'draw' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS draws, SUM(CASE WHEN m.result = 'loss' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS losses, SUM(CASE WHEN m.full_time_score IS NOT NULL THEN CAST(SUBSTR(m.full_time_score, 1, INSTR(m.full_time_score, '-') - 1) AS INTEGER) - CAST(SUBSTR(m.full_time_score, INSTR(m.full_time_score, '-') + 1) AS INTEGER) ELSE 0 END) AS goal_difference, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.competition_name ORDER BY SUM(CASE WHEN m.result = 'win' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) DESC, SUM(CASE WHEN m.result = 'win' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN m.result = 'loss' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) DESC) AS team_rank FROM competitions c INNER JOIN matches m ON c.competition_id = m.competition_id INNER JOIN teams t ON m.team_id = t.team_id GROUP BY c.competition_name, t.team_name, c.stage ) SELECT competition_name, team_name FROM CompetitionTeamPerformance WHERE team_rank <= 3 ORDER BY competition_name, team_rank
gold_sql.mysql: WITH CompetitionTeamPerformance AS (SELECT c.competition_name, t.team_name, c.stage, SUM(CASE WHEN m.result = 'win' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS wins, SUM(CASE WHEN m.result = 'draw' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS draws, SUM(CASE WHEN m.result = 'loss' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS losses, SUM(CASE WHEN NOT m.full_time_score IS NULL THEN CAST(SUBSTRING(m.full_time_score, 1, LOCATE('-', m.full_time_score) - 1) AS SIGNED) - CAST(SUBSTRING(m.full_time_score, LOCATE('-', m.full_time_score) + 1) AS SIGNED) ELSE 0 END) AS goal_difference, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.competition_name ORDER BY SUM(CASE WHEN m.result = 'win' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) DESC, SUM(CASE WHEN m.result = 'win' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN m.result = 'loss' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) DESC) AS team_rank FROM competitions AS c INNER JOIN matches AS m ON c.competition_id = m.competition_id INNER JOIN teams AS t ON m.team_id = t.team_id GROUP BY c.competition_name, t.team_name, c.stage) SELECT competition_name, team_name FROM CompetitionTeamPerformance WHERE team_rank <= 3 ORDER BY competition_name, team_rank
gold_sql.postgres: WITH CompetitionTeamPerformance AS (SELECT c.competition_name, t.team_name, c.stage, SUM(CASE WHEN m.result = 'win' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS wins, SUM(CASE WHEN m.result = 'draw' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS draws, SUM(CASE WHEN m.result = 'loss' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS losses, SUM(CASE WHEN NOT m.full_time_score IS NULL THEN CAST(SUBSTRING(m.full_time_score FROM 1 FOR STRPOS(m.full_time_score, '-') - 1) AS INT) - CAST(SUBSTRING(m.full_time_score FROM STRPOS(m.full_time_score, '-') + 1) AS INT) ELSE 0 END) AS goal_difference, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.competition_name ORDER BY SUM(CASE WHEN m.result = 'win' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) DESC NULLS LAST, SUM(CASE WHEN m.result = 'win' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN m.result = 'loss' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) DESC NULLS LAST) AS team_rank FROM competitions AS c INNER JOIN matches AS m ON c.competition_id = m.competition_id INNER JOIN teams AS t ON m.team_id = t.team_id GROUP BY c.competition_name, t.team_name, c.stage) SELECT competition_name, team_name FROM CompetitionTeamPerformance WHERE team_rank <= 3 ORDER BY competition_name NULLS FIRST, team_rank NULLS FIRST

question: What is a detailed demographic summary (including age, education level, hours worked per week, marital status, relationship status, native country, income level, data quality score, and ranking within marital status) of the top 5 individuals within each marital status group, considering only individuals older than 18 years with a data quality score greater than 5?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RankedDemographics AS ( SELECT dd.age, dd.educationnum, dd.hoursperweek, dd.data_quality_score, ms.maritalstatus_name, r.relationship_name, c.nativecountry_name, i.income_name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( PARTITION BY ms.maritalstatus_name ORDER BY dd.fnlwgt DESC, dd.age ASC ) AS rank_within_marital_status FROM demographic_data dd JOIN maritalstatuses ms ON dd.maritalstatus_id = ms.maritalstatus_id JOIN relationships r ON dd.relationship_id = r.relationship_id JOIN nativecountries c ON dd.nativecountry_id = c.nativecountry_id JOIN incomes i ON dd.income_id = i.income_id WHERE dd.age > 18 AND dd.data_quality_score > 5 ) SELECT maritalstatus_name, GROUP_CONCAT( age || ',' || educationnum || ',' || hoursperweek || ',' || maritalstatus_name || ',' || relationship_name || ',' || nativecountry_name || ',' || income_name || ',' || data_quality_score || ',' || rank_within_marital_status ) AS detailed_demographic_summary FROM RankedDemographics WHERE rank_within_marital_status <= 5 GROUP BY maritalstatus_name
gold_sql.mysql: WITH RankedDemographics AS (SELECT dd.age, dd.educationnum, dd.hoursperweek, dd.data_quality_score, ms.maritalstatus_name, r.relationship_name, c.nativecountry_name, i.income_name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ms.maritalstatus_name ORDER BY dd.fnlwgt DESC, dd.age ASC) AS rank_within_marital_status FROM demographic_data AS dd JOIN maritalstatuses AS ms ON dd.maritalstatus_id = ms.maritalstatus_id JOIN relationships AS r ON dd.relationship_id = r.relationship_id JOIN nativecountries AS c ON dd.nativecountry_id = c.nativecountry_id JOIN incomes AS i ON dd.income_id = i.income_id WHERE dd.age > 18 AND dd.data_quality_score > 5) SELECT maritalstatus_name, GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(age, ',', educationnum, ',', hoursperweek, ',', maritalstatus_name, ',', relationship_name, ',', nativecountry_name, ',', income_name, ',', data_quality_score, ',', rank_within_marital_status) SEPARATOR ',') AS detailed_demographic_summary FROM RankedDemographics WHERE rank_within_marital_status <= 5 GROUP BY maritalstatus_name
gold_sql.postgres: WITH RankedDemographics AS (SELECT dd.age, dd.educationnum, dd.hoursperweek, dd.data_quality_score, ms.maritalstatus_name, r.relationship_name, c.nativecountry_name, i.income_name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ms.maritalstatus_name ORDER BY dd.fnlwgt DESC NULLS LAST, dd.age ASC NULLS FIRST) AS rank_within_marital_status FROM demographic_data AS dd JOIN maritalstatuses AS ms ON dd.maritalstatus_id = ms.maritalstatus_id JOIN relationships AS r ON dd.relationship_id = r.relationship_id JOIN nativecountries AS c ON dd.nativecountry_id = c.nativecountry_id JOIN incomes AS i ON dd.income_id = i.income_id WHERE dd.age > 18 AND dd.data_quality_score > 5) SELECT maritalstatus_name, STRING_AGG(age || ',' || educationnum || ',' || hoursperweek || ',' || maritalstatus_name || ',' || relationship_name || ',' || nativecountry_name || ',' || income_name || ',' || data_quality_score || ',' || rank_within_marital_status, ',') AS detailed_demographic_summary FROM RankedDemographics WHERE rank_within_marital_status <= 5 GROUP BY maritalstatus_name

question: Which latest and popular SQL Server editions have the top 3 core features, and what are those features?
external_knowledge:
- 'Core features' are essential functionalities that are considered fundamental to the SQL Server edition.
- 'Latest' and 'popular' editions are those that are currently up-to-date and widely used by the community.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH CoreFeaturesRanked AS ( SELECT e.edition_name, f.feature_name, ef.is_core_feature, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY e.edition_id ORDER BY f.feature_id) AS feature_rank FROM editions e JOIN edition_features ef ON e.edition_id = ef.edition_id JOIN features f ON ef.feature_id = f.feature_id WHERE e.is_latest = 1 AND e.is_popular = 1 AND ef.is_core_feature = 1 ) SELECT edition_name, GROUP_CONCAT(feature_name, ', ') AS core_features FROM CoreFeaturesRanked WHERE feature_rank <= 3 GROUP BY edition_name
gold_sql.mysql: WITH CoreFeaturesRanked AS (SELECT e.edition_name, f.feature_name, ef.is_core_feature, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY e.edition_id ORDER BY f.feature_id) AS feature_rank FROM editions AS e JOIN edition_features AS ef ON e.edition_id = ef.edition_id JOIN features AS f ON ef.feature_id = f.feature_id WHERE e.is_latest = 1 AND e.is_popular = 1 AND ef.is_core_feature = 1) SELECT edition_name, GROUP_CONCAT(feature_name SEPARATOR ', ') AS core_features FROM CoreFeaturesRanked WHERE feature_rank <= 3 GROUP BY edition_name
gold_sql.postgres: WITH CoreFeaturesRanked AS (SELECT e.edition_name, f.feature_name, ef.is_core_feature, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY e.edition_id ORDER BY f.feature_id NULLS FIRST) AS feature_rank FROM editions AS e JOIN edition_features AS ef ON e.edition_id = ef.edition_id JOIN features AS f ON ef.feature_id = f.feature_id WHERE e.is_latest = 1 AND e.is_popular = 1 AND ef.is_core_feature = 1) SELECT edition_name, STRING_AGG(feature_name, ', ') AS core_features FROM CoreFeaturesRanked WHERE feature_rank <= 3 GROUP BY edition_name

question: Which tools have sailed the stormy seas of the latest fiscal year's high-budget projects, and how many times did they navigate those turbulent waters?
external_knowledge:
- "sailed the stormy seas" refers to being used in projects.
- "fiscal year's high-budget projects" means projects with start dates between 2023-01-01 and 2023-12-31 and budgets over $2,000,000.
- "navigated those turbulent waters" symbolically refers to the frequency of tool usage in the projects.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT tools.tool_name, SUM(project_tools.usage_count) AS tool_usage_count FROM projects INNER JOIN project_tools ON projects.project_id = project_tools.project_id INNER JOIN tools ON project_tools.tool_id = tools.tool_id WHERE projects.start_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-12-31' AND CAST(REPLACE(trim(projects.budget, '$'), ',', '') AS REAL) > 2000000 GROUP BY tools.tool_name ORDER BY tool_usage_count DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT tools.tool_name, SUM(project_tools.usage_count) AS tool_usage_count FROM projects INNER JOIN project_tools ON projects.project_id = project_tools.project_id INNER JOIN tools ON project_tools.tool_id = tools.tool_id WHERE projects.start_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-12-31' AND CAST(REPLACE(TRIM('$' FROM projects.budget), ',', '') AS FLOAT) > 2000000 GROUP BY tools.tool_name ORDER BY tool_usage_count DESC
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT tools.tool_name, SUM(project_tools.usage_count) AS tool_usage_count FROM projects INNER JOIN project_tools ON projects.project_id = project_tools.project_id INNER JOIN tools ON project_tools.tool_id = tools.tool_id WHERE projects.start_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-12-31' AND CAST(REPLACE(TRIM('$' FROM projects.budget), ',', '') AS REAL) > 2000000 GROUP BY tools.tool_name ORDER BY tool_usage_count DESC NULLS LAST

question: Find the number of torchbearers in the Admin Group who have the power to write and shine brightly in the organization.
external_knowledge: 'Torchbearers' refers to active users who are part of the organization and have the necessary permissions; 'shine brightly' means the users and their permissions are active; 'power to write' corresponds to the 'Write' permission.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT u.usrkeypk) AS active_users_with_write_permission FROM users u JOIN permission_assignments pa ON u.usrkeypk = pa.usrkeypk JOIN permissions p ON pa.permissionpk = p.permissionpk JOIN group_memberships gm ON u.usrkeypk = gm.usrkeypk JOIN groups g ON gm.grpkeypk = g.grpkeypk WHERE u.is_active = 1 AND p.name = 'Write' AND g.name = 'Admin Group' AND pa.is_active = 1 AND gm.is_active = 1
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT u.usrkeypk) AS active_users_with_write_permission FROM users AS u JOIN permission_assignments AS pa ON u.usrkeypk = pa.usrkeypk JOIN permissions AS p ON pa.permissionpk = p.permissionpk JOIN group_memberships AS gm ON u.usrkeypk = gm.usrkeypk JOIN `groups` AS g ON gm.grpkeypk = g.grpkeypk WHERE u.is_active = 1 AND p.name = 'Write' AND g.name = 'Admin Group' AND pa.is_active = 1 AND gm.is_active = 1
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT u.usrkeypk) AS active_users_with_write_permission FROM users AS u JOIN permission_assignments AS pa ON u.usrkeypk = pa.usrkeypk JOIN permissions AS p ON pa.permissionpk = p.permissionpk JOIN group_memberships AS gm ON u.usrkeypk = gm.usrkeypk JOIN groups AS g ON gm.grpkeypk = g.grpkeypk WHERE u.is_active = 1 AND p.name = 'Write' AND g.name = 'Admin Group' AND pa.is_active = 1 AND gm.is_active = 1

question: Find the top-performing players in each tournament, including their names, playing styles, the tournaments they participated in, their ranks, the teams they played for, and the names of their coaches.
external_knowledge: Top-performing players refers to those who have the highest rank in a tournament, meaning they achieved the best results among all participants; A player's performance summary is a way to describe their achievement in a tournament, including their personal details, the tournament they participated in, and the team they were part of.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH PlayerTournamentStats AS ( SELECT p.player_name, p.playing_style, t.tournament_name, tr.rank, te.team_name, c.coach_name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY tr.tournament_id ORDER BY tr.rank ASC) as player_rank_in_tournament FROM players p INNER JOIN tournament_results tr ON p.player_id = tr.player_id INNER JOIN tournaments t ON tr.tournament_id = t.tournament_id INNER JOIN teams te ON p.team_id = te.team_id INNER JOIN coaches c ON te.coach_id = c.coach_id ) SELECT player_name || ', ' || playing_style || ', participated in ' || tournament_name || ', ranked ' || rank || ' for team ' || team_name || ', coached by ' || coach_name AS player_performance_summary FROM PlayerTournamentStats WHERE player_rank_in_tournament = 1 ORDER BY tournament_name, player_name
gold_sql.mysql: WITH PlayerTournamentStats AS (SELECT p.player_name, p.playing_style, t.tournament_name, tr.`rank`, te.team_name, c.coach_name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY tr.tournament_id ORDER BY tr.`rank` ASC) AS player_rank_in_tournament FROM players AS p INNER JOIN tournament_results AS tr ON p.player_id = tr.player_id INNER JOIN tournaments AS t ON tr.tournament_id = t.tournament_id INNER JOIN teams AS te ON p.team_id = te.team_id INNER JOIN coaches AS c ON te.coach_id = c.coach_id) SELECT CONCAT(player_name, ', ', playing_style, ', participated in ', tournament_name, ', ranked ', `rank`, ' for team ', team_name, ', coached by ', coach_name) AS player_performance_summary FROM PlayerTournamentStats WHERE player_rank_in_tournament = 1 ORDER BY tournament_name, player_name
gold_sql.postgres: WITH PlayerTournamentStats AS (SELECT p.player_name, p.playing_style, t.tournament_name, tr.rank, te.team_name, c.coach_name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY tr.tournament_id ORDER BY tr.rank ASC NULLS FIRST) AS player_rank_in_tournament FROM players AS p INNER JOIN tournament_results AS tr ON p.player_id = tr.player_id INNER JOIN tournaments AS t ON tr.tournament_id = t.tournament_id INNER JOIN teams AS te ON p.team_id = te.team_id INNER JOIN coaches AS c ON te.coach_id = c.coach_id) SELECT player_name || ', ' || playing_style || ', participated in ' || tournament_name || ', ranked ' || rank || ' for team ' || team_name || ', coached by ' || coach_name AS player_performance_summary FROM PlayerTournamentStats WHERE player_rank_in_tournament = 1 ORDER BY tournament_name NULLS FIRST, player_name NULLS FIRST

question: Could you tell me what databases are in high demand and why, for each respondent who has an accepted job match?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RespondentsWithAcceptedJobs AS ( SELECT jm.respondent_id FROM job_matching jm WHERE jm.status = 'Accepted' ) SELECT rwa.respondent_id, GROUP_CONCAT(idb.database || ' - ' || idb.reason, '; ') AS in_demand_databases FROM RespondentsWithAcceptedJobs rwa JOIN in_demand_databases idb ON rwa.respondent_id = idb.respondent_id GROUP BY rwa.respondent_id
gold_sql.mysql: WITH RespondentsWithAcceptedJobs AS (SELECT jm.respondent_id FROM job_matching AS jm WHERE jm.status = 'Accepted') SELECT rwa.respondent_id, GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(idb.`database`, ' - ', idb.reason) SEPARATOR '; ') AS in_demand_databases FROM RespondentsWithAcceptedJobs AS rwa JOIN in_demand_databases AS idb ON rwa.respondent_id = idb.respondent_id GROUP BY rwa.respondent_id
gold_sql.postgres: WITH RespondentsWithAcceptedJobs AS (SELECT jm.respondent_id FROM job_matching AS jm WHERE jm.status = 'Accepted') SELECT rwa.respondent_id, STRING_AGG(idb.database || ' - ' || idb.reason, '; ') AS in_demand_databases FROM RespondentsWithAcceptedJobs AS rwa JOIN in_demand_databases AS idb ON rwa.respondent_id = idb.respondent_id GROUP BY rwa.respondent_id

question: Could you please count how many reviews were written by users who joined the platform in 2023? I need the total count of these reviews!

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT COUNT(tr.review_id) FROM trail_reviews tr JOIN users u ON tr.user_id = u.user_id WHERE strftime('%Y', u.date_joined) = '2023'
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT COUNT(tr.review_id) FROM trail_reviews AS tr JOIN users AS u ON tr.user_id = u.user_id WHERE DATE_FORMAT(CAST(u.date_joined AS DATETIME), '%Y') = '2023'
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT COUNT(tr.review_id) FROM trail_reviews AS tr JOIN users AS u ON tr.user_id = u.user_id WHERE TO_CHAR(CAST(u.date_joined AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY') = '2023'

question: Could you provide the names of the filmmakers, the number of shows they have directed, the names of the series they are associated with, the typical rating of these series, the titles of their episodes, and the total number of viewers for their works?
external_knowledge:
- 'Filmmakers' are synonymous with 'directors'.
- 'Shows' refers to 'episodes' in this context.
- 'Typical rating' is understood as the 'average rating' of the series.
- 'Works' in the context of the filmmakers are the episodes they direct.
- The total viewership is the combined viewership of all episodes directed by each filmmaker.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT d.director_name, COUNT(e.episode_id) AS number_of_episodes, s.series_name, s.average_rating, GROUP_CONCAT(e.title, ', ') AS episode_titles, SUM(vs.viewer_count) AS total_viewers FROM directors d INNER JOIN episodes e ON d.director_id = e.director_id INNER JOIN series s ON e.series_id = s.series_id INNER JOIN viewer_stats vs ON e.episode_id = vs.episode_id GROUP BY d.director_name, s.series_name, s.average_rating ORDER BY d.director_name, s.series_name
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT d.director_name, COUNT(e.episode_id) AS number_of_episodes, s.series_name, s.average_rating, GROUP_CONCAT(e.title SEPARATOR ', ') AS episode_titles, SUM(vs.viewer_count) AS total_viewers FROM directors AS d INNER JOIN episodes AS e ON d.director_id = e.director_id INNER JOIN series AS s ON e.series_id = s.series_id INNER JOIN viewer_stats AS vs ON e.episode_id = vs.episode_id GROUP BY d.director_name, s.series_name, s.average_rating ORDER BY d.director_name, s.series_name
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT d.director_name, COUNT(e.episode_id) AS number_of_episodes, s.series_name, s.average_rating, STRING_AGG(e.title, ', ') AS episode_titles, SUM(vs.viewer_count) AS total_viewers FROM directors AS d INNER JOIN episodes AS e ON d.director_id = e.director_id INNER JOIN series AS s ON e.series_id = s.series_id INNER JOIN viewer_stats AS vs ON e.episode_id = vs.episode_id GROUP BY d.director_name, s.series_name, s.average_rating ORDER BY d.director_name NULLS FIRST, s.series_name NULLS FIRST

question: What is the average number of extra hours that respondents in each age group are willing to work, considering only those with at least 3 years of freelancing experience?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT r.age_group, AVG(r.willing_to_work_extra_hours) AS avg_extra_hours FROM respondents r INNER JOIN freelancing_experience fe ON r.respondent_id = fe.respondent_id WHERE CAST(SUBSTR(fe.years_of_experience, 1, INSTR(fe.years_of_experience, '-') - 1) AS INTEGER) >= 3 GROUP BY r.age_group
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT r.age_group, AVG(r.willing_to_work_extra_hours) AS avg_extra_hours FROM respondents AS r INNER JOIN freelancing_experience AS fe ON r.respondent_id = fe.respondent_id WHERE CAST(SUBSTRING(fe.years_of_experience, 1, LOCATE('-', fe.years_of_experience) - 1) AS SIGNED) >= 3 GROUP BY r.age_group
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT r.age_group, AVG(r.willing_to_work_extra_hours) AS avg_extra_hours FROM respondents AS r INNER JOIN freelancing_experience AS fe ON r.respondent_id = fe.respondent_id WHERE CAST(SUBSTRING(fe.years_of_experience FROM 1 FOR STRPOS(fe.years_of_experience, '-') - 1) AS INT) >= 3 GROUP BY r.age_group

question: For data samples of the 'Ordinal' type added in 2023, return the type name, sample value, and the username of the user who added the sample.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT mt.type_name, ds.sample_value, u.username FROM measurement_types mt JOIN data_samples ds ON mt.type_id = ds.type_id JOIN users u ON ds.created_by = u.user_id WHERE mt.type_name = 'Ordinal' AND strftime('%Y', ds.created_at) = '2023'
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT mt.type_name, ds.sample_value, u.username FROM measurement_types AS mt JOIN data_samples AS ds ON mt.type_id = ds.type_id JOIN users AS u ON ds.created_by = u.user_id WHERE mt.type_name = 'Ordinal' AND DATE_FORMAT(CAST(ds.created_at AS DATETIME), '%Y') = '2023'
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT mt.type_name, ds.sample_value, u.username FROM measurement_types AS mt JOIN data_samples AS ds ON mt.type_id = ds.type_id JOIN users AS u ON ds.created_by = u.user_id WHERE mt.type_name = 'Ordinal' AND TO_CHAR(CAST(ds.created_at AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY') = '2023'

question: How many times did users access protectionist trade policy entities in 1970?
external_knowledge: Protectionist trade policy refers to economic policies that regulate international trade through government intervention, often to restrict imports and promote domestic industries; The year 1970 is a specific point in time for which access events are being counted.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT COUNT(a.access_id) AS access_count FROM access_logs a JOIN entities e ON a.data_id = e.entity_id WHERE e.trade_policy_type = 'protectionist' AND strftime('%Y', a.access_date) = '1970'
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT COUNT(a.access_id) AS access_count FROM access_logs AS a JOIN entities AS e ON a.data_id = e.entity_id WHERE e.trade_policy_type = 'protectionist' AND DATE_FORMAT(CAST(a.access_date AS DATETIME), '%Y') = '1970'
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT COUNT(a.access_id) AS access_count FROM access_logs AS a JOIN entities AS e ON a.data_id = e.entity_id WHERE e.trade_policy_type = 'protectionist' AND TO_CHAR(CAST(a.access_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY') = '1970'

question: Could you provide a comprehensive overview of each media record, including their titles, descriptions, statuses, creation and last modified dates, tags, file URLs, thumbnail URLs, production session counts, company names, performer names, media types, formats, languages, total distributed quantities, access counts, and total session durations, ordered alphabetically by title?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH MediaProductions AS ( SELECT mp.media_id, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY mp.media_id) AS session_count FROM media_production mp ), MediaDistributions AS ( SELECT md.media_id, SUM(md.quantity) OVER (PARTITION BY md.media_id) AS total_distributed FROM media_distribution md ), MediaAccesses AS ( SELECT ma.media_id, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY ma.media_id) AS access_count, SUM(CAST(REPLACE(ma.session_duration, ' minutes', '') AS INTEGER)) OVER (PARTITION BY ma.media_id) AS total_session_duration FROM media_access ma ) SELECT mr.title, mr.description, mr.status, mr.creation_date, mr.last_modified_date, mr.tags, mr.file_url, mr.thumbnail_url, COALESCE(mp.session_count, 0) AS session_count, c.company_name, p.performer_name, mt.type_name, mf.format_name, l.language_name, COALESCE(md_distributions.total_distributed, 0) AS total_distributed, COALESCE(md_accesses.access_count, 0) AS access_count, COALESCE(md_accesses.total_session_duration, 0) AS total_session_duration FROM media_records mr LEFT JOIN performers p ON mr.primary_performer_id = p.performer_id LEFT JOIN companies c ON mr.company_id = c.company_id LEFT JOIN media_types mt ON mr.media_type_id = mt.type_id LEFT JOIN media_formats mf ON mr.format_id = mf.format_id LEFT JOIN languages l ON mr.language_id = l.language_id LEFT JOIN MediaProductions mp ON mr.media_id = mp.media_id LEFT JOIN MediaDistributions md_distributions ON mr.media_id = md_distributions.media_id LEFT JOIN MediaAccesses md_accesses ON mr.media_id = md_accesses.media_id ORDER BY mr.title
gold_sql.mysql: WITH MediaProductions AS (SELECT mp.media_id, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY mp.media_id) AS session_count FROM media_production AS mp), MediaDistributions AS (SELECT md.media_id, SUM(md.quantity) OVER (PARTITION BY md.media_id) AS total_distributed FROM media_distribution AS md), MediaAccesses AS (SELECT ma.media_id, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY ma.media_id) AS access_count, SUM(CAST(REPLACE(ma.session_duration, ' minutes', '') AS SIGNED)) OVER (PARTITION BY ma.media_id) AS total_session_duration FROM media_access AS ma) SELECT mr.title, mr.description, mr.status, mr.creation_date, mr.last_modified_date, mr.tags, mr.file_url, mr.thumbnail_url, COALESCE(mp.session_count, 0) AS session_count, c.company_name, p.performer_name, mt.type_name, mf.format_name, l.language_name, COALESCE(md_distributions.total_distributed, 0) AS total_distributed, COALESCE(md_accesses.access_count, 0) AS access_count, COALESCE(md_accesses.total_session_duration, 0) AS total_session_duration FROM media_records AS mr LEFT JOIN performers AS p ON mr.primary_performer_id = p.performer_id LEFT JOIN companies AS c ON mr.company_id = c.company_id LEFT JOIN media_types AS mt ON mr.media_type_id = mt.type_id LEFT JOIN media_formats AS mf ON mr.format_id = mf.format_id LEFT JOIN languages AS l ON mr.language_id = l.language_id LEFT JOIN MediaProductions AS mp ON mr.media_id = mp.media_id LEFT JOIN MediaDistributions AS md_distributions ON mr.media_id = md_distributions.media_id LEFT JOIN MediaAccesses AS md_accesses ON mr.media_id = md_accesses.media_id ORDER BY mr.title
gold_sql.postgres: WITH MediaProductions AS (SELECT mp.media_id, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY mp.media_id) AS session_count FROM media_production AS mp), MediaDistributions AS (SELECT md.media_id, SUM(md.quantity) OVER (PARTITION BY md.media_id) AS total_distributed FROM media_distribution AS md), MediaAccesses AS (SELECT ma.media_id, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY ma.media_id) AS access_count, SUM(CAST(REPLACE(ma.session_duration, ' minutes', '') AS INT)) OVER (PARTITION BY ma.media_id) AS total_session_duration FROM media_access AS ma) SELECT mr.title, mr.description, mr.status, mr.creation_date, mr.last_modified_date, mr.tags, mr.file_url, mr.thumbnail_url, COALESCE(mp.session_count, 0) AS session_count, c.company_name, p.performer_name, mt.type_name, mf.format_name, l.language_name, COALESCE(md_distributions.total_distributed, 0) AS total_distributed, COALESCE(md_accesses.access_count, 0) AS access_count, COALESCE(md_accesses.total_session_duration, 0) AS total_session_duration FROM media_records AS mr LEFT JOIN performers AS p ON mr.primary_performer_id = p.performer_id LEFT JOIN companies AS c ON mr.company_id = c.company_id LEFT JOIN media_types AS mt ON mr.media_type_id = mt.type_id LEFT JOIN media_formats AS mf ON mr.format_id = mf.format_id LEFT JOIN languages AS l ON mr.language_id = l.language_id LEFT JOIN MediaProductions AS mp ON mr.media_id = mp.media_id LEFT JOIN MediaDistributions AS md_distributions ON mr.media_id = md_distributions.media_id LEFT JOIN MediaAccesses AS md_accesses ON mr.media_id = md_accesses.media_id ORDER BY mr.title NULLS FIRST

question: I want to know the titles of all active journals along with the number of articles in each journal and their average impact factor values, excluding journals with no articles or unknown average impact factors.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT j.title AS Journal_Title, COUNT(a.article_id) AS Article_Count, AVG(if.impact_factor_value) AS Average_Impact_Factor FROM journals j JOIN articles a ON j.journal_id = a.issue_id JOIN impact_factors if ON j.journal_id = if.journal_id WHERE j.status = 'active' GROUP BY j.title HAVING COUNT(a.article_id) > 0 AND AVG(if.impact_factor_value) IS NOT NULL
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT j.title AS Journal_Title, COUNT(a.article_id) AS Article_Count, AVG(`if`.impact_factor_value) AS Average_Impact_Factor FROM journals AS j JOIN articles AS a ON j.journal_id = a.issue_id JOIN impact_factors AS `if` ON j.journal_id = `if`.journal_id WHERE j.status = 'active' GROUP BY j.title HAVING COUNT(a.article_id) > 0 AND NOT AVG(`if`.impact_factor_value) IS NULL
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT j.title AS Journal_Title, COUNT(a.article_id) AS Article_Count, AVG(if.impact_factor_value) AS Average_Impact_Factor FROM journals AS j JOIN articles AS a ON j.journal_id = a.issue_id JOIN impact_factors AS if ON j.journal_id = if.journal_id WHERE j.status = 'active' GROUP BY j.title HAVING COUNT(a.article_id) > 0 AND NOT AVG(if.impact_factor_value) IS NULL

question: Could you tell me the average value of the parameters for each function and module combination, but only for those combinations that have more than one parameter in the preset?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT f.function_name AS function, m.module_name AS module, AVG(pp.value) AS average_preset_value FROM preset_parameters AS pp JOIN parameters AS p ON pp.param_id = p.param_id JOIN functions AS f ON p.function_id = f.function_id JOIN modules AS m ON p.module_id = m.module_id GROUP BY f.function_name, m.module_name HAVING COUNT(pp.param_id) > 1
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT f.function_name AS `function`, m.module_name AS module, AVG(pp.value) AS average_preset_value FROM preset_parameters AS pp JOIN parameters AS p ON pp.param_id = p.param_id JOIN functions AS f ON p.function_id = f.function_id JOIN modules AS m ON p.module_id = m.module_id GROUP BY f.function_name, m.module_name HAVING COUNT(pp.param_id) > 1

question: Could you provide the weather checking methods used by active respondents in US region 1, along with the count of respondents using each method, and the corresponding age ranges, genders, and likelihoods of using a smartwatch, for respondents who check the weather daily?

question: What is the cumulative placement performance of each branch over the years, metaphorically like the growth rings of a tree, where each ring represents the number of students placed in a given year?
external_knowledge:
- 'cumulative placement performance' refers to the total number of students placed over the years for each branch.
- 'growth rings of a tree' is a metaphor to illustrate the cumulative nature of the placement data, with each year's placements adding a new ring to the branch's performance.
- 'placed students' include both on-campus and off-campus placements.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH BranchPlacementStats AS ( SELECT b.branch_name, ps.year, ps.total_students_placed FROM branches b INNER JOIN placement_stats ps ON b.branch_id = ps.branch_id ), CumulativePlacements AS ( SELECT bps.branch_name, bps.year, SUM(bps.total_students_placed) OVER (PARTITION BY bps.branch_name ORDER BY bps.year) AS cumulative_placed FROM BranchPlacementStats bps ) SELECT cp.branch_name || ', ' || cp.year || ': ' || CAST(cp.cumulative_placed AS TEXT) AS cumulative_placement_performance FROM CumulativePlacements cp ORDER BY cp.branch_name, cp.year

question: Find a comprehensive list of shared datasets, including their names, versions, owners, permission levels, creation and update dates, statuses, variable names, data types, units, descriptions, and attribute details, representing a complete picture of all shared datasets and their characteristics.
external_knowledge: This query assumes that a shared dataset refers to a dataset that has been shared with one or more users through the dataset_sharing table; a comprehensive list refers to a detailed view of all available information about the shared datasets; a complete picture refers to a collection of all relevant attributes and characteristics of the shared datasets.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH SharedDatasets AS ( SELECT d.dataset_id, d.name AS dataset_name, d.version, ds.user_id, u.name AS user_name, ds.permission, d.created_date, d.updated_date, d.status FROM datasets d JOIN dataset_sharing ds ON d.dataset_id = ds.dataset_id JOIN users u ON ds.user_id = u.user_id ), DatasetAttributes AS ( SELECT v.variable_id, v.dataset_id, v.name AS variable_name, v.data_type, v.unit, v.description, GROUP_CONCAT(a.name || ': ' || a.value, ', ') AS attribute_details FROM variables v LEFT JOIN attributes a ON v.variable_id = a.variable_id GROUP BY v.variable_id, v.dataset_id, v.name, v.data_type, v.unit, v.description ), CombinedView AS ( SELECT sd.dataset_name, sd.version, sd.user_name, sd.permission, sd.created_date, sd.updated_date, sd.status, da.variable_name, da.data_type, da.unit, da.description, da.attribute_details FROM SharedDatasets sd LEFT JOIN DatasetAttributes da ON sd.dataset_id = da.dataset_id ) SELECT dataset_name || ' - ' || version || ' - ' || user_name || ' - ' || permission || ' - ' || created_date || ' - ' || updated_date || ' - ' || status || ' - ' || COALESCE(variable_name, 'No Variable') || ' - ' || COALESCE(data_type, 'No Type') || ' - ' || COALESCE(unit, 'No Unit') || ' - ' || COALESCE(description, 'No Description') || ' - ' || COALESCE(attribute_details, 'No Attributes') AS combined_details FROM CombinedView

question: Could you please count the number of schools that have an average total rushing yards greater than 1750 in the first season?

question: What are the names of the top 3 most accessed videos, along with the names of the users who accessed them the most, the total number of times each video was accessed by these users, and any available annotations for these videos?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH UserAccessFrequency AS ( SELECT user_id, video_id, COUNT(*) AS access_count, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY video_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS user_rank FROM access_logs GROUP BY user_id, video_id ), TopAccessedVideos AS ( SELECT video_id, access_count, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY access_count DESC) AS video_rank FROM UserAccessFrequency WHERE user_rank = 1 ), VideoAnnotations AS ( SELECT video_id, GROUP_CONCAT(annotation, ', ') AS video_annotations FROM frame_annotations fa INNER JOIN frames f ON fa.frame_id = f.frame_id GROUP BY video_id ) SELECT v.video_name, u.user_name, tav.access_count, va.video_annotations FROM TopAccessedVideos tav INNER JOIN UserAccessFrequency vaf ON tav.video_id = vaf.video_id AND vaf.user_rank = 1 INNER JOIN videos v ON tav.video_id = v.video_id INNER JOIN users u ON vaf.user_id = u.user_id LEFT JOIN VideoAnnotations va ON tav.video_id = va.video_id WHERE tav.video_rank <= 3 ORDER BY tav.video_rank
gold_sql.mysql: WITH UserAccessFrequency AS (SELECT user_id, video_id, COUNT(*) AS access_count, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY video_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS user_rank FROM access_logs GROUP BY user_id, video_id), TopAccessedVideos AS (SELECT video_id, access_count, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY access_count DESC) AS video_rank FROM UserAccessFrequency WHERE user_rank = 1), VideoAnnotations AS (SELECT video_id, GROUP_CONCAT(annotation SEPARATOR ', ') AS video_annotations FROM frame_annotations AS fa INNER JOIN frames AS f ON fa.frame_id = f.frame_id GROUP BY video_id) SELECT v.video_name, u.user_name, tav.access_count, va.video_annotations FROM TopAccessedVideos AS tav INNER JOIN UserAccessFrequency AS vaf ON tav.video_id = vaf.video_id AND vaf.user_rank = 1 INNER JOIN videos AS v ON tav.video_id = v.video_id INNER JOIN users AS u ON vaf.user_id = u.user_id LEFT JOIN VideoAnnotations AS va ON tav.video_id = va.video_id WHERE tav.video_rank <= 3 ORDER BY tav.video_rank
gold_sql.postgres: WITH UserAccessFrequency AS (SELECT user_id, video_id, COUNT(*) AS access_count, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY video_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC NULLS LAST) AS user_rank FROM access_logs GROUP BY user_id, video_id), TopAccessedVideos AS (SELECT video_id, access_count, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY access_count DESC NULLS LAST) AS video_rank FROM UserAccessFrequency WHERE user_rank = 1), VideoAnnotations AS (SELECT video_id, STRING_AGG(annotation, ', ') AS video_annotations FROM frame_annotations AS fa INNER JOIN frames AS f ON fa.frame_id = f.frame_id GROUP BY video_id) SELECT v.video_name, u.user_name, tav.access_count, va.video_annotations FROM TopAccessedVideos AS tav INNER JOIN UserAccessFrequency AS vaf ON tav.video_id = vaf.video_id AND vaf.user_rank = 1 INNER JOIN videos AS v ON tav.video_id = v.video_id INNER JOIN users AS u ON vaf.user_id = u.user_id LEFT JOIN VideoAnnotations AS va ON tav.video_id = va.video_id WHERE tav.video_rank <= 3 ORDER BY tav.video_rank NULLS FIRST

question: Return the top 5 sites with the highest daily traffic for each month, including their site names, locations, latitudes, longitudes, total vehicles, daily ranks, daily total vehicles, daily average vehicles, monthly total vehicles, and monthly average vehicles.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH DailyTraffic AS ( SELECT td.site_id, DATE(td.collection_date) AS date, SUM(td.total_vehicle_count) AS total_vehicles FROM traffic_data td GROUP BY td.site_id, DATE(td.collection_date) ), SiteDetails AS ( SELECT dt.site_id, dt.date, dt.total_vehicles, ms.site_name, ms.location, ms.latitude, ms.longitude FROM DailyTraffic dt INNER JOIN monitoring_sites ms ON dt.site_id = ms.site_id ), DailyRanks AS ( SELECT sd.site_id, sd.date, sd.total_vehicles, sd.site_name, sd.location, sd.latitude, sd.longitude, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sd.date ORDER BY sd.total_vehicles DESC) AS daily_rank, SUM(sd.total_vehicles) OVER (PARTITION BY sd.date) AS daily_total_vehicles, AVG(sd.total_vehicles) OVER (PARTITION BY sd.date) AS daily_avg_vehicles FROM SiteDetails sd ), MonthlyTraffic AS ( SELECT dr.site_id, dr.date, dr.total_vehicles, dr.site_name, dr.location, dr.latitude, dr.longitude, dr.daily_rank, dr.daily_total_vehicles, dr.daily_avg_vehicles, STRFTIME('%Y-%m', dr.date) AS month, SUM(dr.total_vehicles) OVER (PARTITION BY STRFTIME('%Y-%m', dr.date)) AS monthly_total_vehicles, AVG(dr.total_vehicles) OVER (PARTITION BY STRFTIME('%Y-%m', dr.date)) AS monthly_avg_vehicles FROM DailyRanks dr ) SELECT mt.month, mt.site_id, mt.site_name, mt.location, mt.latitude, mt.longitude, mt.total_vehicles, mt.daily_rank, mt.daily_total_vehicles, mt.daily_avg_vehicles, mt.monthly_total_vehicles, mt.monthly_avg_vehicles FROM MonthlyTraffic mt WHERE mt.daily_rank <= 5 ORDER BY mt.month, mt.daily_rank

gold_sql.postgres: WITH DailyTraffic AS (SELECT td.site_id, DATE(td.collection_date) AS date, SUM(td.total_vehicle_count) AS total_vehicles FROM traffic_data AS td GROUP BY td.site_id, DATE(td.collection_date)), SiteDetails AS (SELECT dt.site_id, dt.date, dt.total_vehicles, ms.site_name, ms.location, ms.latitude, ms.longitude FROM DailyTraffic AS dt INNER JOIN monitoring_sites AS ms ON dt.site_id = ms.site_id), DailyRanks AS (SELECT sd.site_id, sd.date, sd.total_vehicles, sd.site_name, sd.location, sd.latitude, sd.longitude, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sd.date ORDER BY sd.total_vehicles DESC NULLS LAST) AS daily_rank, SUM(sd.total_vehicles) OVER (PARTITION BY sd.date) AS daily_total_vehicles, AVG(sd.total_vehicles) OVER (PARTITION BY sd.date) AS daily_avg_vehicles FROM SiteDetails AS sd), MonthlyTraffic AS (SELECT dr.site_id, dr.date, dr.total_vehicles, dr.site_name, dr.location, dr.latitude, dr.longitude, dr.daily_rank, dr.daily_total_vehicles, dr.daily_avg_vehicles, TO_CHAR(CAST(dr.date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY-MM') AS month, SUM(dr.total_vehicles) OVER (PARTITION BY TO_CHAR(CAST(dr.date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY-MM')) AS monthly_total_vehicles, AVG(dr.total_vehicles) OVER (PARTITION BY TO_CHAR(CAST(dr.date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY-MM')) AS monthly_avg_vehicles FROM DailyRanks AS dr) SELECT mt.month, mt.site_id, mt.site_name, mt.location, mt.latitude, mt.longitude, mt.total_vehicles, mt.daily_rank, mt.daily_total_vehicles, mt.daily_avg_vehicles, mt.monthly_total_vehicles, mt.monthly_avg_vehicles FROM MonthlyTraffic AS mt WHERE mt.daily_rank <= 5 ORDER BY mt.month NULLS FIRST, mt.daily_rank NULLS FIRST

question: What is the detailed information, including the data point ID, boolean value, data source name, data category name, data subcategory name, data unit name, and all associated comments (or 'No comments' if none exist), for all data points where the boolean value is true?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT dp.id AS data_point_id, dp.bool_col AS bool_value, ds.data_source_name AS source_name, dc.data_category_name AS category_name, dsc.data_subcategory_name AS subcategory_name, du.data_unit_name AS unit_name, COALESCE(GROUP_CONCAT(dpc.comment, '; '), 'No comments') AS comments FROM data_points dp JOIN data_sources ds ON dp.data_source_id = ds.data_source_id JOIN data_categories dc ON dp.data_category_id = dc.data_category_id JOIN data_subcategories dsc ON dp.data_subcategory_id = dsc.data_subcategory_id JOIN data_units du ON dp.data_unit_id = du.data_unit_id LEFT JOIN data_point_comments dpc ON dp.id = dpc.data_point_id WHERE dp.bool_col = 1 GROUP BY dp.id, dp.bool_col, ds.data_source_name, dc.data_category_name, dsc.data_subcategory_name, du.data_unit_name
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT dp.id AS data_point_id, dp.bool_col AS bool_value, ds.data_source_name AS source_name, dc.data_category_name AS category_name, dsc.data_subcategory_name AS subcategory_name, du.data_unit_name AS unit_name, COALESCE(GROUP_CONCAT(dpc.comment SEPARATOR '; '), 'No comments') AS comments FROM data_points AS dp JOIN data_sources AS ds ON dp.data_source_id = ds.data_source_id JOIN data_categories AS dc ON dp.data_category_id = dc.data_category_id JOIN data_subcategories AS dsc ON dp.data_subcategory_id = dsc.data_subcategory_id JOIN data_units AS du ON dp.data_unit_id = du.data_unit_id LEFT JOIN data_point_comments AS dpc ON dp.id = dpc.data_point_id WHERE dp.bool_col = 1 GROUP BY dp.id, dp.bool_col, ds.data_source_name, dc.data_category_name, dsc.data_subcategory_name, du.data_unit_name

question:

**User**: Just the names and the number of updates.
**Assistant**: Got it. Is there a specific threshold for the number of updates, or should I include all products that have had at least one update?
**User**: Include all products that have had at least one update.
**Assistant**: Understood. I will help you create an SQL query to get the names of the software products and the total number of database updates they have had, excluding any products that have not had any updates. Is there anything else you need?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT sp.product_name, COUNT(du.database_update_id) AS total_updates FROM software_products sp JOIN databases db ON sp.product_id = db.product_id JOIN database_updates du ON db.database_id = du.database_id GROUP BY sp.product_name HAVING COUNT(du.database_update_id) > 0

question: What is the overall performance of researchers across different conditions and test situations, including the total number of researchers, total correct responses, and average researcher success rate for each condition and test situation?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ResearcherCounts AS ( SELECT condition, test_situation, COUNT(DISTINCT researcher_id) AS total_researchers, COUNT(CASE WHEN correct = 1 THEN researcher_id END) AS total_correct_responses FROM experiments GROUP BY condition, test_situation ) SELECT condition, test_situation, total_researchers, total_correct_responses, (total_correct_responses * 1.0 / total_researchers) AS average_researcher_success_rate FROM ResearcherCounts ORDER BY condition, test_situation
gold_sql.mysql: WITH ResearcherCounts AS (SELECT `condition`, test_situation, COUNT(DISTINCT researcher_id) AS total_researchers, COUNT(CASE WHEN correct = 1 THEN researcher_id END) AS total_correct_responses FROM experiments GROUP BY `condition`, test_situation) SELECT `condition`, test_situation, total_researchers, total_correct_responses, (total_correct_responses * 1.0 / total_researchers) AS average_researcher_success_rate FROM ResearcherCounts ORDER BY `condition`, test_situation
gold_sql.postgres: WITH ResearcherCounts AS (SELECT condition, test_situation, COUNT(DISTINCT researcher_id) AS total_researchers, COUNT(CASE WHEN correct = 1 THEN researcher_id END) AS total_correct_responses FROM experiments GROUP BY condition, test_situation) SELECT condition, test_situation, total_researchers, total_correct_responses, (total_correct_responses * 1.0 / NULLIF(total_researchers, 0)) AS average_researcher_success_rate FROM ResearcherCounts ORDER BY condition NULLS FIRST, test_situation NULLS FIRST

question: Find the top 10 most active stock symbols in January 2023, noting their average opening and closing prices during that month, as well as the number of unique users who checked their data; rank the symbols by trading volume and present the results in a formatted string.
external_knowledge: January 2023 refers to the period between January 1st, 2023, and January 31st, 2023; trading volume refers to the total amount of a stock traded during a given period; active stock symbols are those with high trading volumes.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH TopSymbols AS ( SELECT sp.symbol_id, SUM(tv.volume) AS total_volume FROM stock_prices sp JOIN trading_volumes tv ON sp.price_id = tv.price_id WHERE sp.time BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-01-31' GROUP BY sp.symbol_id ORDER BY total_volume DESC LIMIT 10 ), SymbolPrices AS ( SELECT sp.symbol_id, AVG(CAST(sp.open AS REAL)) AS avg_open, AVG(CAST(sp.close AS REAL)) AS avg_close FROM TopSymbols ts JOIN stock_prices sp ON ts.symbol_id = sp.symbol_id WHERE sp.time BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-01-31' GROUP BY sp.symbol_id ), UserCounts AS ( SELECT sp.symbol_id, COUNT(DISTINCT al.user_id) AS unique_users FROM TopSymbols ts JOIN stock_prices sp ON ts.symbol_id = sp.symbol_id JOIN access_logs al ON sp.price_id = al.price_id WHERE al.access_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-01-31' GROUP BY sp.symbol_id ), FinalResults AS ( SELECT sp.symbol_id, sp.avg_open, sp.avg_close, uc.unique_users FROM SymbolPrices sp JOIN UserCounts uc ON sp.symbol_id = uc.symbol_id ) SELECT GROUP_CONCAT( symbol_id || ': ' || avg_open || ' - ' || avg_close || ' (Users: ' || unique_users || ')', ', ' ) AS result FROM FinalResults

question: Could you tell me the average flight duration in minutes for flights departing from the airport named 'LAX'?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT AVG( (CAST(SUBSTR(arrival_time, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) * 60 + CAST(SUBSTR(arrival_time, 4, 2) AS INTEGER)) - (CAST(SUBSTR(departure_time, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) * 60 + CAST(SUBSTR(departure_time, 4, 2) AS INTEGER)) ) AS average_flight_duration FROM flights JOIN airports ON flights.origin_airport_id = airports.airport_id WHERE airports.airport_name = 'LAX'

question: Could you please provide the total count of records for the top weather data from each station and year, including the corresponding processing and access statistics?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH WeatherTopData AS ( SELECT w.station_id, w.year, w.avg_temp, w.max_temp, w.min_temp, w.rainfall, w.snowfall, w.thunderstorms, w.fog_days, w.tornadoes, w.hail_reports, w.quality_flags, w.data_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY w.station_id, w.year ORDER BY w.avg_temp DESC) AS rn FROM weather_data w ), TopRecords AS ( SELECT wd.station_id, wd.year, wd.avg_temp, wd.max_temp, wd.min_temp, wd.rainfall, wd.snowfall, wd.thunderstorms, wd.fog_days, wd.tornadoes, wd.hail_reports, wd.quality_flags, wd.data_id FROM WeatherTopData wd WHERE wd.rn = 1 ), StationInfo AS ( SELECT ws.station_id, ws.station_name, ws.location FROM weather_stations ws ), ProcessingStats AS ( SELECT dpj.data_id, COUNT(*) AS total_jobs, SUM(CASE WHEN dpj.job_status = 'completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS completed_jobs, SUM(CASE WHEN dpj.job_status = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed_jobs FROM data_processing_jobs dpj GROUP BY dpj.data_id ), AccessStats AS ( SELECT a.data_id, COUNT(*) AS total_accesses, AVG(CAST(strftime('%s', a.access_duration) AS INTEGER)) AS avg_access_duration FROM access_logs a GROUP BY a.data_id ), FinalQuery AS ( SELECT tr.year, si.station_name, si.location, tr.avg_temp, tr.max_temp, tr.min_temp, tr.rainfall, tr.snowfall, tr.thunderstorms, tr.fog_days, tr.tornadoes, tr.hail_reports, tr.quality_flags, COALESCE(ps.total_jobs, 0) AS total_jobs, COALESCE(ps.completed_jobs, 0) AS completed_jobs, COALESCE(ps.failed_jobs, 0) AS failed_jobs, COALESCE(ac.total_accesses, 0) AS total_accesses, COALESCE(ac.avg_access_duration, 0) AS avg_access_duration FROM TopRecords tr INNER JOIN StationInfo si ON tr.station_id = si.station_id LEFT JOIN ProcessingStats ps ON tr.data_id = ps.data_id LEFT JOIN AccessStats ac ON tr.data_id = ac.data_id ) SELECT COUNT(*) AS overall_record_count FROM FinalQuery

question: Could you provide a detailed list of all timing parameters, including their names, descriptions, access counts, last access dates, average values, associated diagram names, categories, versions, notes, and conditions, ordered alphabetically by parameter name?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ParameterAccess AS ( SELECT param_id, COUNT(*) AS access_count, MAX(access_date) AS last_access_date FROM access_logs GROUP BY param_id ), ParameterValues AS ( SELECT param_id, AVG(value) AS average_value FROM parameter_values GROUP BY param_id ), ParameterNotes AS ( SELECT param_id, note FROM notes WHERE priority = 1 ), ParameterConditions AS ( SELECT param_id, condition FROM conditions WHERE priority = 1 ), DiagramDetails AS ( SELECT pv.param_id, GROUP_CONCAT(td.diag_name, ', ') AS diag_names, GROUP_CONCAT(td.category, ', ') AS categories, GROUP_CONCAT(td.version, ', ') AS versions FROM parameter_values pv INNER JOIN timing_diagrams td ON pv.diag_id = td.diag_id GROUP BY pv.param_id ) SELECT tp.param_name, tp.description, COALESCE(pa.access_count, 0) AS access_count, COALESCE(pa.last_access_date, 'Never') AS last_access_date, COALESCE(pv.average_value, 0) AS average_value, COALESCE(dd.diag_names, 'None') AS diag_names, COALESCE(dd.categories, 'None') AS categories, COALESCE(dd.versions, 'None') AS versions, COALESCE(pn.note, 'None') AS note, COALESCE(pc.condition, 'None') AS condition FROM timing_parameters tp LEFT JOIN ParameterAccess pa ON tp.param_id = pa.param_id LEFT JOIN ParameterValues pv ON tp.param_id = pv.param_id LEFT JOIN DiagramDetails dd ON tp.param_id = dd.param_id LEFT JOIN ParameterNotes pn ON tp.param_id = pn.param_id LEFT JOIN ParameterConditions pc ON tp.param_id = pc.param_id ORDER BY tp.param_name

question: Which facilities have the highest total environmental impact, considering both emissions and waste, and what is the total environmental impact for each?
external_knowledge:
- The total environmental impact is calculated by summing the total emissions (CO2 and NOx) and total waste (Solid and Liquid) generated by each facility.
- Emissions are considered to have a significant impact on the environment, particularly CO2 and NOx, which contribute to air pollution and climate change.
- Waste, especially solid and liquid waste, can also have a substantial environmental impact due to potential contamination and resource depletion.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH EmissionsTotal AS ( SELECT facility_id, SUM(amount) AS total_emission FROM emissions WHERE emission_type IN ('CO2', 'NOx') GROUP BY facility_id ), WasteTotal AS ( SELECT facility_id, SUM(amount) AS total_waste FROM waste_generation JOIN waste_types wt ON wt.waste_type_id = waste_generation.waste_type_id WHERE wt.waste_type_name IN ('Solid Waste', 'Liquid Waste') GROUP BY facility_id ), FacilityImpact AS ( SELECT COALESCE(et.facility_id, wt.facility_id) AS facility_id, COALESCE(et.total_emission, 0) AS total_emission, COALESCE(wt.total_waste, 0) AS total_waste, COALESCE(et.total_emission, 0) + COALESCE(wt.total_waste, 0) AS total_environmental_impact FROM EmissionsTotal et FULL OUTER JOIN WasteTotal wt ON et.facility_id = wt.facility_id ) SELECT f.facility_name, fi.total_environmental_impact FROM FacilityImpact fi JOIN facilities f ON fi.facility_id = f.facility_id ORDER BY fi.total_environmental_impact DESC
gold_sql.mysql: WITH EmissionsTotal AS (SELECT facility_id, SUM(amount) AS total_emission FROM emissions WHERE emission_type IN ('CO2', 'NOx') GROUP BY facility_id), WasteTotal AS (SELECT facility_id, SUM(amount) AS total_waste FROM waste_generation JOIN waste_types AS wt ON wt.waste_type_id = waste_generation.waste_type_id WHERE wt.waste_type_name IN ('Solid Waste', 'Liquid Waste') GROUP BY facility_id), FacilityImpact AS (SELECT COALESCE(et.facility_id, wt.facility_id) AS facility_id, COALESCE(et.total_emission, 0) AS total_emission, COALESCE(wt.total_waste, 0) AS total_waste, COALESCE(et.total_emission, 0) + COALESCE(wt.total_waste, 0) AS total_environmental_impact FROM EmissionsTotal AS et LEFT OUTER JOIN WasteTotal AS wt ON et.facility_id = wt.facility_id UNION ALL SELECT COALESCE(et.facility_id, wt.facility_id) AS facility_id, COALESCE(et.total_emission, 0) AS total_emission, COALESCE(wt.total_waste, 0) AS total_waste, COALESCE(et.total_emission, 0) + COALESCE(wt.total_waste, 0) AS total_environmental_impact FROM EmissionsTotal AS et RIGHT OUTER JOIN WasteTotal AS wt ON et.facility_id = wt.facility_id WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM EmissionsTotal AS et WHERE et.facility_id = wt.facility_id)) SELECT f.facility_name, fi.total_environmental_impact FROM FacilityImpact AS fi JOIN facilities AS f ON fi.facility_id = f.facility_id ORDER BY fi.total_environmental_impact DESC

question: Return image details and top 3 annotations for each image, including the image id, class id, path, format, resolution, dataset id, capture date, source, class name, description, username, email, role, and annotation details, along with the total number of annotations per image.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH AnnotatedImagesCTE AS ( SELECT ia.annotation_id, ia.image_id, ia.user_id, ia.annotation_date, ia.comments, ia.annotation_type, ia.confidence_level, i.class_id, i.path, i.format, i.resolution, i.dataset_id, i.capture_date, i.source, c.class_name, c.description, u.username, u.email, u.role, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ia.image_id ORDER BY ia.confidence_level DESC) AS annotation_rank FROM image_annotations AS ia INNER JOIN images AS i ON ia.image_id = i.image_id INNER JOIN classes AS c ON i.class_id = c.class_id INNER JOIN users AS u ON ia.user_id = u.user_id ), FilteredAnnotations AS ( SELECT ai.image_id, ai.class_id, ai.path, ai.format, ai.resolution, ai.dataset_id, ai.capture_date, ai.source, ai.class_name, ai.description, ai.username, ai.email, ai.role, GROUP_CONCAT( ai.comments || ' (' || ai.annotation_date || ', ' || ai.annotation_type || ', Confidence: ' || ai.confidence_level || ')' ) AS annotation_details FROM AnnotatedImagesCTE AS ai WHERE ai.annotation_rank <= 3 GROUP BY ai.image_id, ai.class_id, ai.path, ai.format, ai.resolution, ai.dataset_id, ai.capture_date, ai.source, ai.class_name, ai.description, ai.username, ai.email, ai.role ) SELECT fa.image_id, fa.class_id, fa.path, fa.format, fa.resolution, fa.dataset_id, fa.capture_date, fa.source, fa.class_name, fa.description, fa.username, fa.email, fa.role, fa.annotation_details, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY fa.image_id) AS total_annotations_per_image FROM FilteredAnnotations AS fa

question:
**User**: I want to get information about customers who have stopped using our services.
**Assistant**: What kind of information would you like to know about these customers?
**User**: Their names, email addresses, the dates they stopped, the reasons why, and the services they used.
**Assistant**: Would you also like to know about their usage and billing information?

question: Could you please gather outbreak details, including their IDs, the total number of cases, the names of the pathogens involved, and the contributing factors for each outbreak? I'd like the information sorted in descending order by the total number of cases and then by the outbreak ID.

question: For users with at least one annotation in dataset 1, return their usernames, the total number of distinct annotations, total file size of annotated images, and the average accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score of the model's performance on these images.

question: Could you tell me the names of public transportation routes in San Jose, the number of stops on each route, and the average frequency of service for each route, listed in order from A to Z by route name?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH SanJoseRoutes AS ( SELECT route_id, route_name FROM routes WHERE city_id = (SELECT city_id FROM cities WHERE city_name = 'San Jose') ), RouteStops AS ( SELECT sr.route_id, COUNT(*) as number_of_stops FROM stop_routes sr JOIN SanJoseRoutes sjr ON sjr.route_id = sr.route_id GROUP BY sr.route_id ), RouteFrequencies AS ( SELECT sr.route_id, AVG(CASE WHEN service_frequency LIKE '% every %' THEN CAST(SUBSTR(service_frequency, LENGTH('every ') + 1, INSTR(service_frequency, ' minutes') - LENGTH('every ') - 1) AS INTEGER) ELSE NULL END) as average_frequency FROM stop_routes sr JOIN SanJoseRoutes sjr ON sjr.route_id = sr.route_id GROUP BY sr.route_id ) SELECT sjr.route_name, COALESCE(rs.number_of_stops, 0) as number_of_stops, COALESCE(rf.average_frequency, 0) as average_frequency FROM SanJoseRoutes sjr LEFT JOIN RouteStops rs ON sjr.route_id = rs.route_id LEFT JOIN RouteFrequencies rf ON sjr.route_id = rf.route_id ORDER BY sjr.route_name

question: What is the total audio duration for meetings that have a rating greater than 3 and are tagged with 'zoning' or 'planning'?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH QualifiedMeetings AS ( SELECT meeting_id FROM feedback WHERE rating > 3 GROUP BY meeting_id ), TaggedMeetings AS ( SELECT m.meeting_id FROM meetings m INNER JOIN meeting_tags mt ON m.meeting_id = mt.meeting_id INNER JOIN tags t ON mt.tag_id = t.tag_id WHERE t.tag_name IN ('zoning', 'planning') ), FilteredMeetings AS ( SELECT qm.meeting_id FROM QualifiedMeetings qm INNER JOIN TaggedMeetings tm ON qm.meeting_id = tm.meeting_id ) SELECT SUM(CAST(strftime('%s', am.duration) AS INTEGER)) AS total_audio_duration FROM audio_records am INNER JOIN FilteredMeetings fm ON am.meeting_id = fm.meeting_id

question: Could you please gather detailed information on all models, including their names, average validation losses, hyperparameters, total data sizes, data types, comments, comment counts, and user engagement counts? gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ModelDetails AS ( SELECT m.model_id, m.model_name, m.model_type, m.created_at, m.updated_at, m.description, m.tags, AVG(e.valid_loss) AS avg_valid_loss FROM models m LEFT JOIN evaluation_metrics e ON m.model_id = e.model_id GROUP BY m.model_id, m.model_name, m.model_type, m.created_at, m.updated_at, m.description, m.tags ), HyperparametersSummary AS ( SELECT hp.model_id, GROUP_CONCAT(hp.hyperparameter_name || ': ' || hp.hyperparameter_value, ', ') AS hyperparameters FROM hyperparameters hp GROUP BY hp.model_id ), TrainingDatasetSummary AS ( SELECT td.model_id, SUM(td.data_size) AS total_data_size, GROUP_CONCAT(td.data_type, ', ') AS data_types FROM training_data td GROUP BY td.model_id ), CommentsSummary AS ( SELECT mc.model_id, GROUP_CONCAT(mc.comment, ' | ') AS comments, COUNT(mc.comment) AS comment_count FROM model_comments mc GROUP BY mc.model_id ), UserEngagement AS ( SELECT e.model_id, COUNT(DISTINCT e.user_id) AS user_engagement_count FROM experiments e GROUP BY e.model_id ) SELECT md.model_name, md.avg_valid_loss, COALESCE(hs.hyperparameters, 'No hyperparameters') AS hyperparameters, COALESCE(tds.total_data_size, 0) AS total_data_size, COALESCE(tds.data_types, 'No data types') AS data_types, COALESCE(cs.comments, 'No comments') AS comments, COALESCE(cs.comment_count, 0) AS comment_count, COALESCE(ue.user_engagement_count, 0) AS user_engagement_count FROM ModelDetails md LEFT JOIN HyperparametersSummary hs ON md.model_id = hs.model_id LEFT JOIN TrainingDatasetSummary tds ON md.model_id = tds.model_id LEFT JOIN CommentsSummary cs ON md.model_id = cs.model_id LEFT JOIN UserEngagement ue ON md.model_id = ue.model_id ORDER BY md.avg_valid_loss ASC, md.model_name

question: Hey, can you show me the top 5 books with the highest average ratings, including their titles, average ratings, download counts, authors along with their roles, and categories along with subcategories? I'd love to see them sorted by their average ratings and download counts in descending order.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH TopRatedBooks AS ( SELECT book_id, title, avg_rating FROM books ORDER BY avg_rating DESC LIMIT 5 ), BookDownloads AS ( SELECT book_id, COUNT(download_id) AS download_count FROM book_downloads GROUP BY book_id ) SELECT trb.book_id, trb.title, trb.avg_rating, COALESCE(bd.download_count, 0) AS download_count, GROUP_CONCAT(a.author_name || ' (' || ba.author_role || ')') AS authors, GROUP_CONCAT(c.category_name || ' > ' || c.subcategory_name) AS categories FROM TopRatedBooks trb LEFT JOIN BookDownloads bd ON trb.book_id = bd.book_id LEFT JOIN book_authors ba ON trb.book_id = ba.book_id LEFT JOIN authors a ON ba.author_id = a.author_id LEFT JOIN book_categories bc ON trb.book_id = bc.book_id LEFT JOIN categories c ON bc.category_id = c.category_id GROUP BY trb.book_id, trb.title, trb.avg_rating, bd.download_count ORDER BY trb.avg_rating DESC, bd.download_count DESC

question: Find all active records in the music catalog, including their titles, total units sold, units sold, whether they have an active promotion, and promotion details, and return the results sorted by the total units sold in descending order.

question: I want to know the job titles, categories, versions, levels, total application counts, and the number of new, reviewed, rejected, and hired applications for each job posting. Additionally, I want to see the aggregated user experience and skills for each job posting, ordered by the level of the job posting version in descending order and the version number in descending order.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ApplicationStatusSummary AS ( SELECT a.job_id, COUNT(*) as application_count, SUM(CASE WHEN a.status = 'new' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as new_count, SUM(CASE WHEN a.status = 'reviewed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as reviewed_count, SUM(CASE WHEN a.status = 'rejected' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as rejected_count, SUM(CASE WHEN a.status = 'hired' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as hired_count FROM applications a GROUP BY a.job_id ), UserExperience AS ( SELECT u.user_id, u.user_name, ue.job_title, ue.company FROM users u LEFT JOIN user_experience ue ON u.user_id = ue.user_id ), UserSkills AS ( SELECT u.user_id, u.user_name, s.skill, s.level FROM users u LEFT JOIN user_skills s ON u.user_id = s.user_id ) SELECT jp.job_id, jp.job_title, c.category_name, jp.version, jp.experience_level, jp.application_count, ass.new_count, ass.reviewed_count, ass.rejected_count, ass.hired_count, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ue.job_title || ' at ' || ue.company) as user_experience, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT us.skill || ' (' || us.level || ')') as user_skills FROM job_postings jp JOIN categories c ON jp.category_id = c.category_id LEFT JOIN ApplicationStatusSummary ass ON jp.job_id = ass.job_id LEFT JOIN applications a ON jp.job_id = a.job_id LEFT JOIN UserExperience ue ON a.user_id = ue.user_id LEFT JOIN UserSkills us ON a.user_id = us.user_id GROUP BY jp.job_id, jp.job_title, c.category_name, jp.version, jp.experience_level, jp.application_count, ass.new_count, ass.reviewed_count, ass.rejected_count, ass.hired_count ORDER BY jp.experience_level DESC, jp.version DESC

question: What is the completion rate of each survey, ordered from the highest to the lowest?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT s.survey_id, (COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN sl.status = 'Complete' THEN sr.user_id ELSE NULL END) * 100.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT sr.user_id)) AS completion_rate FROM surveys s LEFT JOIN survey_responses sr ON s.survey_id = sr.survey_id LEFT JOIN survey_logs sl ON s.survey_id = sl.survey_id AND sr.user_id = sl.user_id GROUP BY s.survey_id ORDER BY completion_rate DESC

question: Could you please provide a comprehensive report of all projects, including the project name, total number of requirements, number of completed requirements, project completion rate, requirement details (text, estimated effort hours, actual effort hours, and effort variance), stakeholders involved, and the final approval status along with the approval date for each requirement? The report should be sorted by project completion rate in descending order, and then by effort variance in descending order.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ProjectSummary AS ( SELECT p.project_id, p.project_name, COUNT(r.requirement_id) AS total_requirements, SUM(CASE WHEN r.status = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS completed_requirements, (SUM(CASE WHEN r.status = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(r.requirement_id)) AS completion_rate FROM projects p LEFT JOIN requirements r ON p.project_id = r.project_id GROUP BY p.project_id, p.project_name ), EffortVariance AS ( SELECT r.requirement_id, r.project_id, r.requirement_text, r.estimated_effort_hours, r.actual_effort_hours, (r.actual_effort_hours - r.estimated_effort_hours) AS effort_variance FROM requirements r ), FinalApprovalStatus AS ( SELECT ra.requirement_id, ra.approval_status, ra.approval_date FROM requirement_approvals ra WHERE ra.is_final_approval = 1 ) SELECT ps.project_name, ps.total_requirements, ps.completed_requirements, ps.completion_rate, ev.requirement_text, ev.estimated_effort_hours, ev.actual_effort_hours, ev.effort_variance, p.stakeholders, fas.approval_status, fas.approval_date FROM ProjectSummary ps JOIN projects p ON ps.project_id = p.project_id JOIN EffortVariance ev ON ps.project_id = ev.project_id JOIN FinalApprovalStatus fas ON ev.requirement_id = fas.requirement_id ORDER BY ps.completion_rate DESC, ev.effort_variance DESC

question:
