question: Return aggregated user feedback, including user name, size, region, rating, comment, and fit accuracy, for each clothing item, ordered by item name.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT ci.item_name, GROUP_CONCAT( 'User: ' || u.user_name || ', Size: ' || s.size_name || ', Region: ' || r.region_name || ', Rating: ' || uf.rating || ', Comment: ' || uf.comment || ', Fit Accuracy: ' || uf.fit_accuracy, '; ' ) AS aggregated_comments FROM clothing_items ci JOIN user_feedback uf ON ci.item_id = uf.item_id JOIN users u ON uf.user_id = u.user_id JOIN sizes s ON uf.size_id = s.size_id JOIN regions r ON uf.region_id = r.region_id GROUP BY ci.item_name ORDER BY ci.item_name
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT ci.item_name, GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT('User: ', u.user_name, ', Size: ', s.size_name, ', Region: ', r.region_name, ', Rating: ', uf.rating, ', Comment: ', uf.comment, ', Fit Accuracy: ', uf.fit_accuracy) SEPARATOR '; ') AS aggregated_comments FROM clothing_items AS ci JOIN user_feedback AS uf ON ci.item_id = uf.item_id JOIN users AS u ON uf.user_id = u.user_id JOIN sizes AS s ON uf.size_id = s.size_id JOIN regions AS r ON uf.region_id = r.region_id GROUP BY ci.item_name ORDER BY ci.item_name
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT ci.item_name, STRING_AGG('User: ' || u.user_name || ', Size: ' || s.size_name || ', Region: ' || r.region_name || ', Rating: ' || uf.rating || ', Comment: ' || uf.comment || ', Fit Accuracy: ' || uf.fit_accuracy, '; ') AS aggregated_comments FROM clothing_items AS ci JOIN user_feedback AS uf ON ci.item_id = uf.item_id JOIN users AS u ON uf.user_id = u.user_id JOIN sizes AS s ON uf.size_id = s.size_id JOIN regions AS r ON uf.region_id = r.region_id GROUP BY ci.item_name ORDER BY ci.item_name NULLS FIRST

question: Return the names of the models along with their latest versions, associated comments, experiment names, and the number of experiments, ordered by model name.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH LatestVersions AS ( SELECT model_id, MAX(version_id) AS latest_version_id FROM model_versions GROUP BY model_id ), ModelComments AS ( SELECT model_id, GROUP_CONCAT(comment, ' | ') AS comments FROM model_comments GROUP BY model_id ), ExperimentsInfo AS ( SELECT model_id, GROUP_CONCAT(experiment_name, ', ') AS experiment_names, COUNT(experiment_id) AS num_experiments FROM experiments GROUP BY model_id ) SELECT m.model_name, mv.version_number AS latest_version, mc.comments, ei.experiment_names, ei.num_experiments FROM models m JOIN LatestVersions lv ON m.model_id = lv.model_id JOIN model_versions mv ON lv.latest_version_id = mv.version_id LEFT JOIN ModelComments mc ON m.model_id = mc.model_id LEFT JOIN ExperimentsInfo ei ON m.model_id = ei.model_id ORDER BY m.model_name
gold_sql.mysql: WITH LatestVersions AS (SELECT model_id, MAX(version_id) AS latest_version_id FROM model_versions GROUP BY model_id), ModelComments AS (SELECT model_id, GROUP_CONCAT(comment SEPARATOR ' | ') AS comments FROM model_comments GROUP BY model_id), ExperimentsInfo AS (SELECT model_id, GROUP_CONCAT(experiment_name SEPARATOR ', ') AS experiment_names, COUNT(experiment_id) AS num_experiments FROM experiments GROUP BY model_id) SELECT m.model_name, mv.version_number AS latest_version, mc.comments, ei.experiment_names, ei.num_experiments FROM models AS m JOIN LatestVersions AS lv ON m.model_id = lv.model_id JOIN model_versions AS mv ON lv.latest_version_id = mv.version_id LEFT JOIN ModelComments AS mc ON m.model_id = mc.model_id LEFT JOIN ExperimentsInfo AS ei ON m.model_id = ei.model_id ORDER BY m.model_name
gold_sql.postgres: WITH LatestVersions AS (SELECT model_id, MAX(version_id) AS latest_version_id FROM model_versions GROUP BY model_id), ModelComments AS (SELECT model_id, STRING_AGG(comment, ' | ') AS comments FROM model_comments GROUP BY model_id), ExperimentsInfo AS (SELECT model_id, STRING_AGG(experiment_name, ', ') AS experiment_names, COUNT(experiment_id) AS num_experiments FROM experiments GROUP BY model_id) SELECT m.model_name, mv.version_number AS latest_version, mc.comments, ei.experiment_names, ei.num_experiments FROM models AS m JOIN LatestVersions AS lv ON m.model_id = lv.model_id JOIN model_versions AS mv ON lv.latest_version_id = mv.version_id LEFT JOIN ModelComments AS mc ON m.model_id = mc.model_id LEFT JOIN ExperimentsInfo AS ei ON m.model_id = ei.model_id ORDER BY m.model_name NULLS FIRST

question: Could you please get the names of the top 3 users in the fantasy game, along with the names and positions of the players they chose as captain or vice-captain in the most recent gameweek, and list them in order of the users' ranks, prioritizing captains over vice-captains?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH TopUsers AS ( SELECT user_id, user_name, rank FROM users ORDER BY rank ASC LIMIT 3 ), MostRecentGameweek AS ( SELECT MAX(gameweek) AS max_gameweek FROM user_selections ), UserSelections AS ( SELECT us.user_id, us.player_id, us.gameweek, us.captain, us.vice_captain, p.name AS player_name, p.position FROM user_selections us JOIN players p ON us.player_id = p.player_id WHERE us.gameweek = (SELECT max_gameweek FROM MostRecentGameweek) AND (us.captain = 1 OR us.vice_captain = 1) ) SELECT tu.user_name, us.player_name, us.position FROM TopUsers tu JOIN UserSelections us ON tu.user_id = us.user_id ORDER BY tu.rank, us.captain DESC, us.vice_captain DESC
gold_sql.mysql: WITH TopUsers AS (SELECT user_id, user_name, `rank` FROM users ORDER BY `rank` ASC LIMIT 3), MostRecentGameweek AS (SELECT MAX(gameweek) AS max_gameweek FROM user_selections), UserSelections AS (SELECT us.user_id, us.player_id, us.gameweek, us.captain, us.vice_captain, p.name AS player_name, p.position FROM user_selections AS us JOIN players AS p ON us.player_id = p.player_id WHERE us.gameweek = (SELECT max_gameweek FROM MostRecentGameweek) AND (us.captain = 1 OR us.vice_captain = 1)) SELECT tu.user_name, us.player_name, us.position FROM TopUsers AS tu JOIN UserSelections AS us ON tu.user_id = us.user_id ORDER BY tu.`rank`, us.captain DESC, us.vice_captain DESC
gold_sql.postgres: WITH TopUsers AS (SELECT user_id, user_name, rank FROM users ORDER BY rank ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 3), MostRecentGameweek AS (SELECT MAX(gameweek) AS max_gameweek FROM user_selections), UserSelections AS (SELECT us.user_id, us.player_id, us.gameweek, us.captain, us.vice_captain, p.name AS player_name, p.position FROM user_selections AS us JOIN players AS p ON us.player_id = p.player_id WHERE us.gameweek = (SELECT max_gameweek FROM MostRecentGameweek) AND (us.captain = 1 OR us.vice_captain = 1)) SELECT tu.user_name, us.player_name, us.position FROM TopUsers AS tu JOIN UserSelections AS us ON tu.user_id = us.user_id ORDER BY tu.rank NULLS FIRST, us.captain DESC NULLS LAST, us.vice_captain DESC NULLS LAST

question: What are the average temperatures for each location and month over the past few decades, considering only the high-quality weather data?
external_knowledge:
- 'high-quality data' refers to data with a `data_quality_flag` of 1;
- 'past few decades' refers to the period between 2000 and 2023.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT ws.location, strftime('%Y-%m', w.date_time) AS month_year, AVG(w.temperature) AS avg_temperature FROM weather_data w JOIN weather_stations ws ON w.station_id = ws.station_id WHERE w.data_quality_flag = 1 AND w.date_time BETWEEN '2000-01-01 00:00:00' AND '2023-12-31 23:59:59' GROUP BY ws.location, strftime('%Y-%m', w.date_time) ORDER BY ws.location, month_year
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT ws.location, DATE_FORMAT(CAST(w.date_time AS DATETIME), '%Y-%m') AS month_year, AVG(w.temperature) AS avg_temperature FROM weather_data AS w JOIN weather_stations AS ws ON w.station_id = ws.station_id WHERE w.data_quality_flag = 1 AND w.date_time BETWEEN '2000-01-01 00:00:00' AND '2023-12-31 23:59:59' GROUP BY ws.location, DATE_FORMAT(CAST(w.date_time AS DATETIME), '%Y-%m') ORDER BY ws.location, month_year
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT ws.location, TO_CHAR(CAST(w.date_time AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY-MM') AS month_year, AVG(w.temperature) AS avg_temperature FROM weather_data AS w JOIN weather_stations AS ws ON w.station_id = ws.station_id WHERE w.data_quality_flag = 1 AND w.date_time BETWEEN '2000-01-01 00:00:00' AND '2023-12-31 23:59:59' GROUP BY ws.location, TO_CHAR(CAST(w.date_time AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY-MM') ORDER BY ws.location NULLS FIRST, month_year NULLS FIRST

question: For projects with completed mitigation plans in 2023, find the project names and their average assessment scores.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT p.project_name, AVG(ra.assessment_score) AS average_assessment_score FROM projects p JOIN risks r ON p.project_id = r.project_id JOIN risk_assessments ra ON r.risk_id = ra.risk_id JOIN mitigation_status ms ON r.risk_id = ms.risk_id WHERE ms.status = 'Completed' AND strftime('%Y', ms.last_updated) = '2023' GROUP BY p.project_id, p.project_name HAVING COUNT(ra.assessment_id) > 0
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT p.project_name, AVG(ra.assessment_score) AS average_assessment_score FROM projects AS p JOIN risks AS r ON p.project_id = r.project_id JOIN risk_assessments AS ra ON r.risk_id = ra.risk_id JOIN mitigation_status AS ms ON r.risk_id = ms.risk_id WHERE ms.status = 'Completed' AND DATE_FORMAT(CAST(ms.last_updated AS DATETIME), '%Y') = '2023' GROUP BY p.project_id, p.project_name HAVING COUNT(ra.assessment_id) > 0
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT p.project_name, AVG(ra.assessment_score) AS average_assessment_score FROM projects AS p JOIN risks AS r ON p.project_id = r.project_id JOIN risk_assessments AS ra ON r.risk_id = ra.risk_id JOIN mitigation_status AS ms ON r.risk_id = ms.risk_id WHERE ms.status = 'Completed' AND TO_CHAR(CAST(ms.last_updated AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY') = '2023' GROUP BY p.project_id, p.project_name HAVING COUNT(ra.assessment_id) > 0

question:

**Assistant**: Got it. Do you want to see the features for all comparisons made by users, or are you interested in a specific comparison name or date?
**User**: I want to see the features for all comparisons made by users, ordered by the most recent comparison date and then by user ID.
**Assistant**: Understood. I will also include the feature names in the results. Is there anything else you need?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH UserComparisons AS ( SELECT c.user_id, c.selected_editions, c.comparison_date FROM comparisons c ) SELECT uc.user_id, f.feature_name FROM UserComparisons uc JOIN edition_features ef ON uc.selected_editions LIKE '%' || CAST(ef.edition_id AS TEXT) || '%' JOIN features f ON ef.feature_id = f.feature_id ORDER BY uc.comparison_date DESC, uc.user_id
gold_sql.mysql: WITH UserComparisons AS (SELECT c.user_id, c.selected_editions, c.comparison_date FROM comparisons AS c) SELECT uc.user_id, f.feature_name FROM UserComparisons AS uc JOIN edition_features AS ef ON uc.selected_editions LIKE CONCAT('%', CAST(ef.edition_id AS CHAR), '%') JOIN features AS f ON ef.feature_id = f.feature_id ORDER BY uc.comparison_date DESC, uc.user_id
gold_sql.postgres: WITH UserComparisons AS (SELECT c.user_id, c.selected_editions, c.comparison_date FROM comparisons AS c) SELECT uc.user_id, f.feature_name FROM UserComparisons AS uc JOIN edition_features AS ef ON uc.selected_editions LIKE '%' || CAST(ef.edition_id AS TEXT) || '%' JOIN features AS f ON ef.feature_id = f.feature_id ORDER BY uc.comparison_date DESC NULLS LAST, uc.user_id NULLS FIRST

question: Hey! Could you give me a detailed list of all the commands executed by the user with ID 0, including the command name, the user's username, their role, and any error messages they encountered? I need it all in one string, separated by commas.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT GROUP_CONCAT( T3.name || ' - ' || T1.username || ' - ' || T2.role_name || ' - ' || COALESCE(T4.error_message, 'No Error'), ', ' ) AS details FROM users AS T1 JOIN user_roles AS T5 ON T1.user_id = T5.user_id JOIN roles AS T2 ON T5.role_id = T2.role_id JOIN command_logs AS T6 ON T1.user_id = T6.user_id JOIN commands AS T3 ON T6.command_id = T3.command_id LEFT JOIN command_errors AS T4 ON T6.log_id = T4.log_id WHERE T1.user_id = 0 GROUP BY T1.user_id
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(T3.name, ' - ', T1.username, ' - ', T2.role_name, ' - ', COALESCE(T4.error_message, 'No Error')) SEPARATOR ', ') AS details FROM users AS T1 JOIN user_roles AS T5 ON T1.user_id = T5.user_id JOIN roles AS T2 ON T5.role_id = T2.role_id JOIN command_logs AS T6 ON T1.user_id = T6.user_id JOIN commands AS T3 ON T6.command_id = T3.command_id LEFT JOIN command_errors AS T4 ON T6.log_id = T4.log_id WHERE T1.user_id = 0 GROUP BY T1.user_id
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT STRING_AGG(T3.name || ' - ' || T1.username || ' - ' || T2.role_name || ' - ' || COALESCE(T4.error_message, 'No Error'), ', ') AS details FROM users AS T1 JOIN user_roles AS T5 ON T1.user_id = T5.user_id JOIN roles AS T2 ON T5.role_id = T2.role_id JOIN command_logs AS T6 ON T1.user_id = T6.user_id JOIN commands AS T3 ON T6.command_id = T3.command_id LEFT JOIN command_errors AS T4 ON T6.log_id = T4.log_id WHERE T1.user_id = 0 GROUP BY T1.user_id

question: What are the names of projects, listed in order from highest to lowest, that have achieved the most progress towards finishing all requirements?
external_knowledge: Completion rate refers to the ratio of completed requirements to total requirements for each project. In this context, 'progress towards finishing all requirements' means the completion rate of the project; The 'highest to lowest' order is based on the completion rate of the projects.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT p.project_name, (SUM(CASE WHEN r.actual_completion_date IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(r.requirement_id)) * 100 AS completion_rate FROM projects p LEFT JOIN requirements r ON p.project_id = r.project_id GROUP BY p.project_id, p.project_name ORDER BY completion_rate DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT p.project_name, (SUM(CASE WHEN NOT r.actual_completion_date IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(r.requirement_id)) * 100 AS completion_rate FROM projects AS p LEFT JOIN requirements AS r ON p.project_id = r.project_id GROUP BY p.project_id, p.project_name ORDER BY completion_rate DESC
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT p.project_name, (SUM(CASE WHEN NOT r.actual_completion_date IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(r.requirement_id), 0)) * 100 AS completion_rate FROM projects AS p LEFT JOIN requirements AS r ON p.project_id = r.project_id GROUP BY p.project_id, p.project_name ORDER BY completion_rate DESC NULLS LAST

question: Could you please gather the top 3 most frequently accessed IC designs by designers between January 1, 2023, and May 31, 2023? I would like to know the design IDs, design names, roles, access counts, and associated packages (including package type and pin count) for these designs?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH AccessStatsCTE AS ( SELECT d.design_id, d.design_name, u.role, COUNT(*) AS access_count, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS access_rank, GROUP_CONCAT(p.package_type || ' (' || p.pin_count || ' pins)') AS associated_packages FROM ic_designs d JOIN access_logs al ON d.design_id = al.design_id JOIN users u ON al.user_id = u.user_id LEFT JOIN design_pictures dp ON d.design_id = dp.design_id LEFT JOIN ic_pictures p ON dp.picture_id = p.picture_id WHERE u.role = 'designer' AND al.access_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-05-31' GROUP BY d.design_id, d.design_name, u.role ) SELECT design_id, design_name, role, access_count, associated_packages FROM AccessStatsCTE WHERE access_rank <= 3
gold_sql.mysql: WITH AccessStatsCTE AS (SELECT d.design_id, d.design_name, u.role, COUNT(*) AS access_count, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS access_rank, GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(p.package_type, ' (', p.pin_count, ' pins)') SEPARATOR ',') AS associated_packages FROM ic_designs AS d JOIN access_logs AS al ON d.design_id = al.design_id JOIN users AS u ON al.user_id = u.user_id LEFT JOIN design_pictures AS dp ON d.design_id = dp.design_id LEFT JOIN ic_pictures AS p ON dp.picture_id = p.picture_id WHERE u.role = 'designer' AND al.access_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-05-31' GROUP BY d.design_id, d.design_name, u.role) SELECT design_id, design_name, role, access_count, associated_packages FROM AccessStatsCTE WHERE access_rank <= 3
gold_sql.postgres: WITH AccessStatsCTE AS (SELECT d.design_id, d.design_name, u.role, COUNT(*) AS access_count, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC NULLS LAST) AS access_rank, STRING_AGG(p.package_type || ' (' || p.pin_count || ' pins)', ',') AS associated_packages FROM ic_designs AS d JOIN access_logs AS al ON d.design_id = al.design_id JOIN users AS u ON al.user_id = u.user_id LEFT JOIN design_pictures AS dp ON d.design_id = dp.design_id LEFT JOIN ic_pictures AS p ON dp.picture_id = p.picture_id WHERE u.role = 'designer' AND al.access_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-05-31' GROUP BY d.design_id, d.design_name, u.role) SELECT design_id, design_name, role, access_count, associated_packages FROM AccessStatsCTE WHERE access_rank <= 3

question: I want to know the names of all countries, along with their corresponding region names, percentages, average regional GDP per capita, aggregated geographical features, associated organizations, first and last years of historical data, and historical growth rates of GDP per capita, ordered alphabetically by country name.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RegionGDPPerCapita AS ( SELECT r.region_id, AVG(d.gdp_per_capita) as avg_gdp_per_capita FROM regions r LEFT JOIN country_regions cr ON r.region_id = cr.region_id LEFT JOIN demographics d ON cr.country_id = d.country_id GROUP BY r.region_id ), CountryRegionDetails AS ( SELECT c.country_id, c.country_name, r.region_name, cr.region_percentage, rg.avg_gdp_per_capita as region_avg_gdp_per_capita FROM countries c INNER JOIN country_regions cr ON c.country_id = cr.country_id INNER JOIN regions r ON cr.region_id = r.region_id LEFT JOIN RegionGDPPerCapita rg ON r.region_id = rg.region_id ), CountryFeatures AS ( SELECT cf.country_id, GROUP_CONCAT(cf.feature_name, ', ') as country_features FROM geographical_features cf GROUP BY cf.country_id ), CountryOrganizations AS ( SELECT co.country_id, GROUP_CONCAT(o.organization_name, ', ') as organizations FROM country_organizations co INNER JOIN organizations o ON co.organization_id = o.organization_id GROUP BY co.country_id ), HistoricalGrowth AS ( SELECT h.country_id, MAX(h.year) as last_year, MIN(h.year) as first_year, (MAX(h.gdp_per_capita) - MIN(h.gdp_per_capita)) / MIN(h.gdp_per_capita) * 100 AS growth_rate FROM historical_data h GROUP BY h.country_id ) SELECT c.country_name, crd.region_name, crd.region_percentage, crd.region_avg_gdp_per_capita, cf.country_features, co.organizations, hg.first_year, hg.last_year, hg.growth_rate FROM countries c LEFT JOIN CountryRegionDetails crd ON c.country_id = crd.country_id LEFT JOIN CountryFeatures cf ON c.country_id = cf.country_id LEFT JOIN CountryOrganizations co ON c.country_id = co.country_id LEFT JOIN HistoricalGrowth hg ON c.country_id = hg.country_id ORDER BY c.country_name
gold_sql.mysql: WITH RegionGDPPerCapita AS (SELECT r.region_id, AVG(d.gdp_per_capita) AS avg_gdp_per_capita FROM regions AS r LEFT JOIN country_regions AS cr ON r.region_id = cr.region_id LEFT JOIN demographics AS d ON cr.country_id = d.country_id GROUP BY r.region_id), CountryRegionDetails AS (SELECT c.country_id, c.country_name, r.region_name, cr.region_percentage, rg.avg_gdp_per_capita AS region_avg_gdp_per_capita FROM countries AS c INNER JOIN country_regions AS cr ON c.country_id = cr.country_id INNER JOIN regions AS r ON cr.region_id = r.region_id LEFT JOIN RegionGDPPerCapita AS rg ON r.region_id = rg.region_id), CountryFeatures AS (SELECT cf.country_id, GROUP_CONCAT(cf.feature_name SEPARATOR ', ') AS country_features FROM geographical_features AS cf GROUP BY cf.country_id), CountryOrganizations AS (SELECT co.country_id, GROUP_CONCAT(o.organization_name SEPARATOR ', ') AS organizations FROM country_organizations AS co INNER JOIN organizations AS o ON co.organization_id = o.organization_id GROUP BY co.country_id), HistoricalGrowth AS (SELECT h.country_id, MAX(h.year) AS last_year, MIN(h.year) AS first_year, (MAX(h.gdp_per_capita) - MIN(h.gdp_per_capita)) / MIN(h.gdp_per_capita) * 100 AS growth_rate FROM historical_data AS h GROUP BY h.country_id) SELECT c.country_name, crd.region_name, crd.region_percentage, crd.region_avg_gdp_per_capita, cf.country_features, co.organizations, hg.first_year, hg.last_year, hg.growth_rate FROM countries AS c LEFT JOIN CountryRegionDetails AS crd ON c.country_id = crd.country_id LEFT JOIN CountryFeatures AS cf ON c.country_id = cf.country_id LEFT JOIN CountryOrganizations AS co ON c.country_id = co.country_id LEFT JOIN HistoricalGrowth AS hg ON c.country_id = hg.country_id ORDER BY c.country_name
gold_sql.postgres: WITH RegionGDPPerCapita AS (SELECT r.region_id, AVG(d.gdp_per_capita) AS avg_gdp_per_capita FROM regions AS r LEFT JOIN country_regions AS cr ON r.region_id = cr.region_id LEFT JOIN demographics AS d ON cr.country_id = d.country_id GROUP BY r.region_id), CountryRegionDetails AS (SELECT c.country_id, c.country_name, r.region_name, cr.region_percentage, rg.avg_gdp_per_capita AS region_avg_gdp_per_capita FROM countries AS c INNER JOIN country_regions AS cr ON c.country_id = cr.country_id INNER JOIN regions AS r ON cr.region_id = r.region_id LEFT JOIN RegionGDPPerCapita AS rg ON r.region_id = rg.region_id), CountryFeatures AS (SELECT cf.country_id, STRING_AGG(cf.feature_name, ', ') AS country_features FROM geographical_features AS cf GROUP BY cf.country_id), CountryOrganizations AS (SELECT co.country_id, STRING_AGG(o.organization_name, ', ') AS organizations FROM country_organizations AS co INNER JOIN organizations AS o ON co.organization_id = o.organization_id GROUP BY co.country_id), HistoricalGrowth AS (SELECT h.country_id, MAX(h.year) AS last_year, MIN(h.year) AS first_year, (MAX(h.gdp_per_capita) - MIN(h.gdp_per_capita)) / NULLIF(MIN(h.gdp_per_capita), 0) * 100 AS growth_rate FROM historical_data AS h GROUP BY h.country_id) SELECT c.country_name, crd.region_name, crd.region_percentage, crd.region_avg_gdp_per_capita, cf.country_features, co.organizations, hg.first_year, hg.last_year, hg.growth_rate FROM countries AS c LEFT JOIN CountryRegionDetails AS crd ON c.country_id = crd.country_id LEFT JOIN CountryFeatures AS cf ON c.country_id = cf.country_id LEFT JOIN CountryOrganizations AS co ON c.country_id = co.country_id LEFT JOIN HistoricalGrowth AS hg ON c.country_id = hg.country_id ORDER BY c.country_name NULLS FIRST

question: Which locations have environmental conditions that match the ideal ranges for their recommended crops, based on the most recent data?
external_knowledge:
- The ideal temperature, humidity, and pH ranges for crops are stored as strings in the format "min-max", where min and max are the lower and upper bounds of the range, respectively;
- The `crop_recommendations` table links each location to one or more crops that are suitable for cultivation there.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RecentEnvironmentalData AS ( SELECT ed.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY ed.location_id ORDER BY ed.timestamp DESC) AS rn FROM environmental_data ed ), IdealCropConditions AS ( SELECT red.temperature, red.humidity, red.ph, red.location_id, cr.crop_id, cr.confidence_score, cr.recommended_date, c.crop_name, c.ideal_temperature_range, c.ideal_humidity_range, c.ideal_ph_range FROM RecentEnvironmentalData red INNER JOIN crop_recommendations cr ON cr.location_id = red.location_id INNER JOIN crops c ON c.crop_id = cr.crop_id WHERE red.rn = 1 AND red.temperature BETWEEN CAST(SUBSTR(c.ideal_temperature_range, 1, INSTR(c.ideal_temperature_range, '-')-1) AS REAL) AND CAST(SUBSTR(c.ideal_temperature_range, INSTR(c.ideal_temperature_range, '-')+1) AS REAL) AND red.humidity BETWEEN CAST(SUBSTR(c.ideal_humidity_range, 1, INSTR(c.ideal_humidity_range, '-')-1) AS REAL) AND CAST(SUBSTR(c.ideal_humidity_range, INSTR(c.ideal_humidity_range, '-')+1) AS REAL) AND red.ph BETWEEN CAST(SUBSTR(c.ideal_ph_range, 1, INSTR(c.ideal_ph_range, '-')-1) AS REAL) AND CAST(SUBSTR(c.ideal_ph_range, INSTR(c.ideal_ph_range, '-')+1) AS REAL) ) SELECT l.location_name, icc.crop_name FROM IdealCropConditions icc INNER JOIN locations l ON l.location_id = icc.location_id WHERE icc.crop_name IS NOT NULL
gold_sql.mysql: WITH RecentEnvironmentalData AS (SELECT ed.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ed.location_id ORDER BY ed.timestamp DESC) AS rn FROM environmental_data AS ed), IdealCropConditions AS (SELECT red.temperature, red.humidity, red.ph, red.location_id, cr.crop_id, cr.confidence_score, cr.recommended_date, c.crop_name, c.ideal_temperature_range, c.ideal_humidity_range, c.ideal_ph_range FROM RecentEnvironmentalData AS red INNER JOIN crop_recommendations AS cr ON cr.location_id = red.location_id INNER JOIN crops AS c ON c.crop_id = cr.crop_id WHERE red.rn = 1 AND red.temperature BETWEEN CAST(SUBSTRING(c.ideal_temperature_range, 1, LOCATE('-', c.ideal_temperature_range) - 1) AS FLOAT) AND CAST(SUBSTRING(c.ideal_temperature_range, LOCATE('-', c.ideal_temperature_range) + 1) AS FLOAT) AND red.humidity BETWEEN CAST(SUBSTRING(c.ideal_humidity_range, 1, LOCATE('-', c.ideal_humidity_range) - 1) AS FLOAT) AND CAST(SUBSTRING(c.ideal_humidity_range, LOCATE('-', c.ideal_humidity_range) + 1) AS FLOAT) AND red.ph BETWEEN CAST(SUBSTRING(c.ideal_ph_range, 1, LOCATE('-', c.ideal_ph_range) - 1) AS FLOAT) AND CAST(SUBSTRING(c.ideal_ph_range, LOCATE('-', c.ideal_ph_range) + 1) AS FLOAT)) SELECT l.location_name, icc.crop_name FROM IdealCropConditions AS icc INNER JOIN locations AS l ON l.location_id = icc.location_id WHERE NOT icc.crop_name IS NULL
gold_sql.postgres: WITH RecentEnvironmentalData AS (SELECT ed.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ed.location_id ORDER BY ed.timestamp DESC NULLS LAST) AS rn FROM environmental_data AS ed), IdealCropConditions AS (SELECT red.temperature, red.humidity, red.ph, red.location_id, cr.crop_id, cr.confidence_score, cr.recommended_date, c.crop_name, c.ideal_temperature_range, c.ideal_humidity_range, c.ideal_ph_range FROM RecentEnvironmentalData AS red INNER JOIN crop_recommendations AS cr ON cr.location_id = red.location_id INNER JOIN crops AS c ON c.crop_id = cr.crop_id WHERE red.rn = 1 AND red.temperature BETWEEN CAST(SUBSTRING(c.ideal_temperature_range FROM 1 FOR STRPOS(c.ideal_temperature_range, '-') - 1) AS REAL) AND CAST(SUBSTRING(c.ideal_temperature_range FROM STRPOS(c.ideal_temperature_range, '-') + 1) AS REAL) AND red.humidity BETWEEN CAST(SUBSTRING(c.ideal_humidity_range FROM 1 FOR STRPOS(c.ideal_humidity_range, '-') - 1) AS REAL) AND CAST(SUBSTRING(c.ideal_humidity_range FROM STRPOS(c.ideal_humidity_range, '-') + 1) AS REAL) AND red.ph BETWEEN CAST(SUBSTRING(c.ideal_ph_range FROM 1 FOR STRPOS(c.ideal_ph_range, '-') - 1) AS REAL) AND CAST(SUBSTRING(c.ideal_ph_range FROM STRPOS(c.ideal_ph_range, '-') + 1) AS REAL)) SELECT l.location_name, icc.crop_name FROM IdealCropConditions AS icc INNER JOIN locations AS l ON l.location_id = icc.location_id WHERE NOT icc.crop_name IS NULL

question: Can you find the registers that are accessible to everyone like the open doors of a public library, those that are small in stature (less than 16 bits wide), and those that have a secret code (non-null bit mask)? Please present the findings with the registers arranged by their unique identifiers.
external_knowledge:
- 'open doors of a public library' metaphorically refers to registers that do not require any special privilege to access.
- 'small in stature' refers to registers with a bit width less than 16.
- 'secret code' is a metaphor for a non-null bit mask.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT r.register_id, r.name, p.privilege_name AS privilege FROM registers r JOIN privileges p ON r.required_privilege = p.privilege_id WHERE p.privilege_name = 'Non-Privileged' UNION SELECT register_id, name, CAST(bit_width AS TEXT) AS privilege FROM registers WHERE bit_width < 16 UNION SELECT register_id, name, bit_mask AS privilege FROM registers WHERE bit_mask IS NOT NULL ORDER BY register_id
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT r.register_id, r.name, p.privilege_name AS privilege FROM registers AS r JOIN privileges AS p ON r.required_privilege = p.privilege_id WHERE p.privilege_name = 'Non-Privileged' UNION SELECT register_id, name, CAST(bit_width AS CHAR) AS privilege FROM registers WHERE bit_width < 16 UNION SELECT register_id, name, bit_mask AS privilege FROM registers WHERE NOT bit_mask IS NULL ORDER BY register_id
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT r.register_id, r.name, p.privilege_name AS privilege FROM registers AS r JOIN privileges AS p ON r.required_privilege = p.privilege_id WHERE p.privilege_name = 'Non-Privileged' UNION SELECT register_id, name, CAST(bit_width AS TEXT) AS privilege FROM registers WHERE bit_width < 16 UNION SELECT register_id, name, bit_mask AS privilege FROM registers WHERE NOT bit_mask IS NULL ORDER BY register_id NULLS FIRST

question: Hey! Can you help me find all the details for the data point with ID 1, including any comments made on it and the username of the user who created it, but only if the comment is 'This is a comment.' and the user ID is 1, and the data point was created in the year 2009?

AND u.user_id = 1 AND strftime('%Y', dp.created_at) = '2009'

AND u.user_id = 1 AND DATE_FORMAT(CAST(dp.created_at AS DATETIME), '%Y') = '2009'
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT dp.id, dp.bool_col, dp.tinyint_col, dp.smallint_col, dp.int_col, dp.bigint_col, dp.float_col, dp.double_col, dp.date_string_col, dp.string_col, dp.timestamp_col, u.username, dc.comment FROM data_points AS dp JOIN data_point_comments AS dc ON dp.id = dc.data_point_id JOIN users AS u ON dp.created_by = u.user_id WHERE dp.id = 1 AND dc.comment = 'This is a comment.' question: Could you provide a detailed report that includes the monthly total cases and recovered cases for each District Health Board (DHB), along with the cumulative totals and recovery rates over time?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH MonthlyCases AS ( SELECT c.dhb_id, STRFTIME('%Y-%m', c.report_date) AS month, COUNT(c.case_id) AS total_cases, SUM(CASE WHEN o.outcome = 'Recovered' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS recovered_cases FROM cases c LEFT JOIN outcomes o ON c.case_id = o.case_id GROUP BY c.dhb_id, STRFTIME('%Y-%m', c.report_date) ), DHBInfo AS ( SELECT m.dhb_id, m.month, m.total_cases, m.recovered_cases, d.dhb_name FROM MonthlyCases m INNER JOIN dhb d ON m.dhb_id = d.dhb_id ), CumulativeAggregation AS ( SELECT d.dhb_id, d.dhb_name, d.month, d.total_cases, d.recovered_cases, SUM(d.total_cases) OVER (PARTITION BY d.dhb_id ORDER BY d.month) AS cumulative_total_cases, SUM(d.recovered_cases) OVER (PARTITION BY d.dhb_id ORDER BY d.month) AS cumulative_recovered_cases FROM DHBInfo d ) SELECT ca.dhb_id, ca.dhb_name, ca.month, ca.total_cases, ca.recovered_cases, ca.cumulative_total_cases, ca.cumulative_recovered_cases, (ca.cumulative_recovered_cases * 100.0 / ca.cumulative_total_cases) AS recovery_rate FROM CumulativeAggregation ca ORDER BY ca.dhb_id, ca.month
gold_sql.mysql: WITH MonthlyCases AS (SELECT c.dhb_id, DATE_FORMAT(CAST(c.report_date AS DATETIME), '%Y-%m') AS month, COUNT(c.case_id) AS total_cases, SUM(CASE WHEN o.outcome = 'Recovered' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS recovered_cases FROM cases AS c LEFT JOIN outcomes AS o ON c.case_id = o.case_id GROUP BY c.dhb_id, DATE_FORMAT(CAST(c.report_date AS DATETIME), '%Y-%m')), DHBInfo AS (SELECT m.dhb_id, m.month, m.total_cases, m.recovered_cases, d.dhb_name FROM MonthlyCases AS m INNER JOIN dhb AS d ON m.dhb_id = d.dhb_id), CumulativeAggregation AS (SELECT d.dhb_id, d.dhb_name, d.month, d.total_cases, d.recovered_cases, SUM(d.total_cases) OVER (PARTITION BY d.dhb_id ORDER BY d.month) AS cumulative_total_cases, SUM(d.recovered_cases) OVER (PARTITION BY d.dhb_id ORDER BY d.month) AS cumulative_recovered_cases FROM DHBInfo AS d) SELECT ca.dhb_id, ca.dhb_name, ca.month, ca.total_cases, ca.recovered_cases, ca.cumulative_total_cases, ca.cumulative_recovered_cases, (ca.cumulative_recovered_cases * 100.0 / ca.cumulative_total_cases) AS recovery_rate FROM CumulativeAggregation AS ca ORDER BY ca.dhb_id, ca.month
gold_sql.postgres: WITH MonthlyCases AS (SELECT c.dhb_id, TO_CHAR(CAST(c.report_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY-MM') AS month, COUNT(c.case_id) AS total_cases, SUM(CASE WHEN o.outcome = 'Recovered' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS recovered_cases FROM cases AS c LEFT JOIN outcomes AS o ON c.case_id = o.case_id GROUP BY c.dhb_id, TO_CHAR(CAST(c.report_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY-MM')), DHBInfo AS (SELECT m.dhb_id, m.month, m.total_cases, m.recovered_cases, d.dhb_name FROM MonthlyCases AS m INNER JOIN dhb AS d ON m.dhb_id = d.dhb_id), CumulativeAggregation AS (SELECT d.dhb_id, d.dhb_name, d.month, d.total_cases, d.recovered_cases, SUM(d.total_cases) OVER (PARTITION BY d.dhb_id ORDER BY d.month NULLS FIRST) AS cumulative_total_cases, SUM(d.recovered_cases) OVER (PARTITION BY d.dhb_id ORDER BY d.month NULLS FIRST) AS cumulative_recovered_cases FROM DHBInfo AS d) SELECT ca.dhb_id, ca.dhb_name, ca.month, ca.total_cases, ca.recovered_cases, ca.cumulative_total_cases, ca.cumulative_recovered_cases, (ca.cumulative_recovered_cases * 100.0 / NULLIF(ca.cumulative_total_cases, 0)) AS recovery_rate FROM CumulativeAggregation AS ca ORDER BY ca.dhb_id NULLS FIRST, ca.month NULLS FIRST

question: Which emulator has the highest average rating and the most total usage time, given that it has at least one rating and has been used for more than zero minutes?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT e.emulator_name FROM emulators e JOIN user_feedback feedback ON e.emulator_id = feedback.emulator_id JOIN emulator_usage usage ON e.emulator_id = usage.emulator_id GROUP BY e.emulator_id, e.emulator_name HAVING COUNT(feedback.rating) > 0 AND SUM(usage.total_time_used) > 0 ORDER BY AVG(feedback.rating) DESC, SUM(usage.total_time_used) DESC LIMIT 1
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT e.emulator_name FROM emulators AS e JOIN user_feedback AS feedback ON e.emulator_id = feedback.emulator_id JOIN emulator_usage AS `usage` ON e.emulator_id = `usage`.emulator_id GROUP BY e.emulator_id, e.emulator_name HAVING COUNT(feedback.rating) > 0 AND SUM(`usage`.total_time_used) > 0 ORDER BY AVG(feedback.rating) DESC, SUM(`usage`.total_time_used) DESC LIMIT 1
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT e.emulator_name FROM emulators AS e JOIN user_feedback AS feedback ON e.emulator_id = feedback.emulator_id JOIN emulator_usage AS usage ON e.emulator_id = usage.emulator_id GROUP BY e.emulator_id, e.emulator_name HAVING COUNT(feedback.rating) > 0 AND SUM(usage.total_time_used) > 0 ORDER BY AVG(feedback.rating) DESC NULLS LAST, SUM(usage.total_time_used) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1

question: Could you provide a detailed report on all assignments, including their names, types, total points, creation and update dates, grading scales, submission counts, average grades, highest grades, lowest grades, total criteria points, criteria counts, creation and update dates of criteria, and the earliest creation dates and latest update dates, ordered by assignment IDs?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH AssignmentDetails AS ( SELECT a.assignment_id, a.assignment_name, a.assignment_type, a.total_points, a.created_at AS assignment_created_at, a.updated_at AS assignment_updated_at, g.scale_name, g.description AS grading_scale_description, COUNT(s.submission_id) AS submission_count, AVG(s.grade) AS average_grade, MAX(s.grade) AS highest_grade, MIN(s.grade) AS lowest_grade FROM assignments a LEFT JOIN submissions s ON a.assignment_id = s.assignment_id LEFT JOIN grading_scales g ON a.grading_scale_id = g.grading_scale_id GROUP BY a.assignment_id, a.assignment_name, a.assignment_type, a.total_points, a.created_at, a.updated_at, g.scale_name, g.description ), CriteriaDetails AS ( SELECT c.assignment_id, SUM(c.points) AS total_criteria_points, COUNT(c.criterion_id) AS criteria_count, MIN(c.created_at) AS criteria_created_at, MAX(c.updated_at) AS criteria_updated_at FROM criteria c GROUP BY c.assignment_id ), CombinedDetails AS ( SELECT ad.assignment_id, ad.assignment_name, ad.assignment_type, ad.total_points, ad.assignment_created_at, ad.assignment_updated_at, ad.scale_name, ad.grading_scale_description, ad.submission_count, ad.average_grade, ad.highest_grade, ad.lowest_grade, cd.total_criteria_points, cd.criteria_count, cd.criteria_created_at, cd.criteria_updated_at FROM AssignmentDetails ad LEFT JOIN CriteriaDetails cd ON ad.assignment_id = cd.assignment_id ) SELECT cd.assignment_id, cd.assignment_name, cd.assignment_type, cd.total_points, cd.assignment_created_at, cd.assignment_updated_at, cd.scale_name, cd.grading_scale_description, cd.submission_count, cd.average_grade, cd.highest_grade, cd.lowest_grade, cd.total_criteria_points, cd.criteria_count, cd.criteria_created_at, cd.criteria_updated_at, MIN(cd.assignment_created_at, cd.criteria_created_at) AS earliest_creation_date, MAX(cd.assignment_updated_at, cd.criteria_updated_at) AS latest_update_date FROM CombinedDetails cd ORDER BY cd.assignment_id
gold_sql.mysql: WITH AssignmentDetails AS (SELECT a.assignment_id, a.assignment_name, a.assignment_type, a.total_points, a.created_at AS assignment_created_at, a.updated_at AS assignment_updated_at, g.scale_name, g.description AS grading_scale_description, COUNT(s.submission_id) AS submission_count, AVG(s.grade) AS average_grade, MAX(s.grade) AS highest_grade, MIN(s.grade) AS lowest_grade FROM assignments AS a LEFT JOIN submissions AS s ON a.assignment_id = s.assignment_id LEFT JOIN grading_scales AS g ON a.grading_scale_id = g.grading_scale_id GROUP BY a.assignment_id, a.assignment_name, a.assignment_type, a.total_points, a.created_at, a.updated_at, g.scale_name, g.description), CriteriaDetails AS (SELECT c.assignment_id, SUM(c.points) AS total_criteria_points, COUNT(c.criterion_id) AS criteria_count, MIN(c.created_at) AS criteria_created_at, MAX(c.updated_at) AS criteria_updated_at FROM criteria AS c GROUP BY c.assignment_id), CombinedDetails AS (SELECT ad.assignment_id, ad.assignment_name, ad.assignment_type, ad.total_points, ad.assignment_created_at, ad.assignment_updated_at, ad.scale_name, ad.grading_scale_description, ad.submission_count, ad.average_grade, ad.highest_grade, ad.lowest_grade, cd.total_criteria_points, cd.criteria_count, cd.criteria_created_at, cd.criteria_updated_at FROM AssignmentDetails AS ad LEFT JOIN CriteriaDetails AS cd ON ad.assignment_id = cd.assignment_id) SELECT cd.assignment_id, cd.assignment_name, cd.assignment_type, cd.total_points, cd.assignment_created_at, cd.assignment_updated_at, cd.scale_name, cd.grading_scale_description, cd.submission_count, cd.average_grade, cd.highest_grade, cd.lowest_grade, cd.total_criteria_points, cd.criteria_count, cd.criteria_created_at, cd.criteria_updated_at, LEAST(cd.assignment_created_at, cd.criteria_created_at) AS earliest_creation_date, GREATEST(cd.assignment_updated_at, cd.criteria_updated_at) AS latest_update_date FROM CombinedDetails AS cd ORDER BY cd.assignment_id
gold_sql.postgres: WITH AssignmentDetails AS (SELECT a.assignment_id, a.assignment_name, a.assignment_type, a.total_points, a.created_at AS assignment_created_at, a.updated_at AS assignment_updated_at, g.scale_name, g.description AS grading_scale_description, COUNT(s.submission_id) AS submission_count, AVG(s.grade) AS average_grade, MAX(s.grade) AS highest_grade, MIN(s.grade) AS lowest_grade FROM assignments AS a LEFT JOIN submissions AS s ON a.assignment_id = s.assignment_id LEFT JOIN grading_scales AS g ON a.grading_scale_id = g.grading_scale_id GROUP BY a.assignment_id, a.assignment_name, a.assignment_type, a.total_points, a.created_at, a.updated_at, g.scale_name, g.description), CriteriaDetails AS (SELECT c.assignment_id, SUM(c.points) AS total_criteria_points, COUNT(c.criterion_id) AS criteria_count, MIN(c.created_at) AS criteria_created_at, MAX(c.updated_at) AS criteria_updated_at FROM criteria AS c GROUP BY c.assignment_id), CombinedDetails AS (SELECT ad.assignment_id, ad.assignment_name, ad.assignment_type, ad.total_points, ad.assignment_created_at, ad.assignment_updated_at, ad.scale_name, ad.grading_scale_description, ad.submission_count, ad.average_grade, ad.highest_grade, ad.lowest_grade, cd.total_criteria_points, cd.criteria_count, cd.criteria_created_at, cd.criteria_updated_at FROM AssignmentDetails AS ad LEFT JOIN CriteriaDetails AS cd ON ad.assignment_id = cd.assignment_id) SELECT cd.assignment_id, cd.assignment_name, cd.assignment_type, cd.total_points, cd.assignment_created_at, cd.assignment_updated_at, cd.scale_name, cd.grading_scale_description, cd.submission_count, cd.average_grade, cd.highest_grade, cd.lowest_grade, cd.total_criteria_points, cd.criteria_count, cd.criteria_created_at, cd.criteria_updated_at, LEAST(cd.assignment_created_at, cd.criteria_created_at) AS earliest_creation_date, GREATEST(cd.assignment_updated_at, cd.criteria_updated_at) AS latest_update_date FROM CombinedDetails AS cd ORDER BY cd.assignment_id NULLS FIRST

question: What is the running total of revenue generated from sales, considering the monthly sales, returns, and successful payments?
external_knowledge:
- The cumulative revenue is the sum of total revenue from all sales up to a given month.
- The query takes into account the number of sales, returns, and successful payments for each month.

question: Retrieve the names, ages, ranks, residences, occupations, event descriptions, and remarks of all personnel. Additionally, include the concatenated names of users who have the same name as the personnel.

question:
**User**: I want to query some feature information.
**Assistant**: What kind of information would you like to know about the features?
**User**: I want to see their names, categories, and some metrics like stability ratings and error rates.
**Assistant**: And how about user engagement? Would you like to know how many feedbacks each feature has received?
**User**: Yes, that would be great. Can you also summarize this information in one line per feature?
**Assistant**: So, you want a summary that includes the category, stability rating, average error rate, and total feedbacks for each feature?
**User**: Exactly. And can you sort the features by the number of feedbacks they've received?
**Assistant**: In what order would you like them sorted? By the feature with the most feedbacks first or the least?
**User**: I'd like them sorted in descending order, so the feature with the most feedbacks appears first.
**Assistant**: Alright, I'll help you construct a query to get this information.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH FeatureSummary AS ( SELECT f.feature_id, f.feature_name, fc.category_name AS feature_category, sr.rating_name AS stability_rating, COUNT(uf.feedback_id) AS total_feedbacks, AVG(fm.error_rate) AS avg_error_rate FROM features f LEFT JOIN feature_category_links fcl ON f.feature_id = fcl.feature_id LEFT JOIN feature_categories fc ON fcl.category_id = fc.category_id LEFT JOIN stability_ratings sr ON f.stability_rating_id = sr.rating_id LEFT JOIN user_feedback uf ON f.feature_id = uf.feature_id LEFT JOIN feature_metrics fm ON f.feature_id = fm.feature_id GROUP BY f.feature_id, f.feature_name, fc.category_name, sr.rating_name ) SELECT fs.feature_name, fs.feature_category || ' (' || fs.stability_rating || ' - ' || CAST(fs.avg_error_rate AS TEXT) || ') ' || 'Total Feedbacks: ' || fs.total_feedbacks AS feature_summary FROM FeatureSummary fs ORDER BY fs.total_feedbacks DESC

question: Hey, could you get me a list of all the store names that have a comprehensive report for the current month, including their sales, customer feedback, services offered, active promotions, and ongoing marketing campaigns?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RECURSIVE CurrentMonthSales AS ( SELECT store_id, SUM(total_amount) AS total_sales FROM sales WHERE strftime('%Y-%m', sale_date) = strftime('%Y-%m', 'now') GROUP BY store_id ), FeedbackStats AS ( SELECT store_id, COUNT(feedback_id) AS feedback_count, AVG(rating) AS average_rating FROM feedback WHERE strftime('%Y-%m', feedback_date) = strftime('%Y-%m', 'now') GROUP BY store_id ), ActivePromotions AS ( SELECT store_id, promotion_description, discount_percentage FROM promotions WHERE start_date <= 'now' AND (end_date > 'now' OR end_date IS NULL) ), CurrentMarketingCampaigns AS ( SELECT store_id, campaign_name, budget, target_audience FROM marketing_campaigns WHERE start_date <= 'now' AND (end_date > 'now' OR end_date IS NULL) ), StoreServiceDetails AS ( SELECT s.store_id, serv.service_name, serv.category FROM stores s JOIN store_services ss ON s.store_id = ss.store_id JOIN services serv ON ss.service_id = serv.service_id ), ReportData AS ( SELECT s.store_id, s.name AS store_name, s.address AS store_address, IFNULL(cms.total_sales, 0) AS total_sales, IFNULL(fs.feedback_count, 0) AS feedback_count, IFNULL(fs.average_rating, 0) AS average_rating, GROUP_CONCAT(ssd.service_name || ' (' || ssd.category || ')', ', ') AS services_offered, GROUP_CONCAT(ap.promotion_description || ' - ' || ap.discount_percentage || '%', ', ') AS active_promotions, GROUP_CONCAT(cm.campaign_name || ' - ' || cm.target_audience || ' - ' || cm.budget, ', ') AS current_marketing_campaigns FROM stores s LEFT JOIN CurrentMonthSales cms ON s.store_id = cms.store_id LEFT JOIN FeedbackStats fs ON s.store_id = fs.store_id LEFT JOIN ActivePromotions ap ON s.store_id = ap.store_id LEFT JOIN CurrentMarketingCampaigns cm ON s.store_id = cm.store_id LEFT JOIN StoreServiceDetails ssd ON s.store_id = ssd.store_id GROUP BY s.store_id, s.name, s.address, cms.total_sales, fs.feedback_count, fs.average_rating ) SELECT store_name AS report_column FROM ReportData

question: Hey, could you show me the top three most common traffic stop outcomes along with how many times they occurred and their average citation amounts (or 0 if no citations were given), ranked by the number of stops in descending order?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH OutcomeFrequency AS ( SELECT so.outcome_description, COUNT(ts.stop_id) AS stop_count FROM traffic_stops ts JOIN stop_outcomes so ON ts.stop_outcome_id = so.outcome_id GROUP BY so.outcome_description ), OutcomeAvgCitationAmount AS ( SELECT ts.stop_outcome_id, AVG(CAST(c.citation_amount AS REAL)) AS avg_citation_amount FROM traffic_stops ts LEFT JOIN citations c ON ts.stop_id = c.stop_id GROUP BY ts.stop_outcome_id ) SELECT of.outcome_description, of.stop_count, COALESCE(oaca.avg_citation_amount, 0) AS avg_citation_amount FROM OutcomeFrequency of LEFT JOIN OutcomeAvgCitationAmount oaca ON of.stop_count = (SELECT COUNT(stop_id) FROM traffic_stops WHERE stop_outcome_id = oaca.stop_outcome_id) ORDER BY of.stop_count DESC LIMIT 3

question:
**User**: I want to get detailed information about the configuration settings of our microcontrollers.
**Assistant**: What kind of information are you looking for? Just the current settings or the history of changes as well?
**User**: I need the history of changes, including who made them and when, as well as the current status.
**Assistant**: Do you want this information for all microcontroller instances or just specific ones?
**User**: All instances. And please include details about the products they're installed in and the users who made the changes.
**Assistant**: Would you like to filter the results based on any specific criteria, such as validation status?
**User**: Yes, I only need validated configurations.
**Assistant**: Lastly, how would you like the results presented? Just a list of values or a more detailed, readable format?
**User**: A detailed format would be best, with each setting's information concatenated into a clear string.
**Assistant**: And finally, should the results be ordered in a specific way?
**User**: By instance ID, bit ID, and then by change date, please.
**Assistant**: Alright, I'll help you translate this into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ValidatedConfigurations AS ( SELECT cs.instance_id, cs.bit_id, cs.value AS current_value, cs.last_modified, cs.modified_by, cl.change_date, cl.changed_by, cl.validation_date FROM configuration_settings cs INNER JOIN change_logs cl ON cs.setting_id = cl.setting_id WHERE cl.validation_date IS NOT NULL ), LatestConfiguration AS ( SELECT vc.instance_id, vc.bit_id, vc.current_value, vc.last_modified, vc.modified_by, vc.change_date, vc.changed_by, vc.validation_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY vc.instance_id, vc.bit_id ORDER BY vc.change_date DESC) AS rn FROM ValidatedConfigurations vc ), FinalConfiguration AS ( SELECT lc.instance_id, lc.bit_id, lc.current_value, lc.last_modified, lc.modified_by, lc.change_date, lc.changed_by, lc.validation_date FROM LatestConfiguration lc WHERE rn = 1 ), UserDetails AS ( SELECT user_id, user_name, email, role, department FROM users ), InstanceDetails AS ( SELECT instance_id, mcu_id, product_id, status, location FROM microcontroller_instances ), ProductDetails AS ( SELECT product_id, product_model, description FROM product_models ) SELECT 'Instance ID: ' || fc.instance_id || ', Bit ID: ' || fc.bit_id || ', Bit Name: ' || cb.bit_name || ', Use Description: ' || cb.use_description || ', Default Value: ' || cb.default_value || ', Current Value: ' || fc.current_value || ', Last Modified: ' || fc.last_modified || ', Modified By: ' || mod.user_name || ' (' || mod.email || '), Change Date: ' || fc.change_date || ', Changed By: ' || chg.user_name || ' (' || chg.email || '), Validation Date: ' || fc.validation_date || ', Product Model: ' || pd.product_model || ', Product Description: ' || pd.description || ', Status: ' || id.status || ', Location: ' || id.location AS final_output FROM FinalConfiguration fc INNER JOIN configuration_bits cb ON fc.bit_id = cb.bit_id INNER JOIN UserDetails mod ON fc.modified_by = mod.user_id INNER JOIN UserDetails chg ON fc.changed_by = chg.user_id INNER JOIN InstanceDetails id ON fc.instance_id = id.instance_id INNER JOIN ProductDetails pd ON id.product_id = pd.product_id ORDER BY fc.instance_id, fc.bit_id, fc.change_date
gold_sql.mysql: WITH ValidatedConfigurations AS (SELECT cs.instance_id, cs.bit_id, cs.value AS current_value, cs.last_modified, cs.modified_by, cl.change_date, cl.changed_by, cl.validation_date FROM configuration_settings AS cs INNER JOIN change_logs AS cl ON cs.setting_id = cl.setting_id WHERE NOT cl.validation_date IS NULL), LatestConfiguration AS (SELECT vc.instance_id, vc.bit_id, vc.current_value, vc.last_modified, vc.modified_by, vc.change_date, vc.changed_by, vc.validation_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY vc.instance_id, vc.bit_id ORDER BY vc.change_date DESC) AS rn FROM ValidatedConfigurations AS vc), FinalConfiguration AS (SELECT lc.instance_id, lc.bit_id, lc.current_value, lc.last_modified, lc.modified_by, lc.change_date, lc.changed_by, lc.validation_date FROM LatestConfiguration AS lc WHERE rn = 1), UserDetails AS (SELECT user_id, user_name, email, role, department FROM users), InstanceDetails AS (SELECT instance_id, mcu_id, product_id, status, location FROM microcontroller_instances), ProductDetails AS (SELECT product_id, product_model, description FROM product_models) SELECT CONCAT('Instance ID: ', fc.instance_id, ', Bit ID: ', fc.bit_id, ', Bit Name: ', cb.bit_name, ', Use Description: ', cb.use_description, ', Default Value: ', cb.default_value, ', Current Value: ', fc.current_value, ', Last Modified: ', fc.last_modified, ', Modified By: ', question: Dive into the ocean of commerce and chart the voyage of each category's sales through the waves of time. For each ship (category) in the sea, track the quantity of cargo (total quantity) and the weight of gold (total sales) it carries each month. Also, reveal the treasure (previous month sales) it had from the previous journey (month). Present this journey in the order of the ships' names and the timeline of their voyages (months).
external_knowledge:
- 'Dive into the ocean of commerce' metaphorically refers to exploring commercial data.
- 'Chart the voyage' means to track the progress or changes over time.
- 'Ships' represent categories in this context.
- 'Cargo' stands for the quantity of products sold.
- 'Weight of gold' symbolizes the total sales value.
- 'Treasure' or 'gold' from the previous journey represents the sales from the previous month.
- The timeline of voyages refers to the sequence of months.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH monthly_sales AS ( SELECT c.category_name, STRFTIME('%Y-%m', o.order_date) AS month, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN categories c ON p.category_id = c.category_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY c.category_name, month ) SELECT ms.category_name, ms.month, ms.total_quantity, ms.total_sales, LAG(ms.total_sales) OVER (PARTITION BY ms.category_name ORDER BY ms.month) AS previous_month_sales FROM monthly_sales ms ORDER BY ms.category_name, ms.month
gold_sql.mysql: WITH monthly_sales AS (SELECT c.category_name, DATE_FORMAT(CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME), '%Y-%m') AS month, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN categories AS c ON p.category_id = c.category_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY c.category_name, month) SELECT ms.category_name, ms.month, ms.total_quantity, ms.total_sales, LAG(ms.total_sales) OVER (PARTITION BY ms.category_name ORDER BY ms.month) AS previous_month_sales FROM monthly_sales AS ms ORDER BY ms.category_name, ms.month
gold_sql.postgres: WITH monthly_sales AS (SELECT c.category_name, TO_CHAR(CAST(o.order_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY-MM') AS month, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN categories AS c ON p.category_id = c.category_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY c.category_name, month) SELECT ms.category_name, ms.month, ms.total_quantity, ms.total_sales, LAG(ms.total_sales) OVER (PARTITION BY ms.category_name ORDER BY ms.month NULLS FIRST) AS previous_month_sales FROM monthly_sales AS ms ORDER BY ms.category_name NULLS FIRST, ms.month NULLS FIRST

question: I want to know the names, average ratings, review counts, and active promotions (if any) for all businesses, ordered from highest rated to lowest, and then by the number of reviews in descending order. gold_sql.sqlite: WITH BusinessReviews AS ( SELECT b.business_id, b.name AS business_name, AVG(r.rating) AS average_rating, COUNT(*) AS review_count FROM businesses b INNER JOIN reviews r ON b.business_id = r.business_id GROUP BY b.business_id, b.name ), ActivePromotions AS ( SELECT p.business_id, GROUP_CONCAT(p.promo_description, ', ') AS active_promotions FROM promotions p WHERE p.promotion_status = 'active' GROUP BY p.business_id ) SELECT br.business_name, br.average_rating, br.review_count, IFNULL(ap.active_promotions, 'No active promotions') AS active_promotions FROM BusinessReviews br LEFT JOIN ActivePromotions ap ON br.business_id = ap.business_id ORDER BY br.average_rating DESC, br.review_count DESC

question: Could you provide the game ID and the total score (which is the sum of both parts of the score separated by a dash) of the game with the highest total score?

question: Could you please list the names of the top three salespeople for each store and category in 2017, along with the store names, based on their total sales amount for that year?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH SalesData2017 AS ( SELECT salesperson_id, store_id, category1, SUM(sales_amount) AS total_sales FROM sales_data WHERE strftime('%Y', sale_date) = '2017' GROUP BY salesperson_id, store_id, category1 ), RankedSalespeople AS ( SELECT salesperson_id, store_id, category1, total_sales, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY store_id, category1 ORDER BY total_sales DESC) AS sales_rank FROM SalesData2017 ) SELECT sp.first_name || ' ' || sp.last_name AS salesperson_name, st.store_name, rs.category1, rs.total_sales FROM RankedSalespeople rs JOIN salespeople sp ON rs.salesperson_id = sp.salesperson_id JOIN stores st ON rs.store_id = st.store_id WHERE rs.sales_rank <= 3 ORDER BY st.store_name, rs.category1, rs.sales_rank

question: What are the detailed descriptions of top-selling, highly rated, and compliant products, including their sales and overall ranks?
external_knowledge: Highly rated refers to products with an average rating of 4 or more out of 5; Compliance status is determined by regulatory compliance checks; Top-selling products are those with the highest cumulative sales.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH CumulativeSales AS ( SELECT product_id, SUM(quantity_sold) AS cumulative_sales FROM sales_data GROUP BY product_id ), AverageRating AS ( SELECT product_id, AVG(rating) AS average_rating FROM reviews GROUP BY product_id ), ComplianceStatus AS ( SELECT product_id, MAX(compliance_status) AS compliance_status FROM regulatory_compliance GROUP BY product_id ), HighlyRatedCompliantProducts AS ( SELECT p.product_id, p.product_description, cs.cumulative_sales, ar.average_rating, c.compliance_status FROM products p INNER JOIN CumulativeSales cs ON p.product_id = cs.product_id INNER JOIN AverageRating ar ON p.product_id = ar.product_id INNER JOIN ComplianceStatus c ON p.product_id = c.product_id WHERE ar.average_rating >= 4 AND c.compliance_status = 'Compliant' ), RankedSales AS ( SELECT hrcp.product_id, hrcp.product_description, hrcp.cumulative_sales, hrcp.average_rating, hrcp.compliance_status, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY hrcp.cumulative_sales DESC) AS sales_rank FROM HighlyRatedCompliantProducts hrcp ), FinalResults AS ( SELECT rs.product_id, rs.product_description, rs.cumulative_sales, rs.average_rating, rs.compliance_status, rs.sales_rank, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY rs.average_rating DESC, rs.cumulative_sales DESC) AS overall_rank FROM RankedSales rs ) SELECT product_description || ' - ' || 'Sales Rank: ' || CAST(sales_rank AS TEXT) || ' - ' || 'Overall Rank: ' || CAST(overall_rank AS TEXT) AS DetailedProductDescription FROM FinalResults ORDER BY overall_rank

question: What are the total abundances of each taxon, ranked in descending order, considering all the data collections, access logs, and quadrat summaries?
