question: I want a detailed report of all incidents, including the incident ID, date, state, city, address, latitude, longitude, type of incident, number of people killed and injured, total fatalities and injuries, operational notes, the user who reported the incident, the time the incident was reported, the response time, and the details of the response, with the most recent incidents listed first.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH CasualtyDetails AS ( SELECT cd.incident_id, SUM(cd.fatalities) AS total_fatalities, SUM(cd.injuries) AS total_injuries FROM casualties cd GROUP BY cd.incident_id ) SELECT 'Incident ID: ' || i.incident_id || ' | Date: ' || i.incident_date || ' | State: ' || s.state_name || ' | City: ' || c.city_name || ' | Address: ' || i.address || ' | Latitude: ' || i.latitude || ' | Longitude: ' || i.longitude || ' | Type: ' || it.incident_type_name || ' | Killed: ' || i.killed || ' | Injured: ' || i.injured || ' | Total Fatalities: ' || IFNULL(cd.total_fatalities, 0) || ' | Total Injuries: ' || IFNULL(cd.total_injuries, 0) || ' | Operations: ' || i.operations || ' | Reported By: ' || u.username || ' | Reported At: ' || i.reported_at || ' | Response Time: ' || ir.response_time || ' | Response Details: ' || ir.response_details AS incident_report FROM incidents i JOIN states s ON i.state_id = s.state_id JOIN cities c ON i.city_id = c.city_id JOIN incident_types it ON i.incident_type_id = it.incident_type_id JOIN users u ON i.reported_by = u.user_id LEFT JOIN CasualtyDetails cd ON i.incident_id = cd.incident_id LEFT JOIN incident_responses ir ON i.incident_id = ir.incident_id ORDER BY i.incident_date DESC
gold_sql.mysql: WITH CasualtyDetails AS (SELECT cd.incident_id, SUM(cd.fatalities) AS total_fatalities, SUM(cd.injuries) AS total_injuries FROM casualties AS cd GROUP BY cd.incident_id) SELECT CONCAT('Incident ID: ', i.incident_id, ' | Date: ', i.incident_date, ' | State: ', s.state_name, ' | City: ', c.city_name, ' | Address: ', i.address, ' | Latitude: ', i.latitude, ' | Longitude: ', i.longitude, ' | Type: ', it.incident_type_name, ' | Killed: ', i.killed, ' | Injured: ', i.injured, ' | Total Fatalities: ', COALESCE(cd.total_fatalities, 0), ' | Total Injuries: ', COALESCE(cd.total_injuries, 0), ' | Operations: ', i.operations, ' | Reported By: ', u.username, ' | Reported At: ', i.reported_at, ' | Response Time: ', ir.response_time, ' | Response Details: ', ir.response_details) AS incident_report FROM incidents AS i JOIN states AS s ON i.state_id = s.state_id JOIN cities AS c ON i.city_id = c.city_id JOIN incident_types AS it ON i.incident_type_id = it.incident_type_id JOIN users AS u ON i.reported_by = u.user_id LEFT JOIN CasualtyDetails AS cd ON i.incident_id = cd.incident_id LEFT JOIN incident_responses AS ir ON i.incident_id = ir.incident_id ORDER BY i.incident_date DESC
gold_sql.postgres: WITH CasualtyDetails AS (SELECT cd.incident_id, SUM(cd.fatalities) AS total_fatalities, SUM(cd.injuries) AS total_injuries FROM casualties AS cd GROUP BY cd.incident_id) SELECT 'Incident ID: ' || i.incident_id || ' | Date: ' || i.incident_date || ' | State: ' || s.state_name || ' | City: ' || c.city_name || ' | Address: ' || i.address || ' | Latitude: ' || i.latitude || ' | Longitude: ' || i.longitude || ' | Type: ' || it.incident_type_name || ' | Killed: ' || i.killed || ' | Injured: ' || i.injured || ' | Total Fatalities: ' || COALESCE(cd.total_fatalities, 0) || ' | Total Injuries: ' || COALESCE(cd.total_injuries, 0) || ' | Operations: ' || i.operations || ' | Reported By: ' || u.username || ' | Reported At: ' || i.reported_at || ' | Response Time: ' || ir.response_time || ' | Response Details: ' || ir.response_details AS incident_report FROM incidents AS i JOIN states AS s ON i.state_id = s.state_id JOIN cities AS c ON i.city_id = c.city_id JOIN incident_types AS it ON i.incident_type_id = it.incident_type_id JOIN users AS u ON i.reported_by = u.user_id LEFT JOIN CasualtyDetails AS cd ON i.incident_id = cd.incident_id LEFT JOIN incident_responses AS ir ON i.incident_id = ir.incident_id ORDER BY i.incident_date DESC NULLS LAST

question: What are the ASCII values of the primary characters in each character set, along with the number of times they have been accessed, listed in the order of most accessed to least accessed?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT c.ascii_value AS 'ASCII Value', COUNT(al.access_id) AS 'Access Count' FROM access_logs al INNER JOIN characters c ON al.char_id = c.char_id INNER JOIN char_set_map csm ON c.char_id = csm.char_id WHERE csm.is_primary = 1 GROUP BY c.ascii_value ORDER BY COUNT(al.access_id) DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT c.ascii_value AS `ASCII Value`, COUNT(al.access_id) AS `Access Count` FROM access_logs AS al INNER JOIN characters AS c ON al.char_id = c.char_id INNER JOIN char_set_map AS csm ON c.char_id = csm.char_id WHERE csm.is_primary = 1 GROUP BY c.ascii_value ORDER BY COUNT(al.access_id) DESC
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT c.ascii_value AS "ASCII Value", COUNT(al.access_id) AS "Access Count" FROM access_logs AS al INNER JOIN characters AS c ON al.char_id = c.char_id INNER JOIN char_set_map AS csm ON c.char_id = csm.char_id WHERE csm.is_primary = 1 GROUP BY c.ascii_value ORDER BY COUNT(al.access_id) DESC NULLS LAST

question: What are the names of countries with a population greater than 10 million and more than 10 guns per 100 inhabitants in 2012, along with the number of guns per 100 inhabitants, considering all countries regardless of whether they had mass shootings or not, listed in order from highest to lowest gun ownership rate?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT c.country_name, fs.guns_per_100_inhabitants FROM countries c JOIN population_data p ON c.country_id = p.country_id JOIN firearm_statistics fs ON c.country_id = fs.country_id WHERE p.year = 2012 AND fs.year = 2012 AND CAST(REPLACE(p.population, ',', '') AS INTEGER) > 10000000 AND fs.guns_per_100_inhabitants > 10 ORDER BY fs.guns_per_100_inhabitants DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT c.country_name, fs.guns_per_100_inhabitants FROM countries AS c JOIN population_data AS p ON c.country_id = p.country_id JOIN firearm_statistics AS fs ON c.country_id = fs.country_id WHERE p.year = 2012 AND fs.year = 2012 AND CAST(REPLACE(p.population, ',', '') AS SIGNED) > 10000000 AND fs.guns_per_100_inhabitants > 10 ORDER BY fs.guns_per_100_inhabitants DESC
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT c.country_name, fs.guns_per_100_inhabitants FROM countries AS c JOIN population_data AS p ON c.country_id = p.country_id JOIN firearm_statistics AS fs ON c.country_id = fs.country_id WHERE p.year = 2012 AND fs.year = 2012 AND CAST(REPLACE(p.population, ',', '') AS INT) > 10000000 AND fs.guns_per_100_inhabitants > 10 ORDER BY fs.guns_per_100_inhabitants DESC NULLS LAST

question: What are the detailed records for all fees, including their descriptions, types, departments, quantities, amounts, payment statuses, and any associated remarks?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH FeeDetails AS ( SELECT f.fee_id, f.description AS fee_description, ft.fee_type_name, d.dept_name, f.quantity, f.amount, fp.payment_status AS latest_payment_status FROM fees f JOIN departments d ON f.dept_id = d.dept_id JOIN fee_types ft ON f.fee_type_id = ft.fee_type_id LEFT JOIN ( SELECT fee_id, MAX(payment_date) AS latest_payment_date FROM fee_payments GROUP BY fee_id ) fpd ON f.fee_id = fpd.fee_id LEFT JOIN fee_payments fp ON fp.fee_id = f.fee_id AND fp.payment_date = fpd.latest_payment_date ), FeeRemarks AS ( SELECT fr.fee_id, GROUP_CONCAT(fr.remark_text, ' | ') AS all_remarks FROM fee_remarks fr GROUP BY fr.fee_id ) SELECT fd.fee_id, fd.fee_description, fd.fee_type_name, fd.dept_name, fd.quantity, fd.amount, fd.latest_payment_status, fr.all_remarks FROM FeeDetails fd LEFT JOIN FeeRemarks fr ON fd.fee_id = fr.fee_id ORDER BY fd.fee_id
gold_sql.mysql: WITH FeeDetails AS (SELECT f.fee_id, f.description AS fee_description, ft.fee_type_name, d.dept_name, f.quantity, f.amount, fp.payment_status AS latest_payment_status FROM fees AS f JOIN departments AS d ON f.dept_id = d.dept_id JOIN fee_types AS ft ON f.fee_type_id = ft.fee_type_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT fee_id, MAX(payment_date) AS latest_payment_date FROM fee_payments GROUP BY fee_id) AS fpd ON f.fee_id = fpd.fee_id LEFT JOIN fee_payments AS fp ON fp.fee_id = f.fee_id AND fp.payment_date = fpd.latest_payment_date), FeeRemarks AS (SELECT fr.fee_id, GROUP_CONCAT(fr.remark_text SEPARATOR ' | ') AS all_remarks FROM fee_remarks AS fr GROUP BY fr.fee_id) SELECT fd.fee_id, fd.fee_description, fd.fee_type_name, fd.dept_name, fd.quantity, fd.amount, fd.latest_payment_status, fr.all_remarks FROM FeeDetails AS fd LEFT JOIN FeeRemarks AS fr ON fd.fee_id = fr.fee_id ORDER BY fd.fee_id
gold_sql.postgres: WITH FeeDetails AS (SELECT f.fee_id, f.description AS fee_description, ft.fee_type_name, d.dept_name, f.quantity, f.amount, fp.payment_status AS latest_payment_status FROM fees AS f JOIN departments AS d ON f.dept_id = d.dept_id JOIN fee_types AS ft ON f.fee_type_id = ft.fee_type_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT fee_id, MAX(payment_date) AS latest_payment_date FROM fee_payments GROUP BY fee_id) AS fpd ON f.fee_id = fpd.fee_id LEFT JOIN fee_payments AS fp ON fp.fee_id = f.fee_id AND fp.payment_date = fpd.latest_payment_date), FeeRemarks AS (SELECT fr.fee_id, STRING_AGG(fr.remark_text, ' | ') AS all_remarks FROM fee_remarks AS fr GROUP BY fr.fee_id) SELECT fd.fee_id, fd.fee_description, fd.fee_type_name, fd.dept_name, fd.quantity, fd.amount, fd.latest_payment_status, fr.all_remarks FROM FeeDetails AS fd LEFT JOIN FeeRemarks AS fr ON fd.fee_id = fr.fee_id ORDER BY fd.fee_id NULLS FIRST

question: Who is the reigning champion, the player currently holding the top spot in the rankings?
external_knowledge: 'reigning champion' refers to the player with the highest rank (rank = 1) in the most recent ranking record.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT p.player_name FROM players p JOIN ( SELECT player_id FROM rankings WHERE rank = 1 ORDER BY date DESC LIMIT 1 ) r ON p.player_id = r.player_id
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT p.player_name FROM players AS p JOIN (SELECT player_id FROM rankings WHERE `rank` = 1 ORDER BY date DESC LIMIT 1) AS r ON p.player_id = r.player_id
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT p.player_name FROM players AS p JOIN (SELECT player_id FROM rankings WHERE rank = 1 ORDER BY date DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1) AS r ON p.player_id = r.player_id

question: Could you provide a list of all available datasets, including their titles, dates, producer names, countries, abstracts, citations, keywords, access URLs, publication dates, DOIs, licenses, data formats, file sizes, and update frequencies, as well as the number of annotations and the names of the annotators for each dataset, sorted by the number of annotations in descending order and then alphabetically by title?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH AnnotationDetails AS ( SELECT a.dataset_id, COUNT(a.annotation_id) AS annotation_count, GROUP_CONCAT(u.user_name) AS annotators FROM annotations a INNER JOIN users u ON a.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY a.dataset_id ), DatasetDetails AS ( SELECT d.dataset_id, d.title, d.date, d.abstract, d.citation, d.keywords, d.access_url, d.published_date, d.doi, d.license, d.data_format, d.file_size, d.update_frequency, p.producer_name, p.country FROM datasets d INNER JOIN producers p ON d.producer_id = p.producer_id ) SELECT dd.title, dd.date, dd.producer_name, dd.country, dd.abstract, dd.citation, dd.keywords, dd.access_url, dd.published_date, dd.doi, dd.license, dd.data_format, dd.file_size, dd.update_frequency, COALESCE(ad.annotation_count, 0) AS annotation_count, COALESCE(ad.annotators, '') AS annotators FROM DatasetDetails dd LEFT JOIN AnnotationDetails ad ON dd.dataset_id = ad.dataset_id ORDER BY ad.annotation_count DESC, dd.title
gold_sql.mysql: WITH AnnotationDetails AS (SELECT a.dataset_id, COUNT(a.annotation_id) AS annotation_count, GROUP_CONCAT(u.user_name SEPARATOR ',') AS annotators FROM annotations AS a INNER JOIN users AS u ON a.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY a.dataset_id), DatasetDetails AS (SELECT d.dataset_id, d.title, d.date, d.abstract, d.citation, d.keywords, d.access_url, d.published_date, d.doi, d.license, d.data_format, d.file_size, d.update_frequency, p.producer_name, p.country FROM datasets AS d INNER JOIN producers AS p ON d.producer_id = p.producer_id) SELECT dd.title, dd.date, dd.producer_name, dd.country, dd.abstract, dd.citation, dd.keywords, dd.access_url, dd.published_date, dd.doi, dd.license, dd.data_format, dd.file_size, dd.update_frequency, COALESCE(ad.annotation_count, 0) AS annotation_count, COALESCE(ad.annotators, '') AS annotators FROM DatasetDetails AS dd LEFT JOIN AnnotationDetails AS ad ON dd.dataset_id = ad.dataset_id ORDER BY ad.annotation_count DESC, dd.title
gold_sql.postgres: WITH AnnotationDetails AS (SELECT a.dataset_id, COUNT(a.annotation_id) AS annotation_count, STRING_AGG(u.user_name, ',') AS annotators FROM annotations AS a INNER JOIN users AS u ON a.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY a.dataset_id), DatasetDetails AS (SELECT d.dataset_id, d.title, d.date, d.abstract, d.citation, d.keywords, d.access_url, d.published_date, d.doi, d.license, d.data_format, d.file_size, d.update_frequency, p.producer_name, p.country FROM datasets AS d INNER JOIN producers AS p ON d.producer_id = p.producer_id) SELECT dd.title, dd.date, dd.producer_name, dd.country, dd.abstract, dd.citation, dd.keywords, dd.access_url, dd.published_date, dd.doi, dd.license, dd.data_format, dd.file_size, dd.update_frequency, COALESCE(ad.annotation_count, 0) AS annotation_count, COALESCE(ad.annotators, '') AS annotators FROM DatasetDetails AS dd LEFT JOIN AnnotationDetails AS ad ON dd.dataset_id = ad.dataset_id ORDER BY ad.annotation_count DESC NULLS LAST, dd.title NULLS FIRST

question: What are the manufacturers, models, average original costs, average current values, and counts of the high-value marine equipment that are currently in use and in good condition, listed in order of highest average original cost?
external_knowledge: High-value equipment refers to equipment with an average current value greater than $10,000; good condition refers to equipment with a condition of 'A'; in use refers to equipment with a status of 'In Use'.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT manufacturer, model, AVG(original_cost) AS average_original_cost, AVG(current_value) AS average_current_value, COUNT(ooi_barcode) AS equipment_count FROM marine_equipment WHERE condition = 'A' AND status = 'In Use' GROUP BY manufacturer, model HAVING AVG(current_value) > 10000 ORDER BY average_original_cost DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT manufacturer, model, AVG(original_cost) AS average_original_cost, AVG(current_value) AS average_current_value, COUNT(ooi_barcode) AS equipment_count FROM marine_equipment WHERE `condition` = 'A' AND status = 'In Use' GROUP BY manufacturer, model HAVING AVG(current_value) > 10000 ORDER BY average_original_cost DESC
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT manufacturer, model, AVG(original_cost) AS average_original_cost, AVG(current_value) AS average_current_value, COUNT(ooi_barcode) AS equipment_count FROM marine_equipment WHERE condition = 'A' AND status = 'In Use' GROUP BY manufacturer, model HAVING AVG(current_value) > 10000 ORDER BY average_original_cost DESC NULLS LAST

question: Could you provide a summary of the total number of approved leave requests for each month and year, categorized by the employment status of the employees?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', lr.start_date) AS year_month, e.employee_status, COUNT(DISTINCT lr.leave_id) AS total_approved_leaves FROM leave_requests lr JOIN employees e ON lr.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE lr.status = 'Approved' GROUP BY year_month, e.employee_status ORDER BY year_month, e.employee_status
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(CAST(lr.start_date AS DATETIME), '%Y-%m') AS `year_month`, e.employee_status, COUNT(DISTINCT lr.leave_id) AS total_approved_leaves FROM leave_requests AS lr JOIN employees AS e ON lr.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE lr.status = 'Approved' GROUP BY `year_month`, e.employee_status ORDER BY `year_month`, e.employee_status
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT TO_CHAR(CAST(lr.start_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY-MM') AS year_month, e.employee_status, COUNT(DISTINCT lr.leave_id) AS total_approved_leaves FROM leave_requests AS lr JOIN employees AS e ON lr.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE lr.status = 'Approved' GROUP BY year_month, e.employee_status ORDER BY year_month NULLS FIRST, e.employee_status NULLS FIRST

question: Could you provide a list of stocks along with their industry, sector, market capitalization, exchange name, latest opening and closing prices, average impact of holidays on their prices, and average closing prices during trading hours, ordered alphabetically by stock name?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH LatestPrices AS ( SELECT sp.stock_id, MAX(sp.date) AS latest_date FROM stock_prices sp GROUP BY sp.stock_id ), StockLatestData AS ( SELECT lp.stock_id, sp.open AS latest_open, sp.close AS latest_close, s.stock_name, s.industry, s.sector, s.market_cap, e.exchange_name FROM LatestPrices lp JOIN stock_prices sp ON lp.stock_id = sp.stock_id AND lp.latest_date = sp.date JOIN stocks s ON lp.stock_id = s.stock_id JOIN exchanges e ON s.exchange_id = e.exchange_id ), HolidayImpact AS ( SELECT h.exchange_id, s.stock_id, AVG((sp2.close - sp.close) / sp.close * 100) AS avg_holiday_impact_percentage FROM market_holidays h JOIN stocks s ON s.exchange_id = h.exchange_id JOIN stock_prices sp ON sp.stock_id = s.stock_id AND sp.date < h.date JOIN stock_prices sp2 ON sp2.stock_id = s.stock_id AND sp2.date > h.date WHERE sp.date = (SELECT MAX(date) FROM stock_prices WHERE date < h.date AND stock_id = s.stock_id) AND sp2.date = (SELECT MIN(date) FROM stock_prices WHERE date > h.date AND stock_id = s.stock_id) GROUP BY h.exchange_id, s.stock_id ), TradingHoursImpact AS ( SELECT th.exchange_id, s.stock_id, AVG(sp.close) AS avg_close_during_hours FROM trading_hours th JOIN stocks s ON s.exchange_id = th.exchange_id JOIN stock_prices sp ON sp.stock_id = s.stock_id WHERE strftime('%w', sp.date) = th.day GROUP BY th.exchange_id, s.stock_id ) SELECT sld.stock_name, sld.industry, sld.sector, sld.market_cap, sld.exchange_name, sld.latest_open, sld.latest_close, COALESCE(hi.avg_holiday_impact_percentage, 0) AS avg_holiday_impact, COALESCE(thi.avg_close_during_hours, 0) AS avg_close_within_hours FROM StockLatestData sld LEFT JOIN HolidayImpact hi ON sld.stock_id = hi.stock_id LEFT JOIN TradingHoursImpact thi ON sld.stock_id = thi.stock_id ORDER BY sld.stock_name
gold_sql.mysql: WITH LatestPrices AS (SELECT sp.stock_id, MAX(sp.date) AS latest_date FROM stock_prices AS sp GROUP BY sp.stock_id), StockLatestData AS (SELECT lp.stock_id, sp.open AS latest_open, sp.close AS latest_close, s.stock_name, s.industry, s.sector, s.market_cap, e.exchange_name FROM LatestPrices AS lp JOIN stock_prices AS sp ON lp.stock_id = sp.stock_id AND lp.latest_date = sp.date JOIN stocks AS s ON lp.stock_id = s.stock_id JOIN exchanges AS e ON s.exchange_id = e.exchange_id), HolidayImpact AS (SELECT h.exchange_id, s.stock_id, AVG((sp2.close - sp.close) / sp.close * 100) AS avg_holiday_impact_percentage FROM market_holidays AS h JOIN stocks AS s ON s.exchange_id = h.exchange_id JOIN stock_prices AS sp ON sp.stock_id = s.stock_id AND sp.date < h.date JOIN stock_prices AS sp2 ON sp2.stock_id = s.stock_id AND sp2.date > h.date WHERE sp.date = (SELECT MAX(date) FROM stock_prices WHERE date < h.date AND stock_id = s.stock_id) AND sp2.date = (SELECT MIN(date) FROM stock_prices WHERE date > h.date AND stock_id = s.stock_id) GROUP BY h.exchange_id, s.stock_id), TradingHoursImpact AS (SELECT th.exchange_id, s.stock_id, AVG(sp.close) AS avg_close_during_hours FROM trading_hours AS th JOIN stocks AS s ON s.exchange_id = th.exchange_id JOIN stock_prices AS sp ON sp.stock_id = s.stock_id WHERE DATE_FORMAT(CAST(sp.date AS DATETIME), '%w') = th.day GROUP BY th.exchange_id, s.stock_id) SELECT sld.stock_name, sld.industry, sld.sector, sld.market_cap, sld.exchange_name, sld.latest_open, sld.latest_close, COALESCE(hi.avg_holiday_impact_percentage, 0) AS avg_holiday_impact, COALESCE(thi.avg_close_during_hours, 0) AS avg_close_within_hours FROM StockLatestData AS sld LEFT JOIN HolidayImpact AS hi ON sld.stock_id = hi.stock_id LEFT JOIN TradingHoursImpact AS thi ON sld.stock_id = thi.stock_id ORDER BY sld.stock_name
gold_sql.postgres: WITH LatestPrices AS (SELECT sp.stock_id, MAX(sp.date) AS latest_date FROM stock_prices AS sp GROUP BY sp.stock_id), StockLatestData AS (SELECT lp.stock_id, sp.open AS latest_open, sp.close AS latest_close, s.stock_name, s.industry, s.sector, s.market_cap, e.exchange_name FROM LatestPrices AS lp JOIN stock_prices AS sp ON lp.stock_id = sp.stock_id AND lp.latest_date = sp.date JOIN stocks AS s ON lp.stock_id = s.stock_id JOIN exchanges AS e ON s.exchange_id = e.exchange_id), HolidayImpact AS (SELECT h.exchange_id, s.stock_id, AVG((sp2.close - sp.close) / NULLIF(sp.close, 0) * 100) AS avg_holiday_impact_percentage FROM market_holidays AS h JOIN stocks AS s ON s.exchange_id = h.exchange_id JOIN stock_prices AS sp ON sp.stock_id = s.stock_id AND sp.date < h.date JOIN stock_prices AS sp2 ON sp2.stock_id = s.stock_id AND sp2.date > h.date WHERE sp.date = (SELECT MAX(date) FROM stock_prices WHERE date < h.date AND stock_id = s.stock_id) AND sp2.date = (SELECT MIN(date) FROM stock_prices WHERE date > h.date AND stock_id = s.stock_id) GROUP BY h.exchange_id, s.stock_id), TradingHoursImpact AS (SELECT th.exchange_id, s.stock_id, AVG(sp.close) AS avg_close_during_hours FROM trading_hours AS th JOIN stocks AS s ON s.exchange_id = th.exchange_id JOIN stock_prices AS sp ON sp.stock_id = s.stock_id WHERE TO_CHAR(CAST(sp.date AS TIMESTAMP), '%w') = th.day GROUP BY th.exchange_id, s.stock_id) SELECT sld.stock_name, sld.industry, sld.sector, sld.market_cap, sld.exchange_name, sld.latest_open, sld.latest_close, COALESCE(hi.avg_holiday_impact_percentage, 0) AS avg_holiday_impact, COALESCE(thi.avg_close_during_hours, 0) AS avg_close_within_hours FROM StockLatestData AS sld LEFT JOIN HolidayImpact AS hi ON sld.stock_id = hi.stock_id LEFT JOIN TradingHoursImpact AS thi ON sld.stock_id = thi.stock_id ORDER BY sld.stock_name NULLS FIRST

question: What are the names of the top 10 highest-paid players and the seasons they were active in?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH PlayerSalary AS ( SELECT player_id, player_name, team, salary, CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(salary, '$', ''), ',', '') AS REAL) AS numeric_salary FROM players ), ActiveSeasons AS ( SELECT p.player_id, s.season_name FROM players p JOIN seasons s ON p.contract_start_date <= s.end_date AND p.contract_end_date >= s.start_date ), SeasonSummary AS ( SELECT player_id, GROUP_CONCAT(season_name) AS active_seasons FROM ActiveSeasons GROUP BY player_id ) SELECT ps.player_name, ss.active_seasons FROM PlayerSalary ps JOIN SeasonSummary ss ON ps.player_id = ss.player_id ORDER BY ps.numeric_salary DESC LIMIT 10
gold_sql.mysql: WITH PlayerSalary AS (SELECT player_id, player_name, team, salary, CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(salary, '$', ''), ',', '') AS FLOAT) AS numeric_salary FROM players), ActiveSeasons AS (SELECT p.player_id, s.season_name FROM players AS p JOIN seasons AS s ON p.contract_start_date <= s.end_date AND p.contract_end_date >= s.start_date), SeasonSummary AS (SELECT player_id, GROUP_CONCAT(season_name SEPARATOR ',') AS active_seasons FROM ActiveSeasons GROUP BY player_id) SELECT ps.player_name, ss.active_seasons FROM PlayerSalary AS ps JOIN SeasonSummary AS ss ON ps.player_id = ss.player_id ORDER BY ps.numeric_salary DESC LIMIT 10
gold_sql.postgres: WITH PlayerSalary AS (SELECT player_id, player_name, team, salary, CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(salary, '$', ''), ',', '') AS REAL) AS numeric_salary FROM players), ActiveSeasons AS (SELECT p.player_id, s.season_name FROM players AS p JOIN seasons AS s ON p.contract_start_date <= s.end_date AND p.contract_end_date >= s.start_date), SeasonSummary AS (SELECT player_id, STRING_AGG(season_name, ',') AS active_seasons FROM ActiveSeasons GROUP BY player_id) SELECT ps.player_name, ss.active_seasons FROM PlayerSalary AS ps JOIN SeasonSummary AS ss ON ps.player_id = ss.player_id ORDER BY ps.numeric_salary DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

question: What are the names, total contracts, sales values, commissions, sales ranks, associated unit names, property types, unit sales, and revenues for the top-performing sales agents, considering only their sales transactions and signed sale contracts?
external_knowledge: Top-performing sales agents refer to those with the highest total sales value; Signed sale contracts refer to contracts with a status of 'signed' and a type of 'sale'; Sales transactions of type 'sale' are considered for calculating agent performance.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH AgentPerformance AS ( SELECT s.agent_id, a.agent_name, COUNT(c.contract_id) AS total_contracts, SUM(CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(c.total_price, '$', ''), ',', '') AS INTEGER)) AS total_sales_value, SUM(CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(s.commission, '$', ''), ',', '') AS INTEGER)) AS total_commission, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(c.total_price, '$', ''), ',', '') AS INTEGER)) DESC) AS sales_rank FROM sales_transactions s JOIN contracts c ON s.contract_id = c.contract_id JOIN sales_agents a ON c.agent_id = a.agent_id WHERE s.transaction_type = 'sale' AND c.status = 'signed' AND c.contract_type = 'sale' GROUP BY s.agent_id, a.agent_name ), UnitSales AS ( SELECT c.unit_id, u.unit_name, t.type_name, COUNT(c.contract_id) AS total_sales, SUM(CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(c.total_price, '$', ''), ',', '') AS INTEGER)) AS total_revenue FROM contracts c JOIN units u ON c.unit_id = u.unit_id JOIN property_types t ON u.type_id = t.type_id WHERE c.status = 'signed' AND c.contract_type = 'sale' GROUP BY c.unit_id, u.unit_name, t.type_name ) SELECT ap.agent_name, ap.total_contracts, ap.total_sales_value, ap.total_commission, ap.sales_rank, us.unit_name, us.type_name, us.total_sales, us.total_revenue FROM AgentPerformance ap LEFT JOIN UnitSales us ON ap.agent_id = us.unit_id ORDER BY ap.sales_rank
gold_sql.mysql: WITH AgentPerformance AS (SELECT s.agent_id, a.agent_name, COUNT(c.contract_id) AS total_contracts, SUM(CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(c.total_price, '$', ''), ',', '') AS SIGNED)) AS total_sales_value, SUM(CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(s.commission, '$', ''), ',', '') AS SIGNED)) AS total_commission, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(c.total_price, '$', ''), ',', '') AS SIGNED)) DESC) AS sales_rank FROM sales_transactions AS s JOIN contracts AS c ON s.contract_id = c.contract_id JOIN sales_agents AS a ON c.agent_id = a.agent_id WHERE s.transaction_type = 'sale' AND c.status = 'signed' AND c.contract_type = 'sale' GROUP BY s.agent_id, a.agent_name), UnitSales AS (SELECT c.unit_id, u.unit_name, t.type_name, COUNT(c.contract_id) AS total_sales, SUM(CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(c.total_price, '$', ''), ',', '') AS SIGNED)) AS total_revenue FROM contracts AS c JOIN units AS u ON c.unit_id = u.unit_id JOIN property_types AS t ON u.type_id = t.type_id WHERE c.status = 'signed' AND c.contract_type = 'sale' GROUP BY c.unit_id, u.unit_name, t.type_name) SELECT ap.agent_name, ap.total_contracts, ap.total_sales_value, ap.total_commission, ap.sales_rank, us.unit_name, us.type_name, us.total_sales, us.total_revenue FROM AgentPerformance AS ap LEFT JOIN UnitSales AS us ON ap.agent_id = us.unit_id ORDER BY ap.sales_rank
gold_sql.postgres: WITH AgentPerformance AS (SELECT s.agent_id, a.agent_name, COUNT(c.contract_id) AS total_contracts, SUM(CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(c.total_price, '$', ''), ',', '') AS INT)) AS total_sales_value, SUM(CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(s.commission, '$', ''), ',', '') AS INT)) AS total_commission, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(c.total_price, '$', ''), ',', '') AS INT)) DESC NULLS LAST) AS sales_rank FROM sales_transactions AS s JOIN contracts AS c ON s.contract_id = c.contract_id JOIN sales_agents AS a ON c.agent_id = a.agent_id WHERE s.transaction_type = 'sale' AND c.status = 'signed' AND c.contract_type = 'sale' GROUP BY s.agent_id, a.agent_name), UnitSales AS (SELECT c.unit_id, u.unit_name, t.type_name, COUNT(c.contract_id) AS total_sales, SUM(CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(c.total_price, '$', ''), ',', '') AS INT)) AS total_revenue FROM contracts AS c JOIN units AS u ON c.unit_id = u.unit_id JOIN property_types AS t ON u.type_id = t.type_id WHERE c.status = 'signed' AND c.contract_type = 'sale' GROUP BY c.unit_id, u.unit_name, t.type_name) SELECT ap.agent_name, ap.total_contracts, ap.total_sales_value, ap.total_commission, ap.sales_rank, us.unit_name, us.type_name, us.total_sales, us.total_revenue FROM AgentPerformance AS ap LEFT JOIN UnitSales AS us ON ap.agent_id = us.unit_id ORDER BY ap.sales_rank NULLS FIRST

question: Could you please find the average number of years of experience for respondents who are comfortable with Haskell and have advanced proficiency in Oracle 12c?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT AVG(pl.years_of_experience) AS avg_years_of_experience FROM programming_languages pl INNER JOIN databases db ON pl.respondent_id = db.respondent_id WHERE pl.language = 'Haskell' AND db.database = 'Oracle 12c' AND db.proficiency_level = 'Advanced'
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT AVG(pl.years_of_experience) AS avg_years_of_experience FROM programming_languages AS pl INNER JOIN `databases` AS db ON pl.respondent_id = db.respondent_id WHERE pl.language = 'Haskell' AND db.`database` = 'Oracle 12c' AND db.proficiency_level = 'Advanced'

question: Could you please gather all the components along with their overall performance scores and details such as the list of usernames with their respective permission levels and the versions available for each component? I need the results sorted in descending order of their overall performance scores.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ComponentMetrics AS ( SELECT c.component_id, c.component_name, AVG(cm.sn74) AS avg_sn74, AVG(cm.abt) AS avg_abt FROM components c INNER JOIN performance_metrics cm ON c.component_id = cm.component_id GROUP BY c.component_id, c.component_name ), ComponentPermissions AS ( SELECT cp.component_id, u.username, cp.permission_level FROM user_component_permissions cp INNER JOIN users u ON cp.user_id = u.user_id ), ComponentVersions AS ( SELECT v.component_id, GROUP_CONCAT(v.version, ', ') AS versions FROM component_versions v GROUP BY v.component_id ), ComponentOverallMetrics AS ( SELECT cm.component_id, cm.component_name, (cm.avg_sn74 + cm.avg_abt) / 2 AS overall_performance_score FROM ComponentMetrics cm ) SELECT om.component_id, om.component_name, om.overall_performance_score, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT p.username) AS users_with_permissions, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT p.permission_level) AS permission_levels, v.versions FROM ComponentOverallMetrics om LEFT JOIN ComponentPermissions p ON om.component_id = p.component_id LEFT JOIN ComponentVersions v ON om.component_id = v.component_id GROUP BY om.component_id, om.component_name, om.overall_performance_score, v.versions ORDER BY om.overall_performance_score DESC
gold_sql.mysql: WITH ComponentMetrics AS (SELECT c.component_id, c.component_name, AVG(cm.sn74) AS avg_sn74, AVG(cm.abt) AS avg_abt FROM components AS c INNER JOIN performance_metrics AS cm ON c.component_id = cm.component_id GROUP BY c.component_id, c.component_name), ComponentPermissions AS (SELECT cp.component_id, u.username, cp.permission_level FROM user_component_permissions AS cp INNER JOIN users AS u ON cp.user_id = u.user_id), ComponentVersions AS (SELECT v.component_id, GROUP_CONCAT(v.version SEPARATOR ', ') AS versions FROM component_versions AS v GROUP BY v.component_id), ComponentOverallMetrics AS (SELECT cm.component_id, cm.component_name, (cm.avg_sn74 + cm.avg_abt) / 2 AS overall_performance_score FROM ComponentMetrics AS cm) SELECT om.component_id, om.component_name, om.overall_performance_score, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT p.username SEPARATOR ',') AS users_with_permissions, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT p.permission_level SEPARATOR ',') AS permission_levels, v.versions FROM ComponentOverallMetrics AS om LEFT JOIN ComponentPermissions AS p ON om.component_id = p.component_id LEFT JOIN ComponentVersions AS v ON om.component_id = v.component_id GROUP BY om.component_id, om.component_name, om.overall_performance_score, v.versions ORDER BY om.overall_performance_score DESC
gold_sql.postgres: WITH ComponentMetrics AS (SELECT c.component_id, c.component_name, AVG(cm.sn74) AS avg_sn74, AVG(cm.abt) AS avg_abt FROM components AS c INNER JOIN performance_metrics AS cm ON c.component_id = cm.component_id GROUP BY c.component_id, c.component_name), ComponentPermissions AS (SELECT cp.component_id, u.username, cp.permission_level FROM user_component_permissions AS cp INNER JOIN users AS u ON cp.user_id = u.user_id), ComponentVersions AS (SELECT v.component_id, STRING_AGG(v.version, ', ') AS versions FROM component_versions AS v GROUP BY v.component_id), ComponentOverallMetrics AS (SELECT cm.component_id, cm.component_name, (cm.avg_sn74 + cm.avg_abt) / NULLIF(2, 0) AS overall_performance_score FROM ComponentMetrics AS cm) SELECT om.component_id, om.component_name, om.overall_performance_score, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT p.username, ',') AS users_with_permissions, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT p.permission_level, ',') AS permission_levels, v.versions FROM ComponentOverallMetrics AS om LEFT JOIN ComponentPermissions AS p ON om.component_id = p.component_id LEFT JOIN ComponentVersions AS v ON om.component_id = v.component_id GROUP BY om.component_id, om.component_name, om.overall_performance_score, v.versions ORDER BY om.overall_performance_score DESC NULLS LAST

question: What is the total number of vehicles that passed through the 'Elm St & 2nd Ave' monitoring site during clear weather conditions in the year 2018?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT SUM(td.total_vehicle_count) AS total_vehicles FROM traffic_data td JOIN monitoring_sites ms ON td.site_id = ms.site_id WHERE td.weather_condition = 'clear' AND ms.site_name = 'Elm St & 2nd Ave' AND strftime('%Y', td.collection_date) = '2018'
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT SUM(td.total_vehicle_count) AS total_vehicles FROM traffic_data AS td JOIN monitoring_sites AS ms ON td.site_id = ms.site_id WHERE td.weather_condition = 'clear' AND ms.site_name = 'Elm St & 2nd Ave' AND DATE_FORMAT(CAST(td.collection_date AS DATETIME), '%Y') = '2018'
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT SUM(td.total_vehicle_count) AS total_vehicles FROM traffic_data AS td JOIN monitoring_sites AS ms ON td.site_id = ms.site_id WHERE td.weather_condition = 'clear' AND ms.site_name = 'Elm St & 2nd Ave' AND TO_CHAR(CAST(td.collection_date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY') = '2018'

question: Return a list of all players, including their names, team names, average ranks, number of top 3 finishes, number of wins, number of tournaments played, total competitive scores, total rounds won, win rates, their teams' average ranks, teams' total competitive scores, teams' total rounds won, and their overall ranks, ordered by their win rates in descending order and average ranks in ascending order.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH PlayerPerformance AS ( SELECT tr.player_id, t.tournament_id, tr.rank, tr.comp_score, tr.rounds_won, CASE WHEN tr.rank <= 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS top3, CASE WHEN tr.rank = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS wins FROM tournament_results tr JOIN tournaments t ON tr.tournament_id = t.tournament_id ), PlayerAggregate AS ( SELECT player_id, AVG(rank) AS avg_rank, SUM(top3) AS top3_finishes, SUM(wins) AS wins, COUNT(tournament_id) AS tournaments_played, SUM(comp_score) AS total_comp_score, SUM(rounds_won) AS total_rounds_won, SUM(wins) * 1.0 / COUNT(tournament_id) AS win_rate FROM PlayerPerformance GROUP BY player_id ), TeamAggregate AS ( SELECT p.player_id, p.team_id, AVG(pp.rank) AS team_avg_rank, SUM(pp.comp_score) AS team_total_comp_score, SUM(pp.rounds_won) AS team_total_rounds_won FROM PlayerPerformance pp JOIN players p ON pp.player_id = p.player_id GROUP BY p.player_id, p.team_id ), FinalStats AS ( SELECT pa.player_id, pa.avg_rank, pa.top3_finishes, pa.wins, pa.tournaments_played, pa.total_comp_score, pa.total_rounds_won, pa.win_rate, ta.team_avg_rank, ta.team_total_comp_score, ta.team_total_rounds_won FROM PlayerAggregate pa LEFT JOIN TeamAggregate ta ON pa.player_id = ta.player_id ) SELECT fs.player_id, p.player_name, t.team_name, fs.avg_rank, fs.top3_finishes, fs.wins, fs.tournaments_played, fs.total_comp_score, fs.total_rounds_won, fs.win_rate, fs.team_avg_rank, fs.team_total_comp_score, fs.team_total_rounds_won, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY fs.win_rate DESC, fs.avg_rank ASC) AS overall_rank FROM FinalStats fs JOIN players p ON fs.player_id = p.player_id JOIN teams t ON p.team_id = t.team_id ORDER BY overall_rank
gold_sql.mysql: WITH PlayerPerformance AS (SELECT tr.player_id, t.tournament_id, tr.`rank`, tr.comp_score, tr.rounds_won, CASE WHEN tr.`rank` <= 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS top3, CASE WHEN tr.`rank` = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS wins FROM tournament_results AS tr JOIN tournaments AS t ON tr.tournament_id = t.tournament_id), PlayerAggregate AS (SELECT player_id, AVG(`rank`) AS avg_rank, SUM(top3) AS top3_finishes, SUM(wins) AS wins, COUNT(tournament_id) AS tournaments_played, SUM(comp_score) AS total_comp_score, SUM(rounds_won) AS total_rounds_won, SUM(wins) * 1.0 / COUNT(tournament_id) AS win_rate FROM PlayerPerformance GROUP BY player_id), TeamAggregate AS (SELECT p.player_id, p.team_id, AVG(pp.`rank`) AS team_avg_rank, SUM(pp.comp_score) AS team_total_comp_score, SUM(pp.rounds_won) AS team_total_rounds_won FROM PlayerPerformance AS pp JOIN players AS p ON pp.player_id = p.player_id GROUP BY p.player_id, p.team_id), FinalStats AS (SELECT pa.player_id, pa.avg_rank, pa.top3_finishes, pa.wins, pa.tournaments_played, pa.total_comp_score, pa.total_rounds_won, pa.win_rate, ta.team_avg_rank, ta.team_total_comp_score, ta.team_total_rounds_won FROM PlayerAggregate AS pa LEFT JOIN TeamAggregate AS ta ON pa.player_id = ta.player_id) SELECT fs.player_id, p.player_name, t.team_name, fs.avg_rank, fs.top3_finishes, fs.wins, fs.tournaments_played, fs.total_comp_score, fs.total_rounds_won, fs.win_rate, fs.team_avg_rank, fs.team_total_comp_score, fs.team_total_rounds_won, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY fs.win_rate DESC, fs.avg_rank ASC) AS overall_rank FROM FinalStats AS fs JOIN players AS p ON fs.player_id = p.player_id JOIN teams AS t ON p.team_id = t.team_id ORDER BY overall_rank
gold_sql.postgres: WITH PlayerPerformance AS (SELECT tr.player_id, t.tournament_id, tr.rank, tr.comp_score, tr.rounds_won, CASE WHEN tr.rank <= 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS top3, CASE WHEN tr.rank = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS wins FROM tournament_results AS tr JOIN tournaments AS t ON tr.tournament_id = t.tournament_id), PlayerAggregate AS (SELECT player_id, AVG(rank) AS avg_rank, SUM(top3) AS top3_finishes, SUM(wins) AS wins, COUNT(tournament_id) AS tournaments_played, SUM(comp_score) AS total_comp_score, SUM(rounds_won) AS total_rounds_won, SUM(wins) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(tournament_id), 0) AS win_rate FROM PlayerPerformance GROUP BY player_id), TeamAggregate AS (SELECT p.player_id, p.team_id, AVG(pp.rank) AS team_avg_rank, SUM(pp.comp_score) AS team_total_comp_score, SUM(pp.rounds_won) AS team_total_rounds_won FROM PlayerPerformance AS pp JOIN players AS p ON pp.player_id = p.player_id GROUP BY p.player_id, p.team_id), FinalStats AS (SELECT pa.player_id, pa.avg_rank, pa.top3_finishes, pa.wins, pa.tournaments_played, pa.total_comp_score, pa.total_rounds_won, pa.win_rate, ta.team_avg_rank, ta.team_total_comp_score, ta.team_total_rounds_won FROM PlayerAggregate AS pa LEFT JOIN TeamAggregate AS ta ON pa.player_id = ta.player_id) SELECT fs.player_id, p.player_name, t.team_name, fs.avg_rank, fs.top3_finishes, fs.wins, fs.tournaments_played, fs.total_comp_score, fs.total_rounds_won, fs.win_rate, fs.team_avg_rank, fs.team_total_comp_score, fs.team_total_rounds_won, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY fs.win_rate DESC NULLS LAST, fs.avg_rank ASC NULLS FIRST) AS overall_rank FROM FinalStats AS fs JOIN players AS p ON fs.player_id = p.player_id JOIN teams AS t ON p.team_id = t.team_id ORDER BY overall_rank NULLS FIRST

question: Hey, can you show me a list of all the customers who have made payments, along with their names, the services they use, and their total usage amounts? I'd also like to see the details of their most recent plan changes, if any. Please order the list by customer ID and service name.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH PaidCustomers AS ( SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM payments ), CustomerServiceUsage AS ( SELECT u.customer_id, s.service_name, SUM(u.usage_amount) AS total_usage FROM usage u JOIN services s ON u.service_id = s.service_id WHERE u.customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM PaidCustomers) GROUP BY u.customer_id, s.service_name ), RecentPlanChanges AS ( SELECT pc.customer_id, pc.change_date, pc.change_type, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY pc.customer_id ORDER BY pc.change_date DESC) AS rn FROM plan_changes pc WHERE pc.customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM PaidCustomers) ) SELECT c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS customer_name, csu.service_name, csu.total_usage, rpc.change_date, rpc.change_type FROM customers c JOIN CustomerServiceUsage csu ON c.customer_id = csu.customer_id LEFT JOIN RecentPlanChanges rpc ON c.customer_id = rpc.customer_id AND rpc.rn = 1 WHERE c.customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM PaidCustomers) ORDER BY c.customer_id, csu.service_name
gold_sql.mysql: WITH PaidCustomers AS (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM payments), CustomerServiceUsage AS (SELECT u.customer_id, s.service_name, SUM(u.usage_amount) AS total_usage FROM `usage` AS u JOIN services AS s ON u.service_id = s.service_id WHERE u.customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM PaidCustomers) GROUP BY u.customer_id, s.service_name), RecentPlanChanges AS (SELECT pc.customer_id, pc.change_date, pc.change_type, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY pc.customer_id ORDER BY pc.change_date DESC) AS rn FROM plan_changes AS pc WHERE pc.customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM PaidCustomers)) SELECT CONCAT(c.first_name, ' ', c.last_name) AS customer_name, csu.service_name, csu.total_usage, rpc.change_date, rpc.change_type FROM customers AS c JOIN CustomerServiceUsage AS csu ON c.customer_id = csu.customer_id LEFT JOIN RecentPlanChanges AS rpc ON c.customer_id = rpc.customer_id AND rpc.rn = 1 WHERE c.customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM PaidCustomers) ORDER BY c.customer_id, csu.service_name
gold_sql.postgres: WITH PaidCustomers AS (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM payments), CustomerServiceUsage AS (SELECT u.customer_id, s.service_name, SUM(u.usage_amount) AS total_usage FROM usage AS u JOIN services AS s ON u.service_id = s.service_id WHERE u.customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM PaidCustomers) GROUP BY u.customer_id, s.service_name), RecentPlanChanges AS (SELECT pc.customer_id, pc.change_date, pc.change_type, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY pc.customer_id ORDER BY pc.change_date DESC NULLS LAST) AS rn FROM plan_changes AS pc WHERE pc.customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM PaidCustomers)) SELECT c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS customer_name, csu.service_name, csu.total_usage, rpc.change_date, rpc.change_type FROM customers AS c JOIN CustomerServiceUsage AS csu ON c.customer_id = csu.customer_id LEFT JOIN RecentPlanChanges AS rpc ON c.customer_id = rpc.customer_id AND rpc.rn = 1 WHERE c.customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM PaidCustomers) ORDER BY c.customer_id NULLS FIRST, csu.service_name NULLS FIRST

question: For variants accessed more than once, return the variant ID, the count of accesses, and a list of users who accessed the variant.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT v.variant_id, COUNT(a.access_id) AS access_count, GROUP_CONCAT(u.user_name, ', ') AS accessing_users FROM variants v JOIN access_logs a ON v.variant_id = a.variant_id JOIN users u ON a.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY v.variant_id HAVING COUNT(a.access_id) > 1
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT v.variant_id, COUNT(a.access_id) AS access_count, GROUP_CONCAT(u.user_name SEPARATOR ', ') AS accessing_users FROM variants AS v JOIN access_logs AS a ON v.variant_id = a.variant_id JOIN users AS u ON a.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY v.variant_id HAVING COUNT(a.access_id) > 1
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT v.variant_id, COUNT(a.access_id) AS access_count, STRING_AGG(u.user_name, ', ') AS accessing_users FROM variants AS v JOIN access_logs AS a ON v.variant_id = a.variant_id JOIN users AS u ON a.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY v.variant_id HAVING COUNT(a.access_id) > 1

question: Could you please gather all the ASCII characters that have been accessed more than once? I really need to know their hexadecimal values, the total number of times they've been accessed, and the names of the users who accessed them, and I want the results sorted by the access count in descending order.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT c.hexadecimal_value AS HexValue, COUNT(a.access_id) AS AccessCount, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT u.user_name) AS Users FROM characters c INNER JOIN access_logs a ON c.char_id = a.char_id INNER JOIN users u ON a.user_id = u.user_id WHERE c.ascii_value IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.hexadecimal_value HAVING COUNT(a.access_id) > 1 ORDER BY AccessCount DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT c.hexadecimal_value AS HexValue, COUNT(a.access_id) AS AccessCount, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT u.user_name SEPARATOR ',') AS Users FROM characters AS c INNER JOIN access_logs AS a ON c.char_id = a.char_id INNER JOIN users AS u ON a.user_id = u.user_id WHERE NOT c.ascii_value IS NULL GROUP BY c.hexadecimal_value HAVING COUNT(a.access_id) > 1 ORDER BY AccessCount DESC
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT c.hexadecimal_value AS HexValue, COUNT(a.access_id) AS AccessCount, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT u.user_name, ',') AS Users FROM characters AS c INNER JOIN access_logs AS a ON c.char_id = a.char_id INNER JOIN users AS u ON a.user_id = u.user_id WHERE NOT c.ascii_value IS NULL GROUP BY c.hexadecimal_value HAVING COUNT(a.access_id) > 1 ORDER BY AccessCount DESC NULLS LAST

question: What are the facilities, compartments, and resource types that had significant resource consumption on the specified days, and what were the total amounts consumed, given that notifications were sent on the same days of consumption?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT r.facility_id, r.compartment_id, r.resource_type_id, r.unit, SUM(r.amount) AS total_consumption FROM resource_consumption r JOIN notifications n ON r.facility_id = n.facility_id AND r.compartment_id = n.compartment_id AND STRFTIME('%Y-%m-%d', r.timestamp) = STRFTIME('%Y-%m-%d', n.timestamp) WHERE r.timestamp BETWEEN '2022-01-01' AND '2022-01-02' GROUP BY r.facility_id, r.compartment_id, r.resource_type_id, r.unit HAVING SUM(r.amount) > 100
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT r.facility_id, r.compartment_id, r.resource_type_id, r.unit, SUM(r.amount) AS total_consumption FROM resource_consumption AS r JOIN notifications AS n ON r.facility_id = n.facility_id AND r.compartment_id = n.compartment_id AND DATE_FORMAT(CAST(r.timestamp AS DATETIME), '%Y-%m-%d') = DATE_FORMAT(CAST(n.timestamp AS DATETIME), '%Y-%m-%d') WHERE r.timestamp BETWEEN '2022-01-01' AND '2022-01-02' GROUP BY r.facility_id, r.compartment_id, r.resource_type_id, r.unit HAVING SUM(r.amount) > 100
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT r.facility_id, r.compartment_id, r.resource_type_id, r.unit, SUM(r.amount) AS total_consumption FROM resource_consumption AS r JOIN notifications AS n ON r.facility_id = n.facility_id AND r.compartment_id = n.compartment_id AND TO_CHAR(CAST(r.timestamp AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY-MM-DD') = TO_CHAR(CAST(n.timestamp AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY-MM-DD') WHERE r.timestamp BETWEEN '2022-01-01' AND '2022-01-02' GROUP BY r.facility_id, r.compartment_id, r.resource_type_id, r.unit HAVING SUM(r.amount) > 100

question: Could you provide a detailed summary for each configuration, including its version, build environment, number of build attempts, successes, and failures, total and shared dependencies, creator and last modifier, and the latest roles of users associated with the configuration, along with the date these roles were assigned, ordered by configuration ID?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ConfigBuildLogs AS ( SELECT bl.config_id, bl.build_environment, COUNT(*) AS build_attempts, SUM(CASE WHEN bl.build_status = 'Success' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS build_successes, SUM(CASE WHEN bl.build_status = 'Failure' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS build_failures FROM build_logs bl GROUP BY bl.config_id, bl.build_environment ), ConfigDependencies AS ( SELECT c.config_id, COUNT(*) AS total_dependencies, SUM(CASE WHEN d.is_shared = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS shared_dependencies FROM configurations c LEFT JOIN dependencies d ON c.config_id = d.config_id GROUP BY c.config_id ), ConfigurationsWithDetails AS ( SELECT c.config_id, c.config_version, c.build_environment, cb.build_attempts, cb.build_successes, cb.build_failures, cd.total_dependencies, cd.shared_dependencies, c.created_by, c.last_modified_by, u1.username AS creator, u2.username AS last_modifier FROM configurations c LEFT JOIN ConfigBuildLogs cb ON c.config_id = cb.config_id LEFT JOIN ConfigDependencies cd ON c.config_id = cd.config_id LEFT JOIN users u1 ON c.created_by = u1.user_id LEFT JOIN users u2 ON c.last_modified_by = u2.user_id ), UserRoles AS ( SELECT up.user_id, up.config_id, u.role, MAX(up.created_date) AS permission_creation_date FROM user_permissions up INNER JOIN users u ON up.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY up.user_id, up.config_id, u.role ) SELECT c.config_id, ( SELECT 'Configuration ' || c.config_version || ' in ' || c.build_environment || ': ' || CASE WHEN c.build_attempts = 0 THEN 'No builds yet.' ELSE 'Builds: ' || c.build_attempts || ', Successes: ' || c.build_successes || ', Failures: ' || c.build_failures || '. ' || 'Dependencies: ' || c.total_dependencies || ', Shared: ' || c.shared_dependencies || '. ' || 'Created by: ' || c.creator || ', Last modified by: ' || c.last_modifier || '. ' || 'Latest user roles: ' || GROUP_CONCAT(ur.role || ' (since ' || ur.permission_creation_date || ')') END FROM UserRoles ur WHERE ur.config_id = c.config_id GROUP BY ur.config_id ) AS config_summary FROM ConfigurationsWithDetails c ORDER BY c.config_id

question:
**User**: Can you help me get a report on our inventory items?
**Assistant**: Of course! What specific information are you looking for?
**User**: I need details on items that have sold units or have pending requests, and also have less than 10 units in stock.
**Assistant**: Got it. Would you like all the details for these items, including their names, categories, locations, and quantities?
**User**: Yes, and also include the total number of sold units and pending requests for each item.
**Assistant**: Alright, and do we need to know the current condition of these items?
**User**: Yes, please include the most recent condition status as well.
**Assistant**: Is there anything else you'd like to know about these items?
**User**: No, that’s everything I need.
**Assistant**: OK, I will help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH SoldItems AS ( SELECT item_id, COUNT(*) AS total_sold FROM requests WHERE action = 'Sold' AND status = 'Approved' GROUP BY item_id ), PendingRequests AS ( SELECT item_id, COUNT(*) AS total_requests FROM requests WHERE status = 'Pending' GROUP BY item_id ), ItemCondition AS ( SELECT item_id, condition FROM item_condition ic WHERE condition_date = ( SELECT MAX(condition_date) FROM item_condition WHERE item_id = ic.item_id ) ) SELECT i.item_id, i.item_name, c.category_name, l.location_name, i.quantity, COALESCE(SoldItems.total_sold, 0) AS total_sold, COALESCE(PendingRequests.total_requests, 0) AS total_pending_requests, ItemCondition.condition FROM inventory_items i LEFT JOIN SoldItems ON i.item_id = SoldItems.item_id LEFT JOIN PendingRequests ON i.item_id = PendingRequests.item_id LEFT JOIN ItemCondition ON i.item_id = ItemCondition.item_id INNER JOIN categories c ON i.category_id = c.category_id INNER JOIN locations l ON i.location_id = l.location_id WHERE i.quantity < 10 AND (SoldItems.total_sold > 0 OR PendingRequests.total_requests > 0)

question: What are the names, types, configuration details, optimization results, component highlights, and user access information for all experiments, listed in reverse chronological order by start date, along with their corresponding row numbers indicating the latest experiment?
external_knowledge: ; The term "configuration details" refers to the specific settings and parameters used to run an experiment, such as population size, generations, and mutation rate; The term "optimization results" refers to the outcomes of the experiment, including the maximum generation, total feasible individuals, and average fitness over generations; The term "component highlights" refers to notable features of the experiment's components, such as the largest component size and average component score; The term "user access information" refers to the list of usernames with permission to access the experiment.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ExperimentConfigDetails AS ( SELECT e.experiment_id, e.name, e.experiment_type, e.start_date, ec.population_size, ec.generations, ec.mutation_rate, ec.crossover_rate, ec.selection_method, ec.initial_population_method, ec.termination_condition FROM experiments e INNER JOIN experiment_configs ec ON e.experiment_id = ec.experiment_id ), OptimizationSummary AS ( SELECT er.experiment_id, MAX(er.generation) AS max_generation, SUM(er.feasible_individuals) AS total_feasible_individuals, AVG(er.average_fitness) AS average_fitness_over_generations FROM optimization_results er GROUP BY er.experiment_id ), ComponentHighlights AS ( SELECT cc.experiment_id, MAX(cc.component_size) AS largest_component_size, AVG(cc.component_score) AS average_component_score FROM connected_components cc GROUP BY cc.experiment_id ), UserExperimentAccess AS ( SELECT ue.experiment_id, GROUP_CONCAT(u.username, ', ') AS user_access_list FROM user_experiments ue INNER JOIN users u ON ue.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY ue.experiment_id ), DetailedExperimentInfo AS ( SELECT ec.experiment_id, ec.name, ec.experiment_type, ec.start_date, ec.population_size, ec.generations, ec.mutation_rate, ec.crossover_rate, ec.selection_method, ec.initial_population_method, ec.termination_condition, os.max_generation, os.total_feasible_individuals, os.average_fitness_over_generations, ch.largest_component_size, ch.average_component_score, uea.user_access_list FROM ExperimentConfigDetails ec LEFT JOIN OptimizationSummary os ON ec.experiment_id = os.experiment_id LEFT JOIN ComponentHighlights ch ON ec.experiment_id = ch.experiment_id LEFT JOIN UserExperimentAccess uea ON ec.experiment_id = uea.experiment_id ) SELECT dei.name, dei.experiment_type, dei.population_size, dei.generations, dei.mutation_rate, dei.crossover_rate, dei.selection_method, dei.initial_population_method, dei.termination_condition, dei.max_generation, dei.total_feasible_individuals, dei.average_fitness_over_generations, dei.largest_component_size, dei.average_component_score, SUBSTR(dei.user_access_list, 1, 50) AS user_access_summary, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY dei.start_date DESC) AS latest_experiment FROM DetailedExperimentInfo dei ORDER BY dei.start_date DESC

question: Hey! Could you help me find the labels of all the classes that have usage notes starting with "Use this class for data relating to," descriptions starting with "This class represents," and have been edited? I need the labels concatenated into a single string separated by commas.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(l.label_value, ', ') AS labels_concatenated FROM classes c JOIN labels l ON c.class_id = l.class_id WHERE c.class_id IN ( SELECT u.class_id FROM usage_notes u WHERE u.note_value LIKE 'Use this class for data relating to%' ) AND c.class_id IN ( SELECT d.class_id FROM descriptions d WHERE d.description_value LIKE 'This class represents%' ) AND c.class_id IN ( SELECT a.class_id FROM access_logs a WHERE a.access_type = 'edit' )
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(l.label_value SEPARATOR ', ') AS labels_concatenated FROM classes AS c JOIN labels AS l ON c.class_id = l.class_id WHERE c.class_id IN (SELECT u.class_id FROM usage_notes AS u WHERE u.note_value LIKE 'Use this class for data relating to%') AND c.class_id IN (SELECT d.class_id FROM descriptions AS d WHERE d.description_value LIKE 'This class represents%') AND c.class_id IN (SELECT a.class_id FROM access_logs AS a WHERE a.access_type = 'edit')

question: Students' top grades for each course and the average grade percentage for the course, return the student names and course names.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH RankedQualifications AS ( SELECT q.student_id, s.first_name, s.last_name, c.course_name, g.grade, g.percentage_range, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY q.student_id, c.course_name ORDER BY g.grade DESC) as rank_by_grade FROM qualifications q INNER JOIN students s ON q.student_id = s.student_id INNER JOIN courses c ON q.course_id = c.course_id INNER JOIN grades g ON q.grade_id = g.grade_id ), TopGrades AS ( SELECT rq.student_id, rq.first_name, rq.last_name, rq.course_name, rq.grade, rq.percentage_range FROM RankedQualifications rq WHERE rq.rank_by_grade = 1 ) SELECT tg.first_name, tg.last_name, tg.course_name, tg.grade, AVG(CAST(SUBSTR(tg.percentage_range, 1, INSTR(tg.percentage_range, '-') - 1) AS REAL)) OVER (PARTITION BY tg.course_name) as average_grade_percentage FROM TopGrades tg ORDER BY tg.first_name, tg.last_name, tg.course_name
gold_sql.mysql: WITH RankedQualifications AS (SELECT q.student_id, s.first_name, s.last_name, c.course_name, g.grade, g.percentage_range, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY q.student_id, c.course_name ORDER BY g.grade DESC) AS rank_by_grade FROM qualifications AS q INNER JOIN students AS s ON q.student_id = s.student_id INNER JOIN courses AS c ON q.course_id = c.course_id INNER JOIN grades AS g ON q.grade_id = g.grade_id), TopGrades AS (SELECT rq.student_id, rq.first_name, rq.last_name, rq.course_name, rq.grade, rq.percentage_range FROM RankedQualifications AS rq WHERE rq.rank_by_grade = 1) SELECT tg.first_name, tg.last_name, tg.course_name, tg.grade, AVG(CAST(SUBSTRING(tg.percentage_range, 1, LOCATE('-', tg.percentage_range) - 1) AS FLOAT)) OVER (PARTITION BY tg.course_name) AS average_grade_percentage FROM TopGrades AS tg ORDER BY tg.first_name, tg.last_name, tg.course_name
gold_sql.postgres: WITH RankedQualifications AS (SELECT q.student_id, s.first_name, s.last_name, c.course_name, g.grade, g.percentage_range, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY q.student_id, c.course_name ORDER BY g.grade DESC NULLS LAST) AS rank_by_grade FROM qualifications AS q INNER JOIN students AS s ON q.student_id = s.student_id INNER JOIN courses AS c ON q.course_id = c.course_id INNER JOIN grades AS g ON q.grade_id = g.grade_id), TopGrades AS (SELECT rq.student_id, rq.first_name, rq.last_name, rq.course_name, rq.grade, rq.percentage_range FROM RankedQualifications AS rq WHERE rq.rank_by_grade = 1) SELECT tg.first_name, tg.last_name, tg.course_name, tg.grade, AVG(CAST(SUBSTRING(tg.percentage_range FROM 1 FOR STRPOS(tg.percentage_range, '-') - 1) AS REAL)) OVER (PARTITION BY tg.course_name) AS average_grade_percentage FROM TopGrades AS tg ORDER BY tg.first_name NULLS FIRST, tg.last_name NULLS FIRST, tg.course_name NULLS FIRST

question: Hey, could you please provide a detailed report on all outbreaks, including their etiology, total cases, year, location, start and end dates, status, contributing factors, categories, intervention types, descriptions, effectiveness, total case counts, average patient ages, and the cumulative number of cases over time for each location, ordered by outbreak year, start date, and outbreak ID?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH CaseSummary AS ( SELECT c.outbreak_id, COUNT(c.case_id) AS case_count, AVG(c.patient_age) AS average_age FROM cases c GROUP BY c.outbreak_id ), OutbreakFactors AS ( SELECT ofr.outbreak_id, f.factor_description, f.category FROM outbreak_factors ofr INNER JOIN factors f ON ofr.factor_id = f.factor_id ), OutbreakInterventions AS ( SELECT i.outbreak_id, i.intervention_type, i.description, i.effectiveness FROM interventions i ) SELECT o.outbreak_id, e.name AS etiology_name, o.total_cases, o.outbreak_year, l.location_name, o.start_date, o.end_date, o.status, OF.factor_description, OF.category, OI.intervention_type, OI.description AS intervention_description, OI.effectiveness, CS.case_count, CS.average_age, SUM(o.total_cases) OVER (PARTITION BY l.location_name ORDER BY o.outbreak_year, o.start_date) AS cumulative_cases FROM outbreaks o INNER JOIN etiologies e ON o.etiology_id = e.etiology_id INNER JOIN locations l ON o.location_id = l.location_id LEFT JOIN OutbreakFactors OF ON o.outbreak_id = OF.outbreak_id LEFT JOIN OutbreakInterventions OI ON o.outbreak_id = OI.outbreak_id LEFT JOIN CaseSummary CS ON o.outbreak_id = CS.outbreak_id ORDER BY o.outbreak_year, o.start_date, o.outbreak_id

question: What are the names of the top three services used by customers who have not churned and have been with the company for more than 12 months?

question: What are the names and categories of ETF types with average management fees above 0.5, along with their average management and other expenses, and the names of the users who last accessed them, for the year 2022, sorted by category and average management fee in descending order?
external_knowledge: A management fee is a charge levied by an investment manager for managing an investment fund; Other expenses refer to additional costs associated with the fund that are not included in the management fee; An ETF type category can be, for example, 'equity' or 'fixed income'; The average management fee being greater than 0.5 implies that the average fee is more than half of a percent.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT et.etf_type_name, et.etf_type_category, AVG(ehe.management_fee) AS avg_management_fee, AVG(ehe.other_expenses) AS avg_other_expenses, u.user_name AS last_accessed_by FROM etf_types et INNER JOIN etf_historical_expenses ehe ON et.etf_type_id = ehe.etf_type_id LEFT JOIN ( SELECT al.etf_type_id, al.user_id, al.access_date FROM access_logs al INNER JOIN ( SELECT etf_type_id, MAX(access_date) AS max_date FROM access_logs WHERE strftime('%Y', access_date) = '2022' GROUP BY etf_type_id ) al_sub ON al.etf_type_id = al_sub.etf_type_id AND al.access_date = al_sub.max_date ) latest_access ON et.etf_type_id = latest_access.etf_type_id LEFT JOIN users u ON latest_access.user_id = u.user_id WHERE ehe.expense_date BETWEEN '2022-01-01' AND '2022-12-31' GROUP BY et.etf_type_name, et.etf_type_category, u.user_name HAVING AVG(ehe.management_fee) > 0.5 ORDER BY et.etf_type_category, avg_management_fee DESC

question: Could you provide the yearly ratio of course reviews to enrollments along with a moving average of this ratio over a 6-year window, including the current year and the previous 5 years?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH EnrollmentsPerYear AS ( SELECT STRFTIME('%Y', enrollment_date) as year, COUNT(enrollment_id) as num_enrollments FROM enrollments GROUP BY year ), CourseReviewsPerYear AS ( SELECT STRFTIME('%Y', enrollment_date) as year, COUNT(course_review_id) as num_reviews FROM course_reviews INNER JOIN enrollments ON course_reviews.student_id = enrollments.student_id GROUP BY year ), CourseReviewsAndEnrollments AS ( SELECT epy.year, epy.num_enrollments, IFNULL(cpy.num_reviews, 0) as num_reviews, CASE WHEN epy.num_enrollments > 0 THEN IFNULL(cpy.num_reviews, 0) * 1.0 / epy.num_enrollments ELSE 0 END as review_ratio FROM EnrollmentsPerYear epy LEFT JOIN CourseReviewsPerYear cpy ON epy.year = cpy.year UNION SELECT cpy.year, IFNULL(epy.num_enrollments, 0) as num_enrollments, cpy.num_reviews, CASE WHEN epy.num_enrollments > 0 THEN cpy.num_reviews * 1.0 / epy.num_enrollments ELSE 0 END as review_ratio FROM CourseReviewsPerYear cpy LEFT JOIN EnrollmentsPerYear epy ON cpy.year = epy.year WHERE epy.year IS NULL ) SELECT year, review_ratio, AVG(review_ratio) OVER (ORDER BY year ROWS BETWEEN 5 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) as moving_avg_review_ratio FROM CourseReviewsAndEnrollments ORDER BY year

question: Hey! Can you show me the names of LSOA areas with more than 5000 people, along with their total average electricity demand, population, and area size for each year? I'd love to see the areas with the highest total average demand first.

question:
**User**: I need to get a summary of the top 10 tags with the most recent validation events. Can you help me with that?
**Assistant**: Of course! Could you tell me what specific information you need for each tag?
**User**: I need the tag ID, tag name, the number of validation events, the number of unique validators, and the date of the most recent validation event.
**Assistant**: Got it. Do you want this information for all tags or just the top 10 based on the most recent validation date?
**User**: Just the top 10 based on the most recent validation date.
**Assistant**: Understood. Should the results be formatted in a specific way, such as a single concatenated string?
**User**: Yes, please format the results as a single string with each tag's details separated by semicolons.
**Assistant**: OK, I will help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ValidationSummary AS ( SELECT t.tag_id, t.name AS tag_name, COUNT(tv.validation_id) AS validation_count, COUNT(DISTINCT tv.user_id) AS unique_validators, MAX(tv.validation_date) AS latest_validation_date FROM tags t JOIN tag_validations tv ON t.tag_id = tv.tag_id GROUP BY t.tag_id, t.name ), RankedValidations AS ( SELECT tag_id, tag_name, validation_count, unique_validators, latest_validation_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY latest_validation_date DESC) AS rn FROM ValidationSummary ) SELECT GROUP_CONCAT( tag_id || ',' || tag_name || ',' || validation_count || ',' || unique_validators || ',' || latest_validation_date , '; ') AS summary FROM RankedValidations WHERE rn <= 10
gold_sql.mysql: WITH ValidationSummary AS (SELECT t.tag_id, t.name AS tag_name, COUNT(tv.validation_id) AS validation_count, COUNT(DISTINCT tv.user_id) AS unique_validators, MAX(tv.validation_date) AS latest_validation_date FROM tags AS t JOIN tag_validations AS tv ON t.tag_id = tv.tag_id GROUP BY t.tag_id, t.name), RankedValidations AS (SELECT tag_id, tag_name, validation_count, unique_validators, latest_validation_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY latest_validation_date DESC) AS rn FROM ValidationSummary) SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(tag_id, ',', tag_name, ',', validation_count, ',', unique_validators, ',', latest_validation_date) SEPARATOR '; ') AS summary FROM RankedValidations WHERE rn <= 10

question: What are the titles, statuses, sequence numbers, vote counts, most recent vote dates, access counts, most recent access dates, full category paths, and document counts for all plenary items, ordered by their sequence in the session and then by title?
external_knowledge: This query assumes that a "plenary item" refers to an agenda item or point of discussion in a formal meeting, such as a conference or parliamentary session. Sequence numbers typically reflect the order in which these items are discussed during the session. question:
**User**: I want to get some information about our sales agents.
**Assistant**: What kind of information would you like to know about the sales agents?
**User**: I want to see their sales performance.
**Assistant**: Do you want to see their performance by month or by quarter?
**User**: By quarter would be great.
**Assistant**: Would you like to see their total sales or total commission?
**User**: Both would be useful.
**Assistant**: How would you like the agents to be ranked?
**User**: By their commission earnings, from highest to lowest.
**Assistant**: Do you want to see the agent names along with their IDs?
**User**: Yes, that would be helpful.
**Assistant**: Would you like the results to be ordered by any specific criteria?
**User**: Yes, by year and then by quarter, both in descending order.
**Assistant**: Finally, is there anything else you'd like to know about the sales agents?
**User**: No, that's all.
**Assistant**: OK, I will help you translate your request into an SQL query.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH QuarterlySales AS ( SELECT s.agent_id, strftime('%Y', s.transaction_date) AS year, CASE WHEN strftime('%m', s.transaction_date) IN ('01', '02', '03') THEN 'Q1' WHEN strftime('%m', s.transaction_date) IN ('04', '05', '06') THEN 'Q2' WHEN strftime('%m', s.transaction_date) IN ('07', '08', '09') THEN 'Q3' WHEN strftime('%m', s.transaction_date) IN ('10', '11', '12') THEN 'Q4' END AS quarter, SUM(CAST(replace(replace(s.amount, '$', ''), ',', '') AS REAL)) AS total_sales, SUM(CAST(replace(replace(s.commission, '$', ''), ',', '') AS REAL)) AS total_commission FROM sales_transactions s GROUP BY s.agent_id, year, quarter ), RankedAgents AS ( SELECT qs.agent_id, qs.year, qs.quarter, qs.total_sales, qs.total_commission, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY qs.year, qs.quarter ORDER BY qs.total_commission DESC) AS commission_rank FROM QuarterlySales qs ) SELECT ra.agent_id, sa.agent_name, ra.year, ra.quarter, ra.total_sales, ra.total_commission, ra.commission_rank FROM RankedAgents ra JOIN sales_agents sa ON ra.agent_id = sa.agent_id ORDER BY ra.year DESC, ra.quarter DESC, ra.commission_rank ASC

question: Could you please gather all the model details, including their names, frameworks, devices they can run on, batch sizes for GPU and DLA, workspace sizes, model types, descriptions, creation and update timestamps, and statuses? Additionally, I need the concatenated input and output descriptions, URLs with their types and descriptions, resource details including types and URLs, and version information including numbers, release dates, and statuses for each model, all ordered by the model ID?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH ModelDetails AS ( SELECT m.model_id, m.model_name, m.framework, m.devices, m.batch_size_gpu, m.batch_size_dla, m.ws_gpu, m.ws_dla, m.model_type, m.description, m.created_at, m.updated_at, m.status FROM models m ), ModelAttribute AS ( SELECT model_id, GROUP_CONCAT(input_description || ', ') AS input_details, GROUP_CONCAT(output_description || ', ') AS output_details FROM ( SELECT m.model_id, i.input_description, o.output_description FROM models m LEFT JOIN model_inputs i ON m.model_id = i.model_id LEFT JOIN model_outputs o ON m.model_id = o.model_id ) subquery GROUP BY model_id ), ModelURLs AS ( SELECT model_id, GROUP_CONCAT(url || ',' || url_type || ',' || description || ';') AS url_details FROM model_urls GROUP BY model_id ), ModelResources AS ( SELECT model_id, GROUP_CONCAT(description || ',' || resource_type || ',' || url || ';') AS resource_details FROM resources GROUP BY model_id ), ModelVersions AS ( SELECT model_id, GROUP_CONCAT(version_number || ',' || release_date || ',' || status || ';') AS version_details FROM model_versions GROUP BY model_id ) SELECT md.model_id, md.model_name, md.framework, md.devices, md.batch_size_gpu, md.batch_size_dla, md.ws_gpu, md.ws_dla, md.model_type, md.description, md.created_at, md.updated_at, md.status, ma.input_details, ma.output_details, mu.url_details, mr.resource_details, mv.version_details FROM ModelDetails md LEFT JOIN ModelAttribute ma ON md.model_id = ma.model_id LEFT JOIN ModelURLs mu ON md.model_id = mu.model_id LEFT JOIN ModelResources mr ON md.model_id = mr.model_id LEFT JOIN ModelVersions mv ON md.model_id = mv.model_id ORDER BY md.model_id

question: Return business names, average ratings, review counts, favorite counts, and active promotions for all businesses, ordered by their average ratings and review counts in descending order.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH BusinessRatings AS ( SELECT business_id, AVG(rating) AS average_rating FROM reviews GROUP BY business_id ), BusinessReviews AS ( SELECT business_id, COUNT(*) AS review_count FROM reviews GROUP BY business_id ), BusinessFavorites AS ( SELECT business_id, COUNT(*) AS favorite_count FROM favorites GROUP BY business_id ), BusinessPromotions AS ( SELECT business_id, GROUP_CONCAT(promo_description, ', ') AS active_promotions FROM promotions WHERE promotion_status = 'active' GROUP BY business_id ) SELECT b.name AS business_name, IFNULL(br.average_rating, 0) AS average_rating, IFNULL(brv.review_count, 0) AS review_count, IFNULL(bf.favorite_count, 0) AS favorite_count, IFNULL(bp.active_promotions, '') AS active_promotions FROM businesses b LEFT JOIN BusinessRatings br ON b.business_id = br.business_id LEFT JOIN BusinessReviews brv ON b.business_id = brv.business_id LEFT JOIN BusinessFavorites bf ON b.business_id = bf.business_id LEFT JOIN BusinessPromotions bp ON b.business_id = bp.business_id ORDER BY average_rating DESC, review_count DESC

question: What are the total rushing yards and average stadium attendance for each school in each season, like a scoreboard showing the strength and crowd support of each team?
external_knowledge:
- 'Total rushing yards' is a football statistic that measures the total distance a team's running backs and other players have run with the ball during a game or season.
- 'Average stadium attendance' is the mean number of spectators attending games at a particular stadium over a specified period.

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH SeasonRushingStats AS ( SELECT ss.season_id, ss.school_id, SUM(CAST(ss.stat_value AS INTEGER)) AS total_rushing_yards FROM season_statistics ss WHERE ss.stat_name = 'total_rushing_yards' GROUP BY ss.season_id, ss.school_id ), GameAttendanceStats AS ( SELECT g.school_id, AVG(CAST(ga.total_attendance AS INTEGER)) AS avg_stadium_attendance FROM games g INNER JOIN game_attendance ga ON g.game_id = ga.game_id GROUP BY g.school_id ) SELECT srs.season_id, srs.school_id, srs.total_rushing_yards, gas.avg_stadium_attendance FROM SeasonRushingStats srs LEFT JOIN GameAttendanceStats gas ON srs.school_id = gas.school_id ORDER BY srs.season_id, srs.school_id
gold_sql.mysql: WITH SeasonRushingStats AS (SELECT ss.season_id, ss.school_id, SUM(CAST(ss.stat_value AS SIGNED)) AS total_rushing_yards FROM season_statistics AS ss WHERE ss.stat_name = 'total_rushing_yards' GROUP BY ss.season_id, ss.school_id), GameAttendanceStats AS (SELECT g.school_id, AVG(CAST(ga.total_attendance AS SIGNED)) AS avg_stadium_attendance FROM games AS g INNER JOIN game_attendance AS ga ON g.game_id = ga.game_id GROUP BY g.school_id) SELECT srs.season_id, srs.school_id, srs.total_rushing_yards, gas.avg_stadium_attendance FROM SeasonRushingStats AS srs LEFT JOIN GameAttendanceStats AS gas ON srs.school_id = gas.school_id ORDER BY srs.season_id, srs.school_id

question: Could you please show me the top subject by enrollment for each university where the research efficiency is higher than 0.01, along with the university name and the subject name, sorted by university name and subject name?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH UniversitySubjectEnrollments AS ( SELECT us.university_id, us.subject_id, s.subject_name, us.enrollment, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY us.university_id ORDER BY us.enrollment DESC) AS subject_enrollment_rank FROM university_subjects us JOIN subjects s ON us.subject_id = s.subject_id ), FilteredUniversities AS ( SELECT u.university_id, u.university_name, u.research_output, u.endowment, 1.0 * u.research_output / u.endowment AS research_efficiency FROM universities u WHERE 1.0 * u.research_output / u.endowment > 0.01 ) SELECT f.university_name, use.subject_name FROM UniversitySubjectEnrollments use JOIN FilteredUniversities f ON use.university_id = f.university_id WHERE use.subject_enrollment_rank = 1 ORDER BY f.university_name, use.subject_name
gold_sql.mysql: WITH UniversitySubjectEnrollments AS (SELECT us.university_id, us.subject_id, s.subject_name, us.enrollment, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY us.university_id ORDER BY us.enrollment DESC) AS subject_enrollment_rank FROM university_subjects AS us JOIN subjects AS s ON us.subject_id = s.subject_id), FilteredUniversities AS (SELECT u.university_id, u.university_name, u.research_output, u.endowment, 1.0 * u.research_output / u.endowment AS research_efficiency FROM universities AS u WHERE 1.0 * u.research_output / u.endowment > 0.01) SELECT f.university_name, `use`.subject_name FROM UniversitySubjectEnrollments AS `use` JOIN FilteredUniversities AS f ON `use`.university_id = f.university_id WHERE `use`.subject_enrollment_rank = 1 ORDER BY f.university_name, `use`.subject_name

question: Could you tell me which projects have spent the most time on their tests, and approximately how much time each has spent?
external_knowledge:
- 'Time spent on their tests' refers to the cumulative execution time of all test runs associated with each project.
- 'Most time' implies the projects are ranked by descending total execution time.

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT prj.project_name, SUM(CAST(SUBSTR(tr.time, 1, INSTR(tr.time, ' ') - 1) AS INTEGER)) AS total_time_ms FROM test_runs tr INNER JOIN test_cases tc ON tr.test_case_id = tc.test_case_id INNER JOIN methods m ON tc.method_id = m.method_id INNER JOIN classes cls ON m.class_id = cls.class_id INNER JOIN packages pkg ON cls.package_id = pkg.package_id INNER JOIN projects prj ON pkg.project_id = prj.project_id GROUP BY prj.project_name ORDER BY total_time_ms DESC
gold_sql.mysql: SELECT prj.project_name, SUM(CAST(SUBSTRING(tr.time, 1, LOCATE(' ', tr.time) - 1) AS SIGNED)) AS total_time_ms FROM test_runs AS tr INNER JOIN test_cases AS tc ON tr.test_case_id = tc.test_case_id INNER JOIN methods AS m ON tc.method_id = m.method_id INNER JOIN classes AS cls ON m.class_id = cls.class_id INNER JOIN packages AS pkg ON cls.package_id = pkg.package_id INNER JOIN projects AS prj ON pkg.project_id = prj.project_id GROUP BY prj.project_name ORDER BY total_time_ms DESC
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT prj.project_name, SUM(CAST(SUBSTRING(tr.time FROM 1 FOR STRPOS(tr.time, ' ') - 1) AS INT)) AS total_time_ms FROM test_runs AS tr INNER JOIN test_cases AS tc ON tr.test_case_id = tc.test_case_id INNER JOIN methods AS m ON tc.method_id = m.method_id INNER JOIN classes AS cls ON m.class_id = cls.class_id INNER JOIN packages AS pkg ON cls.package_id = pkg.package_id INNER JOIN projects AS prj ON pkg.project_id = prj.project_id GROUP BY prj.project_name ORDER BY total_time_ms DESC NULLS LAST

question: Could you please determine the average success rate for each software version, but only include completed test runs that have achieved a success rate higher than 50%, and provide the corresponding version numbers?

gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT sv.version_number, AVG(CAST(REPLACE(TRIM(SUBSTR(tr.success_rate, 1, INSTR(tr.success_rate, '%') - 1)), ',', '.') question: What is a summary of the average value, good and poor quality data counts, and access count for weather data related to the US's national seasonal onset?

gold_sql.sqlite: WITH SelectedLocations AS ( SELECT location_id FROM locations WHERE location_name = 'US National' ), SelectedTargets AS ( SELECT target_id FROM targets WHERE target_name = 'Season onset' ), FilteredData AS ( SELECT wd.* FROM weather_data wd INNER JOIN SelectedLocations sl ON wd.location_id = sl.location_id INNER JOIN SelectedTargets st ON wd.target_id = st.target_id ), DataQuality AS ( SELECT AVG(value) AS average_value, SUM(CASE WHEN quality_flag = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS good_quality_count, SUM(CASE WHEN quality_flag = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS poor_quality_count FROM FilteredData ), AccessPatterns AS ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS access_count FROM access_logs al INNER JOIN FilteredData fd ON al.data_id = fd.data_id ) SELECT 'Average Value: ' || CAST(dq.average_value AS TEXT) || ', Good Quality Count: ' || CAST(dq.good_quality_count AS TEXT) || ', Poor Quality Count: ' || CAST(dq.poor_quality_count AS TEXT) || ', Access Count: ' || CAST(ap.access_count AS TEXT) AS summary FROM DataQuality dq, AccessPatterns ap
